doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67479-w.title: Baicalin attenuates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by modulating TLR4/MD-2-associated inflammatory responses and reducing neutrophil‑related tissue injury
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67479-w.abstract: The sterile inflammatory response, particularly the self-amplifying axis involving complement, neutrophils, and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), is a critical driver of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI). However, effective strategies to therapeutically target this amplification cascade are limited. Baicalin (BAI), a flavonoid with known anti-inflammatory properties, may modulate this intricate network, but its specific impact on the sterile immune amplification axis in MIRI remains undefined. An MIRI model was established in SD rats, which were randomly assigned to Sham, I/R, and I/R + BAI groups. Cardiac function and infarct size were assessed via echocardiography, TTC staining, and serum biomarkers. Transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) analyzed differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. Key pathways were validated using immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and Western blot. In an HL-60 cell model, the interaction between BAI and TLR4/MD-2 was investigated via CCK-8, qPCR, Western blot, CETSA, and molecular docking. BAI significantly reduced myocardial infarct size (as assessed by IA/TA), improved cardiac function, and decreased serum cTnI and LDH levels induced by MIRI. Transcriptome analysis suggested that BAI reversed I/R-induced expression of genes related to complement‑related responses, neutrophil degranulation, and TLR signaling. Further experiments indicated that BAI attenuated complement C3a generation, neutrophil infiltration, and markers associated with NETs formation. Mechanistically, BAI interacted with the TLR4/MD-2 complex (likely via MD-2), suppressed downstream NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling activation, and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine release. The TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 mimicked the protective effects of BAI, whereas HMGB1 partially reversed the anti-inflammatory effects of BAI. This study shows that BAI attenuates the pathogenic sterile immune amplification axis, comprising complement‑related responses, neutrophil infiltration, and NETs‑associated markers, to confer cardioprotection against MIRI. Its mechanism of action is functionally linked to the interaction with the TLR4/MD-2 complex and subsequent inhibition of downstream inflammatory signaling. These findings highlight a promising immunomodulatory strategy for MIRI treatment by modulating a critical upstream node within this amplification network; however, direct binding between baicalin and the TLR4/MD-2 complex remains to be indicated in future studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60846-7.title: Coherent eddies redistribute microplastics across the water column
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60846-7.abstract: Abstract The ocean interior is emerging as a hidden reservoir of microplastics, yet the mechanisms governing their accumulation below the surface remain poorly understood. Despite growing interest in microplastic distribution throughout the ocean, in-situ observations within smaller-scale oceanographic features such as mesoscale eddies and fronts remain sparse. Here we present in-situ observations of microplastic distributions from 50 to 1200 m within two coherent mesoscale eddies south of the Canary Islands, an anticyclone and a cyclone. Combining physical oceanographic measurements and microplastic sampling with Lagrangian Coherent Structure (LCS) analyses, we show that both eddies enhanced microplastic concentrations in the upper 200 m by up to threefold relative to regional background waters. Small fragments (< 200 μm) dominated microplastic abundances, while fibers were significantly more abundant in the cyclone and larger fragments prevailed in the anticyclonic eddy. These findings reinforce that coherent eddies act as dynamic drivers of microplastic redistribution in the Atlantic Ocean, emphasizing the role of particle-specific inertial dynamics in shaping the fate of plastics throughout the water column.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69927-z.title: Ultrasound-based radiomics combined with clinical features for predicting myometrial invasion depth in endometrial carcinoma
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69927-z.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most prevalent gynecologic malignancies worldwide, with rising incidence. Preoperative assessment of myometrial invasion depth is crucial for treatment planning and prognostication. Deep invasion (> 50% myometrial thickness) is a well-recognized risk factor for lymph node metastasis, recurrence, and poor survival, often requiring extended surgery and adjuvant therapy. Transvaginal ultrasound is commonly used for evaluation, but subjective interpretation based on morphological features—such as endometrial thickening and myometrial disruption—is highly operator-dependent, limiting its reliability and reproducibility. To address this limitation, we developed an interpretable machine learning model integrating clinical and ultrasound radiomics data to predict the depth of myometrial invasion in EC. Retrospective data from 294 patients were analyzed, with 205 (70%)assigned to the training set and 89 (30%)to the test set. After feature extraction and selection using intraclass/interclass correlation coefficients and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, radscores were calculated and combined with clinical variables—including demographics, tumor markers, and ultrasound characteristics—to build nine machine learning models. The random forest model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.85 and an F1 score of 0.81 for predicting deep myometrial invasion, and an AUC of 0.77 and an F1 score of 0.74 for any myometrial invasion in the test set. The SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis revealed that maximum tumor diameter, age, carcinoembryonic antigen levels, and radscore1 were key predictors for deep invasion, while tumor diameter, age, radscore2, and blood flow signal grade contributed most to predicting any invasion. This explainable model provides a non-invasive, clinically relevant tool for preoperative risk stratification, potentially supporting personalized treatment decisions in endometrial carcinoma.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68552-0.title: Experimental and numerical investigation of voltage-dependent active vibration control on a notch-cracked composite mono leaf spring
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68552-0.abstract: This paper presents combined experimental and numerical research on the application of an Active Vibration Control System (AVCS) to a cracked glass-fibre-reinforced polymer (GFRP) composite mono leaf spring for automotive suspension systems, an application that, to the authors’ knowledge, has received very limited prior attention in open literature. A T-3 tapered E-glass/epoxy mono leaf spring, a typical utility vehicle suspension part, is put in a controlled transverse notch crack at mid-span position - the most harmonic displacement zone as determined by finite element harmonic analysis in HyperWorks OptiStruct. The first six natural frequencies of the undamaged and cracked spring are determined by mode analysis, both computationally (with HyperMesh/OptiStruct) and experimentally (with an OROS OR34 FFT analyzer with roving hammer excitation under free-free boundary conditions). To characterise the voltage-dependent vibration suppression response, and SP-5 H lead zirconate titanate (PZT) patch is bonded between node 3 and 4 at the anti-nodal point of maximum amplitude and energized at two different voltage levels 0.62 V and 3.56 V by custom printed circuit board. The basic natural frequency is decreased to 1.27 Hz at 3.56 V, which is a 95% suppression of the main resonance amplitude. XFEM analysis of the stress intensity factor, with AVCS activated, confirms reduction of Mode I crack-driving force by 80% when AVCS is turned on. The results of the study prove the technical feasibility of PZT-based active control, as a structural health maintenance and fatigue-life extension measure of degraded composite suspension components.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61939-z.title: Selective transport of plasma-derived reactive species through the plant aquaporin channels: a molecular dynamics study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61939-z.abstract: The selective permeability of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS), generated by cold atmospheric plasma (CAP), through plant aquaporins was investigated to identify plasma-derived species capable of intracellular delivery. Using atomistic molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling methods, we quantified the free energy profiles of eight RONS (HNO3, HO2, cis-HNO2, trans-HNO2, N2O4, NO, NO2, and O3) across the PIP2;1 aquaporin channel embedded in a lipid bilayer. Permeation was found to be controlled by two complementary features: the free-energy barrier opposing entry at the aromatic/arginine (ar/R) constriction, and the depth of the free-energy minimum within the pore interior. The strongly polar, hydrogen-bonding species HNO3 exhibited the highest entry barrier (≈ 16 kJ·mol− 1) and is thus the least permeable, whereas weakly polar species such as NO crossed the channel with minimal resistance. Notably, several species, most strikingly N2O4, combined facile entry with deep internal minima, indicating that they are readily admitted into the pore but strongly retained within it rather than freely transported. These results show that RONS selectivity in PIP2;1 is governed by molecular size, polarity, and hydrogen-bonding capacity, and provide a mechanistic basis for the rational selection of CAP-generated species in sustainable plasma-based agricultural technologies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69253-4.title: Anti-biofilm and quorum sensing-modulatory effects of quercetin-functionalized Capparis spinosa fruit-derived silver nanoparticles against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69253-4.abstract: Abstract Biofilm formation and quorum sensing (QS) systems are key determinants of pathogenicity and therapeutic resistance in multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa , making these pathways attractive targets for combating chronic biofilm-associated infections. In this study, green-synthesized silver nanoparticles derived from Capparis spinosa fruit extract were functionalized with quercetin (AgNPs@Qu), and their antibiofilm and QS-modulatory activities were evaluated against MDR clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa . Physicochemical characterization by UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, zeta potential analysis, FE-SEM, DLS, and ICP-OES confirmed the successful formation of nanoparticles with a face-centered cubic (fcc) crystalline structure, an average diameter of approximately 30 nm, and a quercetin surface coating. Compared with unfunctionalized AgNPs, AgNPs@Qu exhibited a 4- to 8-fold reduction in minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) against MDR isolates and significantly suppressed bacterial growth. More importantly, AgNPs@Qu displayed potent antibiofilm activity, reducing biofilm biomass by more than 70–85% in hyper-biofilm-forming isolates, a performance comparable to that of ciprofloxacin. Furthermore, AgNPs@Qu exerted a concentration-dependent, biphasic effect on pyocyanin production, characterized by transient stimulation at low sub-inhibitory concentrations and relative inhibition at higher concentrations, reflecting a modulatory action of quercetin on quorum sensing pathways. These findings indicate that the antibiofilm and QS-modulatory properties of the AgNPs@Qu nanocomposite, beyond its bactericidal action, contribute to its enhanced in vitro efficacy compared with unfunctionalized AgNPs against MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, positioning it as a promising candidate for further preclinical investigation as an antivirulence-based strategy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67919-7.title: The impact of patients suicide on the mental health of psychotherapists
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67919-7.abstract: Abstract A great number of psychotherapists and psychiatrists experience at least one patient suicide during their career. This study aims to build upon previous research findings concerning the impact of experienced patient suicide on the mental health of practicing and trainee psychotherapists in a German sample. A central aspect involves examining the temporal development of perceived distress and identifying short- and long-term emotional effects of suicide through a mixed methods approach to derive corresponding implications for postvention. The online survey revealed relatively low levels of symptoms on the administered PTSD scale. Nevertheless, a subset of participants reported clinically significant symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Particularly intense feelings of grief, shock, and horror also play a prominent role. Suicide leads to psychotherapists experiencing fear when assessing suicidal patients. Factors that could influence the extent of the impact of suicide include the patient-therapist relationship, lack of support, perception of suicide as violent, and its unpredictability. These factors continue to require exploration to gain a comprehensive understanding of their effects following patient suicide.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69229-4.title: Nationwide trends in incidence and in-hospital mortality of ARDS in Germany, 2008–2022
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69229-4.abstract: Abstract Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains a major contributor to morbidity and mortality among critically ill patients. Recent events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and demographic changes have likely influenced its epidemiology. This study aimed to investigate nationwide trends in ARDS incidence and in-hospital mortality among adult intensive care patients in Germany over a 15-year period and to describe demographic and clinical differences between survivors and non-survivors. We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using hospital discharge data from the German Federal Statistical Office. All adult patients diagnosed with ARDS (ICD-10 code J80) and treated in intensive care units between 2008 and 2022 were included. Among 87,488 patients, 52.2% died during hospitalization. The incidence increased significantly before the pandemic, peaking at 21.0 per 100,000 inhabitants in 2021. In-hospital mortality declined from 54.2% in 2008 to 50.8% in 2018, followed by an increase up to 53.8% in 2021 and a slight decline thereafter. Non-survivors were older (68 vs 60 yr), had a greater comorbidity burden (Elixhauser index 17 vs 12), and more severe ARDS (54.2% vs 41.1%). Mortality was highest among patients aged 90 to 94 years (82%). COVID-19–related cases had a higher observed in-hospital mortality (53.5% vs 51.8%) and a higher proportion of severe ARDS (77.2% vs 38.6%). ARDS incidence and in-hospital mortality remain high. The low detection of mild to moderate ARDS highlights the need for better diagnostic tools and standardized criteria. Elderly patients are especially vulnerable, underscoring the need for age-specific therapies and improved early detection.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55288-0.title: AI-driven collision risk prediction and debris optimization in low earth orbit
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55288-0.abstract: Debris congestion and collision in low Earth orbit have become a major point of concern due to the rapid expansion of activities in that region. In this work, an AI-driven framework is developed and deployed to predict, analyze, and optimize collision risk across the altitude inclination space. Local debris object population, mass density distribution, and conjunction derived risk are computed. Then, an AI surrogate model, viz., gradient-boosted decision trees, was trained to predict collision conjunction relative probabilities and risk. Thereafter, data analysis and explain ability techniques are utilized to uncover underlying risk drivers and reveal how altitude, inclination, mass loading, and crowding interact across the orbital space. The analyses showed how the AI surrogate model reliably captures underlying nonlinear risk behavior and interactions. More importantly, it suggested that meaningful capacity increases are achievable with only a moderate rise in predicted risk. Finally, the AI surrogate model was employed in a multi-objective evolutionary optimization to quantify the trade off between minimizing collision risk and maximizing usable orbital capacity, revealing a set of optimal, feasible, and well-balanced points of operation in this regime. Ultimately, the proposed pipeline offers a computationally efficient pathway for prediction and interpreting orbital safety, guiding constellation deployment, and supporting sustainable space traffic management strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69007-2.title: Prevalence of comorbidity symptoms of anxiety and depression and importance of influencing factors among adolescents in Shaanxi Province: a large-scale school-based survey
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69007-2.abstract: Comorbidity symptoms of anxiety and depression disorders (CAD) is common among adolescents and threaten the health and safety of adolescents. This study estimated the prevalence of CAD and examined its relative important influencing factors for formulating targeted intervention programs. Data were from the National Student Common Disease and Risk Factors Surveillance program in Shaanxi province, Northwestern China in 2023. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) respectively. An Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithm (XGBoost) model combined with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) was applied to explore the relative predictive contribution of behavioral factors by school grade. A total of 94 472 students were included, in whom 15 113 (16.00%) had CAD, and the prevalence of CAD in senior high school students (22.08%) was higher than junior high students (12.01%). There was a gender specific difference in the prevalence of CAD, the proportion of CAD in boys was lower than in girl in junior high school (10.22% vs. 13.87%) and senior high school (20.45% vs. 23.64%). The all health-risk behaviors included in this study can influence the CAD among students, but there importance varied with gender and academic stage. The top three contributing factors were unhealthy diet, internet addiction and bully in junior high school boys. The top three contributing factors were unhealthy diet, internet addiction and sleep deprivation in junior high school girls. The top three contributing factors were sleep deprivation, internet addiction and unhealthy diet in both senior high school boys and girls. CAD is common among adolescents in Shaanxi Province, the prevalence of CAD increased with academic stage, while the junior high school students also screen-positive for CAD risk. The prevalence of CAD both in junior high school and senior high school students was mainly related to unhealthy life behaviors, such as unhealthy diet, internet addiction and sleep deprivation, and bully. Integrating behavioral risk surveillance with adolescent mental health services may help improve early identification and targeted intervention.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69077-2.title: Genomic and epidemiological comparative analysis of clinical Campylobacter isolates from public and private healthcare centers in Santiago, Chile
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69077-2.abstract: Abstract Campylobacteriosis remains underestimated in Latin America due to limited surveillance and diagnostic capacity. In this context, a comparison was made of clinical Campylobacter strains from two distinct healthcare settings in Santiago, Chile: a public pediatric hospital and a private tertiary clinic. Through genomic analysis, host-source attribution was observed to vary across socioeconomic profiles: poultry-associated lineages (such as ST-353 and ST-443 complexes) were, as expected, frequently identified across all analyzed populations, although comparatively more frequent in the public health settings; in contrast, cattle-associated strains (ST-22 complex) were primarily isolated from patients of higher incomes. These findings provide the first evidence of Campylobacter infection frequency in a lower-income pediatric population in Chile, highlighting this pathogen as an important cause of gastroenteritis across socioeconomic groups in this setting. Furthermore, a link was identified between the Type 6 Secretion System (T6SS) and clinical severity, corresponding to a subgroup of effectors (CJ488_00960c and CJ488_00961) significantly associated with dehydration. High percentages of resistance determinants to tetracycline (tetO) and fluoroquinolones (gyrA T86I ) are also reported. These data provide information on the main transmission path for distinct socioeconomic groups within the same city, providing valuable data that could help authorities to take informed decisions in case of potential outbreaks and highlighting the urgent need for integrated genomic surveillance in Chile.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64790-4.title: Phosphate removal by spent low temperature shift catalyst through process optimization and mechanistic study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64790-4.abstract: Abstract Natural water bodies become eutrophic due to phosphate pollution from industrial and agricultural sectors. This research addresses waste disposal and water pollution at the same time by recycling spent low-temperature shift catalyst (LTSSC) from the fertilizer industry as a sustainable phosphate adsorbent. High surface area (247 ± 5 m 2 /g), mesoporous structure, and many metal oxide sites (CuO 49%, ZnO 32.2%, and Al 2 O₃ 13.9%) were shown by characterization using XRF, XRD, BET, SEM–EDX, FTIR, particle size analysis, and zeta potential. Under optimum conditions (contact time 1.64 h, dose 5 g/L, initial concentration 9.58 mg/L, stirring 278 rpm), Response Surface Methodology optimization achieved 92.95 ± 2.8% phosphate removal. Chemisorption via inner-sphere complexation is established by endothermic spontaneous thermodynamics (ΔH° = 18.42 ± 1.3 kJ/mol, ΔG° = − 7.56 ± 0.6 kJ/mol, ΔS° = 36.6 ± 2.5 J/mol·K), FTIR-detected M–O-P bonds, XRD-confirmed crystalline AlPO₄ formation, and Langmuir isotherm (qmax = 0.174 ± 0.005 mg/g). Over 15 cycles, regeneration using 0.1 M NaOH demonstrated > 75% capacity retention. Heavy metal leaching tests showed concentrations below WHO/USEPA limits. The treatment cost, according to techno-economic study, is $0.52/m 3 , which is less than that of commercial adsorbents. This study shows how to use a circular economy method to address two environmental concerns by turning hazardous industrial waste into usable phosphate adsorbent.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67585-9.title: Nicotiana glauca leaf extract exhibits synergistic antioxidant and anticancer activities revealed by phytochemical profiling and molecular docking
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67585-9.abstract: Abstract This study aimed to characterize the phytochemical composition and antioxidant, cytotoxic and molecular docking profile of Nicotiana glauca Graham (Solanaceae), a wild plant species naturalized along the Wadi El Natrun–North Coast Road, Egypt. N. glauca was selected from a preliminary screening of ten co-occurring wild plant species collected during the summer of 2022 on the basis of its highest extraction yield (2.20%), the richest qualitative phytochemical profile among the ten species, and its strong antioxidant activity. The aqueous ethanolic leaf extract of N. glauca and its sixteen column fractions were subsequently evaluated using four chemical antioxidant assays: 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS), potassium permanganate (KMnO₄), and dichlorophenolindophenol (DCPIP). Comprehensive phytochemical characterization was performed using thin-layer chromatography (TLC), TLC-bioautography, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), mass spectrometry, 1 H and 13 C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and GC/MS/MS analyses. Total phenolic, flavonoid and alkaloid contents ranged from 0.3–8.4 g GAE/100 g DW, 0.1–2.14 g/100 g DW, and 0.31–7.01 g/100 g DW, respectively, across the extracts; a Pearson correlation analysis between these compound classes and antioxidant activity across the ten species did not reach statistical significance (p > 0.05), consistent with a ceiling effect at the tested concentration and supporting a combined rather than single-compound-class contribution to activity. GC/MS/MS analysis of fraction 11 revealed anabasine as the predominant alkaloid (39.26%), followed by nornicotine (36.50%). Two pure compounds were isolated and identified as N,N-methylenebis(14-docosene) (Compound A) and 14-methylhexadecanoic acid (Compound B). A synergistic interaction was observed between the crude extract and Compound A for both antioxidant (combination index, CI = 0.53) and anticancer activity (CI = 0.139–0.158), whereas an antagonistic effect was observed with Compound B (CI = 2.2–28.8). Both the crude extract and isolated compounds exhibited concentration-dependent cytotoxic activity against HeLa (IC₅₀ = 146.04 µg/mL) and HepG2 (IC₅₀ = 169.38 µg/mL) cancer cell lines. Treatment of HeLa cells with Compound A was associated with upregulation of the pro-apoptotic Bax gene, downregulation of the anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 gene, an increased Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, and elevated malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, findings consistent with, though not direct proof of, apoptosis induction and oxidative stress. Molecular docking analysis indicated that anabasine binds with favorable predicted affinity to the HPV16 E2 (PDB: 2Q79) and E6 (PDB: 7UAJ) oncoproteins; these computational results provide hypothesis-generating support for further exploration of anabasine against HPV-associated oncoproteins and require experimental validation. Overall, these findings characterize N. glauca as a promising wild source of antioxidant and cytotoxic bioactive metabolites and support further mechanistic and translational investigation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68265-4.title: Clinical and molecular correlates of metronidazole resistance in Trichomonas vaginalis: a cross-sectional study from a tertiary-care centre in western India
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68265-4.abstract: Trichomoniasis, caused by the flagellated protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis, is the most prevalent non-viral sexually transmitted infection worldwide. Treatment relies mainly on metronidazole, although resistance increasingly contributes to treatment failure. The nitroreductase genes ntr4 and ntr6 have been implicated in metronidazole resistance, but data from Indian clinical settings remain limited. This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at AIIMS Rajkot between March 2024 and February 2026 among symptomatic women aged 18–55 years. Vaginal aspirates were processed by wet-mount microscopy and cultured in modified cysteine–peptone–liver–maltose medium under microaerophilic conditions. All culture-confirmed isolates underwent broth microdilution minimum inhibitory concentration testing for metronidazole and PCR screening for ntr4 and ntr6 genes. Of 210 women enrolled, Trichomonas vaginalis was isolated from 28 (13.3%; 95% CI 9.1–18.6%). Four isolates (14.3%; 95% CI 4.0–32.7%) demonstrated phenotypic metronidazole resistance (MIC ≥ 8 µg/mL), while 24 were susceptible (MIC ≤ 1 µg/mL). All four resistant isolates were recovered from women with documented metronidazole exposure within the preceding six months, compared with 8 of 24 (33.3%) women whose isolates were susceptible (Fisher’s exact test, P = 0.024). Conventional PCR yielded a discrete ntr4 amplicon (549 bp) in all four resistant isolates and in none of the 24 susceptible isolates or negative control; ntr6 amplification was not detected in any isolate. The significant association between phenotypic resistance and ntr4 detection supports a nitroreductase-mediated resistance mechanism in recurrent or treatment-refractory trichomoniasis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68801-2.title: Exclusive breastfeeding practices and influencing factors among mothers of six-month-old infants in Chongqing China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68801-2.abstract: According to the “Report on the Nutritional Status and Chronic Diseases of the Chinese Population (2020)”, the exclusive breastfeeding rate among infants under six months of age in China stands at 34.1%. As a major city in south-western China, Chongqing lacks city-wide data on exclusive breastfeeding rates. A mixed study of interpretation sequences was performed. In the quantitative research section, the researchers conducted a questionnaire survey of 510 women who gave birth at a Grade A, Level 3 hospital in Chongqing. All 510 women had voluntarily joined the research WeChat group before giving birth, and the questionnaires were distributed and completed via the WeChat mini-program “Wenjuanxing”; a total of 501 questionnaires were returned. The primary outcome measure was exclusive breastfeeding at six months postpartum (defined as feeding only breast milk, with no other liquids or solid foods added, except for vitamins, minerals, or medication). Logistic regression was used to calculate adjusted odds ratios (OR). For the qualitative study, a phenomenological approach was adopted, involving semi-structured interviews with 14 mothers, with themes extracted using Colaizzi’s seven-step analysis method. The rate of exclusive breastfeeding at six months was 38.92%. Multivariate analysis revealed that monthly household income per capita (P = 0.048, OR = 0.354, 95%CI: 0.127–0.989), postpartum breast condition (P = 0.006, OR = 4.152, 95%CI: 1.498–11.510), newborn weight (P = 0.041, OR = 0.509, 95%CI: 0.266–0.972) are important factors influencing exclusive breastfeeding, exclusive breastfeeding for the preceding 24 h (P<0.001, OR = 12.796, 95%CI: 6.667–24.560) was significantly positively correlated with exclusive breastfeeding at 6 months; given the temporal overlap between this variable and the outcome measure, it was considered a concurrent behavioral indicator rather than a causal predictor. Qualitative analysis identified four themes: the multifaceted drivers of feeding decisions; the practical challenges of feeding implementation; the imbalance between supply and demand in support systems; and the dual influence of societal attitudes and the environment. A mixed-methods analysis indicates that “exclusive breastfeeding in the past 24 hours” exhibits both consistency and an expansive relationship in both qualitative and quantitative data; “monthly per capita household income” and “newborn birth weight” exhibit both consistency and a complementary relationship in both qualitative and quantitative data; whilst “postnatal breast condition”, although seemingly contradictory on the surface, is in essence complementary. Future efforts should focus on addressing mothers’ dual physiological and psychological needs, moving away from the “widow-style parenting” approach and strengthening family care support; establishing a social breastfeeding support network to resolve the breastfeeding challenges faced by working mothers; upholding scientific feeding principles, respecting mothers’ feeding choices and fundamental human rights; and, through collaborative efforts among medical, family and community sectors, increasing the rate of exclusive breastfeeding to promote the healthy development of both mothers and infants.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66632-9.title: Computational identification of multi-targeted bioactive phytocompounds as candidate drug molecules against Nipah virus infection
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66632-9.abstract: Nipah Virus (NiV) is a highly virulent zoonotic virus that leads to severe encephalitis and respiratory diseases with mortality rates estimated at 40–75%, sometimes up to 100% in specific outbreaks. NiV has outbreaks in South and Southeast Asia, particularly in Bangladesh, India, Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, and so on. The WHO classifies NiV as a priority pathogen due to its high fatality rate, lack of approved antiviral drugs or vaccines, and pandemic potential spread by human-to-human transmission. Therefore, identifying novel therapeutic agents against NiV remains a critical global health priority now. Natural phytochemicals have gained increasing attention due to their diverse biological activities and, favorable safety profiles. In this study, we investigated 2271 unique phytocompounds as drug candidates induced from 261 medicinal plants having high antiviral activities through molecular docking interaction with the NiV G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and L protein. Phytocompounds with significant binding affinity (< − 7.0 kcal/mol) were further assessed by, drug-likeness screening, ADME/T Profiling, network pharmacology, protein–ligand interaction analysis, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and 100 ns MD simulation to investigate structural stability and interaction behavior. Docking results revealed strong binding affinity of several phytochemicals toward NiV proteins. Among which Absinthin, Cycloepiatalantin, and Diosgenin showed the most favorable interactions results. ADME/T analysis suggested high absorption, low predicted toxicity, and effective blood–brain barrier penetration. DFT analysis indicated a favorable electronic interaction potential of the phytochemicals. MD simulations suggested stable protein–ligand complexes supported by the following analysis, RMSD, RMSF, SASA, RoG, MM-PBSA, DCCM, and PCA. Overall, these findings suggest that these Phytocompounds may serve as potential candidates for further experimental validation as antiviral agents against NiV. Using large-scale Phytocompounds screening, this study identified candidate compounds with predicted bioactivity capable of interacting with NiV proteins, while helping to reduce the cost, time, and labor associated with conventional wet-laboratory experiments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67272-9.title: A unified benchmark of supervised and retrieval-based methods for viral genomic sequence classification
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67272-9.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of genomic sequencing demands fast, accurate, and scalable analysis methods. In viral genomic classification, expanding labeled reference collections can make supervised models costly to update and dependent on fixed label sets, motivating retrieval-based genomic classification as a simpler, more flexible alternative. We present a unified benchmark of supervised and retrieval-based methods for viral genomic sequence classification across three viral classification tasks: hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotyping, COVID-19 discrimination, and human papillomavirus (HPV) genotyping. We compare standard sequence encodings (one-hot, k -mers, FCGR) with dense embeddings (dna2vec, DNABERT). For each representation, we evaluate supervised classifiers (Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost) and retrieval-based classification, where sequence vectors are indexed with FAISS and labels are assigned via similarity-weighted k-NN. Furthermore, we benchmark multiple FAISS index types (Flat, IVF, HNSW, IVFPQ, OPQ) to characterize accuracy-speed–memory trade-offs at scale. The results show that XGBoost and retrieval using Flat or IVF indexes achieve strong classification performance under different computational profiles. Compressed indexes such as IVFPQ and OPQ substantially reduce memory usage, although their accuracy loss depends on the dataset and representation. Overall, supervised XGBoost provides a favorable accuracy–size trade-off, while retrieval-based classification remains competitive and allows labeled reference sequences to be incorporated without retraining a global classifier. This benchmark provides practical guidance for selecting sequence representations, classifiers, and vector-search indexes under different accuracy, memory, and update requirements.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67916-w.title: Antitumor, antioxidant, and antibiofilm activities of chitooligosaccharides by chitosanase from Bacillus cereus
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67916-w.abstract: Abstract Chitooligosaccharides (COSs) are hydrophilic short oligomers produced by the action of microbial chitosanases on chitosan. The aim of this study is to assess the antitumor, antioxidant, and antibiofilm activities of bio-produced COSs from B. cereus strain isolated from Egyptian soil. To evaluate the cytotoxicity of COSs, an MTT assay was performed. To find that COSs exhibit antitumor activity against MCF-7, HepG-2, A549, and CACO-2 cell lines with mean IC 50 of 818.8 µg/mL, 1845.9 µg/mL, 1293.9 µg/mL, and 1432.9 µg/mL, respectively. In addition, the antioxidant activity of COSs was measured by assessing their 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical-scavenging activity relative to ascorbic acid. The tested COSs showed strong DPPH radical-scavenging activity at high concentration (98.6 ± 0.10%). Assessing the antioxidant activity of COSs was also carried out using the HFD-mice model by measuring catalase and other enzyme levels in blood, stomach, and liver samples. The 0.5% COS dose increased catalase, GSH, and GPx levels in liver, stomach, and serum specimens ( P < 0.05). The antibiofilm activity of the tested COSs was assayed using a microtiter plate assay against P. aeruginosa and S. aureus biofilm-forming microorganisms. The tested COS at 125 µg/mL showed promising activity against biofilm formation by S. aureus and P. aeruginosa , with 51.7 ± 4.2 and 43 ± 2.1, respectively. In conclusion, COSs showed promising antitumor, antibiofilm, and antioxidant activities.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69907-3.title: Mechanical and microstructural behavior of earthen materials treated with ceramic waste powder and volcanic ash-based geopolymer binders for compressed brick production
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69907-3.abstract: This study proposes an environmentally sustainable approach for stabilizing high-plasticity clay through a hybrid geopolymer binder produced from ceramic waste powder (CWP) and volcanic ash (VA), using an alkaline activator composed of sodium hydroxide and sodium silicate at a NaOH/Na₂SiO₃ ratio of 2.0. The main innovation of this study is the systematic comparison of single-precursor and hybrid CWP–VA binders at identical overall additive contents of 4%, 8%, and 12%, enabling the individual and synergistic contributions of the two precursors to be clearly distinguished. This approach provides a direct assessment of whether precursor hybridization can deliver greater stabilization efficiency than the use of individual materials. A multi-scale testing program was employed to establish relationships between mechanical performance, bearing capacity, durability, and internal structural quality using unconfined compressive strength (UCS), California Bearing Ratio (CBR), water absorption, and ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV), complemented by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses. The results demonstrate that combining CWP and VA provides substantially greater stabilization efficiency than using either precursor independently at the same total dosage. The optimum mixture, containing 6% CWP and 6% VA, achieved a 28-day UCS of 5.26 MPa, corresponding to an 1182% improvement relative to untreated soil. The mixture also exhibited unsoaked and soaked CBR values of 41.11% and 27.96%, respectively, while maintaining a water absorption of only 6.8%. The measured UPV of 2130 m/s further indicated improved internal densification and structural continuity. SEM analysis revealed that stabilization transformed the initially loose and porous clay structure into a denser matrix characterized by interconnected geopolymer gel bridges. EDS analysis further confirmed the development of a Ca-, Si-, and Al-rich reaction matrix, supporting the formation of aluminosilicate-based geopolymer products. Consistent with these microstructural observations, XRD analysis indicated the development of predominantly amorphous sodium aluminosilicate hydrate (N-A-S-H) and calcium aluminosilicate hydrate (C-A-S-H) gel phases within the broad 20°–40° 2θ region, accompanied by partial dissolution of the original crystalline minerals. Overall, the findings demonstrate the synergistic effectiveness of the cement-free CWP–VA hybrid geopolymer and highlight its potential as a high-performance, waste-derived alternative for sustainable clay stabilization and compressed earth brick applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69877-6.title: Metabolic-microbial crosstalk drives inflammasome activation: fasn and palmitoylation mediate palmitate-Porphyromonas gingivalis synergy in macrophage-like cells
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69877-6.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that is exacerbated by metabolic disorders such as obesity, which is associated with elevated circulating saturated fatty acids and lipotoxic stress. Palmitate, a prominent saturated fatty acid, modulates innate immune responses, while Porphyromonas gingivalis, a key periodontal pathogen, is a potent trigger of inflammation. The NLRP3 inflammasome integrates metabolic and microbial danger signals to promote caspase‑1 activation and the maturation of IL‑1β and IL‑18, yet the interaction between metabolic stress and microbial stimulation remains poorly defined. Using U937 macrophage‑like cells, we investigated how palmitate modulates inflammasome activation and cytokine secretion in response to P. gingivalis and related TLR stimuli. Palmitate alone had limited effects on IL-1β and IL-18 secretion but acted as an enhancer of cytokine release when combined with microbial or TLR stimulation. Inhibition of NLRP3 reduced cytokine secretion but did not prevent palmitate‑induced cytotoxicity, indicating partial inflammasome dependence. Blocking protein palmitoylation partially attenuated IL‑1β potentiation, while inhibition of fatty acid synthase strongly suppressed IL‑1β secretion induced by combined palmitate and P. gingivalis exposure. These findings identify a metabolic-microbial axis that enhances inflammasome‑dependent inflammation and may contribute to heightened periodontal disease severity in individuals with metabolic dysfunction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69329-1.title: Green chemistry oriented synthesis of p-anisic acid and comparative toxicity versus synthetic product in zebrafish embryos and keratinocytes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69329-1.abstract: Abstract p -Anisic acid is an aromatic carboxylic acid used in cosmetic preservation systems. In this study, a trans-anethole-rich essential oil obtained from Pimpinella anisum seeds was converted to p -anisic acid by aqueous potassium permanganate oxidation with acetone as a co-solvent and hydrochloric acid precipitation. Because the route uses a renewable plant-derived feedstock, water as the principal reaction medium, moderate heating, and acetone recovery, it is described as green chemistry-oriented rather than as an intrinsically green process; no comparative life-cycle assessment, process mass intensity, or E-factor calculation was performed. The isolated product was characterized by ¹H and ¹³C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and profiled by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) against analytical standards. The effects of plant-derived p -anisic acid (NAA) and commercial synthetic p -anisic acid (SAA) on the viability of the HaCaT cells (24 h exposure) and on developmental toxicity in zebrafish embryos (up to 72 hpf) were investigated. In HaCaT cells, NAA caused a smaller concentration-dependent reduction in viability than SAA over 0.0125-0.05% (w/v). NAA preserved igf2 , fabp , vtg , and cyp1a expressions as biomarkers of embryonic development, hepatocellular stress, estrogenic activity, and xenobiotic response, while showing no significant elevation in LPO, NO levels, or GST activity. SAA disrupted oxidant-antioxidant status and the expression of developmental genes. Because both materials contain the same target molecule, the observed differences should be interpreted as batch-specific and potentially related to impurity profiles or other physicochemical attributes rather than as a source-dependent change in the intrinsic properties of p -anisic acid.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68787-x.title: Comparative evaluation of hybrid control strategies for fault ride-through enhancement in type-5 wind turbines: MPC-SMC, RL-MPC, and fractional-order SMC-MPC
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68787-x.abstract: This study presents a comparative evaluation of three hybrid control strategies for Fault Ride-Through (FRT) enhancement in Type-5 wind turbines: Model Predictive Control with Sliding Mode Control (MPC-SMC), Reinforcement Learning-enhanced MPC (RL-MPC), and the proposed Fractional-Order SMC-MPC (FOSMC-MPC). While MPC, SMC, fractional calculus, and RL are individually established, the incremental contributions of this work are threefold: (i) a systematic integration of fractional-order sliding dynamics within the MPC prediction horizon rather than as a cascaded add-on; (ii) the first quantitative three-way comparison under identical 70% voltage dip scenarios with standardized metrics; and (iii) implementation-oriented analysis including DSP-based computational benchmarks. In the simulations, FOSMC-MPC achieves a voltage-recovery time of 0.20 s (0.58 s for RL-MPC), a peak-to-peak torque-ripple metric of 3.2 kNm (12.4 kNm for MPC-SMC), and a rotor-speed deviation of ± 5% (± 12% for RL-MPC). These results are interpreted as comparative simulation evidence; hardware-in-the-loop validation, plant-parameter uncertainty sweeps, and a fully documented matched-input test campaign remain outside the present dataset.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68457-y.title: Indoxyl sulfate–associated vascular calcification is linked to mTORC1 and ER stress–integrated stress response signaling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68457-y.abstract: Medial vascular calcification is a major cardiovascular complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), with the uremic toxin indoxyl sulfate (IS) implicated in its pathogenesis. However, the molecular mechanisms by which IS promotes vascular calcification remain incompletely understood. In human aortic smooth muscle cells (hASMCs), IS induced oxidative stress and stimulated the MEK–ERK1/2 and PI3K–AKT signaling pathways, leading to mTORC1 activation. This led to impaired autophagy, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and activation of the integrated stress response (ISR). Collectively, these alterations drove osteochondrogenic transdifferentiation, cellular senescence, and calcium deposition in hASMCs, processes that were further exacerbated by elevated phosphate. Pharmacological intervention with nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) or tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA) attenuated ER stress–ISR signaling and suppressed osteogenic and senescence-associated markers under IS and phosphate conditions. Collectively, these findings identify mTORC1-ER stress–ISR signaling as a central mechanism linking IS to vascular calcification and highlight this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for CKD-associated vascular disease.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65838-1.title: Hybrid encoder-decoder to preserve long-range context in brain tumor segmentation with EfficientNetB7 and a convolutional vision transformer mechanism
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65838-1.abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain tumors in MRI is critically important for clinical diagnosis, particularly challenging for Low-Grade Gliomas (LGGs) in FLAIR sequences where precise delineation directly impacts treatment planning and patient monitoring. Conventional U-Net architectures face limitations in this domain, exhibiting structural degradation from repetitive down-sampling and inefficient feature propagation between encoder and decoder components. Furthermore, most existing approaches rely on manual hyperparameter optimization, which is both computationally intensive and prone to suboptimal convergence. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel hybrid encoder-decoder framework that integrates an EfficientNetB7 backbone with a single-stage Convolutional Vision Transformer (CvT) and a TransUNet style decoder, systematically optimized through Bayesian hyperparameter tuning. The architecture leverages EfficientNetB7 for multi-scale feature extraction while the CvT module implements convolutional token embedding and multi-head self-attention to model long-range dependencies without patch-based transformations, maintaining structural coherence for optimized feature fusion. The decoding pathway employs bilinear upsampling enhanced with residual convolutional blocks for precise boundary refinement. Extensive evaluation on the Kaggle Low-Grade Glioma (LGG) and Brain Tumor Segmentation datasets demonstrates superior performance, achieving Dice coefficients of 0.9290 and 0.9262 respectively. These results confirm that our architecture effectively preserves fine structural details while capturing global context, yielding robust and accurate tumor segmentation, demonstrating strong potential for future integration into clinical decision support systems, pending prospective clinical validation. The integration of Bayesian optimization further ensures reproducible and optimal model configuration, enhancing the framework’s reliability for medical imaging applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69708-8.title: Thermoresponsive mineral grout for autonomous oxygen isolation in underground coal pillars
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69708-8.abstract: A thermo-responsive mineral-based grout composite (GC) was developed for rapid sealing of fracture networks in underground coal pillars, aiming to eliminate oxygen ingress and prevent spontaneous combustion in goaf areas. Coal spontaneous combustion triggered by air leakage poses severe threats to mine safety. Traditional sealants such as rapid-hardening calcium sulfoaluminate (CSA)-sodium silicate systems and polyurethane materials suffer from thermal-runaway risks, poor fire resistance, and complex parameter control requirements. The GC slurry is composed of Mg(OH)2, Al(OH)3, ultra-fine cement and NIPAM-grafted bentonite. It maintains 200 mm flowability at 20 °C for deep penetration, yet triggers abrupt thickening within 3 min when ≥ 40 °C is encountered, forming a dense oxygen barrier. Adiabatic calorimetry revealed a maximum temperature rise of only 18.4 °C (ΔTmax = 18.4 °C, tmax = 7.8 h), 13% and 52% of those measured for polyurethane and cement–sodium-silicate systems, respectively, thereby minimising the thermal-runaway risk during bulk injection. Laboratory micro-CT confirmed 85% reduction in connected porosity (> 50 μm) and crack-free coal–grout interfaces. Field trials in the 102 auxiliary transport roadway (No. 3 coal seam, Hongqinghe Mine, Inner Mongolia, China) reduced O2 concentration from 9 to 17% to 1–5% and decreased CO to 0 ppm within 30 d under mining-induced dynamic loading. The 28-d compressive strength reached 30.1 MPa (w/c = 0.7) while zero bleeding or shrinkage cracks were observed. Raw-material cost analysis shows GC (USD 185 t− 1) achieves 35% lower life-cycle cost than polyurethane over a 5-year horizon. With ΔTmax well below the 60 °C thermal-safety limit adopted in Chinese coal-mine grouting practice (AQ/T 1089–2020, a standard issued for polymeric materials and used here as a conservative benchmark) and goaf O2 maintained below the 7% critical oxygen concentration specified in GB 51,078 − 2015, GC offers a low-exotherm, fire-resistant and environmentally benign alternative to organic sealants for coal-mine fire prevention.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69025-0.title: Relation-aware multimodal knowledge graph learning for drug–drug interaction prediction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69025-0.abstract: Drug–drug interactions (DDIs) can alter therapeutic efficacy and lead to adverse events, making accurate DDI prediction important for drug safety assessment. Existing computational methods often rely on limited drug features or do not sufficiently capture heterogeneous biomedical relations surrounding drugs. We present RA-DDI, a relation-aware knowledge graph framework for DDI prediction. RA-DDI constructs a drug-centered knowledge graph (KG) from DrugBank and initializes drug representations by integrating molecular structures, textual descriptions, and graph-derived relational features. These multimodal representations are then refined through relation-aware graph learning to capture multi-hop dependencies among drugs and related biomedical entities. A prediction module combines the learned drug embeddings with pairwise interaction features to classify DDI types. We evaluated RA-DDI on three public benchmark datasets, DrugBank, DDInter, and PDD-Graph. The proposed framework achieved competitive performance and showed consistent improvements over representative baselines on several key classification and ranking metrics. These findings demonstrate that combining multimodal drug representation learning with relation-aware knowledge graph modeling is effective for DDI prediction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69686-x.title: Assessment of the Japanese national examination for pharmacists using locally fine tuned large language models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69686-x.abstract: Locally deployable large language models (LLMs) offer advantages in data security and customization, making them particularly useful in domains that handle sensitive information. Although commercial cloud-based LLMs have shown strong performance on the Japanese National Examination for Pharmacists (JNEP), the effectiveness of locally deployable, open-weight models for such knowledge-based tasks has not been fully explored. Evaluating these models is important in contexts where data privacy and controlled model deployment are required. In this study, four locally deployable LLMs were evaluated: phi-4, DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen (DSR1-Qwen32B), and two Japanese fine-tuned variants (CA-DSR1-32B and CA-DSR1-14B) based on DSR1-Qwen. Accuracies on the 165 text-based questions from the 109th JNEP ranged from 55.2% to 76.4%. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) improved the accuracy of phi-4 from 60.6% to 66.1%, suggesting that task-specific adaptation enhances performance. Although improvements varied across domains, the results indicate that fine-tuning can improve performance on examination-style questions requiring pharmaceutical knowledge. These results provide preliminary evidence that locally deployable LLMs, as well as resource-efficient adaptation techniques including LoRA, can be applied to structured, knowledge-based assessments such as the JNEP. Further evaluation across broader tasks is required, but locally deployable LLMs may offer a promising approach for knowledge-intensive tasks in pharmacy and related healthcare domains.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65191-3.title: Mycorrhizal inoculation enhances productivity, mineral nutrition, pomology, and bioactive compounds of sweet cherry under field conditions on calcareous soils
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65191-3.abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are increasingly recognized as a sustainable biological approach to improve nutrient acquisition and fruit quality in horticultural crops. Their role is particularly important under calcareous soil conditions where nutrient availability is restricted, thereby reducing reliance on intensive chemical fertilization. This study evaluated the effects of AMF inoculation on root colonization, yield, mineral composition, pomological traits, and fruit biochemical composition of two sweet cherry cultivars (‘0900 Ziraat’ and ‘Sweetheart’) under field conditions. Mycorrhizal inoculation significantly increased root colonization compared to non-inoculated trees (from 54.35% to 95.05%). Fruit mineral concentrations increased under AMF treatment, particularly nitrogen (+ 26.9%), phosphorus (+ 18.9%), potassium (+ 19.1%), calcium (+ 26.1%), and magnesium (+ 12.1%). Main pomological (fruit weight, fruit width, fruit length) and biochemical characteristics (soluble solid content, titratable acidity, and pH) were not significantly affected, whereas functional bioactive compounds were markedly enhanced, including total phenolics (+ 13.9%), total anthocyanins (+ 10.8%), vitamin C (+ 18.1%), and antioxidant activity (+ 15.8%). Principal component analysis separated inoculated and non-inoculated treatments. It also showed that arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi inoculation was associated with higher yield, mineral accumulation, and bioactive compound levels. Obtained results demonstrate how AMF inoculation increases yield without altering pomological traits while simultaneously promoting biochemical enrichment, thereby enhancing the nutraceutical quality of sweet cherry under calcareous soil conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69399-1.title: Genomic diversity reveals breeding pools in Brazilian tetraploid potato germplasm
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69399-1.abstract: Abstract Potato germplasm developed under tropical conditions may contain diversity for breeding, but the Brazilian materials remain poorly characterized. We evaluated 449 tetraploid potato clones, most from Brazilian breeding programs, with 12,595 SNPs. Dosage-aware analyses and STRUCTURE supported four breeding-related clusters. Genetic differentiation between Brazilian and foreign populations was low (Φ ST = 0.04), indicating extensive use of external germplasm in Brazilian breeding. In contrast, differentiation among the genetic clusters was moderate (Φ ST = 0.22), suggesting preferable restricted parental use in their pipelines. Heterozygosity and inbreeding estimates depended strongly on genotype encoding. Tajima’s D was positive (4.46), and suggested selection favoring increased heterozygosity. Three genome scans identified 92 shared candidate outlier SNPs within broad LD-based windows. The functional annotations generated hypotheses related to stress responses for further studies to be functionally validated. The results provide insights at a panel-level baseline for germplasm management and candidate prioritization in Brazilian potato breeding.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68538-y.title: Characteristics and flow measurement of gas-liquid two-phase counter-current flow in vertical annulus
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68538-y.abstract: Gas–liquid two-phase flow measurement in vertical annular pipes remains a challenge in petroleum engineering and related fields, due to the complex flow regimes and asymmetric cross-sectional geometry. In this study, a non-invasive soft-sensing method based on multi-scale differential pressure signals and machine learning is developed for flow rate prediction in vertical annular (inner/outer diameters 75/125 mm) counter-current gas–liquid two-phase flow. Experiments were conducted over a gas superficial velocity range of 0.06–2.91 m/s, a liquid superficial velocity range of 0.02–0.24 m/s, and five eccentricity levels (0–1.0). Differential pressure signals were simultaneously acquired at two spatial scales: a short-span (50 mm, approximately 1 D) and a long-span (1000 mm, approximately 20 D). A total of 53 features were extracted from the time domain, frequency domain (power spectral density), and time-frequency domain (discrete wavelet transform). Three predictive models – Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) – were constructed and hyperparameter-optimized via grid search. Results show that the XGBoost model exhibits the best generalization performance, achieving mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 6.04% for gas superficial velocity and 27.17% for liquid superficial velocity. SHAP-based feature importance analysis indicates that the long-span (1000 mm) differential pressure features play a dominant role in flow rate prediction. Low-frequency energy and the signal mean are crucial for liquid velocity prediction, while high-frequency detail energy governs gas velocity prediction. Although the short-span (50 mm) features rank lower in global importance, they provide critical non-linear corrections under extreme conditions such as high gas velocity. The eccentricity feature (ecce) exhibits a data-driven nonlinear tendency: once the eccentricity exceeds 0.5, the SHAP values for both phases shift markedly negative. This trend is qualitatively consistent with the understanding that wall friction in the narrow gap increases under highly eccentric annular geometries. This study demonstrates that multi-scale differential pressure sensing combined with interpretable machine learning offers a feasible pathway for flow rate measurement in complex wellbore annuli without relying on specific flow regimes (e.g., Taylor bubble flow).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68716-y.title: CLAUNet-LFB0-CBAM a deep learning framework for explainable liver fibrosis stage classification from ultrasound images
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68716-y.abstract: Abstract Automated liver fibrosis staging through ultrasound images is still difficult owing to low contrast, speckle artifacts, and minor differences between successive stages. We propose a hybrid deep learning architecture named CLAUNet-LFB0-CBAM for multi-class liver fibrosis classification from ultrasound images. The method uses a preprocessing pipeline step followed by an augmented EfficientNet-B0 network with CBAM. Moreover, to deal with class imbalance issue, the method employs weighted cross-entropy loss and weighted random sampling, combined with augmentation techniques. The proposed network is compared with baseline architectures like VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, and EfficientNet-B0 within identical experimental conditions. Experimental results show that the proposed method provides superior results in terms of 99.05% accuracy, 0.980 F1-score, and 0.9987 AUC, surpassing all evaluated baseline architectures under identical experimental conditions. Importantly, the performance improvement is achieved mainly in intermediate liver fibrosis stages which are crucial for clinical evaluation. Grad-CAM analysis supports that the network learns the appropriate features from anatomical liver regions. Moreover, the network achieves lightweight implementation with only around 4.8 million parameters.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-57340-5.title: Sex-specific physical activity thresholds influencing muscle function in older adults with XX genotype of ACTN3 R577X
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-57340-5.abstract: Physical activity is widely recommended to maintain muscle health in older adults, yet its effects may vary depending on genetic background. The ACTN3 R577X polymorphism leads to α-actinin-3 deficiency in XX homozygotes and may influence skeletal muscle performance. We examined the association between physical activity and muscle mass and function in 682 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 65 years who participated in annual health examinations between 2021 and 2024. Skeletal muscle mass index was assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, while grip strength, gait speed, and five-time chair stand performance were evaluated according to Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. Physical activity was quantified using metabolic equivalents derived from the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. No significant association was observed between ACTN3 R577X genotype and sarcopenia components. However, in women with ACTN3 XX, physical activity exceeding 441 MET-min/week was significantly associated with poorer chair stand performance (β: 4.19, 95% CI: 0.98 ~ 7.40), revealing a U-shaped relationship between physical activity and physical performance. Sex-specific physical activity thresholds may exist in older adults with the ACTN3 XX genotype, with physical activity above 441 MET-min/week being associated with poorer muscle function in women. This specific MET value is an exploratory finding, requiring more external validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69549-5.title: A rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on vibration sensor signals using adaptive VMD and correlation kurtosis feature enhancement
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69549-5.abstract: Abstract In response to the serious noise interference in the fault signals obtained by the vibration sensors and the difficulty in effectively extracting the fault characteristics, a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on adaptive modal decomposition and correlation kurtosis feature enhancement is proposed. This method is based on the time-domain variation model of the vibration sensor output signal to obtain fault characterization features with enhanced impact and noise suppression capabilities. It uses feature reconstruction and classification networks as the core to achieve rolling bearing fault identification. The Zebra optimization algorithm (ZOA) is employed to adaptively optimize the penalty factor and the number of modal decompositions in the Variational mode decomposition (VMD), using the regularized envelope entropy as the fitness function to achieve adaptive decomposition and modal feature extraction of the vibration signal. The weighted correlation kurtosis (WCK) is used to evaluate and select the effective modes for signal reconstruction, thereby effectively suppressing modal aliasing and noise interference. On this basis, to address the issue of weak impact features being not obvious in the reconstructed vibration signal, the ZOA-optimized maximum correlation kurtosis deconvolution (MCKD) is introduced. By adaptively adjusting the filtering length and shift order, the periodic impact feature expression ability is further enhanced, and the fault characterization effect of the vibration sensor signal is improved. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively suppress noise interference and enhance the ability to express fault features. This method has achieved excellent diagnostic results on the self-built bearing dataset, the publicly available CWRU dataset, and the publicly available PU dataset. The fault identification accuracy rates reached 96.5%, 97.0%, and 95.9% respectively. Compared with the traditional VMD-MCKD method, the method proposed in this paper has achieved significant performance improvements on different datasets, verifying that the proposed method has better fault feature extraction ability and generalization performance under different operating conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69001-8.title: Seismic vulnerability and sustainable retrofit strategies for traditional masonry heritage buildings in Oman
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69001-8.abstract: Traditional masonry buildings constitute an important part of Oman’s architectural heritage; however, their seismic performance has received limited systematic attention despite the country’s exposure to regional and local seismic hazards. This study presents a qualitative assessment of the structural characteristics, seismic vulnerability, and strengthening strategies for four representative traditional masonry typologies: mud brick (adobe), dry-Stone masonry, stone masonry with mud mortar, and coral-stone masonry with lime mortar. The assessment is based on field surveys, documentation of construction practices, and an indicator-based evaluation of architectural, structural, and foundation characteristics. The results are synthesized using radar charts to facilitate comparison of the relative vulnerability of the different typologies, while detailed schematic illustrations are used to document characteristic construction details, identify key structural deficiencies, and present practical strengthening strategies. The study shows that seismic vulnerability is primarily governed by inadequate wall connectivity, discontinuous load paths, weak diaphragm action, and poor structural integrity rather than construction material alone. Among the investigated typologies, dry-stone masonry exhibits the highest seismic vulnerability, followed by adobe masonry, whereas stone masonry in mud mortar buildings demonstrates comparatively improved performance and coral-stone masonry performs relatively better under the considered conditions. Based on the identified deficiencies, typology-specific strengthening measures are proposed with emphasis on improving structural continuity, diaphragm behaviour, and connection detailing while maintaining compatibility with traditional construction materials and heritage conservation principles. The proposed framework provides practical guidance for the seismic assessment, strengthening, and conservation of traditional masonry buildings in Oman and may serve as a useful reference for similar heritage structures in other earthquake-prone regions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69769-9.title: Identification of RAB36 and NINL as potential diagnostic biomarkers for gestational diabetes mellitus and polycystic ovary syndrome
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69769-9.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) are common endocrine and metabolic disorders in women, with PCOS increasing the risk of GDM. However, shared molecular markers that could support early diagnosis and the mechanisms underlying them remain insufficiently defined. This study integrated public transcriptome datasets for GDM and PCOS to identify shared differentially expressed genes, which were then analyzed via machine learning, diagnostic model construction, pathway analysis, regulatory network analysis, drug prediction, molecular docking, and reverse transcription (RT)-qPCR-based validation in clinical blood samples. Among the 15 shared candidate genes identified, RAB36 and ninein-like (NINL) were selected as potential diagnostic biomarkers. Nomogram and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses indicated that the two-gene models have diagnostic value for both GDM and PCOS, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.71 and 0.98, respectively. Functional analyses suggested that RAB36 and NINL may be associated with pathways related to immune regulation, cell cycle-related processes, metabolic signaling, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Drug prediction and molecular docking further identified cinnamaldehyde and valproic acid as potential compounds targeting both biomarkers. RT-qPCR revealed increased RAB36 expression and decreased NINL expression in clinical blood samples. This study identifies potential biomarkers shared between GDM and PCOS and mechanistic clues for early diagnosis and personalized disease management.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69933-1.title: Early changes in renal parenchymal stiffness after partial nephrectomy assessed by shear wave elastography
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69933-1.abstract: To evaluate whether SWE could be used to assess the renal parenchyma in patients undergoing PN for RCC. This prospective single-center study included 36 adult patients who underwent PN due to RCC. SWE values, resistive index (RI), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine, and urea were measured preoperatively and on postoperative days 1 and 7. Univariate and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of the SWE value on postoperative day 7. SWE measurements declined from a preoperative mean of 22.78 ± 11.98 kPa to 18.84 ± 8.24 kPa on postoperative day 1 and partially recovered to 20.51 ± 9.42 kPa by day 7 (p = 0.091). During this period, eGFR decreased (p = 0.010) and serum creatinine increased (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, medial tumor location (B = 7.541, 95% CI: 2.692–12.390, p = 0.003) and preoperative SWE (B = 0.336, 95% CI: 0.132–0.540, p = 0.002) were independently associated with postoperative day-7 SWE. In a sensitivity analysis of change from baseline, medial location was not significant (p = 0.446), whereas preoperative SWE, ischemia duration, diabetes mellitus, right-sided laterality, and tumor size were significant predictors. Renal parenchymal stiffness showed a non-significant, transient fluctuation after partial nephrectomy, whereas conventional functional markers showed significant early impairment. A sensitivity analysis suggested that the association between tumor location and postoperative stiffness was influenced by baseline differences, while ischemia duration and tumor size may better reflect surgery-related parenchymal change. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger cohorts with longer follow-up before SWE can be considered a validated monitoring tool in this setting.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68405-w.title: Cosmogenic 36Cl surface exposure constraints on late Pleistocene coastal refugia in the eastern Mount Edgecumbe volcanic field, Alaska
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68405-w.abstract: The extent to which parts of Southeast Alaska remained ice-free during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) has implications for models of early human migration to the Americas. The Mount Edgecumbe Volcanic Field (MEVF) on Kruzof Island has been proposed as one such ice-free refugium, but evaluating this hypothesis depends critically on the age of its lava flows. We use geologic mapping, in situ cosmogenic 36Cl surface exposure dating, terrain analysis, and forward modeling to determine the emplacement age of a basalt lava flow in the eastern MEVF. We sampled four different surfaces of the lava flow along an elevation transect spanning from above the marine limit to the modern coastline, including surfaces that experienced prolonged marine inundation during the Holocene. Measured and modeled 36Cl concentrations are consistent with postglacial emplacement of the lava flow at ~ 14.8 ka and incompatible with surface exposure in an ice-free refugium during the LGM. The exposure histories document a coastal landscape undergoing rapid reorganization during the late Pleistocene, with changing ice extent, sea level, and volcanism that would have limited the development of persistent refugia for human migration.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68859-y.title: Mechanisms of water exchange in the Chagan Lake Basin, Songnen Plain: hydrochemical and isotopic constraints from August sampling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68859-y.abstract: The Chagan Lake Basin lies in a typical arid–semi-arid transition zone in northern China. Understanding its hydrological connectivity is essential for aquatic ecosystem conservation and sustainable water use. This study integrates major-ion chemistry, stable water isotopes (δ²H and δ¹⁸O), and the Bayesian mixing model MixSIAR to investigate water exchanges among precipitation, shallow groundwater, rivers, and the lake, together with associated hydrogeochemical processes. Precipitation (TDS = 28 mg L⁻¹) represents a low-mineralization recharge endmember. River water is predominantly of the HCO₃–Ca type, with its chemistry controlled mainly by groundwater baseflow. Shallow groundwater exhibits marked spatial heterogeneity, while the co-enrichment of Na⁺, Cl⁻, and SO₄²⁻ in some samples suggests the combined effects of evaporite dissolution and anthropogenic inputs. Lake water displays a transitional HCO₃–Ca–Na facies and pronounced evaporative enrichment in δ²H and δ¹⁸O. MixSIAR identifies groundwater as the dominant water source to Chagan Lake (55.4%), followed by river water (27.8%) and precipitation (16.8%). River-water isotopes differ substantially from those of shallow groundwater and follow the lake-water evaporation trend, indicating inputs of evaporatively enriched lake water to some river reaches. However, major ions retain a strong groundwater-baseflow signature, revealing decoupled hydrochemical and isotopic responses. Overall, the system is governed by precipitation-fed groundwater recharge, groundwater discharge to rivers and the lake, bidirectional river–lake exchange, and in-lake evaporative concentration and cation exchange. These findings support regional water-resource management and pollution control.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-58013-z.title: Generative AI emotion recognition from bodily gestures and vocal tone reveals modality-specific performance and positivity bias
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-58013-z.abstract: Abstract Advances in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) have prompted interest in its application in sensitive fields, including mental health. Yet the validity of its nonverbal social-cognitive abilities remains unclear. This study addresses two issues that probe GenAI’s social intelligence: its capacity to interpret nonverbal channels (bodily gestures and vocal tone) with accuracy comparable to humans, and whether accuracy of emotion recognition is different by emotional valence. Emotion recognition accuracy of three Gemini GenAI models (Pro 1.5, Pro 2 (Experimental) and Flash 2) were evaluated using the EU-Emotion Stimulus Set of bodily gestures and vocal tone depicting basic emotions. Model accuracy was compared to validated human benchmarks. Advanced GenAI models achieved near-human accuracy in recognizing emotions from vocal tone. However, their performance was significantly lower than that of humans in interpreting bodily gestures. GenAI models recognized positive emotions more accurately than negative ones. This bias was significant across all models for bodily gestures and in the advanced models for vocal tone. GenAI models exhibit a non-humanlike social-cognitive profile, excelling with positive emotions but struggling with the negative content. This finding carries profound clinical and theoretical relevance, highlighting the risks of integrating GenAI into sensitive fields and underscoring the need for continued validation.
