doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67995-9.title: Insights into the stabilization mechanisms of coarse-grained landslide dams
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67995-9.abstract: Landslide dams are natural barriers formed by dynamic processes such as landslides and rock avalanches, which block river channels. Due to their loose structure and heterogeneous material distribution, they are highly susceptible to failure, posing significant hazards downstream. However, in the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, there exists a widespread type of coarse-grained landslide dam formed by rock avalanches. Composed of massive boulders, these dams can maintain long-term stability, yet they have received little research attention. This study conducted flume tests on three representative types of coarse-grained landslide dams-the coarse particle group (T1, d₅₀ = 24.0 mm), the medium particle group (T2, d₅₀ = 8.9 mm), the relatively fine particle group (T3, d₅₀ = 1.3 mm) and performed a field investigation on a typical coarse-grained landslide dam (Mugecuo, Kangding City, Sichuan Province). The experiment results indicate that the coarse particles within the coarse-grained structure play a crucial role in the dam’s stability. During the initial formation stage, the large internal voids allow river water to pass relatively easily through the dam from upstream without causing overtopping. In the seepage stage, the massive boulders on the downstream slope are difficult to be entrained by the river flow at a given velocity, ensuring the overall stability of the dam. Under long – term fluvial scouring, the formation of a coarsened layer and a step-pool system by the large boulders resists intense fluvial erosion, thereby enabling the coarse-grained landslide dam to maintain long-term stability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67402-3.title: Tailoring the structural and textural properties of MCM-41 via myristyl trimethyl ammonium bromide templating for enhanced tetracycline adsorption
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67402-3.abstract: Abstract The escalation of pharmaceutical water pollution, particularly from antibiotics, poses a critical environmental crisis. Consequently, developing highly efficient adsorbents has become imperative to tackle this growing threat. Here, highly ordered pure MCM-41 was synthesized using different molar concentration ratio (0.06, 0.12, 0.25 and 0.415 M) of myristyl trimethyl ammonium bromide surfactant to the silica source. The structural, morphological and texture characteristics were investigated by X-ray diffraction (XRD), N 2 adsorption–desorption, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR). It was found that the myristyl concentration has a profound impact on the mesostructural arrangement of the particles. Consequently, it was found that the highest quality and highly ordered pure MCM-41 structure was achieved using myristyl surfactant at concentrations of 0.25 M and 0.12 M, with the 0.25 M concentration producing a higher degree of ordered pure MCM-41 structure than the 0.12 M concentration. The potential of the prepared MCM-41 samples for adsorption of tetracycline (TC) drug was investigated using varying parameters including: adsorbent dosage, initial drug concentration, adsorption isotherms, and contact time. The MM0.25 sample showed remarkable TC-adsorption removal, with maximum adsorption capacity (q max ) of 5.4 mg g −1 at pH 5.4 and room temperature. The adsorption equilibrium data fitted well with Langmuir adsorption model, while the adsorption kinetic followed the pseudo-second-order model (R 2 = 0.99999). The calculated free adsorption energy obtained from D–R isotherm was found to be 1507.6 kJ mol −1 referring to that the adsorption of TC on MM0.25 adsorbent is chemical. These results revealed that MM0.25 sample could be used as effective adsorbent for the removal of TC drug from aqueous solutions with good recovery and recyclability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67882-3.title: Molecular mechanism analysis of natural leaf abscission in sugarcane based on multi-omics and mining of key genes in ABA pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67882-3.abstract: Abstract Poor leaf abscission in sugarcane significantly increases harvesting costs and constrains mechanized efficiency, yet its molecular basis remains poorly understood. Here, we performed an integrated hormone-targeted metabolomics and transcriptomics analysis in three sugarcane cultivars (GT47, LZ02-169, and ROC22) with contrasting abscission phenotypes. A total of 37 differentially accumulated metabolites and 3109 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified. Integrated analysis revealed extensive reprogramming of phytohormone-related pathways, particularly those associated with auxin, jasmonic acid, abscisic acid (ABA), salicylic acid, gibberellin, and cytokinin. Notably, comparisons involving LZ02-169 and GT47 showed a higher enrichment of hormone-related DEGs, indicating dynamic hormonal regulation underlying phenotypic divergence. Focusing on ABA biosynthesis, two key genes, zeaxanthin epoxidase (ZEP) and β-carotene hydroxylase (BCH), were consistently upregulated in abscission-prone cultivars. Metabolomic data further supported increased accumulation of ABA precursors, including zeaxanthin, suggesting activation of the carotenoid-derived ABA biosynthetic pathway. Correlation analysis indicated a strong association between ZEP/BCH expression and ABA accumulation. Importantly, Upregulation of ZEP and BCH is associated with increased ABA accumulation in the leaf abscission zone, suggesting a potential role for this carotenoid-derived pathway in modulating cell separation during natural abscission. This coordinated transcriptional–metabolic regulation suggests that ABA is a potential key correlate of natural leaf abscission in sugarcane. Collectively, this study provides a multi-omics correlative framework linking carotenoid metabolism to hormone signaling and identifies ZEP and BCH as promising targets for improving sugarcane harvesting efficiency.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69557-5.title: Automated segmentation and length measurement of metacarpal and phalangeal bones for hand radiograph evaluation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69557-5.abstract: Abstract Evaluating hand and wrist radiographs is essential in pediatric endocrinology and clinical genetics, particularly for the assessment of suspected skeletal anomalies. In this study, we present Auto-Bone-Caliper , an automated system for the segmentation and length measurement of metacarpal and phalangeal (M&P) bones, trained and evaluated on public datasets comprising both normal and dysmorphic cases. We first introduce InstanceSAM, a two-stage framework that detects and segments all 19 M&P bones in pediatric hand radiographs, achieving Dice scores of 98.7% for normal bones and 95.0% for dysmorphic bones. We further develop and evaluate three methods for bone-length estimation, identifying a k -means–based approach as the most accurate, with relative errors of 2.2% for normal bones and 4.5% for dysmorphic bones. Our automated pipeline, Auto-Bone-Caliper , integrates InstanceSAM with the k -means–based length-estimation method. To enable scale-independent downstream analyses, we derive relative bone-length measures from the automated measurements. Using these relative measures, we statistically compare measurements obtained using Auto-Bone-Caliper on an independent dataset with a healthy reference catalog of normal bone morphologies, observing a high level of agreement (Wasserstein-1 distance = 0.012). Finally, we demonstrate a potential clinical use case of Auto-Bone-Caliper by obtaining relative metacarpophalangeal pattern profiles for three genetic conditions, namely Turner syndrome, achondroplasia, and pseudohypoparathyroidism. Our results highlight the potential of the Auto-Bone-Caliper to streamline and standardize M&P length measurement, providing an objective and reproducible tool suitable for clinical application.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69263-2.title: The interplay of time pressure and AI assistance reveals moral responsibility recalibration in high-stakes decisions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69263-2.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly integrated into high-stakes decision-making environments, understanding how humans interact with these systems under time pressure is critical for ethical and effective human-AI teaming. While previous research has shown that time pressure can impair cognitive flexibility and increase overreliance on automation, little is known about how these phenomena unfold with intelligent systems in morally sensitive contexts where decisions have ethical consequences. This study investigates the interplay of time pressure, AI assistance, and moral responsibility attribution on moral decision-making. In an experimental ad hoc paradigm, military cadets and officers took on the role of drone operators who had to decide whether to bomb a position-with or without AI support- under varying levels of time pressure (high vs. low). Crucially, the AI suggestions were sometimes obviously wrong, allowing us to isolate the impact of time pressure on overreliance. Our results suggest that while AI assistance increased the likelihood that participants followed wrong and morally questionable recommendations, this effect did not increase under time pressure. Contrary to our expectations, time pressure alone did not significantly alter moral decision making or increase reliance on AI, suggesting that moral decision-making is more robust to cognitive constraints than previously thought. Importantly, despite the decrease in subjective responsibility during interaction with the AI, especially under high time pressure, participants appear to recalibrate their sense of responsibility when the AI makes erroneous recommendations. These results shed new light on the interplay between time constraints, AI influence and moral cognition. They suggest that, on morally loaded situations, time pressure alone may not predict AI overreliance or a diminished sense of moral responsibility. Implications for the responsible integration of AI and the development of decision support systems in defence and other areas where the stakes are high are discussed.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69281-0.title: Imaging-based age- and sex-related cardiovascular and skeletal phenotypes in Fbn1C1041G/+ mice
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69281-0.abstract: Marfan syndrome is a multisystem connective tissue disorder with age- and sex-related phenotypic variability. This study characterized early cardiovascular, valvular, transmitral filling, and skeletal phenotypes in Fbn1 C1041G/ + mice. Male and female wild-type and Fbn1 C1041G/ + mice were examined in independent age-specific cohorts from 4 to 20 weeks of age. Transthoracic echocardiography was used to measure aortic root and ascending aortic diameters, anterior mitral leaflet length, and mitral inflow Doppler parameters. Lateral X-ray imaging was used to quantify kyphosis angle. Fbn1 C1041G/ + mice of both sexes showed age-related aortic enlargement, with segment-specific sex-related heterogeneity involving the annulus and sinus. In mutant mice, anterior mitral leaflet elongation was detected from 8 weeks in males and at 20 weeks in females. Reduced E-wave velocity and E/A ratio were observed in both sexes at 4 weeks, with E-wave velocity remaining lower at most subsequent ages and a lower E/A ratio present at all ages; A-wave velocity did not differ between genotypes at any examined age. Reduced kyphosis angle was detected from 4 weeks in females and from 12 weeks in males. These findings show that early Fbn1-related phenotypes follow organ-specific age-related patterns, supporting age-resolved and sex-stratified assessment in preclinical Marfan syndrome studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-025-16010-8.title: A novel laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps: application in animal experiments
doi:10.1038/s41598-025-16010-8.abstract: Background Esophagojejunostomy (EJS) in laparoscopic total gastrectomy is a technically challenging and high-risk procedure. Current EJS techniques possess limitations, and an optimal solution remains uncertain. Therefore, we designed and developed a novel laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps for purse-string suture placement at the distal esophagus. Our study involves laparoscopic total gastrectomy experiments in pigs, comparing EJS outcomes using laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps with the established OrVil™ technique. Furthermore, we evaluated the feasibility and safety of the laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps. In total, 20 experimental pigs were randomly assigned to an experimental (n = 10) and a control group (n = 10). The experimental group underwent EJS using the laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps, whereas the control group underwent EJS using the OrVil™ technique. Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative data were collected for subsequent statistical analysis. All 20 pigs underwent the surgical procedure without mortality. Statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups in anvil head placement and fixation time, with the laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps group exhibiting a shorter duration. Furthermore, the laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps group demonstrated lower surgical consumable costs compared to the OrVil™ technique group. Conversely, the OrVil™ technique group exhibited an advantage in esophageal rupture repair time. No statistically significant differences were observed between the groups regarding postoperative weight change or other surgery-related data. The laparoscopic titanium purse-string forceps can be used safely and effectively to perform EJS during laparoscopic total gastrectomy. Compared to the OrVil™ technique, these forceps allow for faster and more secure placement and fixation of the anvil head, enhance surgical operability, and offer a more cost-effective alternative.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68437-2.title: Association of testosterone, cortisol, and CRP with miR-146a expression and cardiovascular risk indices in dyslipidemic and healthy men: a case–control study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68437-2.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Testosterone, cortisol, and C-reactive protein (CRP) have been implicated in cardiometabolic regulation, while miR-146a plays an important role in inflammatory signaling. This study investigated the associations of testosterone, cortisol, and CRP with miR-146a expression and advanced cardiovascular risk indices in men from the Kerman Coronary Artery Disease Risk Factors Study (KERCADRS). In this case–control study, 155 adult men were evaluated, including dyslipidemic (n = 121) and healthy (n = 34) participants. Serum testosterone, cortisol, and CRP levels were measured by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) method, and miR-146a expression was quantified using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). Advanced cardiometabolic indices were calculated. Dyslipidemic men had significantly lower testosterone levels (4.91 ± 1.84 vs. 6.97 ± 1.48 ng/mL, P < 0.001) and higher miR-146a expression (1.53 ± 1.05 vs. 0.91 ± 0.31, P < 0.001) than healthy controls. Higher testosterone was associated with better lipid profiles and lower cardiometabolic risk indices. In multivariate analyses, testosterone remained independently and inversely associated with the Atherogenic Index of Plasma (AIP) in both groups, and with lower miR-146a expression in the dyslipidemic group (P < 0.001). Cortisol independently predicted higher AIP in dyslipidemic participants, while CRP showed no significant independent associations. Unexpectedly, higher CRP levels were not linked to worse atherogenic indices. Higher testosterone levels were independently associated with more favorable cardiometabolic profiles and lower miR-146a expression in dyslipidemic men, while higher cortisol levels were associated with increased atherogenic risk. These findings suggest that testosterone, cortisol, and advanced atherogenic indices may aid in cardiovascular risk stratification among men with dyslipidemia. However, due to the observational nature of the study, causality cannot be inferred, and prospective longitudinal as well as interventional studies are needed to validate these associations and explore their potential clinical utility.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69542-y.title: Evaluation of indirect hemolysis induced by snake venoms and its neutralization by corresponding antivenoms: comparative study across five genera
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69542-y.abstract: Abstract Hemolytic activity of snake venoms represents a toxic effect with significant biochemical complexity. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive comparative assessment of the indirect hemolytic activity (expressed as HD 50 ) of 25 medically important venom samples, encompassing five genera. Additionally, we evaluated the efficacy of commercial AV in neutralizing this activity (NHD 50 ). Elapidae venoms displayed the highest hemolytic potency (lowest HD 50 ), correlating with high phospholipase A 2 activity. Within the Bothrops genus, we observed wide variation in potency, with species like B. insularis and B. moojeni exhibiting high activity, while the venom of B. erythromelas consistently proved to be the most resistant to neutralization by antibothropic antivenom. The functional activity data were integrated with chromatographic profiles, enzymatic activities, and phylogenetic analyses, revealing that hemolytic potency is not solely determined by PLA 2 activity but also by its molecular context. Ancestral State Reconstruction suggests multiple events of gain and loss of hemolytic potency within the Bothrops clade. These findings highlight the need for improvements in anti-venom composition, especially for the treatment of envenoming caused by species whose venoms exhibit high resistance to neutralization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-49097-8.title: Morpho-electrochemical behavior of particulate Zn electrodes revealed by X-ray and neutron tomography
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-49097-8.abstract: Abstract Aqueous rechargeable Zn-based batteries are gaining attention for their sustainability, safety, and cost-effectiveness; however, no industrially viable solutions are yet available, due to the synergistic issues of passivation and shape change. In particular, flow batteries with particulate Zn anodes are attractive for long-term stationary storage, at the cost of additional morpho-chemical processes involving the Zn particle bed and the interparticle space (IPS). Thus, the understanding of this system requires space-dependent information about the arrangement, dimensions, and chemical states of Zn and its discharge products. To this aim, we employ dual-probe chemically sensitive X-ray and thermal neutron tomography and radiography. Specifically, we analyzed an in situ anode in both pristine and discharged states, and we followed its self-discharge process in operando. In situ X-ray tomography reveals the advancement of Zn particle consumption and IPS development. In situ neutron tomography shows the formation and distribution of hydroxides. In operando, neutron radiography gives access to hydrogen bubble formation and dynamics. This first-of-its-kind analysis provides crucial insights, directly informing anode design strategies. Our findings contribute to paving the way for next-generation Zn flow batteries with improved efficiency and longevity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69531-1.title: Morphological, metabolic, and chemical changes in Candida albicans cells induced by the NaQSA complex
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69531-1.abstract: This study examines the effects of the sodium complex of quercetin-5′-sulfonic acid (NaQSA) on Candida albicans yeast cells. Flow cytometric analysis showed a concentration-dependent decrease in viable cell numbers after incubation with NaQSA, indicating reduced cellular viability in treated cultures. Fluorescence microscopy revealed marked alterations in cell wall organization. Cells exposed to NaQSA displayed increased fluorescence intensity with Calcofluor White and Congo Red staining, especially in intercellular septa and division scars. Morphological abnormalities were common, including cell deformation, aggregation, and the formation of chains of incompletely separated daughter cells. These findings were supported by scanning electron microscopy, which confirmed substantial cell surface deformations and defects in cell division. Further nanoscale characterization by atomic force microscopy showed significant changes in surface topography and nanomechanical properties of treated cells, including increased surface roughness, elasticity, and deformation. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy revealed distinct changes in the chemical composition of the cell walls depending on NaQSA dose compared to control cultures. Specifically, spectral data showed a gradual increase in the relative cell wall lipid content following NaQSA exposure. A similar effect was observed for polysaccharides, including the absorption bands of β-1,3-glucan and α-mannan fibers that form the outer protective layer. In contrast, decreased intensity of the amide I and II bands suggested a reduction in glycoprotein content. Importantly, NaQSA did not cause cytotoxic or cytopathic effects in human fibroblasts, indicating selective activity toward fungal cells. These findings suggest that NaQSA significantly affects the structural and biochemical properties of the C. albicans cell wall, supporting its potential for further biomedical applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69321-9.title: Accuracy and hallucinations in AI-generated medication dosing calculations: a sequential explanatory mixed-methods evaluation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69321-9.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in healthcare education and clinical decision support. However, their reliability for precise numerical tasks, particularly medication dosage calculations, remains inadequately evaluated. To evaluate the accuracy, consistency, and reasoning patterns of three LLMs: ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek, in performing standardized medication dosing calculations. A sequential explanatory mixed methods design was employed. Ninety standardized prompts covering basic, moderate, and advanced dosing scenarios were developed by subject matter experts and administered to each model, yielding 270 responses. Two independent clinical reviewers assessed responses using a structured checklist for numerical accuracy (correct ≤ 5%, minor deviation 5–10%, major deviation > 10%) and hallucination type. Descriptive statistics and Fisher’s exact tests were used for quantitative analysis, followed by directed content analysis of identified reasoning patterns. Interrater reliability was strong (overall agreement 91.3%; Cohen’s κ = 0.75–0.87). Gemini and DeepSeek achieved 100% accuracy across all complexity levels with no hallucinations. ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 83.3%, with performance declining as complexity increased (53.3% correct on advanced items). Hallucinations occurred exclusively in ChatGPT and included incorrect calculation methods (16.7%), arithmetic errors (15.6%), and flawed reasoning chains (4.4%). Qualitative analysis revealed two archetypes: procedural transparency (Gemini/DeepSeek) and computational fragility (ChatGPT), characterised by methodological drift under increasing cognitive load. Significant inter-model differences exist in the accuracy and reasoning integrity of AI-generated medication dosing calculations. All AI-assisted calculations should be independently verified by qualified clinicians, particularly for high-alert medications and complex dosing protocols, before clinical application.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60341-z.title: Bioactive goldenseal (Hydrastis canadensis) fraction suppresses multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a rat burn wound model: oral and topical administration
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60341-z.abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a prominent pathogen implicated in burn wound infections, creating substantial therapeutic obstacles due to its antibiotic resistance and enhanced virulence mediated by quorum sensing (QS). This study explored the anti-infective and wound-healing properties of a standardized extract from Hydrastis canadensis (Goldenseal; GS) using integrated in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches. LC–ESI–MS/MS profiling identified 52 phytochemicals, including alkaloids, flavonoids, phenolic acids, and glycosides, in the extract. Molecular docking against QS regulators (LasR, LasI, RhlR, and RhlI) revealed preferential binding to LasR, with naringenin-7-O-glucoside showing the highest affinity and chlorogenic and orotic acids exhibiting selective interactions. In vitro, GS demonstrated antibacterial activity (MIC = 3.125 mg/mL), significantly inhibited biofilm formation, and reduced lasR and rhlR expression by 95.3% and 84.8%, respectively ( p < 0.001). In a rat model of second-degree burns, both oral and topical GS administration was evaluated in vivo, revealing enhanced wound contraction, increased collagen deposition, and improved histopathological outcomes. These outcomes were linked to a reduction in TNF-α and IL-1β levels, alongside an increase in VEGF and bFGF levels, as well as the upregulation of antimicrobial peptides, including CAMP and RBD2. Moreover, the efficacy of topical application surpassed that of oral administration. These findings indicate that GS suppresses QS-regulated virulence and promotes wound repair, supporting its potential application as an adjunctive therapeutic approach for burn wound infections caused by MDR P. aeruginosa .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-57409-1.title: The impoverishing effect of tobacco expenditures
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-57409-1.abstract: Tobacco consumption is a major source of health and financial burden, yet evidence on its association with household poverty remains limited. This study examines how tobacco-related expenditures are associated with both the incidence and depth of poverty in Albania. Using nationally representative data from the Household Budget Survey, we estimate poverty indicators under three alternative definitions of household resources: observed expenditure, expenditure net of tobacco spending, and expenditure net of both tobacco and smoking-attributable healthcare costs. The results show that accounting for tobacco-related expenditures is associated with higher poverty levels. Under the most comprehensive scenario, approximately 13,000 additional households (representing nearly 60,000 individuals, including over 10,000 children) fall below the poverty line because of related tobacco expenditures. The headcount ratio increases from about 27% to 29%, while the poverty gap widens by around 2% points. Complementary regression analysis further indicates that higher tobacco expenditure shares are associated with a greater likelihood of being poor. These findings suggest that tobacco-related expenditures are closely associated with economic vulnerability and highlight the potential contribution of tobacco control policies to improving financial protection, reducing poverty-related vulnerability, and supporting broader public health and social development objectives.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69378-6.title: The added value of patient education in pulmonary rehabilitation of acute COVID-19 cases: a randomized controlled study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69378-6.abstract: Pulmonary rehabilitation plays a key role in the recovery of patients hospitalized with COVID-19. However, the potential additive effect of structured patient education on clinical outcomes remains underexplored. This study aims to evaluate the impact of a standard versus education-enhanced pulmonary rehabilitation program on cardiopulmonary function, functional capacity, and emotional well-being in patients hospitalized with acute COVID-19. This randomized controlled trial randomized 80 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, of whom 70 completed the study and were included in the final analysis. Participants were assigned to either a control group receiving standard pulmonary rehabilitation or an intervention group receiving the same rehabilitation protocol supplemented by daily health education. Outcomes were measured at baseline and post-intervention using oxygen saturation, arterial blood gases, incentive spirometry, the Barthel Index, HADS depression scale, mMRC dyspnea scale, Borg fatigue scale, and the sit-to-stand test. Both groups showed significant improvements across all measured outcomes (p < 0.001). However, the intervention group demonstrated superior gains in SpO₂ (Δ + 15,0vs. + 8,0), pO₂ (Δ + 17,1vs. + 2,7 mmHg), and lung capacity (Δ + 1500,0vs. + 750,0 mL). Functional and psychological improvements were also greater in the intervention group, including Barthel Index (Δ + 60,0vs. + 45,0), HADS (Δ -16,0vs. -7,0), mMRC (Δ -2,0vs. -1,0), Borg fatigue score (Δ -6,0vs. -4,0), and sit-to-stand repetitions (Δ + 5,0vs. + 2,0) (all p < 0.001). Adding structured patient education to a pulmonary rehabilitation program may contribute to recovery in hospitalized patients with acute COVID-19. This integrative approach leads to improved cardiopulmonary function, greater physical independence, and reduced psychological burden. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06522724), Registry Identifier: NCT06522724, Registration Date:19/07/2024.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55967-y.title: Investigating the wetting effectiveness of surfactant blends on anthracite coal dust: combined experimental and molecular simulation approaches
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55967-y.abstract: Abstract Conventional water spraying methods often prove inadequate due to the poor wettability of these coal dust particles. To address this, the present study introduces a comprehensive strategy that integrates molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with laboratory experiments to systematically explore the, wetting performance of surfactant composite systems and develop high-efficiency wetting agents suitable for anthracite dust in the Yangquan mining area.Characterization of the anthracite samples using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and proximate and ultimate analysis revealed a high prevalence of hydrophobic surface groups. To counter this, MD simulations employing a Spiro anthracite model were conducted to analyze coal-water and coal-surfactant-water systems. Key simulation metrics-including non-bonded interaction energy, mean square displacement (MSD), electrostatic potential (ESP) distribution, and relative concentration demonstrated that selected surfactants significantly enhance water interaction and reduce coal surface hydrophobicity.Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), sodium dodecylbenzene sulfonate (SDBS), and sodium alcohol ether sulfate (AES) were identified as the most effective monomeric surfactants based on simulation data. These findings were further validated through contact angle measurements, surface tension analysis, and penetration tests. Compared to a surfactant-free system, the selected surfactants significantly enhanced wetting performance, demonstrating a 62.3% reduction in contact angle, a 57.15% decrease in surface tension, and a 4.4-fold increase in penetration rate-confirming their practical efficacy in improving wetting behavior.Single-factor tests were carried out to verify the wetting capacity of individual surfactants and measure their critical micelle concentration (CMC). Combined with orthogonal tests, the compound formula was further optimized, and the optimal proportion was confirmed as 0.25 wt% SDS + 0.20 wt% SDBS + 0.35 wt% AES. This optimized surfactant compound exhibited desirable properties, including weak alkalinity, excellent fluidity, low corrosiveness, and strong environmental compatibility, along with significantly enhanced wetting of anthracite dust.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69421-6.title: Development and effectiveness of a basic epidemiological investigation simulation program for aircraft quarantine officials: application of standardized patients
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69421-6.abstract: This study aimed to develop a simulation-based education program on emerging respiratory infectious diseases using standardized patients for aircraft quarantine officials, and to evaluate its effects on basic epidemiological investigation. A total of 53 aircraft quarantine officials (experimental group, n = 27; control group, n = 26) participated in the study from October 21 to 24 in 2024. A simulation-based education program of emerging respiratory infectious diseases was developed based on the ADDIE model. The educational program was structured to include a total of 100 min, comprising both theoretical instruction and simulation practice, targeting aircraft quarantine officials at the Incheon Airport Quarantine Station. To verify the effectiveness of the simulation program utilizing standardized patients, basic epidemiological investigation clinical performance ability, basic epidemiological investigation self-efficacy, and satisfaction with the education were evaluated. The experimental group showed significantly higher scores than the control group for basic epidemiological investigation clinical performance ability (t = 2.18, p =.034), basic epidemiological investigation self-efficacy (t = 2.36, p =.022), and satisfaction with the education (t = 3.98, p <.001). The results suggest that this simulation-based education program using standardized patients may improve self-reported clinical performance ability, self-efficacy, and educational satisfaction among aircraft quarantine officials.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67445-6.title: Food handling practices and associated factors among housemaids and food establishment workers: a comparative cross-sectional study from Ethiopia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67445-6.abstract: Food handling practices are essential for preventing foodborne diseases and protecting public health. However, evidence comparing food handling practices and their associated factors among housemaids working in households and food handlers working in food establishments in Ethiopia remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to compare food handling practices and identify factors associated with good food handling practices among housemaids working in households and food handlers working in food establishments in Dessie City, Ethiopia. A community-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 846 participants (423 housemaids working in households and 423 food handlers working in food establishments) in Dessie City, Ethiopia, from February to April 2021. Data were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires and observational checklists. Binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with good food handling practices. Variables with p < 0.25 in the bivariable analysis were entered into the multivariable model, and variables with p < 0.05 were considered statistically significant. The proportion of participants with good food handling practices was higher among food handlers working in food establishments (62.6%; 95% CI: 58.0–67.2) than among housemaids working in households (47.0%; 95% CI: 42.2–51.8). Food safety knowledge, attitude toward food handling practices, and selected environmental characteristics were also assessed. Overall, food handlers working in food establishments demonstrated higher levels of food safety knowledge than housemaids working in households. Similarly, positive attitudes toward food handling practices were more common among food handlers. Environmental characteristics, including the availability of a three-compartment dishwashing system and the absence of vectors and rodents, also differed between the two study groups. Detailed distributions of these variables are presented in the Supplementary Tables. Among housemaids, work experience > 4 years (AOR 3.37; 95% CI: 1.57–7.26) and positive attitude toward food handling practices (AOR 2.26; 95% CI: 1.39–4.14) were associated with good food handling practices. Among food handlers working in food establishments, a three-compartment dishwashing system (AOR 2.27; 95% CI: 1.43–3.61), absence of vectors/rodents (AOR 3.32; 95% CI: 1.63–6.77), and good food safety knowledge (AOR 2.15; 95% CI: 1.31–3.53) were associated with good food handling practices. In the pooled analysis, a three-compartment dishwashing system, absence of vectors/rodents, and positive attitude toward food handling practices remained significantly associated with good food handling practices. Good food handling practices were higher among food handlers working in food establishments than among housemaids working in households. Work experience, food safety knowledge, attitude toward food handling practices, the availability of a three-compartment dishwashing system, and the absence of vectors and rodents were factors associated with good food handling practices. These findings suggest that strengthening food safety education, improving workplace sanitation, and promoting positive food safety attitudes may contribute to improving food handling practices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63724-4.title: Resin does not safeguard insect DNA during early decay despite preservation of soft tissues
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63724-4.abstract: Abstract The notion that plant resin acts as an exceptional preservative of insect DNA and soft tissues—functioning as a natural dehydration capsule—has been questioned in recent years, yet empirical support remains limited. We applied an actuotaphonomic approach across a 30-day time series to assess DNA and internal soft tissue preservation in two model species of insects, i.e., Drosophila melanogaster (Diptera) and Tribolium castaneum (Coleoptera), under two treatments: embedding in fresh pine resin or remaining unembedded and air-dried. Total nucleic acid concentration, relative dsDNA, and quantitative PCR targeting insect and bacterial genes revealed a similar overall DNA decline through time, with no significant differences between treatments, although some resin-embedded replicates degraded faster. Synchrotron tomography showed taxon- and treatment-dependent soft tissue differences. Unembedded specimens of both orders displayed dried internal tissues after 30 days. Resin-embedded fruit flies largely retained intact muscle structure with minimal gas accumulation. Embedded red flour beetles, while maintaining tissue structure, were more poorly preserved, showing diffuse tissue boundaries and abundant gas likely from bacterial metabolism. These findings indicate that soft tissue preservation in pine resin is group-specific, possibly linked to exoskeletal permeability affecting moisture and resin exchange during decay, and suggest that recovering ancient DNA from amber fossil insects is highly improbable.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69099-w.title: Spatiotemporal vegetation trends and climate attribution across Pakistan’s agro-ecological zones
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69099-w.abstract: Pakistan encompasses the world’s most climatically and topographically diverse landscapes, spanning hyper-arid deserts, glaciated high-mountain ranges, and irrigated plains. Vegetation dynamics in such heterogeneous regions reflect complex interactions among water availability, thermal conditions, and land management. This study characterized spatiotemporal vegetation dynamics and their lag‑resolved climatic drivers across Pakistan’s Agro‑Ecological Zones (AEZs) during 2001–2024, using the MODIS Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) MOD13Q1 product alongside nine ERA5‑Land climate variables. Long‑term vegetation trends were assessed using the Modified Mann–Kendall (MMK) test with autocorrelation correction and False Discovery Rate (FDR) control. Positive vegetation trends (greening) were recorded across all AEZs, with 24% of pixels reaching statistical significance and only 0.8% showing significant browning (declining greenness). Soil moisture was found to be the dominant driver in just over 37% of pixels, confirming that root‑zone water availability governs vegetation variability across most of Pakistan. In the irrigated plains, vegetation trends were strongly correlated with canal irrigation rather than precipitation, consistent with the operation of the Indus irrigation network. The Rainfed Plateau showed the strongest vegetation recovery despite declining rainfall, suggesting improved land management as a contributing factor. In the mountain zones, asymmetric temperature warming was associated with extended growing seasons, while deserts exhibited instantaneous soil‑moisture coupling. Additional drivers included sensible heat flux and dewpoint temperature in the Northern Irrigated Plain, consistent with irrigation‑induced atmospheric humidity feedbacks. The Coastal Zone delta fringe was the only spatially coherent area of browning, associated with freshwater deficits below the Kotri Barrage. These results demonstrate that Pakistan’s vegetation reflects diverse, mechanistically distinct processes across AEZs, and highlight the importance of lag‑resolved, multi‑variable attribution for accurate vegetation–climate diagnosis in climatically heterogeneous irrigated landscapes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69123-z.title: Tailoring mechanical and dielectric behaviours of basalt fiber/epoxy composites via dual ceramic fillers incorporation and Grey–Taguchi optimization
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69123-z.abstract: Abstract For several decades, epoxy thermoset resins have been widely used as dielectric materials in high-voltage electrical insulation systems. However, today''s needs require improved thermal, dielectric and mechanical performances from these materials. Hence the use of basalt fibre reinforcement, in addition to ceramic fillers, is explored to improve the properties of the epoxy composites. This research paper presents a study on the mechanical and electrical performances of hexagonal boron nitride and alumina ceramic fillers/basalt fiber/epoxy composites via experimental method and then utilises Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) to optimise multiple responses based on the input variables of filler weight percentage. The basalt fiber/ceramic fillers reinforced hybrid epoxy composites (BF/CF/HEC) are manufactured using hand lay-up method with compression mould. L9 orthogonal array design is employed with filler loadings of 2.5%, 5% and 7.5% by weight. The impacts of hybrid filler content on ultimate tensile strength (UTS), Izod impact strength and dielectric constant (DC) are investigated. The experimental findings show a significant relationship between mechanical properties and electrical performance with respect to the dispersion of fillers and the interfacial bonding between the fillers and the epoxy matrix. BF/CF/HEC5 exhibits 50.4% higher UTS and the highest Young’s modulus of 8119 MPa, indicating superior tensile strength and stiffness. The composite, having a balanced composition of alumina and hBN, exhibits higher UTS due to better stress transfer mechanisms and crack deflection mechanisms. The increase in impact resistance is attributed to energy dissipation through the fiber–matrix interface and controlled microcrack propagation. The use of Grey Relational Analysis allows the determination of the optimum combination of alumina and hBN to enhance all the mechanical and DC properties.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69939-9.title: Storage symptom burden in women with obesity is associated more with age and smoking than metabolic biomarkers: prospectively collected cross-sectional data
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69939-9.abstract: Obesity frequently coexists with insulin resistance and lower urinary tract symptoms, but the independent contribution of metabolic abnormalities among women with obesity is uncertain. We analyzed prospectively collected cross-sectional data from 139 women with body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m 2 who underwent anthropometric, biochemical, and structured urinary symptom assessment. Storage symptom burden was measured using a locally modified six-item set based on the OAB-q Short Form symptom-bother domain; because wording and scoring differed from the validated instrument, the resulting 6–36 score was treated as study-specific. Internal consistency was high (Cronbach’s α = 0.907). Symptom burden showed weak nominal correlations with HOMA-IR and HDL cholesterol, but neither remained significant after false-discovery-rate sensitivity adjustment. After multivariable adjustment, age (β = 1.81 per SD, 95% CI 0.47–3.15) and current smoking (β = 3.60, 95% CI 0.33–6.88) were associated with greater symptom burden, whereas no individual metabolic marker was independently associated with the primary outcome. No prespecified predictor was independently associated with nocturia ≥ 2/night. Sensitivity analyses did not materially alter the metabolic conclusions. Age and smoking may therefore be useful prompts for urinary symptom assessment in obesity-clinic practice, although these cross-sectional associations are non-causal.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68386-w.title: Language as labels for cross dataset generalization in sign language translation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68386-w.abstract: Sign language translation is a challenging task by large vision-language models due to the complicated temporal-spatial cues, cross-modal semantic alignment and expensive gloss. To alleviate this issue, we propose a novel large language model-based multi-modal boosted method, which achieves language-as-labels and a customized three-stage vision-language fusion pipeline for sign language translation. Specifically, we produce a sign language action description dataset to realize the transformation of sign language label from gloss sequences to action description sequences. Moreover, this study leverages our dataset as labels and visual-caption early fusion approach to encourage the large language model to accurately capture sign language action temporal-spatial cues. Note that this study introduces the large-scale natural language processing datasets for generating sign language action labels for the first time to achieve cross-dataset sign language reasoning. Empirically, extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on widely used benchmarks while demonstrating strong cross-dataset generalization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68724-y.title: Seismic resilience assessment of building structures considering structural damage modes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68724-y.abstract: Abstract Building structure is composed of thousands of various components, and its damage development path and damage modes are complex and diverse. The variation in structural damage modes leads to degradation in structural functionality, consequently influencing the overall seismic resilience of the system. Accordingly, the progressive and intricate nature of damage evolution must be explicitly incorporated into the assessment of structural seismic resilience. Firstly, this paper uses the complex network theory to describe the performance loss under different structural damage modes. Next, by continuously updating the structural functional degradation and repair time during the component rehabilitation, a seismic performance recovery function is obtained, and a new structural seismic resilience index, reflecting the damage modes of structural system, is proposed. Finally, four structural damage modes (Modes A, B, C, and D) are designed based on the damage sequence of energy-dissipating components, and the structural seismic resilience is compared. Results show that structural damage modes can affect structural seismic resilience, and the differences in seismic resilience become more significant as structural damage develops. When the seismic action is large, compared with Mode C, Mode A reduces the performance loss by 48.8%, shortens the repair time by 18.8% and enhances the resilience by 190.2%.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54563-4.title: CaMKIIα mediates feedback effects of wheel-running activity on the circadian pacemaker in mice
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54563-4.abstract: CaMKIIα functional knockout mouse (K42R) showed substantial changes in the entrainment pattern of running-wheel (RW) rhythm to a short (LD6:18) but not to a long (LD18:6) photoperiod. In wild type mice (WT), entrainment to LD6:18 occurred at the light-off phase, whereas in most K42R entrainment took place at the light-on phase. These differences are well explained by lengthening of circadian period (τ) and compromising the couplings between the activity-onset and -end in K42R. Indeed, τ in K42R and WT were longer and shorter than 24 h, respectively, under the following constant darkness (DD). Without RW τ was lengthened in WT, whereas it was shortened in K42R. Similarly, activity time was lengthened in WT but shortened in K42R. Importantly, τ without RW was not different between the two genotypes, which were confirmed in naive mice. Tau and α returned to the pre-removal levels after RW re-introduction in both WT and K42R. These results indicate that the changes of behavioral rhythm in K42R are due to a lack of feedback effects of RW activity, which are mediated by CaMKIIα-dependent mechanisms. A two-oscillator model assuming involvement of CaMKIIα in the coupling between them successfully simulated the effects of RW activity in K42R.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68762-6.title: Analysis and simulation study on typhoon wind speed characteristics based on offshore wind turbine structure
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68762-6.abstract: Abstract Typhoons feature high wind speeds, rapid wind direction changes, and intense turbulence, which bring severe threats to the safe operation of offshore wind turbines. Based on field measurements obtained using a three-dimensional ultrasonic anemometer at an offshore wind farm in Zhejiang Province, China, this paper systematically analyzes the mean and fluctuating wind characteristics under typhoon conditions. Two typical time-varying evolution patterns of mean wind speed are summarized, and the variation rules of wind direction angle are investigated. The results show that the longitudinal turbulence intensity ranges from 0.2 to 0.4 at the height of 35 m. The probability distribution of fluctuating wind speed approximates a Gaussian distribution, and the frequency-domain energy distribution generally follows the von Karman turbulence spectrum. In accordance with the measured typhoon wind statistical properties, the harmonic superposition method is adopted to generate typhoon wind field time histories. On this basis, the typhoon wind speed simulation software is compiled and its reliability and accuracy are validated against measured data. The findings of this study can provide technical support for wind field reconstruction and structural safety evaluation of offshore wind turbines subjected to typhoon loads.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69571-7.title: Quality evaluation of the Salvia miltiorrhiza wine-frying process based on electronic eye, electronic nose, and untargeted metabolomics combined with multivariate fusion algorithm
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69571-7.abstract: Wine-frying is a traditional processing method for Salvia miltiorrhiza ( S. miltiorrhiza ), but the dynamic quality changes during the process lack objective evaluation methods. This study integrates electronic eye, electronic nose, and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the color, odor, and metabolite changes of S. miltiorrhiza during frying. Results showed that, as frying time increases, the color parameter a * decreases, while b * and c * first decrease and then increase. The electronic nose tentatively annotated 20 volatile compounds, with (E)-2-penten-1-ol and acetoin showing significant increases. The orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis based on odor successfully distinguished different frying degrees. Untargeted metabolomics annotated 1486 metabolites, among which dihydromacarpine and saponarin were screened as processing-sensitive differential metabolites showing increasing trends with frying time. Volcano plot revealed that frying for 8–12 min was a critical stage for significant metabolite changes. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis indicated that frying influenced pathways such as isoflavonoid biosynthesis. Correlation analysis established significant relationships between color, odor, and metabolites. A preliminary random forest-based discrimination model was constructed using multi-source fusion variables and optimized by genetic and particle swarm optimization algorithms. The model showed promising internal discrimination performance in the current limited dataset. This study provides a preliminary multi-dimensional framework for evaluating the wine-frying process of S. miltiorrhiza , which requires further validation using larger and more diverse sample sets.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68876-x.title: Exploratory proof-of-concept study and failure mode analysis of a dual-lumen stent graft for transapical off-pump LVAD implantation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68876-x.abstract: Abstract Transapical off-pump implantation of left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) requires a separate inflow cannula and outflow graft. This study represents the first exploratory proof-of-concept evaluation of a dual-lumen stent graft designed to redirect blood from the left ventricle across the aortic valve into the ascending aorta while enabling LVAD support. The stent graft was tested in a mock circulatory loop, during wet-lab experiments on explanted porcine hearts, and in an exploratory acute large-animal study. In vitro testing showed no relevant impairment of pump performance. Wet-lab experiments confirmed that transapical positioning is feasible while revealing incomplete device expansion and myocardial tearing during balloon-assisted apical displacement. In vivo, a reinforced prototype could be positioned across the aortic valve, but myocardial compression impaired inflow expansion and LV unloading, while insufficient apical sealing resulted in bleeding and air embolism. Postmortem analysis confirmed correct device positioning without macroscopic valvular injury but identified myocardial tearing. These failure modes highlight the need for alternative design strategies for transapical off-pump LVAD implantation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67630-7.title: Progression GWAS followed by functional characterization implicates E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM2 as a potential genetic modifier of Parkinson’s disease progression
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67630-7.abstract: ABSTRACT Parkinson’s Disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, affecting 10 million people worldwide. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many genetic variants associated with PD incidence, the genetics underlying PD progression are poorly understood. Here, we aim to address this gap by performing GWAS on longitudinal clinical metrics from well-defined PD cohorts. Specifically, we identify 8 novel GWAS genes for PD progression, including TRIM2, which encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase with loss-of-function mutations that cause neuropathy. Functional genomics data suggest that the GWAS SNPs in the locus of TRIM2 regulate its expression across several PD-relevant brain regions. Further, we show that TRIM2 knockdown and overexpression in primary neurons regulate neurofilament light (NF-L) levels and α-synuclein aggregation-the primary neuropathological hallmark of PD. Peripheral proteomic analysis of a genetically defined PD patient cohort demonstrates increased NF-L protein levels in the plasma and cerebrospinal fluid of TRIM2 SNP carriers, corroborating the role of TRIM2 in NF-L regulation. Overall, by integrating PD progression GWAS with transcriptomic, eQTL analyses, and functional data in PD cellular models, we identify new targets including TRIM2 that may influence the progression rate of PD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68153-x.title: Circulating CXCL9 and CXCL10 in adult secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis: associations with the IFN-γ inflammatory axis and immune-activation profiles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68153-x.abstract: Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled immune activation. The interferon gamma (IFN-γ)-inducible chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10 may provide complementary measures of this inflammatory response, but their clinical associations in adult sHLH remain incompletely defined. We retrospectively studied 42 adults with newly diagnosed sHLH (26 lymphoma-associated HLH [LAHLH] and 16 non-LAHLH). An additional 15 healthy controls (7 males and 8 females; aged 29–60 years) who had complete individual cytokine data were included. Plasma IL-1β, IL-10, IFN-γ, granzyme B, CXCL9, and CXCL10 were measured by cytometric bead array. IL-10, IFN-γ, granzyme B, CXCL9, and CXCL10 were higher in sHLH than in healthy controls (Holm-adjusted P ≤ 0.002). CXCL9 and CXCL10 did not differ between LAHLH and non-LAHLH. After false-discovery-rate correction, CXCL9 correlated with IFN-γ, granzyme B, and CXCL10, while CXCL10 correlated with granzyme B. CXCL9 and CXCL10 distinguished sHLH from healthy controls with areas under the curve of 0.995 and 0.990, respectively. Patients with CXCL10 ≥ 274.8 pg/mL had poorer overall survival than those with lower concentrations (log-rank P = 0.033). In an exploratory multivariable Cox model adjusted for sCD25 and LAHLH, elevated CXCL10 remained associated with mortality (HR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.02–5.95; P = 0.046), although the estimate was imprecise. These findings support CXCL9 and CXCL10 as complementary indicators of IFN-γ/cytotoxic immune activation and identify an exploratory prognostic association for CXCL10 that requires external validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69764-0.title: Multimodal collaborative modeling of teacher verbal and non-verbal classroom behaviors for teaching effectiveness prediction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69764-0.abstract: Abstract Teacher classroom behavior sits at the centre of any serious attempt to understand and improve instructional quality, yet the verbal and the non-verbal channel are still typically examined apart, which leaves their pedagogically meaningful interdependence unmodelled. This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that models the two channels collaboratively and predicts teaching effectiveness from their joint representation. Four modules compose the framework: temporal synchronization of the audio and video streams, parallel unimodal encoding through BERT-based language representation and SlowFast spatiotemporal networks, bidirectional cross-modal attention fusion regulated by a gated modality weighting mechanism, and a dual-head prediction network optimized jointly for effectiveness classification and continuous score regression. On a corpus of 186 classroom sessions recorded in 12 schools, the framework attains 82.3% classification accuracy, 80.1% macro-F1, an RMSE of 6.58 and a Pearson correlation of 0.879, ahead of ten comparison systems spanning unimodal, traditional machine learning and state-of-the-art multimodal fusion approaches. Ablation identifies bidirectional cross-modal attention as the component that matters most, and an attention analysis conducted across all test sessions indicates that verbal-gestural temporal synchrony accompanies higher observer-rated teaching effectiveness. The framework thus offers a scalable, automated route from multimodal teacher behavior to instructional outcomes, with potential applications in teacher professional development and intelligent classroom observation systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68773-3.title: Aspirin use is not associated with metabolic dysfunction associated fatty liver disease in the UK Biobank
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68773-3.abstract: This study investigated the association between aspirin use and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Based on data from the UK Biobank (UKB), this study included a variety of covariates such as age, gender, BMI, lifestyle factors, metabolic indicators and liver function indicators, and assessed the association between aspirin use and MAFLD after balancing the baseline differences by the propensity score matching (PSM) method, and explored the influencing factors by stratified analyses and interaction tests. During a median follow-up period of 9.41 years, among 3,922 participants, aspirin use was not significantly associated with MAFLD after adjusting for a variety of metabolic confounders (OR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.82–1.15), a finding that was consistent across sensitivity analyses. When BMI was modeled categorically, a significant association was observed only among participants with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²; OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52–0.92), whereas no associations were found in normal-weight or overweight groups. An exploratory interaction was observed between aspirin use and stroke history (aspirin × stroke, OR for interaction = 0.07, 95% CI: 0.008–0.646, P = 0.019). In this observational study, aspirin use was not significantly associated with MAFLD. Exploratory analyses suggested possible heterogeneity according to BMI and stroke history; however, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of multiple comparisons and the small number of participants with a history of stroke. Overall, aspirin use was not significantly associated with MAFLD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69142-w.title: The first Tipulomorpha (Insecta, Diptera) from the Oligocene of Poland and new data on fossils from Miocene of Italy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69142-w.abstract: The paper presents the discovery of two new species of the genus Tipula (Diptera: Tipulomorpha). The new species are Tipula (Tipula) lukasiewiczi sp. nov. and Tipula (Yamatotipula) gentilinii sp. nov. The first is described from the marine Oligocene Menilite Formation of Poland. This finding represents the earliest evidence of dipterans in the Polish Oligocene and provides new data on the presence of the genus Tipula (Tipulomorpha, Tipuloidea, Tipulidae) in the northern Paratethys region. The second, new for knowledge species was described from the Upper Miocene deposite of Monte Castellaro (Marche, Central Italy). Detailed morphological analyses, including wing venation reconstructions, are provided. Furthermore, hypotheses regarding the palaeoenvironmental preferences in relation to the biogeographic distribution of the described taxa are proposed. These results contribute to the knowledge of Paleogene and Neogene Tipulomorpha.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69355-z.title: Mindfulness, creative self-efficacy, and communal-agentic orientation in human–AI decision-making with implications for adaptive AI design
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69355-z.abstract: Abstract Human decision-making is increasingly augmented by artificial intelligence (AI), yet individuals vary in whether they revise their judgments after receiving AI-generated input. We examined how trait mindfulness and creative self-efficacy (CSE), together with communal-agentic personality orientations, relate to decision revision following AI input. Data from 549 UK-based professionals were analysed using binary logistic regression, with revision of the initial budget allocation (change versus no change) as the outcome. The mindfulness × CSE interaction was significant, indicating that the association between mindfulness and decision revision varied by CSE. The pattern was positive at lower CSE and negative at higher CSE, although neither median-split simple slope reached conventional significance. CSE showed no independent main effect. Communal-femininity moderated the association between mindfulness and revision, whereas the hypothesised mindfulness × CSE × communal-femininity interaction was trend-level and is treated as suggestive. Because the outcome captured any revision rather than movement toward the AI recommendation, the findings concern the likelihood of reconsidering an initial decision after AI input, not acceptance of AI advice or improvement in decision quality. These results refine understanding of individual differences in human–AI decision revision and identify testable considerations for adaptive AI design.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69110-4.title: Lightweight UAV aerial small object detection based on YOLOv12 via attentional scale sequence fusion
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69110-4.abstract: In Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) aerial imagery, targets are densely distributed, small in scale, and embedded in complex backgrounds. Existing detection methods, when deployed on edge devices, struggle to satisfy both accuracy and real-time requirements simultaneously. Therefore, achieving accurate, real-time, and robust small-object detection remains a critical challenge. To address this, this paper proposes a lightweight UAV small-object detection model, YOLOv12-RepViT-ASF, based on an attention-scale sequence fusion design. Built on the YOLOv12n framework, the model adopts a lightweight convolutional neural network module (RepViT) in the backbone to enhance feature extraction and global modeling capabilities, and introduces an attention scale sequence fusion (ASF) module in the neck to enable interaction and fusion of multi-scale features, thereby improving small-scale object extraction and suppressing background interference. Experimental results show that YOLOv12-RepViT-ASF achieves mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 34.4% and 20.2% on the VisDrone2019 dataset, representing improvements of 4.9 and 3.4 percentage points, respectively, over the YOLOv12n baseline.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68826-7.title: Cumulative dynamic damage evolution and differentiated blasting control in fractured hydrothermally altered rock masses
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68826-7.abstract: Abstract Fractured hydrothermally altered rock masses around roadway excavations are highly susceptible to repeated blasting disturbance, yet the transfer from specimen-scale cyclic degradation to engineering-scale contour deterioration remains insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study establishes a cross-scale framework integrating repeated-impact SHPB testing, RHT constitutive calibration, multi-cycle LS-DYNA simulation, field vibration monitoring, and field assessment. The vibration records exhibit pronounced multi-pulse characteristics and site-dependent attenuation. Repeated-impact tests show that the altered ore rock undergoes progressive dynamic degradation, characterized by decreasing peak stress and increasing deformation under successive high-rate loading. The calibrated RHT model reproduces the principal peak-stress degradation trend of the 0.5 MPa calibration dataset, with a maximum relative difference of 4.56%. Multi-cycle simulations further demonstrate progressive accumulation of stress concentration, damage, and contour deterioration under successive excavation cycles. Based on this response, a differentiated charging strategy was implemented to reduce explosive loading adjacent to the retained contour while maintaining sufficient internal rock breakage. A representative field assessment indicates that the estimated loosening-zone extent decreased from 1.36 m to 1.15 m after optimization. The results provide a mechanism-based framework for linking cyclic material degradation with cumulative excavation damage and for guiding low-disturbance blasting in hydrothermally altered rock masses.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68717-x.title: Trusted collaboration mechanism of blockchain and smart contracts in the circular economy supply chain
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68717-x.abstract: This paper aims to solve the problems of information islands, complex authority management and difficult data traceability in the circular economy supply chain. Utilizing blockchain and its built-in smart contract technology, this study investigates a trustworthy collaborative mechanism designed to enhance the security of circular economy supply chains. This paper first adopts a multi-chain layered architecture and designs the production, recycling and remanufacturing chains into three parallel sub-chains. Each sub-chain optimizes data for its specific business to eliminate information islands. This paper designs an automatic execution protocol based on smart contracts, sets different access rules according to data types and sensitivity, ensures data security access through policy management and permission determination contracts, and reduces human intervention. This paper leverages the blockchain-native hash-chain structure and Merkle tree verification mechanism to achieve end-to-end tamper-proof traceability and enhance supply chain transparency. The PoVT (Proof of Vote and Trust) consensus mechanism can adjust node weights and optimize network resource allocation dynamically. The results show that the average information response time of the multi-chain layered architecture in the production and remanufacturing chains is 2.52 s and 5 s. In terms of data traceability, the method achieves an average traceability accuracy rate of 97.498%; the average TPS (transaction per second) of PoVT is 63.286, and the decentralization score is 0.82. Thirty repeated experiments demonstrated that the average permission verification time was 2.35 s, with a mean false positive rate of 1.05% and a defense success rate of 99.12%, showing statistically significant differences compared to three baseline methods (p < 0.01). In summary, successfully combining blockchain with smart contracts can create an effective method for providing trusted collaboration mechanisms to facilitate the establishment of circular economy supply chains and show great promise as a solution to address information silos and issues with traceability of data.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-41058-5.title: A numerical study on the thermal buffering of bricks integrated with cylindrical phase change material capsules
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-41058-5.abstract: While phase change materials (PCMs) in bricks are known to improve thermal mass, the influence of capsule geometry in hot climates remains poorly understood. This study evaluates the thermal performance of thermally smart bricks (TSBs) integrated with cylindrical heptadecane capsules reinforced with stainless-steel foam. Using a validated CFD model, we investigate a critical yet overlooked parameter: the capsule diameter (2, 3, and 4 cm) under varying peak outdoor temperatures (20–40 °C). Results show that PCM–foam capsules reduce peak indoor temperature by up to 1.9 °C, induce a 2–3-hour thermal lag, and lower heat flux amplitude by 35–40% compared to conventional bricks. At a peak temperature of 40 °C, the 4 cm capsules reduced daily power consumption by 31%, from 130 kWh/day to 90 kWh/day. We conclude that larger PCM–foam capsules offer superior thermal buffering, establishing TSBs as an effective passive solution for enhancing energy efficiency and thermal comfort in hot climates.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64483-y.title: Assessing China’s COVID-19 control measures: a quantitative analysis based on a SIRD model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64483-y.abstract: Abstract This paper established a Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Dead (SIRD) model to fit and predict the COVID-19 epidemic in China. On the premise of passing the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) robustness check, we counterfactually assessed the effectiveness of partial unlocking and vaccination policies. Our key findings are as follows: (1) The SIRD model predicted that China could fully contain COVID-19 in July, 2020, which is consistent with reality; (2) If the strict social distancing policies are relaxed before the epidemic ends, it will lead to a second rebound. Even worse, the rebound increases with the advance of relaxation time and relaxation degree; (3) Timely vaccination is the best strategy if it is available. However, delayed vaccination is much less effective. (4) When further taking natural population growth rates into account, we find that the principal conclusions remain robust. The inclusion of demographic dynamics helps mitigate potential fitting bias resulting from changes in population size over extended epidemic periods like the COVID-19 pandemic. Empirically, the model shows a certain degree of applicability in regions with similar transmission trends.This paper theoretically and quantitatively demonstrates the effectiveness of China's comprehensive prevention and control measures, and empirically verifies that the model has potential reference significance for some regions with similar transmission trends.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69871-y.title: Postoperative survival nomograms integrating preoperative eosinophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and clinicopathological factors in gastric cancer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69871-y.abstract: Survival varies among patients with gastric cancer despite having similar pathological stages. We developed postoperative nomograms integrating routinely available preoperative inflammatory markers with clinicopathological factors while preserving continuous predictor information. All 405 patients from Shandong were used for model development and 1,000-resample bootstrap validation, and 108 patients from Tianjin formed an independent external validation cohort. Cox models for overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) retained age, histological differentiation, nonlinear tumor size, nonlinear lymph-node ratio, and continuous eosinophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (ELR). In this retrospective cohort, higher ELR was inversely associated with the hazard of death (hazard ratio [HR], 0.690; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.546–0.872) and DFS events (HR, 0.720; 95% CI, 0.578–0.898). Fixed-specification bootstrap-corrected C-indices were 0.772 for OS and 0.777 for DFS; external C-indices were 0.767 and 0.756. At 5 years, external areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.847 for OS and 0.817 for DFS, exceeding pathological tumor-node-metastasis (pTNM) values by 0.085 and 0.102, respectively. External calibration showed underestimation of absolute event risk. These findings support the preliminary prognostic value of the nomograms, but recalibration and broader prospective validation are required before clinical use.
