doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69478-3.title: A CD40-Targeted IL-21 fusokine enables rapid generation of human IL-10⁺granzyme B⁺ regulatory B cells
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69478-3.abstract: Regulatory B cells (Bregs) suppress pathogenic immune responses and maintain immune homeostasis, but their rarity and poor ex vivo expandability limit clinical translation as cellular therapeutics. Here, we describe a feeder-free platform for rapid generation of human IL-10⁺Granzyme B⁺ regulatory B cells using a CD40-targeted IL-21 fusion protein (CD40scFv–IL-21) combined with TLR9 activation. Human peripheral blood B cells stimulated with CD40scFv–IL-21 and CpG acquired a distinct CD19⁺CD25⁺CD71⁺CD73low phenotype and robustly expressed IL-10 and granzyme B in more than 95% of input cells. Mechanistically, CD40scFv–IL-21 activated canonical CD40-associated NF-κB and p38 signaling while preserving IL-21–dependent STAT activation. Transcriptomic profiling identified a coordinated regulatory gene program distinct from CpG stimulation alone, including increased expression of IL10, GZMB, CD274, PDCD1LG2, EBI3, PRDM1, and IRF4. Conditioned-media chemokine profiling further supported acquisition of a distinct immunomodulatory secretory phenotype. Functionally, induced Bregs suppressed activated human T-cell proliferation in vitro and significantly prolonged survival in a xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease model. Together, these findings establish a scalable and translationally adaptable strategy for generation of human regulatory B cells for potential application in immune-mediated diseases and cellular immunotherapy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67891-2.title: Impact of oxygen extraction from lunar regolith simulant using fluorinated plasma processes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67891-2.abstract: Abstract Mechanisms whereby measurable quantities of O 2 or CO and CO 2 gases have been extracted from lunar mare simulant (LMS), by treatment with plasma containing either SF 6 or C 4 F 8 , have been investigated using X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) imaging, X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The EDS images show that the SF 6 plasma reacts almost exclusively with the anorthosite component of the LMS. A fluoride layer appears to be formed on the surface of the grains, resulting in strain-broadening of the X-ray diffraction peaks associated with anorthosite and absence of signals from the Si Kα and O Kα channels of the EDS images. No equivalent loss of signal or broadening of the X-ray diffraction lines is found for C 4 F 8 plasma treatment, and reactions are not exclusively with anorthosite. For both plasmas, the mechanisms of oxygen extraction from the LMS are consistent with those deduced for the etching of SiO 2 during semiconductor manufacturing processes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69534-y.title: Fractal dimension analysis of mandibular and cervical regions across hand–wrist maturation stages
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69534-y.abstract: This study evaluated whether fractal dimension (FD) values from mandibular regions and cervical vertebrae on routine panoramic and lateral cephalometric radiographs differ across seven hand–wrist maturation stages in adolescents, using hand–wrist staging as the reference standard, and whether these values are associated with maturation stage and sex. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 105 adolescents aged 8–17 years with hand–wrist, panoramic, and lateral cephalometric radiographs taken on the same day. FD values were calculated from six 40 × 40-pixel regions of interest using a standardized ImageJ box-counting method. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients, and correlations and group comparisons were performed with Holm correction for multiple testing across the six anatomical regions. After Holm correction, hand–wrist maturation stage showed significant positive correlations with FD at the mandibular symphysis, second cervical vertebra (C2), and third cervical vertebra (C3). Significant stage-related differences remained for the mandibular symphysis and C2, whereas no significant sex-related differences remained after multiple-testing correction. In multivariable analyses adjusted for age and sex, maturation stage remained significantly associated with FD at the mandibular symphysis and C2. These findings suggest that FD at the mandibular symphysis and C2 may reflect maturation-related trabecular changes; however, their clinical and diagnostic utility requires further validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64728-w.title: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of first-line EGFR-TKI-based combination strategies for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer with brain metastases
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64728-w.abstract: Brain metastases are common in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and remain clinically challenging despite the improved central nervous system activity of third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs). Because direct comparisons between active first-line combination strategies are limited, this systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) evaluated the relative efficacy and safety of EGFR-TKI-based combinations in this population. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to December 31, 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized comparative studies were eligible if they enrolled patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and brain metastases and compared EGFR-TKI monotherapy with EGFR-TKI-based combinations incorporating chemotherapy, anti-angiogenic therapy, radiotherapy, or bispecific antibody therapy. Bayesian NMAs were performed for overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and intracranial PFS (iPFS). RCT-only analyses were conducted as robustness assessments. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were summarized descriptively. Forty-eight studies involving 5,432 patients were included, of which 17 were RCTs. In the overall network, EGFR-TKI plus anti-angiogenic therapy showed the most favorable OS estimate versus monotherapy (HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.49–0.80), whereas EGFR-TKI plus chemotherapy showed the most favorable estimates for PFS (HR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.44–0.61) and iPFS (HR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.25–0.52). RCT-only analyses most consistently supported the PFS benefit of EGFR-TKI plus chemotherapy; OS rankings were less definitive, and randomized iPFS evidence remained sparse. Radiotherapy-related results were exploratory because the radiotherapy node pooled WBRT, SRS/SRT, mixed approaches, and variable dose-fractionation schedules. EGFR-TKI plus chemotherapy showed the most consistent evidence for delaying progression. The apparent OS advantage of EGFR-TKI plus anti-angiogenic therapy, and findings for radiotherapy- and bispecific antibody-based combinations, should be interpreted cautiously. Treatment selection should be individualized according to treatment goals, EGFR-TKI generation, intracranial disease burden, expected toxicity, and patient tolerability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69504-4.title: Spatial variation in self-reported arthritis/rheumatism among middle-aged and older Chinese adults: an exploratory CHARLS ecological analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69504-4.abstract: Arthritis and rheumatic conditions represent a major source of disability among middle-aged and older adults worldwide. Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), a nationally representative cohort of middle-aged and older Chinese adults, this secondary analysis explored the spatial distribution of self-reported arthritis/rheumatism and its ecological associations with environmental exposure indicators across China. This secondary ecological analysis was conducted using data from the CHARLS. A total of 25,390 participants aged ≥ 45 years were included. Data collected included self-reported arthritis/rheumatism, provincial environmental indicators, and partial dietary data. Multivariate linear regression was used to analyze linear associations between environmental indicators and provincial prevalence of self-reported arthritis/rheumatism. Exploratory chi-square tests were subsequently conducted to compare environmental indicators across prevalence categories. The prevalence of self-reported arthritis/rheumatism in the cohort was 33%, exceeding that of hypertension (30%) and digestive system diseases (23%). The crude proportion of participants reporting physician-diagnosed arthritis/rheumatism ranged from 16% in Zhejiang to 59% in Chongqing. In the primary multivariable analysis, none of the provincial environmental or dietary indicators showed significant linear associations with arthritis/rheumatism prevalence after adjustment for provincial age and sex composition. Exploratory ecological analyses identified differences in the categorical distributions of ozone concentration (O3-8 H-90per), electrical conductivity, permanganate index, ammonia nitrogen, and total nitrogen across provincial prevalence categories. In descriptive comparisons, provinces with lower arthritis/rheumatism prevalence exhibited higher ambient ozone concentrations than high-prevalence provinces, whereas the remaining environmental differences should be considered exploratory. This secondary ecological analysis demonstrated substantial geographic variation in the prevalence of self-reported arthritis/rheumatism across mainland China. Although the primary multivariable analyses did not identify significant linear associations between provincial environmental indicators and arthritis/rheumatism prevalence, exploratory ecological analyses identified several regional environmental patterns that warrant further investigation. Given the ecological design and the potential for ecological fallacy, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of causal environmental effects.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67983-z.title: Supportive care needs among patients with breast and cervical cancer at a tertiary cancer treatment center in ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67983-z.abstract: Abstract The rising incidence of cancer diagnoses alongside improving survival rates in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) has substantially increased the demand for comprehensive supportive care. This study aimed to assess the supportive care needs of patients diagnosed with breast or cervical cancer at Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital Cancer Treatment Center, Ethiopia. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 349 patients with breast or cervical cancer between December 2023 and May 2024. Data were collected using three validated instruments: the Supportive Care Needs Survey Short Form (SCNS-SF34), the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy – Spiritual Well-Being scale (FACIT-Sp-12), and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30). All instruments were scored according to their respective guidelines. Multivariable linear regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with supportive care needs. Patients were relatively young, with a mean age of 42.5 ± 12 years for breast cancer and 49.5 ± 12 years for cervical cancer. The majority reported cancer-related symptoms, and nearly all patients indicated unmet supportive care needs in at least one domain. Greater supportive care needs were significantly associated with the use of traditional or spiritual healing practices (mean difference [MD] 9.15, 95% CI: 3.51–14.59), lower functional performance status (MD 5.53, 95% CI: 3.11–7.96), higher number of children (MD 1.95, 95% CI: 0.90–3.01), and higher educational attainment (MD 2.58, 95% CI: 1.22–3.94). Conversely, having health insurance was associated with significantly lower supportive care needs (MD − 3.78, 95% CI: −7.36 to − 0.19). Unmet supportive care needs were prevalent across all assessed domains: physical and daily living, psychological, sexual health, patient care, and health information underscoring a substantial gap in comprehensive cancer care in this setting. To address these needs, healthcare systems should prioritize patient-provider communication, strengthen social support networks for high-need patients, integrate spiritual well-being into care planning, and develop context-sensitive, multidisciplinary supportive care strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68495-6.title: SHH-functionalized fibrin scaffold improves spinal cord repair in rats and modulates primary neural stem cell behavior in vitro
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68495-6.abstract: The sustained delivery of regenerative cues within the injured spinal cord microenvironment represents a promising strategy for promoting spinal cord injury (SCI) repair. In this study, we developed a fibrin-based scaffold functionalized through the polydopamine (PD)-mediated immobilization of sonic hedgehog (SHH), designated FG/PD@SHH, to achieve localized and sustained SHH delivery. The PD modification increased the SHH loading efficiency from 51.2% to 70.6%, increased the immobilization efficiency from 24.7% to 59.5%, and increased the retention of SHH from 246.6 ± 76.1 to 595.0 ± 8.9 ng per scaffold. The FG/SHH scaffold released 95.3% of the SHH within 3 days, whereas the FG/PD@SHH scaffold released 43.9% by Day 3 and 95.1% by Day 14. In vitro, primary NSCs cultured on FG/PD@SHH scaffolds exhibited enhanced cell–scaffold interactions, increased expression of adhesion- and proliferation-associated genes, increased expression of the neuronal markers growth-associated protein 43 (GAP-43) and class III β-tubulin (TUBB3), and reduced expression of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). The increased expression of proteins related to the canonical SHH pathway indicated that scaffold-presented SHH retained biological activity. In a rat model of complete spinal cord transection, FG/PD@SHH scaffold implantation improved Basso–Beattie–Bresnahan (BBB) locomotor scores from Day 28 onward. At 12 weeks, the lesion cavity area decreased from 59.6 ± 6.5% in the FG group and 45.7 ± 7.1% in the FG/SHH group to 31.6 ± 5.8% in the FG/PD@SHH group. The mean Nissl-positive cell count increased from 6.8 ± 1.1 in the FG group and 11.7 ± 2.3 in the FG/SHH group to 18.7 ± 3.9 in the FG/PD@SHH group. These findings suggest that the FG/PD@SHH scaffold provides sustained SHH delivery and supports neural tissue repair after SCI.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69675-0.title: A data driven hybrid cnn lstm framework for accurate prediction and energy optimization in microgrids
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69675-0.abstract: This paper presents an intelligent data driven method for microgrid energy management using state of the art Deep Learning (DL) models to predict critical control variables like duty cycle, inverter modulation index, reactive power setpoint and DC link voltage. The framework consists of Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN1D) and a hybrid CNN-LSTM network to capture the nonlinear and spatio-temporal characteristics of renewable energy systems. A comprehensive correlation analysis reveals significant relationships between variables, enabling effective modeling of renewable energy generation and storage dynamics. Training outcomes show fast convergence, low mean squared error and low variance for all models, with the hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture showing better stability and generalisation abilities. The evaluated models achieved comparable prediction accuracy, with average R 2 values close to 0.94. The CNN-LSTM model showed stable multi-output prediction behaviour, while the LSTM model achieved slightly better aggregate numerical metrics. Residual and error distribution tests are also performed to find the stability and accuracy of the models. For the microgrid configuration and energy-flow scenario studied, the prediction-assisted dispatch achieves 86.7% renewable penetration and a 90.2% reduction in grid import relative to a fully grid-supplied baseline, corresponding to an approximately 27% improvement in energy saving over a conventional non-predictive rule-based controller applied to the same system. These indicators characterise the studied configuration and sizing rather than establishing the predictive accuracy of the models. The strong negative correlation between renewable energy generation and grid dependency shows the system’s capacity to improve sustainability and reduce grid dependence. In summary, the framework provides a computationally feasible supervisory prediction layer for microgrid energy management. Establishing operational improvement in a deployed system will require closed-loop and hardware-in-the-loop validation, which is identified as future work.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69159-1.title: Latent profile analysis of benefit finding in maintenance hemodialysis patients and its association with treatment adherence
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69159-1.abstract: Abstract Maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients experience prominent negative emotions, and dialysis outcomes/prognosis rely heavily on treatment adherence. Few studies have explored the relationship between latent Benefit Finding (BF) categories and adherence. This study aims to identify BF’s latent characteristics in MHD patients and analyze their link to adherence for targeted interventions. From Oct. 2024 to Mar. 2025, 250 MHD patients were convenience-sampled from 2 tertiary hospitals in Guangzhou. Measurement tools included a General Information Questionnaire, a Benefit Finding Scale, and a Treatment Adherence Scale for MHD Patients with End-Stage Renal Disease. Latent profile analysis, multivariate logistic regression, and one-way ANOVA were used. MHD patients had a mean BF score of (55.36 ± 14.65), with three BF categories: Low benefit-perceived lacking (20.4%), Medium benefit-balanced adaptive (59.6%), and High benefit-personal growth dominant (20%). Literacy, occupational status, and renal transplantation experience influenced patients’ BF categories ( P < 0.05). BF correlated positively with adherence ( r = 0.327, P < 0.001), and adherence scores differed statistically by BF categories ( P < 0.05).MHD patients’ BF has three latent profiles. Clinical staff should design targeted interventions based on BF characteristics to improve adherence.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67088-7.title: Efficacy of a self-guided online resilience intervention for improving mental health among university students: A randomized controlled trial
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67088-7.abstract: Abstract Epidemiological data indicates that university students are an at-risk population for the development of mental disorders. Online interventions have been proposed as promising tools for reducing barriers to treatment and establishing easily accessible health-care services promoting mental health and resilience. This study investigated the efficacy of a Learning Management System (LMS)-based self-guided online resilience intervention. 216 university students took part in a randomized controlled trial with an intervention and a waitlist control group and three measurement points (pre, post and follow-up). We conducted per-protocol (PP) and intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses with mental distress as primary outcome, and self-reported resilience and resilience factors as secondary outcomes. Further, attitudes towards online interventions, adherence, satisfaction and possible negative effects were explored. Satisfaction with the intervention was high and PP analyses ( n = 150) revealed significant improvements in mental distress and self-compassion at post-test and acceptance at follow-up. No favourable effects were found for self-reported resilience and resilience factors. Adherence was low and ITT analyses revealed no significant effects. Overall, the study provides preliminary evidence for the LMS-based self-guided online intervention as a potentially valuable tool for university mental health services under optimal adherence conditions. Further research into determinants of adherence is needed to improve intervention reach.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69641-w.title: Associations between parental marital conflict and short-video addiction among Chinese adolescents: a cross-sectional chain mediation analysis of experiential avoidance and anxiety
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69641-w.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the association between parental marital conflict and short-video addiction among adolescents and assessed indirect associations involving experiential avoidance and anxiety. The Children’s Perception of Interparental Conflict Scale, Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-II, Generalized Anxiety Disorder-2 Scale, and Short-Video Addiction Scale were administered to 4,065 adolescents from six schools across five provinces in China. PROCESS Model 6 and 5,000 bootstrap resamples were used to test the mediation effects. (1) Parental marital conflict, experiential avoidance, anxiety, and short-video addiction were significantly and positively correlated with one another (r = 0.280 – 0.553, p < 0.001). (2) The direct association between parental marital conflict and adolescent short-video addiction remained significant after the mediators were included in the model (β = 0.088, p < 0.001). (3) Experiential avoidance and anxiety independently mediated the association between parental marital conflict and short-video addiction and also formed a significant chain mediation pathway through experiential avoidance followed by anxiety. The total indirect effect accounted for 67.16% of the total effect. The results indicate that parental marital conflict was associated with short-video addiction both directly and indirectly through experiential avoidance, anxiety, and the prespecified chain pathway from experiential avoidance to anxiety. The findings broaden the evidence on family and emotional correlates of short-video addiction and highlight the relevance of supportive family relationships, emotion-regulation skills, media literacy, and adolescent psychological well-being.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54702-x.title: Improving Fairness in Doubly Imbalanced Datasets
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54702-x.abstract: Fairness has been identified as an important aspect of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence solutions for decision making. Recent literature offers a variety of approaches for debiasing, however many of them fall short when the data collection is imbalanced. In this paper, we focus on a particular case, fairness in doubly imbalanced datasets, such that the data collection is imbalanced both for the label and the groups in the sensitive attribute. Firstly, we present an exploratory analysis to illustrate limitations in debiasing on a doubly imbalanced dataset. Then, a multi-criteria based solution is proposed for finding the most suitable sampling and distribution for the label and the sensitive attribute, in terms of fairness and classification accuracy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69352-2.title: Sleep-stage dynamics predict current sleep-disordered breathing and future cardiovascular risk
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69352-2.abstract: Abstract Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is a major contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and disrupts both the macrostructure and dynamics of sleep stages (W, N1, N2, N3, REM). While specific alterations in sleep macrostructure, such as reduced durations of N3 and REM, have been linked to cardiovascular risk, the predictive value of sleep-stage dynamics remains unexplored. Using data from the prospective Sleep Heart Health Study, we applied a flexible forest-based modelling approach to a carefully selected cohort of 2579 subjects free from prior cardiovascular events and sleep-altering medications to minimize confounding. First, we demonstrate that a random forest classifier reliably identifies moderate-to-severe SDB (apnea–hypopnea index; AHI >15), from sleep-stage architecture, dynamics, and common risk factors (demographics, BMI, smoking status) alone, achieving an AUROC of 76.1% without access to direct respiratory measurements. This highlights a dependency chain in which SDB correlates with altered sleep patterns that, in turn, encode a signature of cardiovascular risk. Second, a random survival forest (RSF) robustly predicted future cardiovascular events (concordance-index=73.3%) over >10 years of follow-up. Comparable results with and without including AHI as a predictor indicate that sleep patterns retain cardiovascular prognostic information even without direct SDB measurement. When evaluated against established Framingham risk scores, RSF predictions showed comparable discriminative power and improved 10-year calibration in the primary cohort, with mean predicted 10-year risk differing from the observed event rate by less than 1%. Partial dependence analyses revealed monotonic SDB risk profiles and predominantly U-shaped associations for cardiovascular risk, identifying ranges of total sleep time, wake after sleep onset, and REM/N3 continuity linked to minimal or elevated risk. Notably, rare transitions such as N3 $$\rightarrow $$ N1 or REM $$\rightarrow $$ N3, even occurring once per night, emerged as sensitive markers of cardiovascular vulnerability, increasing risk by up to 10%. Our findings extend prior evidence on linear associations between sleep macrostructure and cardiovascular outcomes, revealing non-linear patterns and positioning sleep dynamics as promising non-invasive biomarkers for diagnostics and early risk stratification.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69280-1.title: Quantitative longitudinal analysis of temporal changes in retinal vessel density and optic nerve head blood flow after optic nerve crush
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69280-1.abstract: Glaucoma is associated with ocular blood flow (BF) dysfunction; however, temporal BF changes following neurodegeneration remain poorly understood. We investigated the temporal relationship among these pathological processes using a mouse optic nerve crush (ONC) model. Outcomes included fundus fluorescein angiography (FA) and laser speckle flowgraphy at baseline and days 4, 7, 14, and 28 after ONC; retinal vessel density (VD), quantified from FA; ocular BF, assessed using optic nerve head (ONH) vessel-area mean blur rate (ONH-MV); and retinal and optic nerve gene expression, evaluated by quantitative PCR. After ONC, VD significantly decreased on days 4 through 28 (P < 0.001). Retinal VD reduction coincided with increased retinal expression of inflammatory mediators (Il6 and Tnf), glial activation markers (Edn2, Tspo, and Gfap), and the necroptosis-related gene Ripk3 on day 4 (P < 0.05). ONH-MV showed a nonsignificant reduction on day 4 (P > 0.05), reaching significance on days 7 through 28 (P < 0.01). ONH-MV reduction coincided with increased expression of genes associated with glial activation and A1 astrocyte-related responses (Tnf, Tspo, C1qa, Gbp2, and Serping1; P < 0.05) on day 28. This suggests that reduced retinal VD and reduced ONH BF after neuronal injury coincide with inflammatory and glial responses in the retina and glial activation in the optic nerve.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69334-4.title: Actor–partner effects of irrational beliefs on marital adjustment in healthy and chronically diseased couples
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69334-4.abstract: Although marital adjustment is inherently a dyadic process, and stressors such as chronic illness can be associated with couple functioning, limited research has examined how irrational beliefs are associated with marital adjustment from a dyadic perspective. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the actor and partner effects of irrational beliefs on marital adjustment between healthy couples and couples living with chronic illness. This cross-sectional dyadic path analysis was conducted in 2022 on 92 couples with common chronic illness and 92 matched healthy couples in Bushehr, Iran. Participants were selected through convenience sampling. Data were collected using a demographic form, the Short Iranian Version of the Jones Irrational Beliefs Questionnaire, and the Dyadic Adjustment Scale. Data were analyzed using SPSS 19 and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in Smart PLS 3. Results showed that in both groups, men’s irrational beliefs were significantly associated with their own marital adjustment (actor effect) (total effect = − 0.641; P < 0.001 for healthy couples, compared to total effect = − 0.445; P < 0.001 for couples living with chronic illness), whereas this association was not significant for women (P > 0.05). Moreover, husbands’ irrational beliefs were positively related to their wives’ irrational beliefs (total effect = 0.487; P < 0.001 for healthy couples, compared to total effect = 0.665; P < 0.001 for couples living with chronic illness), and husbands’ marital adjustment was linked to their wives’ marital adjustment (total effect = 0.739; P < 0.001 for healthy couples, compared to total effect = 0.911; P < 0.001 for patient couples), indicating meaningful cross-partner effects. Most of these interrelations were stronger among couples living with chronic illness. These findings underscore the importance of examining marital adjustment from a dyadic rather than an individual perspective. They also suggest that assessing and addressing irrational beliefs within both partners may be beneficial for promoting marital adjustment, although this possibility requires evaluation in future intervention studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66838-x.title: An optimized tankyrase inhibitor with enhanced anticancer efficacy and safety for APC-mutant colorectal cancer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66838-x.abstract: Tankyrase (TNKS) plays an essential role in Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Despite its potential as a therapeutic target in colorectal cancer (CRC) harboring adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) mutations, the clinical use of TNKS inhibitors is limited by intestinal toxicity and insufficient efficacy. Therefore, this study aimed to design and synthesize novel tetrahydrophthalazine-based TNKS inhibitors and evaluate their therapeutic potential in APC-mutant CRC. We identified and optimized a novel TNKS1/2 inhibitor (TI-61987) based on a tetrahydrophthalazine scaffold and assessed its inhibitory activity against TNKS1 and TNKS2. Effects on β-catenin signaling were assessed via immunoblotting, and antitumor efficacy was evaluated in APC-mutant CRC cell lines and a COLO320DM xenograft mouse model. Combination treatments with 5-fluorouracil or a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase inhibitor were also investigated. TI-61987 potently inhibited TNKS1 and TNKS2 by stabilizing AXIN2 and reducing active β-catenin levels. TI-61987 substantially suppressed tumor cell proliferation in vitro and tumor growth in vivo without inducing apparent intestinal toxicity. Combination therapies further enhanced efficacy and overcame resistance in resistant CRC cells. Overall, TI-61987 is a novel and potent TNKS1/2 inhibitor with notable antitumor activity. Thus, TI-61987 is a promising therapeutic candidate for APC-mutant CRC, both alone and in combination treatments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67950-8.title: Diversity in agro-morphological and phytochemical traits with comparative leaf trichome observations among Iranian common nettle (Urtica dioica L.) populations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67950-8.abstract: Phenotypic diversity within medicinal plants is crucial for identifying elite genotypes and supporting sustainable cultivation and breeding strategies. Urtica dioica L. (common nettle) is a widely distributed perennial species with high concentrations of bioactive compounds, making it an important target for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic industries. In this study, eight Iranian U. dioica populations ( UDP1 – UDP8 ), cultivated under controlled greenhouse conditions, were assessed for their agro-morphological characteristics, phytochemical profiles, antioxidant power, and trichome micromorphology. Significant variability was observed across UDPs in plant height, shoot and root biomass, and biomass allocation patterns. UDP7 demonstrated the highest shoot biomass, whereas UDP4 and UDP2 outperformed in root development. Phytochemical analysis revealed considerable differences in specialized metabolites content among UDPs. UDP4 exhibited the highest levels of total phenolics (4.93 mg gallic acid equivalent/g DW), flavonoids (46.50 mg rutin equivalent/g DW), and antioxidant power (22.60 μmol Fe 2+ /g DW). HPLC profiling identified chlorogenic acid, caffeoylmalic acid, and rutin as key compounds, with UDP5 containing the highest chlorogenic acid and rutin levels, and UDP8 the highest caffeoylmalic acid content. Scanning electron microscopy revealed notable diversity in trichome density, length, and distribution patterns. These findings highlight the rich agro-morphological and phytochemical diversity among native Iranian UDPs and suggest that UDP7 , followed by UDP1 , is particularly promising for biomass production, whereas UDP4 showed superior overall phytochemical and antioxidant potential, and UDP5 and UDP8 represent valuable sources of specific phenolic compounds for future domestication, breeding, and phytopharmaceutical applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69085-2.title: Development of efficient finite population mean estimators using transformed auxiliary variables and hierarchical clustering-based stratification
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69085-2.abstract: Abstract Efficient estimation of a finite population mean depends on both estimator formulation and the quality of the strata. This study develops three classes of mean estimators under stratified simple random sampling without replacement by integrating transformed auxiliary information with data-driven stratification. Auxiliary information available for all population units is first used to construct pre-sampling strata through Ward’s hierarchical clustering, thereby reducing dependence on subjective stratification. Seven transformations of the auxiliary variable are represented through common transformation factors and incorporated into optimized ratio-, product-, and exponential-type estimator structures. First-order expressions for bias and mean squared error (MSE), optimum constants, minimum MSEs, and efficiency conditions are derived. Performance is evaluated using five empirical populations and a Monte Carlo simulation covering small, medium, and large sample sizes (n = 50, 150, and 300) under low, moderate, and high correlation levels. Efficiency is measured through percentage relative efficiency (PRE), while the repeated-sampling behavior of bias and MSE across sample sizes and correlation levels is used to assess empirical stability and consistency. In the examined settings, the proposed estimators generally yield smaller MSEs and higher PREs than the competing estimators, with larger gains under stronger correlation and more homogeneous data-driven strata. These findings support the combined contribution of transformed auxiliary information and objective pre-sampling stratification, while remaining conditional on reliable frame-level auxiliary information, appropriate clustering choices, and stable estimation of the optimum constants.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68818-7.title: A metal-dielectric photonic crystal-based glucose sensor with sensitivity enhancement by using 2D materials
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68818-7.abstract: Abstract Metal-dielectric photonic crystals (MDPhCs) that support the excitation of Bloch-like surface waves (BLSWs) at the interface of an MDPhC and the adjacent medium (analyte) have emerged as a very promising alternative for sensing gaseous analytes with high sensitivity. In this theoretical paper we report on an extension of the concept for glucose sensing when the BLSW-based resonances in the Kretschmann configuration are accompanied by narrow dips and are characterized by ultra-high sensitivities. Moreover, one of the possible solutions to enhance the sensitivity represents an MDPhC with a 2D material overlayer, such as black phosphorus or molybdenum disulfide (MoS $$_2$$ ). For an MDPhC comprising two bilayers of TiO $$_2$$ /Au with a termination layer of TiO $$_2$$ , we demonstrate that the BLSW-based resonances are resolved for TE waves when simulated glucose solutions are considered, and the glucose analyte refractive index (RI) is in a range of 1.32797–1.32867 at a wavelength of 1.55 $$\mu$$ m, corresponding to physiologically relevant glucose concentrations of 0–500 mg/dL. Using the wavelength interrogation, an RI sensitivity of 19.9 $$\mu$$ m/RI unit (RIU), a figure of merit (FOM) of 1047 RIU $$^{-1}$$ , and a limit of detection (LOD) of 5.0 $$\times$$ 10 $$^{-6}$$ RIU, respectively, were attained. The analysis extended to one monolayer of black phosphorus or MoS $$_2$$ on the MDPhC revealed that the RI sensitivity is increased up to 26.9 $$\mu$$ m/RIU for MoS $$_2$$ , the FOM reached 1076 RIU $$^{-1}$$ , and the LOD is as low as 3.7 $$\times$$ 10 $$^{-6}$$ RIU, or equivalently in the glucose concentration domain, the sensitivity is up to 0.0379 nm/(mg/dL), and the LOD is lowered to 2.6 mg/dL. This research is the demonstration of exceptional properties of the BLSW-based sensors employing MDPhCs whose sensitivity can be enhanced by using 2D materials. Such sensors are potentially well suited to a variety of biosensing applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68242-x.title: Microdroplet-based high-throughput screening for antagonistic bacteria targeting penaeid shrimp pathogenic Vibrio harveyi
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68242-x.abstract: Antagonistic bacteria that suppress the growth of specific bacteria have attracted attention as an antibiotics-independent strategy for infectious disease control in aquaculture. Microfluidics-based water-in-oil droplets (microdroplets) enable high-throughput screening of antagonistic bacteria in the field of medicine or agriculture. However, the use of this screening system in aquaculture has not yet been reported. In particular, penaeid shrimp aquaculture, one of the largest sectors of global aquaculture, has a strong demand for alternative disease control strategies because vaccination is ineffective. Here, we demonstrated a proof-of-concept study of microdroplet-based high-throughput screening system for antagonistic bacteria targeting penaeid shrimp pathogenic Vibrio harveyi. Using this screening system, we successfully isolated 18 bacterial candidates with potential growth-inhibitory activity, representing three genera (Pseudoalteromonas, Shewanella, and Tenacibaculum), from the bacterial community of kuruma shrimp Penaeus japonicus rearing water. 16S rRNA gene-based bacterial community analysis revealed that these isolates included several low-abundance, rare taxa. Although these isolates showed no inhibitory activity on agar plates, one out of four tested strains showed a trend toward improved survival during co-infection tests using kuruma shrimp. Overall, our study highlights both the potential and limitation of microdroplet-based antagonistic bacterial screening to accelerate the development of biological control strategies in shrimp aquaculture.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69113-1.title: Surgical and cement-related factors associated with symptomatic adjacent vertebral fractures after percutaneous kyphoplasty for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures: a single-center retrospective nomogram study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69113-1.abstract: Abstract Symptomatic adjacent vertebral fracture (AVF) can occur after treatment with percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP) for osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture (OVCF). This study examined surgical and cement-related factors associated with symptomatic AVF after PKP and developed an exploratory nomogram for postoperative risk stratification. We retrospectively analysed consecutive patients with OVCF who underwent PKP between January 2016 and June 2023 and completed 2-year follow-up. Baseline information, operative data, imaging variables, and laboratory findings were collected. Symptomatic AVF was defined as a new adjacent vertebral fracture confirmed by MRI after recurrent localised back pain during follow-up. Patients were categorised into AVF and non-AVF groups according to imaging-confirmed symptomatic AVF. Key variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and a nomogram was constructed. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, respectively. In total, 463 patients were included, comprising 132 patients with symptomatic AVF and 331 without symptomatic AVF. Cement leakage, lower postoperative height restoration, smaller preoperative Cobb angle, cement diffusion quality, and endplate fracture were retained by LASSO regression and included in the final model. Good cement diffusion was associated with a lower AVF risk, whereas cement leakage and endplate fracture were associated with a higher AVF risk. The model showed high apparent discrimination in the internal training and validation cohorts. Five surgical and cement-related factors were associated with symptomatic AVF after PKP in this single-centre retrospective cohort. The internally assessed nomogram may support exploratory postoperative risk stratification and may assist clinicians in identifying patients who could benefit from closer postoperative assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68403-y.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses elucidates the role of NUPR1 in tumour microenvironment and cancer development
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68403-y.abstract: Nuclear protein 1 (NUPR1), a multifunctional stress-inducible transcription factor, has emerged as a potential target for cancer treatment. However, a comprehensive exploration of NUPR1 across the pan-cancer landscape is still lacking. In this study, we utilized multi-omics data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Genotype Tissue Expression (GTEx) databases to assess the expression, prognostic significance, genomic features, and immunological characteristics of NUPR1 in 33 cancer types. Significant dysregulation of NUPR1 was observed in multiple cancers, where its expression also demonstrated prognostic relevance in several cancer types. Mechanistically, NUPR1 was found to correlate with genomic instability, DNA methylation, tumor-infiltrating immune cells, DNA repair, and apoptosis across various cancers. To investigate the role of NUPR1 in the tumor microenvironment (TME), we analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data, revealing that NUPR1 was predominantly expressed in epithelial cells and macrophages, but not in lymphoid cells, dendritic cells, or mast cells across six cancer types. In BRCA, NUPR1 expression was associated with epithelial cell stemness, and high NUPR1 expression in epithelial cells and macrophages correlated with poorer prognosis. Furthermore, NUPR1 was identified as a potential biomarker for drug sensitivity and as a risk factor in BRCA. Inactivation of NUPR1 by ZZW-115 in BRCA cells resulted in anticancer and radiosensitizing effects, including suppressed migration, proliferation, invasion and mammosphere formation, promotion of macrophage M1 polarization and inhibition of M2 polarization, as well as enhanced irradiation-induced apoptosis, DNA damage and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68978-6.title: Empirical analysis of algorithmic components for improved performance in a baseline genetic algorithm selection hyper-heuristic
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68978-6.abstract: Selection hyper-heuristics represent high-level search algorithms that dynamically select and apply lower-level heuristics to solve various optimization problems. They encompass numerous algorithmic components such as heuristic selection, move acceptance, feedback, and parameter setting. Each of these components offers multiple implementation methods, which creates challenges for algorithm designers who must decide on the most suitable approach for their algorithms. The issue is aggravated by the absence of a definitive best method for these components. Furthermore, there is a lack of a comprehensive empirical study on the efficacy of the implementation methods of these components, where most previous studies focus on heuristic selection and move acceptance. This paper addresses this gap by presenting a comprehensive empirical analysis of seven key selection hyper-heuristic components, including search points, search phases, move acceptance, feedback, Tabu mechanism, restart mechanism, and low-level heuristic parameters, in the context of population-based Genetic Algorithm Hyper-heuristic (GAHH). Implementation methods for these components were derived from 53 algorithms implemented using the HyFlex framework, notably the 20 finalist entries in the Cross-Domain Heuristic Search Challenge 2011. An analytical method is employed to compare their performance and identify the most effective implementation method within the evaluated settings. The analysis indicated that multi-point search, iterated search phases, non-stochastic threshold move acceptance, no learning from search feedback, Tabu mechanism with visited solutions, threshold restart mechanism, and adaptive parameter control as the best-performing strategies for GAHH across a limited set of 12 HyFlex tuning instances. Notably, the performance of the no-learning approach is influenced by genetic algorithm’s evolutionary operators. The results provide valuable insights that serve as a solid foundation for future algorithm development and increase the understanding of selection hyper-heuristic components, specifically in GAHH.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69103-3.title: Multivariate synthesis optimization, comprehensive characterization, and surface ligand determination of palladium nanoparticles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69103-3.abstract: Abstract We present a high-throughput approach for synthesizing palladium nanoparticles (PdNPs), which are widely used as catalysts in industrial processes, employing an aqueous reaction medium and a commercial reaction platform that enables parallel reactions under identical conditions. The optimal synthesis conditions, including reaction temperature and the concentrations of Pd, thiol ligands (3-mercaptopropionic acid (MPA) and L-cysteine (Cys)), and reducing agent, were established using a Doehlert experimental design. The purified thiol-capped PdNPs were characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), confirming the formation of irregularly shaped PdNP-MPA and PdNP-Cys with polydispersity indices up to 0.270. Single particle-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (sp-ICP-MS) enabled determination of particle size and size distribution, demonstrating its suitability for characterizing polydisperse nanoparticles with irregular shapes and yielding results consistent with those obtained by TEM and NTA. Bulk ICP-MS was employed to determine the surface density of thiol ligands from the sulfur-to-palladium ratio. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of multivariate experimental design for PdNP synthesis and the value of complementary analytical techniques for comprehensive nanoparticle characterization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69845-0.title: Adaptive load frequency control for hydrogen integrated power networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69845-0.abstract: Expansion in renewable energy resources and transitioning to low-carbon power systems lead to advanced frequency control methods that include efficient, stable, and sustainable platforms. This work proposes Hydrogen-integrated Adaptive Load Frequency Control (ALFC) for operation both on-grid and islanded power systems. It integrates hydrogen fuel cells, electrolyzers, and H2EV aggregators for a single adaptive control structure to enhance dynamic frequency regulation and optimize resource utilization of hydrogen. A linearized state-space model is formulated for system stability, under which pole-dominance is explored through eigenvalue analysis. All dominant poles are in the left half of the complex plane, meaning that it is asymptotically stable under both modes. Lyapunov is further applied, acknowledging global asymptotic and Bounded Input Bounded Output Stability (BIBO) for nonlinear stability. Experimental performance validation revealed significant enhancement relative to classical LFC systems, with respective 59%, 61%, and 51% reductions in ITAE, ISE, and RMSE. This suggests a quick settling time and minimizes oscillating behaviors. Sensitivity analysis is conducted for uncertainties in the parameters with respect to governor dynamics, fuel cell gain variability in the hydrogen source, EV participation fluctuations, and load disturbances to guarantee its robust control performance without any stability degradation. Energy utilization efficiency is close to 84% in the two modes of operation and looks even more promising with a decrease in hydrogen scheduling of almost 23%. These results prove the robust as well as efficiency impacts of ALFC integrated with hydrogen, thus improving the stability characterized by enhancing frequency stability, robustness, and hydrogen optimization for sustainable grid operation. Therefore, it is a promising adaptive solution to future renewable-dominated smart-power systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68612-5.title: Lithium adipic acid modified multiwalled carbon nanotube reinforced PVA hydrogels with enhanced multifunctional properties
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68612-5.abstract: Poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)-based hydrogels have attracted considerable interest for flexible electronics, wearable devices, and soft energy storage systems owing to their excellent bio-compatibility and water-retention capability. However, their practical applications are limited by poor mechanical strength, inadequate electrical performance, and the agglomeration of carbon nanotubes within the polymer matrix. To address these challenges, PVA-based composite hydrogels reinforced with mono-lithium adipate (Li-AA) modified multi-walled carbon nanotubes (m-MWCNTs) (0.025–0.125 wt%) were successfully fabricated using a simple anti-freeze–thaw-free physical cross-linking strategy. Functionalization with lithium-adipate (Li-AA) effectively reduced nanotube agglomeration and improved interfacial compatibility with the PVA matrix, as confirmed by optical microscopy, TEM, and SEM analyses. DSC studies revealed enhanced crystallization behaviour, while FTIR and Raman spectroscopy confirmed strong inter-molecular hydrogen bonding between PVA and m-MWCNTs. Rheological studies demonstrated the formation of a robust solid-like visco-elastic network with a high storage modulus (~ 2 MPa), and nanoindentation results showed significant improvements in hardness and elastic modulus. Broadband dielectric spectroscopy further revealed enhanced dielectric properties and restricted polymer chain mobility. Overall, Li-AA functionalization promoted uniform nanotube dispersion, strong interfacial interactions, and efficient network formation, resulting in simultaneous enhancement of the thermal, mechanical, and electrical properties of PVA hydrogels. The developed composite hydrogel exhibits significant potential for advanced flexible electronics and soft energy storage applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69760-4.title: Longitudinal associations of habitual and within-person protein intake with BMI in Chinese adults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69760-4.abstract: Abstract China has undergone rapid nutrition and urbanization transitions, yet the longitudinal association between dietary protein composition and body mass index (BMI) remains unclear. The analysis included 62,980 observations from 22,634 adults participating in seven China Health and Nutrition Survey waves (1993–2011). Three-level nutrient-density models distinguished habitual between-person intake from within-person deviations. BMI was 0.361 kg/m 2 higher for each 5-percentage-point increase in habitual protein share of energy (95% CI 0.275, 0.447; p < 0.001), while the within-person estimate was not statistically significant in the primary nutrient-density model ( β = 0.028, 95% CI − 0.003, 0.059; p = 0.090). The between-person association was stronger in men ( β = 0.618) than women ( β = 0.148; interaction p < 0.001) and varied across provinces and long-term urbanization contexts (both p < 0.001). Alternative nutrient-density and energy-residual models retained the positive between-person association. Within-person estimates remained non-significant in the primary and alternative nutrient-density models, whereas the small association observed in the energy-residual analysis was sensitive to the inclusion of gender interaction terms. Additional adjustment for physical activity and leisure sedentary time attenuated gender-specific estimates by 5.8% in women and 1.3% in men. Overall, the protein–BMI association was most evident for habitual between-person differences in protein intake and varied by gender and geographical context. These findings support obesity-prevention strategies focused on sustained dietary quality and population-specific contexts rather than uniform protein restriction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69199-7.title: A multimodal cross-modal explainable retrieval-augmented generation framework for hallucination-grounded visual question answering
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69199-7.abstract: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable performance on visual question answering (VQA) and multimodal reasoning tasks. But one overlooked failure case stubbornly persists: when answers require simultaneous synthesis of evidence from natural images, free-form text, and structured tables, present models suffer from trimodal hallucination—generating content unattributed to any of the input modalities. Prior approaches to hallucination mitigation focus on image-text pairs, and existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for multimodal settings do not readily include supporting evidence and often lack modality-attributed explainability. In this paper, we present MXRAG (Multimodal Cross-Modal Explainable Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a new approach to this trimodal evidence problem with three key innovations that work in concert: (1) a Trimodal Evidence Retriever (TER) that retrieves image patches, text passages, and table rows jointly using a shared semantic manifold; (2) a Cross-Modal Attribution Network (CMAN) that computes fine-grained, token-level attribution scores inline during generation, mapping each generated token to supporting evidence from all three modalities; and (3) a Hallucination-Aware Constrained Decoding (HACD) strategy that penalises generation steps with attribution entropy above a calibrated threshold, suppressing unsupported factual tokens at inference time. CMAN is trained with novel cross-modal attribution and modality-coherence losses using token-level gold annotations; HACD requires no additional training and is calibrated per dataset on the validation split. We cast joint retrieval-generation as a constrained variational problem over a trimodal evidence space and introduce MMTabQA, a new trimodal VQA benchmark derived from WikiTableQuestions and MSCOCO with 12,847 instances and token-level attribution labels. Evaluation on four benchmarks (MMTabQA, WebSRC, ChartQA, MIMIC-CXR-VQA) shows that MXRAG achieves state-of-the-art. +21.4% points (p.p.) exact match accuracy, − 38.6% relative reduction in hallucination rate (− 12.1 p.p. absolute) versus the best multimodal RAG baseline, and 89.4% modality coherence score. Ablation experiments confirm the contribution of each component, with CMAN providing the largest accuracy gain (+ 14.2%) and HACD the largest hallucination reduction (− 23.1%). A supplementary human evaluation on 200 instances confirms that the entropy-based hallucination metric tracks human judgement (human-judged HR: 21.3% vs. metric HR: 19.1%). MXRAG advances the state of the art for reliable, interpretable, evidence-based multimodal AI.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-58622-8.title: Hierarchical multi-label structuring of Japanese SOAP clinical notes with large language models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-58622-8.abstract: Much clinically salient information in Japanese electronic medical records is recorded in SOAP (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) notes, which contain a lot of unstructured text preventing the further usage for analysis. Structuring such unstructured text is essential for secondary data use and clinical research. This study aimed to develop a schema-guided, hierarchical multi-label (15 first-level and 58 second-level labels) framework for structuring respiratory medicine SOAP notes using a locally deployed large language model (LLaMA-3.1-8B adapted with QLoRA). 200 randomly selected notes were annotated and split in two for training and test. Performance was assessed through atomic-cell matching under both strict and tolerant similarity metrics, achieved a micro-averaged F1 of 0.49 (strict) and 0.59 (Levenshtein> 0.7). Common and standardized fields such as vital signs were reliably structured, while ambiguous boundaries and rare labels remained challenging. These findings demonstrate that schema-guided hierarchical multi-label frameworks can support the structuring of Japanese clinical notes and serve as a foundation for downstream research and quality-improvement workflows.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68583-7.title: Tooth loss and risk of incident cardiovascular events in an Iranian adult population: findings from Isfahan Cohort Study 2
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68583-7.abstract: Evidence on the association between tooth loss and incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains inconsistent, particularly in Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This study aimed to investigate the link between tooth loss and CVD risk and all-cause mortality in 1817 Iranian adults from the Isfahan Cohort Study 2 (2018–2023). The self-reported number of unreplaced missing teeth was examined. Acute myocardial infarction (AMI), ischemic heart disease (IHD), CVD, CVD mortality, and all-cause mortality were the outcome measures. After a median follow-up of 60.5 months (interquartile range: 52.8–66.9), the absolute numbers of AMI, IHD, CVD, CVD mortality, and all-cause mortality were 21, 79, 90, 4, and 10, respectively. In adjusted models, each additional unreplaced missing tooth was associated with a higher risk of AMI (HR 1.11; 95% CI 1.06–1.16; P < 0.001), IHD (HR 1.07; 95% CI 1.04–1.10; P < 0.001), and CVD (HR 1.06; 95% CI 1.04–1.09; P < 0.001). Associations with CVD mortality and all-cause mortality were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that tooth loss was associated with an increased risk of AMI, IHD, and CVD events but not with mortality outcomes. Therefore, tooth loss may serve as a simple clinical marker for identifying individuals at increased risk of CVD events.
