doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68012-9.title: Robust adaptive graph signal estimation using Pseudo–Huber loss
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68012-9.abstract: Graph Signal Processing (GSP) has become a crucial tool for analyzing data distributed over irregular and complex domains. Most widely used representations in GSP are the Graph Fourier Transform (GFT) and the Graph Shift Operator (GSO). GFT is the frequency-domain representation, which is suitable only for prior known band-limited signals. In contrast, the GSO is based on vertex domain formulation, making it suitable for adaptive filtering operations. In real-world scenarios, graph signals are often corrupted by non-Gaussian and impulsive noise, whereas most existing algorithms assume Gaussian noise conditions and are based on GFT representation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Graph Pseudo–Huber Loss Adaptive Filter (G-PHLAF) based on GSO. Theoretical convergence analysis in the mean square sense proves that the proposed approach provides better performance and enhanced robustness against non-Gaussian noise when compared to other competing algorithms. Further, extensive experiments on Brazilian temperature and real-time air quality datasets confirm the suitability of the proposed approach for robust graph signal estimation under uncertain and noisy conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69283-y.title: Rapid fruit growth induced by foliar mineral nutrition increases cracking risk in greenhouse grown watermelon (Citrullus lanatus)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69283-y.abstract: Abstract Foliar mineral nutrition is widely used to improve crop growth and productivity; however, its physiological effects and associated trade-offs, such as fruit cracking, in watermelon ( Citrullus lanatus ) remain unclear. This study assessed the effects of various foliar mineral formulations on the vegetative growth, photosynthetic performance, fruit development, cracking incidence, and yield of hydroponically grown watermelon under greenhouse conditions in Japan. Four treatments were applied in a completely randomized design: an unsprayed control (T0) and sprayed Ca, Zn and B (T1); micronutrients with Ca (T2) and micronutrients only (T3) prepared based on our previous studies. Foliar treatments affected growth and physiology; T3 increased leaf area (4.7%), stem diameter (4%), plant height (12%), biomass (29%), chlorophyll content (16.3%), and photosystem II efficiency (17.4%) compared to control. Although it accelerated early fruit growth, T3 markedly increased immature fruit cracking, reaching 45.4% compared with only 13.6% in the control treatment. Fruit growth rate showed a significant positive correlation (r=0.70) with cracking incidence, whereas mineral concentrations in the pulp and rind did not differ significantly between cracked and uncracked fruit, indicating that cracking was primarily due to growth dynamics rather than nutrient imbalance. Foliar treatments increased fruit diameter and individual fruit weight, with T2 producing the highest total yield (36.7% increase vs. control). Fruit quality attributes, including soluble solid content, acidity, and juice pH, were not significantly affected by any treatment. Overall, foliar mineral nutrition application enhanced physiological performance and yield potential in watermelon; however, excessive stimulation of early fruit growth increased susceptibility to cracking, highlighting the need for balanced foliar nutrient management strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69434-1.title: Two-wave average/cumulative TyG-ABSI and incident cardiovascular disease in CKM syndrome: a CHARLS cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69434-1.abstract: Repeated TyG-ABSI measurements may capture longer-term metabolic and adiposity-related exposure, but their contribution beyond a baseline value remains uncertain. We examined associations of two-wave average/cumulative TyG-ABSI and two-time-point exposure-pattern categories with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) among adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0–3 in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. TyG-ABSI was assessed at Wave 1 (2011–2012) and Wave 3 (2015), and CVD was ascertained at Wave 4 (2018). Logistic regression models adjusted for baseline age, sex, education, smoking, and drinking. Among 4755 participants without clinical CVD before Wave 3, 902 developed incident CVD by Wave 4. Compared with the consistently low category, adjusted odds ratios were 2.38 (95% CI 1.63–3.46) for high baseline with decline and 1.64 (1.38–1.94) for persistently low-to-moderate. The odds ratio for moderate-to-high with slight decline was 1.28 (1.04–1.57). Each SD increase in two-wave average/cumulative TyG-ABSI was associated with higher CVD odds (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.10–1.29). Baseline TyG-ABSI was also associated with CVD (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.02–1.19). Two-wave average/cumulative TyG-ABSI and exposure-pattern categories were associated with incident CVD. Whether repeated assessment improves risk stratification beyond a single measurement requires dedicated validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68722-0.title: Analysis of impact factors in prestressed bridges considering effective flexural rigidity
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68722-0.abstract: Abstract The impact factor is one of the most critical parameters in bridge design. Prestress losses inevitably occur throughout the service life of prestressed bridges. However, the specific influence of the prestress force on impact factors has rarely been investigated. Conventional bridge-vehicle interaction analyses generally neglect the prestress‑dependent variation of bridge stiffness, typically characterized as “effective flexural rigidity,” which may undermine the reliability of computed results. To address these limitations, both parametric analysis with consideration of effective flexural rigidity and experimental study have been conducted to assess the effect of key factors on impact factors. The results show that the prestress induces unbalanced impact factor distribution along the continuous spans, and the loss of prestress may enlarge impact factors of single spans except the non-prestress case. The prestress considerably‌ mitigates the effect of bridge deck surface roughness on impact factors. Vehicle-induced impact factors in prestressed bridges could noticeably exceed the design limits prescribed in bridge design codes of a number of nations, requiring meticulous attention. Special consideration should be accorded to existing prestressed bridges. It is hoped that the discoveries presented in this study may provide references for the design of new prestressed bridges and health rating of existing ones.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69372-y.title: Integrative metagenomic profiling identifies unique gut microbial signatures linked to moderate to severe acne
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69372-y.abstract: The microbiota plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of acne vulgaris. While the skin microbiome has been implicated in acne development, emerging research on the gut-skin axis suggests that the gut microbiota also contributes to acne. However, the alterations in species composition and function of the gut microbiome in moderate to severe acne remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we employed a multi-omics approach, integrating metagenomics and metabolomics, to investigate the gut microbiota and metabolites with the aim of elucidating the changes in gut microbiota composition and its profound role in disease pathogenesis. Metagenomic analysis was used to explore the characteristics of gut microbiota in the moderate to severe acne group and the healthy control group. We identified significant alterations in the gut microbiota between the two groups, including 20 species, such as Sutterella wadsworthensis, Clostridium sp. CAG:7, Sutterella parvirubra, Alistipes finegoldii, Alistipes onderdonkii, Eubacterium ventriosum, Eubacterium sp. CAG:274, Collinsella aerofaciens, Bacteroides sp. 1_1_6, Bacteroides clarus, Bacteroides sp. D22, etc., which may contribute to the inflammation of acne. The KEGG functional enrichment and pathway analysis of gut microbiota revealed that acne microbiota may be related to methionyl-tRNA synthetase, tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase, ethanolamine ammonia-lyase large subunit, malonate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase (acetylating)/methylmalonate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase, and participate in the aminoacyl tRNA biosynthesis, glycerophospholipid metabolism pathway, β-alanine metabolism pathway. To understand the interaction between gut microbes and the host, we also examined the fecal metabolome and conducted a correlation analysis with fecal microorganisms. The specific-unique fecal metabolites in acne group were mainly concentrated in glycerolipid metabolism and linoleic acid metabolism, and many microorganisms were positively correlated with Cer (ceramide) (d18:1/16:0), Cer (d18:1/18:1), nicotinic acid, 3-methylxanthine, negatively correlated with 2-hydroxyisocaproic acid. Bacteroides sp. 1_1_6 was positively correlated with a variety of metabolites. Our study suggested that changes in gut microbes of moderate and severe acne may play a role in the inflammatory response of acne. In addition, the gut microbiome of acne patients may affect host function by regulating glycerolipid metabolism and linoleic acid metabolism. Our findings complement the species changes in the gut microbiome and metabolome of acne patients and provide an in-depth analysis of their impact on the host over the course of the disease.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54932-z.title: Low-pass whole-genome sequencing reveals genomic diversity and ecotype-specific adaptation in indigenous Tigrayan chickens
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54932-z.abstract: Abstract Indigenous chickens play a critical role in food security and climate resilience in smallholder systems, yet their genomic diversity and adaptive potential remain insufficiently characterised. This study employed low-pass whole-genome sequencing (LP-WGS; 0.2–1.99×) to investigate genomic diversity, population structure, inbreeding and candidate environment-associated genomic variation in 33 chickens from highland, midland, and lowland agroecologies in the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia. After imputation and stringent filtering, 23.4 million high-confidence SNPs were retained, including ~ 17% novel variants, indicating substantial uncharacterised genetic diversity in these populations. SNP density (13.8 ± 8.6 SNPs/kb) was comparable to values reported from high-coverage Ethiopian chicken datasets, demonstrating the suitability of LP-WGS for population genomics in resource-limited settings. Marked differences in genomic diversity were observed among ecotypes: midland chickens showed the highest nucleotide diversity (π = 0.00267), followed by lowland (π = 0.00233), whereas highland chickens showed the lowest diversity (π = 0.00203) and elevated genomic inbreeding (F ROH and F HOM ≈ 0.18). Population structure analyses revealed clear genetic separation among ecotypes. PCA (13.91% variation explained) distinguished lowland chickens along PC1 and separated highland from midland along PC2, while ADMIXTURE and F ST patterns supported three major ancestral genomic backgrounds. Functional annotation of private missense variants uncovered distinct adaptive signatures reflecting the contrasting agroecological conditions. Highland chickens showed enrichment of candidate genes potentially involved in physiological processes relevant to high-altitude environments, including cold response, angiogenesis, cardiovascular regulation and metabolic homeostasis (eg., PARP1 , ACOX2 , ITGB3 , EDNRB , SOX8 , and SOX10 ). Midland chickens exhibited candidate signals of selection in genes with known roles in innate antiviral immunity, bacterial defence and inflammatory regulation (eg., BAK1 , CLSTN1 , CYSLTR1 , CYSLTR2 , CXCR7 , GIPR , DSCAM , GDAP1 , TLR3 , TLR4 , TLR7 , IFIH1 , ADORA1 , EPHB1 , and TMPRSS2 ). Lowland chickens displayed candidate variants associated with heat-stress response, DNA damage repair, oxidative balance and cardiovascular support under extreme temperatures (e.g., MLH1 , BDKRB1 , GPR19 , FLT1 , CCL18 , TGM2, and RAMP3 ). Overall, the results indicate substantial genomic differentiation among ecotypes and suggest candidate environment-associated genetic divergence across Tigray’s diverse agroecological zones. These populations may represent important reservoirs of adaptive genetic variation for climate-resilient poultry breeding, warranting further functional validation and conservation-oriented management.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67355-7.title: Data-driven modeling and optimization of nano-belite cementitious composites incorporating internal NaCl and Na2SO4 additives
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67355-7.abstract: This study evaluates the interactive effects of nano-belite cement replacement ($$\:0\text{\--}20\%\text{\:wt.}$$) and internal salt additions ($$\:5\%\text{\:wt.}$$ of either $$\:\text{NaCl}$$ or $$\:{\text{Na}}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}$$) on the compressive strength and bulk electrical resistivity of concrete composites up to 180 days of curing. A dataset of 225 experimental records was used to train a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network, which was subsequently coupled with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to optimize the mixture design. Experimental results indicate that under salt-free conditions, a $$\:10\%$$nano-belite replacement optimizes microstructural development, yielding a compressive strength of $$\:50.26\text{\:MPa}$$and an electrical resistivity of $$\:174.40\text{}{\Omega\:}\cdot\:\text{m}$$at 180 days. The internal addition of $$\:{\text{Na}}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}$$acts synergistically with nano-belite by promoting pore refinement through secondary hydration products, elevating the 180-day compressive strength to $$\:52.49\text{\:MPa}$$. In contrast, internal $$\:\text{NaCl}$$incorporation exhibits an antagonistic relationship at nano-belite dosages exceeding $$\:5\%$$, causing a drop in electrical resistivity due to enhanced ionic mobility in the pore network. The developed MLP model predicted the experimental outcomes with high accuracy ($$\:{R}^{2}>0.98$$ for both properties). Multi-objective optimization via NSGA-II identified a balanced optimum replacement level at $$\:9.82\%$$nano-belite. Independent validation testing of ten physical specimens fabricated at this optimal dosage demonstrated close agreement with model predictions, yielding relative errors of $$\:2.94\%$$for bulk electrical resistivity and $$\:13.13\%$$for compressive strength. Additionally, explicit algebraic equations derived from the network weights provide a direct mapping tool for mix design without the need for active machine learning execution.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69510-6.title: Measurement of binding antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 variants elicited by natural infection and COVID-19 vaccines in a sub-Saharan African population
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69510-6.abstract: Abstract Data on immune responses to COVID-19 vaccination in West and Central Africa remain limited, particularly across SARS-CoV-2 variants and vaccine platforms. Using the InVITE cohort in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Guinea, Liberia, and Mali, we evaluated anti-spike (anti-S) antibody binding to nine SARS-CoV-2 variants in 96 participants equally selected from pre-vaccination assay defined seropositive and seronegative groups. Participants received mRNA, adenovirus-vectored, or inactivated virus vaccines. Anti-S binding was measured before vaccination and two months after completion of the primary series using a Meso Scale Discovery 10-plex assay. Before vaccination, antibody binding was significantly higher against pre-Omicron variants (Ancestral, Alpha, Beta, and Delta) than Omicron variants in both seronegative (fold change [FC] 3.85, 99% CI 3.45–4.17) and seropositive (FC 3.57, 99% CI 3.33–3.84) participants. Seropositive individuals showed greater binding than seronegative individuals across all variants. Two months post-vaccination, mRNA vaccines elicited higher antibody binding than adenovirus-vectored or inactivated vaccines, whereas no significant differences were observed between adenovirus-vectored and inactivated vaccines. Antibody binding remained higher against pre-Omicron than Omicron variants across all vaccine platforms and serostatus groups. These findings provide rare data on variant-specific vaccine-elicited antibody binding responses in West and Central African populations with distinct demographic, epidemiologic, and immunologic background. Trial registration: Registration ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05096091, Registration date: 10-26-2021, Clinical trial registry: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05096091?term=NCT05096091rank=1#study-overview .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66976-2.title: Therapeutic potential of gut microbiota metabolites against Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia: a multiomics analysis integrating network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66976-2.abstract: Although gut microbiota metabolites (GMMs) show therapeutic activity against Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia (KPP), their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Therefore, identifying biomarkers associated with the therapeutic effects of GMM on KPP is crucial. Targets associated with gut microbiota (GM), GMM, and KPP were collected from several databases. Intersecting targets were considered candidate biomarkers and subject to Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment and subcellular localization analyses. Key metabolites were screened based on drug-likeness and toxicity. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to evaluate metabolite–biomarker interactions. Furthermore, database predictions yielded 117 GM targets, 686 GMM targets, and 226 KPP targets. Five overlapping targets (IL6, NFKB1, PTGER3, PPARG, and TLR4) were selected as candidate biomarkers. KEGG analysis revealed 67 enriched pathways, including toll-like receptor signaling. Subcellular localization predicted IL6 (extracellular matrix), NFKB1, PPARG (nucleus), PTGER3 and TLR4 (plasma membrane). Ethyl phenyllactate(-)-, 5-(3-hydroxyphenyl) pentanoic acid, and glycocholic acid were identified as key metabolites. Moreover, molecular docking predicted stable binding for all metabolite–biomarker pairs, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested that the ethyl phenyllactate(-)-–NFKB1 complex had the highest conformational stability among the tested complexes. Clinical validation using two independent transcriptomic datasets (GSE33341 and GSE60244) of gram-negative bacterial infections confirmed that NFKB1, PPARG, and TLR4 were substantially upregulated, and a five-biomarker combined model achieved high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve = 0.885–0.982). We identified IL6, NFKB1, PTGER3, PPARG, and TLR4 as potential biomarkers for GMM-based treatment of KPP. Ethyl phenyllactate(-)- is considered a key metabolite that interacts stably with NFKB1. These results offer potential mechanistic insight into the regulatory role of GMM in KPP therapy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65266-1.title: Effect of image exposure on corneal and lens densitometry measurements with Pentacam HR: an exploratory background-based analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65266-1.abstract: Abstract To investigate whether image-level exposure variation affects corneal densitometry (CD) and lens densitometry (LD) measurements obtained with the Pentacam HR, and to explore whether background densitometry (BD) can serve as an image-based surrogate of exposure. This retrospective paired-measurement study included two routine preoperative Pentacam examinations obtained 2–3 months apart under standardized room illumination, without intentional alteration of ambient light. BD was measured in the non-tissue background above the corneal apex on Scheimpflug images. CD and LD parameters were compared between examinations and analyzed in relation to BD and changes in BD. Except for BD, corneal topographic and densitometry parameters did not differ significantly between the two examinations. No robust association was observed between CD and BD after sensitivity analysis and false-discovery-rate adjustment. By contrast, BD showed consistent positive associations with LD, and the change in LD was strongly associated with the change in BD. These findings suggest that BD may reflect image-level exposure variation in Scheimpflug densitometry, particularly for LD measurements. However, the analysis was exploratory and was intended to identify exposure-related trends rather than to propose a numerical adjustment; the interpretation requires validation in independent datasets and in eyes with corneal or lens pathology before clinical application.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69652-7.title: Oxalate induces phosphatidylserine externalization, apoptosis, and crystal-cell adhesion in renal tubular epithelial cells through the ROS-ADAM17-Notch1 axis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69652-7.abstract: Abstract Background Oxalate salts induce reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, leading to phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization from renal tubule epithelial cells and the development of kidney stone. This research investigated the roles of ADAM17 (A Disintegrin and Metalloproteinase 17) and the Notch1 signaling pathway in oxalate-induced cell crystal adhesion through ROS-mediated mechanisms. Methods We treated HK-2 with sodium oxalate to establish a model of damage. ROS were measured using DCFH-DA fluorescence, and apoptosis and PS externalization were measured using flow cytometry. QPCR was applied to evaluate the mRNA of ADAM17 and Notch1, while western blot analysis was employed to assess their corresponding protein levels. Crystal adhesion assays were used to assess cell adherence to calcium oxalate crystals. The function of ADAM17 in oxalate-induced injury was examined by siRNA-mediated knockdown. Results Exposure to oxalate significantly elevated ROS generation, apoptotic incidence, PS externalization, and crystal adhesion in HK-2 cells. Moreover, oxalate exposure upregulated ADAM17 expression and activated the Notch1 signaling pathway. Antioxidant treatment reduces ADAM17 expression and inhibits Notch1 pathway activation. ADAM17 knockdown partially rescued ROS-induced apoptosis and PS externalization, reduced crystal adhesion, and suppressed Notch1 signaling. Conclusion Oxalate triggers apoptosis, PS externalization, and crystal cell adhesion in renal tubular epithelial cells through the ROS-ADAM17-Notch1 axis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66386-4.title: Eco-environmental management in islanded system sizing including battery, wind/photovoltaic/hydropower/bio-waste resources and electric vehicles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66386-4.abstract: The study outlines the planning methodology for an islanded hybrid system incorporating electric vehicle parking, focusing on the optimal capacity determination of controllable and uncontrollable renewable resources, alongside batteries, while addressing both economic and environmental criteria. The goal function minimizes the construction and maintenance costs associated with battery storage systems, power electronic converters, and renewable energy units, as well as mitigating the expenses tied to battery degradation, electric vehicles depreciation, and environmental pollution from bio-waste systems. Within this framework, minimizing the total environmental pollution by the bio-waste renewable source minus the environmental cleanliness from waste by this source is considered. These objectives are governed by operation-planning constraints including resource and storage management, and converter functionality. The design also accounts for uncertainties linked to electric vehicles, fluctuating renewable energy output, and load demands. To address these uncertainties, stochastic optimization is implemented using the Unscented Transformation method. Additionally, the problem-solving approach employs a hybrid evolutionary algorithm combining the Ant-Lion Optimizer and the Red Panda Optimizer to achieve enhanced computational efficiency. Numerical simulations demonstrated that the proposed solution algorithm achieves optimal results with rapid convergence, showcasing a final response standard deviation between 0.91% and 0.92%. Notably, the inclusion of stationary energy storage devices, such as batteries, in the islanded system substantially reduces reliance on hydro and bio-waste energy generation, leading to fewer installed elements and a decrease in system planning costs compared to solely using renewable energy resources. The impact of electric vehicles was analyzed under two scenarios: when vehicles function solely as consumers, the planning cost rises by approximately 23.5%; however, when they serve as mobile storage units, the cost reduces by 1.8% in comparison to scenarios without their incorporation. This finding underscores the strategic advantage of integrating electric vehicles and battery bank as flexible storage assets in hybrid energy systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65133-z.title: Energy from the Sun dissipates into a narrow band around 70$$^\circ$$N geographic latitude
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65133-z.abstract: Abstract Substorms are common phenomena in the northern and southern auroral regions and play an important role in transferring energy from the Sun into the Earth’s magnetosphere-ionosphere system. A substantial part of the energy released during substorms is dissipated in the ionosphere through Joule heating and electron precipitation. The energy transport and dissipation disturb the ionospheric plasma environment and the geomagnetic field, posing a risk to vulnerable satellite and ground-based infrastructure. In this study, we estimate ionospheric energy dissipation and characterize substorm properties using magnetic observations from two ground-based observatories and eight other magnetic stations at northern high latitudes (60–80 $$^\circ$$ N geographic latitude) during 1994–2018. We show that the substorm occurrence and energy dissipation vary largely over latitudes, with the highest substorm occurrence observed at the Bear Island station (74.5 $$^\circ$$ N, 71.5 $$^\circ$$ magnetic latitude) and the most energetic substorms found at the Muonio station (68.0 $$^\circ$$ N, 64.7 $$^\circ$$ magnetic latitude). The majority of the energy dissipates into a narrow latitudinal band: over two thirds (69%) of the total energy dissipates into a three-degree-wide band, corresponding to one sixth of the studied latitude range.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68281-4.title: A retrospective study of mandibular incisor intrusion with invisalign in adult deep-bite patients
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68281-4.abstract: This retrospective study quantitatively evaluated mandibular incisor intrusion and associated vertical skeletal changes during deep-bite correction using Invisalign clear aligner therapy. Twenty-seven adult patients (19–54 years of age) with skeletal Class I or II malocclusion and deep overbite (> 3 mm) treated with Invisalign incorporating precision bite ramps were retrospectively analyzed. Lateral cephalometric radiographs obtained before (T0) and after treatment (T1) were superimposed on the cranial base and mandible. Mandibular incisor movement was assessed using centroid-based measurements to isolate pure intrusion and minimize the influence of tipping. Changes in the occlusal plane angle, mandibular plane angle (FMA), incisor mandibular plane angle (IMPA), and molar vertical position were also evaluated. Paired t-tests were performed for statistical comparisons. The mandibular incisor centroid demonstrated statistically significant pure intrusion of 1.63 mm (p < 0.001). Occlusal plane angle increased significantly (mean change: 2.38°, p = 0.001) and overbite decreased (mean change: -1.98 mm, p = 0.001), whereas changes in the FMA, IMPA, and mandibular molar extrusion were not statistically significant, suggesting limited vertical skeletal changes during treatment. These findings suggest that Invisalign therapy with precision bite ramps demonstrated mandibular incisor intrusion in adult deep-bite patients.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65649-4.title: N2O emission factors across a gradient of pasture intensification in Highlands of Southern Brazil: Towards regionalizing greenhouse gas inventories
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65649-4.abstract: Abstract Accurate greenhouse gas inventories require region-specific emission factors (EFs). Current nitrous oxide (N 2 O) inventories often rely on IPCC Tier 1 defaults, which may not accurately represent subtropical grazing systems where field-based data remain scarce. This study aimed to evaluate how pasture intensification gradients interact with different nitrogen sources (urea fertilizer, cattle urine, and dung) to regulate N 2 O emission factors in the Southern Brazilian Highlands, providing regionally calibrated data to assess their alignment with IPCC default values. Nitrous oxide emissions were measured over 100 days using static chambers in four systems: natural grassland (NG), improved natural grassland (ING), perennial pasture (PP), and annual pasture with soil disturbance (AP). Measured EFs suggested a trend toward lower values than IPCC defaults for most sources. Urea in AP was the only treatment exceeding the 1.6% default (EF = 1.7%), while urea-EFs in PP and ING averaged 0.77%. Urine-EFs averaged 0.71% in AP/ING and 0.23% in NG/PP, while dung consistently showed the lowest values (mean = 0.28%). These findings suggest that N 2 O emissions are governed by two interacting hierarchies: management intensity (NG < ING ≈ PP < AP) and nitrogen source (urea > urine ≈ dung). Overall, these findings suggest that the monitored subtropical grazing systems with stable soil structures tended to exhibit lower N 2 O emission factors than current IPCC Tier 1 default values. Disaggregating EFs by source and management intensity improves national inventories and informs mitigation strategies, such as reducing soil disturbance to preserve the naturally low N 2 O emission potential of subtropical pastures.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69441-2.title: Serverless edge intelligence for SLA-aware function placement and resource slicing in wireless networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69441-2.abstract: Wireless edge networks must support delay-sensitive services under fluctuating traffic, interference, heterogeneous SLA priorities, and limited radio, computing, and memory resources. This paper proposes Serverless-PRONTO, an SLA-aware orchestration framework that jointly controls serverless function placement, task offloading, bandwidth allocation, CPU slicing, and warm-instance management. The system model captures uplink and downlink transmission, queueing, execution, cold-start initialization, and memory occupied by retained function instances. To solve the resulting dynamic, partially observable, mixed discrete-continuous problem, Serverless-PRONTO combines a physics-aware sparse graph encoder with multi-agent TD3 under centralized training and decentralized execution. The encoder represents inter-node coupling through channel, interference, distance, queue, resource, function-demand, and cold-start features, while top- \(\:K\) attention limits signaling. An SLA-risk mechanism prioritizes requests according to urgency, queue state, service class, and cold-start probability. A sequential feasibility projection converts raw actor outputs into valid placement, bandwidth, CPU, and memory decisions. Simulations against four serverless and edge-orchestration baselines under varying traffic loads and network sizes show higher SLA satisfaction, lower end-to-end delay and cold-start ratio, and more stable scalability, demonstrating the benefit of jointly coordinating wireless resources and serverless runtime states.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68696-z.title: Environmental assessment of potentially toxic metals in settled indoor dust of primary school classrooms in suburban communities of Southwestern Nigeria
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68696-z.abstract: Emissions of particle-phase species from on-road motor vehicles are known to be a major contributor to the atmospheric particulate matter burden, which, upon deposition, leads to indoor dust accumulation and acts as a reservoir for particle-bound metals. This study assessed concentrations, pollution status, ecological risk, and sources of potentially toxic metals (PTMs) in classroom dust from pre-/primary schools in areas with diverse traffic densities and evaluated pupils’ exposure to environmental toxins. Thirty-six composite dust samples were collected from classrooms of pre-/primary schools in suburban communities in two States of Southwestern Nigeria. The samples were analysed for PTMs using an Energy-Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence (EDXRF) Spectrophotometer. The mean metal concentrations followed the order Fe > Al > Co > Zn > Mn > Pb > Cu > Ni > As > Ag > V > Cr > Cd, with significantly higher levels generally observed at high-traffic sites (p < 0.05). Pollution indices, including contamination factor, geo-accumulation index, pollution load index, Nemerow pollution index, and potential ecological risk index, indicated varying degrees of contamination and ecological risk across the study locations, with As and Cd contributing substantially to elevated contamination factors and ecological risk at several sites. Ni, Cu, Zn, Pb, and As were the dominant contributors to pollution, with As and Pb presenting extreme pollution and ecological risk at several sites. Principal component analysis (PCA) and positive matrix factorisation (PMF) identified vehicular emissions, mechanical wear, industrial activities, and resuspended soil as the major sources of metal contamination. The results of the study highlight the need for continued environmental monitoring and further studies incorporating human health risk assessments to evaluate potential impacts on children and school staff.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69073-6.title: Subsite-specific prediction of lymphatic spread in head-and-neck cancer using a mixture of hidden Markov models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69073-6.abstract: Abstract Head-and-neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC) metastasize to neck lymph nodes. Radiation treatments include the elective irradiation of lymph node levels (LNLs) at risk of harboring occult (clinically undetected) metastases. We present a statistical model for personalized estimation of ipsilateral occult metastases risk given an individual patient’s clinical LNL involvement, T-stage, and tumor subsite. Each LNL is described by a binary random variable: healthy/metastatic. Lymphatic cancer progression is described by hidden Markov models (HMM) whose transition matrices contain the probabilities of tumor spread to and between LNLs. Specific primary tumor subsites (ICD-codes) are described by a mixture of HMMs. The model parameters are learned via the expectation–maximization (EM) algorithm from a multi-institutional dataset containing 2437 patients across 13 subsites. A mixture model with 4 HMMs identified components corresponding to the characteristic spread patterns associated with the anterior oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, and glottic larynx. The mixture coefficients describe a subsite’s similarity to each component and allow modeling gradual changes in LNL involvement for anatomically neighboring subsites with similar lymphatic spread. Palate tumors are described by mixtures between oropharynx and oral cavity, supraglottic larynx tumors as mixtures between glottic larynx and hypopharynx. The model predicts low risk of occult metastases in LNL III for cN0 oral cavity subsites, and low risk in LNL IV for oropharyngeal subsites without clinical LNL III involvement. This framework provides interpretable and individualized predictions of lymphatic spread in HNSCC. It may support the design of future clinical trials to investigate personalized volume-deescalated elective nodal irradiation strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69234-7.title: Identification and mechanistic elucidation of neutrophil migration-related biomarkers in Kawasaki disease based on single-cell and transcriptome sequencing
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69234-7.abstract: Kawasaki Disease (KD), an acute pediatric vasculitis, predominantly impacts children under the age of five. It stands as the primary etiology of acquired coronary artery lesions. Despite being acknowledged as a systemic inflammatory disorder, the pathogenesis of KD remains unclear, while it exhibits a strong correlation with the activation and dysregulation of innate immune cells. This research aims to explore its mechanisms at the cellular and molecular levels and construct a diagnostic model. Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets (GSE254657) and microarray datasets (GSE73461, GSE68004) were obtained from the GEO database. Single-cell data were processed, annotated, and analyzed for differential abundance using various software packages and algorithms, such as Seurat and harmony. Differential expression analysis, enrichment analysis, functional annotation, and migration activity assessment were performed. Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) was used to identify relevant genes. Diagnostic models were constructed and validated through univariate, LASSO, and multivariate logistic regression analyses. The molecular mechanisms of biomarkers were explored using multiple databases. In Kawasaki disease (KD) blood, the abundance of neutrophils, megakaryocytes, and plasmacytoid dendritic cells was significantly up—regulated. Neutrophils were classified into nine subtypes, among which the neutro7 subtype exhibited the highest activation of migration mechanisms. Five candidate genes associated with neutrophil migration were identified, and four biomarkers (PIM3, S100A12, S100A9, SOCS3) were selected for the construction of a diagnostic model. This model manifested high diagnostic capacity, reliability, and clinical decision—making value in both the training and validation cohorts. The molecular mechanisms and regulatory networks of the biomarkers were elucidated. This research explored the neutrophil-related pathogenesis of Kawasaki disease (KD) and established a diagnostic model with favorable performance, offering novel theoretical evidence and potential targets for comprehending the pathogenesis of KD. Identified genetic features serveras an exploratoryframework for future diagnostic advances, offering potentialdiagnostic relevance in detecting subtypes such as incompleteKawasaki disease that are difficult to diagnoserearly. However, validation through large-scale prospective cohort studies is still required. Furthermore, distinctions from other inflammatory diseases also need further confirmation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67450-9.title: Privacy-preserving intrusion detection in IoT smart homes using a federated hybrid 1D-CNN–LSTM model with explainable AI
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67450-9.abstract: Abstract The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in smart home environments has dramatically expanded the attack surface for cyber threats, particularly botnet-driven Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. Centralized Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are ill-suited to this domain because they violate user privacy, introduce single points of failure, and incur prohibitive communication overhead. Federated Learning (FL) offers a compelling privacy-preserving alternative, yet existing FL-based IDS solutions either deploy convolutional or recurrent models in isolation, lack human-interpretable outputs, or neglect real-world deployability constraints. This paper proposes FedShield-IDS , a novel federated intrusion detection framework that integrates a hybrid one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network with Long Short-Term Memory units to simultaneously capture spatial traffic fingerprints and long-range temporal attack dynamics across IoT edge devices. Model interpretability is addressed through the integration of SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), enabling administrators to receive human-readable justifications for every detected anomaly. The system is trained and evaluated on the large-scale CICIoT2023 dataset, comprising 712,311 flow records spanning eight attack families including DDoS, DoS, Mirai, Reconnaissance, Spoofing, Injection, and Malware. A multi-stage preprocessing pipeline combining infinite-value imputation, logarithmic feature scaling, Min-Max normalization, temporal windowing, and localized SMOTE oversampling is applied within each federated client to address non-IID data and extreme class imbalance. Federated Averaging aggregates encrypted model updates across seven virtual IoT client nodes over five communication rounds without exchanging raw traffic data, under a formal threat model characterizing the system’s adversarial assumptions and data-confidentiality guarantees. Experimental results demonstrate a Mirai F1-score of 0.99, a DDoS precision of 0.97, and a global weighted F1-score of 0.76 across all eight classes. Comprehensive kernel-size, architecture, and preprocessing ablations confirm the necessity of each design choice, and independent cross-dataset evaluation on the Edge-IIoTset benchmark achieves 98.58% accuracy, demonstrating strong generalization beyond CICIoT2023. The framework achieves sub-500 ms threat mitigation, empirically confirmed via a mitigation-gate threshold sensitivity analysis, and generates SHAP-gated explanations for every alert, bridging the gap between high-accuracy detection and the transparency required for trustworthy smart-home security.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66250-5.title: Associations of cooking and food preparation skills with diet quality and body weight among Turkish women
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66250-5.abstract: The relationship between cooking and food preparation skills and health outcomes has received increasing attention, although evidence regarding their independent associations with diet quality and body weight remains inconclusive. This cross-sectional study investigates the relationship between culinary skills, diet quality, and body weight among 281 Turkish women aged 19–64 years using a convenience sampling approach. Cooking and food preparation skills were assessed using the validated 33-item Cooking and Food Skills Scale, while nutrient-based diet quality was measured by the Nutrient Rich Food Index 9.3 (NRF 9.3), calculated from a single 24-h dietary recall. Women in the highest skill tertile (mean score: 214.5 ± 1.1) reported significantly higher confidence in cooking techniques and cooked at home ≥ 5 times per week (p < 0.05) compared to lower tertiles. In addition, higher cooking skills were associated with a 2.1-fold increase in the odds of having a non-normal body mass index (OR 2.1; 95% CI 1.14–3.87; p < 0.05), but this association lost significance after adjusting for socio-demographic and dietary factors. No significant relationship was found between cooking skills and diet quality (mean NRF 9.3 score: 333.4 ± 50.2; p > 0.05). Cooking and food preparation skills were not independently associated with diet quality or body weight after adjustment for potential confounding variables. These findings suggest that culinary skills alone are unlikely to improve dietary quality or weight status and should be integrated with broader nutrition and lifestyle interventions.
