doi:10.1038/s41598-026-59932-7.title: Mineralogical and geochemical provenance reference for turquoise from the Teghout Cu–Mo deposit in Armenia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-59932-7.abstract: Turquoise from the Teghout Cu–Mo porphyry deposit (Lori Province, northern Armenia) forms veinlets and nodules in the supergene zone with quartz, Fe–Mn oxides, jarosite, barite and clay minerals, locally chalcanthite and gypsum. We provide the first integrated reference dataset for a substantial Caucasus turquoise source, providing the mineralogical and geochemical reference data needed to support future archaeological provenance research, collection authentication and heritage-science studies of exchange in the region. We emphasise that the Teghout occurrence was only discovered in 1974 during modern exploration and that no archaeological evidence currently links it to ancient turquoise supply; the reference framework presented here is intended to enable, not to substitute for, such future archaeological investigation. Gemmological testing, SEM imaging, EPMA, FTIR, Raman and LA-ICP-MS define a Cu-Al dominant turquoise near the ideal end-member. Raman spectra include variants with sulphate bands near 983 and 1007 cm−1. Trace elements show MREE-peaked, chondrite-normalised REE patterns with a broad Sm–Gd maximum, weak Eu anomalies, enrichment in Sr-Mo-Zn-Sc and very low V-Cr. Comparison with datasets from Meiduk (Iran) and Tongling (China), two porphyry-hosted turquoise localities, tests discrimination within a shared genetic framework; log-transformed Sr/V–Pb/Ba and Sr/U–Pb/U ratios distinguish the deposits statistically, although the Sr/U–Pb/U field is treated as supportive because Teghout and Meiduk show limited envelope overlap.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68897-6.title: Hybrid particle swarm unbiased extremum seeking control for cooperative drone fleet for gas leak localization in obstructed outdoor environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68897-6.abstract: The study employs a fleet of drones to address gas source localization (GSL) in a dynamic outdoor environment. A hybrid control framework integrating particle swarm optimization (PSO) with unbiased extremum seeking (uES) is proposed to improve GSL performance under turbulent plume conditions. The proposed framework combines the global exploration capability of PSO with the smooth, unbiased gradient refinement of uES to address the limitations of existing algorithms. Comprehensive assessments conducted in two simulated plume environments, along with high-fidelity Gazebo– GADEN simulations, indicate that PSO–uES reliably achieves fast convergence, high success rates, and notably stable trajectories. Unlike classical ESC, which exhibits star-shaped dithering and does not reliably settle near the source, and standard PSO, which may wander within areas of weak gradients, the proposed approach sustains directed movement, minimizes plume-loss occurrences, and converges close to the source location in simulation environments. These findings demonstrate that PSO–uES is a promising approach for simulation-based GSL with complex and turbulent plume characteristics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67795-1.title: Support mechanism and numerical analysis of full-length prestressed self-drilling bolts in fractured roadway surrounding rock
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67795-1.abstract: Conventional resin-anchored bolts rely on stable boreholes and reliable end anchorage in fractured roadway surrounding rock, whereas conventional self-drilling bolts have good construction adaptability but limited active pretensioning capacity. To improve bolt installation reliability, pretension retention, and grouting reinforcement in fractured surrounding rock, this study proposes a full-length prestressed self-drilling bolt that integrates self-drilling installation, end grouting bearing, active pretensioning, and full-length grouting reinforcement. A theoretical model for bolt pretension transfer was established, and a single-bolt pretension-transfer model and a roadway-support numerical model were developed in FLAC3D. The mechanical responses of threaded steel bolts, conventional self-drilling bolts, and full-length prestressed self-drilling bolts under different pretension levels were compared. The results show that, during initial pretensioning, the proposed bolt can maintain a high axial force over most of the bolt length and transfer pretension to the deeper rock mass through the end anchorage section, forming a more continuous axial compressive-stress influence zone. Under the adopted numerical-model conditions, the proposed bolt reduced roof subsidence, rib deformation, and plastic-zone development relative to conventional support schemes. The results indicate that the synergistic action of end grouting bearing, active pretensioning, and full-length grouting reinforcement can improve pretension transfer and surrounding-rock control in fractured rock masses, thereby providing a new bolt-grouting collaborative support method for active support of fractured coal-rock roadways.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69081-6.title: High-fidelity 3D reconstruction of navel oranges using 3D Gaussian splatting
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69081-6.abstract: Reliable 3D visual reconstruction is important for documenting the external quality of navel oranges and supporting future phenotypic analysis. Conventional Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines struggle with the weakly textured characteristics and highly specular surfaces of navel oranges, resulting in incomplete reconstructions, sparse point clouds, and severe visual artifacts. To address these challenges, this study develops a high-fidelity 3D reconstruction framework that integrates deep-learning-based feature matching with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). For the sparse reconstruction phase, the SuperPoint detector and SuperGlue matcher are employed, leveraging deep feature extraction and graph neural networks to enhance matching robustness on complex surfaces. To address the initialization challenges of 3DGS, a spatial-colorimetric cascade purification strategy—combining pass-through filtering, HSV masking, and statistical filtering—is developed to effectively eliminate noise and provide a high-confidence initialization prior. Subsequently, 3DGS is utilized for dense reconstruction and high-fidelity neural rendering. Experimental results demonstrate that the developed framework significantly outperforms the conventional SfM pipeline in terms of registered image count, point cloud density, and trajectory length. The 3DGS-optimized model achieved improved PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS values on held-out views, indicating enhanced novel-view rendering quality and visual fidelity. This approach offers an efficient photorealistic digitization solution for weakly textured and highly specular fruits, thereby establishing a reliable visual foundation for future non-destructive phenotypic analysis in smart agriculture.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69391-9.title: An improved black-winged kite optimization algorithm integrating sparrow behavior and multi-strategy optimization for UAV route planning
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69391-9.abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced Black-winged Kite Optimization Algorithm (SMBKA) to address the issues of slow convergence and poor accuracy in UAV route planning within three-dimensional complex environments. SMBKA enhances planning performance by incorporating sparrow-inspired behavior and multi-strategy optimization mechanisms. Specifically, the proposed method utilizes Latin hypercube sampling to generate the initial population, thereby improving its distribution uniformity and diversity. Furthermore, an adaptive weight factor is adopted to achieve a dynamic balance between exploration and exploitation. Meanwhile, a dynamic opposition-based learning strategy is integrated to effectively improve overall search performance and avoid premature convergence. Finally, the scout search mechanism from the sparrow search algorithm is incorporated to enhance the algorithm’s adaptability to complex environments. In terms of performance verification, SMBKA demonstrates superior performance on the CEC2017 test functions, achieving the best average accuracy in 16 out of 29 test functions. In the application of UAV route planning, the average flight path length is shortened by 7.2% to 18.68%, demonstrating the potential of this algorithm in practical applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69305-9.title: Effectiveness of an improvisational theatre-based intervention for the prevention of workplace sexual harassment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69305-9.abstract: Abstract Workplace sexual harassment remains widespread. The effectiveness of traditional training approaches is mixed and inconsistent, and research is needed to identify effective prevention measures. The present study provides an evaluation of an improvisational theatre-based intervention designed to prevent workplace sexual harassment. We used a randomized wait-list control design to examine the short-term and two-month effects of a 90-minute improvisational theatre intervention among 162 university students preparing for organizational internships. Results showed that participating in the intervention increased participants’ general confidence to respond to sexual harassment at work in the short term, and increased willingness to intervene, as well as reduced hostile sexist attitudes in the long-term. Moreover, inclusive tendencies to improve the ability to identify subtle sexual harassment behaviors and increase intentions to intervene in such situations occurred in the short term, while benevolent sexism and sexual harassment myth acceptance remained unchanged. No evidence for backlash was found. Together, these results suggest that improvisational theatre can lead to favorable and partly durable changes in outcomes relevant for the prevention of sexual harassment, while also emphasizing the need for complementary prevention measures to achieve broader attitudinal changes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65424-5.title: Extend-and-forward relaying through wireless frequency extension for sub-terahertz communication
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65424-5.abstract: This study introduces extended-and-forward relaying for sub-terahertz (sub-THz) extended fronthaul link (EFL) via jointly implemented frequency division multiplexing at the fronthaul and wireless frequency extension for sub-THz relaying. EFL transmission and reception, phase noise (PN) induced symbol error probability, and operable frequency regions are modeled. Aggregated PN significance over distributedly synchronized (DS) and non-synchronized (NS) EFLs is compared. 180 GHz EFL on cascaded software-defined radio (SDR)-THz testbed is demonstrated with off-the-shelf SDRs, frequency extenders, and various radio frequency measurement tools. DS demonstration achieves 0 bit error rate over $$4\times 10^{6}$$ transmitted bits per user at measured signal-to-noise ratios between 11 and 13 dB, whereas NS shows 0.01 bit error floor with software controllable SDR clock aggregated 0.384 radian PN deviation at most. A digital post correction is proposed to suppress PN-related clock offset by dynamic phase correction, which achieves up to 0.088 BER decrement in NS, with the improvement varying by user and link distances.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67637-0.title: Extensively drug-resistant ESBL-producing enterobacterales and coexisting antimicrobial resistance genes are associated with mortality in critically ill patients with cancer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67637-0.abstract: Abstract ESBL-producing bacteria are a problem in patients with cancer. The emergence of XDR phenotypes with ESBLs increases mortality. We aimed to evaluate ESBL-producing bacteria, the prevalence of MDR and XDR phenotypes, ESBL genes, and mortality predictors in patients with cancer in the ICU. Different clinical cultures were collected from patients in oncology ICUs. We used the VITEK2 system to identify isolates and assess antibiotic sensitivity, and the combination disk method to detect ESBL phenotypes. β-lactamase, ESBL, and carbapenem genes were detected using PCR. 136 isolates were ESBL-producing. Respiratory cultures were the main source, followed by blood cultures. K. pneumoniae was the most common, followed by E. coli . Isolates showed high resistance to third- and fourth-generation cephalosporins and carbapenem antibiotics. 84.6% and 13.2% of isolates were XDR and MDR, respectively. The most harbored genes were SHV and TEM (94.1%), CTXM-15 (59.6%), SHV-12 (67.6%), and NDM (78.7%). 38.2% of isolates harbored seven β-lactamase, ESBL, and carbapenem genes. K. pneumoniae significantly harbored more ESBL and carbapenem genes than E. coli . Patient age, relapses, and hospital stay are predictors of mortality in patients. An improved surveillance program and antibiotic stewardship are urgently needed.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69738-2.title: Rainfall redistribution and warming drive future urban hydroclimatic intensification in Trnava, Slovakia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69738-2.abstract: Abstract Urban areas are increasingly exposed to compound hydroclimatic pressures arising from intensified rainfall extremes, progressive warming and the growing sensitivity of urban drainage systems to short-duration rainfall events. However, future urban climate risk cannot be fully understood from changes in annual precipitation or temperature alone. This study investigates future urban hydroclimatic intensification in Trnava, Slovakia, using long-term meteorological observations, statistically downscaled CMIP6 climate projections, climate-extreme indices and a proposed Runoff-Generating Rainfall Index (RGRI). Future projections indicate that annual precipitation changes remain modest, whereas annual maximum 1-day and 5-day precipitation increase by approximately 37–41% and 17–19%, respectively. The RGRI further indicates greater concentration of annual precipitation in runoff-generating events, with significant increases in the contribution of very wet rainfall across all future scenarios. Concurrently, annual maximum air temperature increases from 35.9 °C to 38.6–38.7 °C, while warm-day and warm-night frequencies increase substantially relative to their historical thresholds, indicating both a warmer climate and more frequent warm extremes. Together, these findings highlight rainfall redistribution and progressive warming as key drivers of future urban hydroclimatic risk. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for hydroclimatic assessment and climate adaptation in medium-sized Central European cities with similar climatic and urban characteristics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69049-6.title: Head-to-head comparison of FibroTest and ELF for diagnosing significant fibrosis (F2-F4) in outpatients with type-2 diabetes using Bayesian latent class models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69049-6.abstract: In patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, two serum fibrosis panels with patented algorithms are among the most cited: the Nash-FibroTest combination (FibroTest), which assesses fibrosis, steatosis and inflammatory activity in one sample, and the Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) score, which evaluates fibrosis alone. No head-to-head one-step comparison has been published in type-2 diabetes. Our aim was to compare FibroTest and ELF for diagnosing significant fibrosis stages (F2-F3-F4) in 398 type-2 diabetes outpatients, 59 years old median and 40% females, of the prospective ongoing QUID-NASH study. The standard reference, liver biopsy, is misclassified in about 25% of cases, inducing bias in sensitivity, specificity and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), in both magnitude and direction, and distorting head-to-head differences. To relax the perfect-gold-standard assumption, we used Bayesian latent class models, which privilege no test, histology included. Posterior mean AUC was 0.94 for FibroTest and 0.76 for ELF, with a mean difference (FibroTest-ELF) of 0.18 (95% credible interval, 0.12–0.25); with no prior information imposed, the model estimated biopsy sensitivity at 0.69 and specificity at 0.74. These results highlight the importance of accounting for reference standard imperfection and support the use of head-to-head comparisons combined with latent class modeling. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03634098.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67134-4.title: Correction: Human chorion and placental mesenchymal stem cells conditioned media suppress cell migration and invasion by inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway in cholangiocarcinoma
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67134-4.abstract: Scientific Reports - Correction: Human chorion and placental mesenchymal stem cells conditioned media suppress cell migration and invasion by inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway in cholangiocarcinoma

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69509-z.title: Load frequency control framework of renewable integrated power systems in multi scenario disturbance conditions with the proximal policy optimization
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69509-z.abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources introduces low inertia, generation uncertainty and rapidly varying disturbances, making conventional load frequency control increasingly challenging. This paper proposes a direct policy-based secondary frequency controller using proximal policy optimization for a renewable-integrated power system. Unlike reinforcement-learning approaches used only to tune conventional proportional–integral or fuzzy-controller parameters, the proposed agent directly generates the supplementary generation command from the measured system state. The reward formulation jointly considers frequency deviation, accumulated error, control smoothness, actuator constraints, safety-limit violation and generation cost. The controller is evaluated under four operating conditions involving staged load variation, long-duration cyclic disturbance, oscillatory stress and a realistic multi-event renewable contingency. The results show that the proposed controller maintains the average absolute frequency deviation between approximately 0.000113 and 0.0010 hertz and limits the maximum overshoot to between approximately 0.001144 and 0.0171 hertz across the investigated cases. The findings demonstrate effective disturbance attenuation and stable frequency restoration within the adopted reduced-order simulation framework. Future work will extend the analysis to detailed interconnected multi-area systems and hardware-in-the-loop validation.The PPO controller maintains a comparatively small average absolute frequency deviation, consistent with the quantitative values reported in Table 2.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70040-4.title: Regional inequities in emergency medical services response times: a multi-regional analysis of time-critical emergencies in Saudi Arabia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70040-4.abstract: Timely emergency medical services (EMS) response is a critical determinant of survival in life-threatening emergencies. In Saudi Arabia, response times frequently exceed the 8-min benchmark commonly used in high-income settings, raising concerns about system performance and regional equity. This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 3,398 critical EMS cases recorded in 2023 across five regions (Riyadh, Makkah, Madinah, Dammam, and Asir) using Saudi Red Crescent Authority registry data. Response time was defined as the interval from call receipt to EMS arrival at the scene. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize response durations and resource distribution. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey’s post hoc test assessed regional differences, while logistic regression was used to examine regional differences in the probability of timely EMS arrival. More than 88% of responses exceeded 8 min across all five regions. Among delayed responses (> 8 min), mean response times ranged from approximately 14.4 ± 5.7 min in Dammam to over 17 min in the other regions. Dammam demonstrated significantly shorter response times than Riyadh, Makkah, Madinah, and Asir (all p < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis also demonstrated significant regional differences in the probability of timely EMS arrival, with Makkah showing the highest odds relative to Madinah, the reference region. Substantial differences in EMS performance were observed across the five regions studied, with all regions systematically exceeding the 8-min benchmark. Improving response efficiency may require region-specific strategies that extend beyond resource expansion, including optimized deployment models, infrastructure planning, and technology-enabled dispatch systems. Strengthening EMS should be regarded as a public health priority that supports progress toward the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69365-x.title: Neuromodulated state space models: a dopamine-inspired selective gating framework with memory–stability trade-offs
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69365-x.abstract: Dopamine shapes how the prefrontal cortex filters incoming information, maintains it in working memory, and releases it for action — three computational roles that closely parallel the input, state, and output stages of a sequence model. Here we ask whether formalizing this correspondence yields a sequence architecture that is both computationally competitive and mechanistically interpretable in biological terms. We introduce the Neuromodulated State Space Model (NeuSSM), which reinterprets the selective gating mechanism of modern state space models (e.g., Mamba) as three dopamine-inspired operators — sensory gating, working-memory modulation, and output relay — controlled by a single learnable gain parameter λ. We show theoretically that the classical S4 model arises as a limiting case of NeuSSM at λ = 0 (Theorem 1), and that NeuSSM’s local dynamical stability is governed by a phase-transition criterion based on the real part of the modulated state-transition eigenvalues, which partitions the model’s worst-case behavior into three qualitatively distinct regimes (Theorem 2). Mamba-style selective architectures are recovered qualitatively as λ → 1, though we present this correspondence empirically rather than as a formal approximation guarantee. Training NeuSSM on four long-range sequence benchmarks (≈ 0.45 M parameters, single consumer GPU), we find that the model learns different λ values in different layers depending on the task, with tasks requiring more flexible, long-range reasoning driving higher λ in upper layers — a pattern consistent with the proposed dynamical-stability trade-off (Theorem 2). NeuSSM reaches 98.75% on Sequential MNIST, 49.45% on LRA ListOps, 59.88% on Sequential CIFAR-10, and 76.0% on LRA Text, competitive with or approaching much larger S4 and Mamba baselines at a fraction of the parameter count. These results suggest that neuromodulatory principles from systems neuroscience can inform both the design and the interpretation of sequence models, even at modest computational scale.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69889-2.title: Early radiographic response after root canal treatment in type 2 diabetes and low vitamin D status: a prospective cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69889-2.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) and low vitamin D status (LVD) may influence periapical disease, but their relationship with early radiographic response after root canal treatment (RCT) remains uncertain. This prospective observational cohort included 473 adults classified as control (n = 119), DM (n = 119), LVD without DM (n = 122), or DM with LVD (n = 113). Participant-level treatment need was determined clinically and radiographically. Among 151 treated-tooth records from 133 participants, 132 records from 118 participants had 6-month radiographs. Participant-level treatment need was higher in the DM and DM + LVD strata than in the control and LVD strata, whereas the two diabetes strata did not differ after Holm correction. A Periapical Index (PAI) decrease of at least one category occurred in 20/26 control, 19/25 DM, 32/45 LVD, and 23/36 DM + LVD records (p = 0.651). Complete early radiographic resolution (PAI = 1) occurred in 19/26 (73.1%), 7/25 (28.0%), 41/45 (91.1%), and 10/36 (27.8%), respectively (p < 0.001); the two diabetes strata did not differ. In an exploratory participant-clustered analysis, each 1% higher baseline glycated haemoglobin was associated with lower odds of PAI = 1 at 6 months (odds ratio 0.44, 95% confidence interval 0.28–0.67). This association remained in analyses additionally adjusted for age and sex and when records lost to follow-up were classified as non-resolution. The independent effect of vitamin D could not be determined because supplementation was initiated after enrolment in most participants with low baseline vitamin D. Trial registration: Clinical Trials Registry-India, CTRI/2025/05/087830; registered on 28/05/2025. Recruitment began in June 2025, after registration.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66843-0.title: D2RP-Net: dual-dynamics-based rumor propagation prediction network
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66843-0.abstract: In the era of digital connectivity, social media, as a powerful information transmission medium, weaves a complex web of propagation networks. This unprecedented speed of information flow, while facilitating efficient communication, also gives rise to challenges that are difficult to control, especially in the field of rumor propagation prediction, which has become a core topic in cybersecurity research. However, the open nature of social platforms and the cascading effect of information diffusion make it exceptionally difficult to accurately predict the propagation path of rumors and their potential impact range. To address the limitations of existing models in deeply understanding the interplay between local and global features in rumor propagation, which restricts prediction accuracy and comprehensiveness, we have innovatively proposed a Dual-Dynamics-based Rumor Propagation Prediction Network (D2RP-Net). This method cleverly integrates a temporal attention point process and dynamic equations to capture the microscopic propagation patterns in the temporal diffusion network; at the same time, it leverages the powerful capabilities of hypergraph convolutional networks to analyze the macroscopic propagation characteristics of the diffusion network. Furthermore, we have carefully designed a feature decoupling module aimed at effectively separating the macro and micro elements in the rumor propagation features, thereby enabling multi-scale and more refined rumor propagation prediction tasks.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69495-2.title: An improved RT-DETR algorithm for small-object detection in UAV aerial images
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69495-2.abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of UAV aerial imagery, including the prevalence of small objects, complex background interference, and difficulty in feature extraction that lead to high missed detection rates and compromise detection accuracy in existing RT-DETR algorithms, this paper proposes an improved small-object-oriented detector named MSFE-DETR (Multi-Scale Feature Enhancement DETR). A CMFE (CSP-MultiScale Feature Enhancement) module is integrated into the shallow backbone layers to enhance feature representation of small objects and alleviate feature loss caused by scale and background complexity. In deeper layers of backbone, the C2f module is employed to preserve fine-grained details and improve target–background discrimination, while multi-scale feature fusion further prevents small object information degradation. In addition, Deformable Attention (DAttention) is incorporated to adaptively focus on small target regions, retaining spatial positional information and suppressing background noise. The head integrates MPCA and FSA modules, where MPCA progressively fuses adjacent-scale features to complementarily enhance small object representations and suppress background interference, and FSA further improves detail enhancement and robustness. Moreover, an Inner-SIoU loss is proposed by combining Inner-IoU with SIoU, improving localization accuracy, convergence speed, and robustness in complex scenes. Experimental results on the VisDrone 2019 dataset show that MSFE-DETR outperforms RT-DETR-r18 by 1.9% in Precision, 2.1% in Recall and 2.4% in mAP@0.5, while real-time inference is maintained at 68.7 FPS. On the infrared HIT-UAV and satellite SIMD datasets, mAP@0.5 improves by 5.8% and 2.3% respectively over the baseline.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68123-3.title: Robust dynamic pricing for bike sharing systems under willingness to pay uncertainty
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68123-3.abstract: Bike sharing systems are now an important part of city transport. Their pricing affects revenue, user access, and demand across busy and quiet periods. Many operators still use flat prices, although users may have different willingness to pay by time, trip type, and user group. This study aims to design a pricing model that captures this variation and also protects operators from errors in willingness to pay estimates. A robust linear programming model is developed and tested using 4,505,245 cleaned trips from the 2025 Capital Bikeshare dataset. The model builds willingness to pay uncertainty sets from revealed preference fares for different user segments and time periods. It is tested on a network of 20 origin-destination pairs, six time periods, and three user segments. The proposed model increases annual revenue by 13.5% on average compared with the flat rate baseline. Under reasonable elasticity settings, the revenue gain ranges from 11.8% to 15.2%. Revenue also remains stable under moderate uncertainty and stays higher than the flat rate baseline when robustness levels increase. The equity constrained version shows that access requirements can be maintained while still gaining revenue from dynamic pricing. These findings show that robust dynamic pricing can improve bike sharing revenue without ignoring affordability. The study also provides an empirical price of robustness curve for a real shared mobility network.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69986-2.title: Job satisfaction and its associated factors among medical and health officers in Northeastern Peninsular Malaysia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69986-2.abstract: In Malaysia, medical and health officers are essential to primary healthcare delivery, making their job satisfaction critical for enhancing engagement and commitment, which in turn improves healthcare quality. This study aimed to assess job satisfaction scores and identify associated factors among medical and health officers in Northeastern Peninsular Malaysia. A cross-sectional study involving 200 participants who were selected randomly from district health offices and a state health department was conducted. The Malay version of the Psychosocial Aspect of Work Questionnaire was utilized, measuring job satisfaction, social support, and mental stress. Multiple linear regression analyses were applied to identify the factors associated with job satisfaction scores. It was found that the mean (SD) job satisfaction score was 26.4 (4.7). Factors significantly associated with job satisfaction scores included satisfaction with income (adjusted regression coefficient, b = 1.218, 95% CI: 0.118, 2.317, p = 0.030), permanent employment status (b = 1.754, 95% CI: 0.104, 3.403, p = 0.037), and social support (b = 1.206, 95% CI: 0.979, 1.432, p < 0.001). In conclusion, satisfaction with income, permanent employment status, and social support were identified as significant factors associated with job satisfaction. These findings show the importance of addressing financial and employment stability, as well as linking a supportive work environment, to enhance job satisfaction among healthcare workers. Addressing these factors presents a plausible pathway that may support better professional engagement and commitment, which the broader literature frequently links to the overall quality of healthcare services.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69066-5.title: Covalent linkage of the papillomavirus E2 DNA-binding domain reveals a soluble amyloid-like assembly pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69066-5.abstract: Abstract Early soluble intermediates in amyloid formation are difficult to characterize because they are transient and obscured by competing insoluble aggregation. Here, we use scE2C, an engineered covalently linked version of the HPV16 E2 DNA-binding dimer, as a tractable model to stabilize and characterize soluble amyloid-like assemblies that are poorly resolved in the native dimeric protein. Whereas native E2C progresses toward visible insoluble aggregation upon heating, scE2C undergoes an irreversible transition to a soluble β-rich state. This state displays amyloid-sensitive signatures, including enhanced thioflavin T fluorescence, a Congo Red spectral shift, and increased ANS binding. Dynamic light scattering and atomic force microscopy revealed soluble assemblies comprising small spherical particles, larger spherical particles, and worm-like protofibrillar structures, which were further visualized by negative-stain and cryo-electron microscopy. Quantitative comparison of DLS- and AFM-derived dimensions supports a hierarchical organization in which smaller spherical particles behave as building blocks for larger particles and necklace-like worms. Isothermal circular dichroism kinetics across concentration and temperature were consistent with an assembly-coupled structural transition, with an apparent low-order nucleus of approximately 2 ± 1 scE2C protomeric units and growth compatible with low-order addition. Specific DNA binding fully inhibited the thermal transition, indicating that access to this protofibrillar branch is constrained by the functional DNA-bound state. Together, these results support the view that covalent linkage of the E2C dimer can provide experimental access to soluble early amyloid-like assembly states under conditions where native E2C progresses toward insoluble aggregation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62627-8.title: STAT3-derived EIF4E3 promotes H2O2-induced human trabecular meshwork cell injury by activating TGF-β-SMAD2/3 pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62627-8.abstract: The dysfunction of HTM cells involves key functions in the pathogenesis of glaucoma. In this study, we aimed to explore the functions of EIF4E3 and its regulatory mechanism in HTM cell injury, thereby illustrating the potential role of EIF4E3 in glaucoma. H2O2-treated HTM cells were adopted to mimic the glaucoma pathological condition in vitro. Functional experiments were performed using MTT, EdU, and flow cytometry assays, respectively. Oxidative stress was assessed by measuring the levels of superoxide dismutase (SOD) and malondialdehyde (MDA). The interaction between STAT3 and EIF4E3 was verified using dual-luciferase reporter and ChIP assays. EIF4E3 expression was increased in HTM cells after H2O2 treatment. Functionally, EIF4E3 knockdown reversed H2O2-induced HTM cell apoptosis, oxidative injury and fibrotic changes. Mechanistically, STAT3 promoted EIF4E3 expression by binding to the promoter of EIF4E3. STAT3 could abolish H2O2-induced HTM cell injury, which was rescued by EIF4E3 up-regulation. In addition, STAT3 bound to EIF4E3 to active the TGF-β-SMAD2/3 pathway. The inhibitor of TGF-β receptor I kinase SD-208 could abate EIF4E3 elevation-evoked boost on H2O2-induced HTM cell injury. STAT3 bound to EIF4E3 to active TGF-β-SMAD2/3 pathway, and then promoted H2O2-induced apoptosis, oxidative injury and fibrosis in HTM cells.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64699-y.title: Clinical validation of a handheld structured light device for 3D facial morphometric
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64699-y.abstract: Abstract Handheld systems for three-dimensional (3D) imaging of facial soft tissues are gaining increasing attention due to their affordability, portability, and user-friendliness. However, their reliability for 3D facial analysis should be verified before being integrated into clinical and research settings. We tested a novel device, the Revopoint MIRACO Pro, on 55 adults and a mannequin head, and we compared it with two validated devices. Intra- and inter-instrument reliability for traditional anthropometric parameters was evaluated through several statistical approaches. Additionally, the Root Mean Square (RMS) point-to-point distance was calculated between 3D images acquired through the different devices. Overall, all three instruments consistently reproduced the 3D facial structure across subjects, with 25 out of 27 measurements demonstrating high intra- and inter-device agreement and non-clinically significant biases. Furthermore, surface area assessments proved highly reliable, whereas volume measurements did not, and the RMS showed clinically acceptable congruence with slight variability caused by facial mimicry and involuntary movements of participants. Despite its affordability and practicality, the Revopoint MIRACO Pro requires multiple scans around the face, causing motion artifacts that may limit its applicability in less cooperative cohorts, such as children or patients with cognitive and neurological impairments, unless further validation studies demonstrate its clinical suitabilityin these groups.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68317-9.title: Secure network forensic investigation framework with elliptic curve cryptography-based encryption and enhanced message digest integrity verification
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68317-9.abstract: Forensic evidence can be easily altered or disclosed to those who are not authorized, which reduces the evidence integrity, reliability, and admissibility in cyber forensic investigation. Current forensic approaches are mostly concerned with evidence collection and analysis, and give little attention to ensuring evidence transmission is secure. In this paper, a secure network forensic investigation framework is proposed that combines proactive and reactive forensic modules and means of providing network confidentiality and integrity protection. This framework uses an improved Koblitz encoding with Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) to ensure the security of the transmission of forensic evidence, such as text, images and digital files. A lightweight three-cycle hashing mechanism is embedded to enhance integrity check and resistance against tampering with low computational cost. Architecture is designed for resource-constrained forensic environments and helps reduce computational and storage needs while maintaining security. The datasets consisted of text, images and digital files of different sizes and were subjected to experimental evaluation. The proposed framework successfully implemented the encoding, decoding, encryption, decryption and integrity checking for all type of evidence. The proposed hashing mechanism reduced the computational time of hash by around 20% compared to SHA-256 with a satisfactory integrity check. Moreover, the ECC-based approach provided security similar to RSA with much smaller key sizes, saving not only in computation costs, but in storage as well. The results show that the proposed framework is efficient, lightweight and integrated solution for secure transmission and verification of forensic evidence in resource constrained cyber forensic environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55486-w.title: Explainable and domain-adaptive prediction models for refrigerant charging in air conditioning systems within industrial processes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55486-w.abstract: Accurate prediction of refrigerant deficiency in consumer air conditioning (AC) systems is critical for optimizing energy efficiency and operational stability. However, existing data-driven models often suffer from significant performance degradation due to domain shift across different AC types and a lack of explanatory transparency. To address these challenges, we propose AC-RPX (AC-Refrigerant Prediction eXplainable AI), a unified framework that integrates a Domain Encoder augmented with domain-specific tokens and a Large Language Model (LLM) adapted via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). The Domain Encoder aligns sensor distributions across six consumer AC types to enable domain-robust refrigerant level prediction. Simultaneously, the LoRA-tuned LLM, trained on 280,000 expert-aligned sensor–reasoning pairs, generates case-specific chain-of-thought (CoT) explanations that explicitly link abnormal sensor patterns to the predicted refrigerant charge state. Validation on six AC sensor datasets demonstrates that AC-RPX achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and F1 scores, significantly outperforming conventional deep learning and domain adaptation baselines. Moreover, by providing intuitive natural language explanations, AC-RPX improves predictive performance over conventional rule-based heuristic methods while providing clearer diagnostic explanations on real-world consumer data. These results establish AC-RPX as a practical solution for automated refrigerant monitoring and decision support in real-world maintenance services.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69175-1.title: Long-term outcomes of capsular tension ring implantation during phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation combined with trabeculectomy in acute angle-closure crisis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69175-1.abstract: To evaluate the 3-year efficacy and safety of capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation during phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation (PEI) combined with trabeculectomy (Trab) in patients with acute angle-closure crisis (AACC). Retrospective cohort study. Patients who underwent PEI+Trab were divided into two groups according to whether they received concurrent CTR implantation. Postoperative clinical indicators were collected at 1, 3, 12, 24, and 36 months and compared between the CTR and non-CTR groups. Uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), best-corrected distance visual acuity (BCDVA), refractive prediction error (PE), intraocular lens (IOL) tilt, intraocular pressure (IOP), anterior chamber depth (ACD), corneal endothelial cell density (ECD), and complication rates. Among 114 eyes of 114 patients with AACC, 54 received CTR implantation and 60 did not. Three-year follow-up was completed in 68.4% of patients. At 3 years, UDVA was significantly better in the CTR group than in the non-CTR group (median [IQR] 0.22 [0.10–0.30] vs. 0.30 [0.22–0.60]; P = 0.02) and remained stable throughout follow-up. In contrast, UDVA in the non-CTR group fluctuated markedly and did not stabilize until 2 years after surgery. BCDVA was comparable between groups (median [IQR] 0.10 [0.00–0.16] vs. 0.10 [0.00–0.26]; P = 0.41). PE was consistently lower in the CTR group (0.32 ± 0.73 D vs. 0.77 ± 0.88 D; P = 0.03), and IOL tilt was also significantly reduced (median [IQR] 0.16° [0.12–0.29] vs. 0.42° [0.31–0.61]; P < 0.001). ACD and ECD did not differ significantly between groups (ACD: 3.55 ± 2.86 mm vs. 3.54 ± 2.59 mm, P = 0.85; ECD: 1410.05 ± 470.19 vs. 1558.98 ± 405.97 cells/mm², P = 0.14). IOP remained similar between groups at all time points over the 3-year follow-up (all P > 0.05). The CTR group showed a significantly lower incidence of CCS (0% vs. 20.6%; P = 0.01). However, rates of IOL pupil capture (19.4% vs. 2.9%; P = 0.03) and YAG laser capsulotomy for PCO (40.7% vs. 23.3%; P = 0.046) were higher in the CTR group. One patient in each group required reoperation. The proportion of patients requiring long-term antiglaucoma medications did not differ significantly between groups (9.7% vs. 2.9%; P = 0.26). In AACC patients undergoing PEI+Trab, CTR implantation reduces IOL tilt and PE, improves long-term refractive stability, thereby optimizing long-term UDVA, and lowers CCS risk without compromising IOP control or ACD stability. However, the higher incidences of IOL capture and YAG laser capsulotomy for PCO in the CTR group warrant further clinical investigation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69455-w.title: Adhesive phosphopullulan gel supports bone regeneration with 50% replacement of autologous bone volume in alveolar cleft repair
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69455-w.abstract: Alveolar cleft repair traditionally relies on autologous bone grafting, which is limited by donor-site morbidity, graft availability, and displacement. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of a bioresorbable phosphopullulan (PPL) gel for alveolar cleft repair in preclinical models. Biological safety was assessed according to ISO 10993 guidelines, including cytotoxicity, genotoxicity, sensitization, pyrogenicity, irritation, and systemic toxicity. Osteocompatibility and resorption were evaluated using rabbit bone defect and tooth-erupting alveolar cleft models. The PPL gel showed excellent biocompatibility without adverse biological responses. Although small fragments were detected in the lungs under exaggerated implantation conditions, no pulmonary injury or inflammation was observed; distribution was negligible under clinically relevant conditions. In bone implantation models, the PPL gel demonstrated retention of graft materials, osteoconductivity, and progressive bioresorption, supporting sustained bone formation. In the alveolar cleft model, replacing 50% of the autologous bone graft with PPL gel did not show an apparent adverse effect on bone formation or tooth eruption at 4 weeks compared with autologous bone grafting alone. These findings indicate that PPL gel is a safe and promising bone augmentation material that supports bone regeneration and may reduce graft displacement and the amount of autologous bone required, warranting further translational investigation.
