doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69505-3.title: The plasma protein profile of left ventricular diastolic function
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69505-3.abstract: Abstract We aimed to characterize associations between plasma proteins and indices of left ventricular (LV) diastolic function in two population-based studies. Eighty-six cardiovascular-related plasma proteins measured by proximity extension assay (PEA) and echocardiography were assessed in the population-based studies PIVUS ( n = 1,016; all aged 70) and POEM ( n = 502; all aged 50). PIVUS served as the discovery cohort, and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false-discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05. POEM was used as the replication cohort. The protein panel was related to diastolic echocardiographic parameters. A larger protein panel of 1,322 proteins was examined only in POEM. Seven of 86 proteins showed replicated associations to the E/A ratio: CD40 ligand (CD40LG), proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase Src (SRC), heat shock protein beta-1 (HSPB1), epidermal growth factor (EGF), TNF superfamily member 14 (TNFSF14), vascular endothelial growth factor D (VEGFD), and endothelial cell-specific molecule 1 (ESM1). Using the larger protein panel in POEM, 81 proteins showed significant associations with the E/A ratio, and five showed significant associations with LA diameter. Pathways linked to LV diastolic filling pattern were signal transduction, metabolic, disease and immune system pathways, enhancing the understanding of LV diastolic function and offering potential for future drug development.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69347-z.title: Upcycling PET waste into porous activated carbon via KOH activation using microwave-assisted and conventional direct thermal approaches
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69347-z.abstract: Abstract The increasing accumulation of plastic waste, especially polyethylene terephthalate (PET), raises serious environmental concerns. This study investigates the conversion of PET waste into activated carbon using Direct Thermal Activation (DTA) and Microwave-Assisted Activation (MAA) methods. Production was optimized by varying the KOH to PET mass ratio (1:1 to 3:1) in DTA, and microwave power (600–900 W) with irradiation times (30–60 min) in MAA. The resulting carbons were characterized by BET, TGA/DSC, FESEM-EDX, FTIR, zeta potential, and X-ray fluorescence (XRF). MAA yielded higher carbon production efficiency (57% vs. 29%), whereas DTA achieved a much larger surface area (2035 vs. 371 m 2 /g). Morphological analysis showed that MAA produced smaller and more uniform pores. Elemental analysis confirmed increased carbon content and decreased oxygen in both methods, indicating effective carbonization. XRF analysis verified the high elemental purity of the synthesized carbons, revealing low concentrations of inorganic impurities (e.g., Si, Al, Fe, and Sb). TGA results indicated higher thermal stability for MAA samples, with a decomposition peak at 607–624 °C compared to DTA samples (600 °C). Zeta potential measurements indicated acidic surface groups, with higher microwave power enhancing reactivity and lowering the pH pzc . Consequently, while DTA produces carbons with superior surface area and microporosity, the MAA method is a more efficient alternative due to its significantly reduced processing time and higher product yield. Therefore, the choice of method depends on the target application and its priorities.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66153-5.title: An experimental analysis of diesel engine characteristics using diesel-cetane improver blends
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66153-5.abstract: The majority of the previous studies which use a cetane enhancer (CE) with diesel engine fuels are based on diesel-biodiesel or diesel-alcohol fuel blends, where the addition of biodiesel/alcohol fuel to neat diesel (D100) reduces its cetane number significantly. The studies which investigate diesel engine performance using CE blended with D100 are scarce in the reported literature. This study is aimed at bridging this research gap, by investigating diesel engine outcomes using D100 fuel blended di-tert-butyl peroxide (DTBP); a CE which was added to D100 in proportions of 0.7% and 1.5% by volume respectively. Experiments were performed at 80% engine load and varying engine speed. The results demonstrate that increasing engine speed worsens engine performance and emission characteristics due to shorter cycle time and increased friction losses. The addition of DTBP is found to be highly effective in terms of improving engine performance and emission characteristics except smoke emissions especially at higher engine speeds. However, the effectiveness of DTBP in terms of lowering the ignition delay (ID) declines when its concentration in D100 is increased from 0.7% to 1.5% compared to the case when it is added to D100 by 0.7%. At 1600 rpm, the addition of DTBP by 1.5% into D100 reduces brake specific fuel consumption (BSFC) by 5.4% while carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen oxides (NOx) and hydrocarbon (HC) emissions dropped by 65.0%, 15.8% and 45.7% respectively. However, smoke emissions are increased due to the addition of CE to D100.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67163-z.title: Correction: The mediating role of sleep quality between pre-sleep portable media device use and nursing performance
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67163-z.abstract: Scientific Reports - Correction: The mediating role of sleep quality between pre-sleep portable media device use and nursing performance

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68442-5.title: Two distinct domains in mouse IG-DMR of the Dlk1–Dio3 locus confer imprinted DNA methylation in transgenic mice
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68442-5.abstract: Abstract Faithful maintenance of allele-specific methylation at imprinting control regions (ICR) is essential for genomic imprinting. Using transgenic mice (TgM), we investigated sequence requirements for paternal methylation acquisition and maternal hypomethylation maintenance during early embryogenesis. We previously showed that a 2.9-kb mouse H19 ICR acquires post-fertilization paternal allele-specific DNA methylation via a critical 118-bp region; its deletion from the endogenous H19 ICR abolishes maintenance of germ cell-established paternal methylation. In contrast, TgM with the 2.8-kb rat H19 ICR ortholog failed to acquire post-fertilization imprinted methylation. Although another paternally methylated ICR, the IG-DMR of the Dlk1–Dio3 locus, acquired paternal methylation post-fertilization in TgM, the imprinted state was lost due to maternal de novo methylation post-implantation. Here, we extended previously analyzed ICR sequences to reexamine conservation of the activity across different species and genomic loci. Extending the rat H19 ICR upstream to include candidate cis -motifs still failed to establish imprinted methylation. Conversely, TgM with an extended mouse IG-DMR sequence protected maternal IG-DMR from genome-wide de novo DNA methylation after implantation, maintaining its imprinted DNA methylation state. This finding provides the first in vivo evidence for a bipartite IG-DMR model: 5′ domain for paternal methylation acquisition and 3′ domain for maternal hypomethylation maintenance.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67012-z.title: Research on cross-domain multimodal feature fusion method for ground moving target recognition
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67012-z.abstract: Target recognition of unattended system plays an essential role in guarding key areas. Most of the existing studies based on acoustic and seismic fusion only conduct single-modal analysis on the sensing signals, which leads to the problem of single and one-sided feature extraction, seriously affecting the accuracy of classification and recognition. In this paper, an UGS system specifically designed for collecting seismic and acoustic signals is constructed, and a cross-domain multimodal feature fusion network architecture is proposed. Firstly, based on the different sensing characteristics of acoustic signals and vibration signals, time–frequency graph data are obtained respectively through MEL spectrum calculation and Continuous Wavelet Transform, and the information expression of sensing signals is enriched through time–frequency conversion. Secondly, the time series is input into the Long Short-Term Memory network to extract the time-domain features, and the time–frequency graph is input into the VGG-19 network to extract deep image features. In this way, rich feature information can be extracted and the differences in multimodal data features can be alleviated. The accuracy of the proposed network reached 98.17% on the self-built acoustic-seismic data set. Compared with the single-modal network, the performance of the multi-modal fusion network is significantly improved.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69137-7.title: Assessment of quality of life, burnout and cardiovascular risk factors among French radiologists
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69137-7.abstract: Radiology has historically been perceived as a relatively comfortable specialty with limited clinical pressure. However, increasing imaging demand, evolving working conditions, and the expansion of interventional radiology may have substantially transformed its practice. This study aimed to assess cardiovascular risk factors, quality of life, and burnout among radiologists and to compare them with those of other specialties. In 2025, a 34-item electronic survey was distributed to practitioners across 15 French academic centers. Participants were categorized into radiology, non-radiological diagnostic specialties, medical, and surgical groups. The questionnaire assessed cardiovascular risk factors, quality of life parameters, and burnout dimensions. Between-group comparisons were performed using appropriate parametric or non-parametric statistical tests. A total of 183 participants were included: 120 radiologists (including 62 interventional radiologists) and 63 physicians from other specialties. Radiologists reported a significantly higher on-call burden than non-radiological diagnostic specialties and medical specialties (P<.001 and P=.050, respectively). Severe or extreme self-reported anxiety or depression symptoms were reported by 9/120 radiologists (7.5%) and by 2/63 (3.2%) among non-radiologists. Interventional radiologists had significantly higher working hours (P=.014) and more on-call duties (P=.001) than diagnostic radiologists. None of the assessed cardiovascular risk factors or MBI-HSS dimensions differed significantly between radiologists and other specialties or between diagnostic and interventional radiologists. No statistically significant differences in cardiovascular risk factors or burnout were detected between radiologists and other specialties, although the limited sample size warrants cautious interpretation of these findings. However, they had a higher workload than medical and non-radiological diagnostic specialties, with interventional radiologists experiencing the highest levels. Attention to anxiety and depression symptoms among radiologists is warranted.

doi:10.1038/s41598-025-26610-z.title: Enhanced lung cancer detection using BiLSTM attention and transformer models on clinical text data
doi:10.1038/s41598-025-26610-z.abstract: Lung cancer continues to be a major cause of death globally, making early and precise detection crucial for improving patient outcomes. In this research, we introduce an enhanced method for predicting and detecting lung cancer by combining Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks with an attention mechanism and transformer-based models. This hybrid model effectively tackles common issues such as overfitting, data imbalance, and long-sequence dependencies in textual clinical data. A well-curated dataset of patient medical records, including demographics, symptoms, radiology reports, and other clinical information, was used to assess the model’s performance. The experimental results showed a marked improvement in prediction accuracy, with the proposed model achieving 99.8% accuracy and significantly lowering validation loss to 0.3112, outperforming existing systems. The incorporation of attention mechanisms with BiLSTM and transformer models improved the model’s ability to focus on critical clinical features, thus enhancing its generalization capabilities. Additionally, the model’s faster training time (13.99 s) demonstrates its practicality for clinical use, particularly in resource-constrained settings. While the results are promising, potential overfitting due to the small dataset suggests further research with larger datasets and advanced regularization methods is needed. This research highlights the potential of advanced deep learning techniques in lung cancer detection, providing a robust, efficient, and accurate tool that can be integrated into clinical decision-making processes to enable timely and accurate diagnoses.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69226-7.title: Experimental study of pressure drop in traditional and modified labyrinth seals of Francis turbine
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69226-7.abstract: Abstract Labyrinth seals are primary non-contact seals used to minimise leakage losses between high and low-pressure regions in Francis turbines. This paper describes the development of an experimental setup (consisting of piping method and pressure sensors) for measuring the pressure drop across simple or traditional straight-through (Seal1) and modified labyrinth seals (Seal2). The study aims to verify the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) approach for predicting the pressure drop in labyrinth seals with experimental measurements. The experimental study utilises pressure sensors to investigate pressure data for flow rates of 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 L/s, with a speed range from 0 to 600 rpm. The data are recorded using the LabVIEW program. The study revealed a gradual increase in pressure drop for the lower rotational speed of (0–200) rpm, and then a steeper rise in pressure drop for higher rotational speed above 300 rpm in both Seal1 and Seal2, indicating increased turbulence, vortex formation and energy dissipation within the seal. Similarly, higher flow rates result in significantly larger pressure losses, indicating a strong dependence on flow rate. Moreover, the pressure drop provided by the modified seal is comparatively lower than that of a straight-through unilateral seal due to the difference in cavity shape and clearance gap between the seals. The comparison of CFD predictions and experimental data, collected using both pipe-based and sensor-based measurement approaches for both seal configurations (Seal1 and Seal2), revealed good agreement across all operating conditions, with an uncertainty of 0 to 8%.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69731-9.title: Navigating foundation model selection in digital pathology through performance evaluation and tradeoff analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69731-9.abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital pathology foundation models (FMs), spanning widely in architectural scale, pretraining data, and training strategy, poses a practical challenge for selecting the optimal model for a specific clinical application. To systematically evaluate these trade-offs, We benchmarked 6 FMs representing different model tiers and design profiles, including Lunit, Kaiko-Base, Phikon-v2, UNI2, Virchow2, and Kaiko-Midnight, across whole-slide image (WSI)-level classification, WSI-level survival prediction, and region-of-interest (ROI)-level classification tasks. Our results show that model performance is strongly task-specific, challenging the assumption that larger models are universally better. At the WSI level, Camelyon16 lymph node metastasis detection showed near-ceiling performance across models; Virchow2 achieved the highest observed AUROC and a statistically significant but small difference from the runner-up. For NSCLC subtype classification, Phikon-v2 achieved the highest observed AUROC, although its difference from the runner-up was not statistically significant. For NSCLC survival prediction, Lunit, the smallest model evaluated, achieved the highest observed five-fold cross-validated mean C-index and lowest mean rank, while Kaiko-Base provided the most stable prognostic performance; however, matched-fold analysis did not establish statistically significant superiority. ROI-level classification was evaluated using macro-averaged one-vs-rest AUROC. BACH and TCGA-UT showed near-ceiling performance among the leading models, whereas UNITOPATHO remained more discriminative and showed the clearest statistically supported separation, with Kaiko-Midnight significantly exceeding the runner-up Lunit. Kaiko-Midnight also achieved the highest observed AUROC on TCGA-UT, but its difference from UNI2 was not statistically significant. The Kaiko-Base versus Kaiko-Midnight comparison further showed that a larger model within a related development lineage can achieve higher observed ROI-level AUROC for selected tasks without necessarily improving WSI-level classification or survival prediction. Quantitative embedding-extraction benchmarking also revealed substantial deployment-relevant efficiency differences, with Kaiko-Midnight showing markedly lower throughput than Lunit under maximum feasible batch-size evaluation. Finally, training-data fraction ablations with 50 random seeds per fraction showed that model rankings can shift across data regimes and that low-data settings introduce substantial variability, particularly for WSI-level AMIL training. Together, these findings support a task- and data-regime-aware framework for selecting digital pathology FMs, balancing predictive performance, statistical uncertainty, stability, computational efficiency, and deployment cost.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67519-5.title: Current and future climate hazards for targeting adaptation in pigs in South Asia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67519-5.abstract: Climate change is reshaping thermal and hydro-climatological extremes across South Asia, with direct implications for livestock systems. Like other livestock species, these changes can significantly alter the pig production system. This may impact the availability of animal-source foods for human consumption in the future. We undertake a high-resolution mapping (0.05 degrees) of four major climate hazards: heat stress (measured using the THI metric), cold stress, rainfall deficit, and excess rainfall in current and future climate, in addition to static (baseline) cyclone and flood layers. Baseline hazards are derived from observation‑driven temperature, precipitation, and humidity data. Future projections for the 2050s and 2080s are constructed using five bias‑corrected climate models under two climate change scenarios (SSP2-4.5: middle-of-the-road scenario and SSP5-8.5: high-emission scenario), applied as median deltas to the baseline. We compute intensity and frequency metrics for each hazard. Adaptation suitability is then mapped for 13 options identified through a literature review and multi‑country expert consultations. Heat-stress emerges as the dominant forward‑looking risk. The share of pigs exposed to medium–very high heat stress increases by ~ 32–63% across scenarios, whereas exposure to high cold‑stress declines by ~ 12–78%. Exposure of pigs to extreme rainfall events is projected to increase substantially by the 2080s, while rainfall-deficit exposure shows little net change. Suitability mapping points to shelter modification and climate‑resilient breeding as cross‑hazard options in areas of high heat stress, with mineral supplementation, microclimate protection, water/cooling access, and insurance enhancing resilience portfolios. Our results provide spatially explicit adaptation, prioritisation and targeting the investments by governments and industry.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67696-3.title: Integrating macroeconomic and technical indicators into forecasting the stock market: a hybrid approach for efficient feature selection
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67696-3.abstract: Abstract Stock market prediction is a significant research topic in the financial sector and has been widely investigated by researchers and investors. Forecasting stock markets is challenging because of the nonlinearity, volatility, and dynamics of the data. Additionally, stock markets are affected by various internal and external factors. While most previous studies relied on historical prices and technical indicators (TIs), they ignored the influence of overall economic factors on stock markets. In contrast, this study introduces a robust framework to predict daily log returns by leveraging a combined dataset comprising historical data, TIs, and macroeconomic data, including gold and oil prices, the volatility index, the dollar index, the interest rate, the 10-year Treasury yield, the term spread, and the dividend yield. Moreover, we propose a hybrid feature selection (FS) approach that combines filter and wrapper methods, unlike in previous studies, which relied primarily on a single FS approach or neglected it entirely. The dataset represents diverse sectors and firm sizes, covering five companies: Apple (AAPL Inc.), Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM), Goldman Sachs (GS), Pfizer Inc. (PFE), and Ford Motor Company (F). We apply a hybrid evaluation approach that incorporates 5-fold time series cross-validation (TSCV) with a holdout test set to evaluate the efficiency of the proposed models. The results revealed that despite modest improvements in statistical metrics, FS significantly enhanced the economic performance of the trading strategy, as demonstrated by better returns and Sharpe ratios. The results show that deep learning (DL) models that combine macroeconomic data and the FS process, in addition to historical data and TIs, achieved higher trading returns and produced superior risk-adjusted performance, although they demonstrated slightly higher forecast errors than traditional models. This confirms that statistical accuracy alone is insufficient for evaluating financial forecasting models. This work highlights the benefits of the proposed framework for predicting stock returns across different markets, offering significant insights for financial analysts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69787-7.title: KELM transmission line fault location method incorporating uncertainty estimation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69787-7.abstract: With the widespread application of flexible direct current transmission (MMC-HVDC) in the interconnection of large power grids and the consumption of new energy, the accuracy, reliability, and response speed of transmission line fault location are of crucial importance for the safe operation of the system. To address the issues of noise sensitivity and difficulty in characterizing uncertainty in traditional traveling wave localization methods, the paper proposes a kernel extreme learning machine (KELM) fault localization method that introduces uncertainty estimation. This method first constructs a ± 500 kV MMC-HVDC system simulation model on the PSCAD/EMTDC platform, collects traveling wave signals under different fault conditions, and extracts time-frequency features using wavelet denoising and fixed parameter VMD techniques; Subsequently, a KELM model based on BWO (Beluga Whale Optimization) optimization was constructed to globally optimize the kernel width σ and penalty coefficient C, achieving high-precision regression mapping. In order to further enhance the engineering interpretability of the results, an uncertainty estimation module is introduced to provide confidence intervals and credibility evaluations for the predicted output. Unlike conventional optimized machine-learning-based fault location methods that mainly focus on improving point prediction accuracy, the proposed framework jointly considers traveling-wave feature robustness, KELM hyperparameter optimization, and prediction credibility representation. Therefore, the novelty of this work lies not in the independent use of wavelet denoising, VMD, KELM, or BWO, but in their coordinated integration with uncertainty-aware fault location for MMC-HVDC transmission lines. The simulation results show that the proposed method has an average absolute error (MAE) of only 0.19 km and a 95% confidence interval coverage rate of 95.8%. Under complex operating conditions such as low signal-to-noise ratio (30 dB) and high transition resistance (300Ω), the positioning error is still controlled within 0.31 km, which is significantly better than traditional ELM, KELM, and PSO-KELM methods, verifying the accuracy, robustness, and practicality of the proposed method.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68921-9.title: Model-based comparison of latency estimation methods for the pupillary light reflex
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68921-9.abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of pupillary light reflex (PLR) latency is important in clinical and research settings, yet reported results are often difficult to compare due to differences in hardware, sampling rates, and analysis methods. This study introduces a systematic and reproducible benchmark for evaluating PLR latency estimation algorithms using synthetic data with known ground-truth latency. Synthetic pupillograms were generated using an established dynamic model of the PLR, extended to handle short light impulses. Five commonly used latency estimation methods were evaluated under these conditions, with 1000 traces simulated per configuration. Performance was assessed using the mean absolute error (MAE) between estimated and ground-truth latency. Across many conditions, a method developed by Bergamin and Kardon, combining filtering, interpolation, and analysis of the first and second derivatives achieved promising results, although its performance deteriorated under high noise and low-intensity stimuli. In contrast, a simple piecewise linear fit showed consistent, moderate performance across configurations. Threshold-based detection performed well for strong and medium stimuli but degraded for weak responses, while derivative-based and exponential curve-fitting approaches showed higher sensitivity to noise or stimulus conditions. For practical use, we recommend the Bergamin and Kardon method as the default choice, whereas the piecewise linear fit may be preferable when the hardware or measurement conditions are unknown, such as in cross-device smartphone applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69904-6.title: Effect of endodontic solvents on the push-out bond strength of premixed bioceramic sealer to root dentin: an in vitro study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69904-6.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of two gutta-percha solvents on the push-out bond strength of bioceramic sealer to root dentin. Forty-five extracted human single-rooted premolars with single canals were instrumented using the ProTaper Universal system and randomly assigned to three groups (n = 15): Endosolv, orange oil, and no-solvent (control). After 5-min solvent application and irrigation, canals were obturated with gutta-percha and TotalFill bioceramic sealer using the cold lateral compaction technique. Roots were sectioned horizontally and push-out bond strength was measured with a universal testing machine at a crosshead speed of 0.5 mm/min. Data were analyzed using ANOVA, Bonferroni tests, and linear mixed-effects model (α = 0.05). The orange oil group showed significantly lower bond strength than the Endosolv and control groups (P < .05), whereas no difference was observed between Endosolv and control. Bond strength increased from the coronal to apical thirds (P < .05) and showed a strong negative correlation with canal lumen diameter (r = − 0.976 to − 0.995, P < .001). Failure analysis revealed mainly cohesive failures in the control group and mixed failures in orange oil group. These findings indicate that orange oil significantly reduces the adhesion of the tested bioceramic sealer, whereas Endosolv has minimal influence.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68734-w.title: A Schrödinger and differential evolution framework for PID based liquid level control
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68734-w.abstract: In this study, a hybrid Schrödinger optimizer with differential evolution (h-SRADE) is proposed for optimal tuning of proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controllers applied to a three-tanks liquid level control system. The original Schrödinger optimizer (SRA), inspired by wave–particle duality and quantum mechanics principles, provides a balanced exploration–exploitation mechanism; however, its convergence sensitivity in the later optimization stages motivates further enhancement. To address this limitation, differential evolution mutation and crossover operators are embedded into the SRA framework, forming the proposed h-SRADE algorithm with improved refinement capability and convergence stability. The control problem is formulated using a linearized third-order model of the three-tanks liquid level system derived from mass balance principles. PID controller parameters are optimized by minimizing a composite fitness function that simultaneously accounts for percent overshoot, steady-state error, settling time, and rise time. The optimization process is conducted within predefined practical bounds to ensure controller feasibility and robust closed-loop operation. Extensive simulation studies are carried out to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. Statistical analysis, supported by a non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test, confirms the statistical significance and robustness of h-SRADE over the conventional SRA. Time-domain and frequency-domain analyses demonstrate that the h-SRADE-based PID controller achieves faster settling, reduced overshoot, lower steady-state error, and satisfactory robustness margins. Furthermore, comparative studies with several state-of-the-art optimization-based PID tuning approaches reported in the literature reveal that the proposed method provides superior dynamic performance and overall control quality. The obtained results indicate that the hybridization of the Schrödinger optimizer with differential evolution effectively enhances convergence behavior and control performance. Consequently, the proposed h-SRADE framework offers a reliable and efficient simulation-based solution for PID controller tuning in liquid level systems, providing a strong foundation for future extension toward nonlinear plant models, varying operating points, and other complex engineering control applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68968-8.title: A coupled oscillator based ising chip as a physical entropy source for hybrid true random number generation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68968-8.abstract: Abstract This work presents a dual-purpose Coupled Oscillator Based Ising (COBI) chip that serves as a combinatorial optimization problem (COP) solver and as a physical entropy source for a hybrid True Random Number Generator (TRNG). By disabling coupling weights, oscillator phases drift randomly, creating a physical entropy source for various probabilistic compute applications. To meet the statistical randomness and throughput requirements, we adopted a hybrid approach. Post-layout simulation and static timing analysis project an expanded-output throughput of 351 Mb/s at 0.9 V, corresponding to an estimated energy of 71.2 pJ/bit when using the measured COBI-chip power (Geffe-block power excluded). We report NIST SP 800-22 results for the output obtained by applying von Neumann correction in software after data collection, while the unconditioned raw output was evaluated using NIST SP 800-90B. The proposed TRNG approach was demonstrated in graph decomposers, enabling a real-world probabilistic computing application without the need for a separate physical entropy-source macro or a software algorithm generating pseudo random numbers.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69697-8.title: Revealing the phytochemical diversity and bioactive potential of caterpillar mushroom (Cordyceps militaris L.) using analytical techniques
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69697-8.abstract: Cordyceps militaris is a cultivated mushroom of growing interest for obtaining nutritionally relevant and bioactive components. The nutritional composition, mineral profile, selected bioactive compounds, and antioxidant activity of commercially cultivated C. militaris sourced from the Islamabad Mushroom Spawn Production Lab in Pakistan were characterized. AOAC methods were used to analyze the proximate composition; mineral contents were quantified; HPLC measured selected bioactive compounds; and TPC, TFC, DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP measured antioxidant activity. The fruiting bodies (FB) contained 35.19 ± 2.91% protein, 43.14 ± 0.90% carbohydrates, 7.49 ± 0.87% crude fiber, and 3.52 ± 0.15% crude fat, with an energy value of 390.91 ± 15 kcal/100 g. Phosphorus (8776 ± 69.1 mg/kg), magnesium (5641 ± 24.5 mg/kg), sulfur (4971 ± 15.0 mg/kg), and potassium (2234 ± 13.4 mg/kg) were the predominant minerals. The HPLC analysis revealed various bioactive compounds such as cordycepin (4.25 ± 0.65 mg/g), ergothioneine, cordycepic acid, phenolic content, quercetin, and antioxidant vitamins. The extract exhibited measurable antioxidant activity, with TPC and TFC values of 21.48 ± 1.10 mg GAE/g and 6.91 ± 0.45 mg QE/g, correspondingly, and DPPH, FRAP, and ABTS values of 14.9 ± 0.85 mg GAE/mL, 8.5 ± 0.53 µM Fe²⁺/g, and 0.60 ± 0.01 mg/mL, respectively. In all, the analyzed C. militaris was rich in nutrients and had a wide range of quantified bioactive components. The results obtained here could be used as compositional data for commercially grown C. militaris in Pakistan and could help its further assessment as a functional food and nutraceutical raw material. The results, however, are only a compositional and in vitro antioxidant evaluation and cannot prove bioavailability or therapeutic efficacy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67772-8.title: Deep learning for automatic segmentation of the gestational sac and yolk sac from 3D ultrasound in early pregnancy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67772-8.abstract: Abstract The current standard manual measurements from 2D ultrasound in the early weeks of pregnancy are operator-dependent and subject to inter- and intra-rater variability, particularly for the non-spherical gestational sac. This leads to diagnostic uncertainty, prolonged follow-up and patient anxiety. Several studies have proposed models for automatic standard plane selection and segmentation of the gestational sac from 2D ultrasound. However, these methods do not eliminate variability caused by natural differences in gestational sac shape. As 3D ultrasound is becoming increasingly accessible in the clinics, an automated method for 3D volumetric measurement would be beneficial for both patients and clinicians in terms of reproducibility, accuracy and ease of use. In this study, we trained deep learning models using the nnU-Net framework for automatic segmentation and volumetric measurement of the yolk sac and gestational sac in 3D ultrasound volumes of 42 women pregnant after assisted reproductive technology, for an initial feasibility assessment of automated volumetry in this setting. The best model performance was similar to the human intra-rater variability for the gestational sac, with median Dice scores of 92.2% versus 92.8%, while yolk sac segmentation remained more challenging, with median Dice scores of 84.3% versus 92.8%. Estimated volumes and diameters showed higher agreement with expert volumetric measurements than the manually measured 2D diameters did, with an improved intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) from 0.83 to 0.99 for the gestational sac, and comparable ICCs of 0.64 and 0.68 for the yolk sac. These results support the feasibility of automated 3D volumetry as a promising alternative to the current standard manual measurement method. The proposed method could potentially reduce examination time, facilitate new research on early pregnancy development, and in the future reduce the diagnostic uncertainty that leads to prolonged follow-up in early pregnancy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68570-y.title: Minimal-preprocessing paradigm for robust COVID-19 detection from cough audio using deep learning
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68570-y.abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the need for rapid, accessible, and non-invasive screening tools to complement conventional diagnostic methods. While audio-based analysis of cough signals has emerged as a promising approach, most existing studies rely on complex preprocessing pipelines aimed at noise suppression and signal enhancement. However, the impact of such preprocessing on model generalisation remains insufficiently understood. This study challenges the prevailing assumption that extensive preprocessing is necessary for robust audio-based diagnosis. We propose a systematic evaluation of preprocessing strategies, investigating whether minimal preprocessing can preserve diagnostically relevant acoustic information and improve model performance. Cough recordings were transformed into time–frequency representations using short-time Fourier transform (STFT) and Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) and classified using multiple convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, including ResNet, Inception, and MobileNet variants. Experimental results demonstrate that minimal preprocessing using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) without additional filtering consistently outperforms conventional noise-reduction techniques. The best-performing model, ResNet50V2, achieved a testing accuracy of 86.79%, with balanced precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score. Furthermore, the combination of STFT and MFCC features provided complementary information, improving classification robustness. These findings indicate that preserving full spectral information is critical for effective deep learning–based audio diagnosis, and that aggressive preprocessing may inadvertently suppress subtle pathological signatures. This work establishes a minimal-preprocessing paradigm for cough-based COVID-19 detection and provides practical insights for developing robust, scalable, and non-invasive diagnostic systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69830-7.title: Higher hip flexion decreases tensor fascia latae activation and increases GMed: TFL ratio during seated abduction machine
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69830-7.abstract: Joint position influences neuromuscular recruitment and may affect exercise prescription. This study investigated how hip flexion angle affects electromyographic (EMG) activity of the gluteus medius (GMed) and tensor fasciae latae (TFL) during machine-based seated hip abduction. Twelve recreationally trained participants performed the exercise at 45°, 90°, and 135° of hip flexion with a load corresponding to 60% of their individual six-repetition maximum (6RM). Surface EMG signals were recorded and normalized to maximal voluntary isometric contraction (%MVIC). TFL activation showed a significant angle-dependent reduction. Both peak and mean TFL EMG were significantly lower at 135° than at 45° and 90° (p < 0.01), with no difference between 45° and 90°. In contrast, GMed activation showed fewer differences across conditions. Peak GMed EMG did not differ significantly between angles, whereas mean GMed activation was significantly lower at 135° than at 45° (p < 0.05), with no difference between 45° and 90°. The GMed: TFL ratio was significantly higher at 135° than at both 45° and 90° (p < 0.01). However, this increase was driven primarily by suppression of TFL activity rather than enhanced GMed activation. These findings indicate that hip flexion angle modifies the relative distribution of hip abductor muscle activity. Moderate flexion (45°–90°) maintains higher absolute GMed activation, whereas greater flexion (135°) increases relative GMed contribution by reducing TFL involvement. Adjusting hip position may therefore influence muscle recruitment patterns depending on whether the objective is to preserve absolute activation or reduce TFL dominance.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65992-6.title: Determinants of youth engagement in rural revitalization in China: a mixed-method study based on grounded theory and structural equation modeling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65992-6.abstract: Youth unemployment and rural poverty are pressing issues in developing countries, highlighted by the United Nations’ SDGs. In China, the urban–rural dual structure of the planned economy has contributed to youth unemployment and talent shortages in rural areas. While previous research has focused on urbanization and youth migration to cities, understanding their motivations for rural migration remains limited. This study presents an innovative perspective on youth behavioral motivation, utilizing a substantial sample of 1020 field surveys. To understand the drivers of youth engagement in rural development, this paper proposes a framework based on the Theory of Planned Behavior, utilizing qualitative inquiry and structural equation modeling. The analysis systematically examines the roles of external support, self-perception, behavioral attitudes, and intentions in facilitating youth engagement in these initiatives. The findings demonstrate that material support and behavioral attitudes positively influence behavioral intentions. Conversely, while emotional support significantly enhances behavioral attitudes, material support has a detrimental effect on them. Additionally, external support and self-cognition, mediated by behavioral expectations, enhanced youths’ intentions to migrate. These findings provide critical insights for policymakers and practitioners aiming to boost youth engagement in rural revitalization initiatives in developing countries.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69412-7.title: Comparative effectiveness of corticosteroid choice in hospitalized patients with concurrent COPD and heart failure exacerbations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69412-7.abstract: Hospitalized patients with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) frequently have concurrent acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). Corticosteroids used to treat AECOPD that have mineralocorticoid activity may promote fluid retention, potentially worsening heart failure. To compare the effectiveness of corticosteroids with mineralocorticoid activity to corticosteroids with minimal mineralocorticoid activity in patients hospitalized with both AECOPD and ADHF. Retrospective cohort study using a target trial emulation framework. Adults aged ≥ 50 years, hospitalized between October 2022 and July 2024 with both AECOPD and ADHF present on admission who were treated on hospital day 1 with systemic corticosteroids and parenteral loop diuretics, identified from the Premier Healthcare Database. Initial treatment with corticosteroids with mineralocorticoid activity (hydrocortisone or prednisone) versus corticosteroids with minimal mineralocorticoid activity (methylprednisolone or dexamethasone). The primary outcome was hospital-free days by day 30. Secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay, in-hospital mortality or discharge to hospice, days of parenteral diuretic use, days of corticosteroid use, and 30-day readmission. Among 24,162 hospitalizations meeting inclusion criteria, 2,562 (11%) received corticosteroids with mineralocorticoid activity (median age 71 years, 51% female), whereas 21,600 (89%) received corticosteroids with minimal mineralocorticoid activity (median age 72 years, 47% female). There was no difference in hospital-free days by day 30 (22.8 vs. 23.0 days; difference 0.3 [95% CI − 0.02 to 0.5]) or in-hospital mortality/discharge to hospice (6.2% vs. 5.9%; difference − 0.3% [95% CI − 1.4 to 0.8]). Patients receiving corticosteroids with mineralocorticoid activity had slightly fewer days of parenteral diuretic use (− 0.2 days), fewer days of corticosteroids (− 0.1 days), and shorter length of stay (− 0.3 days). In this large, multicenter study of patients hospitalized with both AECOPD and ADHF, initial treatment with corticosteroids with mineralocorticoid activity was not associated with fewer hospital-free days or increased mortality relative to corticosteroids with minimal mineralocorticoid activity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68020-9.title: Enhancing wheat growth and yield under deficit irrigation using stress-tolerant plant-beneficial rhizobacteria
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68020-9.abstract: Drought is a major abiotic constraint limiting agricultural productivity globally, and is of particular concern in Pakistan. Harnessing drought-adapted plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) offers a promising strategy for sustaining wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) production under water-limited conditions. In this study, 19 rhizobacterial strains were isolated from the rhizosphere of wheat grown in the hyper-arid Cholistan Desert of Pakistan and systematically screened for tolerance to multiple abiotic stresses, including PEG-induced drought (up to 20%), salinity (up to 15% NaCl), high temperature (up to 43 °C), and alkaline pH (up to 11). Strains were further characterized for plant growth-promoting traits (IAA production, phosphate and zinc solubilization, nitrogen fixation, and siderophore production) under both normal and stress conditions. Two highly promising multi-stress-tolerant strains, RF5 and RZ7, were selected and evaluated individually and in a consortium. Multi-location field trials were conducted across three distinct agroecological zones in Pakistan under deficit irrigation regimes (50% of recommended irrigation or skipped irrigations). Inoculation with the RF5 + RZ7 consortium, combined with 80% of the recommended NPK dose, resulted in significant improvements in wheat growth and productivity. Notably, grain yield increased by 18–24% compared to uninoculated controls under the same reduced fertilizer regime, while several key parameters (shoot biomass, chlorophyll content, and grain nutrient uptake) performed comparably to, or better than, the full fertilizer treatment. These positive effects were consistent across different wheat varieties and environmental conditions. These findings demonstrate that desert-adapted PGPR consortia can effectively mitigate drought stress, enhance nutrient use efficiency, and support sustainable wheat production under reduced-input conditions in arid and semi-arid regions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69257-0.title: Intelligent evaluation method for inflammatory response after trans-PRK and FS-LASIK based on multimodal feature fusion
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69257-0.abstract: Assessing postoperative inflammation following trans-PRK and FS-LASIK remains challenging. This study proposes a multimodal fusion framework supported by inflammatory dynamics physical descriptors. The model uses modality-specific encoders for ocular imaging and structured clinical or biomarker sequences, uses explicit observation masks for unavailable modalities, and learns visit-level fusion weights using cross-modal attention modules. In the four de-identified retrospective data partitions evaluated in this study, the proposed fusion model increases the accuracy of the strongest baseline reported in each partition by 2.66 to 4.10% points, and shows similar improvements in F1 score and AUROC. The results indicate that intermediate multimodal fusion can support postoperative inflammation assessment. Before clinical deployment, larger external validation cohorts, calibration analyses, and direct comparisons with medical multimodal fusion methods are still required.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69210-1.title: Retraction Note: Heat transfer analysis of Cu and Al2O3 dispersed in ethylene glycol as a base fluid over a stretchable permeable sheet of MHD thin-film flow
