doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67760-y.title: A compact quad-port multiband frequency-diverse antenna system with high isolation for radar and SATCOM applications
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67760-y.abstract: Abstract A compact quad element multiband frequency diverse antenna with orthogonal heterogeneous geometrical structures is proposed in this paper for wideband wireless communication systems. Isolation among elements is improved using Swastik shaped defected ground structure. Overall dimensions of presented antenna are 60 × 60 × 0.4mm 3 . Antenna elements (M 1 , M 2 , M 3 and M 4 ) achieved operating bands: M 1 element operates from 9.45 – 12.25 GHz, M 2 element operates from 11.49 – 16.18 GHz, M 3 element operates from 7.05 – 8.49 GHz and M 4 operates from 16.47 – 17.89 GHz. The frequency diverse antenna provides multi-band coverage spanning 7–18 GHz through four distinct operating bands across X and Ku frequency bands with isolation greater than 35 dB among elements. It achieved peak gain up to 6.91 dB and radiation efficiency up-to 91.1%.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68336-6.title: Size-dependent top extraction and finite-NA capture in ultra-small blue GaN micro-LEDs via peripheral-emission-weighted FDTD analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68336-6.abstract: Abstract Ultra-small blue GaN micro-LEDs (µLEDs) for near-eye displays require not only efficient top-side light extraction but also optical output that can be captured by finite-numerical-aperture (NA) projection optics. However, in this size regime, wave-optical interference, lateral pixel size, and edge-proximal emission non-uniformity can jointly affect both the extracted power and its angular distribution, making top-extraction-only or single-source analysis insufficient for evaluating usable forward output. Here, to address these limitations and directly evaluate finite-NA captured output under practical collection conditions in the ultra-small pixel regime, we conducted a peripheral-emission-weighted finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) analysis for size-dependent top extraction and finite-NA capture in ultra-small blue GaN µLEDs. The method incoherently combined representative dipole positions and polarizations and incorporated a radius-dependent peripheral weighting factor to effectively account for reduced peripheral radiative contribution associated with sidewall effects. For circular GaN µLEDs with pixel radii ranging from 2.0 to 2.8 μm, we investigated how p -GaN thickness and AlGaN electron-blocking-layer (EBL) insertion reshaped top light-extraction efficiency, angular emission, and NA-limited captured output. The simulations showed that p -side stack variations produced non-monotonic extraction behavior and shifted favorable thickness windows in a radius-dependent manner, while finite-NA metrics revealed changes in practically collectable output that were not captured by top extraction efficiency alone. This work provides a computationally efficient FDTD framework for evaluating how p -side-stack design and pixel size influence top-side extraction, finite-NA captured output, and their sensitivity to peripheral-emission reduction in ultra-small blue µLEDs.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68971-z.title: Dual-modality modeling for depression detection using speech signals
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68971-z.abstract: Abstract Depression is a leading contributor to the global burden of disease and a significant barrier to both personal well-being and societal development. Yet, it remains underdiagnosed, primarily due to social stigma and limited access to clinical resources. This study proposes a dual-modality framework for automated depression detection using speech signals, capturing both what individuals say (text) and how they say it (vocal cues) from speech recordings. The method integrates contextual embeddings and acoustic features extracted from clinical interview recordings. Transcriptions are generated using the Whisper automatic speech recognizer, and text embeddings are derived from a fine-tuned BERT model, while prosodic and spectral features serve as vocal cues. To improve classification sensitivity under class imbalance, random oversampling is applied during fine-tuning. Both feature-level and decision-level fusion strategies are evaluated using fully connected and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. On the E-DAIC dataset, the decision-level OR fusion strategy achieved 96.68% accuracy, 90.41% precision, 95.17% recall, and a 92.73% F1-score. Evaluation on the Chinese MODMA dataset assesses the applicability of the framework to an additional language-specific dataset after dataset-specific training, while indicating that modality contribution may vary across datasets. The reported results are segment-level methodological findings and should not be interpreted as participant-independent clinical performance. The speech-only design avoids visual-data collection but does not eliminate the privacy risks associated with identifiable speech recordings and transcripts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65292-z.title: Cooperative control of multi-microgrids under uncertainty: a multi-agent actor-critic approach with LSTM and deep dense architecture
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65292-z.abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy poses significant source-load uncertainty challenges to the economic and stable operation of microgrids. To address the key challenges of multi-microgrid cooperative optimization, including temporal source-load uncertainty, heterogeneous inter-microgrid coordination, and real-time decentralized decision-making, this paper proposes a cooperative control strategy named Long Short-Term Memory-based Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (L-MAAC). Under the Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) framework, the proposed method learns cooperative policies using global system information during training, while enabling each microgrid to make decisions based only on local observations during execution. Specifically, the Actor network incorporates an LSTM module to extract temporal features from historical source-load data, thereby improving the ability to proactively respond to renewable generation and load fluctuations, while the Critic network integrates an individual attention mechanism with a Deep Dense architecture in Reinforcement Learning (D2RL), which enhances the representation of heterogeneous interactions among microgrids and alleviates information loss in deep value-function approximation. Ablation studies, reward sensitivity, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses confirm the synergistic contributions of these components. Simulation results based on a modified IEEE 13-bus multi-microgrid system show that, compared with advanced algorithms such as MAAC, L-MAAC reduces the total system operating cost by 4.81% on the test set. Furthermore, under multiple uncertainty scenarios, including cloud dynamics, wind power randomness, sudden load changes, and combined electricity price/diesel generator failures, the proposed method demonstrates superior voltage regulation capability and robustness. These results indicate that L-MAAC can effectively improve both the economic efficiency and operational stability of multi-microgrid systems under uncertain environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67975-z.title: Enhancing nasal irrigation adherence through a multimodal health communication strategy: a phased improvement study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67975-z.abstract: Abstract The adherence of chronic rhinitis patients to self-administered treatments is generally very low, which often presents a significant challenge in healthcare. The adherence of chronic rhinitis patients to regular nasal irrigation hygiene care is even lower. Therefore, in this study, we designed, implemented, and evaluated a patient-centered Multimodal Health Communication Strategy intervention, that aimed to improve the adherence to nasal irrigation of adult patients with allergic rhinitis or chronic hypertrophic rhinitis. This was a healthcare quality improvement project conducted from January to July 2025 in the otolaryngology outpatient department of a medical center. The healthcare quality improvement intervention evolved in two stages. The first-stage intervention introduced a “Multimodal Educational Strategy,” combining visual aids, instructional videos, and one-on-one consultation with standard brief verbal instructions. The second-stage intervention, based on patient feedback from the first stage, further optimized the user experience by providing an ergonomic irrigation device and optionally available Herbal Tea Rinse saline solution. The primary outcome measure was that nasal irrigation adherence significantly increased from a baseline of 11.2% to 45.2% after the first stage ( p < 0.001), and further increased to 75.0% after the second stage ( p = 0.013). This represents a 569% relative increase ( p < 0.001) compared to patients who had not undergone the Multimodal Health Communication Strategy intervention. Finally, patients who received the Multimodal Health Communication Strategy educational intervention showed an improvement in knowledge mastery from 51% to 93.8%, and overall satisfaction also significantly increased. The study concluded that low adherence to nasal irrigation is a problem that can be overcome, rather than an insurmountable communication gap between patients and healthcare providers. Systematic patient-centered education through the Multimodal Health Communication Strategy was associated with an improvement in self-nasal irrigation care adherence.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60205-6.title: Effect of pre-emptive operational strategies on product quality and deterioration dynamics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60205-6.abstract: The innovative logistics strategy of cross-docking enables the offloading of goods from incoming vehicles at the receiving dock, followed by loading the products into outgoing trucks, eliminating the need for prolonged product storage. The brisk movement of products within the cross-docking strategy has made this an uncompromisable approach for transporting staples, groceries, and perishable items. Although the goal is to maintain a stable environment within the cross-dock centres and vehicles, the loading and unloading process often fails to achieve this. Exposure to an unstable environment affects the quality of goods and initiates their deterioration. The inclusion of the pre-emption technique in the unloading or loading process leads to frequent exposure to an unstable environment, thereby accelerating deterioration. This study explores how pre-emption affects the deterioration rate variation risk coefficient of the products when a limited number of interruptions in the unloading process is considered. A non-linear programming model that considers pre-emption is developed for this problem, and the optimization is performed using an interior-point algorithm to minimize the deterioration rate variation risk coefficient. Results obtain highlight that the inclusion of the pre-emption technique increases the accumulated deterioration rate variation coefficient by nearly 265%, while an increase in the number of product types and their quantities heavily influences the accumulated deterioration rate variation coefficient value, showing a whopping rise of nearly 152%.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69544-w.title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Pammene nemorosa (Lepidoptera, Tortricidae) and its phylogenetic placement within Grapholitini
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69544-w.abstract: Abstract The intergeneric attraction of Pammene nemorosa to sex pheromone traps targeting the Oriental fruit moth, Grapholita molesta (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae), may compromise the reliability of pest monitoring in apple orchards, yet the evolutionary context of this behavioral overlap remains unclear. Here, we sequenced and characterized the first complete mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) of P. nemorosa and assessed its phylogenetic position within the tribe Grapholitini. The circular mitogenome is 15,457 bp long and contains the canonical set of 37 genes, including 13 protein-coding genes, 22 transfer RNA genes, and two ribosomal RNA genes, with a gene order typical of ditrysian Lepidoptera. The genome exhibits a pronounced A + T bias (80.1%), and its 484-bp control region contains a tandem duplication of an approximately 215-bp sequence unit, with each repeat copy marked by an ATAGA motif. Phylogenetic analyses based on Neighbor-Joining, Maximum Likelihood, and Bayesian Inference consistently recovered P. nemorosa as sister to the Grapholita clade (G. dimorpha + G. molesta), with strong Bayesian support (posterior probability = 0.999), highlighting a potential discordance between its mitochondrial phylogenetic position and its current morphological classification within Pammene. These findings establish the first complete mitogenomic resource for P. nemorosa and provide a phylogenetic framework for interpreting its close evolutionary affinity with Grapholita species. Although mitochondrial data alone cannot establish the functional mechanisms underlying heterospecific pheromone attraction, the genomic resource established here provides a baseline for future integrative studies combining nuclear genomics, transcriptomics, and chemical ecology, and contributes to a broader understanding of the evolutionary relationships and ecological interactions within Grapholitini.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-56890-y.title: Lethal and sublethal effects of copper sulphate and zinc sulphate on Moina macrocopa: implications for freshwater risk assessment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-56890-y.abstract: Abstract Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly threatened by trace metal contamination arising from agricultural, industrial, and domestic effluents. Among these, copper sulphate (CuSO 4 ) and zinc sulphate (ZnSO 4 ) are widely used compounds that, despite their benefits, pose ecological risks to non-target aquatic organisms. The present study was motivated by the urgent need to evaluate their impact on Moina macrocopa , a sensitive cladoceran bioindicator species frequently employed in ecotoxicological assessments. The study systematically evaluates the lethal and sublethal toxic effects of copper sulphate and zinc sulphate on Moina macrocopa . Lethal toxicity was assessed through mortality observations over 8–72 h, with LC 50 values derived via probit regression. CuSO 4 exhibited high toxicity, with LC 50 values declining from 264.46 µg/L (8 h) to 45.3 µg/L (72 h), indicating a sharp increase in lethality with exposure time. ZnSO 4 showed delayed toxicity, with LC 50 values ranging from 2102.31 µg/L (24 h) to 544.48 µg/L (72 h). CuSO 4 exposure resulted in significant toxicity even at low concentrations, with 100% mortality occurring at 250–300 µg/L within 48–72 h. In contrast, ZnSO 4 exhibited delayed toxicity, with complete mortality observed only at concentrations ≥ 1000 µg/L beyond 48 h. Heart rate monitoring served as a sensitive biomarker for physiological stress, with significant bradycardia and complete cardiac cessation at ≥ 5000 µg/L ZnSO 4 after 48 h. Recovery of molting and reproduction was evident at lower concentrations for both metals, suggesting resilience at sublethal levels. LC 50 values declined with exposure duration, indicating cumulative toxicity, with CuSO 4 showing markedly higher potency than ZnSO 4 . These findings reinforce the ecological relevance of M. macrocopa for freshwater risk assessment and highlight the importance of integrating sublethal biomarkers in regulatory ecotoxicology.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69359-9.title: Definition and core characteristics of scarce medicinal resources of Traditional Chinese Medicine and ethnic medicine in Xinjiang, China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69359-9.abstract: Scarce medicinal resources constitute the natural resources of Traditional Chinese Medicine and ethnic minority medicine (TCM-EM). However, the vague understanding of scarce (shortage) medicinal resources and scarce (shortage) medicinal materials makes it impossible to predict scarce resources and fails to effectively meet the demands in cultivation and medical treatment. Following a systematic search of three databases (CNKI, Web of Science, PubMed) that identified > 2,800 initial records, 213 relevant texts were screened, and 74 core documents were included for term extraction. utilized the atomic atlas method, and employed the multi-round Delphi method for expert interviews to clarify the core evaluation dimensions and definition criteria of scarce medicinal resources for Traditional Chinese Medicine and ethnic minority medicine in Xinjiang. After three rounds of expert interviews, the definition of scarce (shortage) medicinal resources was formulated: scarce (shortage) medicinal resources for Traditional Chinese Medicine (ethnic medicine) in Xinjiang refer to medicinal resources with supply constraints that are irreplaceable and essential for Traditional Chinese Medicine products. Such medicinal resources are required for disease treatment in a specific region within a certain period, yet they are constrained by irreplaceable, limited availability, insufficient yield meeting quality standards, and an imperfect supply chain, thereby failing to satisfy the production demand of Traditional Chinese Medicine products. Notably, the Delphi method has been used to define scarce medicinal resources for traditional Chinese medicine (ethnic medicine) in Xinjiang, China. It provides a qualitative evaluation framework for the conservation and rational utilization of traditional Chinese medicinal resources in Xinjiang. Consensus rates achieved through the Delphi method (the coefficient of variation of the indicator was less than 0.20, indicating strong consistent opinions among experts on the three core characteristics) provide operational qualitative criteria for determining scarce resources, and subsequent efforts can integrate data such as resource reserves and demand to establish quantitative models.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67150-4.title: Separating threat, rarity, and outgroup accounts of the other-race P2
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67150-4.abstract: When White participants view Black (vs. White) faces, their brains produce an enhanced P2 ERP response. This has traditionally been interpreted as increased attention to threat, overlooking two alternative accounts: ingroup–outgroup categorisation, or stimulus distinctiveness effects, pertaining to the relative rarity of Black individuals in many Western contexts. The near-complete omission of Black participants from face-processing research renders these accounts difficult to disentangle. Here, 52 Black and 45 White participants viewed target faces while race (Black/White) and gender (female/male) were manipulated. Early frontal P2 responses emerged only in White participants viewing Black targets, suggesting increased cognitive resource allocation resulting from stimulus rarity, not threat, while late parietal P2 increases arose for all participants to their respective racial outgroup. Our results bear implications for the interpretation of P2 effects as neural markers of social cognition, while highlighting intrinsic limitations of assuming results from homogeneous (WEIRD) samples reflect universal socio-cognitive processes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68852-5.title: Dexmedetomidine reduces emergence agitation and catheter-related bladder discomfort after abdominal surgery: a single center, prospective, double blind randomized controlled trial
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68852-5.abstract: We explored whether dexmedetomidine administration during anaesthesia recovery could improve postoperative short-term Catheter-Related Bladder Discomfort (CRBD), emergence agitation (EA), and pain. A total of 269 patients who underwent abdominal surgery were included in the analysis. Patients were randomly assigned to either the dexmedetomidine group (group D, n = 136), which received 0.2 µg/kg dexmedetomidine after being transferred to the Postanesthesia Care Unit (PACU), or the control group (group C, n = 133). The outcome measures included EA, CRBD, pain, blood pressure, and heart rate in the PACU; demand for additional analgesic medication; length of PACU stay and protective restraints; and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). No differences were observed in the baseline data. Patients in group D had lower incidence of EA (1.5% vs. 30.8% at extubation, p < 0.001; 0.0% vs. 9.0% 10 min after extubation, p < 0.001). Group D patients had lower pain scores at all observation time points in the PACU (all p < 0.001) and lower CRBD ratings (all p < 0.001), and no patients in group D had CRBD ≥ 3. Group D patients had a longer PACU stay (50.00 (30.00) vs. 45.00 (25.00) min, p = 0.042). There were no statistical differences in analgesic drug requirements or incidence of PONV, and no significant differences were observed in blood pressure and heart rate. Administration of low-dose dexmedetomidine in the PACU reduced the incidence of EA and CRBD and short-term postoperative pain scores. Trial registration The trial was registered before patient enrolment in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (registry no. ChiCTR2500107721, registration date: August 18, 2025).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69394-6.title: Deviation-aware digital twin-enabled joint user association and task partitioning for industrial IoT offloading
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69394-6.abstract: Latency-critical industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications outstrip on-device computing capability, yet digital twin (DT)-assisted multi-access edge computing (MEC) is typically modeled as a perfectly synchronized mirror and treats edge association and task partitioning separately. This paper proposes a deviation-aware three-layer DT-assisted offloading framework spanning IIoT devices, micro base stations (MBSs), and a macro base station (BS). Twins of devices and MBSs are maintained at the BS and explicitly parameterized by CPU-frequency, transmit-power, and bandwidth deviations, so decisions are made from realistically imperfect twin state and the resulting delay-estimation error is quantified. Under delay and energy constraints, discrete user association and continuous partitioning ratios are jointly optimized to minimize average offloading time plus a service-failure penalty, with distinct delay models derived for parallel independent subtasks and serially dependent subtasks. Because the problem is non-convex, NP-hard, and hybrid-variable, a deep multi-agent parameterized Q-network (DMAPQN) is developed in which each device twin acts as an agent and a global mixing network couples local hybrid-action Q-values, preserving the discrete–continuous action structure. Simulations show a 10 MB task completes in 330 ms versus 415, 596, 617, and 705 ms for dichotomy, random, full-MBS, and local execution—a 20.5% gain over the strongest baseline.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69041-0.title: Mouse bio-behavioral phenotyping using a digital homecage framework for long-timescale, high-resolution, and multi-factor data collection and analytics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69041-0.abstract: Long-term monitoring of behavioral and physiological processes is essential for elucidating complex brain-based phenomena and disorders that develop over extended periods, such as chronic stress, circadian disruption, and metabolic syndromes. Though digital phenotyping is well-established in humans via smart devices, comparable solutions for rodent models remain limited. To address this gap, we present the Digital Homecage (DHC) system, an open-source platform that enables uninterrupted, long-timescale recording of over 20 behavioral metrics in single-housed mice. The DHC integrates video capture, operant task modules, and wheel-running data to achieve sub-second resolution in monitoring behaviors such as actigraphy, sleep, grooming, and food choice over periods spanning weeks. Initial data validate the system's capability to reveal circadian patterns across multiple spontaneous behaviors, consistently reflecting nocturnal activity. Designed for seamless integration with brain recording technologies, the DHC offers unique opportunities for longitudinal analyses of chronic conditions and neuropsychiatric syndromes. Its accessibility and modular design promote community-driven innovation, establishing the DHC as a transformative tool for advancing the study of complex traits in rodent models of brain function and behavior.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-47036-1.title: Influence of chlorophyll-a and environmental drivers on fish landings along the west coast of India
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-47036-1.abstract: Fish landings along the west coast of India account for ~ 65% of the country’s total marine catch, with regional contrasts. This study investigated how fish landings relate to chlorophyll-a and key environmental drivers including sea surface temperature (SST), wind velocity, and mean sea level anomaly using satellite data within 100 km of the shoreline from Gujarat to Kerala. In addition, in-situ sampling was carried out off Goa and Kochi (September 2022, December 2022, and March 2023) to show seasonal variability in water column temperature, dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll-a, and FlowCAM-based microplankton quantity. The results show that fish landings increased during the periods of elevated chlorophyll-a (> 2 mg/m³) and dissolved oxygen (> 4 ml/l), but declined under warmer SSTs (> 28.9 °C), strong winds (> 5.8 m/s). Robust regression analysis indicated a strong positive association between chlorophyll-a and fish landings (slope: 3.56 × 10⁴ tonnes/mg m − 3 , p < 0.001; n = 99). Chlorophyll-a concentrations were consistently higher in the northern Arabian Sea, while total landings were comparable between Gujarat (avg. 6.4 ± 1.4 × 10^5 tonnes/yr), Kerala (avg. 5.6 ± 1.2 × 10^5 tonnes/yr) and Karnataka (avg. 6.1 ± 2.3 × 10^5 tonnes/yr), suggesting similar reported landings despite contrasting environmental conditions and fishing pressure. Higher landings off Kochi were observed during seasons characterized by a dominance of larger autotrophs, whereas off Goa higher landings coincided with relatively greater heterotrophic plankton abundance. This study highlights the need for integrated monitoring that combines water column physics, plankton dynamics, wind forcing, fishing effort, fishing bans, and fleet mobility. Satellite, in-situ, and vessel tracking observations provide mechanistic insights into the match and mismatch between environmental conditions and fish landings, supporting sustainable harvests and evidence-based management along the west coast of India.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68165-7.title: Community wastewater parvovirus B19 signal amid rising maternal–fetal cases
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68165-7.abstract: Parvovirus B19 (B19V) is a small, non-enveloped DNA virus primarily transmitted via respiratory droplets, with the capacity for vertical transmission during pregnancy. B19V infection is associated with fetal anemia and perinatal death, yet it is not included in routine public health surveillance. We present statewide detection of B19V in Texas wastewater using hybrid-capture virome sequencing across 43 sites in 15 cities. Wastewater signal closely tracked clinical case trends at institutional, county, and state levels, with the strongest correlation occurring when wastewater preceded reported cases by one month. Sequencing reads provided full-genome coverage, enabling characterization of population-level genomic composition during the 2024 case surge, including changes in the VP1/VP2 region which warrants functional investigation in clinical or experimental models. These findings highlight the utility of wastewater virome sequencing for real-time detection of underreported viruses and support its application as a complementary viral surveillance approach alongside other commonly used genomic techniques. Given B19V’s clinical significance and the lack of national monitoring programs, this work establishes a framework for scalable wastewater-based detection of B19V and similar threats, particularly where diagnostic testing is limited or delayed. Such applications may be especially valuable in pregnancy, where early awareness and intervention can be critical for fetal health.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69176-0.title: Optimization of paper mill sludge ash in sustainable concrete mixes for enhanced strength and durability performance
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69176-0.abstract: This research studies the feasibility of paper mill sludge ash (PMSA) as a sustainable alternative to conventional cementitious materials to alleviate the environmental and economic issues due to the production of regular cement. The study was done with M30 concrete with water to binder (w/b) ratio of 0.38 to provide a common ground for strength and durability evaluation. Concrete mixes were prepared using 0–30% PMSA as cement replacement according to Indian Standard specifications. The fresh, mechanical and durability properties were tested using slump, compaction factor, fresh density, compressive strength, split tensile strength, flexural strength, water absorption, rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) and sulphate resistance. As the PMSA content increases, the workability and fresh density decrease. The compressive and flexural strengths increase at moderate replacement level (8–10%) due to the increased pozzolanic activity. The durability tests indicated that the resistance to sulphate attack was improved at optimum replacement levels, but the chloride permeability was increased with higher doses of PMSA. In general, the results show that the PMSA can be an economical alternative for concrete production, effectively reducing cement consumption and environmental impact. An optimum replacement level of 8–10% gives a balanced combination of strength, durability and sustainability for M30 concrete.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68736-8.title: All-InGaN/GaN red light-emitting diodes with low-temperature-grown GaN capping layer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68736-8.abstract: Abstract The growth of indium-rich InGaN red light-emitting diodes (LEDs) is essential for realizing all-nitride full-color micro-LED displays. This study presents a strategy for fabricating red LEDs with InGaN/GaN multiple quantum wells (MQWs) by introducing a low-temperature-grown GaN quantum-well capping (LT-GaN QC) layer, without the need for strain-engineered structures. The insertion of LT-GaN QC induces a significant electroluminescence (EL) wavelength shift of MQWs from 506 to 668 nm. This capping layer effectively suppresses indium re-evaporation and sequential InGaN decomposition during the subsequent high-temperature growth of quantum barriers (QBs). Quantitative structural analyses using transmission electron microscopy and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy confirm that the thickness of the LT-GaN QC strongly influences both the QW thickness and indium composition. These findings demonstrate that the LT-GaN QC layer provides a practical approach to preserving indium-rich InGaN QWs during high-temperature processes, thereby enabling the fabrication of high-efficiency nitride-based red and longer-wavelength LEDs.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69521-3.title: Power ultrasound for enhanced particle dispersion and mechanical performance in cement-based materials: a quantitative image analysis approach
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69521-3.abstract: Abstract The performance of cement-based materials heavily relies on the uniform dispersion of particles, yet traditional methods often fall short in efficiency. This study investigated the use of power ultrasound to improve particle dispersion in cement paste and the mechanical performance of cement-based materials. An image-based quantitative characterization approach combining optical microscopy and image processing was applied to derive comparative image-derived metrics for evaluating particle-distribution states. Among the tested nominal electrical power levels, the 750 W treatment produced the most favorable comparative image-derived metrics and the highest mean compressive strength at 3, 7, and 28 d. An exploratory positive association was observed between particle area and early compressive strength, suggesting that the comparative image-derived metrics may serve as indicators of early strength development under the tested conditions. Additionally, X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) indicated differences in hydration products and microstructure following ultrasonic treatment. These findings indicate the potential of power ultrasound as a supplementary physical treatment for cement-based materials.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69261-4.title: An adaptive cruise control system for autonomous vehicles using PRDC–CoROA-based hybrid optimization
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69261-4.abstract: An adaptive cruise control (ACC) system has a key role to play in enhancing the safety and stability of autonomous vehicles, along with ensuring improved ride quality through proper management of vehicle velocity and distance between vehicles. However, the conventional design of an ACC system, such as Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID), Model Predictive Control (MPC), fuzzy logic, and neural network-based controllers, has certain difficulties due to nonlinearity, uncertainty, and real-time parameter optimization. In order to overcome these shortcomings, this study proposes a hybrid optimization-based approach to ACC based on a Probabilistic Robust Damping Controller (PRDC), integrated with the Composed Remora Optimization Algorithm (CoROA). This novel approach seeks to optimize the performance of the ACC through improvements in vehicular stability, distance control, and velocity tracking. The controller uses data about the speed, acceleration, distance between the vehicles, and the velocity error to provide proper control signals while keeping the vehicle’s operation safe and smooth. The algorithm has been developed and verified in the MATLAB environment, and its performance has been compared to other ACC techniques. The simulation outcomes show that the proposed method reduces the errors of velocity and distance by less than 10% and facilitates smoother regenerative braking operation up to 43.65% and vehicle driving stability. The outcomes achieved show that the proposed PRDC-CoROA method improves the performance of adaptive cruise control.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67591-x.title: A hybrid metaheuristic framework for robust photovoltaic model parameter estimation based on crested porcupine and differential evolution algorithms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67591-x.abstract: Abstract Accurate parameter estimation is essential for the efficient design and performance evaluation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. However, the strong nonlinearity of PV equivalent circuit models often causes conventional optimization algorithms to become trapped in local optima. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a novel hybrid optimization framework, termed Crested Porcupine Differential Evolution (CPO-DE), which combines the global exploration capability of the Crested Porcupine Optimizer with the robust mutation mechanism of Differential Evolution. The proposed CPO-DE algorithm is first validated mathematically using 23 benchmark functions alongside three classical engineering design problems. It is subsequently applied to the Single Diode Model (SDM), Double Diode Model (DDM), and Triple Diode Model (TDM) of PV systems. In addition, a novel two-stage evaluation strategy is introduced, where computationally efficient algebraic equations are employed during the iterative optimization process to reduce computational burden, followed by an explicit Newton–Raphson numerical solver to ensure high physical accuracy of the estimated parameters. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated using experimental data from the RTC France solar cell over 300 independent runs. The results demonstrate that CPO-DE achieves a 100% convergence success rate with near-zero standard deviations, indicating excellent robustness and stability. Moreover, the proposed method outperforms eleven state-of-the-art optimization algorithms and consistently attains the top rank according to Friedman statistical tests. These results confirm that CPO-DE is a highly reliable, stable, and efficient engineering tool for advanced photovoltaic model parameter estimation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69610-3.title: Simplified in vivo corneal confocal volumetric imaging using adaptive axial scanning and computational registration
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69610-3.abstract: Corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) provides optical sections with cellular-level detail, but large-depth volumetric visualization is limited by acquisition time and inter-frame motion. Here, we present a simplified optical-digital framework that combines a motorized objective module with a clinically familiar TomoCap contact interface, layer-aware MobileNetV3 speed control, expanded-canvas coarse registration, and dynamic-window VoxelMorph refinement. In 11 matched same-eye sequence pairs, adaptive-speed acquisition produced lower image-estimated stack drift across the tested depth range. Across four test sequences, coarse plus VXM produced the highest adjacent-frame NCC and the lowest masked MAE among the tested processing variants. The registered rabbit and human stacks supported large-depth volumetric visualization and oblique viewing with cellular-level detail. Deformation-field, mask-based, and expert-review analyses found no widespread geometric folding or visually suspicious failure in the reviewed cases. This framework provides a practical route for converting in vivo CCM sequences into interpretable depth-continuous volume representations while retaining cellular-level confocal detail.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68659-4.title: Precise estimation method for electronic absorption of metalloporphyrin dye molecules based on phenomenological formulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68659-4.abstract: Molecular electronic absorption is the most important property that determines the optical behavior and functions of molecules. However, accurate estimation of molecular electronic absorption using theoretical calculations is difficult for relatively large molecules, such as organic dyes and pigments, even at a substantial computational cost. Consequently, it is determined through experimental trial-and-error and empirical guesswork. Development of a unified rule and a practical formula for electronic absorption would enable easier, faster, and more accurate prediction of molecular electronic absorption through direct linkage between such an experimental science and emerging data-driven science. Using porphyrin complexes as a typical dye molecule, this study is the first to demonstrate the concept of a phenomenological formulation for the precise estimation of their electronic absorption. Systematic spectrophotometric analysis of porphyrins in the same environmental condition showed that the spectral parameters associated with wavenumbers and extinction coefficients exhibit a linear or near-linear relationship with various structural factors. By formulating photophysical parameters based on these rules, we identify a new spectral factor as a single function and successfully represent the electronic absorption of porphyrins as a simple formula, which we believe will help in predicting unknown dye molecules and bridging established empirical rules with modern data-driven science.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67432-x.title: Multimodal speckle and polarization fiber sensing for localized, broadband vibration monitoring
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67432-x.abstract: Abstract High-bandwidth and multi-point acoustic and vibration sensing is a critical asset for real-time condition monitoring, maintenance, and surveillance applications. In the case of large scales and harsh environments, optical fiber distributed sensing has emerged as a compelling alternative to electronic transducers, featuring lower installation and maintenance costs, along with compact footprints and enhanced robustness. Yet, current distributed fiber-optic sensing solutions are typically costly and face a resolution-bandwidth tradeoff. This work addresses the current challenges of distributed fiber optic sensors by presenting a dual-modality architecture that combines speckle dynamic analysis and polarization interrogation. The implementation operates under a single-active-source assumption across four discrete points distributed on a 4-m length fiber and uses camera-based speckle analysis to localize the active position, while the polarization interrogation reconstructs the corresponding waveform from 100 Hz to 40 kHz with a 200 kHz acquisition rate, with 35 dB SNR. Overall, the work establishes a general and promising blueprint to harness multimodality in fiber sensing and break single-modality constraints.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68836-5.title: Successive approximation analysis and experimental validation of viscoelastic geometric nonlinear response for thick-walled cylindrical pressure vessels with application to solid rocket motor grains
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68836-5.abstract: The structural response of thick-walled cylindrical pressure vessels made of viscoelastic materials can be strongly affected by finite deformation. This study develops a successive approximation method for the geometrically nonlinear analysis of a case-bonded tubular solid rocket motor grain. A linear hereditary viscoelastic constitutive relation is combined with finite-deformation kinematics; thus, the nonlinearity considered is geometric rather than constitutive. The displacement, strain, and stress fields are expanded into asymptotic power series, from which a first-order linear solution and a second-order geometric nonlinear correction are derived. The resulting analytical solution is compared with the linear viscoelastic, initial-modulus, and equilibrium-modulus solutions to examine the effects of geometric nonlinearity, outer-to-inner radius ratio, and Poisson’s ratio. The model predicts pronounced geometric nonlinear effects near the inner wall, with strains approaching 80% in the investigated large-radius-ratio case. Cold pressurization tests were conducted for M = 4 and M = 6 over the pressure range of 2–10 MPa. The predicted inner-wall radial displacements agreed with the measurements, with relative errors below 15% under the tested conditions. The analysis further indicates that Poisson’s ratio can alter the stress state and may produce a triaxial compressive state throughout the vessel wall under the adopted assumptions. The proposed method provides an efficient analytical estimate of the geometrically nonlinear response of linear viscoelastic thick-walled cylinders. Material nonlinearity, damage, interface degradation, and broader loading conditions require further experimental and numerical investigation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68360-6.title: Study on occurrence, estimation, and health risks of microplastics in outdoor sports venues in Chongqing
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68360-6.abstract: Outdoor artificial sports venues are emerging yet underestimated hotspots of urban microplastic (MP) pollution, with far-reaching ecological and human health implications, particularly in subtropical mountainous megacities. This study systematically investigated MP occurrence, emission characteristics, spatial patterns, and risks of MPs associated with plastic running tracks and artificial lawns in the main urban area of Chongqing. Rainwater runoff sampling and laboratory analyses revealed ubiquitous MP contamination across all venues. The average MP abundance in runoff from artificial lawns was 7.34 × 10 2 ± 3.72 × 10 2 particles L −1 (7.34 × 10 –1 ± 3.72 × 10 –1 particles g −1 ), which was slightly higher than that from plastic running tracks (6.52 × 10 2 ± 2.43 × 10 2 particles L −1 , 6.52 × 10 –1 ± 2.43 × 10 –1 particles g −1 ). Fibrous MPs dominated the samples collected from artificial lawns (75.23%), while fragments prevailed in plastic tracks (85.76%), with over 90% of particles being smaller than 0.5 mm. By integrating remote sensing, GIS spatial analysis, and localized emission factors adjusted for climate, usage intensity, and maintenance conditions, the total annual MP emissions from sports venues were estimated at 293.63 tons. Plastic running tracks contributed 224.09 tons, which was 3.2 times higher than those from artificial lawns (69.54 tons), corresponding to a per capita annual emission of 9.2 g. Although the MP concentration per litre in runoff from artificial turf was higher, plastic running tracks covered a substantially larger total area (3,525,781 m 2 compared with 2,606,282 m 2 for artificial turf). Consequently, the annual MP emission from plastic tracks exceeded that from artificial lawns. Spatial hotspots were concentrated within the inner ring, riverside zones, university towns, and Beibei District, and closely overlapped with densely populated and education-intensive areas. These findings provide a reference for MP management in urban outdoor sports facilities.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67021-y.title: Deep reinforcement learning–driven electric vehicle charging coordination for renewable-integrated intelligent energy districts
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67021-y.abstract: Coordinated electric-vehicle charging in renewable-integrated intelligent energy districts must respond within quarter-hourly operating windows while balancing uncertain photovoltaic generation, tariffs, mobility demand, and distribution-feeder limits. This study develops and evaluates a closed-loop hybrid framework in which a four-head Generalized Value Function Network constructs predictive states, asynchronous IMPALA coordinates ten district controllers, and an SOCP–DistFlow projection screens the aggregate dispatch against relaxed-model voltage and branch-loading constraints. The framework was tested on the IEEE 69-bus feeder using two years of operational records for ten districts and 70 electric vehicles. Within the reported episode histories, IMPALA reached a sustained 90%-of-peak reward threshold by episode 50, retained 99.6% of its best 100-episode reward, and exhibited a 3.0% post-convergence coefficient of variation. These statistics support method selection within the observed histories and do not establish between-seed superiority. The integrated pipeline completed a quarter-hourly schedule in approximately 4.8 min, compared with 26.9 min for the pure-optimization benchmark, representing an 82% reduction in runtime with an approximately 3% cost deviation. Sensitivity and joint-uncertainty analyses indicated stable mean performance over the tested envelopes, while severe joint conditions increased voltage, branch-loading, and upper-tail cost exposure. The results show that predictive-state learning, asynchronous coordination, and feeder-level conic screening can produce deadline-compatible schedules with a transparent cost–latency trade-off for the evaluated simulation. The evidence remains limited to the relaxed SOCP feeder model and reported histories; nonlinear AC replay, repeated seeded trials, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and controlled utility pilots remain necessary before field deployment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67178-6.title: Perceived psychosocial outcomes and perceived neuromuscular competence following a university strength and conditioning program in dance aerobics and sports athletes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67178-6.abstract: The growing popularity of strength and conditioning (S&C) training in university sport has raised awareness of the need to gain a greater understanding of the athletes’ perception of the potential benefits of S&C training in a variety of performance areas such as dance, aerobics and competitive sports. This mixed-methods study aimed to investigate changes in athletes’ perceived performance-related outcomes, psychological well-being, gender responsiveness, training satisfaction, and lived experiences following a structured four-week strength and conditioning program. The participants completed a researcher-developed questionnaire informed by existing literature and adapted from relevant validated instruments using a Likert scale before and after a 4-week training program. The quantitative data were analysed using paired-samples t-tests, repeated-measures ANOVA, correlation analysis and regression modelling, and the qualitative data were analysed using thematic analysis. The results showed that there were statistically significant improvements in perceived neuromuscular competence, injury prevention awareness, psychological well-being, gender responsiveness, and training satisfaction after completing the program (all p < .05). These changes reflect athletes’ self-perceptions rather than objectively measured physiological, biomechanical, or performance outcomes. The qualitative findings showed the following themes: confidence and motivation, body awareness, team belongingness, discipline and accountability, and perceptions of gender inclusivity. The program was frequently mentioned as supportive of the participants’ athletic development and training involvement. The integrated results show that the participants experienced positive changes in perceived neuromuscular competence, injury prevention awareness, psychological well-being, gender responsiveness, training satisfaction, and overall training experiences after participation in the program. The findings should be taken with a pinch of salt, however, because of the single group pre–post design and the reliance on self-reported measures. The study offers practical information for coaches, educators, and sport practitioners who want to create inclusive and multidimensional training environments for university athletes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-49241-4.title: Multicenter evaluation of anatomical landmark versus technology-assisted techniques for chemotherapy venous access device implantation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-49241-4.abstract: Abstract The global incidence of cancer has significantly increased, resulting in the expanded use of innovative systemic treatments that require implantable vascular access devices, thus increasing the frequency of device implantation. These implants are associated with low complication rates, good patient tolerance, and a relatively short learning curve for both surgeons and radiologists. However, various factors, including patient characteristics, anatomical variations, underlying pathologies, and the surgeon’s preferred technique, continue to pose challenges to standardized implementation. This variability may influence procedural success and complication rates. Therefore, a systematic comparison between anatomical landmark-based and technology-assisted approaches is necessary to determine whether differences in outcomes are attributable to the implantation method itself and to support evidence-based clinical decision-making. Hence, the importance of evaluating the outcomes of two common approaches to device implantation: one based on anatomical landmarks, relying solely on surface anatomical references for vascular access, and the other assisted by technology, which incorporates real-time imaging modalities such as ultrasound guidance for venous cannulation and fluoroscopic imaging for catheter tip positioning and procedural verification. This retrospective, multicenter cohort study analyzed oncology patients indicated for intravenous chemotherapy, with data collected from four institutions in Bogotá between June 1, 2016, and December 31, 2021. A total of 867 patients with diagnoses of hematolymphoid, gastric, colon, pancreatic, or breast cancer were included, excluding those with hypercoagulability syndrome, arrhythmias, or pacemaker use at the time of implantation. The data were systematically recorded using the REDCap ® application. Quantitative variables were analyzed using descriptive statistics, whereas categorical variables were analyzed using the chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test, as appropriate. Continuous variables were assessed using t tests or Mann–Whitney U tests. Kaplan‒Meier survival models were used to analyze the time to complications based on the catheter insertion technique, and the anatomical reference point (ARP) technique was compared with the technology-assisted (TA) insertion technique. The incidence of complications was calculated using the relative risk (RR) with a significance level of p < 0.05. A total of 3,308 clinical records of patients undergoing totally implantable venous access device (TIVAD) implantation were reviewed, and 867 individuals who met the inclusion criteria were selected: 464 (53.5%) in the technology-assisted (TA) group and 403 (46.5%) in the anatomical reference point (ARP) group, with equivalent sociodemographic characteristics. The statistically significant findings included the presence of hematomas as a complication and the use of prophylactic antibiotics and fluoroscopy to assess catheter positioning, both of which are associated with a higher complication rate at 90 days post-operation. Additionally, a surgical time greater than or equal to 30 min was associated with a trend toward greater incidence of complications, although this difference did not reach statistical significance (RR = 4.24). No significant differences were found between implantation techniques based on anatomical reference points (ARPs) and those based on technology-assisted (TA) methods in terms of complication rates. The implantation of TIVADs in oncology patients with different primary cancers is safe and feasible. Although this study provides a clear definition of the advantages of different techniques, future research using controlled clinical trials is recommended to validate our findings and definitively determine the optimal TIVAD insertion technique.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69564-6.title: Longitudinal trajectories of kinesiophobia and associated factors in patients with chronic heart failure
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69564-6.abstract: Kinesiophobia is prevalent among patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), adversely affecting exercise adherence and rehabilitation outcomes. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its temporal change patterns and population heterogeneity is scarce. To identify distinct trajectories of kinesiophobia in patients with CHF during the first year post-discharge and to explore their associated factors. A prospective longitudinal observational study was conducted between May 2022 and June 2024 involving 277 patients with CHF. Kinesiophobia was assessed using the Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia-Heart (TSK-SV Heart) at discharge, and at 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months post-discharge. Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) identified alteration patterns by comparing 1 to 5 classes. Random forest analysis ranked variable importance, and multinomial logistic regression identified factors associated with trajectory classes. Three distinct kinesiophobia development trajectories were identified: Persistently Low Fear (43.3%), Progressively Increasing Fear (32.5%), and Persistently High Fear (24.2%). Compared to the Persistently Low group, the Persistently High trajectory was associated with a higher NYHA class ( P < 0.001) and a greater symptom burden ( P = 0.001). Conversely, a higher LVEF was associated with a lower likelihood of belonging to the Persistently High group ( P = 0.024). Compared to the Persistently Low group, the Progressively Increasing trajectory was associated with a greater symptom burden ( P = 0.002) and more severe fatigue ( P = 0.002). Kinesiophobia in patients with CHF exhibited three heterogeneous trajectories during the first year post-discharge. Symptom burden, NYHA class, LVEF, and fatigue were significantly associated factors. These should be incorporated into stratified assessment and continuous follow-up early after discharge to implement targeted interventions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65544-y.title: Bioarchaeological evidence of mycoses during the Late Antiquity–Early Middle Ages transition in Central Italy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65544-y.abstract: The collapse of the Roman Empire led to significant changes in the health status of populations in Italy. Socio-cultural, climatic, and geopolitical shifts, including the migration of the Longobards, influenced the lifestyle of many post-Roman communities. Their conquest led to agricultural intensification and reduced crop diversity, which likely contributed to deteriorating health. In this study, we examine burials from the archaeological site of Selvicciola (Viterbo, central Italy, late fourth - early eighth centuries CE) and find evidence of mycoses infections in several individuals (C14 dated between 426 and 639 CE). We propose that changes in agriculture, limited diet, and environmental factors may have increased infection rates, including those caused by fungi, which are often underdiagnosed by paleopathologists. This is due to the lack of uniform criteria for identifying mycotic infections in the discipline. In this study, we build on the existing clinical and paleopathological literature on fungal disease to develop a structured differential diagnostic approach, using the Selvicciola assemblage as a case study. Our approach integrates lesion morphology, internal bone response, and 3D imaging, and includes a threshold method applied to mycotic infections.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68326-8.title: Cooperative trading and low-carbon economic dispatch in multiple integrated energy systems based on comprehensive contribution
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68326-8.abstract: he cooperative operation of multi-integrated energy systems (MIES) significantly improves stability and reliability. However, achieving fair and efficient energy trading and profit distribution among individual integrated energy systems (IES) remains challenging, particularly when electricity, heat, and carbon quota trading are intertwined. To address this issue, we propose a collaborative optimization framework that simultaneously considers multi-energy trading and a comprehensive contribution index for revenue allocation. First, a peer-to-peer trading platform encompassing electricity, thermal, and carbon quotas is established, with each IES equipped with carbon capture and power-to-gas facilities. Second, a cooperative operation model is formulated using the Nash bargaining approach, quantifying the integrated contribution of each IES and integrating it into the profit distribution mechanism. Finally, the model is solved in a distributed manner via the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), ensuring data privacy for all participants. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy not only reduces the total operating costs and carbon emissions of MIES but also stabilizes the cooperative relationship through a fair profit distribution mechanism.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68385-x.title: Identification and characterization of genes in response to DBP and 2,4-DTBP stress in Glehnia littoralis seedlings
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68385-x.abstract: Mining genes responsive to allelochemicals dibutyl phthalate (DBP) and 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol (2,4-DTBP) stress in Glehnia littoralis to provide a molecular-level scientific reference for addressing continuous cropping obstacles. This study utilized the Illumina MiSeq high-throughput sequencing platform to treat G. littoralis seedlings with exogenous allelochemicals (DBP and 2,4-DTBP). Key genes responsive to allelopathic stress were screened, and their structures and functions were analyzed. The expression of these key genes in different parts of G. littoralis was examined via qPCR, and codon usage bias in G. littoralis was evaluated. The key genes GLERF1 , GLPYL , and GLMAPKKK17-18 in G. littoralis responsive to allelopathic stress were successfully cloned. Bioinformatic predictions indicated that the proteins encoded by these three genes are hydrophilic and lack transmembrane structures. Spatial expression analysis revealed that GLERF1 and GLPYL exhibit similar expression patterns across different tissues, with the highest expression levels observed in leaves and the lowest in roots. In contrast, GLMAPKKK17_18 showed the opposite trend, displaying minimal expression in leaves but high expression in roots, flowers, and other organs. Codon usage bias analysis revealed that G. littoralis prefers codons ending with A/U. Compared with mutational pressure, natural selection exerts a greater influence on the codon usage preference of most G. littoralis genes. Subcellular localization prediction indicated that the proteins encoded by these three genes are all expressed in the nucleus. This study provides a scientific basis for subsequent continuous cropping, genetic breeding, and resource conservation of G. littoralis .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68263-6.title: The mediating role of academic resilience in the relationship between nurse faculty support and clinical adjustment in nursing students: a structural equation modeling analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68263-6.abstract: The global shortage of nurses has intensified the need to effectively recruit and retain new graduates, placing a premium on the successful clinical training of nursing students. Nurse faculty members are pivotal in this process, yet the mechanisms through which their support translates into students’ clinical adjustment remain underexplored. This study aimed to investigate the mediating role of academic resilience in the relationship between nurse faculty support and clinical adjustment among nursing students. Following the STROBE checklist, we conducted an analytical cross-sectional study among 452 nursing students recruited from nursing faculties in Ardabil province, northwest Iran. Data were collected using three validated instruments: the Clinical Adjustment Scale–Student Nurse version (CAS-SN), the Nursing Faculty Support Scale (NFSS), and the Nursing Student Academic Resilience Inventory (NSARI). The data were analyzed using SPSS version 26 and AMOS version 24. A structural equation modeling (SEM) approach with bootstrapping was employed to test the hypothesized mediation model. Students reported high levels of nurse faculty support and moderate to high levels of Academic resilience, along with an overall positive clinical adjustment. Nurse faculty support demonstrated a direct and positive association with clinical adjustment (β = 0.622, p < 0.001). Academic resilience showed a significant mediating role (β = 0.368, p < 0.001), partially mediating the association between nurse faculty support and clinical adjustment. The findings confirm that academic resilience partially mediates the relationship between nurse faculty support and clinical adjustment. This suggests that improving faculty support alone is insufficient; rather, nursing educators should implement targeted strategies to simultaneously support faculty-student interactions and promote academic resilience. Such dual-focused interventions may facilitate a smoother transition into clinical practice and contribute to the development of competent, retained nursing professionals.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68556-w.title: Wearable Gait Biomarkers and Explainable AI Identify High Retrospective Prodromal Burden in Parkinson’s Disease
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68556-w.abstract: Abstract Objective wearable markers of Parkinson’s disease (PD) progression and phenotypic heterogeneity remain clinically relevant, particularly in relation to the burden of non-motor features that often precede or accompany the motor diagnosis. In patients with established PD, the retrospective accumulation of prodromal symptoms may identify a clinically meaningful subgroup with broader multisystem involvement. This study developed an interpretable machine-learning framework using wearable inertial gait data to model high retrospective prodromal burden within established PD, defined as the anamnestic presence of at least three prodromal symptoms. A total of 274 individuals with PD performed 30-m walking trials using a single lumbar inertial sensor. Thirty-five biomechanical and clinical variables were extracted, and feature selection identified five key predictors: multiscale entropy ( $$\:MSE$$ ) along three axes, vertical improved harmonic ratio ( $$\:{iHR}_{v}$$ ), and body weight. A Random Forest classifier balanced through CTGAN-based training-set augmentation reached a cross-validated ROC AUC of 0.84 ( $$\:{PR}_{AUC}$$ = 0.86, $$\:F1-score$$ = 0.76); on the untouched real held-out test set, discrimination was $$\:{ROC}_{AUC}$$ = 0.74 and $$\:{PR}_{AUC}$$ = 0.71, consistent with an internally developed phenotyping model requiring external validation. Explainability analyses highlighted that increased $$\:MSE$$ and reduced $$\:{iHR}_{v}$$ were the strongest contributors to high retrospective prodromal burden, indicating elevated gait complexity and altered spatio-temporal symmetry. These findings delineate an interpretable gait phenotype associated with high retrospective prodromal burden in established PD, supporting wearable gait analysis as a tool for within-PD digital phenotyping.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69648-3.title: Mechanical behavior and failure mechanisms of waste rock–phosphogypsum cemented backfill
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69648-3.abstract: This study investigates the mechanical behavior and failure mechanisms of cemented backfill composed of waste rock and phosphogypsum. Slump tests were conducted on slurries containing fine-grained waste rock (Type A aggregate, 0–3 mm), coarse-grained waste rock (Type B aggregate, 3–5 mm), and varying proportions of phosphogypsum to determine the optimal mix concentration. Uniaxial compression tests, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and numerical simulations were then employed to examine stress–strain responses, acoustic emission characteristics, energy evolution, and fracture development. The results demonstrate that phosphogypsum addition effectively improves slurry workability. At a mass concentration of 78%, all slurry mixtures exhibited slump values within the favorable pipeline transport range of 27.5–28.5 cm. For the same phosphogypsum content, Type B aggregate specimens exhibited peak strengths 144%–183% higher and elastic moduli 125%–245% higher than those of Type A specimens. As phosphogypsum content increased from 30% to 50%, the peak strength and elastic modulus of both aggregate types decreased by 74%–76% and 65%–76%, respectively. Input energy density and elastic energy density increased with larger aggregate particle size but decreased with higher phosphogypsum content, whereas dissipated energy density showed the opposite trend. Type A specimens predominantly failed in tension, whereas Type B specimens transitioned from tensile to mixed tensile–shear failure as phosphogypsum content decreased. For both aggregate types, the ratio of tensile to shear cracks decreased with declining phosphogypsum content. These findings provide new insights into optimizing waste rock–phosphogypsum backfill design within the tested ranges.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69089-y.title: Sustainable pulse electrodeposition of copper from cyanide-free alkaline baths enables high-performance and additive-free industrial coatings
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69089-y.abstract: Cyanide-free alkaline copper electrodeposition represents a sustainable alternative to traditional hazardous baths, yet direct current (DC) methods often suffer from severe non-uniformity and poor aesthetic quality. This study investigates pulse current (PC) electrodeposition as an efficient strategy to overcome these limitations. Results show that, in cyanide-free baths, PC deposition improves coating homogeneity, reduces grain size and increases gloss to values exceeding 1000 compared with DC (171). This dramatic aesthetic and structural enhancement stems from the high peak current densities during pulse times, which generate elevated cathodic overpotentials that strongly promote high crystal nucleation rates over grain growth. Furthermore, PC parameters enable effective additive-free deposition, avoiding the local coating burning and decomposition caused by organic additives under high instantaneous current densities. When applied to complex 3D fashion accessories, optimized PC deposition achieved exceptional thickness uniformity, reducing standard deviation from ± 3.7 μm (DC) to just ± 0.4 μm. These findings demonstrate that tailored PC electrodeposition provides a green, high-performance and additive-free solution for decorative industrial plating.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68948-y.title: Efficacy of bioelectric toothbrush in reducing gingival inflammation: a randomized controlled trial
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68948-y.abstract: Abstract Mechanical plaque control is the cornerstone of preventing dental plaque-induced gingivitis; however, conventional methods often fail to disrupt the protective extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix of mature biofilms. Bioelectric (BE) technology, utilizing low-level microcurrents (50–200 µA), has emerged as an innovative approach to electrochemically weaken this matrix. In this 4-week randomized, examiner-blinded, parallel-group clinical trial, 99 systemically healthy adults with mild-to-moderate dental plaque-induced gingivitis were randomly assigned ( n = 33 per group) to a BE, manual, or sonic toothbrush. All participants brushed twice daily using a standardized fluoride dentifrice. At week 4, the BE group achieved a significantly lower baseline-adjusted mean Gingival Index (GI) score (0.82) than the manual (1.41; P < 0.001) and sonic (1.08; P = 0.023) groups. For plaque control (adjusted Plaque Index [PI]), both the BE and sonic groups outperformed the manual group ( P < 0.05), with no significant difference between the two powered toothbrushes. For bleeding on probing (adjusted %BOP), the BE group achieved a significantly lower score than the manual group (8.76% vs. 14.30%; P = 0.033). No adverse events were reported. The bioelectric toothbrush significantly improved gingival inflammation compared with both manual and sonic toothbrushes, demonstrated plaque-control efficacy comparable to sonic toothbrushing, and achieved greater reductions in bleeding on probing than manual toothbrushing. Trial registration: Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS), KCT0011422, first registered 07 January 2026. doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69192-0.title: Soil erosion, soil and water conservation and water environment coupling in the Luofu River watershed, Dongjiang River Basin
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69192-0.abstract: Soil erosion and its coupled interaction with water environment have become critical threats to drinking water security in the hilly red soil regions of southern China. This study targeted the Luofu River Watershed, a typical agricultural headwater catchment in the upper reaches of Dongjiang River Basin. We integrated the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE), field monitoring, geospatial analysis, and principal component analysis (PCA), coupling coordination degree model and Pearson correlation analysis to systematically quantify the spatiotemporal patterns, driving mechanisms of soil erosion, its coupling relationship with water environment, and the comprehensive efficiency of soil and water conservation (SWC) measures. The results revealed that hydraulic erosion is the dominant erosion type across the watershed. The average soil erosion modulus was 892 t·km⁻²·a⁻¹, which falls into the mild erosion grade at the watershed scale, while local high-intensity erosion hotspots were widely distributed. Moderate and intense erosion areas only accounted for 8.38% of the total watershed area, and these regions were mainly concentrated in densely populated agricultural villages. Sloping farmland acted as the primary sediment source, contributing 67.2% of the total soil loss. Significant positive coupling relationships were detected between soil erosion and water quality degradation: the erosion modulus showed extremely significant positive correlations with sediment concentration and total phosphorus (TP) concentration, with correlation coefficients of 0.96 and 0.93 respectively ( P < 0.001). TP derived from soil erosion contributed 78.5% to the total agricultural non-point source TP loading, which pushed the water environment carrying capacity (WECC) close to the early warning threshold. Natural factors explained 58.2% of the total variability in soil erosion, among which topographic (LS) factor and rainfall erosivity (R) were the dominant natural controls. Anthropogenic activities accounted for 41.8% of erosion variation and served as key amplifiers for local high-intensity erosion. The combined application of engineering, ecological and agronomic SWC measures reduced total soil loss by 60.1% and TP loading by 45.8%. The zoned classified management framework proposed in this study can provide scientific support for soil erosion control and drinking‑water‑source protection within the Luofu River watershed in the upper Dongjiang River Basin, and may serve as a potential practical reference for comparable small agricultural headwater catchments in southern China’s red‑soil hilly regions. Further local calibration would be required before direct application to other watersheds.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68828-5.title: Boundary-interior ratio: a spatially decomposed evaluation framework for CNN and mamba-based breast ultrasound segmentation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68828-5.abstract: Breast tumour segmentation in ultrasound imaging requires both fine boundary delineation and global contextual understanding. Existing evaluation metrics such as the Dice Similarity Coefficient provide aggregate performance estimates but do not distinguish segmentation behaviour between boundary and interior tumour regions. This study presents a hypothesis-driven comparative evaluation examining whether CNN, pure SSM, and hybrid SSM-CNN architectures exhibit distinct boundary-interior segmentation profiles. U-Net (ResNet-34 encoder), Vision Mamba (pure SSM), and VM-UNet (hybrid SSM-CNN) were trained on 3,333 breast ultrasound images (BUSI, BUS-BRA, BUS-UC) and externally validated on three independent sites (BrEaST, BLUI, BUS-UCLM; n = 748). We introduce the Boundary-Interior Ratio (BIR), a spatially decomposed metric quantifying relative segmentation performance between boundary and interior regions, together with a Grad-CAM-based Boundary-Interior Activation Ratio (BIAR) for mechanistic analysis. A structured four-variant ablation study examines the contributions of skip connections, VSS blocks, and hierarchical encoding. U-Net achieves the highest internal Dice (0.874) and strongest external generalisation (mean Dice = 0.771). Both SSM-based architectures exhibit higher BIR than U-Net (VM-UNet: 0.707; Vision Mamba: 0.722 vs. U-Net: 0.683), indicating distinct relative boundary-interior performance profiles. The ablation study shows that removing VSS blocks substantially improves absolute segmentation performance (Dice: 0.777→0.832; HD95: 18.75→12.61 px) while leaving BIR essentially unchanged (0.707→0.708), whereas removing skip connections produces the largest BIR change (0.707→0.652). These findings demonstrate that aggregate segmentation quality and boundary-interior performance provide complementary information, and that BIR reveals architectural differences not captured by Dice alone. The ablation results further indicate that, under the present training configuration, hierarchical encoding and skip-connected pathways have greater effects on overall segmentation performance and BIR variation, respectively, than the inclusion of VSS blocks alone. Under the present training configuration, the evaluated SSM architecture does not provide an absolute performance advantage, highlighting the need for future evaluation with pretrained SSM representations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69269-w.title: Comparison of anesthesiologist and Large Language Model recommendations for maintenance anesthetic dosing during upper extremity reconstruction without neuromuscular blockade
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69269-w.abstract: Maintaining an optimal depth of anesthesia is crucial for surgical success and patient safety. While large language models (LLMs) offer potential for clinical decision support, comparative studies evaluating their judgment against expert anesthesiologists remain scarce. This study aimed to compare the performance of three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Copilot, and Gemini 1.5 Pro) against experienced anesthesiologists in determining maintenance doses of intravenous anesthetic agents during muscle relaxant-free upper extremity reconstructive surgery. This retrospective observational comparative study evaluated 198 patients undergoing upper extremity reconstructive surgery at Hazrat Fatemeh Hospital (March–April 2025). Demographic parameters, patient body weight, and clinical signs of light anesthesia were extracted retrospectively from perioperative medical records. Standardized prompts were evaluated across the three LLMs, and their suggested maintenance doses (defined as total cumulative bolus dose in mg administered during the entire maintenance phase) were compared against actual administered doses. Statistical analysis utilized paired t-tests, Intraclass Correlation Coefficients [ICC (2,1), Bland–Altman agreement analysis, Cohen’s kappa, and linear regression to assess agreement and diagnostic performance. Among 198 analyzed patients (89.4% male; mean age: 33.13 ± 11.53 years; mean weight: 81.19 ± 17.28 kg), intraoperative signs of light anesthesia occurred in 10.1% of cases ( n = 20). Anesthesiologists significantly escalated total maintenance doses in response to these clinical signs (23.55 mg vs. 15.58 mg; p < 0.001), whereas evaluated LLMs exhibited minimal dynamic adjustment (28.08 mg vs. 27.74 mg; p = 0.472). LLM-suggested doses correlated strongly with patient weight ( r = 0.881, p < 0.001; R-squared = 77.6%), compared to a moderate correlation in human decisions ( r = 0.363, p < 0.001; R-squared = 13.2%). Following patient parameter adjustments, Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a substantial reduction in mean bias to -1.67 mg (SD = 5.87; 95% CI: -2.48 to -0.85 mg), with 95% limits of agreement ranging from − 13.16 to + 9.83 mg and an adjusted ICC (2,1) of 0.270. The raw ICC (2,1) for unadjusted LLM outputs was 0.041. The adjusted Bland–Altman analysis was performed using a post-hoc calibration factor derived from the mean human expert dose within the same study cohort; therefore, this adjustment does not reflect the intrinsic performance of the raw LLM outputs. Although LLMs demonstrated high specificity (100%) in identifying necessary dose increases, their sensitivity remained low at 36.0% (kappa = 0.496). Standalone commercial LLMs cannot replace clinical judgment in dynamic intraoperative environments. Their primary reliance on static parameters such as body weight and limited adaptation to real-time clinical signs can lead to sub-optimal dose titration. Future integration should focus on hybrid decision-support models, where medically fine-tuned AI acts as a real-time advisory tool under primary human supervision.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65676-1.title: Abundance and ecophysiology of MiDAS 4 family f37-13 filamentous bacteria in Japan possessing the Eikelboom morphotype 1863
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65676-1.abstract: Abstract Members of the Bacteroidota family MiDAS 4 f37-13 are plentiful in activated sludge microbial communities, although most are uncultured.
