This study focused on their identification and influence on activated sludge bulking. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) analysis of samples from a Japanese enhanced biological nutrient removal (EBNR) plant showed they possessed a filamentous morphology, sharing an Eikelboom 1863 morphotype, previously described for the Gamma-proteobacteria Acinetobacter. Members of two genera, midas_g_535 and midas_g_543, exhibited higher relative abundances than the other genera in the family MiDAS 4 f37-13. Neither were members of the Gamma - proteobacteria . Both showed a statistically significant correlation with plant sludge volume index, suggesting they were responsible for activated sludge bulking in this WWTP. Metagenome analyses revealed that existing metagenome-assembled genomes within the MiDAS 4 f37-13 family possessed genes associated with denitrification, polyphosphate accumulation, and polyhydroxyalkanoate synthesis, and their potential role in nitrogen and phosphate removal in EBNR WWTPs is discussed.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68458-x.title: A nighttime pedestrian detection method based on YOLOv8s with joint image enhancement and network structural optimization
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68458-x.abstract: Accurate pedestrian detection in nighttime traffic scenarios remains a critical challenge for autonomous driving perception systems, mainly due to contrast degradation caused by insufficient illumination and the loss of target information caused by occlusion. To address these issues, this study adopts YOLOv8s as the baseline detector and proposes a joint framework that integrates image enhancement and structural optimization for nighttime pedestrian detection. Specifically, an I-SCI illumination enhancement strategy is embedded into the front-end of the improved YOLOv8s detector to enhance the visibility of low-light images. Furthermore, three structural optimization strategies are introduced to overcome the challenges of poor illumination and target occlusion. First, RepGFPN is employed to construct multiple cross-layer feature interaction paths, enhancing multi-scale feature fusion capability and enabling the network to better distinguish pedestrian contours from background light interference. Second, a Dynamic Attention Transformer (DAT) module is incorporated to focus on critical spatial response regions. By leveraging contextual information from visible body parts, such as the head and legs, DAT can infer the semantic information of occluded regions, thereby reducing missed detections and suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. Third, the MPDIoU loss function is introduced to improve localization accuracy. Through refined corner constraints, MPDIoU effectively reduces prediction box deviation and enhances the spatial consistency between predicted and ground-truth bounding boxes. The proposed optimization strategies work collaboratively to improve the accuracy and robustness of pedestrian detection under low-light conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLO-PN achieves significant improvements over the baseline YOLOv8s, with Precision, Recall, and mAP increased by 4.15, 4.57, and 3.88% points, respectively. These results indicate that the proposed method substantially enhances the adaptability and detection stability of the YOLOv8s framework in complex nighttime traffic scenarios, providing an effective solution for nighttime perception in autonomous driving systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68664-7.title: Thermal–hydraulic performance of high-angle twisted tapes with MWCNT–Fe3O4 hybrid nanofluids under turbulent flow
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68664-7.abstract: Abstract The thermo-hydraulic performance of plain tube (PT) and twisted-tape (TT) inserts having different swirl angles (30°, 45°, 60°, and 90°) using base fluid (DW) and hybrid MWCNTs–Fe 3 O 4 nanofluids was numerically solved in this study. The physical problem was solved at various fluid-flow velocities (Re = 5000–17,000) and inlet temperatures (T in = 293.15–323.15 K). The two geometries were solved using the SST k-ω turbulence model and validated against the Dittus–Boelter and Blasius correlations, with four grid sizes. The numerical results demonstrate that TT inserts significantly enhance convective heat transfer, yielding Nu improvements of 45–87% relative to PT, while incurring pressure-drop penalties (ΔP) of 115–140%. The TT-90° configuration consistently achieved the highest thermo-hydraulic performance (η TH ), with η TH = 1.3975 at Re = 5000, corresponding to a 39.8% net improvement under equal pumping power. The hybrid nanofluid alone provided reasonable heat-transfer augmentation (≈ 0.3–0.8%) relative to DW but introduced additional hydraulic resistance (≈ 13–21%). Flow-structure analysis revealed intensified secondary vortices and swirl-induced mixing as the primary mechanisms governing heat-transfer enhancement. Overall, the integration of MWCNTs–Fe 3 O 4 /DW and high-angle TT offers superior thermo-hydraulic performance, particularly at lower fluid flow velocity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69112-2.title: Comparative analysis of ANN and COMBI models for predicting thermal-hydraulic performance of fly ash nanofluid
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69112-2.abstract: Abstract This study presents a machine learning–based comparative analysis of artificial neural network (ANN) and Combinatorial Algorithm (COMBI) models for predicting the thermal–hydraulic performance of fly ash nanofluids under turbulent flow conditions. Fly ash, an abundant industrial by-product, is employed as a sustainable and cost-effective nanoparticle source for enhanced heat transfer applications. Published experimental data (75 observations) from Kanti et al. was used in this study, with Reynolds number (7,042–45,155), nanoparticle concentration (0–2 vol%), and inlet fluid temperature (30–60 °C) as input variables, while heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number, pressure drop, and friction factor were output responses. Both ANN and COMBI models were trained using an 80/20 train–test split with Min–Max normalization and evaluated using R², RMSE, MAE, and MAPE metrics. The COMBI model demonstrated consistently superior performance over the ANN across all outputs, achieving higher predictive accuracy with R² values up to 0.9968 for pressure drop prediction. In contrast, the ANN exhibited comparatively lower accuracy across the same outputs. Five-fold cross-validation confirmed the robustness of the COMBI model, with a mean R² of 0.9841 (σ = 0.0027), indicating stable generalization compared to ANN (0.9759, σ = 0.0061). Sensitivity analysis identified Reynolds number as the most influential parameter (~ 83.6%), followed by inlet temperature (~ 9.2%) and concentration (~ 7.2%). A key advantage of the COMBI framework is its ability to generate explicit polynomial equations for all output variables, enabling transparent interpretation and direct implementation without retraining.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66642-7.title: Explainable attention-based multi-omics fusion with protein language models for CML-versus-control classification and biomarker discovery
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66642-7.abstract: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) is a well-defined hematological malignancy driven principally by the BCR::ABL1 fusion oncogene and aberrant tyrosine kinase signaling. Computational methods to predict leukemia suffer from the limitation of using single-modality data or black-box models, which cannot adequately incorporate complementary molecular evidence and deliver interpretable biomarker support. In this study, we introduce an explainable multi-omics fusion approach that combines protein language model embeddings, gene-expression data, mutation-level data, and pathway-informed representations to classify CML-positive and control samples and identify candidate biomarkers. The pre-trained protein language models encode context from the sequence, and dense encoders represent modalities based on transcriptomic, mutational, and pathway information. They are fused adaptively for classification using an attention module, and biomarkers are ranked by SHAP, Integrated Gradients, and attention attribution to support biological interpretation. The proposed framework achieved an accuracy of (98.14%), precision (98.0%), recall (98.4%), F1-score (98.14%), ROC–AUC (0.991), and PR–AUC (0.987), outperforming classical machine learning, deep learning, single-modality, and conventional fusion baselines. Reliability analysis yielded a Brier score of 0.031, and an Expected Calibration Error of 0.024, and stable performance on five-fold cross-validation (97.9 ± 0.4% accuracy and 0.988 ± 0.003 ROC–AUC). Biologically relevant biomarkers identified by explainability analysis included the BCR::ABL1 fusion gene, ABL1 kinase-domain mutations, BCL2, HSP90, RUNX1, ASXL1, PARP1 and RB1, and key pathways were identified: JAK–STAT, PI3K–AKT, RAS–MAPK, apoptosis and DNA repair. The findings indicate that the proposed model achieved improved predictive performance under the evaluated experimental conditions and provided interpretable identification of candidate biomarkers in CML and control samples.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68231-0.title: Fallibility, persuadability, and correctability of large language models under sustained conversational misinformation pressure
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68231-0.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence has emerged as a transformative global force, yet the reliability of large language models (LLMs) under sustained conversational misinformation pressure remains poorly characterized. While recent work has begun to evaluate multi-turn LLM behavior, the full spectrum of conversational susceptibility — encompassing fallibility, persuadability, and correctability — has not been systematically assessed. Here we systematically evaluated seven widely used LLMs - ChatGPT (GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini), Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama-3-70B, and DeepSeek - across three dimensions of conversational susceptibility. We assessed fallibility (susceptibility to accepting misinformation under repetitive exposure), persuadability (susceptibility to acceptance under progressively argumentative pressure), and correctability (capacity to recognize and correct self-generated misinformation). One hundred purposefully false statements spanning a range of informational obscurity were presented across 50-repetition conversational sequences. Under repetitive engagement, misinformation affirmation rates ranged from 0.08% to 12.3%, a greater than 150-fold difference across architectures, with ChatGPT 3.5 demonstrating the greatest vulnerability and Claude 3.5 Sonnet the greatest resistance. A novel phenomenon of conversational reverberation was identified, in which models oscillated unpredictably between accepting and rejecting the same false statement across successive turns. Misinformation susceptibility was significantly modulated by informational obscurity under repetitive but not argumentative conditions (χ² = 11.13, p = 0.0038), implicating training data frequency as a determinant of factual resistance. Correctability was heterogeneous: four models achieved 100% self-correction, while the model with the lowest error rate failed to correct any of its rare errors, a dissociation with important implications for deployment. These findings demonstrate that conversational dynamics expose LLM failure modes invisible to standard evaluation, with direct consequences for model selection and use in truth-critical domains.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67376-2.title: A methodological approach for creating virtual patient cohorts reflecting real-world diabetes treatment outcomes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67376-2.abstract: Abstract Virtual patients (VPs) are widely used to evaluate the performance, scope, and robustness of glycemic-control strategies. However, existing virtual cohorts often include too few subjects or fail to reflect the diversity of the intended clinical population. Generating new VPs that reproduce real-patient (RP) characteristics is therefore crucial for advancing diabetes therapies. We present a data-driven method to construct VP cohorts matched to individual RPs using routine therapy and outcome data. Starting from published probability distributions of Hovorka model parameters, we generated candidate VPs by Monte Carlo sampling and retained only physiologically plausible parameter sets. For each RP, the common pool of physiologically plausible VPs was evaluated separately. VPs passing the RP-specific basal-insulin prefilter were then simulated under meal-and-exercise scenarios derived from that RP’s data. We then used a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) to select, for each RP, the strictest similarity thresholds that preserved at least 20 matched VPs. Similarity was assessed using therapy parameters and CGM-derived outcomes. The method was tested using anonymized data from eight adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) who participated in a clinical trial conducted at the Hospital Clínic of Barcelona. From 20,000 candidate VPs, 8,387 passed the physiological plausibility screening. The CSP-based filtering procedure retained 20–43 matched VPs per RP. The selected cohorts were characterized at the patient level using therapy and CGM-derived metrics, including basal insulin, TIR, hypoglycemia, severe hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, and severe hyperglycemia. Across five protocol-matched in silico scenarios, 43 of 45 endpoint-by-scenario comparisons did not reach nominal significance in paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Two comparisons in Scenario 2 reached nominal significance: severe hyperglycemia and glucose coefficient of variation. These findings support the feasibility of constructing VP cohorts matched to individual RP profiles, reproducing key therapy and CGM features under protocol-matched conditions. The approach may support preclinical controller tuning and robustness assessment, although further validation in larger and more heterogeneous datasets is required.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67889-w.title: Both iron overload and ferroptosis induce trophoblast dysfunction and impair hCG secretion in cell models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67889-w.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that iron-related cell death may contribute to placental dysfunction. During pregnancy, placenta-mediated iron supply is critical for fetal development. Iron demand rises substantially during gestation and must be tightly regulated: while insufficient iron compromises fetal growth, excessive iron accumulation can be highly toxic. In particular, iron overload can trigger ferroptosis, an iron-dependent, non-apoptotic form of programmed cell death characterized by redox imbalance and accumulation of lipid-reactive oxygen species. In this study, we investigated ferroptosis and iron toxicity in various trophoblast cell models (BeWo, differentiated BeWo, and JEG-3). Treatment with ferroptosis inducers (erastin and RSL3) or iron (ammonium ferric citrate and hemin arginate) caused a significant, specific concentration-dependent reduction in hCG secretion, increased cytotoxicity, and oxidative stress. Iron chelator or antioxidant effectively reversed only some of these iron-induced effects. Here, we report that, in BeWo and JEG-3 choriocarcinoma cell models, iron overload and ferroptosis impair hCG secretion without affecting other endocrine functions. Further studies in primary trophoblasts and in vivo models are needed to determine whether these observations extend to placental function during pregnancy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66040-z.title: Influence of treatment experience on awareness and re-selection of orthodontic appliances among adolescents receiving fixed orthodontic therapy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66040-z.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate awareness, perceptions, and treatment preferences regarding alternative orthodontic appliances among adolescents undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment. This cross-sectional study included 302 adolescents (mean age: 16.57 ± 1.11 years; range, 15–18 years) receiving fixed orthodontic treatment with metal brackets at the Department of Orthodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Ege University. Data were collected using a structured 15-item online questionnaire assessing treatment experiences, awareness of orthodontic options, perceived effectiveness, esthetic perceptions, and oral hygiene considerations. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used, with Cramer’s V calculated to quantify effect sizes. Binary logistic regression was performed to evaluate whether gender and treatment duration were independently associated with treatment re-selection. Peers and social media were the primary sources of treatment-related information. Metal brackets were the most recognized modality, whereas lingual appliances were the least known. Difficulty eating and maintaining oral hygiene were the most frequently reported treatment-related challenges. Although clear aligners were associated with easier oral hygiene and fewer clinical visits, metal brackets were more frequently perceived as the most effective modality and remained the most commonly preferred option. Gender was significantly associated with treatment re-selection (χ 2 = 6.30, p = 0.012). After adjustment for treatment duration, male participants had higher odds of selecting clear aligners than female participants (adjusted odds ratio = 2.31, 95% confidence interval: 1.25–4.30; p = 0.008), whereas treatment duration was not independently associated with re-selection ( p = 0.421). Adolescents generally preferred the appliance with which they had direct treatment experience. Perceived effectiveness and gender-related differences were associated with treatment re-selection, whereas treatment duration was not. Because the study was conducted at a single center and included only adolescents treated with metal brackets, the findings should be interpreted primarily within this population. Providing balanced information on available treatment options before treatment initiation may support informed and patient-centered decision-making.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68237-8.title: Clinicopathological characteristics of DLBCL-associated HLH and an exploratory transcriptomic investigation of the underlying microenvironment in primary DLBCL
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68237-8.abstract: Abstract Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that can complicate diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), yet its clinicopathological characteristics and inflammatory tumor microenvironment (TME) remain incompletely understood. We retrospectively analyzed 579 newly diagnosed patients with DLBCL, including 22 with HLH and 66 matched controls without HLH, to compare their clinical and pathological characteristics. Because fresh tumor biopsies are rarely available during active HLH, publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data from treatment-naïve primary DLBCL were used as an exploratory model to characterize inflammatory TME programs. Based on these analyses, a trajectory-derived TME inflammatory signature was developed and subsequently validated in independent bulk transcriptomic cohorts. DLBCL-associated HLH occurred in 3.8% of patients and was associated with severe systemic inflammation, high tumor burden, poor survival, and enrichment of the non-germinal center B-cell-like (non-GCB) subtype and double-expressor lymphoma (DEL). Exploratory single-cell analyses identified inflammatory TME programs characterized by macrophage activation and CD8⁺ T-cell dysfunction, leading to the development of a 29-gene trajectory-derived inflammatory signature. In external validation cohorts, higher inflammatory risk scores were associated with elevated lactate dehydrogenase and International Prognostic Index scores and remained independently associated with inferior overall survival, including within the GCB subtype. These findings indicate that DLBCL-associated HLH is a highly aggressive clinical entity. Exploratory transcriptomic analyses suggest that inflammatory TME programs may represent an additional layer of biological heterogeneity in DLBCL, and the trajectory-derived inflammatory signature provides independent prognostic value across multiple DLBCL cohorts. Further studies are warranted to determine whether these inflammatory programs are associated with susceptibility to DLBCL-associated HLH.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68951-3.title: Altered ANG/TIE gene expression in advanced ovarian cancer is not accompanied by disproportionate body water accumulation relative to perioperative fluid balance
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68951-3.abstract: Abstract Abdominal cytoreductive surgery due to advanced-stage ovarian cancer (OC) often requires extensive fluid administration to stabilize hemodynamic conditions. Recently, systemic changes in the expression profile of Angiopoietin (ANG)/TIE axis genes have been demonstrated in those patients, raising the question whether they exhibit an inherent clinical phenotype associated with vascular dysfunction and leakage that may explain the significant perioperative fluid demands. Abdominal muscle tissue gene expression analysis as well as pre- and postoperative whole-body bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) in patients with OC ( n = 20) and in control subjects ( n = 16) were performed, and Total Body Water (TBW), Extracellular Water (ECW) and the ECW/TBW ratio were calculated. Intraoperative management comprised advanced hemodynamic monitoring and goal-directed therapy. Data are given as median values with interquartile range (IQR). Postoperative fluid balance normalized to duration of surgery was greater in OC group (11.2 (IQR 9.8–13.2) vs. 8.3 mL/min (6.3–10.8) in controls, p = 0.01), as was the maximum body weight-adjusted norepinephrine administration rate ( p < 0.001), whereas the intraoperative fluid administration rate did not differ between groups ( p = 0.29). Gene expression analysis revealed significantly increased ANG-2/1 and ANG-2/TIE2 expression ratios in peripheral muscle tissue from OC patients ( p < 0.01), while additional markers of angiogenesis, endothelial activation, adhesion, and vascular barrier integrity showed no significant intergroup differences. ANG-2/1 gene expression ratio was significantly associated with postoperative fluid balance in the whole cohort ( r = 0.54, p < 0.001). There were no pre- or postoperative intergroup differences in TBW, ECW and in the ECW/TBW ratio. However, intraoperative percentage increase in BIA parameters was significantly more pronounced in the OC group, compared to controls (TBW: 12.3 (9.9–14.6) vs. 8.1% (5.2–9.0), p < 0.001; ECW: 21.7 (17.1–25.9) vs. 15.5% (11.0–18.1), p < 0.001; ECW/TBW: 8.7 (7.7–10.4) vs. 6.9% (5.1–8.5), p = 0.006). Importantly, the relationships between perioperative fluid balance and changes in TBW, ECW and ECW/TBW ratio did not differ between groups (group × fluid balance interactions: p = 0.614, p = 0.511, and p = 0.545, respectively). In contrast, these BIA-derived changes increased progressively with longer duration of surgery in OC patients but not in controls, resulting in significant group × duration of surgery interactions ( p = 0.030, p = 0.018, and p = 0.037, respectively). Patients with advanced-stage OC exhibited altered ANG/TIE gene-expression profiles, greater vasopressor requirements, and a distinct time-dependent pattern of perioperative body-water accumulation during cytoreductive surgery. However, BIA did not demonstrate a disproportionate increase in body water relative to positive fluid balance compared with controls. Thus, the observed alterations in ANG/TIE gene expression were not accompanied by a detectable systemic vascular leakage phenotype using BIA.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69746-2.title: Association of air pollution with mental and behavioral disorders in young and middle-aged adults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69746-2.abstract: This study investigated the association between air pollutants and mental and behavioral disorders (MBD) among young and middle-aged people. MBD daily outpatient visits, air pollutants and meteorological data for 2017–2019 were collected. Daily data on MBD outpatient visits, air pollutants, and meteorological conditions were analyzed using a distributed lag nonlinear model (DLNM) within a generalized additive model (GAM) framework with quasi-Poisson regression. We controlled for long-term trends, day of the week, holidays, temperature, and humidity. Stratified analyses by gender were also performed. A total of 24,689 outpatient cases of MBD, 11,415 outpatient cases of depression, and 7,598 outpatient cases of anxiety were collected during the study period. From 2017 to 2019, the presence of high concentrations of SO 2 and NO 2 significantly increased the number of outpatient visits for MBD in young and middle-aged adults. High concentrations of SO 2 , NO 2 and PM 2.5 significantly increased the number of outpatient visits for depression in young and middle-aged adults. Similarly, high concentrations of SO 2 , NO 2 , and PM 10 have been observed to significantly increase outpatient visits for anxiety in this age group. This study suggested that exposure to high concentrations of air pollutants, especially SO 2 and NO 2 , will significantly increase the risk of outpatient MBD, depression, and anxiety in young and middle-aged adults.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67397-x.title: Self-compassion links premenstrual symptom severity to social and emotional well-being in nursing students
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67397-x.abstract: Abstract Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is associated with impaired quality of life in women. Although self-compassion has been associated with psychological well-being, its role in the relationship between premenstrual symptom severity and PMS-specific quality of life (PMS-QoL) remains unclear. This study investigated the mediating role of self-compassion among nursing students. In this cross-sectional study, 164 nursing students with Premenstrual Syndrome Scale (PMSS) scores ≥ 110 completed the Self-Compassion Scale and the Premenstrual Syndrome–Specific Quality of Life Scale (PMS-QoL). Pearson’s correlation and mediation analyses were conducted using PROCESS Model 4 with 5,000 bootstrap samples, adjusting for age, body mass index, and menstrual pain intensity. Greater premenstrual symptom severity was associated with lower self-compassion ( r = − 0.263, p < 0.01) and poorer PMS-QoL ( r = − 0.367, p < 0.01), whereas self-compassion exhibited a positive association with PMS-QoL ( r = 0.353, p < 0.01). Self-compassion partially mediated the association between premenstrual symptom severity and overall PMS-QoL (indirect effect = − 0.045, 95% bootstrap CI: −0.085 to − 0.015), as well as the social and emotional well-being domains, but not the physical well-being domain. These findings highlight the potential of self-compassion as a psychological resource for improving PMS-specific quality of life and fostering health and well-being among university nursing students.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68347-3.title: Resistome and virulome of multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae clinical isolates from Peru
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68347-3.abstract: Abstract Gonorrhea is a global public health issue, with the highest number of cases in Peru originating from Lima, the capital. This study conducted whole genome sequencing on 72 Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates collected from various regions of Peru between 2018 and 2023 to characterize their resistome and virulome. Among these, 31 isolates displayed high-level azithromycin resistance (MIC ≥ 256 µg/mL). The analysis revealed significant resistance rates to ciprofloxacin (95.8%), penicillin (70.8%), tetracycline (68.1%), azithromycin (55.6%), and reduced susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins, observed in 4.2% for ceftriaxone and 9.7% for cefixime. Genetic diversity assessments identified multiple sequence types (STs) using MLST, NG-MAST, and NG-STAR methods. MLST revealed 16 distinct STs and one unassigned strain, with ST-9363 being the most prevalent (52.78%, 38/72), found in five out of seven departments. NG-MAST identified 22 STs, with 15 unassigned strains, highlighting ST-3935 as the most frequent (25.0%, 18/72). NG-STAR analysis discovered 35 STs, including 14 novel types, with ST-5804 accounting for 31.94% (23/72). The resistome analysis uncovered diverse mutations linked to antibiotic resistance, while the virulome analysis detailed various virulence factors facilitating infection, immune evasion, and disease propagation. Interestingly, some isolates lacked specific virulence genes. These findings provide critical insights into the genetic diversity, antibiotic resistance profiles, and virulence characteristics of N. gonorrhoeae strains circulating in Peru from 2018 to 2023, offering essential information to guide future control and prevention strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69630-z.title: Interactive effects of salinity and nitrogen fertilization on soil ion accumulation and ion uptake in quinoa
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69630-z.abstract: Salinity is a major constraint in arid-region agriculture, where selecting appropriate irrigation water quality and optimizing nitrogen (N) fertilization are critical for maintaining soil health and sustaining quinoa production. This two-year field lysimeter experiment evaluated how different salinity levels (5, 10, 20, and 25 dS m⁻ 1 ) and N application rates (0, 150, and 300 kg N ha⁻ 1 ) affect ion dynamics in soil, nutrient uptake, and crop performance. Results showed a clear management-relevant threshold: quinoa maintained acceptable seed yield at EC e of 13 dS m⁻ 1 under adequate N supply as 150 kg N ha⁻ 1 . Under irrigation water salinity up to 10 dS m⁻ 1 , 150 kg N ha⁻ 1 is recommended to maximize seed yield. However, for highly saline water (20–25 dS m⁻ 1 ), 300 kg N ha⁻ 1 is required to mitigate salt stress and maintain acceptable yield. Increasing irrigation water salinity from 5 to 25 dS m⁻ 1 sharply elevated soil Na⁺ and Cl⁻ (227% increase), and altered the K⁺/Na⁺ balance; however, higher N rates improved plant K⁺/Na⁺ ratios, supporting better ionic homeostasis under salt stress. High salinity reduced N translocation to seeds, shifting more N to vegetative tissues. Overall, the study demonstrates that integrating moderate irrigation water salinity with optimal N fertilization can enhance ionic balance and maintain quinoa productivity under saline conditions, offering practical guidelines for irrigation and nutrient management in salt-affected cropping systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66933-z.title: Neural cellular automata approach for reducing security and privacy hazards of augmented reality environment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66933-z.abstract: The applications of the Augmented Reality (AR) environment are getting traction in the field of healthcare, smart city navigation, and industrial training and collaboration working environments. Nevertheless, this constant streaming of multimedia and the exchange of sensor information may subject the security and privacy threat of illegitimate access, data capture, and inference. Unlike prior AR frameworks, the proposed study incorporates a novel Neural Cellular Automata (NCA) layer that actively learns AR behavior and dynamically enforces spatial-temporal anomaly detection, adaptive access control and encryption. The proposed NCA layer leverages the localized state evaluation to define the spatial dependence and distributed behavioral pattern in the AR stream. The NCA layer defines rules for each stream and monitors the AR environment activities elegantly, anomaly detection with adaptive neural models, in its dynamic access decision. The layer further incorporated with an optimized key generation algorithm on a symmetric encryption technique to ensure secure transmission with minimal computational overhead. The experimental results of the proposed study show the intrusion detection rate is 96.8%, access control decision accuracy is 94.3%, and the overhead of encryption was below 6%. Analysis of a deployment in the post-deployment stage indicated that this multi-layered mechanism of privacy lessened measurable AR security and privacy risk by more than 85% in simulated attack conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69266-z.title: Sodium octanoate attenuates early post-resuscitation renal injury after hemorrhagic-induced cardiac arrest in a porcine model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69266-z.abstract: Hemorrhage is the most common cause of traumatic cardiac arrest (TCA), and post-resuscitation renal injury remains a challenging clinical research focus. Sodium octanoate has been reported to exert protective effects in models of cerebral, cardiac, and intestinal injury. To investigate the effects of sodium octanoate on post-resuscitation renal injury, we established a porcine model of controlled hemorrhage-induced cardiac arrest, which simulates the ischemic injury of TCA. A total of 18 pigs were enrolled as experimental subjects and divided into three groups: SHAM group (n = 6), TCA group (n = 6), and Sodium octanoate (SO) group (n = 6). The SHAM group underwent anesthesia only, with endotracheal intubation and arterial/venous cannulation. In the TCA group, in addition to the procedures performed in the SHAM group, a TCA model was established by withdrawing blood via the femoral artery using a blood pump and reinfusing it through the femoral vein for resuscitation. In the SO group, after the TCA model was established, sodium octanoate was intravenously infused at a total dose of 30 mg/kg, starting 5 min after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), with the infusion completed within 1 h. Resuscitation parameters and survival outcomes were recorded for all groups. Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels were measured at baseline and at multiple time points after resuscitation. Euthanasia was performed 24 h post-resuscitation, and renal tissue samples from the same anatomical location were collected to evaluate histopathological changes, expression of proteins associated with pyroptosis, and levels of inflammatory cytokines. All animals were successfully resuscitated and remained alive at 24 h post-resuscitation. Following TCA model establishment, serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels increased in both the TCA and SO groups. At 4 and 24 h post-resuscitation, SCr levels were significantly lower in the SO group than in the TCA group (both P < 0.05). BUN levels were significantly lower in the SO group than in the TCA group at all time points post-resuscitation (all P < 0.01). At 24 h post-resuscitation, renal tissue levels of NGAL, KIM-1, NLRP3, caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-1β, and IL-18 were significantly lower in the SO group than in the TCA group (all P < 0.05). Histopathological examination revealed prominent inflammatory cell infiltration and focal cellular necrosis in the TCA group, whereas the SO group treated with sodium octanoate exhibited only minimal inflammatory cell infiltration with no significant necrosis. Furthermore, at 2 and 4 h post-resuscitation, HR, MAP, and CO differed significantly between the TCA and SO groups (all P < 0.05). At 4 h post-resuscitation, Lac levels were significantly lower in the SO group than in the TCA group ( P < 0.05). This study suggests that sodium octanoate may attenuate early renal injury at 24 h post-resuscitation in a porcine model of controlled hemorrhage-induced cardiac arrest. The potential mechanism may involve the modulation of inflammasome-associated inflammatory signaling, leading to reduced inflammatory response and cellular necrosis. Sodium octanoate shows potential therapeutic value for early renal injury following resuscitation from TCA.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65051-0.title: A multivariable predictive model for trial without catheter success: integrating clinical parameters and ultrasonographic markers
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65051-0.abstract: Abstract Acute urinary retention secondary to benign prostatic hyperplasia is a common urological emergency. Although a trial without catheterisation is routinely performed after initial catheterisation, predictors of successful spontaneous voiding remain inconsistent. This study evaluated the predictive value of ultrasonographic and clinical parameters for TWOC success in patients with BPH-related AUR. This retrospective observational study enrolled 202 men aged 50–79 years who presented with AUR secondary to BPH between January 2022 and March 2026. All underwent urethral catheterisation followed by a standardised TWOC protocol. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and ultrasonographic variables, including intravesical prostatic protrusion and bladder wall thickness, were analysed using multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of TWOC success. TWOC succeeded in 98 patients (48.5%) and failed in 104 (51.5%). Successful cases were characterised by significantly lower body mass index, bladder wall thickness, and IPP grade, as well as a shorter catheter duration (all p < 0.05). TWOC success rates were 71.4% for BWT < 5 mm versus 32.2% for BWT ≥ 5 mm, and declined progressively with higher IPP grades. ROC analysis yielded a BWT cutoff of 5.35 mm (sensitivity 71.2%, specificity 84.7%). Multivariable analysis confirmed lower BMI, lower IPP grade, angiotensin receptor blocker use, and lower BWT as independent predictors. The model demonstrated good discriminatory ability (AUC 0.893, 95% CI 0.849–0.938). TWOC failure was strongly associated with subsequent surgical intervention (88.5% of patients in the failure group). Incorporating these non-invasive markers into pre-TWOC assessment may help identify patients at higher risk of catheter removal failure and inform counselling on the likelihood of requiring surgical intervention; however, external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65150-y.title: Bioreactor-based production of eumelanin nanoparticles by Streptomyces glaucescens NEAE-H: physicochemical characterization, anticancer and anti-inflammatory activities, and in silico analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65150-y.abstract: Abstract Microbial eumelanin nanoparticles (EuM-NPs) have attracted increasing attention as biocompatible and biodegradable nanomaterials with promising biomedical applications. In the present study, the production of EuM-NPs by Streptomyces glaucescens NEAE-H was optimized in a 7-L stirred-tank bioreactor under controlled fermentation conditions. The study investigated the physicochemical characteristics and the in vivo, in vitro, and in silico anticancer and anti-inflammatory activities of EuM-NPs. The maximum EuM-NPs yield reached 367.51 μg/mL after 22 h of cultivation at an agitation rate of 200 rpm. Physicochemical characterization revealed the formation of nearly spherical nanoparticles with particle sizes ranging from 1.23 to 26 nm and a mean diameter of 15.64 ± 4.576 nm. ζ-potential measurements demonstrated good colloidal stability with a surface charge of − 32.6 ± 4.65 mV. Thermogravimetric analysis confirmed high thermal stability, whereas X-ray diffraction analysis verified the characteristic amorphous structure of the produced EuM-NPs. LC–MS/MS analysis detected the oxidative degradation products pyrrole-2,3-dicarboxylic acid (PDCA) [ m/z 156.9] and pyrrole-2,3,5-tricarboxylic acid (PTCA) [ m/z 199.9], supporting the presence of eumelanin-derived structural components. In vivo investigations demonstrated significant anticancer activity against Ehrlich ascites carcinoma and solid tumors, reducing tumor volume by up to 78% and tumor weight by up to 83%. Furthermore, EuM-NPs exhibited potent anti-inflammatory activity, achieving 62.62% inhibition of carrageenan-induced paw edema. In vitro cyclooxygenase inhibition assays revealed selective inhibition of COX-2 (IC 50 5.61µg/mL , selectivity ratio > 8.91) compared with COX-1 (IC 50 > 50 µg/mL ) In silico drug-likeness, pharmacokinetics and molecular docking analyses of seven potential eumelanin 5,6-dihydroxyindole (DHI)-precursors highlighted 2,4′-DHI-dimer as the most promising, showing binding affinities of − 5.93 kcal/mol (COX-1) and − 5.27 kcal/mol (COX-2). These findings demonstrate that controlled bioreactor cultivation significantly reduced the production time required to obtain EuM-NPs by Streptomyces glaucescens NEAE-H while maintaining comparable production levels and highlighted their potential as multifunctional nanomaterials for anticancer therapy, inflammation management, and future nanomedicine applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69550-y.title: Hydroxyl groups tune the pH sensitivity of Imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine acrylonitrile derivatives as revealed by spectroscopy and DFT calculations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69550-y.abstract: Abstract We investigated the potential of imidazo[4,5- b ]pyridine acrylonitrile derivatives as pH sensors, focusing on their spectroscopic responses to varying pH conditions. By incorporating different numbers of hydroxyl groups and evaluating the role of the unsubstituted NH group on the heterocyclic core, we characterized their UV–Vis absorption properties in solvents of variable polarity and buffer solutions (pH 1–13). The results demonstrate significant solvatochromic behavior, with hydroxyl group substitution and NH proton availability driving bathochromic and hypsochromic shifts. UV–Vis pH titrations revealed enhanced sensitivity in compounds with multiple hydroxyl groups, particularly in acidic and basic conditions. Computational DFT analysis identified the pyridine nitrogen as the primary protonation site and confirmed the role of phenolic hydroxyl groups in increasing acidity. NMR analysis validated these findings, showing chemical shift changes consistent with pyridine nitrogen protonation. Importantly, the combined experimental-computational approach enabled deconvolution of overlapping protonation equilibria and assignment of individual spectral features to specific protonation states. These compounds show promise as versatile pH sensors for optical sensing, optoelectronic purposes, and organo-electronic materials due to their robust spectroscopic properties. Notably, compound 8 emerged as an encouraging candidate for monitoring transitions from neutral to higher pH values, owing to its significant red shift in UV–Vis spectra near neutral pH, making it particularly suitable for detecting subtle alkalinity changes in environmental and biomedical applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66790-w.title: A genome-guided phylogenetic framework predicts the phytochemical similarity and quality consistency of Lonicera japonica
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66790-w.abstract: Abstract Ensuring quality consistency in botanical drugs remains a global challenge. Through whole-genome analysis of 130 honeysuckle (Lonicera japonica Thunb. ) germplasms, we established a phylogenetic framework revealing eleven evolutionary lineages. Parallel quantification of 16 phytochemical components demonstrated 73.08% congruence between phytochemical profiles and genetic clustering, supporting our “Phylogenetic Proximity-Phytochemical Similarity (PPPS)” hypothesis, and multi-component analysis outperformed single-class metabolite comparisons in predicting quality relationships. RSD profiling shows that phytochemical variability increases with greater genetic divergence, but stabilizes when genetic variation approaches saturation, thereby supporting the PPPS principle. Independent validation using five newly collected germplasms further confirmed PPPS, with phylogenetically proximate accessions showing significantly higher phytochemical similarity than distant relatives. These findings suggest that genomic approaches could offer a promising strategy for enhancing quality assessment of botanicals and potentially help address key challenges in herbal medicine standardization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-43907-9.title: Coupled fractional-order, rotational, and hall current effects on deformation in a magneto-micropolar thermoviscoelastic half-space
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-43907-9.abstract: This study develops a fractional-order magneto-micropolar thermoviscoelastic model to examine the coupled influence of viscosity, rotation, and Hall current in a rotating half-space. The governing equations, formulated using the fractional-order heat conduction law, are solved through the normal mode analysis method. The results demonstrate that viscosity acts as a stabilizing factor by dissipating mechanical energy and reducing displacement and temperature amplitudes. The fractional-order parameter introduces memory-dependent and nonlocal behavior, amplifying deformation at lower orders, while the rotation parameter enhances oscillatory motion through Coriolis coupling and delays attenuation. The findings reveal a distinct coupling mechanism between fractional-order and rotational effects, which governs the propagation and dissipation of thermoelastic and micropolar fields. This framework provides new physical insight into wave behavior in rotating conductive materials and offers potential applications in the design of smart composites, magneto-viscoelastic structures, and high-speed aerospace components.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69069-2.title: An end-to-end patient-level coronary artery disease severity assessment based on altered cardiac-hemodynamic signal coupling characteristics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69069-2.abstract: There is a growing interest in developing interpretable and non-invasive approaches for coronary artery disease (CAD) screening with severity assessment. This work presents an end-to-end patient-level framework for CAD severity assessment using short-duration synchronously acquired Lead II electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals. The proposed framework integrates signal quality assessment, nonlinear cardiac-hemodynamic coupling analysis, and interpretable machine learning to distinguish severe CAD (sCAD), minor CAD (mCAD), and non-CAD (nCAD) patients. Novel morphological event-independent signal quality indices are introduced using bounded reconstructed phase space and modulation spectral representations of ECG and PPG signals, eliminating the need for accurate fiducial point detection. Nonlinear ECG-PPG coupling characteristics associated with CAD severity are then characterized using multifractal detrended moving average analysis, multifractal detrended moving average cross-correlation analysis, cross-recurrence quantification analysis, and cross-recurrence network measures. The framework was evaluated on an in-house dataset comprising 230 patients who underwent coronary angiography. Three ensemble classifiers, including extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), balanced random forest (BRF), and adaptive boosting (AdaBoost), were evaluated and compared. The AdaBoost classifier achieved the best average F1-score of 0.84 for three-class CAD severity assessment, with AUROC values of 0.89 and 0.95 for distinguishing sCAD and mCAD from nCAD patients, respectively. Furthermore, to improve model interpretability, counterfactual explanation-based analysis identified sensitive and stable features based on the magnitude of perturbation required to change CAD severity predictions. The proposed framework with competitive state-of-the-art performance demonstrates the potential of synchronously acquired short-duration Lead II ECG-PPG signals to assist cardiologists in automated CAD severity assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68310-2.title: Maternal serotonin transporter genotype influences offspring’s anxiety-like behavior through prenatal and early postnatal routes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68310-2.abstract: Maternal serotonin transporter (5-HTT) genotype has been linked to offspring’s risk for neuropsychiatric disorders, yet the contribution of prenatal versus early postnatal routes remains unresolved. We combined a 5-HTT −/− rat model with a fostering procedure to disentangle these effects. 5-HTT +/− offspring genotype was kept constant by crossing 5-HTT −/− or 5-HTT +/+ dams with males of opposite genotypes. Prenatally, compared with 5-HTT +/+ dams, 5-HTT −/− dams produced smaller embryos with impaired serotonergic maturation. Their placentas exhibited alterations in serotonergic-related signaling. Postnatally, 5-HTT −/− dams exhibited reduced licking and grooming. Adult offspring from 5-HTT −/− dams showed lower anxiety-like behavior alongside altered corticosterone recovery following stress and elevated infralimbic Gad67 expression relative to offspring from 5-HTT +/+ dams. To dissociate prenatal from postnatal influences, offspring were cross-fostered with genotype-mismatched dams. Under cross-fostering, offspring from 5-HTT −/− dams exhibited a higher serotonin/tryptophan ratio and reduced Bdnf isoform VI expression in the medial prefrontal cortex compared to offspring from 5-HTT +/+ dams. Independent of biological dam genotype, cross-fostering reduced body weight, increased anxiety-like behavior, and downregulated HPA-axis- and GABA/glutamatergic-related signaling. Here, we demonstrate that maternal 5-HTT genotype shapes offspring’s anxiety-like behavior through combined prenatal and early postnatal effects, highlighting the intertwined roles of maternal genetics and environment in neuropsychiatric disorders' pathophysiology.
authors: Petronella D. H. van den Burg
Petra H. H. van den Broek

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69187-x.title: 3′ untranslated region of ubiquitous dystrophin isoform Dp71 regulates its expression to impact suborganellar localization and mitochondrial morphology
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69187-x.abstract: Abstract Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a progressive skeletal muscle-wasting disease caused by abnormalities in DMD , which encodes the muscle protein dystrophin. The DMD 3′ untranslated region (3′UTR) is suspected to repress dystrophin translation through binding of microRNAs miR-31 and miR-146a-5p. Given that mitochondrial abnormalities are among the first pathological events in DMD, the role of the DMD 3′UTR in mitochondrial biogenesis remains an important open question. Here, we investigated how the DMD 3 ' UTR influences the effects of overexpression of its ubiquitous isoform, Dp71, on mitochondrial biogenesis. Expression constructs carrying the Dp71 coding sequence with the full-length 3 ' UTR or a 101-bp truncated 3 ' UTR sequence were introduced into cultured HeLa cells to assess the protein expression and subcellular localization of Dp71, and its effects on mitochondrial morphology. While the full-length and short 3 ' UTR constructs produced identical Dp71 polypeptides, the short 3 ' UTR construct strongly enhanced Dp71 expression, leading to fragmented mitochondrial morphology with increased levels of dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp1) and mitochondrial fission factor (Mff). By contrast, the full-length 3 ' UTR construct produced modest levels of Dp71, promoting hyperfused mitochondrial morphology with downregulation of Mff. Intriguingly, suborganellar fractionation revealed enhanced mitochondrial membrane anchoring of Dp71 translated from the short 3 ' UTR construct, but not the full-length 3 ' UTR construct. These findings implicate the DMD 3 ' UTR as a key regulator of mitochondrial dynamics through its influence on Dp71 protein expression, underscoring its potential as a target for modulating protein activity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68564-w.title: Land subsidence hazard mapping using a federated learning architecture with satellite and local environmental data
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68564-w.abstract: Land subsidence has become one of the most critical environmental and geomorphological hazards in recent years, threatening groundwater resources, urban infrastructure, and ecosystem stability. This study presents a novel Federated Learning (FL)-based framework for land subsidence hazard mapping in Poldokhtar County, Iran, without requiring direct access to centralized raw data. The proposed framework integrates Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR)-derived subsidence rate maps from Sentinel-1 time-series data (2015–2025) with 13 environmental conditioning factors across multiple spatial clients. Five machine learning and deep learning algorithms Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Deep Neural Network (DNN), and Logistic Regression (LR) were employed as local base models within the FL framework, using FedAvg and FedProx aggregation strategies. The results revealed generally weak to moderate correlations between subsidence and individual environmental factors, highlighting the complex and multi-factorial nature of the subsidence process. Client-based data distribution analysis confirmed a non-IID (Non-Independent and Identically Distributed) condition, with Client 1 representing severe subsidence areas (wider range of negative values) and Client 3 representing areas with weak or negligible subsidence (narrower range near zero). Among the global federated models, RF achieved the highest accuracy (R 2 = 0.963), followed closely by LSTM (R 2 = 0.956) , demonstrating their strong capability in capturing complex spatiotemporal patterns. In contrast, LR exhibited the poorest performance (R 2 = 0.375) with the highest error rates, confirming its limitation to linear relationships. Feature importance analysis identified Digital Elevation Model (DEM), groundwater level, and soil type as the most influential predictor variables associated with subsidence risk in the study area. The findings demonstrate that the proposed FL-based framework not only enhances prediction accuracy through collaborative learning across distributed clients but also preserves data privacy by avoiding raw data sharing. This approach offers a scalable and effective decision-support tool for sustainable groundwater management and land-use planning in subsidence-prone regions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-56013-7.title: SML-YOLO: a lightweight insulator defect detection algorithm for transmission lines under harsh weather conditions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-56013-7.abstract: Efficient defect detection of insulators in transmission lines is critical to ensuring the reliability and safety of power systems. However, adverse outdoor conditions such as rain, fog, and low illumination can reduce the contrast between targets and background, resulting in blurred defect details. Meanwhile, insulators often coexist with towers, conductors, and other elements within complex backgrounds, which can lead to inaccurate target segmentation and subsequently cause missed or false detections. This study introduces a lightweight insulator defect detection algorithm, SML-YOLO, designed for harsh weather scenarios. Built upon the YOLO11 framework, the algorithm achieves performance optimization through three core innovations. Specifically, StarNet-nano is proposed as the backbone network, thereby improving the perception of features without compromising the model's lightweight architecture to improve the detection of small-scale defects. In addition, a multi-branch modulated feature pyramid network (MMFPN) is developed to optimize feature fusion while adhering to lightweight objectives, and an LSCD detection head is employed to balance model compactness with high detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that SML-YOLO reduces model size by 21.1% and parameter count by 20.9%, while achieving a 2.4% improvement in detection accuracy and a 23.8% increase in detection speed. Moreover, it exhibits strong adaptability under adverse weather conditions. These findings confirm that the proposed algorithm combines lightweight design, high detection performance, and robust generalization capability. It not only provides an efficient solution for automated inspection of transmission lines, reducing manual inspection workload and minimizing maintenance downtime, but is also well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained UAV applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60804-3.title: Low-MESF fluorescent reference particles for flow cytometry analysis of extracellular vesicles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60804-3.abstract: Abstract Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold strong potential as non-invasive biomarkers for early detection of diseases. However, their clinically relevant quantitative flow cytometric (FCM) analysis remains limited by the lack of suitable calibration particles with low single-particle fluorescence values. Although fluorescent labeling of silica particles is well established, traditional approaches typically yield heterogeneous fluorophore distributions in the low MESF (Molecules of equivalent soluble fluorophore) range, which is required for single-EV fluorescence calibration. To this end, we introduce a labeling strategy that overcomes this limitation by using fluorescently tagged silica-binding peptides (R5-FITC) to produce submicron silica particles with homogeneous low-level fluorophore coverage. Silica particles of three different sizes were synthesized and labeled in a fast and straightforward manner. After comprehensive characterization, FCM investigations revealed that the resulting dim fluorescent silica particles (as low as 278 MESF with narrow distribution) are suitable for calibrating the fluorescence intensity of EVs isolated from red blood cells. Our findings show that fluorescent particles resembling EVs in both size and fluorescence can improve calibration accuracy and foster standardization in FCM-based EV characterization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68877-w.title: Remote Raman detection of seven groups of plastics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68877-w.abstract: At present, only two groups of plastic, polyethylene (PET) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE) among seven plastic groups are widely and easily recycled. However, the majority of plastic wastes are diverted to landfills due to insufficient identification. Therefore, there is a need for remote sensing techniques with rapid and non-contact identification for plastics without requiring physical handling to increase sorting efficiency in future industrial applications for recycling. This study demonstrates the detection of seven common plastic groups using a remote Raman system utilizing a 532 nm frequency doubled Nd:YAG pulsed laser for excitation. Remote detection of plastics is accomplished at 10 m distance with 1 s integration time. Clear Raman peaks over the fluorescence background were observed with good spectral resolution. In addition, color of the plastic samples did not affect the Raman detection suggesting Raman measurements are insensitive to coloring chemicals which are usually present in low concentration. This allowed dependable differentiation among the polymer groups based on their molecular vibrational signatures. The results in this study suggest that remote Raman spectroscopy is an ideal technique that can provide rapid detection with very high confidence for chemical specificity that is required for reliable identification and sorting of diverse plastic types.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69169-z.title: Microbiome alterations in mismatch-repair deficient metastatic colorectal cancer patients
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69169-z.abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Many efforts have been made to stratify CRC cases, from investigating the genomic characteristics of the tumor to – more recently – considering the gut microbiome. Differences in the composition of the gut microbiome occur along CRC stages and according to primary tumor location. The microbiome links with other tumor characteristics remain underinvestigated, including those related to microsatellite instability, that have been so far assessed only with respect to intratumoral bacterial presence and not to the whole gut or oral microbiome. Here we study associations between tumor microsatellite instability and the microbiome by collecting oral and gut microbiome samples from two clinical trials, ARETHUSA and AtezoTRIBE, enrolling metastatic CRC (mCRC) patients with microsatellite stable (MSS) tumors and with high microsatellite instability (MSI-H) tumors. We identified a significant reduction in microbial diversity in oral and gut microbiomes of CRC patients with MSI-H compared to patients with MSS (Wilcoxon rank-sum test P = 0.001 and 0.005, respectively). In addition, the MSI-H condition could be predicted by machine learning algorithms (AUC of 0.7 for both stool and oral microbiome) and the microbial signature for this condition comprises fewer microbial species compared to MSS with Ligilactobacillus salivarius and Rothia mucilaginosa detected as the strongest MSI-H associated intestinal and oral species, respectively. Our work provides evidence of human microbiome connections with tumor genetic stability, and poses the basis for larger validating investigations and mechanistic studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67022-x.title: Optimization of photovoltaic efficiency in arid regions via IoT-controlled jute fabric evaporative cooling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67022-x.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Photovoltaic (PV) modules in arid regions suffer efficiency losses up to $$25\%$$ due to overheating, while conventional cooling methods consume large amounts of water or energy. This study develops a sustainable, low-water passive evaporative cooling system using jute fabric with IoT-based deterministic control. Methodology: A $$30\textrm{Wp}$$ monocrystalline module was cooled by three jute layers with $$0^{\circ }/90^{\circ }$$ fiber orientation, wetted via a threshold-controlled pump $$(P_{\textrm{ref}} = 22\textrm{W}, T_{\textrm{ref}} = 55^{\circ }\textrm{C})$$ . Field tests were conducted in July 2025 (ambient up to $$45.4^{\circ }\textrm{C}$$ , irradiance $$848\textrm{W}/\textrm{m}^2$$ ). Results: Maximum temperature reduction of $$21.4^{\circ }\textrm{C}$$ (28.34%) and relative power gain of $$40.44\%$$ (absolute efficiency $$+1.5$$ percentage points, from $$15.3\%$$ to $$16.8\%$$ ). Water consumption $$0.14\textrm{L}/\textrm{h}/\textrm{m}^2$$ , recovery rate $$81.3\%$$ , evaporation loss $$0.026\textrm{L}/\textrm{h}/\textrm{m}^2$$ , payback $$< 3$$ years. Conclusions: The biodegradable jute-IoT system enables large-scale deployment in desert climates with minimal water footprint. $$\mathrm {CO_2}$$ emissions reduction is estimated at $$58\textrm{kg}/\textrm{m}^2/\textrm{year}$$ .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67920-0.title: Research on anti-dislocation technologies for tunnels crossing active faults considering fault heterogeneity
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67920-0.abstract: Active faults are widely distributed in China and severely restrict the construction and safe operation of transportation tunnels, as fault dislocation easily induces uneven deformation, stress concentrations and structural damage to tunnel linings. Most existing relevant studies oversimplify fault zones as homogeneous rock mass, which fails to reflect real geological conditions and reduces the accuracy of tunnel mechanical responses. Taking fault heterogeneity into consideration, this study established a refined numerical model to investigate the mechanical response of tunnels subjected to fault dislocation, as well as the mitigation effects of over-excavation and articulated designs. The main results show that the over-excavation design can effectively reduce the horizontal convergence of the lining, mitigate lining deformation, and decrease the peak internal forces of the lining; as the over-excavation thickness increases, the horizontal convergence of the lining gradually decreases, and the reduction in peak internal forces gradually increases. The articulated design can effectively reduce the peak internal forces of the lining; as the lining segment length decreases, the peak internal forces gradually decrease, although excessive shortening of the segment length may increase convergence deformation. The research provides a reference for the structural design and safety protection of tunnels crossing active faults.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68218-x.title: Repetitive exoskeleton use induces persistent coordination changes in wearers
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68218-x.abstract: Abstract Exoskeletons are redefining occupational ergonomics, offering a promising solution to mitigate musculoskeletal strain in repetitive tasks. However, their long-term effects on motor control remain poorly understood. This study investigates whether repeated short-duration exposure to an upper-limb exoskeleton induces persistent changes in motor performance. Over five consecutive days, 24 participants performed reaching tasks under one of three conditions: (1) low-magnitude gravitational support from a robotic exoskeleton, (2) exposure to a viscous force field in the same exoskeleton, or (3) no exoskeleton exposure. Spontaneous movements performed before daily exposure were analyzed in order to characterize the evolution in upper limb kinematics. While no significant changes in task duration or overall joint range of motion were observed, substantial alterations in patterns of shoulder-elbow coordination were seen to emerge. Participants exposed to gravitational support, outside of the exoskeleton, progressively decreased shoulder involvement while increasing elbow contribution, with temporal synchronization evolving over time. In contrast, those exposed to the viscous field exhibited initial disruptions in shoulder-elbow synchrony, which gradually subsided throughout the five-day protocol. These findings challenge the assumption that exoskeleton effects vanish upon removal, demonstrating instead that repeated exposure to small-magnitude force fields can induce lasting changes in motor coordination. Given the growing adoption of exoskeletons in industrial and healthcare settings, understanding these prolonged motor modifications is critical. If unaccounted for, such changes could inadvertently elevate musculoskeletal risks rather than mitigate them.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68718-w.title: Computationally unraveling genetic factors underlying morphological patterns of wheat’s root growth: a scientific data analysis approach
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68718-w.abstract: Abstract A collection of 53 wheat varieties’ root-growth trajectories was clustered into seven distinct morphological growth patterns. Across more than 30K DNA variants, we used Categorical Exploratory Data Analysis (CEDA) to examine all 21 pairwise contrasts between these patterns. Short single- and multi-locus genotype combinations were evaluated by entropy reduction and a finite-sample reliability check based on alternative and null ensembles of contingency tables. Bipartite networks between wheat varieties and retained genotype combinations were displayed as presence–absence heatmaps to reveal pair-specific block structures. As an out-of-pair negative control, the genotype combinations derived from each focal pair were examined, without feature reselection, in varieties belonging to the other five phenotype groups. These excluded groups did not reproduce the focal-pair block structure, supporting the pair specificity of the displayed information within the analyzed dataset. For methodological context, the same samples, markers, and phenotypes were also analyzed with mixed-model association, interaction-detection, and machine-learning methods. Among the four recurrent CEDA markers, marker-level support was strongest for RAC875_c60191_947, which had a FarmCPU PC1 Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted value of $$q=0.0275$$ and ranked ninth by random-forest importance in the same dataset. These comparisons characterized complementary, method-specific outputs. CEDA thereby characterized genotype-pattern information associated with MRL trajectories in this wheat panel. Across the 21 pairwise contrasts, recurring category-associated genotypes highlighted three putative positional or functional candidates at two loci.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69389-3.title: Electric-circuit reconstruction of urban bus passenger loads on service-frequency-weighted networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69389-3.abstract: Abstract Detailed origin–destination records provide direct information on public transport use, but their public release is often restricted because they contain sensitive mobility information. This raises a simple question: how much aggregate information is actually needed to reconstruct passenger loads on a bus network? Using bus origin–destination data from Hirosaki, Japan, we separate passenger movements into flows travelling outward from the core station and flows travelling toward it. Boarding–alighting imbalances at stops define source–sink fields, while empirical service frequencies define route-segment conductances. Solving the resulting conductance-weighted graph Poisson equation yields edge currents interpreted as reconstructed passenger loads. To clarify the domain of applicability of the model, we compared reconstructions using datasets that included and excluded circular and circular-like routes. With the full source–sink field, the baseline directional dataset retained 93.3% of the valid OD records and yielded $$R^2=0.901$$ for and $$R^2=0.818$$ for . After excluding circular and circular-like routes, the retained coverage decreased to 60.0%, while $$R^2$$ increased to 0.989 for and 0.963 for . Cross-period reconstruction between the first and second halves of June and December yielded $$R^2=0.970$$ –0.983 for and 0.938–0.965 for on the non-circular network. Even when only the core-station source–sink imbalance was provided, the model reproduced a substantial part of the spatial load distribution without post-hoc scaling, with $$R^2=0.907$$ for and 0.768 for . The framework was additionally applied to Goshogawara, where the CORE-only reconstruction yielded $$R^2=0.456$$ for and $$R^2=-0.016$$ for , reflecting the weaker dominance of the station core. These results identify predominantly radial, non-circular bus networks as the principal domain of the present electric-circuit formulation and show that CORE-only reconstruction is most effective when the selected station core is dominant.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68711-3.title: DFT and molecular docking investigation of rivastigmine and pyridostigmine derivatives as AChE inhibitors and their interaction with carbon nanocages
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68711-3.abstract: This study investigates rivastigmine and pyridostigmine derivatives as acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors and evaluates their delivery via carbon-based fullerenes (C 20 , C 32 , and C 60 ). AChE regulates cholinergic neurotransmission by catalyzing the rapid hydrolysis of acetylcholine; consequently, the inhibition of human AChE (hAChE) remains a cornerstone therapeutic strategy for the symptomatic management of Alzheimer’s disease. Utilizing Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations in both gas and aqueous phases, the structural stability and feasibility of these nanocages as drug delivery platforms were assessed. Among the candidates, the C 60 fullerene exhibited superior thermodynamic stability, establishing it as the most viable nanocarrier. The formation of stable drug-fullerene complexes in both environments confirms energetically favorable host-guest interactions. Frontier-orbital energy analysis revealed significant perturbations in the electronic properties of pyridostigmine derivatives upon interaction with the nanostructures, indicating enhanced chemical reactivity and delivery compatibility. Molecular docking simulations were subsequently employed to compare the binding affinities of rivastigmine and pyridostigmine within the hAChE active site, identifying optimal precursors for structural modification. The adsorption behavior of the novel derivatives, specifically R3 and P2, was then rigorously characterized. Analysis of adsorption energies, charge transfer, and HOMO-LUMO gap variations, complemented by Molecular Electrostatic Potential (MEP) and mapping Density of States (DOS), elucidated the electronic structures and reactive sites of these systems. The findings illustrate that while both derivatives exhibit inhibitory potential, C 60 provides a promising nanoplatform for delivery of the P2 derivative through non-covalent physical interactions. The work extends fullerene-based carrier design to a permanently cationic anticholinesterase and shows that cage curvature and guest charge state together determine whether adsorption proceeds by chemisorption or physisorption.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68584-6.title: Mechanical, volumetric, and stress-dependent cyclic behavior of expansive clay stabilized with pumice-based geopolymer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68584-6.abstract: This study investigates the use of a pumice-based geopolymer as a sustainable stabilizer for expansive clay, with emphasis on strength development, volumetric stability, and stress-dependent cyclic behavior. Although geopolymer binders have been widely explored, pumice-based systems for clay soils remain limited, particularly in terms of cyclic stiffness and stress-dependent behavior. An experimental program was designed to evaluate the effects of pumice content (10–30%), alkaline liquid ratio (0.20–0.30), and NaOH molarity (8–12 M). The results demonstrate that geopolymer stabilization significantly enhances soil performance, with unconfined compressive strength increasing by up to 1089% at 7 days and 820.6% at 28 days relative to the corresponding age-matched untreated controls, while swelling potential decreases from 43.75% to approximately 10%. The highest unconfined compressive strength was achieved at a moderate pumice content (~ 20%) and an intermediate alkaline liquid ratio (0.25), whereas the highest resilient modulus was obtained at 10% pumice. Increasing NaOH molarity further enhanced compressive strength. Resilient modulus results reveal stress-dependent behavior, characterized by increasing stiffness with confining pressure and a non-monotonic response to deviatoric stress. A stress–strength-based formulation is proposed, enabling consistent prediction of cyclic stiffness across different mixtures and loading conditions. Sustainability assessment indicates improved strength–carbon efficiency relative to cement-treated soils, highlighting the potential of pumice-based geopolymers as a sustainable solution for ground improvement.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60177-7.title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals distinct vascular-associated microglia signatures in cerebral small vessel disease
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60177-7.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major cause of cognitive impairment, characterized by neuroinflammation and microvascular dysfunction. A specialized subset of microglia, known as vascular-associated microglia (VAM), intimately interacts with the cerebral vasculature and plays a pivotal role in mediating neuroinflammation originating from the vasculature. However, the phenotypic changes of microglia in CSVD, particularly VAM subsets, and their crosstalk with microvascular cells remain largely unknown. Using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on isolated cerebral microvessels from the renal hypertension rat (RHR) model of CSVD, we identified an increased proportion of VAM that is distinct from perivascular macrophages. Critically, a novel Spp1 + VAM subset emerged in the RHR model, exhibiting enhanced phagocytic, adhesive, and anti-inflammatory profiles. CellChat analysis further highlighted intensified VAM-endothelial interactions. Morphological changes and low proliferation rate suggested that VAM expansion arises from the recruitment of parenchymal microglia rather than in situ proliferation. These findings position the Spp1 + VAM subset as a key modulator of CSVD neuroinflammation. Targeting VAM recruitment and activation represents a promising therapeutic strategy to mitigate microvascular dysfunction and cognitive decline in CSVD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69519-x.title: Prevalence and risk factors for oropharyngeal carriage of Neisseria meningitidis and circulating genogroups in eastern and southwestern Ethiopia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69519-x.abstract: Abstract Neisseria meningitidis is a leading cause of meningitis epidemics in the African meningitis belt. Where invasive meningococcal disease surveillance is limited, carriage studies can identify circulating sero/genogroups to inform vaccine policies. We aimed to estimate the prevalence, identify the circulating genogroups and risk factors for N. meningitidis carriage in Ethiopia. We conducted a random cross-sectional survey among residents of Health and Demographic Surveillance Systems in Kersa, eastern Ethiopia and Gilgelgibe, southwestern Ethiopia between February and May 2024. Posterior oropharyngeal swabs were collected and cultured for N. meningitidis . Genogroups and clonal complexes were determined using whole genome sequencing. Overall and age-stratified carriage prevalence were estimated, and risk factors identified by logistic regression. Of 2000 targeted individuals, 1966 provided analysable oropharyngeal samples. Bacteria were cultured from 574 participants, and 105 were confirmed as N. meningitidis. Overall carriage prevalence was 5.3% (95% CI: 4.4–6.4%), being 9.3% (95% CI: 7.6–11.3%) in Kersa and 1.7% (95% CI: 0.7–2.2%) in Gilgelgibe. Prevalence varied by age, being highest among 10-14-year-olds and lowest among 1–4-year-olds (c²=17.6, p = 0.014). The 105 cultures comprised 39 MenW (all Clonal Complex 11) 7 MenB, 5 MenE, 3 MenC, and 51 nongroupable. None were MenA. MenW: CC11 strains, linked to epidemics, predominated and MenA was not identified. Future prevention of meningococcal disease in Ethiopia may require a vaccine targeting multiple serogroups.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68757-3.title: Impact of velocity evolution on AE event location and fracture process interpretation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68757-3.abstract: The ability to reliably locate microseismic events is crucial for monitoring the fracture process in the subsurface. However, changes in rock properties during fracturing alter seismic velocity, impacting event localization and potentially misinterpreting damage evolution. We investigated the impact of seismic velocity changes on the reconstruction of acoustic emission (AE, i.e., lab-scale microseismicity) evolution during the deformation of sandstone samples under controlled laboratory conditions. We localized the AE events using a novel approach that integrates double difference (DD) with real-time velocity updates, accounting for rock damage. This approach significantly improves the reliability of the reconstructed spatio-temporal AE distribution, as validated against CT imaging of the main fracture. By quantifying how AE characteristics—distribution and event rate—evolve across stress stages from pre-failure to post-failure, we demonstrate their correlation with measurable velocity changes, underscoring the importance of incorporating dynamic velocity in AE localization. Neglecting velocity variations can cause systematic location bias, misrepresenting damage progression and crack coalescence into a major fracture—highlighting the need for dynamic velocity models. By integrating insights from rock mechanics and rock physics into seismological methods—specifically the DD approach— we establish a more reliable framework for tracking damage progression. This integrated approach enhances passive seismic monitoring and holds broad applications for subsurface reservoir management, including CO 2 geological storage and Enhanced Geothermal Systems, where reliable tracking of fracture evolution is critical.
