doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68175-5.title: Same‑track coupled experimental and numerical investigation on hard rock fragmentation mechanisms and damage evolution in HPWJ‑assisted TBM cutting
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68175-5.abstract: High-pressure waterjet (HPWJ) precutting prior to tunnel boring machine (TBM) disc cutters has emerged as a promising technique to improve hard rock fragmentation efficiency. However, the mechanical correlation between precut kerf geometry and rock damage evolution remains insufficiently understood. This study carries out full-scale, same-track coupled experiments, in which a 17-inch disc cutter penetrates granite specimens at a constant penetration depth of 6 mm under pure disc cutting conditions and along HPWJ-prefabricated kerfs with systematically varied depths of 2, 4, 6, and 8 mm. The experimental results demonstrate that HPWJ precutting reduces the mean normal force by up to 32% and the peak normal force by 22% compared with those under conventional pure disc cutting. In particular, the specific cutting energy is decreased by 34% under the maximum kerf depth condition. With increasing kerf depth, rock cutting chips exhibit a progressive morphological transition from powdery debris to lamellar fragments. Complementary finite element simulations are performed using the JH2 constitutive model, which is calibrated by uniaxial compression and Brazilian splitting tests with good agreement in stress‑strain curves between experimental and numerical results. The simulation results further reveal that same-track HPWJ precutting nonlinearly restrains the growth of the crushed dense core zone. Notably, the projected area of the dense core under a kerf depth of 8 mm accounts for only 11.3% of that in the non-kerf baseline case. The precut kerfs also redirect rock damage patterns, shifting dispersed microcracking to lateral macroscopic fracturing, which promotes crack coalescence during the subsequent disc rolling process. These mechanical findings establish a systematic design framework for HPWJ-disc cutter coupled cutterheads, providing quantitative references for waterjet nozzle parameter optimization, cutter spacing configuration, and zoned cutting track arrangement. This study further lays a solid theoretical basis for the engineering application of waterjet technology in TBM excavation in extremely hard rock formations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64629-y.title: Instruction-based learning difficulties in developmental dyslexia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64629-y.abstract: Individuals with developmental dyslexia often experience difficulties in skill acquisition, attributed to atypical cortico-striatal networks. But while extensive research has focused on the formation of familiar stimulus–response (S–R) associations in dyslexia, less attention has been given to the ability to form novel S–R associations, which occurs very rapidly with few practice trials following verbal instructions. Instruction-based learning refers to the unique human ability to rapidly acquire and implement new behaviors based on verbal guidance, a process that has been shown to promote the development of skill expertise. In this study, we examined how university students with and without dyslexia learn to implement verbally instructed familiar and novel S–R rules across number and letter domains. Our results show that individuals with dyslexia demonstrate a reduced ability to implement S–R rules compared to neurotypicals, especially for novel S–R associations. Most significantly, individuals with dyslexia did not show the expected performance improvement during the first practice trials of novel S–R rules seen in the neurotypical group. These findings indicate difficulties in the ability to rapidly learn verbally instructed novel S–R associations among individuals with dyslexia, which may have implications for the development of expertise in novel domains.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-59789-w.title: Triglyceride-glucose index associated with the risk of future renal function decline: a 13-year prospective cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-59789-w.abstract: We aimed to characterize the role of triglyceride–glucose index (TyG index), a surrogate marker of insulin resistance (IR), and renal function decline (RFD) in a large community-based prospective cohort study. A sum of 85,569 participants were included in the current study, all participants were categorized based on quartiles of the TyG index levels. The primary outcome of this study was future RFD, which was defined as a reduction of ≥ 25% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate from the baseline to below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Incidence rate was expressed as cases per 1,000 person-years. The association between the TyG index and the risk of RFD was investigated using Cox proportional hazards models. During a median follow-up period of 14.01 years (interquartile range: 13.63–14.21 years), a total of 3668 cases RFD were recorded. The incidence rate of incident RFD increased substantially with the quartiles of TyG index, presenting 2.529, 3.110, 3.431, and 4.050 per 1,000-person year in quartile 1 to quartile 4. Multivariate Cox regression analysis revealed that the hazard ratio of RFD risk was 1.656 (95% confidence interval: 1.479–1.854) in quartile 4 compared with the quartile 1. The findings of this study indicate that an elevated TyG index correlates with an increased risk of future RFD, suggesting that IR could play a pivotal role in the onset of RFD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69002-7.title: Multi agent retrieval validation and knowledge reasoning for enhanced retrieval augmented generation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69002-7.abstract: Knowledge-intensive Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, such as open-domain question answering, multi-hop reasoning, and fact verification, require systems capable of accurately retrieving, validating, and synthesizing information from large-scale knowledge sources. Although Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has improved the factual grounding of large language models, existing single-agent architectures suffer from incomplete retrieval, inadequate cross-source validation, and limited compositional reasoning. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MARCO (Multi-Agent Collaborative Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a novel framework that decomposes the RAG pipeline into four specialized cooperative agents: a Retriever Agent for hybrid dense-sparse evidence acquisition, a Reasoner Agent for dynamic query decomposition and multi-step inference, a Validator Agent for cross-source consistency assessment and confidence-based filtering, and a Synthesizer Agent for coherent evidence-grounded response generation. Agent interactions are coordinated through a structured Shared Memory Pool and a formal communication protocol. Experimental evaluation on Natural Questions, HotpotQA, and MuSiQue demonstrates that MARCO achieves improvements of 4.2–8.1% in Exact Match and 4.5–7.8% in F1 over strong single-agent RAG baselines, with ablation studies confirming the contribution of each agent module. MARCO establishes a scalable, modular paradigm for next-generation knowledge-intensive AI systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68540-4.title: Elucidation of inflammatory-fibrotic microenvironment in human urethral stricture disease
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68540-4.abstract: Abstract Urethral stricture disease (USD) is marked by inflammation with subsequent tissue fibrosis that disrupts urinary flow. Recent studies suggest lower urinary tract biome dysbiosis increases proinflammatory cytokines, impeding tissue repair as well as promoting fibrotic scarring of the urethra. Despite these insights, the comprehensive molecular mechanisms underlying the formation, progression, and recurrence of the USD remain unclear. We aim to identify molecular targets and designate pathways contributing to USD, thereby identifying potential targets for future therapeutic interventions. We performed a comprehensive multi-modal analysis in USD patient urine and scar tissues. Urinary cytokines were assayed, transcriptome profiling and pathway enrichment were performed, and network mapping identified fibrotic hubs. Biomechanical tissue stiffness was quantified by atomic force microscopy (AFM), and protein and histological analysis employed both immunostaining and Western blotting. IFN-β, IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-8.were significantly elevated in USD. Transcriptomic profiling revealed 745 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment in ECM organization, cytokine storm, TGF-β, integrin, IL-17A, WNT/β-catenin. ECM organization and cytokine storm are identified as central interactive hubs, dominated by collagen and fibrogenic regulators such as SMAD3 and TGF-β1. Tissue stiffness increased threefold in USD tissues compared to controls, highlighting ECM remodeling. Immunostaining demonstrated enhanced vimentin, elastin, COL1, and TGF-β expression, along with Western blot studies for observing the trend of elevated protein levels. The integrative approach evaluating pathway enrichment with transcriptome profiling reveals interconnections between mechanisms of inflammation, matrix remodeling, and mechanotransduction driving USD. The findings provide a mechanistic foundation for individualized models and therapeutic targets.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67511-z.title: Screening Luxembourg's older general population for probable REM sleep behaviour disorder with a nationwide online survey
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67511-z.abstract: Abstract REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder (RBD) is a hallmark of the prodromal phase of α-synucleinopathies. We aimed to describe the prevalence of probable RBD and to assess its associations with demographics, cognition, and location in a large sample of older adults in Luxembourg, as a first step toward identifying individuals with RBD symptoms for future prodromal-marker assessment. In 2021, residents of Luxembourg aged 55–75 were invited to complete an online survey including the RBD Screening Questionnaire (RBDSQ); with a threshold of ≥ 7 defining screen-positive probable RBD (sppRBD). Screen-positive participants underwent a telephone interview, and those confirmed were categorised as telephone-assessed probable RBD (pRBD). Bayesian spatial mapping assessed the geographical distribution of pRBD, and logistic regression identified determinants of sppRBD and pRBD. Among 15,915 participants (54% male; median age 62 [IQR 58–67]), 12.4% had sppRBD. The telephone interview confirmed only 34.8% of these as pRBD, yielding a projected prevalence of 4.3%. Self-reported cognitive impairment, male sex, and Portuguese as questionnaire language were associated with pRBD, which showed heterogeneous geographical distribution. Online questionnaires may yield false positives, potentially reflecting e-health literacy issues; therefore, a confirmation step is essential. This analysis identifies individuals with RBD symptoms warranting further prodromal-marker assessment, a candidate group for, rather than a validated instance of, an at-risk-for-α-synucleinopathy cohort.

doi:10.1038/s41598-025-30463-x.title: Preparation and characterization of a Syrian pumice-based ion exchanger for copper (II) ion adsorption
doi:10.1038/s41598-025-30463-x.abstract: Heavy metal contamination of water resources, particularly by copper Cu(II) originating from industrial effluents, poses a significant threat to ecosystems and human health due to its toxicity and non-biodegradability. While adsorption is a widely recognized remediation technique, its economic viability is often hampered by the high cost of conventional adsorbents like activated carbon and synthetic ion-exchange resins. This economic constraint has driven the search for sustainable, low-cost alternative materials derived from abundant natural resources. Naturally occurring pumice, a volcanic rock with inherent porosity, has emerged as a promising candidate due to its global availability and low cost. However, a critical review of the literature reveals that the raw pumice typically exhibits limited adsorption capacity , restricting its practical application. Furthermore, while some studies have explored chemical activation to enhance its performance, the potential of Syrian pumice deposits remains significantly underexplored . There is a distinct lack of comprehensive studies that systematically investigate (a) a highly effective yet cost-effective chemical modification route for this specific pumice type, (b) a detailed analysis of its adsorption mechanisms beyond simple isotherm fitting, and (c) a rigorous economic assessment comparing it to incumbent technologies. This study addresses these critical gaps by presenting a novel, cost-effective adsorbent synthesized from locally sourced Syrian pumice for the efficient removal of Cu(II) ions. Through a simple alkaline modification, we produced a sodium hydroxide-treated pumice (P Na ) ion exchanger. The research quantitatively demonstrates an 18-fold increase in specific surface area and characterizes the material’s exceptional adsorption performance across a wide range of operational parameters. We comprehensively analyze the kinetics, equilibrium isotherms, and thermodynamics to elucidate the hybrid adsorption mechanism. Crucially, this work demonstrates that the developed P Na material achieves performance comparable to conventional adsorbents while incurring production costs 70-90% lower, thereby establishing Syrian pumice as a sustainable and economically transformative alternative for wastewater treatment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68008-5.title: Comprehensive proximity proteomics expand the known interactome of the oncoprotein β-catenin
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68008-5.abstract: Abstract The oncoprotein β-catenin has critical roles in cell adhesion and cell signalling. β-catenin affects human physiology and pathology through numerous interaction partners, of which many have been discovered by standard affinity purification-based proteomics. However, the interaction landscape of β-catenin remains incompletely understood, highlighting a need for new experimental approaches for the exploration of β-catenin biology. Proximity proteomics, which facilitate the discovery of molecules vicinal to proteins-of-interest by mass spectrometry, have recently emerged as a powerful complementary tool for the study of protein–protein interactions, but have not been applied to β-catenin so far. We investigated the interactome of β-catenin in model cell lines by proximity proteomics using expression constructs with the biotin ligases BioID and TurboID. Mass spectrometry analyses following biotin labelling identified numerous candidate interactors of β-catenin, including many that had not been observed in earlier studies using standard proteomics. Enrichment analyses suggested that proximity proteomics capture proteins associated with the known biological functions of β-catenin, including cell adhesion, Wnt/β-catenin signalling, and transcription regulation. The molecular tools and data generated in this study provide new insights into β-catenin biology and highlight potential new regulators of β-catenin function that warrant further exploration.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69692-z.title: Experimental and numerical analyses of microwave induced damage and cutability evolution in basalt
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69692-z.abstract: As mining extends to greater depths, microwave-assisted rock breaking offers a promising solution to enhance excavation efficiency by weakening rock structures. However, the mechanisms underlying microwave-induced damage and its influence on rock cutability remain unclear. This study presents a multiscale investigation of basalt irradiated at 3 kW and 6 kW for 30–120 s. Cutability was evaluated through uniaxial and single-cycle loading–unloading compression tests based on strain energy evolution. Acoustic emission monitoring, SEM imaging, and finite element simulations were integrated to reveal damage evolution. Results show that microwave exposure enhances basalt cutability, though the improvement rate declines with time. The incremental damage decreases with prolonged irradiation, indicating diminishing weakening efficiency at higher energy inputs. Simulations reveal spatial heterogeneity in temperature fields, with high-energy zones showing faster degradation. Early-stage damage is driven by thermal stress, mineral transitions, and selective heating, while late-stage damage slows due to microstructural changes and reduced thermal gradients. These findings clarify the thermal–mechanical coupling in microwave–rock interaction and provide theoretical guidance for optimizing power input and irradiation time. The study contributes to energy-efficient, sustainable excavation strategies, supporting the broader goals of green mining.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67524-8.title: Geochemical characterization and source identification of tarmat deposits along the coast of Qatar (Arabian/Persian Gulf)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67524-8.abstract: Tarmat deposits along the Qatar coastline were investigated using trace-metal concentrations and diagnostic ratios (Co/Ni, V/Ni, Co/V, V/Cu, and Fe/Ni) to assess weathering effects, spatial variability, and potential sources. The samples were collected between September and November 2019 from 13 different locations along the west, north, and northeastern coasts of the Qatar Peninsula. Trace-metal concentrations were on average significantly higher in island samples (V 1284 µg/g; Ni 492 µg/g; Co 6.48 µg/g) compared with mainland sites (V 305 µg/g; Ni 108 µg/g; Co 1.66 µg/g; p < 0.05). Multivariate statistical analyses (PCA and HCA) revealed systematic patterns linking metal composition with spatial distribution and weathering categories. Regression analysis of metal-to-aluminum (Me/Al) ratios against marine suspended particulate matter and aeolian dust showed strong correlations (R² = 0.83–0.89; p < 0.01), suggesting potential combined atmospheric and marine influences on trace metal signatures. The composition of the tarmats is influenced by environmental factors as well as their degradation and weathering. Diagnostic metal ratios were consistent with crude oil signatures reported from the northern and northwestern Arabian/Persian Gulf, indicating predominantly regional inputs rather than long-range transport. Overall, the study demonstrates that trace-metal ratios, supported by multivariate analysis, provide a useful framework for tarmat characterization and environmental assessment and support other scientific investigations on tarmats in the Gulf region.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67746-w.title: Explosive synchronization and high-dimensional connectivity in fibromyalgia: A brain network mechanism of chronic pain
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67746-w.abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a chronic pain disorder characterized by widespread pain and hypersensitivity, yet its brain network mechanisms remain poorly understood. We investigated the network conditions of explosive synchronization (ES)—a phenomenon of abrupt state transition to hypersensitivity—and its structural underpinnings using topological data analysis (TDA). In this pilot study, we recorded electroencephalography (EEG) in 19 FM patients and 15 healthy controls. We computed ES indices and quantified high-dimensional topological structures using integrated Betti numbers (IBs). FM patients exhibited a significantly stronger ES index at rest ( p < 0.05). In the FM group, ES indexes significantly correlated with clinical outcomes, including symptom severity (e.g., FIQR total score; ρ = 0.602, p < 0.05). The abundance of high-dimensional topological cycles significantly correlated with pain severity (e.g., FIQR score; ρ = 0.590, p < 0.05) and ES strength during evoked pain. Moreover, pain-induced topological changes (|ΔIB|) were positively associated with clinical severity. Our findings suggest that chronic pain in FM is linked to specific alterations in brain network structure, highlighting a strong interplay between high-dimensional topology and ES-prone states. We propose that these features create a topological landscape hindering flexible network integration, thereby facilitating abrupt hypersensitive transitions. These network features may serve as mechanistic indicators for pain severity and represent novel targets for neuromodulation therapies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68573-9.title: Bilayer construction with desired thermoelectric behavior as a promising candidate for anode materials of magnesium-ion batteries: DFT and AIMD Study on GBS2 hetero-bilayer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68573-9.abstract: The development of high-performance anode materials is essential for advancing next-generation magnesium-ion batteries (MIBs), which offer superior safety, sustainability, and energy density compared to conventional lithium-ion systems. In this study, first-principles calculations were employed to systematically evaluate the novel graphdiyne /borophene hetero-bilayer (GBS 2 ) as a potential anode material for MIBs. Its structural, thermal, and electronic properties were thoroughly investigated. The GBS 2 hetero-bilayer exhibits a work function of 4.82 eV—significantly lower than graphdiyne (5.29 eV) and comparable to borophene (4.81 eV)—indicating favorable electronic characteristics for anode applications. The hexagonal hole in the interlayer region was identified as the most stable Mg adsorption site, with an optimal adsorption energy of approximately −2.0 eV that supports reversible Mg storage. Electronic structure analyses (Bader charge, PDOS, and charge density difference) confirm predominantly ionic bonding, accompanied by a substantial charge transfer of 1.62 electrons per Mg atom. Furthermore, the material demonstrates excellent kinetic performance, with low Mg diffusion barriers of 0.42 eV on the surface and 0.50 eV between layers. Although the GBS 2 hetero-bilayer can accommodate up to 37 Mg ions, its anodic performance is optimized at a loading of 21 Mg atoms. Beyond this critical concentration, Mg clustering occurs, which impairs the electrochemical performance and distinguishes true anode behavior from simple ion storage. At the optimal loading, the anode delivers a high theoretical specific capacity of 2366.42 mAhg⁻ 1 and a suitable average open-circuit voltage of 0.55 V. Thermoelectric calculations further reveal excellent electrical conductivity upon Mg intercalation, along with efficient heat dissipation, which is highly beneficial for battery thermal management. Overall, these findings establish the GBS 2 hetero-bilayer as a highly promising anode material for fast-charging, high-performance MIBs. This work also provides a strategic framework for hetero-bilayer engineering, highlighting significant advantages over monolayer structures.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69031-2.title: Resonance-enhanced evanescent optical lattices: comparison of guided-mode, surface-wave, and plasmonic platforms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69031-2.abstract: Abstract Resonant diffraction by periodic photonic structures can generate strongly enhanced evanescent optical lattices near material interfaces. Here we compare this mechanism in three representative platforms: leaky guided modes, Bloch surface waves, and surface plasmon polaritons. Using Fourier modal method simulations and a semi-analytical nearest-neighbour model, we analyze linear, square, and hexagonal grating geometries under normally incident monochromatic illumination. The results show that the three platforms occupy distinct regimes of resonant near-field design. In the studied structures, leaky guided modes provide the largest resonant field enhancement and can yield very high absolute near-surface intensities, even when only a modest fraction of the stored intensity extends into the superstrate. Bloch-surface-wave and plasmonic lattices place their field maxima directly at the upper interface and can exhibit longer evanescent tails, but with platform-specific constraints such as multilayer coupling or metallic loss. We identify the trade-off between resonant enhancement, surface accessibility, penetration depth, visibility, and polarization response, providing design guidelines for structured near fields in nanophotonic sensing, microscopy, and surface-based light–matter interaction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69433-2.title: General self-efficacy in the cross-sectional indirect association of emotion suppression with athlete burnout among individual sport athletes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69433-2.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to examine a cross-sectional indirect association involving general self-efficacy in the relationship between emotion suppression and athlete burnout. A total of 336 athletes aged 18–34 years (M = 22.07, SD = 4.27) participated in the study, including 184 women (54.8%) and 152 men (45.2%). The athletes’ training experience ranged from 10 to 444 months (M = 90.54, SD = 61.85). Participants represented fifteen individual sports disciplines. The results indicated a significant association between emotion suppression and athlete burnout through general self-efficacy, with negative associations observed both between emotion suppression and self-efficacy, and between self-efficacy and burnout. Detailed analyses indicated significant associations through general self-efficacy linking anger suppression and depressive emotion suppression with the specific dimensions of athlete burnout. In each case, anger suppression and depressive emotion suppression were negatively related to self-efficacy, while self-efficacy was negatively associated with burnout dimensions. However, no significant association was found for anxiety suppression – the indirect association between anxiety suppression and burnout through general self-efficacy was not statistically significant. These findings indicate that the suppression of anger and depressive affect is cross-sectionally associated with lower general self-efficacy, and that lower general self-efficacy, which is concurrently associated with higher levels of athlete burnout, whereas anxiety suppression is not significantly associated with a comparable pattern of indirect associations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65755-3.title: Remote sensing and noise processing methods for rock mass vibration information in complex tunnel environment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65755-3.abstract: Abstract During tunnel construction, the surface of surrounding rock is often unstable, making traditional contact sensors (e.g., accelerometers) difficult to install reliably and highly susceptible to detachment or damage. Although scanning laser Doppler vibrometers (SLDVs) offer advantages such as non-contact measurement, high precision, and full-field monitoring, their application for non-contact vibration monitoring in tunnels is subject to numerous constraints. These constraints stem from the specific complexities of tunnel construction environments and the inherent limitations of laser vibrometry technology. To address the challenges of acquiring valid vibration information using laser vibrometers, this chapter presents breakthroughs in both hardware and algorithms. In terms of hardware, an adaptive vibration-damping and noise-reducing carrier platform was developed. This platform mitigates noise interference through physical passive isolation and active control technologies. Furthermore, based on the characteristics of tunnel environments, the scanning laser vibrometry monitoring equipment was optimized for complex tunnel conditions. In terms of algorithms, a hybrid noise reduction method integrating AVMD and K-SVD was proposed. By leveraging complementary enhancement, multi-dimensional analysis, and robustness improvement, this method achieves noise separation and signal enhancement, thereby significantly improving the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and accuracy of micro-vibration measurements. The effectiveness of this noise reduction approach was verified through the analysis of simulated signals and measured data, successfully enabling the extraction of valid vibration information from rock masses.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65951-1.title: Community Agricultural Model Platform (CAMP) for multi-model ensemble simulations of crop growth and development
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65951-1.abstract: Uncertainty in crop growth simulations arises from model structure, input data, parameter values, and calibration procedures. Multi-model ensembles can reduce the influence of individual model-structure errors and extreme single-model predictions, but their application is often hindered by the need to prepare different computing environments for each crop model. Here we propose the framework where containers are used to provide a uniform interface for a diverse set of crop models in order to support the multi-model ensemble within a computing platform. This platform was referred to as Community Agricultural Model Platform (CAMP). CAMP was designed to launch individual crop models through an application programming interface (API) implemented within the container. The platform consisted of subsystems for management, storage and administration of containers. In particular, a web based interface for data exchange was provided within each container where an object-oriented programming approach was used to facilitate the implementation of the API for individual crop models. As a case study, the CAMP was used to estimate the heading dates of rice using five models that had different computing environments such as operating system and programming languages. The ensemble estimate showed errors comparable to the better-performing individual models and reduced the influence of large errors produced by individual members although calibration-related uncertainty remained. Our results demonstrated that CAMP would facilitate the application of multi-model ensemble simulations using crop models developed and shared by crop model developers. This would benefit a wide range of stakeholders allowing for the ensemble simulations to make reasonable decisions on crop management practices as well as climate change impact assessment, which merits further studies to extend functionality of CAMP for Model as a Service (MaaS).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65172-6.title: Mine water inflow (inrush) source identification model based on the RFE-GA-LightGBM model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65172-6.abstract: Accurate identification of mine water inflow sources is essential for water hazard prevention and emergency decision-making in underground coal mining. However, source discrimination is often difficult because different aquifers may exhibit similar hydrochemical characteristics, and mining-induced fractures can enhance hydraulic connection and water–rock interaction. In this study, the 5110 working face of Yushupo Coal Mine was selected as the engineering case, and a mine water source identification model based on recursive feature elimination and genetic algorithm-optimized Light Gradient Boosting Machine, namely RFE-GA-LightGBM, was developed. Piper trilinear diagrams were first used to analyze the hydrochemical types and ion composition characteristics of different aquifers. Field observations showed that the maximum measured height of the water-conducting fractured zone reached 178 m, indicating that roof sandstone aquifers may be hydraulically connected during mining. Recursive feature elimination was then employed to screen key hydrochemical indicators, and Ca 2+ , Na + , SO₄² – , HCO₃ – , and Cl – were selected as input variables for model training. The GA-LightGBM model was compared with default LightGBM, PSO-LightGBM, and Bayesian-LightGBM models to verify the effectiveness of feature selection and hyperparameter optimization. The results show that Cl⁻ is an auxiliary indicator for identifying Lower Shihezi Formation water, whereas SO₄² – is sensitive to coal-measure sandstone aquifers affected by pyrite oxidation and water–rock interaction. Compared with the other models, GA-LightGBM achieved the best overall classification performance, with an accuracy of 96.1%, precision of 89.2%, recall of 89.5%, F1 score of 90.2%, specificity of 98.42%, and AUC of 0.96. The prediction results indicate that the water inflow at the 5110 working face is mainly related to the Taiyuan Formation sandstone aquifer and the K2 aquifer of the Shanxi Formation. This study provides a data-driven and hydrogeochemically interpretable method for rapid mine water source identification under complex mining conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68707-z.title: Leveraging temporal patterns in forecasting
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68707-z.abstract: Recurring temporal patterns emerge naturally from underlying processes and interactions in a variety of disciplines, ranging from epidemiology and ecology to social sciences and physics. These patterns hold considerable promise for enhancing time series forecasting. This study introduces a method that identifies these repeating patterns and incorporates them as dynamic covariates in traditional time series forecasting models. Using subsequence time series clustering, we obtain cluster solutions for various window lengths and k combinations, and only retain the ones with the lowest standard deviation at \(t+1\) , indicative of the level of signal entailed in the clusters. Our methodology is evaluated with three widely used forecasting models: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest (RF), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Each model is implemented in its standard form and subsequently augmented with dynamic covariates. The empirical evaluation draws on a data set comprising 1000 time series spanning a broad array of domains. The results show that the introduction of dynamic covariates significantly improves the prediction accuracy. Through combining static and dynamic variants in a compound model, our algorithm effectively filters out conditions under which time series clusters pick up meaningful signal and discards noise.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69739-1.title: Klebsiella variicola MSK86 as a novel agent for SDS bioremediation and phytochemical enhancement in chili plants
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69739-1.abstract: Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) is an anionic surfactant and one of the major constituents in cleaning agents. It is one of the main contributors to chemical pollution in water bodies. The present study mainly focuses on SDS bioremediation from domestic graywater. In this study, the SDS-basal medium treated with Klebsiella variicola MSK86 showed the presence of 1-dodecanol, a product of SDS degradation pathway detected using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. The isolate was positive for phosphorus and potassium solubilization. The bacterial isolate was applied to laundry wash water, and its ability to remediate SDS was studied. Later, the treated water enriched with K. variicola MSK86 was used to irrigate chili plants. After 45 days of growth, harvested plants were analyzed for phytochemicals such as phenol and flavonoid content. The results showed that K. variicola -treated plants had a fourfold increase in phenol content and a 2.3-fold increase in flavonoid content, suggesting that the bacterial isolate helps plants cope with stressed conditions. The focus of the investigation was to identify a bioremediation agent for SDS with many potentialities that can be used for sustainable environmental concerns. K. variicola MSK86 may be a good candidate for SDS bioremediation and plant growth enhancement.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69402-9.title: Context-dependent walkability: built-environment associations and nonlinear contributions to pedestrian space quality–walking behavior mismatch in Xi’an, China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69402-9.abstract: In the context of urban regeneration, substantial investments in pedestrian space quality (PSQ) do not always translate into corresponding gains in walking behavior (WB). Existing studies often assume a linear PSQ–WB relationship, which cannot capture nonlinear associations and contribution patterns observed in practice. This study uses Xi’an’s core urban area as a case study and integrates multi-source urban data, including mobile phone signaling data and street-view imagery, with statistical and machine-learning methods to quantify and map the spatial patterns of PSQ–WB mismatch. Ordered logistic regression and XGBoost-SHAP models are employed to examine built-environment factors associated with the mismatch and further reveal their nonlinear contribution patterns and empirical transition points. The results show that: (1) 84.72% of traffic analysis zones in Xi’an’s core urban area exhibit a mismatch between PSQ and WB; (2) floor area ratio, population density, road network density, and public transport stop density are positively associated with the relative position of WB to PSQ, whereas building density and distance to the city center are negatively associated with it; (3) a higher position of WB relative to PSQ is more likely to occur when floor area ratio exceeds 1.0, population density exceeds 10,000 persons/km 2 , road network density exceeds 6 km/km 2 , and public transport stop density ranges from 9 to 17 stops/km 2 . These findings provide new evidence for context-dependent walkability and offer policy implications for shifting urban pedestrian regeneration from undifferentiated investment toward targeted interventions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62618-9.title: Enhancing Arabica and Robusta coffee prices forecasting through machine learning approaches

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69661-6.title: Exogenous putrescine and calcium nitrate alleviate water deficit stress in sesamum indicum L. by modulating antioxidant defense and nutrient homeostasis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69661-6.abstract: Water deficit is a major constraint for sesame ( Sesamum indicum L.) production in arid and semi-arid regions. This study evaluated the effects of foliar application of calcium nitrate )Ca(NO₃)₂; 0, 5, and 10 mM( and putrescine (Put; 0 and 0.5 mM) on the physiological and biochemical responses of sesame under three irrigation regimes (100%, 75%, and 50% of crop water requirement) during the 2018–2019 growing seasons. The experiment was conducted under field conditions using a split-plot factorial design with three replications. Severe water deficit (50% irrigation) significantly reduced chlorophyll content by 38.6%, relative water content by 27.2%, and membrane stability index by 28.6% compared with full irrigation ( P ≤ 0.01). Foliar application of 10 mM Ca(NO₃)₂ increased total chlorophyll by 19.3% and relative water content by 17.1% ( P ≤ 0.05), whereas 0.5 mM Put improved membrane stability by 30.8% under severe stress ( P ≤ 0.01). Both treatments reduced electrolyte leakage by 18–23% and increased leaf calcium content by up to 60.6%, soluble carbohydrates by 45.6%, proline by 34.3%, catalase activity by 32.8%, and peroxidase activity by 27.4%. Significant interaction effects were detected for chlorophyll and calcium content ( P ≤ 0.01). This study provides field-based evidence that the combined foliar application of Ca(NO₃)₂ and Put can mitigate drought-induced injury in sesame through coordinated improvements in water status, membrane stability, and antioxidant defense. These findings suggest that this treatment combination may serve as a practical complementary agronomic strategy for improving sesame performance under water-limited conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69772-0.title: A multi-objective secure multicast routing architecture using multi-scale dilated LSTM and hybrid coati–dolphin optimization in MANET environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69772-0.abstract: In this research work, an innovative MD-LSTM (Malicious Detection Long Short-Term Memory) framework has been proposed for the accurate detection of malicious nodes and a Hybrid Coati-Dolphin Swarm Optimization (HCDSO) algorithm for secure multicast routing in MANETs. The research aims to address major MANET challenges, including dynamic topology changes, routing vulnerabilities, and malicious attacks that affect network security and communication reliability. The MD-LSTM model uses a dilation-aware recurrent memory mechanism and multi-scale convolutional feature extraction to capture long-range temporal dependencies and complex attack patterns from network traffic data, thus improving the accuracy of malicious activity detection. The HCDSO algorithm combines the global exploration capability of the Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA) with the local exploitation capability of the Dolphin Swarm Optimization (DSO) to determine optimal routing paths that maximise throughput and PDR while minimising delay, hop count, and energy consumption. The experiments were conducted on three standard datasets, namely CICIDS-2017, NSL-KDD, and KDD Cup 99, and compared against conventional deep learning models (NN, DNN, SVM, and LSTM) as well as the latest state-of-the-art models. MD-LSTM achieved maximum accuracies of 97.802%, 96.905%, and 97.807% across the three datasets, respectively, representing performance improvements of 10.12–18.12% over conventional classifiers. The HCDSO routing framework increased throughput by 8.14%, 9.13%, 10.78% and 14.28% compared with DSO, COA, POA and BCO, respectively. The findings indicate that the proposed integrated framework can significantly improve malicious-node detection accuracy, routing efficiency, network reliability, and security, providing a strong foundation for future MANET applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68986-6.title: Prevalence, patterns, and factors associated with antibiotic self-medication among university students in Erbil, Iraq: a cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68986-6.abstract: Inappropriate antibiotic use is a major driver of the emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, patterns, and factors associated with antibiotic self-medication among university students in Erbil, Iraq, as the student population serves as a sentinel group for monitoring antibiotic-use behaviors. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Erbil, Iraq, from November 27, 2025, to March 3, 2026. Data were collected from a convenience sample of 354 university students using a researcher-developed self-administered questionnaire. The prevalence of antibiotic self-medication over the last three months was 26.6% (95% CI 22.0-31.2). The main illnesses leading to self-medication were upper respiratory tract infection (63.8%) and fever (16%). The reasons for self-medication rather than visiting a health facility included considering the disease not serious (28.7%) and seeking quick relief (26.6%). Self-medication with antibiotics was significantly higher ( P = 0.010) among students living in student hostels (40.4% (95% CI 27.6–53.1)) than among those living with family (23.9% (95% CI 19.1–28.8)). It was also significantly higher ( P = 0.018) among those enrolled in health-related disciplines (31.6% (95% CI 25.0-38.2)) than among those enrolled in non-health-related disciplines (20.5% (95% CI 14.3–26.7)). Living in a student hostel was significantly independently associated with antibiotic self-medication (aOR = 3.67, 95% CI: 1.40–9.64, P = 0.008). Antibiotic self-medication was relatively common among university students in Erbil, particularly among hostel residents and students in health-related disciplines. Inappropriate practices, including antibiotic use for minor illnesses, use without medical consultation, and premature treatment discontinuation, were frequently reported. Based on these findings, universities need targeted antimicrobial stewardship interventions through educational programs for students in health-related disciplines and hostel residents, emphasizing appropriate antibiotic use and the importance of completing treatment. Health authorities should also strengthen enforcement of existing regulations against dispensing antibiotics without a prescription and emphasize the role of community pharmacies in promoting responsible antibiotic use. It is recommended to regularly monitor antibiotic self-medication among university students to assess the effectiveness of these measures.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69349-x.title: China’s information technology-based video anomaly detection for water treatment plants
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69349-x.abstract: The safety and security in water treatment plants (WTPs) is critically important, since they face various potential risks. Conducting real-time anomaly detection in WTPs is of great significance for risk prevention, and emergency response. This work proposes an China’s information technology-based intelligent video anomaly detection approach for WTPs. This approach employs a unidirectional information transmission framework, and conducts real-time detection through 21 alarm algorithms. The algorithms are classified into 6 types: production safety regulations, smoke and fire, environmental safety, abnormal personnel behaviors, operations of production equipments, and illegal intrusion. Multiple mechanisms are employed to increase the accuracy. Meanwhile, an interactive platform is developed to virtually view, automatically analyze, and permanently store alarm information. The whole system has been put into use in a real WTP in Beijing, experiments are conducted to substantiate the feasibility of the proposed method. After 1 year, 1572 alarms were generated successfully. Among these alarms, 11 emergencies have been detected, including 9 fall downs and 2 smokes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69216-9.title: Localization of the infraorbital foramen in cleft lip and palate patients: a retrospective study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69216-9.abstract: Accurate localization of the infraorbital foramen (IOF) is essential in patients with unilateral cleft lip and palate (CLP) to facilitate safe local anesthesia and maxillofacial surgical procedures. This study evaluated IOF morphometry using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and compared the cleft side, non-cleft side, and healthy controls. This retrospective CBCT study included 14 patients with unilateral CLP and 14 age- and sex-matched controls. Bilateral measurements were obtained from the unilateral CLP group, generating three comparison groups: control ( n = 14), non-cleft side (NCS; n = 14), and cleft side (CS; n = 14). Distances between the IOF and predefined anatomical landmarks were measured using standardized CBCT images. Group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA or the Kruskal–Wallis test, followed by Tamhane’s T2 post-hoc analysis where appropriate. Age and sex distributions were comparable among the groups ( p > 0.05). Significant differences were observed for the IOF–IOM distance ( p < 0.001) and the IOF–Midline distance ( p = 0.005). The control group demonstrated greater IOF–IOM values than both the NCS and CS groups. For the IOF–midline distance, a significant difference was detected only between the control and NCS groups. No significant differences were identified for IOF–LNW, IOF–FH, IOF–PP, or IOF-Soft tissue thickness measurements (all p > 0.05). Unilateral CLP is associated with alterations in selected IOF morphometric parameters, particularly the distance to the infraorbital margin and the midsagittal plane. These findings may contribute to more accurate preoperative assessment and safer anesthesia and surgical planning in patients with unilateral CLP.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68848-1.title: Family role overload and nomophobia: a cross-sectional analysis of indirect associations via perceived stress and depressive symptoms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68848-1.abstract: Building on the Transactional Model of Stress and Coping and the I-PACE framework, this cross-sectional study used a serial multiple mediation approach to examine whether perceived stress and depressive symptoms sequentially mediated the relationship between perceived family role overload and nomophobia, while controlling for age and gender. The sample included 671 community-recruited Romanian adults aged 18 to 49 ( M = 24.44, SD = 7.11). Results suggested that perceived family role overload was associated with nomophobia both directly and indirectly. The strongest indirect association was through depressive symptoms alone, followed by a smaller but significant serial indirect association through perceived stress and depressive symptoms; this serial pathway accounted for only a small share of the total indirect association and should not be interpreted as the primary mechanism. Perceived stress alone was not significantly associated with nomophobia when depressive symptoms were included in the model, a pattern consistent with depressive symptoms being more closely associated with nomophobia than perceived stress in this cross-sectional design. The results nonetheless suggest that family stressors and emotional well-being may be relevant considerations in interventions addressing nomophobia in clinical and counseling settings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69088-z.title: A laser capture microdissection-based method for high-sensitivity transcriptomics from archived FFPE tissue slides with single-cell resolution using LCM-FFPEseq
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69088-z.abstract: Abstract Understanding gene expression within its spatial context is essential for unravelling biological processes. Laser Capture Microdissection (LCM) has emerged as a transformative technology, enabling targeted isolation of individual cells or regions from tissue sections while preserving spatial context. However, its application to formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues has been limited by RNA degradation, leaving the vast repository of clinical FFPE samples underutilized. To address this, we introduce LCM-FFPEseq, a novel method combining LCM with the advanced Smart-seq3xpress protocol and FFPE-specific adaptations for spatial transcriptomics of FFPE sections. Unlike traditional protocols requiring thousands of cells to generate high-quality libraries, LCM-FFPEseq achieves high sensitivity, reproducibility, and transcript coverage. With as few as 30 FFPE-embedded K562 cells and Sertoli cells, we detected over 14,000 protein-coding genes per sample, with no substantial gains when a higher number of cells were isolated. Even individual LCM-isolated cells yielded an average of 7,353 or 6,490 protein-coding genes per K562 or Sertoli single cell, respectively. To demonstrate its clinical utility, we applied LCM-FFPEseq to archived testicular FFPE samples from transgender females receiving gender-affirming hormone therapy. Transcriptomic profiling of isolated seminiferous tubules revealed tubular hyalinization to be associated with greater upregulation of extracellular matrix remodelling and inflammatory pathways, alongside stronger downregulation of spermatogenesis-associated pathways. These findings suggest that testicular fibrosis and/or tubular hyalinization may contribute to germ cell loss following inappropriate hormonal exposure. By enabling high-resolution transcriptomics in archived FFPE samples, LCM-FFPEseq unlocks new possibilities for investigating rare cell types, spatial heterogeneity, and therapy-induced tissue remodelling in vast FFPE repositories.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68688-z.title: A high-resolution chronology and terrestrial ecosystem record of Early Pliocene Warmth onset in Europe from Camp dels Ninots, NE Iberia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68688-z.abstract: Abstract The Early Pliocene Warmth (EPW) was one of the most recent intervals of sustained global temperatures above present, but its expression in European terrestrial environments remains poorly constrained. Here we establish a continental chronological and paleoenvironmental framework for the Camp dels Ninots maar-lake succession (NE Spain) using integrated ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar geochronology, magnetostratigraphy, and multiproxy analyses. Incremental-heating ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar dating of welded spatter deposits yields an eruption age of 4.70 ± 0.07 Ma, anchoring the onset of subsequent lacustrine sedimentation. Correlation of the polarity record with the Geomagnetic Polarity Time Scale, combined with sedimentation-rate modelling, dates the fossil-bearing interval to ~ 4.42 Ma and constrains the terrestrial onset of EPW conditions at ~ 4.45 Ma. Palynological assemblages indicate increased arboreal pollen and reduced aridity indicators, while mineralogical data support enhanced effective precipitation. Vertebrate faunas, including ectotherms and large mammals associated with closed habitats, further indicate ecosystem restructuring under warm-humid conditions. The preservation and chronological control of Camp dels Ninots provide a rare terrestrial archive for assessing continental paleoenvironmental responses during the EPW in Europe.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67640-5.title: Dynamic gating and attention masking for multimodal conditional diffusion image translation in autonomous driving scenarios
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67640-5.abstract: Virtual-to-real image translation is important for autonomous driving scenario generation, but existing conditional diffusion models still struggle to maintain semantic contour and spatial depth consistency when multimodal conditions exhibit varying reliability. In this study, we propose an adaptive multimodal conditional diffusion framework that dynamically regulates multimodal feature reliability through dynamic gating and attention masking.Semantic segmentation maps and depth maps are used as dual conditions. The dynamic gating module adaptively rebalances multimodal features by estimating spatial semantic importance and channel-level modal contribution, while the attention masking module suppresses interference from non-critical regions and enhances key traffic elements such as vehicles, road boundaries, and traffic signs. The optimized conditional features are injected into the U-Net denoising network to guide noise prediction with aligned semantic and depth constraints at the pixel level. Experiments on CARLA-to-Cityscapes translation show that the proposed method achieves an FID of 42.80 and an LPIPS-diversity value of 0.412. Downstream evaluations further obtain an mIoU of 82.2% and a Depth MAE of 0.12 m, indicating improved semantic structure preservation and spatial depth consistency.These results indicate that adaptive multimodal conditioning improves image realism, diversity, and semantic-depth consistency in autonomous driving image translation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61888-7.title: Region-specific forest structure pathways reveal climate effects on old-growth tropical forest biomass
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61888-7.abstract: Abstract Old-growth tropical forests store vast amounts of carbon in their aboveground biomass (AGB), yet the relative roles of abiotic factors such as climate, soil, and topography in governing its spatial distribution remain poorly understood. In particular, the degree to which climate acts on AGB through forest structure is still poorly quantified at the pantropical scale. Using a pantropical dataset of more than 2,000 old-growth forest plots and a structure-explicit framework, we assess how climate influences AGB through its effects on four structural attributes: basal area, mean diameter, stem density, and basal area-weighted wood density. We find that climate shapes AGB primarily through its effects on forest structure. However, structural attributes respond to climate in opposite directions, so climate’s net effect on AGB largely cancels out, and no clear climate-AGB relationship emerges across tropical regions. Moreover, only wood density responds consistently, decreasing with annual precipitation and increasing with precipitation seasonality, whereas all other attributes respond to climate differently from one region to another. This geographical variation further obscures any global climatic signal on AGB and points to the role of biogeographic history in shaping forest structure. Our findings highlight the central role of the climate-structure nexus in explaining AGB variation, and call for structure-explicit models to improve carbon stock predictions and inform climate adaptation strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68466-x.title: Neuromagnetic representation of vowel prosody in the auditory cortex
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68466-x.abstract: Abstract A key feature of vowels in spoken language is that their fundamental frequency ( f 0 ), which underlies perceived pitch, can change dynamically over time. However, it remains elusive how such prosodic glides shape the neural response in the auditory cortex. The current magnetoencephalography (MEG) experiment was designed to study the transient and sustained neuromagnetic correlates of prosodic contour information in vowels, with a particular focus on the P2 component. Twenty-four normal-hearing participants passively listened to vowel sequences in which both vowel type and prosodic contour were either unchanged or varied between successive vowels. At the level of single vowels, the results showed that falling contours elicit larger and earlier P2 responses than rising and flat prosodic contours. At the level of vowel triplets, the P2 was larger in response to stimulus sequences in which prosodic contour was varied across stimuli. The data indicate that the P2 might be a neural correlate of the early processing of prosodic contour information; moreover, they suggest that the P2 might be particularly sensitive to pitch glides, possibly due to longer time constants that are encompassed within the P2.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66819-0.title: A new dynamic operability index based on on-specification production for continuous pharmaceutical manufacturing under uncertainty
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66819-0.abstract: Operability analyses provide a general framework for assessing the process ability to satisfy its performance metrics under uncertain or disturbance conditions. The process operability is often quantified by the so-called operability index. However, most existing operability indexes assume steady-state operation, and thus, are suitable for high-volume processes running for extended periods such as those in the oil and gas industries. On the other hand, continuous manufacturing of fine chemicals such as pharmaceuticals are typically performed campaign-wise, which means the operation time is limited to a few weeks. Consequently, the process is mostly in transient, and steady state, if any, will occur for a short period only. This renders current steady-state operability indexes inapplicable for operability studies of such processes. A new operability index tailored for campaign continuous manufacturing is introduced in this paper, which unlike existing indexes, accounts for both transient and steady-state phases of the operation in a single formulation. Motivated by stringent product quality requirements in pharmaceutical industry, the index quantifies the process ability to maintain the desired amount of on-specification production over a range of process uncertainties. This is done by a special dynamic optimization problem that finds optimal process trajectories maximizing on-specification production for each uncertainty realization. The operability index is then defined as the ratio of the uncertainty realizations for which the maximum on-specification production is no less than the desired value to the entire uncertainty set. The new index is demonstrated by two examples including a campaign continuous aspirin crystallization process. The usefulness of the proposed index in screening different design alternatives and enhancing operability is also highlighted.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69357-x.title: Distinct social and psychological risk patterns define latent classes associated with smoking susceptibility in never-smoking adolescents and young adults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69357-x.abstract: Smoking-related cognitions are relevant to understanding tobacco prevention needs during adolescence and young adulthood. This study aimed to identify latent classes of adolescents and young adults who had never tried cigarettes based on social and psychological factors associated with smoking susceptibility and to examine their association with the Expanded Susceptibility to Smoking Index (ESSI). A cross-sectional study was conducted with 597 participants aged 12–22 years recruited from educational institutions in Extremadura, Spain, who reported never having tried cigarettes. Indicators of social exposure to tobacco (family, peers, classmates, and tobacco offers) and psychological factors (impulsivity, positive and negative affect, and emotion regulation) were used in the latent class analysis. Multinomial logistic regression was used to examine the associations between latent class membership and ESSI levels, adjusting for age, sex, and socioeconomic status. Three latent classes were identified. The lowest-risk class had low probabilities across indicators and included the largest proportion of nonsusceptible participants. Class 2 was defined by high social exposure to tobacco, and Class 3 by intermediate social exposure combined with high impulsivity and elevated negative affect. Both were associated with high susceptibility to smoking, to a similar degree (adjusted OR 5.00, 95% CI 2.84–8.79 and 6.01, 95% CI 2.79–12.90, respectively). Thus, among adolescents and young adults who have never tried cigarettes, distinct psychosocial profiles were associated with different levels of smoking susceptibility, which may support the development of more targeted prevention strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69488-1.title: Recovery of pectin and hemicellulose from hibiscus sabdariffa and their application in biofilm production
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69488-1.abstract: The increasing demand for environmentally sustainable packaging materials has intensified research on biodegradable films derived from plant-based polysaccharides. In this study, pectin and hemicellulose were extracted from Hibiscus sabdariffa var. sabdariffa calyces and used to develop biodegradable composite films. Film formulations were optimized using response surface methodology based on a central composite design to evaluate the effects of the pectin–hemicellulose ratio and glycerol concentration on water solubility, tensile strength, and elongation at break of the films. The optimal formulation, containing a pectin-to-hemicellulose ratio of 73.50% and 24.31% glycerol, yielded films with a tensile strength of 15.77 MPa, elongation at break of 15.58%, and water solubility of 66.33%, demonstrating a favorable balance between mechanical strength and flexibility. Hemicellulose incorporation enhanced film stability compared with pure pectin films. Moreover, the films exhibited substantial biodegradability, losing over 56% of their mass after 12 days of soil burial. These findings highlight pectin–hemicellulose films from Hibiscus sabdariffa as a promising sustainable alternative to petroleum-based packaging for food applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69079-0.title: Comparative effects of silibinin and deferoxamine on skeletal muscle injury and regeneration in a rat model of compartment syndrome
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69079-0.abstract: Compartment syndrome (CS) causes ischaemia–reperfusion-related skeletal muscle injury, and adjunct pharmacological strategies may reduce secondary tissue damage. This study compared silibinin and deferoxamine in a rat model of CS. Thirty-six male Sprague–Dawley rats were randomised into six groups ( n = 6). CS was induced by applying 140 mmHg external cuff pressure to the right hind limb for 3 h, followed by reperfusion. Animals received vehicle, silibinin (200 mg/kg/day by oral gavage), or deferoxamine (100 mg/kg/day intraperitoneally) until Day 4 or Day 14. CS + vehicle rats received oral distilled water and intraperitoneal 0.9% NaCl without active drug; active treatment groups received route-matched vehicle through the alternative route. Functional performance was assessed using the inclined plane test, and gastrocnemius muscles were examined using hematoxylin-eosin, Masson’s trichrome, Pax7, and Myogenin staining. At Day 14, both treatment groups showed higher inclined plane performance and lower myofiber necrosis and collagen-associated remodeling scores than the CS + vehicle group. Pax7 and Myogenin showed distinct patterns of expression between the Day 4 and Day 14 cohorts. Overall, silibinin and deferoxamine were associated with lower histopathological injury and higher functional performance in the Day 14 groups than in the corresponding Day 4 groups in this experimental CS model, while Pax7 and Myogenin findings indicated differences in myogenic marker expression between the Day 4 and Day 14 cohorts rather than definitive regenerative kinetics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68704-2.title: Open-field and closed-field aberrometry to measure ocular refraction in a prospective semi-randomized crossover study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68704-2.abstract: To assess the agreement and repeatability of closed-field and open-field pyramidal wavefront aberrometers in measuring non-cycloplegic spherocylindrical refraction, compared to subjective refraction and open-field autorefractometry. Fifty healthy adults (27 non-presbyopic, 23 presbyopes) were tested using four methods: closed-field aberrometer (CFA), open-field aberrometer (OFA), open-field autorefractor (OFAUTO), and subjective refraction. Measurements were performed monocularly and binocularly. Significant differences in the M component of the power vector were primarily observed when comparing OFA and subjective refraction, and OFAUTO and subjective refraction, across both age groups and in both eyes, and CFA comparing subjective refraction limited to presbyopic participants. In non-presbyopic participants, CFA showed more negative M values than OFA, consistent with a possible accommodative response or instrument myopia under closed-field non-cycloplegic conditions. No clinically relevant differences were found between monocular and binocular measurements when using the OFA and OFAUTO devices, regardless of age group. All reliability coefficients for the various procedures were relatively high in the Presbyopic group for both eyes. In the Non-presbyopic group, the reliability of M measurements showed a notable decline in the case of CFA in both eyes. OFA demonstrated high reliability comparable to OFAUTO, but a non-negligible clinical difference compared to subjective procedure. The outcomes of CFA in non-presbyopic participants highlights the challenge of accommodation control in non-cycloplegic conditions for closed-field systems. The effect of pupil size warrants further investigation to enhance understanding of objective refraction accuracy compared to the subjective procedure.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68949-x.title: Abundance of cord and maternal serum proteins and IgG transfer ratio in a Chinese population: a cross-sectional observational study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68949-x.abstract: There are inter-population differences in the maternal-to-fetal transfer ratio of immunoglobulin G (IgG), and there is currently a lack of research on the Chinese population. In this cross-sectional observational study, the serum concentrations of total protein, albumin, and total IgG in 71 paired samples, and IgG1–4 in 50 paired maternal and cord blood samples, were measured in Chinese mothers who delivered live births at ≥ 37 gestational weeks. The results show cord and maternal serum albumin concentrations were 36.98 ± 3.16 g/L and 36.53 ± 2.33 g/L, respectively ( t = -0.98, P > 0.05). The cord serum total IgG concentration was 9.00 (8.20–9.90) g/L, and the total protein concentration was 55.63 ± 5.30 g/L, whereas the maternal serum total IgG concentration was 10.80 (9.40–11.80) g/L, and the total protein concentration was 65.14 ± 4.57 g/L ( z = -5.38, P < 0.0001; t = 11.45, P < 0.0001). The maternal-to-fetal transfer ratio of total IgG was 0.82 (0.76–0.93), and the hierarchy of the maternal-to-fetal transfer ratios of IgG1–4 was as follows: IgG1 (1.28 ± 0.38) > IgG4 (1.06 ± 0.41) > IgG3 (0.86 ± 0.34) ≥ IgG2 (0.75 ± 0.28). Cord and maternal serum showed similar albumin but lower total protein; IgG1–4 transfer hierarchy matched prior studies, while ratios were lower than in most populations. These findings may help to understand the immune protection mechanisms in newborns among the Chinese population.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69403-8.title: Single-session estimation of cardiorespiratory fitness, lower-limb strength, and core strength using a wearable hip-joint exoskeleton
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69403-8.abstract: Laboratory criterion tests for cardiorespiratory fitness and muscular strength are valid but require specialised equipment and trained personnel, limiting scalability in real-world settings. Wearable hip exoskeletons already deployed for exercise and rehabilitation can standardise short bouts while capturing kinetic and physiological signals, enabling compact “smart tests” for multi-domain fitness estimation without additional laboratory infrastructure. In healthy adults ( \(n = 42\) ), a single-session knee-up protocol with a hip-joint exoskeleton yielded heart-rate–derived and kinetic features to estimate (i) cardiorespiratory endurance (estimated VO \(_{2}\) max), (ii) lower-limb strength, and (iii) core strength. We prioritised simple multivariable linear regression and used polynomial+LASSO only as a comparator. Targets were validated by (i) benchmarking treadmill-estimated VO 2 max against directly measured VO 2 max in a feasibility subset ( \(n = 30\) ) and (ii) correlating isometric abdominal crunch with plank hold time. Agreement was examined via Bland–Altman analysis. We also introduced absolute percentile-weighted and relative Pareto-based composite scores. Linear models explained 62–88% of the variance across the three fitness targets within the development sample (VO 2 max \(R^2\) up to \({\sim }0.88\) ), with in-sample Bland–Altman analyses showing negligible mean biases (VO 2 max: 0.00 ml \(\cdot\) kg -1 \(\cdot\) min -1 ; lower-limb: 0.00 Load/BW; core: 0.00 Load/BW). Polynomial+LASSO did not provide consistent improvements over linear regression. Target-level checks supported convergent validity (treadmill-estimated VO 2 max vs. directly measured VO 2 max: \(r = 0.92\) –0.94) and core capacity (crunch vs. plank: \(r \approx 0.80\) , \(\rho \approx 0.78\) ). Pairwise correlations among the three targets were strong ( \(r = 0.78\) –0.82). Bootstrap resampling ( \(B = 1000\) ) and Gaussian noise perturbation provided supplementary evidence regarding model stability within the development sample. The absolute composite summarised standing within sex–age peers, while the Pareto-based ranking highlighted balanced profiles. These proof-of-concept findings show that a brief, exoskeleton-guided single-session protocol can provide promising, internally consistent estimates of multi-domain fitness using simple linear regression, supporting interpretable, low-overhead deployment as a structured monitoring tool within existing exoskeleton-assisted sessions pending independent external validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67833-y.title: Correction: Ciguatoxin reduces regenerative capacity of axotomized peripheral neurons and delays functional recovery in pre-exposed mice after peripheral nerve injury
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67833-y.abstract: In the Original Article, specifically in Figure 4a part of the image in the “solvent control (SC)” group was erroneously used to represent the “SC + TTX” group. The authors acknowledge the errors and have to the best of their ability reconstructed the original figure using the materials still available. Specifically, the SC + TTX has been replaced to correct the error of overlapping in the SC panel. The CTL panel has been replaced with a verifiable source image from the same experimental condition, as the original source image could not be recovered. The 25 pg/ml P-CTX-1 + TTX panel have been replaced with a verifiable source image from the same experimental condition, as the original source image could not be recovered. The errors made do not affect the major conclusions or the quantification of neurite outgrowth in the first place presented in our manuscript. The corrected Figure 4a is shown below: Fig. 4 Full size image Blockade of excess sodium ion influx abolishes the growth inhibitory effects of P-CTX-1 on DRG neurons in vitro . ( a ) Representative photomicrographs of DRG neurons immunolabelled with antibodies against anti-β -tubulin III. DRG neurons treated with 0.3 μM TTX were able to extend their neurites to lengths comparable to the solvent controls (SC, 0.13% methanol) in the presence of 25 pg/ml P-CTX-1. TTX-treated DRG neurons exhibited significantly longer neurites in the presence of 100 pg/ml P-CTX-1 than those treated with 100 pg/ml P-CTX-1 alone. Scale bar: 500 μm. ( b ) Blockade of sodium influx with TTX significantly enhanced neurite extension in DRG neurons treated with 25 and 100 pg/ml P-CTX-1. ( c ) Neither P-CTX-1 nor TTX affected the survival of DRG neurons at any of the tested concentrations. The values represented the mean ± SEM values of triplicates; * P < 0.05, one-way ANOVA, followed by Bonferroni’s post hoc test. All treatment conditions, except for CTL (medium only), contained 50 μM ouabain (O) and 5 μM veratridine (V). There was no significant difference in neurite outgrowth between DRG neurons cultured with or without O/V. CTL, control; OV, 50 μM ouabain and 5 μM veratridine; TTX, 0.3 μM tetrodotoxin; n.s., not significant.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65603-4.title: Targeting hormone treatment for the brain in menopause
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65603-4.abstract: Abstract Estrogens are neuroprotective, and menopause may contribute to neurodegeneration. Estriol preferentially binds estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) in brain to induce neuroprotection. Previously, oral estriol improved cognitive processing speed and reduced cerebral cortex atrophy at treatment month twelve in women with multiple sclerosis (MS). Here, treatment with a blisterpack designed for healthy menopausal women which contains estriol and progesterone (Pearlpak) was assessed for its effect on cognitive domain-specific symptoms in a case series of twenty menopausal women (mean age 53.5 years). At treatment month twelve, there were significant improvements in self-reported brain fog, concentration, working memory, processing speed, verbal memory, and problem solving. A preclinical model explored mechanisms. Midlife female mice (age 12-13 months), previously ovariectomized either at 2 months or at 11 months of age, exhibited cognitive deficits on Morris Water Maze, with glial activation and synaptic loss on dorsal hippocampal pathology. Astrocytes had increased levels of Enolase 1 (ENO1), a key protein in glucose utilization. Increased ENO1 correlated with worse cognitive performance. Deletion of ERβ in astrocytes in gonadally intact midlife females recapitulated deleterious effects of ovariectomy. Conversely, treatment of midlife female mice with estriol from age 11 months to age 12 months reduced ENO1 expression in hippocampal astrocytes, reduced glial activation and synaptic loss, and improved cognitive performance. This preliminary study suggests that Pearlpak treatment for cognitive symptoms of menopause warrants further investigation given the safe use of these hormones in Europe and Asia for decades to reduce other menopausal symptoms.
