doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69754-2.title: Comparative study of hybrid quantum-classical models for cold-start drug–target affinity prediction: a partial pilot analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69754-2.abstract: Cold-start drug–target affinity (DTA) prediction requires evaluation on genuinely unseen chemical and protein entities. We considered QVGAT-DPI (Quantum Variational Graph Attention Network for Drug–Protein Interaction) as a residual hybrid model combining full molecular graphs, permutation-invariant Breaking of Retro-synthetically Interesting Chemical Substructures (BRICS) fragment queries, ESM-2 and ChemBERTa representations, fingerprints, cross-attention, and two simulated six-qubit residual modules. QVGAT-DPI was compared with specification-based implementation of Q-BAFNet, the closest structured hybrid architecture, under identical local fold manifests. Because of the limitation of the computational resource, the planned ten paired folds were completed only for DAVIS S2 (unseen drugs) and S4 (unseen drugs and targets). For S2, paired differences were + 0.060 CI (bootstrap 95% interval − 0.000 to 0.123; exact p = 0.0996) and − 0.094 RMSE (− 0.145 to − 0.046; p = 0.0098). For S4, differences were + 0.087 CI (0.032–0.143; p = 0.0195) and − 0.135 RMSE (− 0.294 to − 0.005; p = 0.1191). After Holm adjustment, only S2 RMSE remained below 0.05, and no protocol supported both endpoints. The prespecified aggregate S2–S4 conclusion was unevaluable because S3 was incomplete. These results support further controlled evaluation, not system-wide superiority or quantum advantage.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67686-5.title: Data-driven prediction of information diffusion in online social networks using sparse dynamic mode decomposition
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67686-5.abstract: Predicting how information spreads in online social networks requires models that can handle both evolving network structures and dynamic user interactions. Existing popular approaches, either based on variants of epidemic models or learning from raw data, either oversimplify the network dynamics or demand high computational resources, and often result in limited interpretability. This paper proposes a data-driven prediction of information diffusion in dynamic online social networks, based on Sparse Dynamic Mode Decomposition (Sparse DMD). This model learns from structural and diffusion dynamics captured from temporal network snapshots by extracting dominant spatio-temporal modes that capture both local and global patterns of information spread. Experimental results from five real-world datasets (Higgs, Facebook Forum, Digg, Email-EU, Wiki-Talk) show that our approach consistently outperforms classical machine learning baselines on isolated prediction tasks (Level 1) by 15-30%. Compared to complex deep learning architectures on the joint co-evolution forecasting problem (Level 2), Sparse DMD achieves accuracy within 1.3%, while cutting computational costs by a factor of 7 to 30. The modal decomposition provides interpretable insights into dominant diffusion pathways and temporal trends. These results establish Sparse DMD as an efficient, interpretable, and scalable framework for understanding and forecasting information diffusion in dynamic social systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67185-7.title: Artificial vegetation restoration enhances soil organic carbon in abandoned mines through chemical property-driven modulation of bacterial communities
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67185-7.abstract: Abstract Restoration of artificial vegetation in mining areas can improve soil health and quality. A healthy soil ecosystem has suitable characteristics and diverse microbes, which can be assessed for balance and stability. This study investigated how cultivating alfalfa, Pennisetum giganteum , Chrysanthemum indicum , Chrysanthemum zawadskii , and Amorpha fruticosa affects mine soil rehabilitation. We analyzed soil chemical properties, bacterial diversity, and composition. Compared with the unplanted control, plant cultivation significantly improved multiple soil chemical properties; alfalfa notably increased soil pH, total carbon (TC), total nitrogen (TN), and total potassium (TK). Proteobacteria, Acidobacteriota , Bacteroidota , and Actinobacteriota dominated at the phylum level, with Haliangium and Sphingomonas as key genera. Alfalfa raised Bacteroidota levels, and all plants elevated Sphingomonas beyond CK. Soil bacterial communities differed significantly between control and cultivated soils. Proteobacteria correlated positively with soil potassium but negatively with phosphorus, nitrogen, and pH. Sphingomonas was positively associated with carbon and nitrogen, and negatively with phosphorus, pH, and potassium. Bacterial relationships varied: cooperative with MBB (bulk soil after cultivation of Chrysanthemum zawadskii Herbich ) and competitive with JB (bulk soil after cultivation of Pennisetum giganteum ). Soil pH and total nitrogen (TN) emerged as the primary chemical drivers that positively influenced soil organic carbon (SOC). Furthermore, bacterial community characteristics played crucial modulatory roles within this process: higher bacterial diversity significantly amplified the positive effects on SOC sequestration, whereas greater richness (indicative of shifts in community composition) was unexpectedly associated with a negative effect. These results collectively support our core hypothesis that vegetation restoration reshapes soil chemical properties, which in turn regulates bacterial community structure to influence carbon dynamics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67384-2.title: Spermidine mitigates acute lung injury through activation of the Keap1-Nrf2-ARE pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67384-2.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical pulmonary disorder precipitated by infection or trauma, characterized by heightened inflammation and oxidative stress. The nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) is a pivotal transcription factor that regulates these processes and may act as a significant modulator in ALI. Spermidine, a naturally occurring polyamine with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, is postulated to mitigate ALI by activating Nrf2. This study aims to evaluate the potential of spermidine in attenuating lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms involved. An ALI mouse model was generated via intraperitoneal administration of LPS, with spermidine provided as an intervention. Additional experimental groups were treated with either an Nrf2 activator (4-OI) or an inhibitor (ML385). Real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and Western blot analyses were employed to quantify the expression levels of Keap1, Nrf2, inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-18, IL-1β), and NF-κB in lung tissues and macrophages. To further explore the molecular mechanisms, inhibitors of PI3K and MAPK pathways were utilized. Spermidine increased Nrf2 expression and nuclear translocation in LPS-stimulated macrophages and lung tissues. In vivo, spermidine improved respiratory function, alleviated histopathological lung injury, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and attenuated inflammatory responses. Pharmacological modulation of Nrf2 altered these protective effects, supporting the involvement of Nrf2 signaling. Spermidine also altered PI3K and ERK/MAPK signaling, while inhibition of these pathways produced distinct changes in Nrf2, Keap1, and HO-1 expression. Spermidine alleviates LPS-induced ALI and enhances Nrf2 activation while modulating Keap1-Nrf2-ARE signaling. PI3K and ERK/MAPK signaling may participate in spermidine-mediated regulation of Nrf2, although their precise hierarchical relationship remains to be clarified.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68624-1.title: A reduction law for cohesive crack model in large-scale quasi-brittle fracture simulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68624-1.abstract: Large-scale fracture simulation in rock engineering is vital in understanding the real geotechnical and geological behaviors. It has become increasingly important, as an enabling technique, when some emerging fields of underground exploration are being developed, e.g., geothermal energy, underground energy storage, faults and earthquakes, etc. Finite and Discrete Element Method (FDEM) based on cohesive crack model is a widely used simulation method for rock fracture propagation due to meaningful physical parameters and reliable algorithm implementation. However, in large-scale simulations, the cohesive element size often increases with the model scale and may become larger than the characteristic length of the fracture process zone (FPZ). It will cause significant errors or inaccuracy as the damage zone is insufficiently represented. This paper establishes a reduction law for fracture simulations when using relatively large element size. The size effect law of FPZ length is proposed by D-B model and Bazant size effect law. A series of three-point bending tests with Digital Image Correlation (DIC) technique and FDEM models are carried out to obtain FPZ length results and verify the size effect law. Worked examples on large-scale three-point bending tests and compressed air energy storage in rock caverns are demonstrated. This method can provide a useful and practical tool for low-cost simulation of large-scale rock fracture and failure, while not sacrificing the accuracy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68691-4.title: Localization of blue-on cells in the lateral geniculate nucleus of the macaque monkey using a tungsten marking technique
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68691-4.abstract: Abstract The lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) relays color information from the retina to the cerebral cortex via anatomically segregated pathways. Although accumulating evidence suggests that neurons conveying signals from short-wavelength-sensitive (S) cones reside in the koniocellular (K) layers, it has been technically challenging to definitively correlate physiological recordings with their histological locations in macaques, which are routine trichromatic primate. In this study, we investigated the distribution of blue-responsive (S+) cells in the macaque LGN using extracellular single-unit recordings combined with a novel, high-resolution, and minimally invasive technique for marking recording sites. Recorded units were classified using cone-isolating stimuli to identify their cone inputs, and the recording site of S+ units were marked for histological verification. We found that the majority of cells responsive to S+ stimulation were located either within the K-layers or at the border between the K- and parvocellular (P) layers. We also found one instance located in the pregeniculate nucleus. Our results provide strong evidence that both New World and Old World monkeys share this color-segregating pathway in the LGN.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68194-2.title: A data-informed framework for individualized exercise prescription in post-stroke gait rehabilitation: a pilot randomized feasibility study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68194-2.abstract: Most individuals with stroke experience walking difficulties, while standardized exercise training may not address heterogeneous gait deviations. This pilot feasibility study evaluated a data-informed intervention for individuals with post-stroke lower-extremity impairments. Participants were randomized to a data-informed intervention or control group. In the experimental group, exercises were prescribed using a predefined biomechanical mapping framework based on lower-limb gait deviations identified through inertial measurement units and Statistical Parametric Mapping. The control group received standardized task-oriented training. Both groups completed five exercises per session across 12 supervised sessions over 6 weeks. Feasibility and acceptance were evaluated based on attendance, safety, and participant feedback. Gait, clinical, and sEMG outcomes were analyzed exploratorily using aligned rank transform models, supplemented by selected sensitivity and participant-level analyses. Seventeen individuals registered, sixteen met the eligibility criteria, and all enrolled participants completed the intervention and post-intervention assessment. All participants attended every scheduled session, with no dropouts or intervention-related adverse events. Participant feedback indicated good acceptance of the intervention. For the exploratory outcomes, the experimental group showed a greater numerical reduction in Gait Profile Score, although the group-by-time interaction was not significant ( p = 0.187). Exploratory group-by-time interactions favoring the experimental group were observed for the composite gait deviation score ( p = 0.014), FMA-LE ( p = 0.032), TUG ( p = 0.008), and TIS ( p = 0.006). No significant interactions were observed for SIPSO, SPPB, BBS, rectus femoris S-iEMG ( p = 0.294), or tibialis anterior S-iEMG ( p = 0.596). Overall, this pilot feasibility study demonstrated that the data-informed assessment-to-prescription workflow was feasible, safe, and acceptable under supervised laboratory conditions. This was supported by complete attendance, no dropouts, full intervention completion, and positive participant feedback. The exploratory gait, clinical, and sEMG findings warrant further investigation in a larger, adequately powered trial.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67414-z.title: Multifunctional luminescence, electrochemical, and antibacterial performance of Pr0.1Ag0.9NbO3−δ perovskite ceramic
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67414-z.abstract: Abstract Pr 0.1 Ag 0.9 NbO 3−δ ceramic has attracted extensive attention as a material capable of serving multiple roles simultaneously. This work correlated the luminescence, electrochemical, and antibacterial properties of this ceramic. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) analysis of the Pr 0.1 Ag 0.9 NbO 3−δ ceramic showed the formation of an NbO 6 octahedral structure. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) of this ceramic revealed four phase transitions at 317, 436, 528, and 742 K. UV–Visible analysis showed that this ceramic exhibits semiconducting behavior, with direct and indirect band gaps of 3.8 and 2.2 eV, respectively. The excitation spectrum of the Pr 0.1 Ag 0.9 NbO 3−δ ceramic at λ em = 620 nm exhibited several bands in the UV and visible regions. The emission spectrum at λ ex = 240 nm exhibited several bands spanning the blue, greenish-blue, and reddish-orange regions of the visible spectrum. The emission spectrum at λ ex = 456 nm exhibited broad bands in the red region, with weaker bands assigned to the green region. Electrochemical measurements of the Pr 0.1 Ag 0.9 NbO 3−δ ceramic exhibited pseudocapacitive behavior. This ceramic exhibited higher antibacterial activity against Gram-negative than Gram-positive bacteria. These results suggest that Pr 0.1 Ag 0.9 NbO 3−δ is a promising candidate for advanced multifunctional applications in luminescence, energy storage, and antibacterial activity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67714-4.title: A novel sustainable CMC/XG/KAO biopolymer–clay composite hydrogel for efficient dye removal and water treatment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67714-4.abstract: A sustainable biopolymer clay composite hydrogel based on carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), xanthan gum (XG), and kaolinite (KAO) was successfully synthesized via ionic crosslinking using Ca 2 ⁺ ions and evaluated for the removal of anionic Orange II (OII) and cationic Malachite Green (MG) dyes from aqueous solutions. Structural and morphological analysis by SEM, XRD, FTIR, and EDX improved the formation of a porous three-dimensional hydrogel network with strong polymer–clay interactions. The FTIR bands at 912, 756, 700 and 537 cm −1 confirmed the presence of kaolinite in the hydrogel matrix. The adsorption performance was investigated as a function of adsorbent dosage, contact time, initial dye concentration, and solution pH. The hydrogel exhibited significantly higher adsorption efficiency toward MG than toward OII, which was attributed to the strong electrostatic interactions between the negatively charged functional groups (–COO⁻ and –OH) in the hydrogel matrix and the cationic dye molecules. Maximum removal efficiencies of approximately 97.15% for MG at pH 12 and 85% for OII at pH 2 were observed. Adsorption equilibrium was attained within 180 min. Isotherm studies revealed that MG adsorption followed the Langmuir model, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 90.09 mg/g, whereas OII adsorption was better explained by the Freundlich model, suggesting heterogeneous multilayer adsorption. According to the kinetic analysis, the pseudo-first-order model better explained the adsorption mechanism for both dyes. Furthermore, the hydrogel demonstrated good reusability with minimal loss in performance after five adsorption–desorption cycles. The hydrogel surface becomes negatively charged at pH values above the pHPZC (≈6.0), resulting in strong electrostatic attraction toward the cationic MG molecules. These results demonstrate the potential of the CMC/XG/KAO hydrogel as an effective, affordable, and eco-friendly adsorbent for treating wastewater contaminated with dyes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68227-w.title: VEGFA gene expression levels in patients with Parkinson’s disease and first-degree relatives
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68227-w.abstract: Abstract Vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) contributes to angiogenesis and exerts neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects. Altered VEGFA expression has been implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), but findings from peripheral transcriptomic studies remain inconsistent. Data from clinically unaffected first-degree relatives (FDRs) of patients with PD are limited. To evaluate peripheral blood VEGFA mRNA expression in patients with PD and FDRs compared with healthy controls (HCs), and to explore age-related patterns and the discriminatory performance of VEGFA expression. Peripheral blood VEGFA expression was analyzed in 123 participants (PD patients, FDRs, HCs) using one-step RT-qPCR normalized to B2M . Relative expression was log-transformed (logVEGFA). Group differences, age correlations, and diagnostic discrimination were assessed using ANOVA, Pearson correlation, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and multiple linear regression. Both patients with PD and FDRs had significantly higher logVEGFA levels than HCs (p = 0.004), with larger between-group differences in the exploratory subgroup aged ≤ 60 years (p < 0.001). A positive correlation between age and logVEGFA was observed only in HCs. In an exploratory ROC analysis of participants aged ≤ 60 years, logVEGFA yielded an AUC of 0.897 (95% CI 0.771–1.000), with 100% sensitivity and 73.3% specificity. Peripheral VEGFA expression was higher in patients with PD and FDRs than in HCs, particularly in the exploratory subgroup aged ≤ 60 years. Further longitudinal validation is required before its potential biomarker relevance can be established.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60561-3.title: Metabolomics reveals how culture cycles affect muscle quality changes in offshore vessel-farmed Larimichthys crocea
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60561-3.abstract: Abstract To explore the correlation between culture cycles and quality of offshore vessel-farmed Larimichthys crocea (initial weight: 505.32 ± 35.34 g), this study analyzed muscle quality changes at 0 (TK 0 , control group), 1 (TK 1 ), 2 (TK 2 ), 3 (TK 3 ) and 4 (TK 4 ) months via metabolomics. Extended culture cycles significantly increased body length/depth, caudal peduncle length/depth, springiness and crude protein, but significantly decreased condition factors, adhesiveness and crude lipid, with these traits plateauing at TK 3 ( P < 0.05). Although most parameters showed no significant difference between TK 3 and TK 4 , flavor-related indicators slightly decreased at TK 4 . Culture cycles also significantly regulated muscle amino acid/fatty acid profiles, electronic tongue taste (umami, sweetness) and volatile flavors ( P < 0.05). KEGG analysis indicated that phenotypic variations were closely correlated with alterations in amino acid metabolism and antioxidant-related pathways, with optimal nutritional and flavor performance observed at the TK 3 stage. In short, the 3-month culture stage corresponded to superior muscle nutritional quality and flavor characteristics, which coincided with comprehensive changes in amino acid metabolism and antioxidant-related pathways. This study provides a scientific basis for optimizing culture cycles and promoting the sustainable development of high-quality aquaculture.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69020-5.title: Hybrid BiLSTM-CapsNet for dynamic assessment of entrepreneurship ability in business plans
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69020-5.abstract: Proper assessment of business plan entrepreneurial potential is instrumental in facilitating innovation and stimulating economic growth. However, accurate assessment of unstructured text data within these plans using conventional techniques is extremely difficult. In an effort to transcend these limitations, the current research introduces a novel two-stage deep learning-based approach that incorporates the latest techniques to release more accurate analysis. The methodology designed involves two fundamental steps: first, text feature description and extraction, and second, intelligent classification. In the first step, the Global Vectors for Word Representation (GloVe) approach is used to transform the text into machine-understandable numerical vectors. Thereafter, in the second step, these representations from GloVe are modeled and analyzed through a hybrid Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory-Capsule Neural Network (BiLSTM-CapsNet) model. This hybrid deep learning model, leveraging in turn the advantage of BiLSTM’s sequential modeling and hierarchical modeling abilities of CapsNet along with part-to-whole relationships, enables deep text processing, and the prediction is made on the basis of CapsNet output. The proposed BiLSTM-CapsNet approach was evaluated using a large text dataset, and the results show exceptional performance of the model; its accuracy and F-measure reach 95.70% and 0.9568, respectively. This performance confirms the high capability of the BiLSTM-CapsNet approach in detecting complex patterns and extracting key information from text and proves its improved classification capabilities.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69332-6.title: Causal-aware training with counterfactual supervision and structural causal models improves the robustness of LLM-based vulnerability detection
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69332-6.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned for vulnerability detection achieve impressive performance on standard benchmarks, yet growing evidence suggests they exploit spurious correlations—such as code style, comment presence, or identifier naming conventions—rather than learning genuine vulnerability root causes. Recent rigorous evaluations have revealed that models reporting F1-scores above 90% on Big-Vul collapse to near-random performance on properly deduplicated datasets, with F1 dropping by up to 34 \(\times \) . This paper introduces CausalVul , a causal-reasoning framework that addresses this fundamental limitation through four synergistic contributions: (1) Counterfactual Vulnerability Analysis, which identifies minimal code perturbations that flip vulnerability labels to isolate root causes from confounders; (2) Structural Causal Model (SCM) Construction over 25 code features using the PC algorithm with chi-square independence tests, from which we derive adjusted association scores —observational associations adjusted for the observed feature set rather than interventional effects—used to rank and inject features; (3) Causal-Aware Model Training, combining a CodeBERT encoder with LoRA adaptation, contrastive learning on counterfactual pairs, and multi-task CWE classification; and (4) Mechanism-Grounded Accuracy, a novel evaluation metric validated against CVE patches. Under a rigorous project-level group-aware evaluation protocol, CausalVul achieves an F1-score of 76.4% on Devign—an improvement of +18.0 points over its own fine-tuned CodeBERT backbone under identical conditions, and +4.8 points over the strongest cross-backbone baseline (UniXcoder, 71.6%)—with an AUC-ROC of 0.862 and a Mechanism-Grounded Accuracy (the joint accuracy of the detection and CWE heads) of 54.8%. Matched non-causal controls indicate that approximately 9–10 of the 18.0 points are attributable to the causal selection of features and counterfactual edits, with the remainder coming from generic training improvements and from the presence of extra features and pairs. Under combined semantics-preserving lexical perturbations, CausalVul exhibits only a 5.1% F1 drop compared to 12.1–22.3% for baselines, a 2.4 \(\times \) improvement indicating reduced reliance on lexical shortcuts; we do not claim mechanism-level robustness, which would require control-flow- and data-flow-altering rewrites that we leave to future work. On the strict PrimeVul pair-level evaluation, all methods—including ours—perform poorly, a finding we report transparently to characterize the limits of current causal-aware training.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66649-0.title: A mixed-methods evaluation of an AI-powered adaptive learning system for professional english training
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66649-0.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to personalize language learning, but evidence from workplace-oriented programs remains limited, especially regarding the mechanisms through which adaptive systems influence learning and implementation. This study evaluated an integrated AI-powered adaptive learning framework for occupational English development in which learner modeling, analytics, content adaptation, autonomous pacing, and reinforcement-learning-informed sequencing operated as a coordinated intervention. A 16-week quasi-experimental mixed-methods design compared the adaptive platform with non-adaptive e-learning and instructor-led provision. Condition allocation was non-random and used stratified matching within partner-organization and cohort constraints; attrition was low and similar across conditions, and the intended weekly learning dose was standardized. Outcomes combined CEFR-aligned proficiency assessment, authentic communication rubrics, interaction logs, motivation and stakeholder measures, and qualitative evidence. The adaptive condition produced a statistically significant and large advantage in overall proficiency ( p < .001; η² = 0.19), with particularly strong improvements in domain-specific vocabulary and functional communication, as well as better retention. Documented routine instructor and administrative workload, assessment and scoring, content preparation and assignment, learner follow-up, progress monitoring, and reporting, was also lower than under instructor-led provision. These findings contribute system-level evidence that integrated adaptive delivery can connect fine-grained learner information with timely instructional adjustment in organizational language education. Because the intervention bundled multiple adaptive and implementation components, it does not identify reinforcement learning as the sole causal mechanism. Nevertheless, it provides a practical basis for designing human-supervised, privacy-conscious adaptive programs and for testing individual mechanisms through factorial or ablation studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65604-3.title: Knowledge and perspectives of primary care providers regarding prediabetes in rural India: a mixed-methods study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65604-3.abstract: Abstract With the current prevalence of 8%, recent studies have predicted a rising trend in prediabetes. Primary healthcare providers need to have a sufficient understanding of prediabetes to enable early detection and management at the community level. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the knowledge of prediabetes among primary healthcare providers and to explore the management strategies used by primary care physicians in rural South India. A cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted among primary healthcare providers, including accredited social health activists, auxiliary nurse midwives, staff nurses, and primary care physicians, in rural Bengaluru. Quantitative data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing knowledge of prediabetes. Eight in-depth interviews were conducted among primary care physicians and analysed thematically. A total of 208 primary healthcare providers participated in the quantitative component. Of these, 107 (51.4%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 44.4–58.4) had inadequate knowledge of prediabetes. Most participants incorrectly answered questions regarding its definition (n = 174; 83.6%) and symptoms (n = 187; 90.0%), while nearly two-thirds (n = 134; 64.4%) were unaware of the methods used to screen for prediabetes. Having less than five years of professional experience was significantly associated with inadequate knowledge (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] = 2.8; 95% CI: 1.10–6.9; p = 0.029). The qualitative findings identified limited community awareness, absence of evident symptoms, reluctance to adopt dietary and physical activity changes, negligence towards the condition, and insufficient training on prediabetes as important barriers to its management. Context-specific training and decision-support interventions are needed to strengthen the early identification and management of prediabetes at the primary healthcare level.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64862-5.title: High-performance zinc tungstate photocatalyst: tailoring crystallinity, bandgap, and charge separation via controlled calcination
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64862-5.abstract: Zinc tungstate (ZnWO 4 ) nanoparticles were successfully synthesized via a simple co-precipitation method and calcined at a temperature range of 400–700 °C to optimize their catalytic performance. Structural characterization confirmed the formation of monoclinic wolframite-phase ZnWO 4 , with crystallite size increasing from 9.6 to 17.5 nm with the calcination temperature. Optical studies revealed that the bandgap can be tuned from 2.5 (as-prepared) to 3.2 eV (500 °C), with a decrease to 2.6 eV at 700 °C. ZnWO 4 calcined at 500 °C exhibited optimal properties, including balanced crystallinity, surface area (8.58 m 2 /g), and charge separation efficiency, leading to exceptional photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue under UV irradiation (96.5% removal in ~ 4.3 h). Kinetic analysis followed a pseudo-first-order model, with the highest rate constant (~ 1.24 × 10 −2 min −1 ) observed for the 500 °C-calcined sample. Scavenger tests identified hydroxyl radicals (·OH) as the dominant reactive species, with holes contributing moderately and superoxide radicals playing a negligible role. Photoelectrochemical measurements confirmed enhanced charge carrier separation, and cycling tests demonstrated remarkable stability (> 95% efficiency retention after five uses). XRD analysis of the used catalyst confirmed structural stability with negligible phase changes. This work highlights the critical role of calcination temperature in tailoring the structural, optical, and photocatalytic properties of ZnWO 4 , establishing it as a highly efficient, stable, and cost-effective photocatalyst for wastewater treatment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69582-4.title: Systemic delivery of fluorophore-conjugated antibodies enables ex vivo fluorescence mapping of intestinal GLP-1 and GIP: a preclinical feasibility study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69582-4.abstract: Bariatric surgery provides substantial weight loss and metabolic improvements in severe obesity. RYGB, DS, OAGB, and SADI-S share a mechanism of diverting nutrient flow away from the duodenum and proximal jejunum, altering gut hormone signalling and incretin responses. However, bypass length is guided largely by surgeon experience and retrospective evidence, limiting precision due to variability in individual small-bowel anatomy. Target-specific visualization of enteroendocrine and absorptive markers could enable more precise bypass design. We evaluated the feasibility of systemic in vivo delivery and subsequent ex vivo fluorescence detection of fluorophore-conjugated antibodies targeting GLP-1, GIP, and SGLT-1 in rat small intestine. Following intravenous administration of fluorophore-conjugated monoclonal antibodies, rats were euthanized and the small intestine was harvested and divided into proximal, mid, and distal segments. Tissue was fixed in formalin and processed into paraffin sections for fluorescence imaging. Fluorescein-anti GLP-1 demonstrated detectable fluorescence localization in the terminal ileum, while IR800CW-anti GIP showed detectable fluorescence localization in the proximal small bowel. In both cases, fluorescence was localized predominantly to enterocytes and to capillary/vascular structures within the lamina propria and subserosal layers, consistent with segment-specific targeting. In contrast, MB633-anti SGLT-1 showed no detectable uptake across examined segments and dilutions, and this negative signal was interpreted as most likely technical rather than biological, including possibilities such as reduced antibody affinity after fluorophore conjugation, steric hindrance affecting epitope recognition, limited extracellular epitope accessibility following systemic delivery, and/or species/isoform mismatch. These findings demonstrate feasibility of detectable, segment-specific ex vivo localization of incretin-marker antibodies (GLP-1 and GIP) after systemic delivery, supporting future optimization and translation toward real-time intra-operative fluorescence imaging (e.g., probe-based confocal laser endomicroscopy or fluorescence laparoscopy).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67248-9.title: Partial resection of the sternocleidomastoid muscle in the treatment of congenital muscular torticollis in children
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67248-9.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of partial resection of the sternocleidomastoid muscle (SCM) in the treatment of congenital muscular torticollis (CMT) in children. A total of 149 patients (76 males and 73 females, mean age 3.40 ± 3.58 years) with CMT who underwent partial resection of the SCM at our hospital from December 2011 to July 2021 were retrospectively analyzed, among whom 67 patients presented with right-sided involvement and 82 with left-sided involvement. A total of 109 patients aged 1–4 years were allocated to Group 1, while 40 patients aged 5–16 years were assigned to Group 2. Postoperative efficacy was evaluated using the Cheng and Tang scales, and the average follow-up duration was 5.34 ± 2.43 years. According to the Cheng and Tang scale, 109 patients achieved an excellent score, 34 patients attained a good score, and six patients received a fair score. The operation time was longer in Group 2 than in Group 1 ( P < 0.001). Postoperative complications included recurrence in five patients, wound infection in one patient, and hematoma in one patient, whereas no other significant permanent complications occurred in any patient. Our findings demonstrate that partial SCM resection represents an effective treatment option for pediatric CMT.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66586-y.title: Miltirone suppresses proliferation and induces apoptosis in ovarian cancer cells in association with modulation of the RBM15/E2F2/PI3K/Akt signaling axis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66586-y.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a lethal malignancy with limited treatment due to chemoresistance and recurrence, necessitating new agents. Miltirone has anti-tumor activity in other cancers, but its role in OC is unknown. This study investigated miltirone’s effects on OC cells and underlying mechanisms. We assessed proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis using CCK-8, colony formation, wound healing, Transwell, and TUNEL assays. Molecular docking predicted miltirone-RBM15 binding; Western blot analyzed RBM15/E2F2/PI3K/Akt proteins. Functional rescue experiments employed siRNA-mediated knockdown and lentivirus-mediated overexpression of RBM15. Finally, a nude mouse xenograft model was used to assess miltirone’s in vivo anti-tumor efficacy. Miltirone dose-dependently inhibited OC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and induced apoptosis. It downregulated RBM15, E2F2, and PI3K/Akt phosphorylation. RBM15 knockdown mimicked miltirone’s anti-tumor effects, while overexpression partially reversed them. In vivo, miltirone suppressed tumor growth, reduced Ki67-positive cells, increased apoptosis, and downregulated the RBM15/E2F2/PI3K/Akt axis. This first report demonstrates that miltirone inhibits OC progression and induces apoptosis in association with modulation of the RBM15/E2F2/PI3K/Akt axis, positioning miltirone as a preclinical lead compound and this axis as a novel therapeutic target.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66169-x.title: Effect of confining pressure on mechanical behavior and acoustic emission characteristics of rock masses with different dissolution degrees
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66169-x.abstract: To reveal the mechanical behavior, acoustic emission response and failure mechanism of rock masses with different dissolution degrees under confining pressure, rock-like specimens with dissolution degrees of 0%, 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% were prepared using the pre-embedded ice ball melting method. Conventional triaxial compression tests coupled with AE monitoring were conducted to systematically investigate the effects of confining pressure and dissolution degree on mechanical parameters, AE ring counts, RA-AF characteristics, b value, energy release, peak frequency and macroscopic failure morphology. The results show that: (1) Increasing confining pressure significantly enhances specimen strength and deformation resistance. When the confining pressure increased from 3 MPa to 12 MPa, the peak strength increased by 22.85%~33.90%, the elastic modulus increased by 18.88%–37.88%, and the deformation modulus increased by 24.83%–30.48%. In contrast, increasing dissolution degree weakened the effective load-bearing skeleton and structural continuity. At 3 MPa, the peak strength decreased by 26.51% as the dissolution degree increased from 0% to 20%, while the corresponding reduction reached 31.71% at 12 MPa. (2) AE ring counts become markedly active after the crack propagation stage and further increase near the peak and in the post peak stage. Increasing confining pressure transforms AE activity from concentrated and abrupt release to continuous and progressive release, whereas increasing dissolution degree lowers the crack initiation threshold, activates AE activity earlier and significantly widens the pre-peak damage accumulation interval. (3) Tensile cracks and shear cracks develop simultaneously during specimen failure, indicating a tensile shear failure mode. Increasing confining pressure promotes the transition of cracking mode from tensile cracking to shear sliding, whereas increasing dissolution degree enhances local tensile stress concentration around cavity boundaries and increases the proportion of tensile cracks. (4) The damage process is accompanied by the transition from small scale microcracking to large scale coalescence failure, and dissolution defects accelerate this crack scale transition. The macroscopic failure morphology shows that intact and low dissolution specimens are dominated by overall shear failure, whereas high dissolution specimens gradually transform into defect controlled tensile shear failure. These findings provide experimental evidence for evaluating the stability and early warning characteristics of karst tunnel surrounding rock affected by dissolution defects.”

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68443-4.title: A novel muscle property score and its sex-specific associations with fatigue, physical activity, and nutrition in middle-aged adults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68443-4.abstract: A single measure cannot adequately represent overall muscle health. Although muscle properties include structural, functional, and mechanical dimensions, an integrated metric combining muscle mass, strength, and mechanical properties is lacking. This study developed a composite muscle health index, the Total Score of Muscle Properties (TSMP), and examined its associations with fatigue, physical activity, and nutrient intake in middle-aged Japanese adults. A total of 122 participants (59% women; aged 40–64 years) were assessed for appendicular muscle properties, including muscle mass, handgrip strength, knee extensor strength, muscle tone, and stiffness. Principal component analysis was performed separately by sex, with the first principal component defined as TSMP. Fatigue, physical activity, and nutrient intake were assessed using validated questionnaires. The first principal component explained 43.4% of the variance in men and 40.4% in women. In women, higher TSMP was associated with lower upper-body fatigue, instability, uneasiness, and local pain or dullness. In men, higher TSMP was associated with lower risks of physical inactivity and insufficient total physical activity after adjustment, and with higher intake of dietary fiber, calcium, magnesium, iron, B-complex vitamins, and vitamin D. These findings provide initial support for TSMP as an index of musculoskeletal health.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69250-7.title: Voltage peak shaping for increased PV hosting capacity using a multi-frequency DVR
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69250-7.abstract: This work shows how a multi-frequency Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) equipped with voltage peak-shaping capability can raise the amount of photovoltaic (PV) power that low-voltage (LV) distribution feeders are able to accept. Peak shaping is realized with Proportional-Resonant (PR) regulation, which lowers the crest factor of the waveform so that, for a fixed instantaneous peak-voltage limit, the fundamental component—and hence the injectable current—can be increased within the shaped feeder section before the same instantaneous peak-voltage limit is reached. Because the binding constraint is the instantaneous peak rather than the fundamental, flattening the crest releases headroom under that limit, which the PV inverters use to feed additional current into the grid, increasing the power-injection headroom of the feeder section. The multi-frequency injection and its multi-PR control were validated experimentally on laboratory hardware, and the resulting gain in hosting capacity was evaluated for two feeder arrangements, a 3-wire and a 4-wire one. In the 3-wire case, holding the crest at the 360 V ceiling raises the injectable active power from a baseline of 64.4 kW with the DVR disabled to 91.84 kW with the DVR enabled, at the same peak limit. The 4-wire arrangement performs even better: at the identical 360 V peak limit the injectable power reaches 120 kW. In both cases the DVR reshaped the voltage waveform while holding distortion low; the fundamental is unchanged by the reshaping itself, and it is the resulting peak-voltage headroom that permits a larger fundamental and hence a larger injected current. Overall, the multi-frequency DVR offers a practical, retrofit-based route to greater PV power-injection headroom that avoids reconductoring the feeder or altering its connections on the studied feeder section and represents an attractive alternative to conventional feeder reinforcement when rising distributed generation pushes voltages toward their limits.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67908-w.title: Discovery of plastid gene mutations causing albinism in chimeric Cornus cultivars (Cornaceae)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67908-w.abstract: Abstract Chimera plants are becoming popular due to their ornamental and aesthetic appeal. Here, we examined the complete plastid genomes (plastomes) and 45S nuclear ribosomal DNAs (nrDNAs) from green and albino leaf tissues (GLT and ALT) of five Cornus cultivars ( Cornus florida Cherokee Daybreak and four Cornus kousa cultivars). We identified deleterious plastome mutations unique to the ALT of three cultivars: a missense mutation (Y29D) in matK (Cherokee Daybreak) impairing transcript splicing, a 1-bp deletion in rpoB (Melanie), and a 7-bp tandem repeat insertion in ycf3 (Doudou). The latter two induced frameshifts and premature stop codons. Rutban and Tom Wood exhibited identical GLT and ALT plastome sequences, and no 45S nrDNA variations were detected across any cultivars. Furthermore, phylogenetic analyses clustered these cultivars within big-bracted dogwoods and resolved the maternal lineage of the hybrid Rutban as C. florida , correcting prior ambiguities. We also developed five specific molecular markers (two intergenic high-resolution melting and three gene-specific) that successfully discriminated these morphologically similar cultivars. These findings elucidate the diverse genetic causes of albinism and highlight plastid super-barcoding for precision breeding.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67810-5.title: Global maps of silicate, nitrate, and carbon export and resupply fluxes from Biogeochemical Argo observations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67810-5.abstract: The redistribution of nutrients and carbon from the surface ocean to the ocean interior regulates marine productivity and climate, yet global observation-based estimates of export and resupply fluxes remain poorly constrained because most existing estimates rely on fixed stoichiometric assumptions. Here, we develop a hybrid multiple-linear-regression and neural-network framework to reconstruct silicate, nitrate, and dissolved inorganic carbon from hydrographic observations and apply it to 106,905 Biogeochemical Argo profiles collected between 2003 and 2021. This approach produces the first observation-based global maps of annual downward export and upward resupply fluxes of silicate, nitrate, and carbon. The maps reveal pronounced regional decoupling among silicon, nitrogen, and carbon cycling. Silicic acid (Si(OH)₄; hereafter referred to as silicate) export exhibits substantially greater spatial variability than nitrate export, with the highest silicate:nitrate export ratios occurring in the Southern Ocean and decreasing northward across the Indo-Pacific, whereas much of the Atlantic is characterized by silicate:nitrate export ratios below 1. The Southern Ocean south of 45° S accounts for approximately 30% of both global biologically mediated carbon export and net carbon removal to the ocean interior. These observation-based global maps provide a new baseline for investigating nutrient–carbon coupling and its response to future climate change.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68997-3.title: Discharge deficits in the Central Himalaya linked to greening and warming
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68997-3.abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic climate change and rapid infrastructure development have drastically altered the hydrology of many watersheds, influencing the rate at which water is absorbed, stored, and distributed. In this work, we use long-term daily discharge records in the Central Himalaya alongside rainfall and snowmelt data to explore whether there have been large-scale shifts in the conversion of upstream water into discharge throughout the region. We find that, for the majority of watersheds studied over decadal time scales ( $$\sim $$ 1960s to 2024), both rainfall and snowmelt are taking longer to be converted into discharge. We link these changes to increasing water storage deficits, where relatively more surface water is being diverted to soil moisture, vegetation uptake, and deeper water storage reservoirs. We propose that large-scale climate change and vegetation greening have modified catchment-level precipitation-discharge relationships in the Central Himalaya.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67618-3.title: Development of a measurement scale for driving factors of digital transformation in university research management in the Chinese university context
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67618-3.abstract: Digital transformation in university research management is a strategic imperative for modern higher education, yet its implementation remains inconsistent across institutions due to an insufficient understanding of its catalytic elements. This study aimed to develop and validate a robust measurement scale to evaluate the driving factors behind this transition. Drawing on a mixed-methods design, the scale was constructed through qualitative interviews and then rigorously tested using a large-scale survey of 1,875 stakeholders, including administrators, research leaders, and faculty within the Chinese higher education sector. The resulting 23 items instrument identifies six critical dimensions: equipment and technical support, university leadership attitudes, digital cognition, government policy support, university-enterprise collaboration, and digital technology capabilities. Psychometric evaluation confirmed the scale's high internal consistency and strong construct validity. This study fills a gap by operationalizing the driving factors of digital transformation in university research management into a validated six-dimensional framework, thereby extending existing models to the context of academic research governance. The findings offer a diagnostic tool for administrators to identify institutional bottlenecks and provide policymakers with an evidence-based foundation for targeted interventions that foster an integrated and efficient research ecosystem.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69162-6.title: Market participation and sales intensity among dairy farmers in Sululta District, Ethiopia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69162-6.abstract: This study examined the determinants of milk market participation and sales intensity among smallholder dairy producers in Sululta District, Ethiopia, an area with high dairy production potential but persistent market constraints. Primary data were collected from 150 systematically selected households and analyzed using the Heckman two-stage selection model. The findings showed that household size had a negative impact on market participation, with each extra household member lowering the likelihood of participation increased by 8% ( p < 0.05), most likely as a result of higher milk consumption. On the other hand, the amount of milk sold increased by 4.3 L per day ( p < 0.01) for every extra milking cow, indicating higher production capacity and marketable surplus. The chance of market participation was considerably raised by education level, experience in dairy farming, access to extension services, membership in a cooperative, availability of market information, and proximity to urban markets. The amount of milk sold was likewise found to be positively impacted by access to market information. Additionally, while the volume of milk marketed decreased with increasing distance to urban markets, education, dairy farming experience, livestock size, and milk yield significantly boosted sales intensity. These results imply that increasing market accessibility and expanding farmers' access to cooperative networks, education, extension services, and market knowledge can boost dairy market participation and commercialization. These findings offer practical insights for policymakers and development practitioners to strengthen extension services, improve market information systems, enhance dairy productivity, and reduce market access constraints to promote smallholder market integration and dairy sector development in Ethiopia.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68496-5.title: Early cessation of exclusive breastfeeding and associated factors among mothers of children Aged 6–24 months in South Ethiopia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68496-5.abstract: Early cessation of exclusive breastfeeding increases the risk of childhood morbidity, mortality, malnutrition, and poor development. This study assessed the prevalence and determinants of early EBF cessation among mothers in a pastoralist community. A concurrent mixed-methods study was conducted from December 1–30, 2024, among 633 mothers of children aged 6–24 months selected. Quantitative data were collected using a structured questionnaire, while qualitative data were obtained through focus group discussions. The prevalence of early EBF cessation was 42.7% (95% CI: 38.8–46.6%). Higher odds of early cessation were observed among mothers with no religious affiliation (AOR = 5.98, 95% CI: 3.1–11.4), severe (AOR = 4.70, 95% CI: 2.6–8.5) or moderate food insecurity (AOR = 4.00, 95% CI: 2.0–7.7), breastfeeding problems (AOR = 1.85, 95% CI: 1.03–3.3), and primiparity (AOR = 5.72, 95% CI: 2.95–11.1). Factors associated with lower odds of early cessation included primary (AOR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.2–0.7) and secondary or higher maternal education (AOR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.2–0.9), higher birth order (second: AOR = 0.35, 95% CI: 0.2–0.6; third: AOR = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.2–0.7; fourth or higher: AOR = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.1–0.9), antenatal (AOR = 0.51, 95% CI: 0.3–0.8) and postnatal EBF counseling (AOR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.3–0.7), good EBF knowledge (AOR = 0.18, 95% CI: 0.1–0.3), and a positive attitude toward EBF (AOR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.4–0.9). Qualitative findings showed that cultural beliefs, traditional practices, maternal workload, misconceptions and food insecurity contributed to early EBF cessation. Early cessation of EBF remains common in this pastoralist community. Strengthening maternal education, breastfeeding counseling, and support for first-time mothers, while addressing food insecurity, breastfeeding problems, and sociocultural barriers, may improve EBF practices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68545-z.title: Transient topological entanglement of chromatin fiber in human cells during interphase
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68545-z.abstract: Topological entanglement of the chromatin polymer may influence its three-dimensional organization in ways that are not captured by pairwise chromatin contacts. We propose a practical method for detecting linking between Cohesin-mediated chromatin loops based on pairwise interaction data from ChIA-PET experiments. Our algorithm analyzes chromatin interaction networks and detects complete graph (K 6 ) graph minors that guarantee linking of the corresponding chromatin interaction graph. This implies the presence of linked chromatin loops provided that the interactions required to realize the minor coexist in a cell. We applied our algorithm to in situ ChIA-PET datasets from the GM12878, H1-hESC, HFFc6, and WTC11 cell lines, as well as to long-read ChIA-PET data for GM12878, with analyses performed separately for individual chromatin contact domains (CCDs). We found that 1–17% of CCDs contain K 6 minors, indicating potential linking. In GM12878, linked CCDs are enriched for multiplex ChIA-Drop interactions, 63% of which support the simultaneous spatial proximity of at least four loci. Loop extrusion simulations show an increased propensity for link formation in linked CCDs. Finally, linked CCDs are enriched at compartment boundaries and exhibit distinct compartment organization, lower CTCF occupancy, and slightly later replication timing.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67608-5.title: Benchmarking large language models for target-specific financial stance detection in 10-K MD&A sections and earnings call transcripts
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67608-5.abstract: Financial disclosures contain rich narrative information about firm performance, but their length, specialized terminology, and target-dependent language make sentence-level analysis challenging. Existing financial sentiment methods typically assess overall positive or negative tone, rather than stance toward specific financial targets. In this study, we introduce a sentence-level benchmark for target-specific financial stance detection in Form 10-K Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) sections and quarterly earnings call transcripts (ECTs). The benchmark focuses on three financial targets–debt, earnings per share (EPS), and sales–and assigns each target-relevant sentence a positive, negative, or neutral stance label. The corpus is drawn from five public companies. The study is intended as a benchmark for NLP methods and does not support broad claims about financial disclosures in general due to the limited set of companies and financial targets. For scalability, the training split is labeled using ChatGPT-o3-pro, while the held-out test split is independently annotated by human annotators and adjudicated to form a human-consensus gold standard. Using this benchmark, we evaluate four contemporary large language models under zero-shot, few-shot, Chain-of-Thought, and document-context prompting conditions. Model outputs are assessed using accuracy, macro-averaged and weighted precision, recall, and F1, with paired statistical tests used to evaluate performance differences. Results show that LLMs can provide useful baselines for low-label, target-specific financial stance detection, but performance varies across models, document types, targets, and prompting strategies. GPT-4.1-mini and Gemma4-31B generally achieved the strongest overall performance, followed by Llama 3.3-70B and Mistral Small 3.2-24B, although no single model or prompting strategy dominated across all settings. The no-document-context condition achieved the highest Macro-F1 score. However, this result is best interpreted as alignment with the sentence-level annotation protocol, in which annotators did not have access to the full document context, rather than as evidence that document context is generally unhelpful. These findings highlight both the promise and the remaining limitations of LLM-based financial stance detection, particularly the need for broader industry coverage and economic validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67671-y.title: Association of cumulative cholesterol-HDL-glucose index with cardiovascular disease risk in individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0–3: a nationwide prospective cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67671-y.abstract: Abstract Background Cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome integrates cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic risk factors, highlighting their interaction and shared progression. The cholesterol–HDL–glucose (CHG) index is an emerging surrogate marker of insulin resistance, and growing evidence suggests its association with cardiovascular disease risk. However, the association between cumulative CHG exposure and cardiovascular disease risk in the CKM stages 0–3 population remains unclear. Methods Data were obtained from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 3,002 participants with CKM stages 0–3 were included. Cumulative CHG exposure was assessed using CHG values measured at Wave 1 and Wave 3. K-means clustering was applied to classify participants into three groups based on CHG change patterns. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were used to evaluate the association between cumulative CHG and incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was further performed to assess the predictive performance of cumulative CHG for incident CVD and to compare it with cumulative TyG. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to examine the robustness of the results. Results Among the 3,002 participants included in the analysis, 569 (19%) developed incident CVD during a median follow-up of 5 years. In the fully adjusted model, each one-unit increase in cumulative CHG was associated with a 13% higher risk of CVD (HR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.04–1.23). Compared with participants in the lowest quartile, those in the highest quartile had a 34% higher risk of CVD (HR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.02–1.75). Restricted cubic spline analysis indicated a linear association between cumulative CHG and CVD risk. When categorized by CHG clusters, CVD risk increased progressively from Cluster 1 (persistently low levels) to Cluster 2 (persistently moderate levels) and Cluster 3 (high levels with a moderate decrease over time) (P for trend < 0.05). ROC analysis showed that cumulative CHG had limited but comparable discrimination ability for incident CVD compared with cumulative TyG (3-year AUC: 0.560 vs. 0.554; 5-year AUC: 0.569 vs. 0.557; all P for DeLong test > 0.05). Conclusions In individuals with CKM stages 0–3, elevated cumulative CHG is associated with an increased risk of CVD. Cumulative CHG may help identify individuals at higher risk of CVD and provide evidence to support cardiovascular risk stratification and early preventive strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69750-6.title: Analysis of the factors affecting the construction mechanical characteristics of small-spacing tunnel groups
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69750-6.abstract: The construction mechanical response of small-spacing tunnel groups is strongly influenced by surrounding rock grade, tunnel spacing, and burial depth. Based on the close-stacked tunnel group project in Hongyan Village, Chongqing, this study establishes a PLAXIS 3D numerical model to investigate the deformation and stress response of the tunnel group under different conditions. The results show that surrounding rock grade mainly controls the deformation magnitude. As the surrounding rock grade decreases from Grade I to Grade IV, the maximum arch crown settlement of the main tunnel increases from 1.51 mm to 10.45 mm. Tunnel spacing mainly affects the interaction intensity between adjacent tunnels. When the spacing decreases to 1.0 m, the arch crown settlement reaches 8.94 mm, indicating a strengthened group-tunnel effect. Burial depth primarily amplifies the overall deformation level. When the burial depth increases from 3.0 m to 23.8 m, the arch crown settlement increases by 7.81 mm. These results indicate that the stability of small-spacing tunnel groups is jointly controlled by surrounding rock quality, spatial spacing, and burial-depth-induced stress conditions. The findings provide a reference for stability evaluation and support design of close-stacked tunnel groups under complex geological conditions.
