doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62643-8.title: Development of new imidazopyridine-based chalcones hybrids as potent antidiabetic and antioxidant agents: synthesis, in silico and in vitro evaluation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62643-8.abstract: Nowadays, diabetes mellitus (DM) is a rapidly growing global health concern. In this study, we synthesized a novel series of six imidazopyridine-based chalcone hybrids ( 5a-f ) and evaluated their in vitro biological activities, including total antioxidant capacity, iron-reducing power, and radical scavenging (DPPH, ABTS, NO), as well as antidiabetic potential against α-amylase, α-glucosidase, and aldose reductase. All compounds showed moderate to potent activity, with derivatives 5c and 5f being the most effective. Compound 5f exhibited the highest antioxidant performance (total capacity: 78.63 mg GAE/g; reducing power: 68.88 µg/ml) and strong radical scavenging (IC 50 : 5.68, 4.75, and 6.52 µg/ml for DPPH, ABTS, and NO, respectively), comparable to ascorbic acid. It also potently inhibited α -amylase, α -glucosidase, and aldose reductase (IC 50 : 6.71, 4.78, and 4.04 µg/ml). Molecular docking and 100 ns MD simulations further supported these findings: compound 5f showed the best aldose reductase binding (–8.97 kcal/mol), outperforming reference IDD594, while 5c bound favorably to α-amylase and α-glucosidase (–7.28 and − 6.64 kcal/mol) through π-interactions, ionic contacts, and key hydrogen bonds. The 5f -aldose reductase complex remained stable throughout the simulation, with maintained active-site and loop conformations after minor early fluctuations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69530-2.title: A cost-efficient vision-based robotic manipulation system for smart IIoT production lines
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69530-2.abstract: A low-cost, vision-based robotic manipulation framework designed for intelligent IIoT-enabled production lines is presented in this research. To achieve reliable performance under various industrial settings, the proposed system presents an edge-aware perception pipeline that combines calibration-aware localization, monocular vision, and GAN-assisted augmentation for real-time robotic manipulation. The framework maintains excellent detection accuracy while drastically lowering hardware complexity and cost, in contrast to traditional methods that rely on cost-prohibitive depth-sensing hardware. To enable precise and dependable pick-and-place operations, a tightly connected perception calibration control architecture is created to guarantee accurate mapping from image-space observations to robot workspace coordinates. Real-time decision-making and low-latency inference are made possible by the system's deployment on an edge computing platform. A collection of about 900 annotated photos taken in various lighting scenarios, object orientations, and spatial arrangements is used for experimental evaluation. With a mean detection accuracy of 94.2% with low variance, the results show robust convergence behavior and better performance than baseline models. The system meets real-time industrial needs with an average inference time of about 35 ms per frame. Additionally, scalable deployment and smooth communication across dispersed production environments are made possible by integration with lightweight IIoT communication protocols. All things considered, the suggested framework offers a workable and scalable way to connect IIoT system integration, real-time robotic manipulation, and vision-based perception. The creation of a perception calibration control coupling architecture that synchronizes visual perception, spatial synchronization, edge inference, and robotic execution within a single IIoT production environment is the study's primary contribution rather than the individual adoption of current algorithms like YOLOv8 detection, GAN-based augmentation, or hand-eye calibration. Real-time closed-loop manipulation is made possible by this concept in industrial settings with limited resources.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62159-1.title: A temporal graph attention autoencoder framework quantifies geopolitical trade risk through the evolutionary embedding of international trade networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62159-1.abstract: The increasing complexity of global trade networks demands analytical tools capable of capturing higher-order relational structures and their co-evolution with geopolitical tensions. Building on the limitations of static graph embeddings such as DeepWalk and Node2Vec and on prior temporal models including EvolveGCN, DySAT and TGAT, we present a Temporal Graph Attention Autoencoder (TGAA) that integrates multi-head graph attention with Gated Recurrent Unit sequential modelling and reinforces the encoder with residual connections to mitigate over-smoothing on dense trade graphs. Using United Nations Comtrade data covering 178 countries from 2001 to 2023, the model is implemented in PyTorch 2.1 and torch_geometric 2.4 with all hyperparameters selected by grid search and cross-validation. Evolutionary features are distilled from the learned embeddings and synthesised into a three-tier Geopolitical Trade Risk Index (GTRI) whose indicator weights are derived through the entropy method rather than imposed a priori. Empirical results show that the TGAA model attains a link prediction AUC of 0.932, outperforms both static and contemporary dynamic graph baselines, and produces a GTRI that captures major geopolitical disruptions—including the 2014 Crimea crisis and the 2022 Russia–Ukraine conflict—while preserving robustness under sensitivity tests on β and λ. Augmented Toda–Yamamoto Granger tests, complemented by effective transfer entropy, confirm that the GTRI carries linear and nonlinear predictive content for the Caldara–Iacoviello GPR index across an expanded sample of twelve major economies. We interpret these findings as evidence that network-embedding-derived structural signals encode forward-looking information about geopolitical tensions that text-based indices alone cannot fully capture.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66600-3.title: Three-dimensional anatomical analysis of the horizontal part of the third segment of the vertebral artery in the low retrosigmoid approach
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66600-3.abstract: Iatrogenic injury to the horizontal part of the third segment of the vertebral artery (V3h) is a catastrophic complication of the low retrosigmoid approach. This study aimed to delineate three-dimensional (3D) anatomical variations of the V3h through quantitative analysis and to establish an anatomical risk-stratification framework to improve surgical safety. A multimodal study was performed using 10 cadaveric specimens and 217 clinical computed tomography angiography (CTA) datasets. Key measurements included the V3h-C1 and V3h-OC distances. A novel classification system was developed based on the spatial relationship between the V3h and two surgical reference lines. The mean V3h-C1 and V3h-OC distances were 8.77 ± 2.34 mm and 7.78 ± 2.72 mm, respectively. Only 11.1% of V3h segments were Type I (Closely Adherent), while 88.9% exhibited varying protrusions, with Type IV (Posteriorly Horizontal Projecting) being the most prevalent (55.6%). A high-position anatomical group, defined by V3h-C1 > 10 mm and V3h-OC < 5 mm, accounted for 6.2% of sides, and Type IIIb, characterized by prominent posterosuperior protrusion, accounted for 12.2%. These findings indicate substantial V3h variability and support individualized preoperative CTA-based 3D assessment. The proposed classification and measurements may help identify configurations requiring heightened caution during the low retrosigmoid approach.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69572-6.title: A rapid LNA-PCR assay from blood lysate without DNA purification for the diagnosis of homozygous SMN1 deletion in spinal muscular atrophy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69572-6.abstract: Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive disorder most often caused by homozygous deletion of exon 7 in the SMN1 gene. Early and reliable molecular diagnosis is essential for clinical management, genetic counseling, and implementation of emerging therapeutic interventions. However, many molecular diagnostic methods require DNA purification and complex laboratory workflows, which may increase turnaround time and cost. In this study, we aimed to develop a rapid and simplified molecular diagnostic assay based on direct locked nucleic acid polymerase chain reaction (LNA-PCR) for the detection of homozygous SMN1 deletions without the need for DNA purification. Peripheral blood samples were collected from 792 individuals, including 61 multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) confirmed SMA patients, 45 MLPA validated healthy controls, 56 MLPA validated SMA carriers and 630 clinical controls comprising healthy individuals aged over 40 years with no SMA-related symptoms reported between September 2022 and January 2025. Direct real-time polymerase chain reaction was performed using locked nucleic acid–modified primers targeting the SMN1 gene and the β-actin gene as an internal control. Reactions were conducted in a total volume of 10 µL using 2.5 µL of blood lysate without DNA extraction. Amplification status was used to determine the presence or absence of homozygous SMN1 deletions. Amplification of the β-actin control gene was successfully achieved in all samples, indicating adequate reaction performance. Among the 60 patients with MLPA-confirmed homozygous SMN1 deletion, the direct LNA-PCR assay correctly identified 57, corresponding to a sensitivity of 95.00% (95% CI: 86.3–98.4%). No false-positive results were observed among the 102 MLPA-validated negative individuals (45 healthy controls, 56 carriers, and 1 compound heterozygous patient), yielding a specificity of 100% (95% CI: 96.5–100%), a PPV of 100% (95% CI: 93.7–100%), an NPV of 97.14% (95% CI: 92.1–99.1%), and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 98.15% (95% CI: 94.7–99.6%). The compound heterozygous patient was classified as SMN1 -positive, reflecting the known limitation of real time polymerase chain reaction based approaches in identifying sequence variants. Overall, the assay demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy and robust performance for detecting homozygous SMN1 deletions. The direct LNA-PCR assay enables rapid, reliable, and cost-effective detection of homozygous SMN1 deletions directly from blood samples without DNA purification. This simplified workflow may facilitate broader implementation of molecular testing for SMA in routine clinical laboratories and resource-limited settings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68665-6.title: Long-term effects of cognitive-behavioral therapy for adults with ADHD: results from an 8-year randomized controlled trial follow-up
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68665-6.abstract: Abstract Background To evaluate the provisional long-term durability of group cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) benefits 8 years post-baseline and to explore tentative associations between digital booster engagement and the maintenance of treatment gains in adults with ADHD. Methods Forty-eight participants recruited from outpatient clinics across Japan ( M age = 39, 87% female) were randomized to group CBT or treatment-as-usual (primary outcome self-reported). At 5 years, CBT participants were offered a digital booster with periodic assessments (optional; non-random uptake). The primary outcome was CAARS Inattention/Memory; secondary outcomes covered ADHD symptoms, anxiety, depression, functioning, and time management. Follow-up occurred at 8 years. Intention-to-treat linear mixed models tested Group × Time effects. Sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and three-way comparisons (CBT+booster vs. CBT-only vs. treatment-as-usual); exploratory analyses used Bayesian and within-subject models. Results At 8-year follow-up, 24 participants (50%) completed assessments. CBT nominally showed lower inattention than TAU ( p = .038, d = -0.65), though results were not robust to imputation. No adverse events were recorded. DSM inattentive symptoms ( p = .025, ηp² = .09) and family functioning ( p = .025, ηp² = .08) appeared more robust and survived imputation. Bayesian models yielded consistent preliminary support. Reliable Change Index analyses indicated higher rates of reliable individual-level improvement in the CBT group (43%) than in the Control group (10%), with all CBT improvers belonging to the booster subgroup. Conclusions This 8-year follow-up (representing a rare longitudinal window) provides preliminary and exploratory evidence that group CBT benefits on inattention and specific functional domains may persist in some adults with ADHD. However, firm conclusions are precluded by the small sample size, high attrition, non-random booster allocation, and reliance on self-reports within a predominantly female Japanese sample. These results should be viewed as hypothesis-generating, requiring replication in larger, more diverse cohorts. Trial registration : UMIN000026916 (2017/04/09)

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69426-1.title: Enhancing liu-type estimation for poisson-modified quasi-lindley regression
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69426-1.abstract: Abstract This study develops an improved Liu‑type estimator for the Poisson‑modification of the quasi‑Lindley regression model (PMQL‑RM) to handle overdispersed count data in the presence of severe multicollinearity. We first formulate the PMQL‑RM and review existing shrinkage estimators, including the PMQL ridge estimator, the PMQL Liu estimator, and a previously proposed PMQL Liu‑type estimator. Building on recent work on improved Liu‑type estimators in generalized linear models, we introduce a new PMQL improved Liu‑type estimator (PMQL‑ILTE) that incorporates an eigenvalue‑dependent biasing function, yielding a flexible one‑parameter shrinkage scheme so that the shrinkage applied to each regression direction is tailored to the corresponding eigenvalue of the information matrix. We derive closed‑form expressions for the bias, variance–covariance matrix, matrix mean squared error (MMSE), and scalar MSE. A comprehensive Monte Carlo study is then conducted, varying multicollinearity levels, sample sizes, number of predictors, and dispersion parameters. The simulation results show that the PMQL‑ILTE uniformly achieves the smallest MSE across all scenarios, with especially pronounced gains under high multicollinearity and moderate‑to‑large samples. Finally, an application to Swedish football league data demonstrates the practical relevance of the proposed estimator. Relative to PMQL‑MLE and other shrinkage competitors, PMQL‑ILTE substantially reduces the estimated MSE while stabilizing regression coefficients without altering their signs or substantive ranking. Overall, the results indicate that the proposed estimator provides an efficient alternative for modeling overdispersed count responses with multicollinear covariates.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67574-y.title: Parity-aligned control allocation for stochastic aeroelastic systems with distributed actuation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67574-y.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence generates stochastic aerodynamic loads that excite coupled rigid-body and flexible aeroelastic modes, producing transient rotational disturbances that may affect structural integrity, actuator usage, and passenger comfort. Conventional constrained control-allocation methods distribute actuator commands directly in actuator coordinates and usually treat actuator geometry as a passive constraint rather than an exploitable stabilizing structure. Here, we develop a symmetry-structured control-allocation framework for distributed aeroelastic systems with bilaterally paired actuators. The framework is based on an equivariant control-effectiveness relation, $$M{P}_{g}={Q}_{g}M,$$ where $${P}_{g}$$ represents reflection symmetry in actuator space and $${Q}_{g}$$ represents the corresponding action on roll, pitch, and yaw moment space. This formulation permits symmetric and antisymmetric actuator modes to generate their physically appropriate even and odd moment components, avoiding the incorrect implication that antisymmetric modes vanish. Under equivariance and compatible actuator constraints, the allocation problem admits a parity-aligned decomposition into convex subproblems; under asymmetric saturation or effectiveness loss, the same structure provides a block-preconditioned allocation with feasibility correction. A covariance-based stochastic analysis shows that, when the symmetry-aligned residual operator satisfies a spectral contraction condition, the maximal eigenvalue of the residual disturbance covariance decreases, yielding sharper Gaussian concentration bounds for extreme residual loads. Numerical experiments using a three-axis reduced-order moment-level allocation model with twenty-four distributed actuators show that, in the nominal exactly equivariant case, parity-aligned allocation reproduces the full-space damped-pseudoinverse response to numerical roundoff, with identical residual loads, covariance metrics, actuator-utilization patterns, and saturation statistics. These results validate the corrected parity formulation while showing that tail-risk reduction should be claimed only in regimes where spectral contraction is empirically observed. An additional controlled nonlinear stress-test with cubic disturbance deformation, quadratic cross-axis coupling, and smooth actuator-effectiveness terms shows that residual scales increase under moderate nonlinear perturbation, while the full-space and parity-aligned responses coincide to numerical roundoff.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69409-2.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of healthcare professionals in anesthesia-related departments regarding postoperative delirium: a scale development and cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69409-2.abstract: This study examined the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of healthcare professionals in anesthesia-related departments regarding postoperative delirium (POD). A single-center, cross-sectional, self-reported online survey using snowball sampling was conducted at Second Xiangya Hospital from September to November 2024, and 550 valid questionnaires were included, corresponding to a valid questionnaire proportion of 96.15% (550/572) among the submitted questionnaires. Most respondents were nurses (80.7%) and female (71.8%), with 44.4% having 11–15 years of experience; 86.6% had managed POD before. Mean KAP scores were as follows: self-perceived knowledge 20.00 ± 7.33 (out of 32, 62.5%), attitude 42.43 ± 4.79 (84.9%), and practice 29.83 ± 6.44 (74.6%). According to predefined classification criteria, the mean perceived knowledge score fell within the moderate range. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive relationships: knowledge correlated with attitude ( r = 0.741) and practice ( r = 0.688), and attitude with practice ( r = 0.703). Structural equation modeling showed significant associations among knowledge, attitude, and practice, with knowledge associated with both attitude and practice, and attitude associated with practice. Healthcare professionals in anesthesia-related departments exhibited moderate perceived knowledge, positive attitudes, and relatively positive practices toward managing POD, with these domains being significantly interrelated. Addressing practical deficiencies requires integrating evidence-based tools, fostering continuous professional development, and tailoring interventions to specific cultural and organizational contexts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67902-2.title: Heavy oil compositional changes through bioupgrading process in the presence of Geobacillus stearothermophilus
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67902-2.abstract: The exploitation and processing of unconventional heavy oil resources are constrained by high viscosity, abundant heavy fractions, and associated environmental concerns. Biological upgrading has therefore attracted interest as a potentially lower-impact approach for modifying heavy-oil composition. This study investigated compositional changes in heavy crude oil following incubation with Geobacillus stearothermophilus at 60 °C for different treatment periods. Biotic experiments and abiotic controls were conducted in duplicate. Among the tested conditions, the most pronounced changes occurred after 14 days. Quantitative FTIR analysis showed that the aromaticity index decreased from 0.21305 to 0.08230, whereas the aliphatic index increased from 0.71945 to 0.85934. GC–MS analysis further showed that cyclohexane, 1,1,3-trimethyl-, and 1R,2c,3t,4t-tetramethylcyclohexane were no longer detected under the applied analytical conditions, while the estimated contents of octacosane and dodecane, 2,6,10-trimethyl-, increased by approximately 21% and 86.9%, respectively. Abiotic controls showed only minor changes in the corresponding FTIR indices and viscosity. Overall, the findings provide preliminary evidence that G. stearothermophilus can modify heavy crude oil composition and viscosity under the tested laboratory conditions. Further validation under pressurized, saline, anaerobic, and reservoir-relevant conditions is required before practical application can be assessed.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68096-3.title: Adaptive federated edge intelligence with semantic communication and trust-aware optimization for heterogeneous IoT networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68096-3.abstract: The rapid growth of heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) networks introduces significant challenges in communication efficiency, energy consumption, and reliable distributed intelligence due to diverse device capabilities, dynamic channel conditions, and limited computational resources. Existing bit-level communication and conventional federated learning approaches often suffer from excessive communication overhead, inefficient resource utilization, and unstable model convergence under non-IID data and unreliable device participation. To address these limitations, this paper proposes FEI-SemCom, an adaptive federated edge intelligence framework that integrates semantic communication, federated learning, and joint resource optimization for heterogeneous IoT systems. The proposed framework introduces a heterogeneity-aware semantic encoder, adaptive semantic compression mechanism, semantic contribution-based client selection strategy, and trust-aware aggregation scheme to improve communication efficiency and learning robustness. Unlike existing approaches that optimize communication, learning, and resource allocation independently, FEI-SemCom jointly adapts semantic representation, client participation, transmission parameters, and aggregation weights according to device capability, channel quality, and energy availability. Furthermore, the proposed framework improves resilience under intermittent connectivity conditions by enabling adaptive client participation, reliability-aware aggregation, and resource-aware communication decisions, allowing federated edge intelligence to operate effectively despite temporary link failures and unstable device availability. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves 91.2% accuracy at 5 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), converges within approximately 120 training rounds, and reduces communication overhead, energy consumption, and latency to 45 MB, 48 J, and 110 ms, respectively. Compared with conventional approaches, FEI-SemCom reduces communication overhead by up to 38% while maintaining stable convergence and robust learning performance. These results demonstrate the potential of adaptive semantic communication combined with federated edge intelligence for scalable and resource-efficient IoT applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68898-5.title: Probiotic supplementation mitigates antibiotic-associated gut dysbiosis and improves clinical and physiological outcomes in adult Rex rabbits
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68898-5.abstract: Antibiotic-associated gut dysbiosis (AAD) is a life-threatening condition in rabbits due to severe disruption of cecal microbiota. This study evaluated the protective effects of probiotics against AAD induced by co-trimoxazole in adult Rex rabbits. Twenty-five rabbits were randomly allocated to five groups ( n = 5): Group 1 (control, saline), Group 2 (co-trimoxazole only), Group 3 ( Saccharomyces boulardii + antibiotic), Group 4 ( S. boulardii + Enterococcus faecium + antibiotic), and Group 5 ( S. boulardii + Pediococcus acidilactici + antibiotic). Antibiotic and probiotics were co-administered for 14 days, followed by probiotics alone until day 28. Fecal microbiology, hematology, serum biochemistry, body weight, feed intake, fecal consistency, and histopathology were assessed. The group receiving only antibiotic showed severe dysbiosis according to culture-based findings, characterized by a depletion of Escherichia coli , overgrowth of Klebsiella spp. and spore-forming anaerobes, reduced counts of lactic acid bacteria, 34.5% body weight loss, and 100% mortality during the study period. By contrast, probiotic-treated groups exhibited significant changes in selected cultivable fecal microbial populations, including partial restoration of beneficial bacteria and suppression of opportunistic pathogens ( P < 0.05). Clinically, probiotics helped prevent diarrhea, maintain feed intake, and improve survival. Notably, the combination of S. boulardii and P. acidilactici resulted in a significant increase in body weight (21.4% by day 14 and 27.5% by day 28) and was associated with complete survival throughout the study period. The biochemical and hematological parameters remained within normal ranges in the multi-strain probiotic groups; in contrast, the antibiotic-only group showed elevated blood urea nitrogen, hypoproteinemia, reduced serum AST and ALT levels, and leukopenia. Histopathological findings confirmed severe intestinal, hepatic, and renal lesions in antibiotic-treated rabbits, whereas the apparent severity of these lesions was lower in probiotic-supplemented groups.In conclusion, multi-strain probiotics, particularly S. boulardii + P. acidilactici , were associated with attenuation of antibiotic-induced dysbiosis, improved clinical outcomes, and enhanced survival in rabbits receiving co‑trimoxazole. These findings suggest that probiotic supplementation may represent a promising approach for mitigating antibiotic-associated complications in rabbits.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69656-3.title: Simulation-informed kernel-based regression models for predicting temperature distribution in microwave hyperthermia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69656-3.abstract: This work analyzes heat transfer in microwave heating process using hyperthermic approach. Predictive performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models coupled with data of mechanistic model were evaluated. The resulting predictive models provide a surrogate representation of the simulated temperature field and may support temperature assessment in microwave hyperthermia applications. The model is developed in two stages, where in the first stage, electromagnetic heating is modeled via solution of bioheat equations to compute temperature field in the tissue. Then, the results are used for building several artificial intelligence-based models. The predictive stage of the study was carried out using three nonlinear kernel-driven learning approaches, namely Support Vector Machine (SVM), Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), and Relevance Vector Machine (RVM), with the spatial coordinates serving as predictors of the temperature field. Model-specific hyperparameters were determined through a Cuckoo Search-based optimization procedure. Among the evaluated algorithms, SVM delivered the strongest overall predictive performance, yielding R 2 values of 0.9766 for the training data and 0.9768 for the test data. Its mean R 2 obtained from five-fold cross-validation was likewise 0.9768, with a very small standard deviation of 0.00063, while it also produced the minimum MSE and MAE values. In contrast, RVM exhibited the smallest worst-case deviation, with a maximum absolute error of 9.3946 K. Although KRR and RVM achieved satisfactory test-set R 2 values of 0.9200 and 0.9560, respectively, the collective evaluation of predictive accuracy, error magnitude, and validation stability identified SVM as the most suitable approach for dependable and precise estimation of the spatial temperature distribution. These results offer significant insights into the utilization of kernel-based regression models for predicting spatial temperatures, with implications for diverse domains including cancer therapy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62470-x.title: CrystalGRW: generative modeling of crystal structures with targeted crystallographic properties via geodesic random walks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62470-x.abstract: Determining whether a candidate crystalline material is thermodynamically stable depends on identifying its true ground-state structure, a central challenge in computational materials science. We introduce CrystalGRW, a diffusion-based generative model on Riemannian manifolds that proposes candidate crystal configurations in stable phases, validated through density functional theory calculations. Our model is designed for de novo generation, which creates crystal structures together with their compositions. The crystal properties, such as fractional coordinates, atomic types, and lattice matrices, are represented on suitable Riemannian manifolds, ensuring that new predictions generated through the diffusion process preserve the periodicity of crystal structures. We also incorporate an equivariant graph neural network to account for rotational and translational symmetries within the model. CrystalGRW generates crystal structures that are stable and closely resemble their density-functional-theory ground states. The model also supports conditional control, such as enforcing a specified crystallographic point group, thereby accelerating materials discovery and inverse design by providing symmetry-consistent, energetically stable candidate crystals for experimental validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64927-5.title: Endophytic bacteria associated with turmeric, ginger and white radish exhibit dual roles as producers of antibacterial metabolites and carriers of multidrug resistance
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64927-5.abstract: Abstract The increasing global burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates the exploration of unconventional microbial niches for novel bioactive compounds. Simultaneously, it is also necessary to evaluate their role in the dissemination of resistant bacteria through the food chain. Endophytic bacteria inhabiting edible plant tissues represent a largely underexplored interface between environmental microbiota and human exposure. In this exploratory study, endophytic bacteria were isolated from fresh rhizomes of Zingiber officinale (ginger), Curcuma longa (turmeric), and Raphanus sativus (white radish), and characterized for their antimicrobial activity and antibiotic resistance profiles. A total of 24 endophytic bacterial isolates were isolated from fresh rhizomes of turmeric, ginger and white radish using tissue segmentation method. Among them, eight isolates (33.33%) exhibited weak to strong inhibitory activity against multidrug-resistant clinical pathogens, including Escherichia coli , Escherichia fergusonii , Shigella spp. , Staphylococcus aureus , and Bacillus cereus . Molecular identification based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing revealed that the isolate RD-1(b) was affiliated with Burkholderia contaminans and TM-4(b) and RD-2(c) with Enterobacter cloacae . Crude extracellular metabolites extracted from the RD-1(b) retained broad-spectrum antibacterial activity. Notably, these isolates demonstrated resistance to multiple antibiotics, including β-lactams, macrolides, and tetracyclines, while remaining susceptible to selected agents such as ciprofloxacin and cotrimoxazole. The coexistence of antimicrobial activity and multidrug resistance within endophytic bacteria highlights their dual role as both potential sources of bioactive metabolites and reservoirs of AMR determinants. Given that these rhizomes are commonly consumed raw or minimally processed, the presence of such bacteria potentially raises food safety concerns. The possible beneficial role of these endophytes should also be explored.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69699-6.title: Antibacterial activity and corrosion behavior of thermally evaporated copper coated AZ31 magnesium alloy with and without substrate homogenization
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69699-6.abstract: Biodegradable Mg alloys such as AZ31 are attractive for temporary implant applications, yet their rapid degradation in physiological media remains a major limitation. Here, AZ31 was evaluated in the as-received and homogenized conditions before and after deposition of a Cu thin film by thermal evaporation. The combined effects of substrate condition and Cu deposition on surface characteristics, antibacterial activity, and corrosion behavior were systematically investigated. XRD confirmed the presence of α-Mg and fcc Cu phases, with Scherrer-estimated crystallite sizes of 47.34 nm for the uncoated substrate and 72.43 nm for the Cu-containing layer. FE-SEM revealed a relatively continuous Cu-containing surface layer with dispersed nanoscale features, while EDS and elemental mapping confirmed the presence and distribution of Cu on the coated surfaces. AFM showed a marked reduction in the measured surface roughness after homogenization and standardized surface preparation, with Ra values of 29.63 nm for AZ31 and 6.88 nm for AZ31A; after Cu deposition, Ra values were 7.18 nm for AZ31–Cu and 9.21 nm for AZ31A–Cu. Electrochemical testing in simulated body fluid (SBF) showed that Cu deposition substantially reduced the corrosion resistance of AZ31, as evidenced by lower impedance and polarization resistance and higher corrosion current density. Antibacterial assessment against Escherichia coli by disk diffusion demonstrated enhanced antibacterial activity for the Cu-coated samples, with inhibition-zone diameters of 22 mm for AZ31, 24 mm for AZ31–Cu, and 26 mm for AZ31A–Cu. Ion-release measurements further supported accelerated substrate degradation, with Mg²⁺ concentration reaching 334.04 ppm after 7 days for AZ31A–Cu. Although Cu deposition enhanced antibacterial activity, it simultaneously accelerated Mg degradation in SBF, highlighting the need to balance antibacterial functionality with corrosion control in the development of Cu-functionalized biodegradable Mg surfaces.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67992-y.title: Comparative study of whispering gallery modes in fluorescence and dark-field scattering spectra of single microspheres
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67992-y.abstract: Herein, we report the comparative analysis of whispering gallery modes (WGMs) in fluorescence and dark-field scattering spectra of single dye-doped dielectric microspheres. In detail, single dye-doped microspheres are selected, and the fluorescence and dark-field scattering spectra for each microsphere are recorded one after another using a transmission-mode dark-field optical microscope with fluorescence attachment. Later, the quality factors, intensities, and wavelengths of the WGMs in both types of spectra obtained for each microsphere are compared. The experimentally observed WGMs are characterized using the Lorenz–Mie scattering theory. Moreover, the role of the numerical aperture of the microscopic objective lens on the WGMs observed in these spectra is studied in detail. Finally, the merits and demerits of the WGMs observed in both types of spectra are discussed in detail. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report presenting a direct comparison of WGMs in fluorescence and dark-field scattering spectra obtained from the same single optical microspheres.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69396-4.title: From aesthetics to authenticity: a stimulus–organism–response model of audience responses to AI-generated intangible cultural heritage design
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69396-4.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in heritage visualization, yet its outputs often raise concerns about cultural authenticity. Prior studies have focused more on technical fidelity and symbolic preservation than on how audiences evaluate the authenticity of AI-generated heritage imagery. To address this gap, this study develops and tests a Stimulus-Organism-Response model using AI-generated Wuxi clay figurine images. A randomized between-subjects online experiment with 330 participants examined the associations of visual information quality, AI technical novelty, and symbol salience with perceived aesthetics, perceived authenticity, cultural identity, and acceptance intention. The theory-specified model showed that visual information quality, technical novelty, and symbol salience were positively associated with perceived aesthetics, while perceived aesthetics and symbol salience were positively associated with perceived authenticity. Perceived aesthetics and perceived authenticity were also associated with cultural identity and acceptance intention. However, the HTMT analysis indicated limited discriminant validity, particularly among visual information quality, technical novelty, symbol salience, and perceived aesthetics. A supplementary second-order model representing these four perceptions as facets of an overall perceived design quality factor showed acceptable fit and comparable downstream associations. In this alternative specification, perceived authenticity was no longer independently associated with acceptance intention. Accordingly, the construct-specific path estimates should be interpreted cautiously. Overall, the findings are consistent with the presence of a substantial holistic evaluative component in audience responses to AI-generated heritage imagery.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61989-3.title: Microstructural and mechanical effects of biochar particle size on clay compressibility and lead immobilization
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61989-3.abstract: The demand for sustainable soil stabilizers has driven interest in soil–biochar mixtures for geotechnical applications such as landfill liners and subgrade systems. However, the role of biochar particle size in governing compressibility, shear strength, and heavy metal immobilization remains unclear. This study examines the influence of fine (FB) and coarse biochar (CB) derived from bamboo on the compressibility, shear strength, and Pb 2+ immobilization in clayey soil at dosages of 1–10%. One-dimensional consolidation tests reveal that FB at 10% increased the void ratio by 31.7%, whereas CB reduced it by 22.7% relative to untreated soil. Both biochar types decreased compression and swell indices at higher dosages, with FB-treated soils exhibiting greater stiffness under elevated stress. Void index analysis indicates the formation of a stable and stress-resistant soil–biochar matrix. Microstructural observations show denser particle packing in FB mixtures, while CB mixtures exhibit particle fragmentation at higher dosages. Toxicity characteristic leaching procedure (TCLP) tests demonstrate that 5% FB reduces Pb 2+ concentrations below regulatory limits within 14 days, whereas CB requires higher dosages or longer curing periods. These findings highlight the critical role of biochar particle size in optimizing soil performance and contaminant immobilization for barrier applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69297-6.title: Microfungi of volcanic thermal environments of Avachinsky volcano (Kamchatka Peninsula, Russian Far East)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69297-6.abstract: Studying the biodiversity of volcanic environments can help reveal the potential for microbial survival, adaptation, and widespread habitat in extreme conditions of life on Earth. 15 species from 11 genera were isolated and identified from different habitats of Avachinsky volcano. The species Acidomyces acidothermus , Alternaria alternata , Daldinia loculata , Penicillium velutinum , Simplicillium aogashimaense , Talaromyces helicus and Verruconis gallopava were isolated at temperatures of 35–45 °C and can be considered thermophilic and thermotolerant species. Acidomyces acidothermus and Aspergillus sydowii were isolated in high abundance from sulfurous fumaroles with extremely acidic conditions. Microbial diversity analyses show that the richness and abundance of microfungi decrease with increasing temperature, and that physicochemical parameters play an important role in the formation of microfungal communities. Most microfungal cultures isolated isolates from volcanic thermal habitats showed bactericidal activity as well as antagonistic activity against the studied bacteria which deserves attention and further study. The microfungi showed high levels of amylolytic and cellulolytic activity. The ability to produce organic acids and the lignolytic activity was somewhat lower. These results may be useful for assessing the potential of cultured species from volcanic habitats as a source of new strains producing thermostable enzymes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69469-4.title: Age-related changes in left ventricular systolic and diastolic function and their histological and ultrastructural correlates in male WKY rats
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69469-4.abstract: To investigate age-related changes in left ventricular systolic function (assessed by multi-dimensional strain) and diastolic function (assessed by –dP/dt and Tau), and to explore their histological and ultrastructural correlates in male Wistar–Kyoto (WKY) rats. WKY rats were observed from 12 to 102 weeks, including echocardiography, cardiac catheterization, myocardial histology, and ultrastructure. Relative wall thickness increased at 64 weeks, left ventricular mass index and left atrial diameter increased at 72 weeks (all p < 0.05). LVEF kept normal at all weeks. Subendocardial myocardial longitudinal strain (GLS-endo) and LV ± dp/dtmax decreased at 72 weeks and declined with age, Tau increased at 84 and 102 weeks (all p < 0.05). The global collagen volume fractions (CVF) increased at 72 weeks, perivascular collagen area (PVCA) increased significantly until 102 weeks (all p < 0.05). Disorganized myofibrils and localized clustering of mitochondria appeared at 72 weeks. GLS-endo, GRS, and LV-dp/dtmax were negatively correlated with CVF-endo. Tau was positively correlated with CVF and PVCA. Multiple linear regression analysis indicated that GLS-endo and circumferential strain were independently correlated with PVCA. Age-related decline in both systolic and diastolic function are observed in male WKY rats. Systolic dysfunction manifests as reduced subendocardial strain, while diastolic dysfunction manifests as impaired relaxation. These changes likely share a common structural basis of progressive myocardial fibrosis and ultrastructural damage.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67442-9.title: Baseline statin therapy and short-term mortality in acute pulmonary embolism: a multicenter cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67442-9.abstract: Abstract Background Statins exert anti-inflammatory and antithrombotic effects and have been associated with a reduced incidence of venous thromboembolism. Their impact on outcomes following acute pulmonary embolism (PE), however, remains uncertain. Objective To evaluate the association between baseline statin use and short-term mortality in patients with acute PE. Methods We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study of adults with imaging-confirmed PE across National Guard Health Affairs hospitals in Saudi Arabia. Patients were stratified by baseline statin use. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score matching were used to account for confounding. Results Statin users were older and had a higher burden of cardiometabolic comorbidities. Thirty-day mortality was numerically higher among statin users (4.2% vs 2.6%). After adjustment, statin use was associated with higher observed mortality (OR 2.16, 95% CI 1.16–3.94), with consistent findings in propensity-matched analysis. However, substantial baseline differences and residual imbalance suggest the presence of confounding by indication. Conclusions Baseline statin use was not associated with improved short-term outcomes following acute PE. The observed association with higher mortality likely reflects underlying comorbidity burden rather than a causal relationship. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68813-y.title: Graded buried-oxide engineering in vertically stacked SOI–GAA complementary FETs: a broadband DC and noise investigation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68813-y.abstract: Vertically stacked complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) offer a promising route to high-density CMOS scaling beyond the 14 nm node, but their tightly coupled architecture introduces parasitic capacitance, interlayer electrostatic coupling, and trap-assisted conduction that degrade both DC and noise performance. This work proposes and analyses a structurally optimized CFET that integrates a tri-layer multi-κ buried-oxide (BOX) stack composed of 18 nm SiO 2 + 7 nm Si 3 N 4 + 15 nm HfO 2 , evaluated against a baseline CFET without BOX through a self-consistent three-dimensional Synopsys Sentaurus TCAD framework. The device combines a bottom silicon-on-insulator (SOI) nMOS FinFET with a top SiGe (25% Ge) gate-all-around (GAA) pMOS nanosheet transistor sharing a common TiN gate. Hydrodynamic transport with piezo-stress mobility tensors, MLDA quantum corrections, and a complete Green-function diffusion plus flicker/GR noise model with a Gaussian trap distribution are solved over fourteen frequency decades (0.1–10 13 Hz, 3 points/decade). Simulation results show that the multi-κ BOX architecture raises I ON from 102.7 µA/µm to 110.2 µA/µm for the SOI nMOS and from 519.8 µA/µm to 542.3 µA/µm for the GAA pMOS, with OFF-state leakage suppressed by more than three orders of magnitude and I ON /I OFF ratios above 10 14 for the nMOS and approximately 6 × 10 8 for the pMOS. Subthreshold swing remains tightly controlled at 58–64 mV/dec (nMOS) and 68–82 mV/dec (pMOS), while threshold voltages stay balanced at 0.435–0.445 V and − 0.54 to − 0.57 V. Noise simulations predict a reduction in S id (f) for the nMOS and pMOS across the band, terminal noise correlation coefficients reduced into physically benign limits, and a 0.4–0.6 dB (nMOS) and 0.3–0.5 dB (pMOS) decrease in minimum noise figure (NF min ) at 10 GHz, while high-frequency intrinsic transport remains intact. The proposed multi-κ BOX CFET therefore offers a scalable platform for low-power, low-noise, and RF-compatible logic beyond the 14 nm node.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67494-x.title: A comprehensive German claims data analysis of care pathways, risk factors and comorbidities among acetylcholinesterase inhibitor initiators in Alzheimer’s disease
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67494-x.abstract: Early stages of Alzheimer's Disease (AD), commonly referred to as early AD (eAD), represent a critical phase for timely diagnosis and intervention. However, significant gaps remain in understanding real-world care of individuals initiating first-line treatment such as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (AChE-I) in Germany. A retrospective study was conducted using the German InGef claims database with a pragmatic proxy approach, identifying de novo AChE-I initiators as individuals suspected of having eAD. Two cohorts were defined: a pre-cohort (2022) capturing eight-years prior to AChE-I initiation, and a post-cohort (2017), analyzing five-years following initiation. Patients were matched 1:1 to controls without AD based on demographic characteristics. Outcomes included comorbidities, risk factors, diagnostics, prescriptions, and survival. The study identified 1,994 (pre-cohort) and 2,051 (post-cohort) AChE-I initiators, and respective controls. Mobility disorders increased significantly (+ 55%) over the eight years preceding treatment. Eight years pre-initiation, 81.9% of initiators exhibited at least one modifiable risk factor compared to 76.2% in controls (p < 0.001). Advanced diagnostic procedures were underutilized (MRI: 39.0%, cerebrospinal fluid analysis: 9.2%, in year -1). Only 78.6% received an AD-specific diagnosis within the first year post-initiation. Extensive use of psycholeptics and psychoanaleptics was observed, with a notable decline in dementia-specific medications post-initiation. Post-initiation, initiators showed higher comorbidity burden (e.g., urinary incontinence: 40.2% vs. 10.7% by year 5) and higher observed, unadjusted mortality (53.3% vs. 21.7%, p < 0.001). This study highlights patterns suggestive of gaps in the management of AChE-I initiators in Germany, including underutilization of guideline-based diagnostics, high comorbidity burden, and higher observed mortality. Improved management strategies and the development of more precise diagnostic coding that reflects disease stages could help to address these issues.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68162-w.title: Security and usability evaluation of handwritten Arabic CAPTCHA systems based on Saudi calligraphic fonts
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68162-w.abstract: Abstract A Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart (CAPTCHA) is a widely adopted security mechanism used to distinguish human users from automated programs and mitigate cyberattacks. Given the extensive use of the Internet among Arabic speakers, Arabic CAPTCHA systems have attracted increasing research attention in recent years. Prior studies indicate that handwritten text-based CAPTCHAs provide enhanced security compared to their printed counter-parts. This study proposes the development of a handwritten Arabic CAPTCHA generator based on Saudi fonts, aiming to preserve linguistic and cultural identity while achieving a balanced trade-off between security and usability. The proposed framework introduces a structured classification model for Saudi calligraphic fonts and evaluates their effectiveness using both meaningful and meaningless Arabic words. To further enhance robustness against automated attacks, the adversarial perturbation technique Jacobian-based Saliency Map Attack (JSMA) is applied to the generated CAPTCHA samples. Extensive experimental evaluations are conducted to assess security resistance using optical character recognition (OCR)-based attacks, alongside usability testing involving human participants. The results demonstrate that Saudi handwritten calligraphic fonts can significantly improve CAPTCHA robustness while maintaining acceptable usability levels. From a security perspective, it achieves an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) recognition rate of 90%, the human accuracy reaches 88%, and the average solving time is 9.6 s. These findings highlight the potential of culturally grounded handwritten Arabic CAPTCHA systems as effective authentication mechanisms in modern cybersecurity applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66273-y.title: Workplace ostracism and job performance: revisiting the limits of employee engagement in addressing workplace exclusion
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66273-y.abstract: Workplace ostracism represents a subtle but damaging form of workplace exclusion that can weaken employees' psychological functioning and job-related outcomes. Drawing on self-regulation theory (SRT), this study examines the association between workplace ostracism and employee job performance and investigates whether employee engagement moderates this relationship. Data were collected from 477 employees working in IT, banking and insurance, BPO, and supply-chain/service roles and analysed using partial least square structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS 4. The findings show that workplace ostracism is significantly and negatively associated with job performance, whereas employee engagement is significantly and positively associated with job performance. The model explained 24.10% of the variance in job performance. Contrary to the proposed moderation hypothesis, employee engagement did not significantly buffer the negative association between workplace ostracism and job performance. This suggests that engagement may enhance performance directly but may not operate as a sufficient protective condition against the adverse performance-related consequences of workplace exclusion. The study contributes to organizational behavior literature by clarifying the limits of employee engagement as a buffering resource and highlighting the need for organizations to directly address exclusionary workplace practices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68892-x.title: Taguchi-based multi-response optimization of lead flotation from a complex Zn–Pb sulfide ore
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68892-x.abstract: This study presents a systematic statistical optimization framework for improving the selective flotation performance of a complex Zn–Pb sulfide ore by maximizing Pb recovery and concentrate grade while minimizing Zn misplacement. A Taguchi orthogonal array was first employed to efficiently design the experimental matrix, followed by Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) modeling combined with stepwise F-test analysis to quantify the effects and statistical significance of flotation variables. Subsequently, multi-response optimization using the Desirability Function was applied to identify the optimal operating conditions while resolving the inherent grade-recovery trade-off. The optimum conditions corresponding to the maximum global desirability (0.98) were determined as: pH = 11, [ZnSO 4 ] = 500 g/t, [NaCN] = 335 g/t, [PEX] = 30 g/t, and [2-MBT] = 10 g/t. Under these conditions, the developed models predicted a Pb recovery of 88.68%, a Pb concentrate grade of 72.06%, and a minimized Zn content of 2.91% in the concentrate. The statistical analysis further revealed that increasing collector (PEX) and collector-aid (2-MBT) dosages beyond critical levels did not provide significant improvements in flotation performance within the investigated range. This integrated statistical approach not only demonstrates significant improvements over baseline metallurgical performance but also provides a scalable, data-driven blueprint for optimizing complex mineral processing circuits.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69186-y.title: Association between maternal exposure to tobacco smoke and fever frequency in children: results from the Japan Environment and Children’s Study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69186-y.abstract: The effects of tobacco smoke exposure on vulnerable populations, such as pregnant women and children, constitute a major public health concern. However, quantitative data linking tobacco smoke exposure to the frequency of fever is lacking. This study investigated the association between maternal tobacco smoke exposure during pregnancy and the frequency of fever in children aged 0 to 3 years. Data from a birth cohort of 68,242 mothers and their children were analyzed. Maternal smoking history and secondhand smoke exposure were assessed. The mother’s urinary cotinine levels were used as an objective biomarker to classify participants as non-smokers, passive smokers, and active smokers. The analysis revealed significant associations between maternal smoking and secondhand smoke exposure during pregnancy and a modestly increased frequency of fever in children. The children of mothers who smoked or were exposed to secondhand smoke during pregnancy had a modestly increased frequency of fever (risk ratio [RR] = 1.071, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.020–1.126 and RR = 1.087, 95% CI: 1.039–1.135, respectively). Cotinine analysis confirmed these findings; active smoking was associated with fever frequency (RR = 1.082, 95% CI: 1.044–1.122). Overall, maternal tobacco smoke exposure was associated with a modestly increased frequency of fever in children.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66257-y.title: Sustainable powering of data centers: a techno-economic and environmental optimization of renewable hybrid energy system
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66257-y.abstract: Data centers (DCs) are a very energy intensive business and with the rising electricity demand, it is essential to have reliable, cost-effective and eco-friendly power facilities in Pakistan. The use and optimization of hybrid energy systems that utilize renewable energy sources for the Pakistani DCs have been given very little attention. A framework is developed in this research to optimize the integration of hybrid standalone renewable energy systems in 22 DCs in Islamabad, Karachi, and Lahore from techno-economic and environmental perspectives. The optimization results showed that the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of the investigated DCs was in the range of USD 0.108 to 0.123/kWh, which highlighted the economic potential of the proposed systems. Based on the above analysis, it was found that PV-DG- battery systems are optimal in Islamabad and Lahore because of comparatively low wind potential. However, the PV-wind-DG-battery system is optimal for Karachi due to its comparatively high wind potential. The uncertainties of solar irradiance, wind speed, discount rate, and inflation rate were considered in the sensitivity analysis, and environmental analysis was done considering the associated carbon emissions. The outcomes show that hybrid renewable-energy systems can be a technically reliable, economically viable, and environmentally friendly alternative to the conventional diesel-based power supply for data centers in Pakistan depending on their location.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68926-4.title: Microstructure-property correlation in sustainable Al7075-T6 aluminium matrix composites reinforced with nanoscale banana peel ash derived from agro-waste
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68926-4.abstract: Abstract The development of lightweight aluminium matrix composites (AMCs) with improved mechanical performance and reduced environmental impact remains a significant challenge, particularly in replacing conventional ceramic reinforcements with sustainable and low-cost alternatives. This study investigates the potential of nanoscale banana peel ash (nano-BPA), derived from agricultural waste, as a sustainable reinforcement for Al7075-T6 aluminium matrix composites. Banana peels were dehydrated, calcined, and subjected to high-energy ball milling to produce nano-BPA with an average particle size of 20.2 nm. Al7075-T6 composites reinforced with 0, 2, and 4 wt% nano-BPA were fabricated by stir casting. The developed materials were evaluated using particle size analysis, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), tensile testing, and Brinell hardness measurements. The results demonstrate a clear improvement in mechanical performance with increasing nano-BPA content. The ultimate tensile strength increased from 110 MPa for the unreinforced Al7075-T6 alloy to 197.5 MPa for the 4 wt% nano-BPA composite, representing a 79.5% increase. Similarly, Brinell hardness increased from 148 HBW to 173.11 HBW, corresponding to a 17.0% improvement. TGA confirmed the thermal stability of the nano-BPA, while SEM and EDS analyses revealed relatively uniform reinforcement distribution and effective matrix-particle interfacial bonding. Among the investigated compositions, the 4 wt% nano-BPA composite exhibited the highest tensile strength and hardness, together with satisfactory thermal stability and microstructural integrity. These results indicate that nano-BPA can effectively enhance the mechanical performance of Al7075-T6 while simultaneously utilizing agricultural waste as a value-added reinforcement.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69563-7.title: Reference intervals for macular ganglion cell complex parameters using spectral-domain OCT in a healthy persian adult population: a cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69563-7.abstract: To establish reference intervals (RIs) for macular ganglion cell complex (GCC) parameters measured by spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) in a healthy adult population. In this cross-sectional study, healthy participants underwent macular SD-OCT imaging. Reference intervals for GCC-related parameters, including inner retinal thickness, full retinal thickness, outer retinal thickness, asymmetry indices, and loss metrics, were established in accordance with CLSI EP28-A3 guidelines. Reference intervals were calculated using non-parametric rank-based methods or robust parametric approaches with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. A total of 491 participants (mean age 40.62 ± 7.35 years; 218 females and 273 males) were included. Thickness-based GCC parameters demonstrated approximately symmetric distributions with low variability, whereas loss-based indices showed greater dispersion. Pooled reference intervals were appropriate for most GCC parameters. Sex-specific partitioning was required only for outer retinal thickness measures, with males demonstrating slightly higher values than females. Age-based partitioning was generally not required, although selective age dependence was observed for certain loss-related indices. The overall reference interval for inner retinal average thickness was 86.56–108.96 μm, and for outer retinal average thickness 161.68–192.66 μm. This study provides robust, CLSI-compliant reference intervals for GCC parameters measured by spectral-domain OCT in healthy adults. These normative data may serve as a reference framework for future studies investigating GCC alterations in glaucomatous and neuro-ophthalmic diseases and may contribute to the development of population-specific diagnostic and monitoring strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69158-2.title: Learning multiple consistent representation for vehicle re-identification
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69158-2.abstract: This paper addresses the challenges in vehicle re-identification, including high intraclass variance, low interclass variance, lack of fine-grained annotation, and misalignment of feature space. Our research is grounded in deep learning and weakly supervised learning theories, examining these challenges from multiple perspectives. A novel vehicle re-identification framework, the Learning Multiple Consistent Embeddings Network (MCEN), is proposed to address the difficulty of accurately locating and extracting key areas of vehicles, which is a result of limited fine-grained annotations. First, a multi-branch, multi-attention network is constructed, and a part diversity regularization term is introduced to encourage different attention branches to concentrate on deep features with distinct semantic meanings. Next, a part consistency regularization term is introduced to align features extracted by each branch within their respective Euclidean spaces, mitigating inter-class inconsistency and ensuring the alignment of local features. The network is trained in an end-to-end manner. The experimental results show that MCEN outperforms existing methods. In the VeRi-776 dataset, MCEN achieves an 8.3% improvement in mAP and a 3.1% increase in Top-1 accuracy over the PRN model. Unlike traditional feature-based methods and local feature detection approaches, MCEN regularization strategies improve robustness against occlusion and variations in camera angles. Furthermore, in the VehicleID dataset, MCEN shows superior performance in all three subsets (small, medium, and large), surpassing the state-of-the-art methods. These results validate the effectiveness of our proposed model in addressing real-world challenges in vehicle re-identification.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68519-1.title: Factors associated with hyperuricemia in overweight or obese adults of Shenzhen, China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68519-1.abstract: The rising prevalence of hyperuricemia poses health risks and financial burdens, particularly among overweight or obese individuals. This study aimed to identify factors associated with hyperuricemia in overweight or obese adults of Shenzhen, China. This is a population-based cross-sectional study conducted in Longhua District of Shenzhen, China. Overweight or obese individuals were recruited using a multi-stage stratified random sampling method. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify factors associated with hyperuricemia. Totally 662 overweight or obese individuals were included, and the prevalence of hyperuricemia was 43.2% (95% CI: 39.4–47.0%). Multivariable analysis showed that female sex was associated with a lower risk of hyperuricaemia (OR = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.07–0.19). Additionally, exposure to secondhand smoke for more than 3 days per week (OR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.06–2.27) and consumption of more than 75 g of aquatic products per day (OR = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.12–4.73) were associated with a higher risk of hyperuricemia. Sugar-sweetened beverage intake presented a borderline significant association with higher risk of hyperuricemia (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.00–2.11, P = 0.052). The prevalence of hyperuricaemia was high among obese or overweight individuals in Shenzhen, and those with male sex should be given special attention. Secondhand smoke exposure, aquatic products consumption and sugar-sweetened beverage intake may be served as intervention targets to reduce hyperuricemia.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66397-1.title: SGSR: structure-guided semantic recovery for event-based spiking semantic segmentation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66397-1.abstract: Event-based spiking semantic segmentation is well suited to sparse and asynchronous visual sensing, but dense prediction remains challenging because event responses are spatially non-uniform. Object contours and motion boundaries usually generate strong responses, whereas object interiors and regions with weak brightness changes provide limited evidence. This imbalance often results in incomplete semantic regions and inaccurate boundaries. To address this problem, we propose SGSR, a structure-guided spiking framework for event-based semantic segmentation. SGSR employs a multi-scale spiking separable convolution block to capture local structures at different spatial scales with low computational cost. A spiking parallel aggregation pyramid pooling module aggregates high-level context to improve the representation of weakly observed regions. In addition, a lightweight boundary-prior branch extracts boundary cues from intermediate features. The predicted priors are injected into successive decoder stages to guide spatial recovery, rather than being used only for auxiliary supervision. Under the event-only SNN setting, SGSR achieves mIoU scores of $$52.93\%$$ on DDD17-Seg and $$52.45\%$$ on DSEC-Semantic. The results show that SGSR provides competitive segmentation accuracy while maintaining a compact computational profile.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66677-w.title: Risk-aware multiple-choice question answering with conformal P-values
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66677-w.abstract: Multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) systems are often required to act on uncertain evidence while still providing a concise decision to a user. We introduce a risk-aware MCQA interface that converts normalized option probabilities into conformal prediction sets, allowing the system to retain every answer option supported at a user-selected risk level. The option-wise conformal p-value provides an interpretable rank-based view of this decision. Across five instruction-tuned language models and common-question subsets of MMLU and MMLU-Pro, the procedure is evaluated with 100 random 1:1 calibration-test splits at target miscoverage levels [Formula: see text]. At [Formula: see text], mean empirical miscoverage ranges from 0.0390 to 0.0399 on MMLU and from 0.0469 to 0.0487 on MMLU-Pro; the same target-tracking pattern persists at the larger operating points and across diverse subjects. Prediction sets contract smoothly as the allowable risk increases, while the more demanding MMLU-Pro questions retain broader sets. These results position conformal p-values as a practical reliability layer for MCQA systems that must communicate calibrated ambiguity rather than conceal it behind a single top-ranked answer.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66617-8.title: Determinants of pro-environmental behaviors among Iranian High School students using the theory of planned behavior and locus of control
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66617-8.abstract: The environment is one of the key determinants of health and well-being. Humans play a central role in creating, maintaining, and promoting a health-supportive environment. On the other hand, promoting pro-environmental behaviors is one of the fundamental challenges for educational systems in societies. Understanding and analyzing these behaviors based on scientific theories is a crucial step for designing appropriate educational interventions, and schools provide a structured environment for the development and implementation of environmental education. Therefore, this study aimed to identify the determinants of pro-environmental behaviors among Iranian high school students Using the Theory of Planned Behavior and Locus of Control. This analytical cross-sectional study involved 410 middle school students in Shiraz, selected through cluster sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-made questionnaire based on the Theory of Planned Behavior and Locus of Control, with a Cronbach’s alpha above 0.80 and external reliability above 0.75. Data were analyzed using SPSS 27 software, employing Pearson correlation and linear regression tests. The results indicated no significant differences between girls and boys in the constructs of the Theory of Planned Behavior, except for Locus of Control, where boys scored higher (26.17 ± 3.84 vs. 27.04 ± 4.24, p = .030). Pro-environmental behaviors were most strongly correlated with subjective norms ( r = .485, p < .01) and attitudes ( r = .352, p < .01). Multiple regression analysis showed that subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, intention, locus of control, and attitude were the main predictors of behavior, whereas knowledge was not a predictor. Among these predictors, subjective norms (β = 0.341, p < .001) were the strongest predictor of pro-environmental behaviors, followed by perceived behavioral control (β = 0.147, p = .001), intention (β = 0.125, p = .007), locus of control (β = 0.119, p = .005), and attitude (β = 0.097, p = .047), While Knowledge was not a significant predictor of pro-environmental behaviors in the present regression model, pro-environmental behaviors among students were more strongly associated with subjective norms, positive attitudes, and a sense of personal control than with knowledge. Therefore, it is recommended that schools identify and strengthen these determinants before designing educational interventions, to enhance effectiveness and promote sustainable behavioral change.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69029-w.title: Correction: Antidiabetic and antioxidant effects of Armillaria gallica and Armillaria cepistipes extracts and their silver nanoparticles against streptozotocin induced diabetes in mice
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69029-w.abstract: The original version of this Article contained an error in the figure assembly of Figure 14, where panel ‘G-X-A.C (T)’ was incorrect. The underlying experimental data, statistical analysis, interpretation, and conclusions of the article remain unchanged. The original Figure 14 and accompanying legend appear below.
