G: glomerulus; DT: distal tubules; PT: proximal tubules; S: bowman’s space; V: Visceral; P: parital.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69473-8.title: Effect of water on CO2 adsorption and diffusion in low-rank coal nanopores
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69473-8.abstract: In this study, the nanopore structure of low-rank lignite was obtained using scanning electron microscopy, N 2 and CO 2 adsorption methods. Based on these data, the nanopore models of lignite with varying moisture volume fractions were constructed. Then, CO 2 adsorption and diffusion performances on lignite were researched. The findings indicate that moisture is the dominant factor limiting CO 2 storage capacity. Water molecules can preferentially occupy high-energy adsorption centers and form dense water films, creating a significant “shielding effect” that substantially reduces CO 2 adsorption density. With increasing moisture volume fraction, CO 2 interaction energy distribution shifts from a heterogeneous “high-energy long-tail” pattern under dry condition to a homogenized low-energy distribution, accompanied by a marked decrease in thermodynamic stability. As moisture volume fraction enhances, the CO 2 diffusion coefficient shows a non-monotonic variation under the present simulation conditions, which can be attributed to the difference between surface-energy smoothing at low-to-moderate moisture volume fraction s and water-film blocking at high moisture volume fraction moisture volume fraction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69298-5.title: LAG-TabNet: A lightweight attention-gated tabular network for leak-free, interpretable cyberattack detection in internet of health things (IOHT)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69298-5.abstract: The increasing integration of connected medical devices within the Internet of Health Things (IoHT) has intensified the need for intrusion detection systems that combine predictive performance with computational efficiency and interpretability. This study proposes LAG-TabNet, a lightweight attention-gated tabular network designed for cyberattack detection in resource-constrained IoHT environments. Using a leakage-free experimental pipeline, the model was evaluated on the ECU-IoHT dataset across three tasks: multiclass attack classification, packet-length regression, and unsupervised clustering. LAG-TabNet was benchmarked against traditional machine learning, ensemble, distance-based, and deep learning approaches. The proposed model achieved 99.6% classification accuracy, compared with 99.4% for Random Forest and 99.2% for XGBoost, while using only 48,632 trainable parameters. It achieved an R² of 0.974 for packet-length regression, and its learned representations increased clustering adjusted Rand index from 0.79 to 0.87. Attention-derived feature importance strongly correlated with SHAP explanations (Spearman ρ = 0.97), supporting intrinsic interpretability. Ablation and sensitivity analyses further confirmed the contribution and stability of the proposed architecture. Independent retraining on CICIoMT2024 yielded 99.1% accuracy, exceeding Random Forest at 98.9%. Overall, LAG-TabNet provides a promising balance between accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability for IoHT cybersecurity, warranting further validation on representative edge hardware.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68607-2.title: An adaptive hierarchical class-aware deep ensemble strategy for robust brain tumor classification
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68607-2.abstract: Abstract Automated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) classification can support differentiation of brain tumor categories, but conventional ensembles often depend on opaque probability fusion. This study proposes a validation-driven adaptive hierarchical class-aware ensemble that treats VGG19 and Darknet53 as complementary experts. A balanced working set of 7,200 images representing glioma, meningioma, no tumor, and pituitary classes was stratified into training (70%), validation (15%), and independent test (15%) partitions. Training-only enhancement and best-validation-checkpoint retention were used. Validation data alone produced a frozen expert map: Darknet53 was assigned to glioma, meningioma, and no-tumor cases, whereas VGG19 was assigned to pituitary cases. At test time, the router accepted model consensus, consulted the expert map during disagreement, and used confidence only for residual conflicts. On 1,080 unseen test images, the proposed strategy correctly classified 1,060 cases (98.15% accuracy; 98.16% macro precision; 98.15% macro recall; 98.14% macro F1-score). Darknet53 and VGG19 achieved 97.87% and 97.69% accuracy, while weighted soft voting, and stacking each achieved 98.06%. The proposed strategy therefore achieved the strongest benchmark while preserving a transparent, auditable, and leakage-free decision pathway.

doi:10.1038/s41598-025-30434-2.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals members and expression characteristics of innate immunity genes in Chinese scorpion Mesobuthus martensii
doi:10.1038/s41598-025-30434-2.abstract: Humoral immunity is a fundamental component of the innate immune system, and it regulates the expression of key genes through signal transduction and immune pathways, resulting in the production of antimicrobial peptides and other effector molecules. Scorpions, whose fossil records dates back 430 million years, have adapted to moist environments over extensive periods. However, the expression profiles of immune-related genes across their different tissues remain poorly understood. This study identified 52 innate immune genes from 14 tissues, excluding repressors, within the transcriptome of Mesobuthus martensii collected from the Langya Mountain in Baoding using Illumina High-Throughput sequencing technology. Then we identified the transcriptome annotations and validated through online BLAST searches to confirm. We described four primary immune pathways in M. martensii: (I) Toll signaling pathway appeared relatively complete compared with that of Drosophila melanogaster; (II) the upstream components of the IMD pathway were missing and downstream genes were expressed to some extent in different tissues; (III) IMD homologous genes were found in most components of the JNK pathway; (IV) the JAK-STAT pathway had core genes JAK and STAT, but lacked the membrane receptor Dome. In this study, transcriptome analyses of different M. martensii tissues revealed significant variability in immune gene expression, particularly in the blood. The innate immune gene members of scorpions exhibited notable similarities to those found in Tetranychus urticae, Acanthoscurria gomesiana, and Acyrthosiphon pysum, while significantly differing from those of Drosophila melanogaster. These differences might reflect variations in innate immune capabilities influenced by evolutionary processes and behavioral adaptations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68963-z.title: Multi-horizon stock price prediction with an informer-based framework leveraging inter-stock correlations and commodity inputs
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68963-z.abstract: A significant goal of stock price prediction research is to understand the relationships among stocks and how they move over time, enabling better stock price forecasts and portfolio risk assessment. This has the potential to impact asset allocation, price forecasts, and portfolio risk over time through changes in cross-asset movements. In this study, we develop an Informer-based framework to examine how inter-stock relations and exogenous commodity variables support multi-horizon stock price prediction. The proposed approach combines multi-source inputs with a deterministic sinusoidal encoding implemented in the encoder. This combination addresses the difficulty of correctly mapping intricate temporal and cross-asset relationships. The study examines whether time-varying and cross-asset relationships affect the price movements of individual stocks within an index when there is high inter-stock correlation. The framework utilizes both endogenous (historical prices and technical indicators) and exogenous commodity inputs (e.g., crude oil, gold, and silver prices). The experiments evaluated four feature selection approaches, including correlation-based filtering, k-best selection, shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and the full-feature set. Among these feature sets, the SHAP-based feature set achieved the best empirical performance under the evaluated configuration. The proposed model is evaluated using the time-series cross-validation method (k = 3, 5, 7) in four stocks, including INFY, TCS, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank, as well as the NIFTY 50 index. It achieves an average coefficient of determination (R \({^2}\) ) score of 0.987, along with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 3.098%, and a mean absolute scaled error (MASE) of 0.277, showing improved performance over the evaluated baseline models. A comparative ablation study was done comparing the performance of the proposed model against Transformer, Autoformer, and Reformer baselines, to examine the contribution of the proposed framework under the evaluated settings. We further evaluated the proposed framework using a profitability analysis with a rule-based trading simulation under simplified trading assumptions. Finally, two statistical tests, including the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Diebold–Mariano (DM) test, were conducted to statistically compare the proposed model against benchmarks. The results suggest that related stock inputs provide useful information beyond individual stock histories and improve forecasting performance across multiple horizons.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68481-y.title: Bmi1 is a key effect molecule of p27-Shh signal pathway in mouse alveolar bone formation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68481-y.abstract: Abstract Previous studies have suggested that Bmi1 is a positive regulator of osteoblast formation and osteogenesis, while p27 is a negative regulator. Mice lacking p27 display larger mandibles which accompanied with the upregulated Bmi1. To clarify the interaction between p27 and Bmi1 in alveolar bone formation, we compared the mandible phenotypes of homozygous p27-deficient (p27 −/− ) mice, homozygous Bmi1-deficient (Bmi1 −/− ) mice, double homozygous p27 and Bmi1-deficient (p27 −/− Bmi1 −/− ) mice to those of their wild-type (WT) littermates at 4 weeks of age by radiograph, histochemistry and immunohistochemistry. Results showed the mandible mineral density, alveolar bone volume, cortical thickness, osteoblast number and surface, type I collagen positive area were all increased obviously in p27 −/− mice compared to WT mice, which implied p27 deletion activated alveolar bone formation. However, these parameters were decreased significantly in Bmi1 −/− and p27 −/− Bmi1 −/− mice compared to WT mice and similar between Bmi1 −/− and p27 −/− Bmi1 −/− mice. To explain the phenomenon of Bmi1 deficiency blocking p27 deletion induced active alveolar bone formation, Sonic hedgehog N-Terminus Protein (Shh-N) and Shh antagonist KAAD-cyclopamine were treated with the bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) derived from alveolar bone in vitro. Bmi1 deletion blocked the cell proliferation and osteogenic effect of Shh agonist on BMSCs in vitro. In conclusion, this study indicated that Bmi1 was an essential effect molecule of p27-Shh signaling in regulation of alveolar bone formation which provided new evidence on alveolar bone anabolic action.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68896-7.title: Exogenous galectin-1 mitigates inflammation and lipopolysaccharide-induced myocardial injury in experimental sepsis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68896-7.abstract: Myocardial injury is common in sepsis and may be attributed to overwhelming inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Galectin-1 (Gal1) is an immunomodulatory protein, but its role in sepsis-associated cardiac dysfunction remains unclear. We enrolled 125 septic ICU patients, including 34 (27.2%) with initially low cardiac output (CO < 4.0 L/min). Patients with low CO had impaired cardiac contractility, greater disease severity, higher mortality, and higher circulating Gal1 and NT-proBNP concentrations. Experimental sepsis was induced by lipopolysaccharide in male mice. Septic mice developed transient reductions in CO and left ventricular ejection fraction during the first 24 h after LPS injection. Treatment with recombinant Gal1 (rGal1) was associated with attenuated cardiac dysfunction and improved survival in the murine model. In vitro, pre-treatment with rGal1 showed a trend toward reduced inflammatory cytokine production in cultured macrophages and attenuated mitochondrial membrane depolarization in cultured cardiomyocytes. Overall, circulating Gal1 was associated with greater disease severity and mortality in septic patients; whereas rGal1 treatment was associated with improved cardiac function and survival in experimental sepsis. These findings support further investigation of the biological role of Gal1 in sepsis but require validation in additional experimental models and independent clinical studies before any prognostic or therapeutic application can be established.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66920-4.title: Metabolomic and microbiome analysis of Nanmas as a rare Yogurt‑like fermented dairy product with sourdough as a natural starter culture
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66920-4.abstract: Abstract Ancient inhabitants of Zagros used a unique method to produce a fermented dairy product similar to Yogurt (in the local dialect "Nanmas"), in which wheat sourdough served as a starter. This study scientifically investigated this product and compared it with commercial Yogurt. Comprehensive analysis of physicochemical properties, including pH, titratable acidity, and Syneresis; texture profiling; microbial Viability; NMR based metabolomics; microbiome analysis with 16S rDNA sequencing; and sensory evaluation were performed by a trained team. Compared with commercial Yogurt, Nanmas had lower pH, higher titratable acidity, and less syneresis during storage ( P ≥ 0.05). NMR analysis revealed a qualitatively greater diversity and a wider range of desirable metabolites in Nanmas, which also exhibited a denser texture and more complex flavor profile compared to commercial yogurt. Two strains of Pediococcus acidilactici and Pediococcus pentosaceus were confirmed as the dominant flora, which explains the mechanism of action of the traditional process. Sensory analysis showed that Nanmas scored higher in terms of taste, texture and overall acceptability compared to commercial Yogurt. These findings not only confirm the scientific value of this ancient method, but also demonstrate the high potential of wheat sourdough as a natural and efficient industrial starter alternative.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68678-1.title: Damage evolution mechanism and multiscale characterization of expansive soil under unidirectional freeze-thaw cycles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68678-1.abstract: In seasonal frozen regions, expansive soil freezes in winter and thaws in spring from the ground surface downward. The temperature fluctuation triggers severe engineering failures, such as continuous landslides and collapses on road embankments. Conventional laboratory studies typically expose samples directly to cold environments, resulting in freezing from all boundaries, which fails to replicate the vertical temperature gradient in nature. This study investigated the evolution of internal damage in expansive soil under unidirectional freeze-thaw (F-T) cycles from macroscopic, mesoscopic, and microscopic perspectives using deformation monitoring, mercury injection tests (MIP), and computed tomography (CT) tests. The results indicated that the peak vertical deformations for 19.6%, 21.6%, and 23.6% water contents samples were 1.46 mm, 1.70 mm, and 2.25 mm, which eventually stabilized at 0.70 mm, 1.40 mm, and 1.80 mm respectively. Unidirectional F-T cycles caused the most pronounced pore expansion at the 13.5 cm height of the samples, where section porosity increased by 3.57%, 5.34%, and 6.15% after 50 cycles, accompanied by a maximum 10.3% increase in large pores (> 4 μm). The frost heave damage mechanism was divided into three steps. The first step was primarily characterized by original frost heave due to water migration and ice crystallization. The change in the second step can be attributed to particle agglomeration. Finally, the shift in the third step resulted from the dispersion of agglomerates and the development of microfractures. These findings provide vital engineering significance for reducing disasters and ensuring the safety of transportation systems in seasonal frozen regions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67734-0.title: Prevalence, patterns, and predictors of outpatient antibiotic prescribing in Saudi Arabia: an observational study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67734-0.abstract: Inappropriate antibiotic use in outpatient settings is a key driver of antimicrobial resistance globally. In Saudi Arabia, real-world population-level evidence on outpatient antibiotic prescribing remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, describe the prescribing patterns, and identify predictors of outpatient antibiotic prescribing using national electronic prescription data. This retrospective population-based study analyzed outpatient prescriptions issued through the Wasfaty system between January 2023 and December 2024 in Taif and surrounding governorates in the Makkah region. Descriptive analyses characterized prescribing patterns, while temporal trends were assessed using monthly and quarterly aggregation. Logistic regression identified demographic and regional predictors of antibiotic use. Among 731,755 patients, 416,776 (57.0%) received at least one antibiotic during the study period, and 880,064 of 7,351,813 outpatient prescriptions (12.0%) included an antibiotic. Prescribing varied by region, with higher prevalence in Ranyah (74.6%; aOR 2.42, 95% CI 2.38–2.47) and Turubah (70.5%; aOR 1.98, 95% CI 1.93–2.04) compared with Taif. Toddlers (64.1%; aOR 1.45, 95% CI 1.42–1.47) and school-age children (65.4%; aOR 1.56, 95% CI 1.54–1.57) had the highest odds, while infants (aOR 0.51, 95% CI 0.50–0.52) and elderly patients (aOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.70–0.73) had lower odds. Amoxicillin, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, and azithromycin accounted for 75.3% of prescriptions. Prescribing peaked during the first and fourth quarters. Outpatient antibiotic use remains substantial in Saudi Arabia, with marked demographic, geographic, and seasonal variation. These findings highlight priority areas for targeted antimicrobial stewardship and demonstrate the value of national electronic prescribing data for surveillance and policy planning.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68483-w.title: Mechanochemical valorization of grape vinegar pulp into functional activated carbon for efficiency removal of malachite green and Hg(II) from water
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68483-w.abstract: Industrial effluents containing synthetic dyes and toxic metal ions pose persistent risks to aquatic ecosystems and human health. Herein, grape vinegar pulp, an agro-industrial residue, was valorized into mechanochemically activated carbon (aGVP) through H₃PO₄-assisted activation, N₂-assisted carbonization, and high-energy ball milling for the removal of malachite green (MG) dye and Hg(II) ions from water. FTIR, BET, SEM, and pH pzc analyses revealed a porous carbonaceous structure enriched with oxygen-containing functional groups and a pH pzc of approximately 4.06. Batch experiments demonstrated strong dependence of adsorption on solution pH, adsorbent dosage, initial concentration, contact time, and temperature, with rapid uptake and near-equilibrium attained within 90 min. Adsorption kinetics were best described by the pseudo-second-order model (R² = 0.995–0.999). Equilibrium data were better represented by Freundlich model for both pollutants, supporting adsorption on energetically heterogeneous surface sites. The Langmuir model estimated maximum adsorption capacities of 107.76 mg g⁻¹ for MG and 1244.17 mg g⁻¹ for Hg(II), though depicting low correlation coefficient values. Thermodynamic analyses confirmed that the adsorption processes were spontaneous and endothermic. Process optimization using Central Composite Design-based Response Surface Methodology predicted maximum removal efficiencies of 97.26% for MG and 96.10% for Hg(II), closely agreeing with experimental validation. Despite the relatively low BET surface area, aGVP exhibited high removal performance attributed to oxygen-rich surface functionalities, favorable adsorbate–surface interactions, and enhanced pore accessibility. This work presents a cost-effective waste-to-resource approach for producing multifunctional biomass-derived adsorbents with significant potential for sustainable wastewater treatment and circular bioeconomy applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68328-6.title: Slope reliability analysis of tailings dam under coincidence of rainfall and pseudo-static motions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68328-6.abstract: Tailings dam failures pose catastrophic risks to downstream communities and ecosystems, yet conventional stability assessments rarely account for the coincident effects of rainfall and pseudo-static motions or the spatial variability of soil properties. This study proposes a reliability analysis framework integrating unsaturated seepage simulation, random field modeling, and an XGBoost surrogate model to evaluate transient factor of safety (FoS) and failure probability under coupled hazards. A tailings dam case study shows that the timing of minimum FoS under advanced rainfall shifts from rainfall cessation to during-rainfall when cumulative rainfall exceeds 100 mm. Neither moderate rainfall (40 mm) nor pseudo-static action ( k h =0.05) alone induces instability, but their concurrency drives the dam to a critical state. Incorporating horizontal pseudo-static force uncertainty increases failure probability by up to 2 orders of magnitude under 40 mm rainfall. Beyond conventional wisdom, our results identify a 100-mm rainfall threshold governing peak risk timing under advanced rainfall patterns, and quantify the significant failure probability amplification driven by pseudo-static uncertainty. The XGBoost surrogate model achieves a validation R 2 of 0.78 for FoS prediction and ~ 95% computational savings versus traditional Monte Carlo simulation, providing a robust, generalizable tool for reliability assessment of tailings dams and other geotechnical systems under compound hazards.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68180-8.title: Probabilistic multiplication operation via chaotic polarity switching in a single magnetic vortex
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68180-8.abstract: We propose a vortex-state nanomagnetic device that generates tunable, chaos-derived probabilistic bitstreams by encoding vortex-core polarity dwell times. By applying oscillating magnetic fields, the vortex enters a chaotic regime, enabling controllable bitstream probability through a single digital threshold parameter T . Using this output, we implement probabilistic multiplication of two fractional numbers via simple down-counting logic. Unlike conventional digital multipliers that require cascaded logic gates for fractional operations, our approach performs probability-domain fractional multiplication with minimal hardware. This compact, CMOS-compatible architecture provides a proof-of-concept route toward stochastic, neuromorphic, and in-memory computing. The present work demonstrates both highly irregular vortex-polarity switching and a compact single-oscillator stochastic arithmetic primitive.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68502-w.title: Using the clean portion of a CHIRP pulse to determine the time of arrival of a hydroacoustic signal under strong reflection conditions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68502-w.abstract: Determining the time of arrival of a hydroacoustic signal is one of the fundamental problems in positioning systems that use propagation-time measurements, especially solutions based on Time of Arrival (ToA) and Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA). Under strong multipath conditions, estimation accuracy deteriorates because the direct signal overlaps with reflected waves. This study evaluates whether restricting the analysis to the initial, least distorted part of a CHIRP pulse can improve time-of-arrival determination. Experiments were conducted in a laboratory swimming-pool environment for ranges of 2 m and 4 m using 30–25 kHz CHIRP signals with durations of 1, 2, 5 and 10 ms and GNSS PPS synchronization. The analysis showed that the influence of reflections on the received-signal structure increases with pulse duration, and that for longer pulses the overlap between reflected waves and the direct signal becomes increasingly evident. The proposed approach, based on using the clean part of the pulse, substantially improved time-of-arrival accuracy. In representative configurations, the mean absolute error was reduced from 20.7 to 2.7 \(\mu \) s and from 175.6 to 3.1 \(\mu \) s, while maintaining 100% correct detections within a \(\pm 20\,\mu \) s tolerance. For a range of 4 m and a 2 ms pulse, the mean absolute error was 1.7 \(\mu \) s, also with 100% correct detections. The results confirm that using the initial, weakly distorted signal fragment can significantly increase the stability and accuracy of time-of-arrival estimation in strongly reflective environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69496-1.title: A bilayer model for magnetic stimulation of neural tissue using a micro dual-coil system
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69496-1.abstract: The bilayer model (BM) represents neural tissue locally as a two-layer structure (conductive electrolyte and low-conductivity membrane). An admittance lattice derived based on pseudo-3D BM model from a mesoscopic image of the neural structure which is digitized using image processing methods is used to discretize and solve Maxwell’s equations for induced current density. The orientation of this induced current can be aligned with the axon axis by adjusting the phase and amplitude of the magnetic field’s x- and y-components. A micro dual-coil system with 180° phase shift generates a stronger and almost more uniform magnetic field than a micro single coil or an in-phase micro dual-coil system.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66897-0.title: Meta-domain adaptive framework for efficient diagnostic assessment of lung infection using CT radiographs
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66897-0.abstract: Abstract Computed Tomography (CT) scans are widely used to diagnose lung infections; however, manual interpretation is labor-intensive. Artificial intelligence has accelerated the development of computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) systems, allowing faster and more accurate diagnosis. Nevertheless, many existing CAD systems lack robust cross-dataset generalization and interpretability, limiting their reliability and resulting in suboptimal diagnostic performance. To address these limitations, we propose a semantic attention-driven retrieval framework based on a lightweight Meta-Domain Adaptive Segmentation Network (MDA-SN) with an adaptive data normalization strategy to enhance infection detection in cross-dataset analysis. This framework quantifies infection ratios and retrieves relevant CT slices from the database, closely matching the input test sample to further support medical experts in making more accurate diagnostic decisions. The MDA-SN design leverages multi-scale dilated grouped convolution with residual attention to ensure real-time performance while maintaining accuracy. Our framework achieved an average cross-dataset performance of 75.93% Dice index and 67.42% Intersection over Union, surpassing state-of-the-art methods by 3.32% and 3.28%, respectively. Additionally, it achieves real-time execution, processing an average of 29 slices per second, due to its significantly reduced number of training parameters, approximately 70% fewer than its closest competitor. The implementation and materials are available at our GitHub repository: https://github.com/Owais-CodeHub/MDA-SN .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68856-1.title: Prevalence and predictors of unhealthy weight control practices among postpartum women attending public health facilities in Southwest Ethiopia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68856-1.abstract: Unhealthy weight control practices (UWCPs), such as fasting, meal skipping, and the use of diet pills, are increasingly prevalent among postpartum women, even in low- and middle-income countries like Ethiopia. These behaviours, fuelled by body image dissatisfaction, media influence, and societal pressure, pose considerable health risks to both the mother and the child. Despite growing evidence from high-income settings, data on the prevalence and predictors of UWCPs among Ethiopian postpartum women remain scarce, hindering the development of targeted interventions in postnatal care. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence and predictors of unhealthy weight control practices among postpartum women attending public health facilities in Southwest Ethiopia. A facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted from 1 May to 30 June 2025. The calculated sample size was 332 postpartum women (6–9 months post-delivery) attending selected public health facilities; 320 women completed the interview (response rate 96.4%). Participants were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected through interviewer-administered structured and semi-structured questionnaires and anthropometric measurements. Descriptive statistics and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify predictors of unhealthy weight control practices (UWCP). The prevalence of unhealthy weight control practices was 41.0% (95% CI: 35.6–46.4%). Factors independently associated with UWCP in the multivariate analysis included body image dissatisfaction (AOR = 4.50; 95% CI: 2.40–8.40), social pressure (AOR = 3.20; 95% CI: 1.70–6.00), media influence (AOR = 2.30; 95% CI: 1.20–4.30), primiparity (AOR = 2.65; 95% CI: 1.40–5.00), low household income (AOR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.18–3.75), unplanned pregnancy (AOR = 2.20; 95% CI: 1.10–4.30), non-exclusive breastfeeding (AOR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.10–4.00), and lack of counselling (AOR = 2.40; 95% CI: 1.30–4.30). A substantial proportion of postpartum women engaged in unhealthy weight control practices, influenced by psychosocial, economic, and reproductive factors. There is an urgent need for targeted interventions, including integration of weight management counselling into routine postnatal care, promotion of exclusive breastfeeding, and addressing media and societal pressures.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69258-z.title: Association between maternal periodontitis and fetal growth restriction among singleton pregnant women at a tertiary care hospital in Karachi – cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69258-z.abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a serious concern for newborn health, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where the health of mothers often does not receive adequate attention. Recent studies have shown that maternal periodontitis, a common gum disease, can negatively impact pregnancy outcomes and may play a role in the development of FGR. This analytical cross-sectional study examined the relationship between maternal periodontitis and FGR among 136 pregnant women at ≥ 32 weeks of gestation, utilizing clinical dental exams and the Delphi Consensus criteria, with Firth logistic regression used to estimate odds ratios. Results showed that women with periodontitis had 4.12 times higher odds of FGR compared to those without (POR = 4.12; p < 0.05). Additionally, gestational diabetes mellitus was associated with a lower likelihood of FGR (POR = 0.08; p = 0.01), and lower maternal education increased the risk of FGR (6.96-fold higher odds; p < 0.01). These findings highlight the importance of integrating oral health assessment and management into routine preconception and antenatal care. Early identification and treatment of periodontal disease can reduce adverse pregnancy outcomes and enhance maternal and fetal health. Preventive oral health strategies should be prioritized for all women of reproductive age to promote healthier pregnancies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68429-2.title: The relationship of quantity and quality of carbohydrate intakes with sleep quality: a cross sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68429-2.abstract: Sleep quality is crucial for daily functioning and health, and diet, particularly carbohydrate (CHO) intake, is a modifiable influence. Existing research on CHO and sleep is limited and often contradictory. This study investigated the association between carbohydrate quality/quantity and sleep quality. A cross-sectional study included 1904 participants. Food intake was assessed using a 106-item semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ), capturing percentage of energy intake from CHO, total dietary fiber, Dietary Glycemic Index (DGI), Dietary Glycemic Load (DGL), whole grain/total grain intake, and fiber/total CHO intake. Sleep quality was evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Binary and ordinal regression analyses were performed. The population (45% male) had a mean age of 39.63 ± 10.24 years and BMI of 27.08 ± 4.91 kg/m 2 . Higher fiber intake was associated with better overall sleep quality (e.g., third tertile vs. first: 35% lower odds of bad overall sleep quality; 95% CI: 0.47–0.91), subjective sleep quality, and reduced sleep onset latency. Higher fiber/total CHO intake correlated with better subjective sleep quality. Increased percentage of energy intake from CHO was linked to reduced sleep medication. Conversely, higher DGL was associated with increased odds of daytime dysfunction. Both quantity and quality of carbohydrate intake significantly relate to sleep quality. Higher dietary fiber intake is linked to some better sleep outcomes, higher DGL may impair daytime function and lower sleep medication usage associate to higher CHO intake. While our findings reveal significant associations, the cross-sectional design precludes conclusions regarding causality, necessitating longitudinal or interventional studies for definitive insights.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69684-z.title: A neuromarketing recommender based on EEG sensing and LSTM with attention
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69684-z.abstract: Conventional EEG-based recommendation systems, such as those employing standard LSTM, bidirectional LSTM, or attention-augmented LSTM, have demonstrated potential in decoding consumer preferences. However, these models often fail to account for irregular temporal intervals between decision-making events and tend to underutilize critical neural dynamics, leading to suboptimal performance in neuromarketing applications where timing and cognitive state transitions are pivotal. To address these limitations, we propose a distributed attention-aware long short-term memory (ataLSTM) framework designed for EEG-driven recommendation systems. This approach explicitly models temporal irregularities and leverages a distributed attention mechanism to prioritize EEG features most predictive of consumer “like” or “dislike” responses. Evaluated on an open-access neuromarketing dataset of EEG recordings from neurologically healthy adults (aged 18–38) using the 14-channel EMOTIV EPOC + headset (configured according to the 10–20 system), the framework analyzed brain activity during real-time assessments of 14 consumer product categories. Through a robust evaluation protocol employing stratified 10-fold cross-validation with five repeated runs, ataLSTM achieved a classification accuracy of 92.42%, surpassing LSTM, biLSTM, and attention-enhanced LSTM baselines by an average of 3.2% across categories. Optimal performance was observed with the 10–20-window configuration and 30% overlap, highlighting the model’s ability to capture nuanced neural variations. The distributed attention mechanism significantly reduced false negatives and enhanced preference discrimination. By embedding cognitive-state modeling into the recommendation pipeline, ataLSTM enables precise, real-time personalization of product suggestions, thereby improving targeted advertising, cross-selling, and customer conversion rates. This work establishes a new standard for brain–computer interface applications in consumer analytics, bridging neuromarketing research and practical recommender systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69021-4.title: Variable performance of HSV-2 IgG assays highlights the importance of western blot confirmation in a low-prevalence population
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69021-4.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) is a highly prevalent sexually transmitted infection, underscoring the importance of accurate serodiagnosis. While enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) are commonly used clinically, their diagnostic performance compared to gold standard western blot (WB) remains uncertain. To compare the diagnostic accuracy of two ELISA-based assays, HerpeSelect 2 and NovaLisa, with the Euroimmun HSV-2 WB assay for the detection of HSV-2-specific IgG antibodies. Four hundred serum samples from adult males residing in Qatar were analyzed. Diagnostic metrics including sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), overall accuracy, and Cohen’s kappa coefficient were calculated for each ELISA assay relative to the Euroimmun HSV-2 WB assay. HerpeSelect had a sensitivity of 78.8%, specificity of 78.3%, PPV of 25.7%, NPV of 97.5%, and fair agreement with WB (Cohen’s kappa = 0.296). NovaLisa performed less well, with a sensitivity of 69.7%, specificity of 66.9%, PPV of 18.3%, NPV of 95.4%, and poor agreement with WB (Cohen’s kappa = 0.162). Both assays significantly overestimated HSV-2 seropositivity compared with WB (HerpeSelect: 26.8%, NovaLisa: 33.5%, WB: 8.3%). A high proportion of false positives was observed for both ELISA assays. Although HerpeSelect demonstrated stronger agreement with the Euroimmun HSV-2 WB reference assay compared with NovaLisa, both ELISA-based assays exhibited low PPVs and high false-positive rates in this low prevalence population. These findings support the need for confirmatory testing or the adoption of automated chemiluminescent immunoassay platforms to enhance diagnostic accuracy for HSV-2.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68743-9.title: Field experimental study on optimal compaction parameters for vibratory compaction of soil–sandstone mixtures
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68743-9.abstract: Reliable selection of field compaction parameters is essential for improving the compaction quality and construction efficiency of soil–sandstone mixture subgrades. In this study, field rolling tests were conducted at the Tongzi Expressway site to evaluate the effects of loose lift thickness and rolling speed on vibratory compaction performance. The tested variables included loose lift thicknesses of 30, 40, and 50 cm, rolling speeds of 3 and 4 km/h, low- and high-amplitude vibration modes, and one to four roller passes. Acceleration sensors installed in the fill and on the roller drum were used to collect dynamic responses, while the sand-cone method was used to determine the degree of compaction. The relationship between the Compaction Meter Value (CMV) and conventional compaction indicators was also analyzed. The results show that, within the tested material, equipment, and parameter ranges, a 50 cm loose lift thickness combined with a rolling speed of 3 km/h produced comparatively favorable compaction performance. The average degree of compaction reached approximately 94% under low-amplitude vibration and 95% under high-amplitude vibration. The variation in CMV was generally consistent with that in the measured degree of compaction, suggesting that CMV can serve as a continuous monitoring indicator for field compaction quality control and parameter adjustment under the tested conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68692-3.title: CD44 variant 9 expression in M2 macrophages enhances gastric cancer progression by modulating the tumor microenvironment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68692-3.abstract: M2 macrophages constitute a major stromal component of gastric cancer (GC) and actively contribute to tumor progression through angiogenesis, tissue remodeling, and epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT). Our previous study identified CD44 variant 9 (CD44v9) expression in cytokeratin-negative stromal compartments as a marker with diagnostic and prognostic significance in gastric adenocarcinoma (GA); however, its cellular localization within the tumor microenvironment and functional relevance remain unclear. In this study, public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from the Human Protein Atlas were analyzed to characterize CD44 expression across gastric tissue cell populations. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to validate the spatial distribution of CD44v9-positive cells in clinical GA specimens. CD44v9 expression was predominantly enriched in macrophages and showed significant co-localization with stromal M1 macrophages (CD68 + CD86 + CD163 − ), M2 macrophages (CD68 + CD86 − CD163 + ), and regulatory T (Treg) cells (CD3 + CD4 + FOXP3 + CD8 − ). Functionally, CD44v9 was overexpressed in THP-1-derived M2 macrophages through lentiviral transduction, and these modified cells retained their inherent M2 macrophage phenotype. CD44v9 overexpression significantly enhanced TNF-α secretion ( P < 0.05), without affecting IL-6 production ( P > 0.05). In a co-culture system, CD44v9 overexpression M2 macrophages markedly promoted GC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. These pro-tumorigenic effects were accompanied by EMT induction, characterized by decreased E-cadherin and increased N-cadherin and Vimentin (all P < 0.05) expression, along with elevated MMP2 and MMP9 ( P < 0.05) levels in AGS cells. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that CD44v9 expression in stromal M2 macrophages promotes a pro-tumorigenic phenotype, possibly through TNF-α-mediated tumor-stroma crosstalk, thereby promoting EMT and enhancing cancer cell aggressiveness. CD44v9 expressed by M2 macrophages may represent a promising biomarker and therapeutic target in GA development.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68890-z.title: CeO-CuInS2 nanocomposite as an efficient absorber layer for high-performance thin film solar cells: structural, optical, and photovoltaic investigation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68890-z.abstract: The relatively low photovoltaic efficiency of CuInS 2 absorber layers, caused by severe charge-carrier recombination and inefficient interfacial charge transport, remains a major challenge for thin-film solar cells. In this work, a CeO–CuInS 2 heterostructure absorber was synthesized via a hydrothermal approach to enhance charge separation and carrier transport. X-ray diffraction confirmed the coexistence of tetragonal CuInS 2 and cubic CeO phases with high crystallinity and an average crystallite size of 34.8 nm. Raman spectroscopy verified structural integrity through characteristic A 1 and F 2 g vibrational modes, while SEM revealed a porous cauliflower-like morphology favorable for light harvesting. HR-TEM analysis demonstrated well-defined lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 3.217 Å, indicating excellent crystallinity. Optical investigations showed a red-shifted absorption edge and a reduced bandgap from 2.22 to 2.09 eV, enhancing visible-light absorption. Photoluminescence measurements evidenced suppressed electron–hole recombination owing to efficient interfacial charge separation. The fabricated FTO/TiO 2 /CeO–CuInS 2 /Spiro-OMeTAD/Au device achieved a V oc of 0.733 V, J sc of 13.82 mA cm −2 , FF of 0.62, and PCE of 6.29%, outperforming pristine CuInS 2 . EIS and EQE analyses further confirmed reduced charge-transfer resistance, suppressed recombination, and enhanced carrier collection efficiency. These findings demonstrate that CeO incorporation is an effective strategy for improving CuInS 2 -based absorber layers for high-performance thin-film solar cells.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69082-5.title: RBDYOLO improves small object detection in low altitude remote sensing imagery
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69082-5.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery at low altitude is increasingly used for traffic oversight, infrastructure inspection, and emergency awareness, yet bird's-eye views exhibit pronounced scale diversity, minute object footprints, and cluttered backgrounds. Default YOLO-style single-stage detectors on a P3-P5 pyramid can therefore suffer coupled cross-scale misalignment and within-scale receptive-field mismatch, increasing misses and unstable calibration on tiny instances. Built on the Ultralytics YOLO11 macro graph and training recipe for strict comparability, RBD-YOLO addresses these bottlenecks with three coordinated methods: (R) within-scale adaptive receptive-field reweighting, (B) learnable cross-scale weighted fusion, and (D) scale-space-task joint dynamic calibration. Under one unified protocol, with VisDrone-DET validation as the primary benchmark and UAVDT as an auxiliary cross-dataset check, RBD-YOLO achieves 49.6% precision, 39.4% recall, and 40.1% mAP@0.5 on VisDrone, outperforming the same-series YOLOv11n baseline (44.4%, 33.2%, 33.1%) and remaining ahead of newly added larger-scale YOLO-family comparisons in mAP@0.5. On UAVDT, it reaches 98.2% mAP@0.5 and 95.4% recall, indicating competitive cross-dataset behavior on a nearly saturated vehicle-centric benchmark. Ablations attribute decomposable gains to methods B and R, a dominant increment from widening fusion bandwidth, and further refinement from method D once cross-scale capacity is sufficient; at 640 × 640 the full model uses about 3.47 M parameters and 16.4 GFLOPs, yielding an interpretable accuracy-complexity trade-off for VisDrone-like aerial small-object detection.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67573-z.title: Epidemiological and entomological assessment of persistent onchocerciasis transmission after long-term ivermectin treatment in communities along the Kéllé river, Cameroon
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67573-z.abstract: Despite two decades of annual Community-Directed Treatment with Ivermectin (CDTI) in the Eséka health district, onchocerciasis transmission persists in frontline villages along the Kéllé River. This study assessed the current epidemiological and entomological status to guide elimination strategies. We conducted cross-sectional clinical and parasitological surveys in two first-line villages (Pouth-Kéllé and Mapan) during June and July 2021. Skin snips were examined for Onchocerca volvulus microfilariae, and clinical manifestations were assessed. Monthly blackfly collections by human landing catches (HLC) were performed at four river sites over one year. Flies were dissected to detect O. volvulus larvae. Microfilarial prevalence was 18.7% (14/75) in Pouth-Kéllé and 15.6% (5/32) in Mapan. Palpable nodules were found in 10% and 6.3% of adults, respectively, reflecting chronic lesions despite recent ivermectin distribution. Reduced visual acuity was frequent (46.7% in Pouth-Kéllé, 47% in Mapan) and was significantly associated with microfilarial positivity in Pouth-Kéllé ( p = 0.04). Entomological surveys yielded a total of 9,163 blackflies collected across the four capture sites, of which 6,036 were dissected to detect O. volvulus larvae. Analysis of biting rates showed that collected point I (P1) exhibited the highest annual biting rate (40,500 bites/person/year), with marked seasonality peaking in April. Transmission risk persisted at collected point II (P2 –annual transmission potential: 14.3 infective larvae/person/year) and collected point IV (P4 − 10.0 infective larvae/person/year). Onchocerciasis transmission remains active in the Kéllé River basin despite two decades of ivermectin treatment. These findings support the urgent need for complementary and/or alternative strategies to achieve elimination of onchocerciasis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67906-y.title: Collaborative innovation in biological breeding for wheat leaf rust resistance: a tripartite evolutionary game analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67906-y.abstract: Key common agricultural technologies are the core driving force for upgrading the agricultural industrial chain. This paper takes the development of biological breeding technology for wheat leaf rust resistance as a scenario, constructs a tripartite evolutionary game model involving the government, wheat breeding enterprises, and agricultural and forestry universities, and introduces factors such as the success probability of technology, technology spillover coefficient, and revenue distribution ratio. Through replicator dynamic equations and numerical simulation, it analyzes the evolutionary stable strategies of the collaborative innovation system and their influencing mechanisms. The research results show that: (1) The government’s social benefits and support costs are the key threshold factors affecting the government’s strategy choice; the government’s active support strategy is sustainable and effectively transmitted to wheat breeding enterprises and agricultural and forestry universities. (2) The participation willingness of wheat breeding enterprises is significantly constrained by the research and development costs of biological breeding technology for wheat leaf rust resistance and the losses from technological failure. (3) The willingness of agricultural and forestry universities to deeply cooperate is comprehensively influenced by multiple factors such as financial support for biological breeding technology for wheat leaf rust resistance, revenue from achievements, academic reputation, and the collaborative demands of wheat breeding enterprises. (4) The revenue distribution mechanism has a significant regulatory effect on the system’s evolution. The revenue distribution ratio for wheat breeding enterprises has a positive incentive effect on their participation willingness, while the regulatory role of the revenue distribution ratio for agricultural and forestry universities needs to be coordinated with government investment and the participation of wheat breeding enterprises in collaboration. The findings clarify how public value, technical risk, spillovers, and benefit allocation jointly shape collaborative breeding and provide a basis for staged support, risk-sharing, and benefit-allocation mechanisms.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68420-x.title: H2, CO2, 222Rn, and Hg degassing from soil gas after a strong earthquake with implications for concealed fault detection in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68420-x.abstract: Subsurface fault structures are generally difficult to delineate, particularly in areas covered by thick sediments. Soil-gas geochemical surveys can provide useful constraints on concealed structures after major earthquakes and complement conventional geophysical methods in sediment-covered basins. This study investigates the 2023 Jishishan M 6.2 earthquake as a representative case. Previous studies have suggested that the nearby Lajishan fault alone cannot fully account for the seismogenic structure of this earthquake, while no obvious surface rupture has been identified within the epicentral basin, complicating post-earthquake reconstruction planning and fault-avoidance measures. The spatial distribution of coseismic damage suggests the possible presence of previously unrecognized concealed structures. To investigate post-seismic soil-gas degassing and its spatial relationship with these structures, we measured Rn, Hg, H 2 , and CO 2 along two profiles across the severely damaged area. Two prominent gas-anomaly zones were identified and showed spatial correspondence with the inferred concealed structures. Integration of the soil-gas anomalies with aftershock relocation, shallow seismic reflection, and ambient-noise surface-wave tomography provides preliminary constraints on the location and geometry of a concealed active structure spatially associated with the broader seismogenic fault system. Hg and H 2 anomalies were more closely associated with the inferred major structural zone than those of Rn and CO 2 , suggesting that their distributions may be preferentially influenced by permeable fault-related pathways. These findings provide new constraints on concealed active structures associated with the Jishishan earthquake sequence and highlight the potential value of integrating soil-gas geochemistry with geophysical observations as a complementary approach for post-earthquake concealed-fault investigation in sediment-covered basins.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61205-2.title: Novel antimicrobial peptides derived from Brevibacillus laterosporus DSM 25 targeting MurT ligase exhibit broad-spectrum activity against drug-resistant pathogens
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61205-2.abstract: The rapid rise of multidrug-resistant pathogens, poses a serious global threat, highlighting the need for new antimicrobial solutions. In this context, antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have emerged as strong therapeutic candidates. Among potential targets, the MurT ligase, an ATP-dependent and highly conserved enzyme in Gram-positive bacteria that supports cell-wall stability and resistance towards antibiotics, stands out as an attractive yet underexplored candidate for anti-Gram-positive drug development. In this study, we predicted 100 potential AMPs from Brevibacillus laterosporus DSM 25 proteome, most of which possessed desirable AMP features such as cationicity, hydrophobicity, and non-toxicity. Docking and simulation analysis identified two peptides, BLA4 and BLA60, as the most stable and strong binders to MurT compared with its native ligand over 200 ns. Helical wheel projection analysis revealed a distinct amphipathic nature in both peptides, suggesting favorable membrane-penetration properties, which were subsequently validated through in vitro antibacterial assays. Both AMPs demonstrated potential antibacterial activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations of 32 µg/mL against the drug-resistant Gram-positive MRSA strain and 64 µg/mL against the Gram-negative Klebsiella quasipneumoniae. Notably, time-kill kinetics displayed BLA60 as faster bactericidal in nature compared to BLA4. SEM analysis revealed peptide-induced membrane perforation and structural degradation in bacterial cells. Further in vitro and in vivo validation of these novel AMPs may support their potential as promising candidates and structural templates for broad-spectrum antibacterial drug development.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68745-7.title: Email spam detection using gated recurrent unit (GRU) optimized by improved triangulation topology aggregation optimizer (ITTAO)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68745-7.abstract: Email spam detection is essential for preserving the security and integrity of digital communication systems by eliminating potentially dangerous and unwanted messages. This research investigates the effectiveness of advanced machine learning methods, with particular emphasis on a gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural network optimized using the improved triangulation topology aggregation optimizer (ITTAO). Through a thorough preprocessing approach, including stop word removal, normalization, lemmatization, and stemming, combined with the Bag of Words (BoW) model, the proposed system significantly enhanced email content classification. When the proposed model was evaluated on established datasets, such as Ling-Spam, the SMS Spam Collection v.1, and Enron, the model demonstrated remarkable precision, recall, and F1-score values of 96.87%, 96.98%, and 96.92%, respectively. The findings indicated that the proposed GRU-ITTAO model surpassed traditional algorithms and other neural network architectures, including GRU, Long Short‑Term Memory (LSTM), and Bidirectional Long Short‑Term Memory (BiLSTM). This study emphasized the potential of deep learning methods and machine learning in improving spam detection systems and pointed out that the model was capable of identifying the majority of spam emails.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66048-5.title: Long-term stability of GMP cryopreserved mesenchymal stromal cells after 10 years of storage
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66048-5.abstract: Abstract Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are multipotent progenitors with regenerative, paracrine, and immunomodulatory properties widely investigated for clinical applications. For therapeutic use, MSCs must be manufactured under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) conditions and cryopreserved to ensure product availability and reproducibility, yet evidence on their long-term stability remains limited. In this study, bone marrow-derived MSCs (BM-MSCs) expanded under GMP conditions and cryopreserved for more than ten years were evaluated for post-thaw viability, phenotypic identity, differentiation capacity, karyotype stability, and immunomodulatory function. Two reconstitution media, human platelet lysate (HPL) and Gelofusine, were compared. After a mean storage period of 13.2 years, thawed BM-MSCs retained high viability (80–86%), normal karyotype, proliferative recovery after an initial adaptation phase, full compliance with ISCT criteria, and preserved osteogenic, adipogenic, and chondrogenic differentiation. HPL and Gelofusine showed comparable performance in post-thaw recovery, adhesion, and expansion. Functional assays further showed that MSC-derived secretome consistently reduced absolute lymphocyte number and attenuated phytohemagglutinin-induced T-cell expansion, with a more evident effect on CD8⁺ populations. Given the limited number of biological replicates, immunomodulatory data were analyzed descriptively. These findings support the feasibility of long-term GMP biobanking and the use of cryostored MSCs as reliable sources of both viable therapeutic cells and biologically active secretome.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68503-9.title: Age and seasonal patterns of respiratory pathogens and their codetections revealed by multiplex PCR
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68503-9.abstract: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) remain a major cause of morbidity worldwide owing to their diverse etiologies and overlapping clinical presentations. Multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) enables simultaneous detection of multiple respiratory pathogens and provides comprehensive epidemiological data. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, alterations in respiratory pathogen circulation and increasing recognition of viral–bacterial co-detection have highlighted the need for updated molecular epidemiological surveillance. This retrospective cross-sectional study included consecutive nasopharyngeal swab specimens obtained from patients with clinically suspected RTIs who underwent multiplex RT-qPCR testing at Siirt Training and Research Hospital, Türkiye, between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were stratified into predefined age groups. Positive specimens were classified into mutually exclusive viral-only, bacterial-only, and viral–bacterial co-detection categories. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent factors associated with respiratory pathogen detection. Among 1,666 nasopharyngeal swab specimens, respiratory pathogens were detected in 1,166 (70.0%). Bacterial-only detection accounted for 473 (40.6%), viral-only detection for 395 (33.9%), and viral–bacterial co-detection for 298 (25.6%) of positive specimens. Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae were the most frequently detected bacterial pathogens, whereas human rhinovirus and influenza A virus predominated among viral pathogens. Children had significantly higher odds of respiratory pathogen detection than adults (aOR 2.27, 95% CI 1.72–2.99; p < 0.001). Respiratory pathogen detection also varied significantly by season, with significantly lower odds during summer (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.43–0.78; p < 0.001) and autumn (aOR 0.57, 95% CI 0.43–0.75; p < 0.001) than during winter. Respiratory pathogen detection during the post-pandemic period demonstrated distinct age-related and seasonal patterns together with frequent viral–bacterial co-detection. Separate evaluation of viral-only, bacterial-only, and viral–bacterial co-detection provided a more comprehensive understanding of respiratory pathogen epidemiology. Because multiplex RT-qPCR detects microbial nucleic acids rather than confirming active infection, bacterial detections—particularly for common nasopharyngeal colonizers—should be interpreted together with clinical findings and complementary microbiological investigations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67826-x.title: Cardiometabolic, thyroid, and cardiac biomarker associations with insulin resistance: cross-sectional study from a Romanian cohort
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67826-x.abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) is a key driver of the cardiometabolic continuum. However, its associations with thyroid dysfunction, systemic inflammation, and subclinical myocardial injury have not been jointly evaluated at population scale using adjusted analyses. This study aimed to characterize the biomarker profile of IR and to determine which associations with HOMA-IR persist after adjustment for age, sex, and the triglyceride/HDL-cholesterol (TG/HDL) ratio. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using anonymized laboratory data from a national private network in Romania. Of 104,406 individuals with at least one HOMA-IR determination, 98,442 adults (≥ 18 years) formed the primary cohort. Associations between HOMA-IR and 16 biomarkers were assessed using Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg correction in paired sub-cohorts. Four pre-specified multivariable models were fitted on complete-case datasets: logistic regression for subclinical hypothyroidism ( n = 8,039) and linear regression for log(TSH) ( n = 12,370), log(hsCRP) ( n = 1,700), and log(hsTnT) ( n = 297), each with HOMA-IR as the exposure and adjustment for age, sex, and TG/HDL ratio. The derivation of every analytical cohort is set out in Table 1. At least one HOMA-IR value > 2 was recorded in 69.3% of tested individuals. HOMA-IR showed a very strong correlation with insulin (ρ = 0.969) and moderate correlations with triglycerides (ρ = 0.499), fasting glucose (ρ = 0.498), and HDL-cholesterol (ρ = −0.413). hsCRP showed a weak positive correlation (ρ = 0.346), whereas thyroid and hsTnT correlations were weak or very weak. In adjusted analyses, HOMA-IR remained associated with log(hsCRP) (β = 0.071, 95% CI 0.056–0.086, p < 0.001; model R² = 7.4%) and with log(TSH) (β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.004–0.013, p < 0.001; model R² = 0.9%). HOMA-IR was not independently associated with subclinical hypothyroidism (OR = 1.015, p = 0.253) or with log(hsTnT) (β = 0.004, p = 0.635) after adjustment. In this large retrospective laboratory cohort, HOMA-IR was associated primarily with atherogenic dyslipidemia and, after adjustment, with hsCRP. The association with TSH was statistically significant but small in magnitude and accounted for less than 1% of TSH variance. Associations with subclinical hypothyroidism and hsTnT did not persist after adjustment. These findings should be interpreted as cross-sectional associations in a referral-based population and require prospective confirmation before any screening or therapeutic implication can be inferred.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69363-z.title: DemoGCL: Demographic-augmented graph contrastive learning for cold-start recommendation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69363-z.abstract: One of the most persistent problems in e-commerce recommendation is what happens when a new user signs up or a new product goes live the system knows almost nothing about them, and graph-based collaborative filtering, which depends entirely on interaction history, produces embeddings that are essentially random. Existing approaches tend to address cold users and cold items as two separate problems, often at the cost of serving-time language model inference that is far too slow for production systems. In this work, we present DemoGCL, a unified Demographic-Augmented Graph Contrastive Learning framework that resolves both cold-start scenarios within a single lightweight model. At its core, DemoGCL builds on a three-layer LightGCN backbone for warm collaborative signal and augments it with two dedicated branches: a two-layer MLP that projects a five-dimensional behavioral proxy vector derived from publicly observable demographic signals into the shared embedding space for cold users who have no purchase history, and a LoRA-adapted DistilBERT encoder (rank 8, 332K trainable out of 66.7M parameters, or 0.50%) that generates cold-item embeddings from product text alone. A sigmoid-gated fusion layer harmonizes the warm and cold representations, and a cross-view InfoNCE objective aligns them during training so that cold embeddings land in the same semantic neighborhood as their warm counterparts. We evaluate on Amazon Beauty, Amazon Clothing, and Epinions under a sampled ranking protocol and find that DemoGCL achieves warm-split NDCG@10 of 0.0612, 0.0487, and 0.0831, cold-user NDCG@10 of 0.0543, 0.0411, and 0.0762 (retaining 88.7%, 84.4%, and 91.7% of warm performance), and cold-item NDCG@10 of 0.0388, 0.0319, and 0.0594. On Amazon Beauty, based on LLMDiRec’s published numbers under its own evaluation setup, DemoGCL improves over LLMDiRec by 0.18% on cold users and 77.2% on cold items, although the evaluation protocols differ. Ablation studies confirm that the demographic branch is the single most critical component, with its removal causing up to a 41.4% drop in cold-user NDCG@10, while dropping LoRA fine-tuning reduces cold-item performance by up to 37.9%. Because warm embeddings are precomputed and cached as lookup tables, the serving path avoids online large-language-model generation and keeps cold-user inference limited to a small projection module, which supports a lightweight deployment structure for e-commerce pipelines.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69148-4.title: Neurofunctional recovery effects of a Si-based agent in traumatic brain injury-induced chronic neuroinflammation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69148-4.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) causes long-term cognitive and motor deficits driven partly by chronic neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. We evaluated whether an orally administered silicon (Si)-based antioxidant generating hydrogen in the intestine improves functional recovery after TBI. Male C57BL/6J mice were fed a 2.5% Si-based diet or control diet starting 1 week prior to controlled cortical impact (CCI) and subjected to CCI. The assigned diets were continuously administered for 1 week or 6 weeks after CCI. Behavioral outcomes were assessed using the Y-maze and open field tests at 1 and 6 weeks post-CCI. Histology, SV2A-PET imaging, systemic oxidative stress assays (d-ROMs and BAP), and brain qPCR for antioxidant-related genes were performed. At 1 week post-CCI, the Si group showed improved short-term memory in the Y-maze compared with controls. At 6 weeks post-CCI, locomotor activity was significantly higher in the Si group in the open field test. Microglial activation and SV2A-PET–derived synaptic density did not differ between groups. Systemic oxidative stress indices were similar; however, cortical and thalamic expression of Nrf2 pathway–related genes tended to be higher in the Si group at 6 weeks. In conclusion, oral administration of a Si-based agent improved short-term memory and locomotor function after CCI, potentially via localized antioxidant effects within the brain that support recovery of corticothalamic networks.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68050-3.title: Concrete strength prediction using domain-driven feature engineering and explainable LightGBM
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68050-3.abstract: Accurately predicting the compressive strength of concrete is essential for optimizing mix designs, ensuring structural integrity, and reducing construction costs. This study integrates domain-informed feature engineering with optimized tree-based ensemble models to benchmark concrete strength prediction on a widely recognized Yeh dataset. We expanded the baseline feature set with 11 engineered variables, evaluating five architectures: Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Extra Trees, and a Voting Regressor. Among these, LightGBM emerged as the top-performing architecture with [Formula: see text] of 0.959 and [Formula: see text] of 3.47 MPa. SHAP analysis revealed that the newly engineered features were the most influential predictors, with Age-Cement Interaction and Cementitious-to-Water Ratio identified as the primary drivers of model accuracy. To facilitate practical adoption, the optimized framework was deployed via a PyQt5-based desktop interface and a FastAPI web service, enabling mix design optimization across different user environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69574-4.title: Sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 2 plays a regulatory role in PM2.5 exposure-induced airway hyperresponsiveness through exosomal trafficking
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69574-4.abstract: Previous studies have highlighted the involvement of PM 2.5 in the pathogenesis of airway hyperresponsiveness, but the precise role of exosomes in mediating intercellular communication in this context remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify the function and underlying mechanisms of exosomes in PM 2.5 -induced airway hyperresponsiveness. Exosome inhibitors were used to assess their functional significance at both animal and cellular levels. Exosome sequencing revealed differential gene expression profiles following PM 2.5 exposure, with the functional relevance of these genes validated through the creation of gene-deficient mouse models. Treatment with exosome inhibitors alleviated PM 2.5 -induced airway hyperresponsiveness and inflammatory damage in mice. Exosome sequencing further identified an upregulation of Sphingomyelin Phosphodiesterase 2 (SMPD-2) expression in HBE cells after PM 2.5 exposure. Functional analysis in SMPD-2 knockout mice and SMPD-2 knockdown cells demonstrated that attenuation of SMPD-2 reduced PM 2.5 -induced airway hyperresponsiveness and inflammation. Exo-PM2.5 stimulation markedly upregulated the expression of S1PRs and elevated intracellular S1P levels. However, such phenotypic changes were abrogated following SMPD-2 silencing via Exo-PM2.5-siRNA intervention. These findings suggest that SMPD-2 regulates PM 2.5 -induced airway hyperresponsiveness through exosome-mediated S1P/S1PRs signaling.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69416-3.title: Combined hydrogen and oxygen therapy attenuates vascular cognitive impairment in rats via gut microbiota-derived SCFA-GPR41/PI3K/Akt/Nrf2 signaling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69416-3.abstract: Abstract Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI), a consequence of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH), is characterized by neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis. Hydrogen-rich and hyperoxygenated solution (HHOS) may attenuate CCH-induced brain injury through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and gut microbiota-modulating mechanisms. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of HHOS via the GPR41/PI3K/Nrf2 pathway, comparing its efficacy to hyperoxygenated solution (HOS) and hydrogen-rich solution (HRS) alone. We found that HHOS significantly improved spatial memory and reduced anxiety-like behaviors in BCCAO rats. It also attenuated hippocampal neuronal apoptosis (reduced TUNEL-positive cells) and microglial activation (decreased Iba-1 expression level), enriched SCFAs-producing gut microbiota (e.g. Clostridia_UCG-014 , Bacteroides ) and activated the SCFAs/GPR41/PI3K/Nrf2 pathway, upregulating antioxidant proteins (HO-1, GST). HRS partially restored microbiota and reduced apoptosis, while HOS showed limited efficacy. Collectively, HHOS outperformed monotherapies by coupling microbiota-SCFA restoration with GPR41/PI3K/Akt/Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense, supporting a novel dual-gas strategy for VCI.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65164-6.title: Correction: Hypoxia and aspirin additively increase intracellular glutamine accumulation in PIK3CA-mutated colorectal cancer cells
