doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67890-3.title: LINC01419–miR-132-3p–USP38 axis mediates high glucose-induced ferroptosis in vascular endothelial cells
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67890-3.abstract: Abstract Long non-coding RNA LINC01419 has been implicated in ferroptosis in various pathological conditions, yet its role in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) associated vascular endothelial dysfunction remains unclear. This study investigated the mechanism by which LINC01419 modulates ferroptosis in human vascular endothelial cells under high-glucose conditions. A high-glucose cellular model was established to evaluate cell proliferation, ferroptosis, and oxidative stress. Bioinformatics predictions and dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed direct interactions between LINC01419 and miR-132-3p, and between miR-132-3p and ubiquitin-specific peptidase 38 (USP38). Quantitative real-time PCR validated regulatory interactions within the LINC01419–miR-132-3p–USP38 axis. Cell viability, reactive oxygen species levels, and ferroptosis markers were assessed via CCK-8, ROS detection, and Western blotting. Results showed that high glucose upregulated LINC01419 and USP38, downregulated miR-132-3p, elevated ROS, suppressed proliferation, and induced ferroptosis, as evidenced by increased ACSL4 and COX2 and decreased FTH1 and GPX4. LINC01419 acted as a competing endogenous RNA for miR-132-3p, and both molecules oppositely regulated USP38 expression. Notably, USP38 knockdown reversed high-glucose-induced abnormalities, restoring proliferation and ferroptosis-related protein expression. These findings reveal that the LINC01419–miR-132-3p–USP38 axis mediates ferroptosis in vascular endothelial cells under hyperglycemia, and suggest USP38 as a potential therapeutic target for T2DM.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68733-x.title: A decision-oriented multivariate copula framework for assessing wet–dry encounters and hydrological compensation potential in interbasin systems: a case study of Jiangsu, China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68733-x.abstract: Abstract The interaction between the Yangtze River and Huaihe River Basins plays a critical role in regional water security under interbasin water-resource systems. However, existing studies rely primarily on bivariate or single-basin analyses and rarely address how multivariate dependence structures influence hydrological compensation potential from a source-receiving perspective. In this study, a decision-oriented multivariate framework is proposed to quantify wet-dry encounter patterns and the estimated probability by explicitly linking upstream runoff and regional precipitation. A three-dimensional C-vine copula model is constructed using precipitation and runoff data from 1968 to 2024 for the Yangtze River (Datong Station), the Huaihe River (Wujiadu Station), and three subregions of Jiangsu Province. The results reveal distinct dependence structures across regions, with upper-tail dependence characterizing the Datong-Sunan system and more symmetric dependence patterns observed in the Wujiadu-Huaibei and Datong-Wujiadu pairs. A detrending-based sensitivity analysis indicates that the significant increasing trend in Sunan precipitation does not substantially alter the main Datong-Sunan dependence pattern. Under dry receiving-region conditions, the joint probabilities that at least one upstream source remains wet or normal are 0.23 for Huaibei and 0.22 for Sunan, corresponding to conditional hydrological compensation potentials of 62.2% and 62.9%, respectively. These values should be interpreted as theoretical hydrological source-availability indicators rather than direct operational water-diversion feasibility. This study provides a transferable probabilistic approach for assessing wet-dry encounter risks and the estimated probability in multisource water-resource systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-025-30253-5.title: Coumarin application modulates antioxidant defense to enhance resistance against Fusarium in mung bean
doi:10.1038/s41598-025-30253-5.abstract: Plant-derived bioactive compounds contribute a major role in plant defense against fungal pathogens. Among these, coumarin proved to be a major controller in root-pathogen interactions, exhibiting diverse protective mechanisms. This study investigates the effects of coumarin (50 mg.L− 1), applied through seed priming and foliar spray, on the biochemical responses of Mung bean and its impact on root colonization by Fusarium solani. Mung bean seeds pre-treated with coumarin were sown under both infected and non-infected conditions. Once the seedling established up to two-leaf stage, weekly foliar sprays of 50 mg.L− 1 coumarin (treatment group) and water (control group) were applied for 4 weeks. The results showed that the application of coumarin significantly reduced Fusarium colonization in Mung bean roots while enhancing shoot and root growth under pathogen stress. Coumarin treatment significantly increased leaf area, shoot density, and photosynthetic pigments. It also caused a substantial reduction in oxidative stress markers, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and malondialdehyde (MDA) contents. Antioxidant enzyme activities, including superoxide dismutase (SOD), ascorbate peroxidase (APX), catalase (CAT), and guaiacol peroxidase (GPX) were markedly increased with coumarin treatment. Likewise, enzymes involved in secondary metabolism, such as polyphenol oxidase (PPO) and phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL), also showed increased activities. This was associated with higher levels of total phenolics and flavonoid alongside stronger antioxidant activitiy, indicated by DPPH and ABTS assays. HPLC analysis further revealed increased levels of gallic, coumaric, ferulic, and chlorogenic acids in coumarin-treated plants. These findings demonstrate that coumarin applications enhance the synthesis of beneficial secondary metabolites, strengthen plant defense mechanisms, and promote overall plant health. Therefore, coumarin shows a promising sustainable biostimulant for improving crop resilience and advancing eco-friendly agricultural practices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64995-7.title: An integrated risk-based inspection approach for enhancing process safety in hydrocarbon storage tanks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64995-7.abstract: Abstract Petroleum hydrocarbon releases from storage facilities represent a major environmental risk, particularly under harsh operating conditions where corrosion can compromise asset integrity. Our study presents an integrated framework combining hazard analysis and Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) to improve the environmental safety of petroleum storage tanks. The methodology was applied to the SP1/RTI storage terminal operated by SONATRACH-TRC (National Company for Research, Production, Transport, Transformation, and Marketing of Hydrocarbons) in In-Amenas, Algeria, which comprises ten atmospheric storage tanks with a documented operational incident history. First, a systematic hazard study conducted by INERIS identified and ranked the hazardous phenomena associated with storage operations, providing an objective basis for equipment prioritization. Based on the resulting risk ranking, Tank A12 was selected as the most critical asset, and a routine visual inspection confirmed degradation mechanisms consistent with the identified hazards. Subsequently, an RBI assessment was performed using complementary non-destructive testing techniques, including Magnetic Flux Leakage (MFL) and Ultrasonic Testing (UT). The inspection revealed severe corrosion damage that substantially reduced the remaining service life of the tank and increased the likelihood of hydrocarbon leakage with potentially significant environmental consequences. Based on these findings, corrective maintenance was implemented in accordance with API 653 requirements, restoring the tank to safe operating conditions. Our proposed framework demonstrates that integrating systematic hazard analysis with RBI enables objective asset prioritization, improves inspection planning, and supports proactive integrity management. This approach provides a practical strategy for reducing environmental risks and enhancing the long-term safety and reliability of petroleum storage facilities operating under severe environmental conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69380-y.title: Enhancing microwave heating performance of imidazolium ionic liquids in well stimulation process: the role of magnetic anions and structural modifications
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69380-y.abstract: This study investigates the synthesis, characterization, and microwave heating performance of imidazolium-based ionic liquids (ILs) and their magnetic analogs, specifically [BIM][FeCl 4 ] and [OIM][FeCl 4 ]. The ILs were synthesized and characterized using FTIR, NMR, CHN analysis, and VSM, confirming the successful incorporation of Fe 3+ -containing tetrachloroferrate anions in the MILs. Microwave heating experiments were conducted on 0.1 wt% aqueous dispersions of these ILs, and the temperature evolution was measured under 2.45 GHz microwave irradiation at power levels of 200 W and 400 W. Results showed that the presence of ILs significantly enhanced heating compared to pure water, with [BIM][FeCl 4 ] reaching a final temperature of 81 °C and [OIM][FeCl 4 ] reaching 93 °C at 400 W after 60 s. The effect of alkyl chain length on microwave heating was minimal in chloride-based ILs, with only a 2 °C difference between [BIM]Cl and [OIM]Cl. However, a more pronounced effect was observed in MILs, where [OIM][FeCl 4 ] exhibited an 8 °C higher final temperature than [BIM][FeCl 4 ]. Increasing IL concentration from 0.05 to 0.10 wt% led to a 10–15 °C increase in heating efficiency, with [OIM][FeCl 4 ] reaching the highest final temperature at 0.10 wt%. VSM analysis confirmed weak paramagnetism in both MILs, indicating that the enhanced microwave heating was primarily due to increased dielectric loss from ionic conductivity and dipolar polarization, rather than magnetic losses. These findings demonstrate the critical role of ionic liquid structure, anion type, and concentration in optimizing microwave absorption, with significant implications for applications in energy storage and heavy oil upgrading. Future work should focus on improving magnetic responsiveness and exploring the long-term stability of these materials in industrial settings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69344-2.title: Synthesis and characterization of a novel UV-resistant epoxy based on vinyl ester/ZnO nanocomposite coatings
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69344-2.abstract: This research reports on the fabrication of a novel UV-resistant epoxy vinyl ester nanocomposite coating reinforced by ZnO nanoparticles to enhance the resistance of the coating against UV-induced degradation and improve long-term durability. The epoxy vinyl ester resin was synthesized by reacting of an industrial-grade epoxy resin with acrylic acid. For the preparation of UV-resistant coatings, ZnO nanoparticles were dispersed in the resin formulation at two different concentrations (0.1 wt% and 0.5 wt%) using a controlled dispersion technique, followed by curing under optimized conditions. The esterification process was carried out in the presence of triethylamine as a catalyst and hydroquinone as an inhibitor at 90–100 °C. The resulting resin was structurally characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, field-emission scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and elemental mapping analysis. The results demonstrated that the incorporating of ZnO nanoparticles significantly improved the UV resistance, adhesion, and mechanical stability of the coatings. Pull-off adhesion tests (n = 2 replicates per sample) showed that the addition of 0.5 wt% ZnO nanoparticles enhanced the bonding strength from 4.91 MPa for the neat resin to 8.05 MPa, indicating a remarkable improvement in interfacial adhesion. Moreover, the contact angle test under UV exposure revealed that the 0.5 wt% ZnO nanocomposite maintained its hydrophobicity more effectively, showing minimal variation even after 20 days of UV irradiation. These findings indicate the potential of the developed nanocomposite coatings for protective applications and support the value of further long-term outdoor and accelerated weathering studies to confirm performance under harsher and more extended environmental conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54416-0.title: GEN-SPARC – a pathway-aware framework for reliable and interpretable biomarker discovery in multi-cancer transcriptomics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-54416-0.abstract: High-dimensional transcriptomic studies frequently struggle with the imbalance between the vast number of measured genes and the limited number of patient samples, leading to instability, overfitting, and unreliable biomarkers. To address this enduring challenge, we propose GEN-SPARC (Gene Selection and Pathway-Aware Regularized Classifier), a novel framework that integrates stability learning, knockoff-based false discovery control, and biologically informed regularization within a unified architecture. GEN-SPARC begins by deriving robust gene importance estimates through bootstrap ensemble modeling and SHAP-based stability aggregation, then applies the Model-X knockoff principle to rigorously control the false discovery rate, ensuring that only statistically reliable genes are retained. These selected features are further organized into co-expression modules via partial-correlation graph learning, enabling the model to capture higher-order biological structure. A pathway-regularized sparse optimization step then leverages these modules to perform classification in a manner that is both interpretable and resistant to overfitting. Applied to eight major cancer families—breast, colorectal, brain, renal, prostate, liver, lung, and leukemia—on CuMiDa microarray datasets, GEN-SPARC consistently demonstrates strong internal validation performance, higher AUROC and precision–recall scores, and markedly lower feature volatility compared to standard lasso, elastic-net, and ensemble approaches. By coupling knockoff-driven statistical rigor with pathway-level interpretability, GEN-SPARC offers a reproducible, interpretable, and biologically meaningful framework for robust biomarker discovery in small-sample, high-dimensional cancer genomics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66605-y.title: An investigation on the performance assessment of copper-coated aluminium air battery using electro deposition method
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66605-y.abstract: In the present work, copper coatings deposited electrochemically on AA5083 alloy anodes for aluminium-air batteries (AABs) are studied with respect to their influence on electrochemical performance. Copper is deposited on the surface of aluminium alloy by electrodeposition, and the morphology is characterized by scanning electron microscope (SEM). Four different trials are conducted with copper coating to aluminium anode and each trial contained mixed solution of different composition. The current supply for each trial is maintained at 0.3A and the deposition time for trial 1 to trial 4 are 15 min at 35 °C, 30 min at 60 °C, 1 h at 45 °C and 1 h at 55 °C respectively. The deposition efficiency of the sample 4 is 80.75% and the coating thickness is 1.1014 cm. The investigation on the electrochemical behaviour of the coated and non-coated anodes is obtained by open-circuit potential (OCP), cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), hydrogen evolution, and corrosion rate tests. The scan rate of Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurement is 10 mV s -1 . Potentio-dynamic polarization of the samples range from − 250 mV to + 250 mV with respect to the stabilized OCP at a scan rate of 1 mV s -1 . The open circuit potential of the bare AA5083 aluminium-air battery and copper-coated AA5083 battery are 1.42042 V and 1.20145 V, respectively. FESEM analysis confirmed copper deposition on the surface of AA5083. Electrochemical test showed that the non-coated anode had better corrosion resistance than copper-coated anode. The Icorr value increases from 3.24 µA cm⁻ 2 to 6.10 µA cm⁻ 2 after copper coating, indicating enhanced anodic dissolution. The corrosion rate measurements are 0.0358 mm y -1 for the bare alloy and 0.0675 mm y -1 for the copper-coated alloy. The corrosion rate of coated anode is higher than bare aluminium anode. EIS analysis revealed a significant reduction in the impedance of AA5083 after copper coating. The charge-transfer resistance decreased from 68Ω to 4.2 Ω corresponding to an approximately 94% reduction, showing enhanced interfacial electron transfer kinetics in coated anode. The solution resistance also decreased from 11 Ω to 3.8 Ω, indicating improved electrolyte/electrode conductivity. The total impedance decreased from 79 Ω to 9.8 Ω, corresponding to an 87.6% reduction, demonstrating that copper coating effectively improves the electrochemical performance of AA5083 and promotes its suitability as an anode material for aluminium–air battery applications. The hydrogen evolution rate of copper-coated anode is 29.98 mL cm -2 h -1 . In short, the performance improvement is due to a copper barrier layer that forms to control aluminium dissolution and inhibit unwanted parasitic corrosion reactions. It illustrates the potential of low-cost surface modification method, such as copper electrodeposition for the durability and electrochemical performance enhancement of AA5083 alloy anodes in aluminium-air battery applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62587-z.title: Polyphenols intake and expression of insulin signaling genes in adipose tissue of obese adults: a cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62587-z.abstract: Evidence suggests that polyphenol-rich diets enhance insulin sensitivity; however, their molecular mechanisms in human adipose tissue remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether habitual intake of total polyphenols and their major subclasses is associated with the expression of PI3K , Akt , and PTEN , key components of the PI3K/Akt insulin-signaling pathway, in visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue (VAT and SAT) of adults with obesity, and how these associations relate to markers of insulin sensitivity. In this cross-sectional study, 135 adults with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m 2 ), aged ≥ 18 years, undergoing elective abdominal surgery, provided paired VAT and SAT samples. Dietary polyphenol intake was estimated using a validated food-frequency questionnaire (FFQ), and gene expression was quantified by RT-qPCR. Fasting insulin concentrations were measured, and insulin resistance was estimated using the HOMA-IR index. Higher total polyphenol intake was associated with lower expression of PI3K , Akt , and PTEN , with depot- and subclass-specific patterns. Total polyphenols and stilbenes were inversely related to Akt expression in both VAT and SAT, while flavonoids, particularly anthocyanins and flavanones, showed additional downregulation in SAT. PI3K expression decreased in both depots with higher polyphenol intake, driven primarily by stilbenes in VAT and by flavonoids, anthocyanins, and flavanones in SAT. PTEN expression was reduced in SAT among participants with higher total polyphenol and stilbene intakes, and in VAT with greater hydroxycinnamic acid intake. In adults with obesity, higher dietary polyphenol intake was associated with altered expression of key genes involved in the PI3K/Akt insulin-signaling pathway in adipose tissue. These associations appeared to be depot-specific and varied across polyphenol subclasses, suggesting potential interactions between dietary polyphenols and adipose tissue insulin-signaling-related gene expression.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69387-5.title: Publicity exposure is associated with anti-food-waste knowledge and practices after China’s Anti-Food Waste Law
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69387-5.abstract: Legal food-waste controls depend on public understanding and routine compliance, but empirical evidence after China’s Anti-Food Waste Law remains limited. We conducted a cross-sectional online knowledge-attitude-practice survey using non-probability snowball sampling. The Wenjuanxing questionnaire was disseminated through social media over two weeks in September 2025; 1000 questionnaires were distributed and 719 valid anonymous responses were retained (71.9%). After reverse scoring two items, internal consistency was acceptable to high (Cronbach’s alpha: knowledge 0.867, attitude 0.921, practice 0.872). Attitudes were favourable (mean 42.92/50), practices moderately high (38.53/50), and legal knowledge lower (27.83/50). Publicity/training exposure showed the largest group-level association with total KAP (H = 115.98, P < 0.001, epsilon²=0.159), whereas most demographic differences were small to moderate. Knowledge, attitudes and practices were positively correlated, with the strongest correlation between attitudes and practices (Spearman rho = 0.516, P < 0.001). In HC3 robust standardized ordinary least-squares models, attitudes, knowledge, publicity exposure, age and education were independently associated with practice. The sample over-represents women (61.8%), students (30.0%), and urban residents (89.8%); such demographic imbalance warrants caution when generalising findings to the broader national population. The non-probability cross-sectional design further precludes causal inference. Scenario-based legal communication across catering, delivery and canteen settings and easier low-waste choices may support more consistent practices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69091-4.title: Expanding access to spine surgery simulation through smartphone-based augmented reality
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69091-4.abstract: This study presents the development and validation of a low-cost, portable augmented reality (AR) simulator for screw placement training in the spine. Designed to operate on existing smart devices, the system uses image-based tracking to overlay virtual anatomical structures, landmarks, ideal screw placements and trajectories, and surgical tool animations onto 3D-printed vertebrae, eliminating the need for external tracking hardware or head-mounted displays. Vertebral models (C1 and C2, C5, T10, L5, and sacrum) were generated from segmentations of CT scans, and 3D printed with bases to place image targets. Virtual tools and animations of screw placement procedural steps were integrated into an interactive AR application developed in Unity. Technical validation included assessing the accuracy of 3D prints using Hausdorff distance analysis and image-tracking experiments evaluating linear displacement, angular rotation, and overlay accuracy on an iPhone and iPad. Mean Hausdorff distances were below 0.25 mm. Relative displacement errors were 1.78% (iPhone) and 2.09% (iPad), with mean rotation errors under 1° for both devices. Overlay accuracy averaged approximately 1 mm (iPhone: 0.99 mm ± 0.24 mm, iPad: 1.41 mm ± 0.20 mm). System accuracy met suggested benchmarks for surgical AR simulation systems, supporting its feasibility as an accessible training tool for spine surgery education.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68944-2.title: Topological-spectral fusion of secondary acoustic echoes for identity recognition in non-line-of-sight environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68944-2.abstract: Identifying individuals in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environments is a challenging problem. This difficulty stems from the absence of direct signal propagation and the dominance of multipath components in measurements. A significant portion of current studies focuses on suppressing these components as noise, which can lead to the loss of potentially discriminative individual-specific biometric information. In this study, a controlled, multichannel acoustic experimental setup representing NLOS conditions was designed. Using the data obtained from the designed experimental setup, multipath components were analyzed as a source of discriminative information, and an identification framework based on this analysis was developed. For this purpose, data were collected from 10 different subjects through an acoustic experimental setup consisting of 8 speakers and 8 microphones. In this study, secondary echo is treated as a delayed multipath component due to subject environment interaction, observed after the early time region dominated by direct speakers to microphone leakage and early wall reflections. Therefore, the raw signal from each microphone channel was divided into non-overlapping 1024 sample windows, and the last window exceeding the adaptive energy threshold was selected as the secondary echo segment. While this process temporally filters out early components, the selected segment may include the effects of room reverberation as well as delayed subject–environment interactions. Two different feature representations were extracted from the secondary echo segments. First, a time-averaged spectral representation (STFT) based on the short-time Fourier transform was obtained. Then, topological features based on the Limited Penetrable Visibility Graph (LPVG) were extracted. Spectral and topological representations were combined at the feature level to create a hybrid feature space. These obtained features were classified using Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees, and SVM. Model performance was evaluated under varying environmental conditions within the same room geometry. For this purpose, an object-configuration-based Leave-One-Scene-Out validation protocol was applied. The highest performance was obtained with the RF classifier under the configuration combining single and simultaneous multi speaker excitations. Under these conditions, STFT and LPVG representations achieved mean accuracies of 94.17% ± 6.48% and 88.83% ± 9.18%, respectively. The average accuracy of the fusion representation was found to be 96.17 ± 4.07%. The findings showed that the combined use of spectral and topological representations generally provided higher accuracy than either individual representation. A lower inter-fold standard deviation was also observed for the fusion approach. Furthermore, the results indicate that secondary acoustic echo components can carry discriminative patterns between individuals in NLOS environments. It was observed that environmental object configurations can influence discriminability by altering the multipath structure, and under certain conditions, this effect can be enhanced.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68462-1.title: Association of the CNP index with mortality risk in patients with pneumonia receiving glucocorticoid therapy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68462-1.abstract: As a composite index for severe infection, the clinical utility of the C-reactive protein-neutrophil/platelet (CNP) index for predicting mortality in specific patient populations remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between the CNP index and mortality risk in patients with pneumonia who had received glucocorticoid therapy. A dataset including 716 patients with pulmonary infection who had undergone glucocorticoid treatment from the Dryad database was analyzed. The primary outcomes were 30-day and 90-day mortality. Kaplan–Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression models were used to explore the association between the CNP index and mortality risk. In this cohort, Kaplan–Meier curves showed that patients with elevated CNP index tended to have higher 30-days or 90-day mortality rate. After controlling for confounding factors, patients in the highest CNP tertile (Tertile 3) had a significantly higher 30-day mortality risk (HR: 2.550, 95% CI 1.213 to 5.359, P = 0.01352) and 90 days mortality risk (HR: 2.126, 95% CI 1.089 to 4.152, P = 0.02720) compared with Tertile 1 (reference). Of note, when analyzed as a continuous variable, the CNP index was not significantly associated with mortality in the fully adjusted model (per 1-SD increase, P value = 0.33772 for 30-day and P value = 0.31373 for 90-day), suggesting a non-linear relationship by curve analysis. A multivariable ROC model combining the CNP index with other indicators showed improved discriminative ability for 30-day (AUC: 0.729) and 90-day (AUC: 0.717) mortality. In this cohort, an elevated CNP index, particularly in the highest tertile, was associated with increased 30-day and 90-day mortality risk. The CNP index may serve as a potential biomarker of mortality risk for patients with pneumonia receiving glucocorticoids, but further validation is needed.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68030-7.title: Increased brain white-matter extracellular free water is associated with memory function in end-stage renal disease patients
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68030-7.abstract: Previous studies have revealed brain white-matter microstructural alterations in hemodialysis patients. However, traditional diffusion tensor imaging cannot differentiate tissue-specific white matter alterations from extracellular free water changes. Here, we aimed to characterize white-matter microstructural alterations and extracellular free-water volume and their relationships with neurocognitive function in hemodialysis patients. Fifty-nine hemodialysis patients and 46 healthy controls underwent diffusion MRI and a series of neuropsychological assessments. A free-water imaging technique was applied to assess the microstructural alterations and extracellular free water volume. Group differences were examined using t-tests, Mann–Whitney U tests, chi-square tests, and tract-based spatial statistics with permutation testing. Associations between diffusion measures and neurocognitive performance was investigated using Pearson’s or Spearman’s correlation analyses. Hemodialysis patients had significantly higher white-matter extracellular free water than the healthy controls, particularly affecting projection fibers, callosal fibers, and association fibers ( p < 0.05, family-wise-error corrected). Increased white-matter free water was initially associated with poorer performance on trials 1–5 in hemodialysis patients (R = − 0.37, p = 0.025), although this association was attenuated after adjustment for age and sex. In contrast, hemodialysis patients exhibited reduced free-water-corrected fractional anisotropy compared to healthy controls and showed more robust associations hemoglobin levels and memory performance. Elevated extracellular free water in the white matter may reflect microvascular compromise or neuroinflammation, which could contribute to memory decline in hemodialysis patients. These findings suggest that free water imaging provides additional insight into white-matter alterations in this population.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68684-3.title: Combining semantic and geometric features for robust VSLAM in dynamic environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68684-3.abstract: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM) is the core technology for intelligent and autonomous unmanned systems such as robots and autonomous vehicle. It uses camera sensors to collect feature information in complex environments to achieve its own pose estimation, which is of great significance in the field of unmanned systems such as robots. However, the core of traditional SLAM is based on the assumption of static environment, which fundamentally contradicts the reality of dynamic scenes, leading to pose estimation errors in dynamic environments. Therefore, this paper proposes a SEM-VSLAM method that combines multitask network semantic information and geometric feature information to solve the normalization interference of dynamic objects, thereby achieving efficient and stable visual camera pose estimation. Firstly, an improved semantic segmentation network is used to assign semantic labels to each pixel in the input image, in order to better segment semantically prior objects such as pedestrians in dynamic environments. Then design an edge extraction network to obtain contour information of dynamic target objects, thereby improving the recognition accuracy of dynamic target objects. Finally, this paper proposes a motion weight estimation method that uses gaussian distribution to identify potential dynamic targets and combines maximum between-cluster variance to obtain point feature information in static regions. The comparative experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of visual camera pose estimation in the presence of dynamic object interference.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68377-x.title: Impact of wedge angle on flow heat mass transfer and entropy generation in Falkner–Skan flow
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68377-x.abstract: This study employs the hybrid analytical and numerical method (HAN method) to investigate the influence of wedge angle on the thermo-fluid and mass transfer characteristics of Falkner–Skan boundary layer flow. The analysis examines how the Hartree pressure gradient parameter, ranging from β = 0 (flat plate) to β = 1.0 (90° wedge), affects velocity, temperature, and concentration profiles, as well as entropy generation and the Bejan number. Results demonstrate that increasing the wedge angle substantially enhances the wall gradients of velocity, temperature, and concentration—by 162%, 19.8%, and 19.0%, respectively—which translate directly into corresponding improvements in the engineering coefficients: the skin friction coefficient (85.7% increase), Nusselt number (69.4% increase), and Sherwood number (68.4% increase). This simultaneous enhancement is physically attributed to the favorable pressure gradient generated by larger wedge angles, which accelerates the external flow, compresses the velocity profile near the wall, and consequently steepens the thermal and concentration gradients through the Reynolds analogy. While larger wedge angles intensify entropy generation due to increased velocity and thermal gradients, the Bejan number decreases near the wall, indicating a growing dominance of fluid friction irreversibilities. Unlike previous Falkner–Skan studies that primarily focused on hydrodynamic or thermal aspects in isolation, this work contributes a comprehensive entropy generation analysis that simultaneously quantifies the thermodynamic trade-offs between heat transfer, fluid friction, and mass transfer irreversibilities under varying wedge geometries. Furthermore, the application of the HAN method provides closed-form analytical expressions for the velocity, temperature, and concentration profiles, enabling direct engineering use without recourse to repeated numerical computations. These findings provide valuable design insights for optimizing heat and mass transfer performance in wedge-shaped configurations subjected to favorable pressure gradients, with direct applicability to aerospace components such as turbine blades and aircraft wings, heat exchangers, chemical vapor deposition systems, and thermal management of electronic cooling devices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69222-x.title: Transcriptional landscape of canine hematopoiesis and cross-species comparisons revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69222-x.abstract: Abstract Hematopoiesis is a complex process that begins with hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that progressively differentiate into the cellular components found in blood. Dogs develop spontaneous, biologically similar hematopoietic diseases as humans, yet transcriptomic maps of normal canine hematopoiesis are lacking. Understanding the transcriptional landscape of this process in dogs may advance translational hematology studies. Here, we aimed to (1) identify bone marrow hematopoietic cell type gene signatures, (2) characterize temporal gene expression patterns, and (3) integrated comparisons to human bone marrow. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on normal canine bone marrow and FACS-isolated CD34⁺ precursors. Unsupervised clustering revealed 29 transcriptionally distinct populations across four major lineages: erythroid, monocytic/dendritic, granulocytic, and lymphocytic. Pseudotemporal analysis classified gene expression dynamics as early, intermediate, or late within lymphoid, erythroid, and granulocytic lineages. Key regulators of cell fate at the granulocytic-monocytic branch point included CIITA and LMO1. Granulocyte subclusters were validated by immunophenotyping and compared to human granulocytes, revealing 1,522 conserved (78%) and 417 divergent (22%) genes during granulopoiesis. Overall, this study provides a high-resolution transcriptional atlas of canine hematopoiesis and highlights conserved regulatory programs between dogs and humans, offering a reference for future studies of hematologic disease and cross-species comparisons.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69748-0.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals dysregulated biological process in ALS mouse models with sod1 mutation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69748-0.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the degeneration of motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord. It is often associated with specific genetic mutations, such as Sod1 genes. However, the exact mechanism by which Sod1 leads to ALS remains unclear. We used a spatial transcriptomic (ST) technique called Stereo-seq to analyze the molecular changes during the progression of ALS. We observed dysregulated pathways related to RNA and protein synthesis and processing, as well as increased inflammatory signaling in ALS samples. Additionally, in the hypothalamus, showed more serious damage in ALS samples compared to ALS_pre samples, as indicated by the changes in enriched pathways. Our study provides a comprehensive spatially resolved molecular roadmap of ALS mouse model with Sod1 mutation, highlighting the potential of spatial transcriptomics in ALS research.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69362-0.title: Effects of E-cigarette and tobacco use on heart rate variability: a case-control study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69362-0.abstract: This study aims to examine heart rate variability (HRV) parameters, hemodynamic parameters, and serum cotinine levels difference across the following groups: tobacco smokers, e-cigarette users and non-smokers. This study explicitly examined healthy people. Ninety healthy volunteers, aged between 18 and 45, were enrolled in the study. Participants were divided into three groups of thirty each: e-cigarette users, tobacco smokers and non-smokers. HRV data were examined in both the frequency and temporal domains. Additionally, statistical analyses were performed in Python 3.8 using the scikit-learn, pandas, and SciPy packages. Tobacco smokers had a significantly longer smoking history than e-cigarette users (p = 0.027). The baseline systolic blood pressure (SBP) and mean blood pressure (MBP) of the groups varied considerably (p = 0.037 and p = 0.021, respectively), with the non-smoker group exhibiting significantly higher SBP and MBP. For diastolic blood pressure (DBP), the change was borderline (p = 0.073) but nearly significant. All HRV variables displayed standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN): -0.73 ms, root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD): -0.86 ms, proportion of consecutive RR intervals that is different by more than 50 ms (pNN50): -0.60% year and triangular interpolation of normal-to-normal intervals (TINN): -4.07 ms annually as age increased (all p ≤ 0.01). No statistically significant differences in cotinine levels or HRV indices were observed among tobacco smokers, e-cigarette users and non-smokers in this exploratory study. The long-term effects of nicotine products require more research, including longitudinal designs, higher cohort sizes and other physiological and biochemical inflammatory indicators, such as endothelial function markers and cytokines.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68965-x.title: Tobacco-rice rotation ensures safe and high-quality rice production in a three-year field experiment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68965-x.abstract: Crop rotation, particularly the paddy-upland system, is a viable strategy to mitigate soil degradation and increased accumulation of hazardous elements under long-term continuous rice monoculture, yet the temporal stability of its benefits on rice quality and heavy metal regulation remains to be fully elucidated. This study conducted a three-year field experiment (2022–2024) across two sites in Southern China to investigate the impacts of a tobacco-rice rotation system compared to continuous rice monoculture. The results demonstrated that the tobacco-rice rotation consistently enhanced rice quality, significantly increasing head rice yield and grain protein content while reducing chalkiness. Although the rotation system resulted in lower soil organic matter and available nitrogen due to high biomass removal, it elevated soil pH and enriched available phosphorus and potassium through legacy fertilization effects in tobacco season. More importantly, the rotation system served as a sustainable strategy for mitigating grain Cd accumulation, increasing the compliance rate with food safety standards from 57.14% to 71.43%. Multivariate analyses further revealed that these improvements were primarily driven by the synergistic effects of the rotation cropping system and the elevated soil pH. These findings confirmed tobacco-rice rotation as a sustainable, long-term agronomic strategy that harmonizes soil health regulation with the rice production with higher quality.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67617-4.title: Quantitative estimation of active motor-unit subpopulations in contracting muscles of children and adults, corroborated by independent findings
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67617-4.abstract: The study proposes a quantitative i.e., motor-unit subpopulation identification approach with contextual validation against compatible, independently-derived findings. Twenty men and 20 boys performed ramped isometric knee extensions to 70%MVC. Vastus-lateralis surface EMG signals were decomposed (Delsys’ Neuromap) and derived identification-ordered MU properties were converted to size-ordered sequences. Residual-sum-of-squares analysis showed segmentation as superior to continuous polynomial regression in describing the MU data. This formed the basis for differentiating 2‒3 MU-subpopulation via segmental slope changes, defined as boundaries and quantified by their relative locations along the MU-yield sequence (%MUY). A first/single boundary, detected in all participants, was 25.6% higher in the boys than in the men (70.85 vs. 56.42%MUY, respectively; p = 0.0005). A second boundary was identified in 19/20 men but only 12/20 boys (80.98 vs. 87.10%MUY, respectively; p = 0.022). The boundary-demarcated MU-subpopulations closely resembled previously-observed child‒adult differences in electromyographic and other thresholds, as well as known inter-relationships among the three classical muscle-fibre/MU types (I, II A , II X/B ). A definite identification of the MU-subpopulations as those MU/fibre types could not be confirmed or refuted by the available data. The findings’ congruence with independent threshold data, however, constitutes contextual validation of the proposed method. Elucidating the nature of the identified subpopulations warrants further research.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65821-w.title: A causal inference framework integrating causal graph discovery and double machine learning: estimating the impact of IDC deployment on corporate ESG performance

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69059-4.title: Identification and validation of shared inflammatory transcriptomic signatures across multiple tissues in severe acute pancreatitis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69059-4.abstract: Abstract Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is frequently accompanied by systemic inflammatory responses and multi-organ injury; however, the shared transcriptomic programs underlying its systemic progression remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify conserved inflammatory signatures across SAP-affected tissues using an integrative cross-tissue transcriptomic framework. Six independent transcriptomic datasets encompassing pancreatic and extra-pancreatic tissues were analyzed using differential expression analysis and robust rank aggregation. To reduce potential bias from immune-cell composition, neutrophil infiltration was computationally estimated and incorporated into adjusted differential expression analyses. A total of 16 hub genes, including S100A8, S100A9, VCAN, and PROK2, were consistently dysregulated across multiple tissues. Although adjustment for neutrophil abundance reduced the overall number of differentially expressed genes, key cross-tissue inflammatory signals remained largely preserved. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these genes were mainly involved in neutrophil activation, inflammatory responses, and IL-17 signaling pathways. External validation further showed that 11 hub genes were significantly associated with disease severity. In clinical validation, serum levels of PROK2 and VCAN were significantly elevated in SAP patients and correlated with disease severity. In silico perturbation analysis further suggested that VCAN may be associated with leukocyte migration-related transcriptional networks. Collectively, these findings define a conserved inflammatory transcriptomic program shared across multiple SAP-affected tissues and identify PROK2 and VCAN as candidate biomarkers reflecting disease severity. This study provides a systems-level framework for understanding systemic inflammation in SAP and supports future mechanistic and translational investigations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68620-5.title: Boundary aware dual encoder learning for accurate cell segmentation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68620-5.abstract: Accurate cell segmentation is a fundamental task in computational pathology and biomedical image analysis, directly impacting applications such as disease diagnosis, cancer grading, and drug discovery. Despite recent advances in deep learning, existing methods often struggle with precise boundary delineation in densely packed and morphologically complex cellular structures. In this paper, we propose a novel boundary-guided dual encoder architecture that explicitly separates semantic region representation from structural boundary modeling. The proposed framework integrates a ResNet-50 based region encoder with a lightweight ResNet-18 boundary encoder, enabling effective multi-scale feature fusion through a boundary guided attention mechanism. This design enhances segmentation accuracy, particularly along ambiguous and low contrast boundaries. Experimental results on the BCCD dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a Dice score of 95.85% and pixel accuracy of 97.47%, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods while maintaining significantly lower computational complexity. Specifically, the model requires only 12.70 M parameters and 36.86 GFLOPs, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained medical environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69172-4.title: Students perceptions, wellbeing, and engagement with university landscape spaces: evidence from Wolkite University
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69172-4.abstract: University campuses function as multifaceted environments that influence students’ academic experiences, well-being, and overall learning outcomes. This study examined students’ perceptions, well-being, and engagement with campus landscape green spaces at Wolkite University, Ethiopia, employing a mixed-methods explanatory sequential design. A total of 90 students were randomly surveyed and interviewed to assess utilization patterns, awareness levels, students’ perceptions, well-being, and engagement with campus landscape green spaces and management practices. Results indicated that disciplinary background strongly influenced landscape use, with agriculture-related fields such as horticulture, plant sciences, and natural resources management showing higher engagement compared to non-agricultural departments. Although 82.2% of respondents reported general knowledge of landscape spaces, only 20% could identify plant species by name, highlighting a significant knowledge gap. Recreational (41.1%), educational (22.3%), and studying (21.1%) values were the most recognized benefits, while ecological and social functions were less acknowledged. Students overwhelmingly preferred modern designs (90%) and judged the aesthetic performance of Wolkite University landscapes as good (77.8%), though concerns about misuse, inadequate facilities, and weak management practices persisted. Misuse was reported through cross-walking green spaces, detaching plant parts, and improper waste disposal, with limited enforcement of rules and regulations. The findings revealed that the importance of landscape spaces in supporting student well-being, academic activities, and recreational needs, while also revealing systemic challenges in management and awareness. To address these issues, the study recommends strengthening orientation and training programs, enhancing infrastructure such as seating, lighting, and water fountains, and integrating culturally significant plants to reinforce ecological identity. Improved management practices, including regular maintenance, soil fertility enhancement, and enforcement of rules, are essential to ensure sustainability. Furthermore, student-led initiatives and interdisciplinary engagement should be encouraged to maximize the academic, ecological, and social potential of campus landscapes. Generally, the study highlights the critical role of university green spaces as living laboratories that foster well-being, learning, and community development.
