doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68213-2.title: In-situ regeneration of permeable reactive barriers via the electrokinetic process for phenol-contaminated groundwater remediation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68213-2.abstract: Abstract Phenol contamination poses a significant challenge for groundwater remediation, while the limited longevity of permeable reactive barriers (PRBs) remains a major obstacle to their long-term application. This study evaluates an in-situ electrokinetic (EK) regeneration approach for PRBs treating phenol under continuous-flow conditions and simultaneously investigates regeneration efficiency, PRB longevity, and intermediate by-product formation. Experiments were conducted using a continuous glass reactor consisting of a granular activated carbon (GAC) bed positioned between two graphite electrodes. The effects of initial phenol concentration and influent flow rate on PRB performance were optimized, followed by assessment of EK regeneration performance. Optimal PRB operation was achieved at an initial phenol concentration of 150 mg L −1 and a flow rate of 20 mL min −1 . Increasing the applied voltage improved regeneration efficiency, and considering both longevity and energy consumption, 15 V was identified as optimal, restoring up to 86% of the adsorbent capacity within 5 h. Regeneration was confirmed by SEM imaging and nitrogen adsorption–desorption analysis. Under optimal conditions, EK integration extended operational longevity by up to 2.75 times compared with PRB alone. During regeneration, benzoquinone was detected as an intermediate product, whereas hydroquinone was not observed. The results demonstrate the potential of in-situ EK regeneration to extend PRB operational longevity; however, the limited number of regeneration cycles and the formation of benzoquinone indicate that further techno-economic assessment and field-scale validation are required.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69206-x.title: Clinicopathologic and molecular characteristics of colorectal cancer patients with brain metastases: a multicenter cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69206-x.abstract: Abstract Brain metastases (BM) from colorectal cancer (CRC) are uncommon but clinically consequential. We characterized clinicomolecular features of CRC patients with BM and evaluated the prognostic impact of BM timing. We screened CRC patients treated/followed between 2015 and 2024 and included those with radiologically confirmed BM. Primary tumor location was classified as rectum, left-sided colon or right-sided colon. BM timing was defined as de novo (≤ 90 days from CRC diagnosis) versus interval (> 90 days). Biomarkers included MSI status, RAS(KRAS/NRAS) mutations, BRAF and HER2. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and Cox regression. We screened 5,617 CRC patients and identified 94 (1.7%) with radiologically confirmed BM. Median age was 60 years; 60.6% were male. Primary tumors were rectal in 44.7%, left colon in 33.0%, and right colon in 22.3%, with left-sided/rectal primaries comprising 77.7% of cases. dMMR/MSI-H was observed in 6.2% (5/81), RAS mutations in 45.1% (37/82), BRAF mutations in 8.1% (6/74), and HER2 positivity in 10.8% (8/74). Median OS from CRC diagnosis was 36.1 months; median time from CRC diagnosis to BM was 21.8 months (IQR, 7.3–41.1), and median post-BM OS was 5.8 months. Interval BM was associated with longer OS than de novo BM (42.5 vs. 18.7 months; log-rank p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis adjusting for age, sex and ECOG performance status, de novo BM remained independently associated with worse OS (aHR 6.86; p < 0.001). CRC brain metastases occurred predominantly in left-sided colon and rectal primaries. HER2 positivity and BRAF mutations were identified among tested patients. BM timing provides clinically meaningful, independent prognostic stratification, and outcomes after BM remain poor. Prospective studies integrating standardized molecular profiling, treatment data, and longitudinal neuroimaging are warranted to refine risk stratification and risk-adapted surveillance.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68835-6.title: Stability analysis of rock mass in underground caverns of pumped storage power station: experimental study and numerical simulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68835-6.abstract: Pumped storage caverns are often constructed in deep granite formations with complex tectonic stress conditions. Faults and random fractures widely distributed in rock masses seriously threaten the long-term safety of underground powerhouses. This paper investigates the rock mass stability of underground powerhouse caverns in pumped storage power stations via laboratory tests (uniaxial/compression, static/dynamic triaxial, AE tests) and orthogonal numerical simulations. Granite shows brittle/quasi-brittle failure under uniaxial compression; its strength increases linearly with confining pressure under static triaxial conditions, conforming to the Mohr-Coulomb criterion. High confining pressure makes rock ductile under dynamic loading, inhibits microcrack propagation and AE activities. Numerical simulations reveal rock mass mechanical parameters dominate cavern stability, with cohesion exerting the most significant effect on stress, displacement and plastic zone depth. The results provide theoretical and technical references for cavern stability evaluation and excavation support design.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69197-9.title: State-dependent drought propagation from soil moisture to vegetation under a non-stationary climate
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69197-9.abstract: Abstract Drought propagation from soil moisture to vegetation is a complex process influenced by ecosystem characteristics and climate. The combined effects of ecosystem characteristics and a non-stationary climate on this process remain poorly understood. In this study, the dynamics of drought propagation across Iran from 2000 to 2025 were analyzed via ERA5-Land soil moisture and MODIS normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) data. Ecosystem-specific root-zone soil moisture was estimated for forests, grasslands, and croplands, and propagation dynamics were quantified with lagged cross-correlation analyses under both stationary and moving-baseline frameworks. State-dependent responses were examined under dry, normal, and wet conditions. Propagation behavior differed markedly among ecosystems. Croplands exhibited the strongest association and the shortest observed lag ( r = 0.138, lag = 0 months), grasslands showed an intermediate response ( r = 0.091, lag = 1 month), whereas forests displayed the weakest but most delayed coupling ( r = 0.042, lag = 12 months). Under the 10-year moving-baseline framework, peak correlations increased from 0.138 to 0.254 in croplands, from 0.091 to 0.200 in grasslands, and from 0.042 to 0.161 in forests, while the dominant propagation lags remained unchanged for forests and croplands. These results indicate that drought propagation is strongly state-dependent and that evolving climatological baselines primarily modify propagation strength rather than propagation timing.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67888-x.title: UAV formation control for multi-target tracking based on an improved multi-agent double soft actor–critic
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67888-x.abstract: In recent years, formation control strategies based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) have shown great potential for coordinating unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in multi-target tracking (MTT) tasks. However, in complex, high-dimensional decision-making environments, the value evaluation networks in MADRL are prone to overestimation bias, undermining the stability of policy learning. Meanwhile, the risk of collisions among UAVs and uneven spatial distribution further limit the coordination efficiency and tracking performance of multi-UAV systems. To address these challenges, an improved multi-agent double soft actor–critic (i-MADSAC) framework is proposed for cooperative MTT tasks. Specifically, a centralized double-critic network based on an attention mechanism is developed to reduce variance and adapt to varying input dimensions by optimizing the double-critic network. Then, a distance-based inverse-square repulsion function is designed to effectively mitigate collision risks. In addition, a spatial information-entropy-based reward function is designed to optimize the spatial distribution and coverage of UAVs. It works in conjunction with the repulsion function to ensure efficient collision avoidance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed i-MADSAC exhibits superior robustness, scalability, and tracking performance as the number of UAVs and task complexity increase, providing an efficient and reliable solution for MTT applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69467-6.title: Failure mechanism and synergistic control of gob-side entry under thick hard roof conditions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69467-6.abstract: To address the problem of large-scale deformation failure caused by stress concentration in gob-side entry retainment under thick and hard roof conditions, this study takes the return airway of the 9303 working face at Hengsheng Coal Mine as the engineering background. Through field measurements, theoretical calculations, and numerical simulations, the asymmetric instability mechanism of the gob-side entry under a thick and hard roof was determined. Based on theoretical calculations and numerical simulation results, a comprehensive “support-grouting” zoned asymmetric synergistic control technical scheme combining anchor cable clusters with deep and shallow hole grouting was proposed. Engineering practice verified that after implementing this technology, roof and sidewall stabilized at 58–61 mm and 144–157 mm, with rates of 0.11–0.12 and 0.14–0.16 mm/month, respectively. Consequently, the “support-grouting” synergistic control technology effectively maintained the surrounding rock of the gob-side entry under a thick, hard roof in a stable state. No abnormal mining pressure phenomena, such as support failure, rib spalling, or crack propagation, occurred, thereby validating the rationality of the “support-grouting” zonal asymmetric synergistic control technology.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69149-3.title: A medical image classification algorithm based on a hierarchical and complementary attention-enhanced Swin Transformer model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69149-3.abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of precision medicine and intelligent diagnostic technologies, automatic medical image classification has become an important tool for assisting clinical decision-making. However, substantial variations in lesion scale, complex long-range dependencies of tissue structures, and the need to capture subtle anatomical features present significant challenges to existing deep learning models. To address the limitations of the Swin Transformer in modeling multi-scale lesions and multi-level feature interactions, this study proposes a hierarchical complementary feature enhancement framework based on the Swin Transformer for medical image classification. The proposed architecture performs collaborative feature learning at three representation levels, including macro-scale lesion perception, global contextual interaction, and local detail refinement. Specifically, a Multi-scale Depthwise SE Block (MSD-SE Block) is introduced at the input of each stage of the Swin Transformer to enhance the model’s multi-scale feature representation capability. Subsequently, a Residual Convolutional Attention (RCA) module is integrated following the self-attention mechanism and the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to strengthen global contextual modeling, while a Local Detail Enhanced Residual Channel-Spatial Attention (LDERCSA) module is employed to refine subtle anatomical structures and discriminative local features. Through the coordinated interaction of these components, the proposed framework establishes a hierarchical feature enhancement mechanism that effectively improves medical image representation across multiple scales and feature levels. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on eight core subsets of MedMNIST v2, including BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, OrganSMNIST, PathMNIST, PneumoniaMNIST, and RetinaMNIST, using an input resolution of 224 $$\times$$ 224. Single-module comparison and ablation studies demonstrate that each proposed component contributes positively to the overall performance. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves significant performance improvements on BreastMNIST, OCTMNIST, OrganSMNIST, and PneumoniaMNIST. Furthermore, comparative evaluations across all datasets confirm that the proposed framework exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability when processing multiple medical imaging modalities, including ultrasound, CT, X-ray, endoscopic, and microscopic images, thereby providing reliable technical support for computer-aided medical diagnosis systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68903-x.title: Reliability and concurrent validity of a handheld smart spirometry system (Spirokit) in Korea and Vietnam
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68903-x.abstract: Abstract We aimed to evaluate the test–retest reliability and concurrent validity of a smart spirometry system with real-time software guidance compared to conventional laboratory spirometers. We included adult patients with asthma and/or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease from South Korea ( n = 633) and Vietnam ( n = 452). Participants underwent spirometry using the smart device and reference spirometers. Within-device test–retest reliability was assessed by repeating smart device measurements after a 30-min interval, whereas concurrent validity was evaluated by comparing smart device measurements with those obtained using reference spirometers. In South Korea, concurrent validity showed high agreement (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] range: 0.922–0.973 across forced vital capacity [FVC], forced expiratory volume in 1 s, forced expiratory flow at 25%–75% of FVC, and peak expiratory flow); moreover, test–retest reliability was excellent (ICC range: 0.941–0.983). Similarly, in Vietnam, the concurrent validity was high (ICC range: 0.965–0.992), with excellent reliability (ICC range: 0.973–0.997). Across both sites, Bland–Altman analyses showed that the 95% limits of agreement for FVC and FEV 1 exceeded published method-comparison thresholds, whereas ICCs indicated high relative agreement. The smart spirometry system demonstrated high test-retest reliability and small mean between-device biases, suggesting potential utility in primary care and other settings with limited spirometry infrastructure, pending confirmation in future real-world studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69651-8.title: Human glaucoma is associated with sphingomyelin depletion and acid sphingomyelinase elevation in retinal ganglion cells
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69651-8.abstract: Glaucoma is linked to altered phospholipid metabolism, which may contribute to the death of retinal ganglion cells (RGC). Here, we investigate the impact of glaucoma on the phospholipid sphingomyelin (SM) and the mechanisms that mediate SM biosynthesis and degradation in human RGCs. Using retinas from donors with or without a glaucoma diagnosis, we assessed RGC-associated SM with enhanced green fluorescent protein conjugated to non-toxic lysenin (EGFP-Lysenin), which specifically binds SM, combined with a detergent-free histochemistry method to identify RNA-binding protein with multiple splicing (RBPMS)-positive RGCs. We further performed immunohistochemistry to evaluate enzymes that catabolize SM - neutral and acid sphingomyelinases (NSM, ASM) - and enzymes that synthesize SM - sphingomyelin synthases 1 and 2 (SMS1, SMS2) - and we measured ASM catalytic activity and ceramide, the direct product of SM catabolism, in retinal tissue. RGC density was significantly reduced in donor eyes diagnosed with glaucoma. Glaucoma significantly reduced EGFP-Lysenin labeling of SM in RGCs, a finding we confirmed in flash-frozen retinal homogenates by dot blot. In parallel, ASM protein expression was significantly increased within RGCs, and the Zn 2+ -independent lysosomal pool of ASM activity was significantly elevated in glaucomatous retinas, whereas the Zn 2+ -dependent secretory pool was unchanged. Glaucoma was not associated with significant changes in the expression of NSM, SMS1, or SMS2. Although overall RGC ceramide was not significantly altered, glaucoma increased the incidence of RGCs harboring ceramide aggregates. Our results suggest that increased lysosomal ASM expression and activity drives the reduction of RGC-associated SM and may promote ceramide clustering in RGCs marked for degeneration in glaucoma.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67977-x.title: Validated stability indicating reverse phase liquid chromatography method for oxcarbazepine and its degradation products with greenness evaluation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67977-x.abstract: Oxcarbazepine is a widely prescribed anticonvulsant used in the management of epilepsy through modulation of abnormal neuronal excitability. The objective of the present study was to synthesize oxcarbazepine in the laboratory and develop a reliable, stability-indicating, and environmentally conscious reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) method for its quality assessment, including the quantification of impurities and degradation products. Oxcarbazepine was synthesized and characterized using infrared spectroscopy (IR), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) techniques. Chromatographic separation was achieved using a Supelco Discovery C18 column (4.6 × 250 mm, 5 µm) with a mobile phase consisting of 75% potassium phosphate monobasic buffer (pH 5.0) and 25% acetonitrile at a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min. Detection was performed at 257 nm, and oxcarbazepine exhibited a retention time of approximately 11 min. The developed RP-HPLC method was validated according to ICH, USP, and FDA guidelines. Forced degradation studies were conducted under acidic, basic, oxidative, thermal, and photolytic conditions to evaluate the stability-indicating capability of the method. In addition, the environmental impact of the analytical procedure was assessed using Green Analytical Chemistry (GAC) metrics, including the Analytical Eco-Scale, GAPI, and AGREE tools. The developed method demonstrated excellent specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, robustness, and sensitivity. All degradation products were well resolved from the parent oxcarbazepine peak, confirming the stability-indicating nature of the method. Excellent linearity was observed over the concentration range of 0.24–2000 ppm with a correlation coefficient (R2) of 0.9995. Accuracy values ranged from 99.4% to 101.5%, while the limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantification (LOQ) were 0.3 ppm and 0.9 ppm, respectively, indicating high sensitivity suitable for trace-level analysis. Robustness studies confirmed the reliability of the method under deliberate variations in chromatographic conditions. Furthermore, greenness assessment revealed an Analytical Eco-Scale score of approximately 75, a GAPI pictogram with predominantly green and yellow zones, and an AGREE score of 0.57/1.0, indicating moderate environmental friendliness. Overall, the validated RP-HPLC method provides a reliable, precise, sensitive, stability-indicating, and environmentally conscious analytical approach for routine quality control, impurity profiling, and stability studies of oxcarbazepine in raw materials and pharmaceutical formulations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66701-z.title: Combined associations of physical activity, BRI, and TyG index with incident stroke among middle-aged and old adults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66701-z.abstract: To examine the independent and joint associations of physical activity (PA), body roundness index (BRI), and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index with incident stroke, and to assess effect modification and longitudinal mediation by changes in TyG and BRI. This prospective study included 5,034 participants from CHARLS (2011–2018). PA was categorized, BRI and TyG were calculated from baseline data. Cox models evaluated associations, with restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessing non-linear relationships. Longitudinal mediation examined whether 4-year changes in TyG and BRI (2011–2015) mediated the PA-stroke link in a subsample ( n = 1,867). Each 1-unit increase in TyG was associated with higher stroke risk (HR = 1.17, 95% CI 1.00–1.38). High PA showed a non-significant association (HR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.59–1.02). No multiplicative interactions were found ( P ≥ 0.24). Non-linear dose-response relationship for TyG was significant only in the Low ‑ Moderate PA group ( P = 0.001), while BRI showed no evidence of non-linearity in either group. Hypertension modified the TyG×BRI product association ( P -interaction = 0.028). No mediation through 4-year metabolic changes was observed. TyG independently predicts stroke, while BRI and PA show no multiplicative interaction. However, short-term metabolic changes do not mediate the PA-stroke link. Exploratory mediation analyses failed to identify 4-year TyG/BRI changes as mediating pathways, though these results are limited by temporal measurement constraints and poor model fit and cannot rule out long-term metabolic mediation effects.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69244-5.title: A label-free adaptive signal reconstruction strategy within a supervised framework for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69244-5.abstract: Rolling bearing fault diagnosis remains challenging because weak impulsive components are easily masked by mechanical interference, and the performance of variational mode decomposition is highly sensitive to parameter selection and modal screening. To address these issues, this study proposes a label-free adaptive signal reconstruction framework in which an improved crested porcupine optimizer is used to optimize VMD parameters without using fault label information. Label-free refers only to parameter optimization and IMF selection, not the classification stage. A composite IMF selection index combining envelope entropy and Pearson correlation is further designed to identify fault-sensitive modes for signal reconstruction. The reconstructed signals are transformed into concentrated time-frequency representations using synchrosqueezed wavelet transform, and a dual-branch ICNN-BiLSTM network is developed to learn multi-scale spatial textures and temporal dependencies. Experiments were conducted on the CWRU and Paderborn bearing datasets using physically isolated data partitioning, repeated trials, ablation studies, and comparative evaluations. The results demonstrated that the proposed method achieved average accuracies of 99.75% ± 0.22% and 99.88% ± 0.10% on the CWRU and Paderborn datasets, respectively. Precision, recall, macro-F1, per-class F1-score, and confusion matrix analyses further confirmed the class-wise diagnostic performance of the proposed framework. This framework alleviates classification confusion caused by damage patterns with highly similar physical morphologies. The results indicate that the proposed framework is effective for bearing fault diagnosis under the evaluated fixed-load benchmark conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66603-0.title: Investigating purge gas recycling and optimal injection point selection in a methanol plant using operability energy exergy and environmental metrics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66603-0.abstract: This research focuses on the possibility of purge gas recycling and reutilization in the methanol plant and investigates the effect of purge gas injection point on the process performance. In this regard, three scenarios, including the injection of purge gas into the methanol reactor, primary reformer and autothermal reformer are defined and simulated by Aspen Plus simulator. The accuracy of the simulation is established by comparing the results with the industrial plant data. Among all scenarios, purge gas recycling to the methanol reactor yields the most favorable stoichiometric number of 3.82, which is closest to the ideal value of approximately 2.1 for methanol synthesis. Although purge gas recycling increases the concentration of inert gases in the inlet feed stream to the methanol reactor, the superior stoichiometric ratio and higher partial pressures of CO and CO₂ achieved in the first scenario compensate for the inert dilution penalty. Based on the simulation results, purge gas recycling to the autothermal reformer decreases the CO₂ emission rate to 0.62 kg kgMeOH − 1 . Finally, the best scenario is selected from list of alternatives by TOPSIS decision making method considering production capacity, energy efficiency, rate of exergy destruction, and CO 2 emission rate as objectives. Feeding the purge gas stream to the methanol reactor enhances the methanol production rate up to 6.6% and reduces the CO₂ emission rate to 0.65 kg kgMeOH − 1 , making it the best scenario.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67681-w.title: Primary stability comparison of three implant microgeometries in synthetic bone blocks: an in vitro study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67681-w.abstract: Achieving optimal primary stability is critical for successful osseointegration. This initial mechanical fixation is significantly influenced by the implant macrogeometry and the surgical drilling protocol. This in vitro study aimed to evaluate and compare the primary stability of three distinct implant systems, each with specific macrogeometries and manufacturer-recommended drilling protocols, across varying simulated bone densities. Ninety implants ( n = 30 per group), conventional tapered (DC), tapered with healing chambers (MAE), and cylindrical-conical (VEL), were tested in synthetic polyurethane blocks (10, 20, and 30 PCF). Primary stability was assessed via insertion torque (IT) and implant stability quotient (ISQ). The VEL system consistently demonstrated superior primary stability across all densities, achieving the highest mean IT (74.5 ± 2.8 Ncm) and ISQ (76.3 ± 1.2) at 30 PCF. The MAE system demonstrated biomechanical efficiency in low-density bone (10 PCF), achieving adequate ISQ values (54.0 ± 0.8) while generating comparatively lower IT (6.0 ± 2.1 Ncm), potentially minimizing surgical trauma. Significant differences ( p < 0.001) were observed between groups and densities. The tested implant systems, evaluated using their respective manufacturer-recommended osteotomy protocols, demonstrated significantly different primary stability across bone densities. Because implant design and drilling protocol differed among systems, the present study compares the overall biomechanical performance of each implant system rather than the isolated effect of implant microgeometry. The undersized drilling protocol of the VEL system offers high stability through increased bone compression, while the MAE design provides efficient stability with minimal torque in low-density bone.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68024-5.title: The influence of tree canopy on GPS positioning accuracy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68024-5.abstract: Abstract Accurate outdoor localization in vegetation-rich environments remains a significant challenge for satellite-based positioning systems. Tree canopy and dense foliage degrade GPS signal quality and may considerably reduce positioning accuracy, especially in applications related to smart mobility and assistive navigation systems. This study investigates the influence of tree canopy on GPS positioning accuracy in a park environment using a smartphone-based GNSS receiver. Experimental measurements were performed at five locations under two different seasonal conditions: with foliage and without foliage. The obtained positioning data were analyzed using several statistical indicators, including variance, cumulative distribution functions (CDF), Circular Error Probability (CEP), R95, DRMS, and carrier-to-noise ratio (C/N). The results showed that positioning errors in the presence of foliage were between 1.86 and 3.66 times higher compared to measurements performed without foliage at most measurement positions. Average positioning variance increased from 1.54 m 2 without foliage to 5.99 m 2 with foliage. In addition, foliage reduced the carrier-to-noise ratio of received satellite signals, and C/N values below 30 dB-Hz were observed more frequently in dense canopy conditions. The results also indicate that foliage has a stronger influence on signal quality than on the number of visible satellites. The obtained results confirm that tree canopy significantly affects GPS localization accuracy and signal reliability in outdoor environments. The study contributes to a better understanding of GNSS performance degradation in vegetation-rich areas and may be useful in the development of outdoor assistive mobility and navigation systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66997-x.title: Tissue-specific trace element accumulation in the coconut crab Birgus latro and its implications for dietary risk assessment and non-lethal biomonitoring
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66997-x.abstract: The coconut crab ( Birgus latro ) is the world’s largest terrestrial crustacean and has the potential to accumulate trace elements owing to its longevity and omnivorous diet. Trace element studies in terrestrial crustaceans are scarce, and none has been reported for B. latro . Here, we quantified concentrations of 33 elements, including potentially hazardous metals and metalloids, in B. latro ( n = 9) and evaluated body-size-dependent variation in element concentrations, differences among tissues, and the safety of B. latro as food. We further evaluated the feasibility of a non-lethal monitoring approach for long-term surveillance of this rare species, which has potential as a bioindicator of coastal ecosystem conditions. Cadmium (Cd) and Mercury (Hg) concentrations in cheliped tissue were higher in both the smallest and largest body-size classes than in intermediate-sized individuals. In addition, risk screening indicated that heavy or frequent dietary intake of the hepatopancreas, in which the Cadmium (Cd) concentration reached a maximum of 0.928 µg/g w.w., may raise human health concerns regarding Copper (Cu), Zinc (Zn), Cd, and Lead (Pb), even at the study site, which lacks notable industrialization or intensive agriculture. Non-lethal monitoring using the third pereiopod tissue showed promise, as elemental concentrations in this tissue were positively associated with those in cheliped tissue for multiple elements (e.g., Cu: R² = 0.640, Hg: R² = 0.452). These findings identify the third pereiopod as a promising non-lethal sampling tissue for long-term biomonitoring while also highlighting potential food safety concerns associated with hepatopancreas consumption.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68375-z.title: Viability assessment of matching control for grid-forming inverters in future low-inertia grids
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68375-z.abstract: This article investigates the operational viability of matching-controlled grid-forming inverters in power systems with varying grid strength. A combined small-signal and electromagnetic transient analysis is used to examine converter-grid stability mechanisms under representative disturbance scenarios consistent with IEEE Std. 2800–2022 requirements. Small-signal analysis based on a 17-state state-space model shows that matching control distributes swing dynamics between DC-link voltage and phase-angle states, providing an intrinsic energy-balancing mechanism as grid strength decreases. Representative tuning within the stable operating region corresponds to a nominal matching gain corresponding to the ratio of nominal frequency to nominal DC-link voltage, which lies within the well-damped stable operating region identified by the small-signal sweep, and voltage and current loop feedforward gains of 0.7 and 0.8, respectively. IEEE 9-bus simulations demonstrate that matching control stabilizes a severe 0.9 p.u. load-step event, whereas the baseline droop configuration reaches its stability limit despite auxiliary enhancements. Matching control limits DC-link voltage deviation to about 2% with a 0.15 s recovery time and no sustained oscillations. Additional validation in the IEEE 39-bus system with 80% renewable penetration confirms that the observed stability characteristics persist in larger networks. These results indicate an architecture-specific trade-off, as matching control extends the stability margin under severe energy-imbalance conditions where droop control approaches its stability limit, while producing larger and less-damped frequency excursions under moderate disturbances and large-scale fault conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-50686-w.title: First use of triple-element stable isotope analysis of elasmobranch vertebrae reveals strong ontogenetic shifts in smooth hammerhead sharks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-50686-w.abstract: Abstract Shark populations are declining globally, yet fundamental knowledge about their ecology and critical habitats across life history remains scarce, often preventing more effective conservation measures. To address these knowledge gaps for the vulnerable smooth hammerhead shark ( Sphyrna zygaena ), we conducted triple-element (carbon, nitrogen, and sulphur) stable isotope analysis of vertebral growth layers from individuals from the Atlantic Ocean. This approach, including the first analysis of δ 34 S in elasmobranch vertebrae, produced individual lifetime records of assimilated feeding ecology and habitat use from birth to their maximum recorded age. We found consistent ontogenetic shifts with early juveniles characterized by coastal-associated isotope signatures followed by a transition around 2.5 years towards a progressively more oceanic-associated habitat and diet until adulthood. Isotopic variation was greatest in juveniles and females, reflecting pronounced interindividual variability that may arise from the use of isotopically distinct nurseries, niche partitioning, or both. Sulphur isotope data revealed many of the clearest patterns, underscoring the value of δ 34 S in elasmobranch vertebrae as a robust ontogenetic environmental tracer. Taken together, our results demonstrate, how time-resolved stable isotope records can inform life stage-specific ecological dynamics, highlighting the importance of integrating ontogenetic patterns into management efforts of highly mobile marine species.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69545-9.title: Doping strategy of BSe/WSe2 heterostructures to realize the adsorption and sensing of harmful NH3 and NO2 gas molecules: a density functional theory study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69545-9.abstract: In the present study, density functional theory calculations were used to examine different stacking configurations of BSe/WSe 2 van der Waals heterostructures. Then, the binding of noble metals (Ag, Au, Pd and Pt) on the surface of heterostructures was investigated. Adsorption behaviors of NH 3 and NO 2 molecules on the considered Ag modified BSe/WSe 2 heterostructures was also explored. The lattice mismatch rate is calculated to be 1.22%, which is lower than the threshold value, indicating the feasibility of BSe/WSe 2 heterostructure formation. The binding energy of Ag atom on the hollow site of BSe/WSe 2 substrate is determined to be -1.35 eV, implying the stability of Ag modified material for gas adsorption. However, the highest binding strength belongs to the Pt adsorption on the hollow position with significant binding energy of -2.25 eV. The band structures, charge density difference, recovery time and work functions were also analyzed for the adsorption systems. Both NH 3 and NO 2 molecules are chemisorbed on the Ag modified BSe/WSe 2 heterostructure. Among the adsorption configurations, NO 2 adsorption by double O atoms exhibits the large adsorption energy of -2.04 eV, revealing the strong interaction between gas molecule and substrate. The results suggest that the Ag modified BSe/WSe 2 heterostructure has a great potential for application as effective gas sensor.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69448-9.title: Blood leukocyte telomere length dynamics in the first year of life in Thoroughbred horses
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69448-9.abstract: Telomeres maintain genomic integrity, shortening with ageing and influenced by environmental factors. Informed interpretation requires understanding normal telomere length (TL) dynamics at different stages of life. Although lengthening can occur, attrition rate has been demonstrated in numerous species to be greatest during high growth periods, slowing with maturation. TL dynamics have not been investigated during rapid growth in horses. It was hypothesised that TL dynamics differ between young, rapidly growing horses and adult horses. Venous blood was collected from Thoroughbred mare-foal dyads ( n = 34) from one farm every three months from birth for 12 months. DNA was extracted from blood leukocytes and relative TL (RTL) assessed by RT-qPCR. Linear mixed models were fitted with covariates (foal sex, birth weight, dam/sire age, maternal care style [MCS]) with post-hoc analysis. Foal RTL increased at three ( p = 0.040) and 12 months of age ( p = 0.003) compared to birth. Mare RTL did not change between timepoints. Foal RTL at birth was not associated with mare RTL. None of the covariates influenced foal RTL while high MCS mares had significantly higher RTL values than low MCS mares ( p = 0.021). These results demonstrate that telomere lengthening occurred in this group of rapidly growing horses.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68414-9.title: Photoperiod-dependent photosynthetic apparatus organization and efficiency in seedlings of common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) cultivars from Andean and Mesoamerican gene pools
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68414-9.abstract: Abstract Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) cultivars from Andean and Mesoamerican gene pools exhibit distinct genomic characteristics, yet their photosynthetic apparatus organization remains poorly characterized. We investigated photochemical efficiency and chlorophyll-protein (CP) complex organization in four cultivars: Cranberry and Dark Red Kidney (Andean origin) versus Calypso and Black Turtle (Mesoamerican origin) grown under long-day (16 h) and short-day (8 h) conditions. Using pulse-amplitude-modulated fluorescence, low-temperature fluorescence spectroscopy, circular dichroism, and Blue Native PAGE, we assessed photosystems' performance and CP complex organization. Contrary to expectations based on ecogeographic origin, photosynthetic characteristics of studied cultivars did not correlate with gene pool classification. All four cultivars showed reduced photosynthetic efficiency under short-day conditions, with no clear separation between Andean- and Mesoamerican-origin plants. Black Turtle exhibited markedly different behavior from other cultivars, displaying superior PSII efficiency but reduced PSI performance under short-day conditions, along with unique CP complex organization characterized by distinct fluorescence emission patterns and altered supercomplex assembly. Surprisingly, Mesoamerican Calypso responded similarly to both Andean cultivars. These findings indicate that, within the four cultivars examined, photosynthetic apparatus organization and efficiency did not cluster by gene pool of origin. Our results indicate that cultivar-level photosynthetic profiling may provide information that is not captured by ecogeographic classification alone.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69245-4.title: Instability criterion and integrated control technology for sector coal pillars based on a modified Drucker–Prager energy criterion
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69245-4.abstract: Narrowing sector coal pillars in thick coal seams can improve coal recovery but may intensify mining-induced stress concentration, plastic-zone expansion, and energy-driven instability. This study investigates a 12 m-wide sector coal pillar between the 15,104 working face and the 15,106 intake roadway in the No. 15 coal seam of Shangshe Coal Mine, China. A panel–roadway compound abutment-pressure model was established, and an approximate three-dimensional stress state was constructed using an elastic half-plane solution and the plane-strain assumption. A modified Drucker–Prager energy criterion was then developed using stored elastic energy density, ultimate elastic energy density, and stability margin. Theoretical calculation, FLAC3D simulation, and field monitoring were combined to evaluate stress redistribution, energy accumulation, and roadway deformation. As the roadway-side/goaf-side plastic-zone widths increased from 3/5 m to 4/7 m, the peak vertical stress increased from 24.973 to 28.757 MPa, and the peak ultimate elastic energy density increased from 0.10 to 0.14 MJ/m³. The 6–8 m region behind the working face was identified as the main energy-instability-sensitive zone. After integrated control, maximum roof subsidence, pillar-side rib convergence, solid-coal-side rib convergence, and floor heave were 218, 240, 228, and 208 mm, respectively.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68749-3.title: Clinical value of the endoscopic scratch sign in diagnosing Helicobacter pylori infection status
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68749-3.abstract: Accurate assessment of Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection status is essential for clinical decision-making. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical utility of the endoscopic scratch sign which refers to linear reddish streaks observed along the greater curvature of the gastric body in identifying H. pylori -negative status. In this prospective observational study, consecutive patients who underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy between January and August 2025 were enrolled. Clinical, endoscopic, and histopathological data were collected. The diagnostic performance of the scratch sign for predicting H. pylori -negative status was assessed by calculating sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Multivariate analysis was performed to identify independent factors associated with the presence of the scratch sign. A total of 587 patients were included, comprising 363 H. pylori -uninfected individuals, 143 with past infection, and 81 with active infection. The prevalence of the scratch sign was significantly higher in H. pylori -uninfected (86.8%) and previously infected patients (88.1%) than in those with active infection (22.2%). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that female sex, H. pylori infection status, atrophic changes of the gastric mucosa, and bile reflux were independently associated with the presence of the scratch sign. Female patients and those without active H. pylori infection were more likely to exhibit a positive scratch sign, whereas chronic atrophic gastritis and bile reflux were negatively associated with its presence. For predicting H. pylori -negative status, the scratch sign demonstrated an accuracy of 85.9%, sensitivity of 87.2%, specificity of 77.8%, PPV of 96.1%, and NPV of 49.2%. Moreover, patients with moderate-to-severe chronic inflammation or active inflammation showed a significantly lower prevalence of the scratch sign (both P < 0.001). Endoscopists with different experiences have a high degree of consistency in the diagnosis of scratch signs (kappa values:0.61–0.80). The endoscopic scratch sign is a reliable and practical indicator for identifying H. pylori -negative status and appears to be independent of exogenous pharmacological influences.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69178-y.title: Enhanced photocatalytic removal of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid in soil using biochar and graphitic carbon nitride nanocomposites optimized by central composite design
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69178-y.abstract: This study optimized the remediation of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) in soil using a Rumex abyssinicus biochar/g-C 3 N 4 nanocomposite under visible-light irradiation (400–700 nm) via a central composite design. The hybrid catalyst was synthesized by ball-milling biochar and g-C 3 N 4 nanoparticles at a 2:1 ratio. Physicochemical characterization confirmed a stable fixed carbon backbone (73.6%) and an accumulation of catalytic alkaline oxides (45.71% K 2 O and 16.67% CaO). Morphological and structural analyses revealed well-distributed polymeric g-C 3 N 4 sheets embedded within porous carbon networks, yielding a specific surface area of 285.2 m 2 /g, a point of zero charge at pH 8.0, and a narrowed semiconductor bandgap of 2.30 eV. The experimental results demonstrate that the removal of 2,4-D is achieved through a synergy of adsorption and photocatalytic degradation. Under optimized treatment parameters, a maximum 2,4-D soil remediation efficiency of 94.84% was achieved within 30 days, following pseudo-first-order kinetics. Radical scavenging assays suggest that superoxide radicals, photogenerated holes, and hydroxyl radicals contribute to the photocatalytic portion of the herbicide removal. The synergy between the condensed biochar core and reactive nitrogen-bearing functionalities optimizes surface chemistry and electrostatic attraction, enhancing visible-light-responsive charge separation for efficient 2,4-D remediation in soil matrices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67829-8.title: A two-layer diffusion-reaction model for quantifying internal carbon loop efficiency in algal-bacterial biofilms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67829-8.abstract: Algal-bacterial biofilms function as stratified microecosystems in which photosynthetic oxygen production and heterotrophic respiration are coupled through counter-diffusive \(\:{\text{O}}_{2}-{\text{C}\text{O}}_{2}\:\) transport. Quantifying this internal carbon loop is critical for designing carbon-neutral and energy-efficient wastewater treatment systems. This study develops a mechanistic two-layer diffusion–reaction model representing an outer phototrophic layer, where CO 2 is assimilated and O 2 is produced, and an inner heterotrophic layer, where O 2 is consumed, and CO 2 is released. Steady-state mass balances with interfacial flux continuity are solved to obtain coupled O 2 and CO 2 profiles across the biofilm. A new dimensionless Carbon Loop Efficiency Index (CLEI) is introduced to quantify the degree of photosynthetic–respiratory coupling based on interfacial gas fluxes. By definition, CLEI = 0 represents a carbon-positive regime with no internal CO 2 recycling, CLEI = 1 denotes complete loop closure and carbon-neutral operation, and CLEI > 1 indicates a potentially carbon-negative regime in which CO 2 assimilation exceeds internally generated CO 2 under the modeled conditions. Model results suggest that, within the validated parameter ranges considered in this study, CLEI approaches unity only within a constrained design window characterized by intermediate total biofilm thickness (approximately 300–500 μm), where oxygen and carbon dioxide transport are balanced through coupled diffusion–reaction processes. Thinner biofilms are carbon-limited (CLEI > 1), whereas thicker biofilms develop oxygen diffusion limitation (CLEI < 1), preventing complete loop closure. Thinner biofilms are carbon-limited (CLEI > 1), whereas thicker biofilms develop oxygen diffusion limitation (CLEI < 1), preventing full loop closure. The framework demonstrates how stratified algal–bacterial biofilms can achieve self-oxygenation and intrinsic CO₂ mitigation through transport-controlled coupling, and provides a mechanistic basis for the rational design of carbon-neutral or potentially carbon-negative wastewater treatment and photobioreactor systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67582-y.title: Effect of fiber size difference on acoustic and mechanical properties of natural fiber reinforced concrete containing oil palm mesocarp fiber
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67582-y.abstract: To mitigate environmental noise pollution, this study investigated the acoustic absorption and mechanical properties of concrete incorporating raw oil palm mesocarp fiber (OPMF). Fine and coarse OPMF fractions were evaluated as partial fine aggregate replacements at volume substitution levels of 0.0 to 10.0%. Acoustic performance was characterized across a frequency range of 50–5000 Hz using an impedance tube, while compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths were determined per standard testing specifications. The incorporation of untreated OPMF significantly improved acoustic absorption, yielding sound absorption coefficients (SAC) of 0.003–0.43, sound absorption averages (SAA) of 0.087–0.14, and noise reduction coefficients (NRC) of 0.074–0.13, markedly outperforming plain concrete (SAC: 0.005–0.22, SAA: 0.06, NRC: 0.058). Mechanical properties exhibited dosage-dependent reductions relative to control: 12.48–44.89% for compressive strength, 2.34–18.07% for flexural strength, and 0.86–29.17% for splitting tensile strength. Notably, fine OPMF mixtures retained 28-day compressive strengths between 43.47 and 36.13 MPa across 2.0–10.0% loading, satisfying the minimum structural material strength thresholds specified by Eurocode 2 (C25/30–C30/37). Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) evaluation via a Normalized Weighted Performance Index confirmed that 4% fiber loadings establish an optimal balance between acoustic attenuation and structural capacity. While full structural element design analysis was beyond the scope of this study, the findings demonstrate strong material-level feasibility for semi-structural and acoustic envelope applications.
authors: Wan Mohd Amri Wan Mamat Ali

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67928-6.title: Behavioral thermal variation across phylogenetic and environmental gradients in neotropical ectothermic terrestrial tetrapods
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67928-6.abstract: Behavioral thermoregulation is a primary way in which ectotherms avoid overheating, but whether these behavioral limits adjust to climate across broad spatial scales remains poorly understood. Here, we measured the voluntary thermal maximum (VTMax), the temperature at which animals retreat from heat, across 130 species of Neotropical amphibians and reptiles. Comparative analyses were conducted using the subset of 126 species for which complete climatic, geographic, morphological, and phylogenetic information was available. We combined VTMax measurements with species distributions, ERA5 climate records from 1940 to 2024, and time-calibrated phylogenies to test whether behavioral thermal responses are shaped by geography, climate, or evolutionary history. Despite strong climatic contrasts among Neotropical ecoregions, VTMax did not differ significantly among them. Broad-scale climatic and macroecological predictors explained little variation in VTMax after accounting for lineage-level random effects. Amphibians, but not reptiles, showed a modest positive association between VTMax and geographic range size. Overall, VTMax exhibited weak associations with broad-scale climatic and macroecological gradients, while mixed models indicated that part of its variation remained associated with lineage-level structure. These findings suggest that behavioral upper thermal limits respond weakly to broad climatic gradients, supporting the hypothesis that behavioral thermoregulation and local thermal buffering may reduce the coupling between behavioral thermal thresholds and atmospheric conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69023-2.title: Batatasin III alleviates inflammatory bowel disease by suppressing MMP7 and NFκB signaling in macrophages and restoring gut microbial balance
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69023-2.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, is characterized by chronic intestinal inflammation, disruption of the mucosal barrier, and immune dysregulation. Recent evidence underscores the role of gut macrophages, microbiota, and proinflammatory mediators in driving disease pathology. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms of Batatasin III, a stilbenoid compound derived from Dendrobium scabrilingue , in a murine model of IBD. A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis model in mice was used to evaluate the efficacy of Batatasin III. Clinical parameters including body weight, colon length, and disease activity index (DAI) were measured. Histological analysis, cytokines analysis, macrophage polarization assays, gut microbiota sequencing, RNA sequencing, and molecular docking were performed to elucidate the underlying mechanism of Batatasin III. Batatasin III significantly alleviated DSS-induced colitis by improving colon length, reducing DAI, and preserving body weight. It enhanced gut barrier function through increased goblet cell count and upregulated tight junction proteins. The compound reduced proinflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-α, elevated anti-inflammatory IL-10, and shifted macrophage polarization from the M1 to M2 phenotype. Furthermore, Batatasin III favorably modulated the gut microbiota composition and downregulated MMP7 expression. Mechanistically, it inhibited NF-κB activation and MMP7 upregulation in macrophages; pharmacological reactivation of NF-κB with Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate attenuated these inhibitory effects on MMP7 activity, MMP7 expression, and inflammatory cytokine expression, supporting an NF-κB-dependent mechanism. Batatasin III exhibits multi-faceted protective effects against colitis by promoting M2 macrophage polarization, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines and reactive oxygen species, enhancing epithelial integrity, and reshaping gut microbiota. These findings provide a compelling rationale for its further development as a therapeutic agent for IBD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69211-0.title: Co-hydrothermal carbonization of sewage sludge and coffee grounds: combustion characteristics and hydrochar properties
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69211-0.abstract: To simultaneously address the pressing challenges of sewage sludge (SS) disposal and coffee grounds (CG) valorization, herein, co-hydrothermal carbonization (Co-HTC) of SS and CG was performed at a dry mass ratio of 1:2 over a temperature range of 180–260 °C to evaluate hydrochar properties and synergistic interactions. Results revealed that hydrochar produced from SS alone (SS260) exhibited poor fuel quality with an ash content of 64.04% and a higher heating value (HHV) of merely 8.56 MJ·kg − 1 . In contrast, co-hydrochar (SC260) demonstrated substantially enhanced fuel characteristics: ash content reduced to 38.53%, fixed carbon increased to 10.53%, and HHV elevated to 15.11 MJ·kg − 1 (a 76.5% increase relative to SS260), achieving an overall energy recovery efficiency of 64%. Combustion performance was also markedly improved, with SC180 exhibiting a combustibility index (C i ) of 1.06 and a comprehensive combustion index (S) of 6.37, values far exceeding those of raw SS (0.75 and 2.92, respectively). Notably, significant synergistic effects were observed during Co-HTC: SC260 achieved a carbon retention synergy coefficient of 7.92% and a yield synergy coefficient of 3.05%. Additionally, the resulting co-hydrochar possessed a higher specific surface area (31.54 m 2 ·g − 1 ) and more developed porous structure compared to single-feedstock hydrochar. These findings demonstrate that Co-HTC of SS and CG is an effective strategy to upgrade hydrochar fuel quality, offering a technically viable approach for the clean and sustainable co-valorization of these two problematic organic wastes.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69227-6.title: Nanotechnology-based full-adder design with three-input majority and XOR gates using quantum-dots technology
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69227-6.abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) is an emerging nanocomputing paradigm in which binary information is represented and propagated through cell polarization and Coulombic interactions. QCA technology provides a potential alternative to conventional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor circuits for implementing compact digital logic structures. This paper presents a multilayer QCA architecture for implementing a one-bit full adder using a three-input XOR gate and a three-input majority gate. The three-input XOR gate generates the SUM output, whereas the majority gate directly produces the CARRY output. The proposed full-adder cell is subsequently employed as the basic building block of a four-bit ripple-carry adder, in which the carry output of each stage is connected to the carry input of the following stage. The proposed layouts are implemented using a three-layer arrangement and provide direct accessibility to the input and output cells. The functional behavior of the proposed circuits was evaluated using QCADesigner, whereas their energy-dissipation characteristics were analyzed using QCADesigner-E, which supports the evaluation of the adopted multilayer structures. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed one-bit full adder consists of 21 QCA cells, occupies an area of 0.02 μm², and produces the SUM and CARRY outputs with a latency of 0.5 clock cycle. The proposed four-bit ripple-carry adder consists of 141 cells, occupies an area of 0.25 μm², and generates the final carry output after two clock cycles. The simulated output waveforms verify the functional correctness of both circuits for the applied input combinations. The results indicate that the proposed multilayer structures provide compact implementations of a one-bit full adder and a four-bit ripple-carry adder while maintaining direct access to their input and output cells.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69238-3.title: Circulating extracellular vesicle–enriched miR-144-3p and functional regulation of the mTOR pathway in multiple myeloma
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69238-3.abstract: Extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched microRNAs (miRNAs) are increasingly recognized as biologically relevant components of circulating EV-enriched fractions in multiple myeloma (MM), but the functional relevance of individual EV-enriched miRNAs remains incompletely defined. We profiled EV-enriched miRNAs in an outcome-selected screening cohort of patients with MM ( n = 48) and assessed selected candidates in a second clinical cohort ( n = 81) for exploratory clinical associations, followed by mechanistic analyses using quantitative reverse-transcription PCR, western blotting, luciferase reporter assays, and Argonaute-2 ribonucleoprotein immunoprecipitation. Among the exploratory candidates, miR-144-3p was nominally lower in patients with poor clinical outcomes. In the second clinical cohort, low EV-miR-144-3p expression was associated with higher bone marrow plasma cell infiltration, whereas its independent prognostic significance for overall survival was not confirmed. Mechanistically, miR-144-3p directly targeted the 3′ untranslated region of mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) mRNA, reduced mTOR expression, and attenuated mTOR-related signaling. MiR-144-3p overexpression suppressed MM cell proliferation and clonogenic growth and was associated with a greater reduction in viability-associated signal following rapamycin treatment under the tested conditions. These findings identify EV-enriched miR-144-3p as an exploratory candidate associated with adverse clinical features and disease burden and support further investigation of the miR-144-3p/mTOR axis as a biologically relevant pathway in MM.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68553-z.title: Association between plate position and hinge fracture after high tibial osteotomy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68553-z.abstract: Medial open-wedge high tibial osteotomy (MOWHTO) can lead to lateral hinge fractures, which may lead to serious complications, such as delayed union or nonunion of the medial opening gap. The purpose was to investigate whether plate position influences the occurrence of hinge fracture in MOWHTO. We enrolled 51 patients (51 knees) undergoing MOWHTO for primary medial osteoarthritis. Plate position was quantified by measuring the plate angle, defined as the angle between a line connecting the two ends of the plate and a line tangent to the posterior cortical surface. Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence or absence of lateral hinge fracture. The mean plate angle was significantly smaller in the hinge fracture group (36.4° ± 5.6°) than in the non-fracture group (44.7° ± 7.4°, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that plate angle alone served as the significant predictor of lateral hinge fracture occurrence (Adjusted odds ratio = 0.837, P < 0.001) Patients in the hinge fracture group exhibited a plate angle approximately 8.2° smaller than that observed in the group without fracture, suggesting that anterior placement on the proximal tibia is associated with an increased likelihood of hinge fracture.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68341-9.title: PSMD14 reduced microglial M2 polarization to promote ferroptosis and aggravate traumatic brain injury through the induction of BMP6/SMAD3 pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68341-9.abstract: The present study aimed to investigate the functional role of proteasome 26S subunit non-ATPase 14 (PSMD14) in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and further elucidate its molecular mechanisms linking ferroptosis to microglial M2 polarization. A total of 52 clinical samples from TBI patients and 52 matched healthy volunteers samples were collected in this study. Both clinical specimen validation and in vivo animal experiments demonstrated significant upregulation of PSMD14 at both mRNA and protein levels in TBI patients and TBI mouse models. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence staining further confirmed elevated PSMD14 expression primarily in microglia of TBI mouse brain tissues. In vivo functional evaluation showed that genetic inhibition of PSMD14 effectively alleviated brain pathological injury in TBI mice. In terms of inflammatory cytokine profiling, shRNA-mediated PSMD14 knockdown reduced the secretion of pro-inflammatory factors IL-6 and TNF-α, while increasing the levels of anti-inflammatory cytokines IL-10 and TGF-β in TBI model mice. Consistent with the altered inflammatory phenotype, PSMD14 inhibition decreased the proportion of M1-type microglia (IL-6/CD86) and increased the abundance of M2-type microglia (IL-10/CD206) in TBI brain tissues. Mechanistic exploration revealed that PSMD14 overexpression aggravated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, oxidative stress activation, and mitochondrial structural and functional damage in microglia, thereby facilitating microglial ferroptosis under TBI pathological conditions. Moreover, PSMD14 prominently activated the BMP6/SMAD5/SMAD3 signaling axis in microglia following TBI injury. In conclusion, PSMD14 suppresses microglial M2 polarization during TBI progression by promoting mitochondrial oxidation-induced ferroptosis through the activation of the BMP6/SMAD3 pathway. Targeted inhibition of PSMD14 may serve as a promising therapeutic strategy for TBI treatment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68167-5.title: A novel POA multi-stage PIDn(1 + PD) based SHAF with adaptive hysteresis current controller for PQ improvement
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68167-5.abstract: This paper presents an innovative Multi-Stage Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller integrated with an N-filter, along with a plus-one (1 + PD) derivative controller PIDn(1 + PD) controller-based Shunt Hybrid Active Filter (SHAF) to compensate for reactive power and harmonics in the distribution network. Harmonic issues primarily arise from the extensive use of non-linear loads in both industrial & residential areas. Harmonics can lead to adverse outcomes, including improper operation of delicate devices, resonant problems, conductor heating, energy losses, and reduced efficiency in the distribution network. To address harmonic problems, passive filters (PFs) are employed; however, as the harmonic components rise, the design of PFs becomes intricate and tends to be oversized. Advances in power electronics have led to the proposal of the Active Filter (AF). Typically, the rating of the AF is quite high for specific applications; thus, SHAFs are created using low-rated Shunt Active Filters (SAF) alongside low-cost Shunt Passive Filters (SPF). The gains of this suggested PIDn(1 + PD) controller, PIDn(1 + PD)C, are refined using an innovative Pelican Optimization Algorithm (POA) technique. In this work, the multi-stage PIDn(1 + PD) controller is utilized here to meet the reference current and control the DC Link Voltage (DLV), and for generating the switching pulses for the voltage source inverter (VSI), a new method, i.e., the adaptive hysteresis current controller (AHCC), is considered. The effectiveness of the suggested POA-PIDn(1 + PD)-controlled AHCC-based SHAF is examined under stable-state and transitory-state conditions using Simulink/MATLAB and real-time settings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65570-w.title: Flexible regulation and cooperative optimization method of electric vehicle charging load for active distribution networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65570-w.abstract: Driven by the dual-carbon goals, the number of electric vehicles (EVs) in China has maintained a rapid growth. Large-scale uncoordinated charging of EVs poses severe challenges to the safe and stable operation of active distribution networks (ADNs). To realize the cooperative optimization between EV charging loads and ADNs, this paper proposes a flexible regulation method for EV charging loads based on demand response. First, the characteristics of EV charging behaviors are analyzed, and an EV charging load model covering both random and coordinated charging modes is established. The Monte Carlo method is adopted to perform sampling simulation of charging loads. Second, aiming at the defects of traditional NSGA-II algorithm, such as easy trapping in local convergence and uneven solution distribution, an improved NSGA-II algorithm based on chaotic initialization and elite selection is proposed. On this basis, a source-load cooperative optimization model is constructed, which takes the maximum comprehensive user satisfaction and the minimum net load variance of ADNs as optimization objectives, with constraints including battery state of charge and the lower limit of user comfort. Finally, an ADN in a residential area of China is taken as a numerical example to verify the regulation performance of EV charging on working days and rest days respectively. The results show that the proposed method reduces the peak-valley difference of ADN load from 1002.0 kW to 329.8 kW on working days, with a reduction rate of 63.5%. The charging cost for users is cut by 29.98%, and the comprehensive user satisfaction increases by 5.59%. The proposed method effectively improves the accommodation capacity of clean energy and the operational stability of power grids.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68837-4.title: Hydrogel electrolytes as dynamic ion-regulation platforms for safe and sustainable metal batteries
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68837-4.abstract: Dendritic zinc growth in aqueous zinc-ion batteries originates from coupled ionic-transport heterogeneity, concentration polarization, electric-field localization, and mechanically unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Here, a three-dimensional electro-chemo-mechanical framework was developed to quantify how zeolite loading regulates these interconnected processes in polyacrylamide-based nanocomposite hydrogel electrolytes. The model integrates Zn²⁺ transport, electric-current conservation, Butler–Volmer kinetics, phase-field dendrite evolution, swelling, and solid mechanics using experimentally constrained composition-dependent properties. The PAM/15 wt% zeolite electrolyte provided the best baseline compromise, exhibiting an ionic conductivity of 13.48 mS cm⁻¹, an interfacial Zn²⁺ concentration of 0.74 mol L⁻¹, a maximum electric field of 1.18 × 10 5 V m⁻¹, and a current-density nonuniformity factor of 1.17. Its ionic-flux variance decreased to 2.61 × 10 − 12 , corresponding to a Flux Oscillation Index of 0.42, while the Mechanical Stability Index reached 0.91. Excessive loading at 20 wt% caused agglomeration, increased tortuosity, renewed transport heterogeneity, and localized stress despite greater bulk stiffness. Multilevel validation showed strong agreement with experimental transport, dendrite-growth, field, deformation, and cycling data. Sensitivity analysis identified current density as the dominant operating variable, whereas diffusivity, conductivity, tortuosity, and modulus governed distinct transport and mechanical responses. The predicted optimum shifted only between 12.9 and 16.2 wt%, confirming a robust intermediate-loading design window rather than a single universal composition.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68487-6.title: Individual metabolic differences predict the spontaneous emergence of breast muscle myopathy in broiler chickens
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68487-6.abstract: Individual variability is a fundamental characteristic and one of the long-standing mysteries in biology. Significant differences in health are observed even among isogenic, simple organisms such as yeast or worms, maintained under homogeneous and strictly controlled laboratory conditions. The inability to predict which individuals will be fit and resilient and which will be more susceptible to frailty and disease has led to the hypothesis that a fundamental aspect of healthspan is stochastic. Here, we use isogenic broiler chickens ( Gallus gallus domesticus ) as an animal model for a breast muscle pathology known as wooden breast (WB). Intensively selected for exceptional growth rate and meat yield, broilers exhibit natural and spontaneous emergence of varying degrees of WB myopathy among individuals, making them a unique model for studying natural variability in muscle pathologies. Applying metabolic profiling and physiological measurements, we found that metabolic differences among individuals were associated with and predictive of variability in the emergence of WB myopathy. Molecularly, we identified metabolic biomarkers that predict which animals will remain healthy and which will develop severe WB. Physiologically, WB development was significantly associated with metabolic efficiency; WB birds grew faster and consumed less feed to achieve the same weight gain. Because molecular markers are often conserved across species, future studies may use broilers to further investigate the molecular phenotype and improve our understanding of individual susceptibility to muscle pathologies - not only in birds, but potentially in other vertebrates as well.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68795-x.title: MOO-IDS: multi-objective optimization-based lightweight intrusion detection system for in-vehicle networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68795-x.abstract: With the proliferation of intelligent connected vehicles, the Controller Area Network (CAN) bus, as the backbone of in-vehicle communication, is vulnerable to cyberattacks due to lack of authentication and encryption. Existing Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) exhibit limitations in addressing data imbalance, complex attack recognition, and resource-constrained deployment. This paper proposes a lightweight intrusion detection system based on multi-objective optimization, termed MOO-IDS. The system integrates a Hybrid Deep Restricted Boltzmann Machine Generator (HyDRBM-Gen) to mitigate attack sample scarcity and class imbalance in vehicular network data. To address targeted ID fabrication and masquerade attacks, two novel features, ID Frequency (IDF) and ID-Data Correlation (IDC), are introduced. An Adaptive-Enhanced Non-Dominated Sorting Dung Beetle Optimizer (AE-NSDBO) optimizes XGBoost hyperparameters to achieve an optimal balance among F1-score, model size, and inference latency, enabling the optimized XGBoost to accomplish intrusion detection. Experimental results on the real-world dataset Real ORNL Automotive Dynamometer (ROAD) demonstrate that MOO-IDS achieves outstanding performance, with a weighted-average F1-score of 0.9907, a model size of only 0.199 MB, and substantially reduced inference latency. The model also performs excellently on the Car Hacking and Survival Analysis datasets. This study provides a high-precision, lightweight, and strongly generalizable multi-class intrusion detection model for resource-constrained vehicular environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68840-9.title: Effects of land use on soil biological parameters across ecosystems in northwestern Iran
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68840-9.abstract: Abstract Land use change has become a major environmental challenge in northwestern Iran, including the Namin region of Ardabil Province, where agricultural expansion has accelerated the degradation of forests and rangelands over recent decades. This study aimed to compare soil biological properties among four representative land use types (forest, rangeland, shrubland, and rainfed agriculture) and to identify the most informative indicators of soil quality in the Namin region, Ardabil Province, Iran. In July 2023, 36 soil samples (nine per land-use type) were collected and analyzed for organic carbon, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), soil texture, calcium carbonate equivalent (CCE), basal respiration (BR), substrate-induced respiration (SIR), microbial biomass carbon (MBC), microbial biomass nitrogen (MBN), the microbial quotient (q mic ), and the metabolic quotient (qCO 2 ). Statistical analyses included analysis of variance (ANOVA), Tukey’s honestly significant difference (HSD) test, factor analysis (FA), principal component analysis (PCA), and permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA). Forest soils exhibited significantly higher BR, SIR, MBC, and MBN than the other representative land-use types. PCA identified three principal components that explained approximately 78% of the total variance, demonstrating that soil quality is governed by interacting biological, chemical, and physical processes. From the Total Data Set (TDS) of 12 soil properties, PCA identified a Minimum Data Set (MDS) consisting of four non-redundant indicators: soil pH, EC, silt, and BR. These indicators represented key chemical, physical, and biological dimensions of soil quality and collectively accounted for more than 61% of the total variance. Comparison of the soil quality indices showed that the highest and lowest IQI TDS values were observed in the representative forest (0.792) and scrubland (0.262) sites, respectively. For IQI MDS , the rainfed agricultural and forest sites exhibited the highest values (0.690 and 0.671, respectively), whereas the scrubland and rangeland sites exhibited lower values (0.412 and 0.479, respectively). Nevertheless, both indices consistently identified the scrubland site as having the lowest soil quality. Overall, the results indicate that differences in soil biological functioning and overall soil quality were observed among the representative land use sites. In addition, the proposed MDS retained much of the information contained in the TDS while requiring fewer indicators, suggesting that it may serve as a practical and cost-effective framework for soil quality assessment and long-term ecological monitoring in semi-arid land use systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68491-w.title: In silico mining and validation of microsatellite markers in Phlebotomus argentipes (Diptera: Psychodidae)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68491-w.abstract: Abstract Phlebotomus argentipes is the primary vector of Leishmania donovani , the causative agent of leishmaniasis. This study aimed to expand genomic resources for P. argentipes by in silico mining and characterization of simple sequence repeats (SSRs) from a scaffold-level genome assembly retrieved from GenBank, followed by wet-lab validation of selected SSR markers. A total of 22 SSR loci were identified from intergenic regions and used for primer design. Laboratory validation using PCR amplification of genomic DNA from laboratory-reared flies confirmed successful amplification across all loci. Based on amplification quality and verification of SSR motifs, 11 primer pairs were selected for fragment analysis and allelic characterization in field-collected P. argentipes ( n = 20) from Ambalantota (Geo 1) and Polpithigama (Geo 2). All selected loci exhibited polymorphism, with allelic diversity ranging from 1 to 8 alleles per locus. Observed heterozygosity (H O ) ranged from 0.00 to 0.75, expected heterozygosity (H E ) from 0.29 to 0.85, and polymorphism information content (PIC) from 0.26 to 0.81, with five markers (IC27, IC02, IC51, IC68, IC74). Genetic differentiation between populations (F ST ) ranged from 0.03 to 0.10, while F IS ranged from 0.10 to 1.00, indicating heterozygote a deficit across loci, except for IC21, which showed heterozygote excess, supporting the utility of these SSR markers for population genetic studies.
