doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65863-0.title: State-of-charge estimation for a pouch-type lithium cobalt oxide battery using an adaptive generalized maximum correntropy strong-tracking cubature kalman filter
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65863-0.abstract: Accurate state-of-charge estimation is essential for the safe and efficient operation of lithium-ion battery management systems. However, measurement outliers, time-varying noise statistics, model mismatch, and abrupt operating-condition changes can degrade the accuracy and stability of conventional Kalman-filter-based estimators. To address these problems, this study develops an adaptive generalized maximum correntropy strong-tracking cubature Kalman filter (AGMCC-STCKF) for a pouch-type lithium cobalt oxide battery. The principal methodological contribution is a residual-statistics-based adaptive kernel-width strategy. At each sampling instant, the kernel width is updated using a weighted combination of the standard deviation of a sliding innovation-residual window and the instantaneous innovation magnitude, followed by bounded projection to prevent kernel-width degeneration. The generalized maximum correntropy criterion is used to attenuate abnormal measurements, while the strong-tracking fading factor and Sage–Husa estimator improve responsiveness to model mismatch and time-varying noise statistics, respectively. A second-order RC equivalent-circuit model is established, and its parameters are identified using forgetting-factor recursive least squares. Experimental validation is conducted at 25 °C under UDDS and DST operating conditions. Across 30 paired Gaussian-noise realizations, the proposed method achieves mean MAE, RMSE, and MaxAE values of 0.4040%, 0.4571%, and 0.8653%, respectively, corresponding to reductions of 19.15%, 28.51%, and 72.50% relative to CKF. Under weak, medium, and strong non-Gaussian disturbances, the proposed method also achieves the lowest mean errors among the compared CKF-based estimators. External validation using the CALCE CS2_35 dataset yields an RMSE of 0.7183%. The mean single-step runtime is 0.871 ms, which is substantially lower than the 1 s sampling interval. These results demonstrate improved estimation accuracy and robustness within the investigated cell type, temperature, and operating conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68278-z.title: Microstructural changes in the optic tract and optic radiation on diffusion tensor imaging as biomarkers of glymphatic dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68278-z.abstract: The role of ocular glymphatic function in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains incompletely understood. This study investigated whether diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics of the optic tract (OT) and optic radiation (OR) are associated with putative glymphatic imaging markers across the AD continuum and evaluated their diagnostic value. Data from 226 participants in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, including 59 healthy controls, 120 patients with mild cognitive impairment, and 47 with AD, were analyzed. Group differences in DTI metrics and putative glymphatic imaging markers, including the DTI-ALPS index and choroid plexus volume fraction (CPVF), were assessed with adjustment for age, sex, education, and APOE ε4 status. Patients with AD showed significantly higher mean, axial, and radial diffusivity in both OT and OR than other groups ( p ≤ 0.02). The DTI-ALPS index was lower in AD than in healthy controls and mild cognitive impairment ( p ≤ 0.009), whereas CPVF was higher in AD ( p < 0.001). Diffusivity parameters correlated positively with CPVF ( r = 0.31–0.36) and negatively with Mini-Mental State Examination scores ( r = − 0.36 to − 0.47). Logistic regression achieved an AUC of 0.84 (95% CI, 0.78–0.88) for distinguishing AD from controls. OT and OR DTI parameters may be associated with putative glymphatic imaging markers in AD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68854-3.title: The impact of dietary fibres on gut microbiome of young children: insights from in vitro experiments and an observational cohort
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68854-3.abstract: Abstract During weaning period, the intake of dietary fibres changes and increases dramatically. Given the considerable structural differences, we hypothesized that different fibres may vary in their function. The objective of the study was to explore the impact of specific dietary fibres (arabinoxylan, cellulose, pectin and xyloglucan) on the gut microbiome of children below 3 years. By using in vitro fecal fermentation experiments, cellular models and cohort data analysis, we assessed how these fibres and their combinations influence infants’ gut microbiota composition, diversity, metabolite production and possible actions on the gut epithelial barrier function. We found that the fermentation with arabinoxylan, xyloglucan and pectin resulted in an increased production of short-chain fatty acids. These fibres also promoted the generation of metabolites with potential health benefits, such as indole-3-lactic acid. By combining the in vitro fermentation and cellular co-culture experiments, arabinoxylan and xyloglucan were found to maintain gut epithelial barrier integrity upon lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge, and a blend of cellulose, pectin, and xyloglucan dampened different LPS induced cytokines. Moreover, pectin was found to supportthe growth of a wide range of microbial species in vitro and correlated positively with α-diversity in young children in an observational cohort. Our findings provide insights into the potential benefits of diverse fibre intakes during early life. Further studies are needed to investigate the causal relationship, mechanisms and the effectiveness of specific fibres on the gut microbiome development in young children.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64337-7.title: Histological evaluation of pulpal healing following direct pulp capping with polytetrafluoroethylene or melatonin, with or without adjunctive low-level laser therapy in Wistar rat molars
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64337-7.abstract: Abstract This study evaluated pulpal healing following direct pulp capping with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) or melatonin (MEL), with or without adjunctive low-level laser therapy (LLLT), in Wistar rat molars. Fifty-two maxillary first molars from 26 male Wistar rats were included. Forty-eight molars with standardized pulp exposures were randomly allocated to four groups ( n = 12): Group I, PTFE; Group II, MEL; Group III, PTFE + LLLT; and Group IV, MEL + LLLT; four unexposed molars served as negative controls. LLLT (650 nm, 100 mW; fluence 11.9 J/cm 2 ) was applied after placement of the capping material. Irradiation was performed on alternate days, with animals receiving either three sessions (1-week group) or six sessions (2- and 4-week groups). Histological evaluation was performed after 1, 2, and 4 weeks, assessing inflammation, necrosis, vascularity, fibrosis, odontoblast-like layer organization, dentin bridge formation, and dentin bridge thickness. LLLT-treated groups showed reduced inflammation, improved odontoblast-like layer organization, enhanced vascularity, and greater dentin bridge thickness compared with non-irradiated groups. The MEL + LLLT group demonstrated the most favorable overall histological profile. Adjunctive LLLT was associated with improved pulpal healing outcomes, while melatonin showed supportive effects on the pulpal microenvironment. Their combined application produced the most favorable histological outcomes and warrants further investigation in vital pulp therapy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65184-2.title: MDFNet: a lightweight multi-stream network tailored for real-time GIS and disaster monitoring applications
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65184-2.abstract: Very high-resolution remote sensing image scene classification (RSSC) is a key enabling technology for geographic information systems (GIS) in disaster prevention, emergency response, and recovery. Current methods often suffer from excessive complexity, restricting their capability to meet the stringent computational efficiency requirements of time-sensitive edge deployment. To address these structural bottlenecks, this paper presents MDFNet, a lightweight multi-stream dual-stage fusion network based on transfer learning. The model uses parallel low-, middle-, and high-level streams to extract hierarchical features, adopts a dual attention mechanism to enhance discriminative regions, and employs multi-source feature aggregation to reduce redundancy. Extensive experiments on AID, UC Merced, and NWPU-RESISC45 datasets demonstrate that MDFNet achieves competitive or superior accuracy with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational costs. This parameter-efficient design provides a foundational accelerated architecture highly tailored for prospective real-time GIS inference and emergency mapping.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68401-0.title: Elastoplastic analysis of tunnels in Hoek–Brown rock masses exhibiting strain softening
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68401-0.abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive ring-by-ring semi-analytical framework for elastoplastic analysis of circular tunnels in strain-softening Hoek–Brown rock under hydrostatic in-situ stress. The excavation unloading process is discretized via equal radial stress increments, with the number of concentric calculation rings dynamically growing synchronously with plastic zone expansion from 1 to a preset maximum value n . The solution is implemented outward-inward to track the full evolution of surrounding rock stress and displacement. Three key improvements are made over existing fixed-ring algorithms: (1) an adaptive ring strategy balancing computational efficiency and precision; (2) elimination of extra geometric interpolation assumptions between adjacent ring radii; (3) a normalized radius transformation technique to avoid numerical termination. Convergence analysis shows that negligible calculation error is achieved when n = 1000, and the linear degradation relation of Hoek–Brown strength parameters with plastic shear strain is adopted, whose applicability range for fractured rock masses is clarified. Three groups of comparative cases (existing analytical solutions and FLAC3D numerical results) verify the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method, with relative errors below 3.4%. The proposed approach provides an efficient, stable tool for ground response curve calculation and stability evaluation of fractured tunnel rock masses.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68807-w.title: Dense soccer video captioning with global context and player position awareness
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68807-w.abstract: Abstract Sports video captioning plays an important role in understanding and describing dynamic visual content, and it is particularly challenging for long soccer broadcasts. Existing dense captioning methods often rely on local clips and may miss match-level temporal context or player-position cues, which can lead to captions with insufficient spatial and event-sequence detail. To address these challenges, we propose Spatio-Contextual Perceiver Resampler (SCPR), a framework for single-anchored dense soccer video captioning. SCPR combines three components: (1) global-local feature integration for incorporating long-range video context around each caption anchor; (2) spatial position encoding based on the absolute 2D locations of players; and (3) cross-modal feature fusion that aligns global, local, and spatial features with a trainable language decoder. Evaluated under the SoccerNet-Caption protocol, SCPR improves several captioning metrics, especially CIDEr, and increases recall and F1 in the spotting stage, while some strict localization and ROUGE-style metrics remain stronger for competing baselines. These results suggest that global temporal context and explicit player-position cues are useful for generating more detailed soccer commentaries, while also revealing remaining trade-offs in precise timestamp localization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68633-0.title: The development and contributions of secondary ecological succession to protecting eroding mangrove dominated muddy coasts: evidence from the vietnamese mekong delta
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68633-0.abstract: Recent literature reveals that the ecological restoration of eroding mangrove-dominated muddy coasts (MDMCs) requires human intervention. However, there is limited information regarding secondary ecological succession (SES) in abandoned MDMCs. The Vietnamese Mekong Delta (VMD) coast was selected as a case study in this study to address partially the aforementioned questions. This study was undertaken by the use of semi-structured interviews, field observations, regular monitoring, and analysis of Google images. The findings show that SES development has existed in two forms in two contrasting environments, which are small and fully exposed areas with no structural protection. The SES development first commenced with the formation of entrapping microsites, consisting of patches of grass species ( Ischaemum sp. and Ipomoea pes-caprae ), plant species ( Cyperus stoloniferus ), uprooted Casuarina trees, marine debris, and the aerial roots of mangrove species. These microsites subsequently trapped floating mangrove seeds and propagules to promote the growth of Avicennia and Rhizophora trees. Despite their size, extent, and exposure, these SES areas withstood the region’s strong seasonal waves. However, they have been cleared to make way for other coastal protection measures or replaced by costly coastal erosion control measures, as they were considered as wastelands and/or abandoned areas.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68873-0.title: A bandgap optimization scheme for phononic crystals coupled with acoustic black hole structure
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68873-0.abstract: Abstract A new phononic crystal with an acoustic black hole (ABH) structure and a response surface methodology (RSM)-based optimization scheme for low-frequency bandgap design are proposed in this study. The band structure, formation mechanism, and attenuation characteristics of the proposed design were systematically investigated and compared with two reference models. Through single-factor analysis, six geometric parameters were screened, among which the ABH width, short edge height, and short board width were identified as the most influential on the first bandgap. A Box-Behnken design with 13 numerical experiments was then conducted using the finite element method, and second-order regression models were established to quantitatively link the three key parameters to the bandgap boundaries. The results show that the new phononic crystal exhibits a first bandgap of 12–805 Hz with 70% coverage below 40 Hz. The optimization framework enables accurate customization toward a target frequency range (10–600 Hz), with a maximum prediction error of only 2.0%, confirming its effectiveness as a predictive design tool for low-frequency vibration control.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66497-y.title: Leveraging immunoinformatic techniques for the development of a multi-epitope subunit vaccine targeting virulence-associated proteins of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66497-y.abstract: Abstract Among infectious diseases, tuberculosis is the biggest cause of death worldwide. Thus, controlling TB, a global epidemic, is a major public health concern on a worldwide scale. According to epidemiological modelling, a new vaccination that can prevent TB, especially in adults and adolescents, is necessary to control the disease’s spread, even while medication therapies for the disease are still improving. The development of novel vaccines with broader applicability and improved, long-lasting effectiveness becomes increasingly crucial as strains resistant to various drugs emerge. This work designed a multi-epitope subunit vaccine (MESV) candidateusing immunoinformatic approaches that targets five virulence-associated proteins, Rv0227c, Rv0584, Lipoprotein LprA, Phospholipase C, and Antigen 85 C. Antigenicity, non-allergenicity, and non-toxicity were the criteria used to identify and filter potential CTL, HTL, and B-cell epitopes. High-affinity epitopes connected with suitable spacers and an adjuvant for improved immunogenicity were included in the carried-out vaccine formulation. Validation and structural modelling verified the MESV’s quality and stability. TLR2 and TLR4 receptors have strong interactions, which were further demonstrated through molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations showed low fluctuations and good structural stability. Further, the MMPBSA analysis was introduced to determine the binding affinity of the vaccine construct, and a more pronounced binding affinity was established by the designed vaccine with TLR4. Increased cytokine release, memory cell development, and the developed MESV candidateare viable options warranting further experimental validation, as it may elicit potent humoral and cellular immune responses against M. tuberculosis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68713-1.title: SIGN-AIR: real-time sign language recognition and translation using gesture-aware neural networks on aerial robotic platforms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68713-1.abstract: Abstract Communication barriers experienced by deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals remain a significant challenge, particularly in situations where conventional communication infrastructure is unavailable or fixed-camera systems have limited coverage. This paper presents SIGN-AIR, a UAV-assisted framework for real-time sign language recognition and bidirectional translation. Unlike conventional approaches based on fixed cameras, wearable sensors, or depth cameras, the proposed framework integrates a drone-mounted stabilised RGB camera with onboard edge computing to enable flexible gesture recognition in indoor and outdoor environments. The system combines MediaPipe-based hand landmark extraction with a hybrid CNN–BiLSTM architecture to model both the spatial and temporal characteristics of American Sign Language gestures. Experimental evaluation on a combined dataset comprising the ASL Alphabet and WLASL achieved an overall recognition accuracy of 98.63%, together with high precision, high recall, and a median inference latency of less than 2 s. These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of the proposed UAV-assisted recognition framework under the evaluated experimental conditions and indicate its potential to support communication in scenarios where fixed-camera systems may be affected by occlusions, limited fields of view, or environmental variability. Furthermore, the proposed bidirectional translation pipeline has the potential to facilitate both sign-to-speech and speech-to-sign communication for prospective applications in accessibility, education, public service interactions, and emergency response. Although the current study demonstrates promising technical performance, comprehensive real-world field validation under representative operational conditions remains an important direction for future work.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69499-y.title: Pre-operative serum microRNA profiles differ between metabolic phenotypes and predict metabolic response to sleeve gastrectomy in severe obesity
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69499-y.abstract: Abstract People with severe obesity show marked heterogeneity in cardiometabolic risk, classified as metabolically healthy (MHO) or unhealthy obesity (MUO). In this exploratory pilot study, we performed genome-wide serum microRNA (miRNA) profiling using Agilent SurePrint G3 microarrays (8 × 60 K; 2,549 probes) before and three months after sleeve gastrectomy (SG) in eight people with severe obesity (MHO n = 4; MUO n = 4) classified per Japanese national criteria. Despite comparable body mass index and visceral fat area, people with MUO had significantly higher HOMA-IR, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HbA1c, and AST at baseline (all p = 0.029). Pre-operative miR-5100 expression correlated with baseline HOMA-IR (ρ = 0.805, p = 0.016) and predicted post-operative HOMA-IR reduction (ρ=−0.878, p = 0.004). Pre-operative miR-5585-3p predicted post-operative CRP reduction (ρ=−0.854, p = 0.007). Set analysis identified ten miRNAs, including miR-22-3p, detected in all MUO but no MHO participants. Welch’s t-test identified 23 miRNAs significantly altered post-operatively in MUO versus 8 in MHO. miR-8069 was consistently down-regulated after SG across all participants (Wilcoxon p = 0.016). Consistency across complementary analytical methods supports reliability despite the small sample. These preliminary findings suggest that pre-operative serum miRNA profiles may differ between MHO and MUO phenotypes and may predict metabolic responsiveness to bariatric surgery, and warrant validation in larger independent cohorts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69213-y.title: Comparative germination and early seedling responses of five chickpea genotypes (Cicer arietinum L.) under hexavalent chromium stress
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69213-y.abstract: Abstract Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] is among the most phytotoxic heavy metals entering the agricultural ecosystems of South Asia. It originates almost entirely from industry and is discharged in the untreated effluents of leather tanning, chrome plating and electroplating, textile dyeing, pigment and paint manufacture, wood preservation and metal finishing units, from where it reaches farmland through canal and groundwater irrigation. Chickpea ( Cicer arietinum L.) is the leading rainfed pulse crop of Pakistan, yet the Cr(VI) tolerance of its locally released varieties has never been compared. We hypothesised that Pakistani chickpea genotypes differ significantly in germination and early seedling tolerance to Cr(VI), and that root-related traits discriminate genotypes more effectively than shoot-related traits. Five chickpea genotypes (Paider-91, Punjab-2008, Bhakkar-2011, Thal-2020, and Bittle-2021) were subjected to five concentrations of potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇): 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100 mg L⁻¹ in a completely randomized factorial design with five replicates. Nine morpho-physiological traits were evaluated over 14 days: germination rate (GR), mean germination time (MGT), seedling vigor index (SVI), shoot length (SL), root length (RL), seedling length (S.L), root collar diameter (RCD), fresh weight (FW), and dry weight (DW). Data were analysed by two-way ANOVA, Fisher’s LSD post-hoc test, and Pearson correlation. Chromium stress induced dose-dependent, statistically significant ( p ≤ 0.001) inhibition across all traits. Grand mean GR declined from 94.4% (control) to 80.8% at 100 mg L⁻¹ (-14.4%), while MGT increased by 79.2% (1.97 to 3.53 days). SVI suffered the greatest relative suppression (-69.0%). Punjab-2008 and Bhakkar-2011 consistently outperformed the other genotypes, retaining superior GR, SVI, root and shoot lengths and biomass at maximum stress. Bittle-2021 was the most sensitive genotype for almost every trait measured. Pearson correlation analysis revealed highly significant positive relationships among the growth- and biomass-related traits ( r = 0.561-0.966) and significant negative relationships between MGT and all growth parameters ( r = -0.491 to -0.550). Pakistani chickpea varieties differ appreciably in Cr(VI) tolerance, confirming the study hypothesis. Punjab-2008 and Bhakkar-2011 are accordingly prioritised as donor genotypes for breeding chromium-tolerant varieties, and root length and SVI are recommended as discriminating traits for rapid genotypic screening. The findings provide a practical basis for varietal selection on chromium-affected agricultural soils in Pakistan.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67531-9.title: Experimental investigation of adjustable circular steel connectors for modular steel beam splices
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67531-9.abstract: This study proposes an Adjustable Circular Steel Connector (ACS) for beam-to-beam connections in modular steel structures, which enables continuous on-site length adjustment through the threaded engagement of two cylindrical shanks. The load path through the connection was first examined by finite element analysis, and one monolithic beam and three ACS specimens with connector lengths of 450, 500 and 535 mm (RCS-450, RCS-500 and RCS-535) were then tested under monotonic four-point bending. The threaded engagement remained intact in all tests, with no pull-out or thread stripping; inelastic deformation developed instead in the end bracket and in the adjacent portion of Shank B. Across the tested range of adjustment, the three specimens developed 94%, 86% and 82% of the peak moment (316.9 kN m) and 92%, 84% and 80% of the maximum load (633.8 kN) of the monolithic specimen. Increasing the connector length reduced strength and rotational stiffness but increased rotation capacity. All specimens exceeded a ductility index of 3.0, although in the two specimens exhibiting the larger initial slip the index is affected by the identification of the yield displacement. On-site length adjustment can therefore be accommodated without a disproportionate loss of flexural resistance, with connector length acting as a design parameter that trades strength against deformation capacity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67821-2.title: Effect of the asymmetry of plasmonic multi-shell nanoparticles on the optical response of semiconductor quantum dot-nonconcentric nanoshell hybrid systems
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67821-2.abstract: In this study, the plasmon-exciton interaction in a hybrid system comprising a semiconductor quantum dot (SQD) coupled to a spherical multilayer metallic nanoshell (MNS) with symmetry breaking is theoretically and numerically investigated within the density matrix framework. It is shown that the presence of an asymmetric MNS can strongly affect the optical response of the SQD-MNS system. The effect of the geometrical symmetry breaking of MNS induced by offsetting the core or shell on the optical absorption of the system is demonstrated and discussed. Since asymmetric plasmonic nanoshells with an additional degree of freedom introduce unique and tunable optical properties compared to symmetric nanoshells, we study the linear optical susceptibility of the proposed hybrid molecule interacting with a linearly polarized laser field. The key feature of these nanoscale hybrid structures is their ability to tune and control the optical absorption spectrum, which is crucial for many practical applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68425-6.title: Serial sputum galactomannan as an adjunctive biomarker for the diagnosis of Aspergillus-related airway involvement in patients with cystic fibrosis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68425-6.abstract: Sputum galactomannan index (GMI) has been proposed as an adjunctive biomarker for diagnosing Aspergillus -related airway involvement. This study evaluated sputum GMI as a screening biomarker for Aspergillus colonization and chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF). In this two-year multicenter prospective study, pwCF referred to the Iranian CF Foundation who provided at least two sputum samples within 6 months were enrolled. The optimal sputum GMI cut-off was determined by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Participants were classified as negative, transient colonization (TC), persistent colonization (PC), or CPA using an operational case definition for resource-constrained settings in the absence of Aspergillus -specific IgG testing. The diagnostic performance of sputum GMI was evaluated across these groups. Among 235 pwCF, 545 sputum specimens were analyzed for fungal culture and GMI. Of 304 Aspergillus isolates, A. flavus (30.9%) was the predominant species. Overall, 13.6%, 6.8%, 41.3%, and 38.3% of participants were classified as CPA, PC, TC, and negative, respectively. Median sputum GMI was significantly lower in the negative group (0.58) than in the CPA (0.68) and PC (0.87) groups. GMI was also significantly higher in the combined clinical group (CPA and PC) than in the non-clinical group (TC and negative) ( P < 0.001). ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.67 (95% CI, 0.584–0.768), with an optimal GMI cut-off of ≥ 0.67 (sensitivity, 62%; specificity, 62%). Sputum GMI may serve as a useful adjunctive screening biomarker for clinically significant Aspergillus airway involvement in pwCF but should complement, rather than replace, conventional microbiological and clinical assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67691-8.title: Multiscale insights into the diffusion of SF6/N2 mixtures via machine-learning interatomic potentials
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67691-8.abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF 6 ) is widely used as an insulating and arc-extinguishing medium in high-voltage electrical equipment due to its excellent dielectric properties and insulation performance. However, SF 6 is also a potent greenhouse gas, so mixing SF 6 with an inert gas such as N 2 is a promising way to reduce its usage. The diffusion properties of SF 6 /N 2 mixtures play a crucial role in gas-mixture separation or replenishment, because they determine the proportion and uniformity of the mixtures. By combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) simulations of SF 6 and N 2 in SF 6 /N 2 mixtures, we systematically characterize their multiscale diffusion dynamics. At short times, both SF 6 and N 2 exhibit the expected ballistic regime with super-diffusive scaling. At intermediate times, SF 6 shows a more pronounced plateau-like crossover than N 2 , which is consistent with the molecular flexibility of SF6 and the associated rotational and vibrational dynamics. At longer times, both SF 6 and N 2 gradually approach normal diffusion. A theoretical model is also proposed to quantitatively describe the non-Fickian features of the MSD curves. This work provides a more complete physical picture of SF 6 and N 2 dynamics in SF 6 /N 2 mixtures and offers a useful reference for gas replenishment in SF 6 /N 2 mixed electrical equipment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69367-9.title: Geospatial assessment of household food safety risk and microbial contamination vulnerability in an urbanising Nigerian City
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69367-9.abstract: Foodborne illnesses remain an important public health issue in fast-growing urban areas of Nigerian cities and household food safety knowledge and practices are anomalously distributed. In Ibadan metropolis social, economic, and environmental conditions may play a role in increasing household vulnerability to food safety risks, but these influences are not well understood spatially. This study was based on household-level questions about food safety knowledge, practices and contamination, and was driven by a desire to understand food safety vulnerabilities at the household level and how this state is affected by socioeconomic and environmental factors across the city. This cross-sectional study was conducted across 604 households in five Local Government Areas of Ibadan Metropolis using proportional multi-stage sampling. A structured questionnaire administered via REDCap with GPS-recorded household locations captured food safety knowledge, behaviours, and perceived control. A random subsample of 250 households (500 food contact surfaces) underwent microbiological assessment using ATP bioluminescence and Total Coliform testing; a matched comparison group of 50 households (100 surfaces) was included; this group was not a randomised or experimental control, so “comparison group” is used throughout to avoid implying an experimental design. Spatial distribution of food safety indicators and household vulnerability were mapped using ArcGIS 10, with vulnerability levels derived from an index-based framework adapted from Schwarz and Kuleshov. Across 604 households in Ibadan, food safety knowledge and practices showed clear spatial and socioeconomic disparities. Between 22 and 27% of households exhibited unsafe food handling behaviours, particularly in low-income areas with limited infrastructure. Only 28.9% had access to piped water, 46.5% had adequate kitchen facilities, and 39.7% accessed formal waste collection services. More than half (53.5%) prepared food in semi-open or outdoor spaces. Perceived control over food safety was lowest in Ibadan North East and Ibadan South East. Microbiological testing of 500 food contact surfaces showed 48.2% ATP failure (threshold: manufacturer-recommended RLU cutoff), compared to 18% in the comparison group. Total Coliform analysis revealed that 61.2% of tested food contact surfaces (306 of 500) were contaminated, with 42.4% classified as highly contaminated (≥ 100 CFU/cm²) and 38.8% undetected. Visually apparent co-occurrence (not tested using formal spatial statistics) suggested that low knowledge, unsafe behaviours, limited perceived control, and high contamination co-occurred in high-vulnerability neighbourhoods. Household food safety risks in Ibadan are influenced by multiple, interlinking socioeconomic and environmental factors that create distinct spatial patterns in vulnerability. The study provides insights into targeted, context-bound interventions focusing on high-risk neighbourhoods, addressing both knowledge gaps and structural limitations in household food safety practices. Strengthening community-based education, improving household food-handling environments, and engaging local stakeholders are important for curbing foodborne illness risks in rapidly growing urban settings. These findings provide empirical evidence from Nigeria to inform equitable and place-based food safety planning for urban households.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69102-4.title: Multi-cancer profiling and breast cancer validation reveal YME1L1 as a potential immune-related factor and prognostic biomarker
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69102-4.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction constitutes a fundamental driver of neoplastic transformation. YME1L1, an inner mitochondrial membrane-resident AAA+ metalloprotease, is associated with protein homeostasis in the inner mitochondrial membrane and intermembrane space, thus participating in cellular metabolic reprogramming. Nevertheless, systematic interrogation of YME1L1 across Multiple cancers remains conspicuously absent. We harnessed public repositories including TCGA, GTEx, GEO, HPA, cBioPortal, and GSCA to comprehensively delineate YME1L1 expression landscapes, prognostic implications, diagnostic performance, genomic alteration patterns, and predicted immuno-oncological correlations across diverse malignancies via bioinformatics. Subsequent in vitro assays and BALB/c nude xenograft models verified cell-intrinsic oncogenic phenotypes of YME1L1. YME1L1 was notably upregulated in most solid carcinomas, with its amplified expression consistently predicting inferior patient outcomes. YME1L1 transcript levels were significantly correlated with TMB, MSI and HRD, well-known molecular markers related to immunotherapy response, suggesting a potential multidimensional association between YME1L1 expression and tumor immune characteristics. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that genes correlated with YME1L1 were enriched in ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis, mitochondrial translation, and multiple pro-tumorigenic signaling cascades such as the Wnt and Hippo pathways ; however, direct regulation of these pathways by YME1L1 was not experimentally validated. In BRCA specimens, YME1L1 expression markedly exceeded that of normal mammary counterparts. Experimental manipulation suggests that elevated YME1L1 expression may contribute to enhanced proliferative capacity, clonogenic potential, migratory behavior, and invasive properties of breast cancer cells; xenograft studies further corroborated that YME1L1 overexpression accelerated subcutaneous tumor growth, whereas its knock down effectively restrained neoplastic proliferation. Of note, nude mice lack mature T cells and cannot confirm these predicted immune phenotypes. Through multi-tumor profiling coupled with breast cancer functional validation, this investigation reveal YME1L1 as a predicted immune-related influencing factor and therapeutic target, .Our data underscore YME1L1’s clinical relevance and its promise as a novel therapeutic target for various cancers.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69287-8.title: A two-step phosphorus–sulfur wet-process phosphoric acid route enabling simultaneous rare earth leaching and co-production of high-whiteness hemihydrate gypsum whiskers
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69287-8.abstract: The conventional wet-process phosphoric acid production results in most associated rare earth elements (REEs) being retained in phosphogypsum, rendering their recovery uneconomical. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel two-step phosphorus-sulfur wet process. In the first step, phosphate concentrate was leached with phosphoric acid to simultaneously dissolve phosphorus and REEs. In the second step, sulfuric acid was added for selective calcium precipitation, enabling phosphoric acid recovery and the production of high-whiteness hemihydrate gypsum whiskers. Characterizations and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to elucidate REE migration mechanisms. Experimental results indicated that the leaching rates of phosphorus and REEs reached 97.68% and 90.25%, respectively, in the leaching stage. Fluorapatite lattice dissociation occurred during this process, synchronously releasing REEs embedded in the lattice. In the decalcification stage, the phosphoric acid yield reached 98.57%, gypsum whiteness reached 98.4%, and 30.72% of REEs were lost via co-precipitation. The overall phosphorus utilization efficiency and total rare earth element (ΣREE) recovery rate of the process were 96.28% and 62.53%, respectively. Simulations based on simplified aqueous systems verified that all crystallographic planes of hemihydrate gypsum can adsorb Y³⁺, suggesting that surface adsorption may contribute to REE loss under certain conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68105-5.title: Effect of RNA minimum free energy and spacer on silencing of four Sclerotinia sclerotiorum virulence genes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68105-5.abstract: Development of RNA silencing technologies offer new options to manage plant diseases. During the silencing process the minimum free energy (MFE) of the siRNA/miRNA structures used can significantly influence their ability to silence the target genes. Therefore, this research focused on the impact of MFE in silencing of four S. sclerotiorum genes, Chitin binding domain, Mitogen-activated protein kinase, oxaloacetate acetylhydrolase, and Abhydrolase-3. For this, double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), individually and as a combination of genes, was synthesized in vitro. The hairpin RNA (hpRNA) from these genes as a tandem repeat sequence was synthesized in vitro and in vivo. Treating S. sclerotiorum mycelial colonies with 7 ng/µl of dsRNA completely silenced all target genes when compared to the control, independently of their MFE. In a separate study, the application of 0.12 ng/µl of low MFE (LMFE) hpRNA resulted in greater ( P = 0.05) silencing of all genes compared to the control and of three of the four genes when compared to the high MFE (HMFE) sequences. Spraying canola ( Brassica napus ) plants with LMFE hpRNA reduced ( P = 0.05) disease severity compared to control and to the HMFE hpRNA. Additionally, the presence of a spacer in hpRNA increased ( P = 0.05) silencing efficiency. Under the conditions of this study, the MFE and RNA spacers evaluated played a critical role in the efficacy of RNA silencing and should be considered when designing strategies for pathogen control.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69243-6.title: AFF-net: adaptive feature fusion network for efficient medical image segmentation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69243-6.abstract: Medical image segmentation is essential for clinical diagnosis and treatment. Existing convolution and self-attention-based segmentation methods suffer from heavy computational overhead, while complex lesion morphology and blurred anatomical boundaries further degrade segmentation performance. To address the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in medical segmentation, this work proposes a lightweight adaptive feature fusion network (AFF-Net) with an optimized adapter fine-tuning paradigm. AFF-Net embeds a plug-and-play multi-scale perception adapter (MSPA) in the backbone to achieve efficient multi-scale feature learning and avoid feature drift caused by conventional full fine-tuning on limited medical data. Furthermore, we integrate a lightweight multi-scale convolutional attention block (LMCAB) into the efficient multi-scale convolutional attention decoder (EMCAD) to adaptively fuse multi-level spatial and channel features and mitigate information attenuation. Benefiting from this streamlined embedded decoder design, the network strengthens semantic representation and effectively refines ambiguous anatomical edge details. Evaluated on Synapse and ACDC datasets, AFF-Net achieves competitive or superior performance against state-of-the-art methods with lower computational costs. Ablation experiments validate the efficacy of core modules and the adapter fine-tuning strategy, demonstrating the practical clinical application potential of the proposed lightweight network. The codes and models are available at https://github.com/wangru1026/AFF-Net .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67787-1.title: Genetic and molecular analyses of HDAC11 in diabetes and its complications
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67787-1.abstract: Abstract Diabetes mellitus (DM) and its complications remain major clinical challenges despite advances in prevention and treatment. Histone Deacetylase 11 (HDAC11) has been implicated in glucose metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and inflammatory cytokine (IC) regulation, suggesting potential relevance to diabetes-related phenotypes. This study investigated the associations among genetically proxied lower HDAC11 expression, ICs, and DM-related outcomes. We applied a drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) framework to evaluate genetically proxied lower HDAC11 expression. The primary analysis used inverse-variance weighting (IVW), with MR-Egger, weighted median, simple mode, and weighted mode as complementary methods. Robustness was evaluated using heterogeneity tests, MR-Egger intercept tests, leave-one-out analysis, and MR-PRESSO. Two-step MR was used to assess IC-mediated pathways. Colocalization analysis assessed whether HDAC11 eQTL and diabetes-related outcome signals shared a causal variant. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis and molecular docking explored potential molecular links. The primary instrument retained eight single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Genetically proxied lower HDAC11 expression was associated with lower odds of diabetic ketoacidosis, diabetic nephropathy, and type 2 diabetes and with higher odds of diabetic neuropathy; associations with diabetic maculopathy and diabetic retinopathy were not statistically significant. Effect directions were generally consistent under stricter LD clumping, although statistical support weakened as fewer variants were retained. Heterogeneity tests, MR-Egger intercept analyses, and MR-PRESSO did not detect substantial heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy. Colocalization provided low support for shared causal variants. ICs, including IL-2, IL-10, IL-13, and IL-18, showed evidence of potential direction-consistent mediation, whereas selected ICs showed opposite-direction or suppressive pathways. PPI and molecular docking analyses identified HDAC11-related molecular relationships for further study. These analyses identify hypothesis-generating associations between genetically proxied lower HDAC11 expression and selected diabetes-related outcomes. Inflammatory pathways provide candidate mechanisms, while threshold-dependent estimates and limited colocalization support motivate tissue-relevant studies of HDAC11 biology and inhibition.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68747-5.title: Seismic behavior and failure assessment of historical masonry minarets in the Bitlis urban conservation area with numerical analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68747-5.abstract: Abstract Bitlis, in the Eastern Anatolia Region, has hosted many civilizations and has a rich cultural heritage. Historical masonry minarets are an important part of this heritage. These structures reflect the architectural and aesthetic features of their period and link the past and the present. In this study, eight historical masonry minarets in the urban conservation area of Bitlis were examined. Field observations and measurements were carried out, and the minarets were evaluated in terms of their structural characteristics. They were classified based on plan type, layout, shaft form, base type, transition zone, balcony arrangement, material type, and structural system. The results show both similarities and differences among the minarets. A detailed numerical analysis was performed for the minaret of Kureyşi Mosque in the city center of Bitlis. The three-dimensional finite element model was created based on data obtained from field measurements. Modal analysis was carried out to identify the dynamic characteristics of the structure. The resulting natural frequencies were calibrated against the empirical period-height relationships reported in the literature. Nonlinear time-history analyses were carried out to evaluate the seismic behavior of the minaret. Plastic strain energy (PE) was used as the main indicator. Before strengthening, the minaret showed clear nonlinear behavior and large displacements at an early stage of the ground motion. After FRP strengthening, the structural stiffness increased, and the natural frequencies became higher. The plastic strain energy was distributed more evenly after strengthening. The model also exhibited lower displacements and remained stable throughout the analysis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68671-8.title: Understanding the determinants influencing middle-aged and elderly users’ continuous use intention of mobile news apps
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68671-8.abstract: This study aims to examine the determinants of middle-aged and older users’ continuous use intention toward mobile news apps. Based on the ECM and the UTAUT2, this study developed a theoretical model to explain users’ continuous use intention after adopting mobile news apps, while incorporating two individual characteristic variables closely related to middle-aged and older users: technology anxiety and health condition. A total of 385 valid responses were collected through an online questionnaire, and structural equation modeling was subsequently employed to test the proposed hypotheses. The results indicate that effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, hedonic motivation, habit, and health condition all have significant positive effects on expectation confirmation. Expectation confirmation further has significant effects on satisfaction and performance expectancy and indirectly influences continuous use intention through both variables, with the indirect effect through satisfaction being stronger than that through performance expectancy. Both satisfaction and performance expectancy have significant positive effects on continuous use intention, but the direct effect of satisfaction is stronger than that of performance expectancy. In contrast, technology anxiety does not have a significant effect on expectation confirmation. The findings indicate that middle-aged and older users’ continued use of mobile news apps depends not only on functional value but also on factors such as physical condition, convenience, social support, entertainment experience, and daily habits. This study provides new evidence for understanding the continued use behavior of mobile news apps among middle-aged and older users and offers practical implications for the age-friendly design and optimization of mobile news apps.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69379-5.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis identifies a senescence-associated myeloid transcriptional program in acute myocardial infarction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69379-5.abstract: Abstract Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) triggers extensive immune activation that critically contributes to cardiac injury and post-infarction remodeling. Although senescence-associated molecular programs have been increasingly implicated in cardiovascular disease, their cellular distribution and systemic immune relevance in AMI remain incompletely understood. Herein, we use multi-omics analyses to identify a myeloid-centered senescence-associated program in AMI. Senescence-associated transcriptional activity was predominantly enriched in myeloid cells, with myeloid populations showing higher senescence-associated transcriptional scores exhibiting inflammatory and secretory features. Senescence-associated transcriptional activity was spatially associated with myeloid-enriched regions within the infarcted myocardium during the early post-MI phase. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the cell-cycle-arrest/DDR-associated component was not fully explained by inflammatory/SASP activity. Integrative analyses across cardiac tissue and peripheral blood datasets identified a reproducible senescence-associated gene signature across cardiac and peripheral blood datasets. Among the identified genes, AQP9 and SOCS3 showed robust discriminative performance across independent cohorts, with consistent performance across multiple classification algorithms. Immune cell infiltration analysis and single-cell analyses linked both genes to myeloid-enriched inflammatory states, while gene set enrichment analyses associated their expression with innate immune activation and repression of cell cycle related pathways. Validation using coronary blood samples in our in-house cohort further supported elevated expression of AQP9, SOCS3, and the cell-cycle arrest-associated gene CDKN1A in patients with AMI. Collectively, our findings identify a conserved myeloid-centered senescence-associated inflammatory program in AMI and highlight coordinated changes between tissue-level immune remodeling and systemic transcriptional alterations. These findings provide insight into senescence-associated immune remodeling in AMI and highlight AQP9 and SOCS3 as candidate genes linked to this myeloid inflammatory activation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68223-0.title: Lycopene attenuates ischemic-hypoxic injury in random skin flaps via the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68223-0.abstract: Random skin flaps are commonly used in plastic and reconstructive surgeries. However, one of the most serious postoperative complications is the necrosis of distal portion of flap, which is mainly caused by a lack of blood flow. The nuclear factor erythroid-2 related factor 2 (Nrf2) can directly regulate the activity of heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1). Previous studies have shown that the powerful antioxidant lycopene (Lyc) attenuates renal injury by mitigating inflammation and apoptosis, which aroused our interest as to whether Lyc could promote the survival of ischemic flaps. In this study, we focused on analyzing the mechanism of Lyc after ischemic-hypoxic injury to skin flaps. The potential targets and mechanisms of Lyc in the ischemic situation can be predicted by network pharmacological analysis. Our results showed that Lyc promotes angiogenesis and attenuates oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis to improve the survival of random skin flaps. These findings could be attributed to the mediation and regulation of the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway by Lyc, as the blocking effect of brusatol on this pathway effectively inhibited the abovementioned occurrences. In conclusion, our study sheds new light on the therapeutic potential and clinical application of Lyc in enhancing random skin flap viability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69203-0.title: Unraveling the dual interaction patterns of land use intensity on carbon balance: spatial heterogeneity and drivers in a transitional region of China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69203-0.abstract: Abstract Under China’s “Dual Carbon” goals, accurate assessment of regional carbon balance is of critical importance. Land use acts as a core factor governing carbon balance. However, the differentiated effects of land use intensity (LUI)—a comprehensive indicator quantifying human intervention on carbon storage, sequestration, and emissions, as well as their spa-tial driving factors, remain poorly understood. Here we incorporate multi-source remote sensing datasets and the GeoDetector model to systematically explore the spatio-temporal linkages between LUI and carbon balance components in Anhui Province, Chi-na, during the period 2000–2020. Our results reveal that LUI exhibits dual spatial associations on car-bon balance components: LUI shows significant negative spatial correlations with carbon storage (CSt), sequestration (CSeq), and net carbon (NetC), but a significant positive corre-lation with carbon emissions (CE). Notably, in 2020, negative association clusters, covering approximately 22% of the study area, were located in the southern mountains. In contrast, the “High LUI - High CE” agglomerations are centered in the northern urban clusters. GeoDetector further demonstrates that the spatial patterns of CSt and CSeq are primarily associated with interactions between LUI and natural factors (NDVI) (q > 0.4), while the spatial pattern of CE is dominated by interactions between LUI and socio-economic factors (GDP) (q > 0.6). These findings reveal dual interaction patterns through which LUI is associated with carbon balance—a strong joint explanatory effect of LUI and NDVI in the south and a strong joint explanatory effect of LUI and GDP in the north—providing scientific support for regional carbon governance strategies that target these two distinct patterns: protecting existing sinks in the south and curbing emissions in the north.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65422-7.title: TRIM26 aggravates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury via promoting TAK1-mediated JNK/P38 MAPK pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65422-7.abstract: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide, with ischemic stroke accounting for the majority. During ischemic stroke, timely intervention of blood flow is life-critical, but cerebral injury after reperfusion is most related to patient prognosis. A thorough understanding of regulatory mechanisms would be helpful in exploring effective drugs for cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. As an E3 ubiquitin ligase, TRIM26 has been demonstrated to play a significant regulatory role in viral infections as well as in various types of cancers. In this study, we found that the protein level of TRIM26 was increased in both in vivo and in vitro models of cerebral I/R injury. In mice, Trim26 knockout alleviated cerebral infarcted area, reduced inflammatory cytokine expressions and the activation of NF-κB signaling pathway, and decreased apoptosis. Likewise, knocking down Trim26 reduced cell inflammatory responses and apoptosis in primary neurons. However, overexpressing Trim26 produced opposite effects. The expressions of activated TAK1, JNK and P38 were found positively correlated with the expression of TRIM26. Inhibiting the activity of TAK1 abolished the regulatory effect of TRIM26 overexpression on inflammatory responses and apoptosis in primary neurons. TRIM26 exerted detrimental roles in the regulation of cerebral I/R injury depending on the activation of TAK1. TRIM26-TAK1 axis would shed light on new therapeutic strategy development for ischemic stroke.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69511-5.title: Microwave-assisted engineering of spinel ferrite–graphene nanohybrids for high-energy asymmetric supercapacitors
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69511-5.abstract: Supercapacitors are widely known for their high power density, fast charge-discharge rates, and excellent cycling stability. However, enhancing the energy density of supercapacitors while maintaining their high power remains a key challenge for this electrochemical energy storage device. In this work, spinel ferrite–graphene nanohybrids are synthesized via a microwave-assisted co-precipitation method. This approach enables the rapid, uniform decoration of ferrite nanoparticles on graphene nanosheets. Structural characterization confirms the in-situ formation of crystalline spinel phases embedded within the graphene matrix under controlled thermal conditions. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the charge storage process is mainly diffusion-controlled due to the redox activity of the ferrite phase. The optimized electrode delivers a specific capacitance of 1467 F g –1 at a current density of 1 A g –1 , along with reasonable rate capability. Moreover, an all-solid-state asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device is assembled using the optimized nanohybrid. The ASC device achieves a notable energy density of 86.53 Wh kg –1 and a power density of 4882.35 W kg –1 . Furthermore, the device maintains stable cycling performance over 10,000 cycles. These results provide an evolution of spinel ferrite–graphene nanohybrids and the critical role of interfacial design in enhancing the electrochemical performance of such nanohybrids.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69246-3.title: Comparing radial and brachial blood pressure measurements among people with large arm circumference: MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69246-3.abstract: Recently, radial blood pressure cuffs have been developed for use among individuals with large arm circumferences although unique hypertension thresholds for radial assessment are not defined. We compared systolic and diastolic blood pressure measured from the upper arm and forearm among individuals with obesity. In a sub-study of participants who were living with HIV and without HIV with upper arm circumference > 40 cm ( n = 88, 2022–2023) in the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study/Women’s Interagency HIV Study-Combined Cohort Study, both brachial and radial BP were measured with an automated monitor using a thigh cuff and a forearm cuff, respectively. Among 88 participants, 81% were female, 90% were Black, and 72% were living with HIV. The correlation between radial and brachial measurements was 0.60 for systolic and 0.69 for diastolic blood pressure. Average radial values were higher than brachial values for both systolic (16.5 mmHg higher: 148.3 versus 131.8 mmHg, p < 0.001) and diastolic (13.2 mmHg higher: 85.2 versus 72.0 mmHg, p < 0.001) blood pressure. When measured in the same participants, radial blood pressure was substantially higher than brachial blood pressure. When measuring radial blood pressure, a different threshold for hypertension diagnosis or use of a model to estimate brachial blood pressure may be needed.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68212-3.title: Pricing autonomy under global shocks: a parsimonious and empirically validated SVAR-transformer framework for Shanghai crude oil futures market maturity
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68212-3.abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic response of Shanghai crude oil futures (INE) to international benchmark price shocks and evaluates the evolution of market maturity from its inception to early 2025. Using weekly data from March 30, 2018, to April 30, 2025, we propose a hybrid modeling framework that integrates a Structural Vector Autoregression (SVAR) with a Transformer architecture. The SVAR component captures linear structural relationships and enables economic interpretation through impulse response and variance decomposition, while the Transformer—specifically its linear attention mechanism—models nonlinear dynamics and extreme event patterns that elude purely linear models. Rather than assuming that the neural component is superior by construction, the framework is evaluated against a conventional VAR/SVAR, a multilayer perceptron (MLP), and a linear-attention-only specification using chronological holdout evaluation, expanding-window validation, ablation tests, and alternative structural identification schemes. The full hybrid specification reduces the out-of-sample RMSE for INE returns by approximately 7.7% relative to VAR(2), while the improvement over the linear-attention-only specification is concentrated in high-volatility weeks. The mean nonlinear contribution ratio is approximately 0.184 in crisis weeks compared with 0.051 in normal weeks. Empirical results reveal a three-stage maturation process: an initial cultivation period (2018–2019) characterized by external-dependent mild fluctuations; an extreme shock period (2020–2022) marked by resonance-driven volatility; and a mature transition period (2023–2025) where internal and external shocks achieve more balanced contributions. The findings indicate that INE has moved toward greater market maturity, with improved but still incomplete pricing autonomy. The unconditional variance decomposition remains close to the conventional SVAR result, whereas the principal incremental contribution of the hybrid model lies in identifying state-dependent nonlinear adjustments during crisis periods. Results remain qualitatively robust under sign restrictions, a long-run restriction, and reverse recursive ordering.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69323-7.title: Palestinian consumers’ perspectives on integrating traditional, folk, and home remedies with conventional medicine for illness prevention and management in the northern West Bank
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69323-7.abstract: Traditional, folk, and home remedies (TFHR) are deeply embedded in Palestinian culture and healthcare-seeking behavior, shaped by centuries of historical occupation, limited healthcare access, and rich ethnomedical heritage. Despite their widespread use, there remains a scarcity of qualitative, community-level research documenting the perceptions, attitudes, and practices surrounding TFHR in Palestine. This study aimed to explore and document the perceptions, attitudes, and practices related to traditional, folk, and home remedies among adults in the northern West Bank, Palestine, and to examine how these are integrated with conventional medicine in the prevention and management of illness and disease. A qualitative descriptive design employing directed qualitative content analysis, following the approach described by Hsieh and Shannon, was used. Face-to-face, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 35 community-dwelling adults recruited from Nablus Governorate in the northern West Bank, Palestine, including Nablus city, the surrounding villages of Beit Dajan, Salem, and Asira al-Shamaliya, and the Balata and Askar refugee camps. Participants were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling. Data collection continued until thematic saturation was achieved, defined as the point at which no new themes emerged from the data and confirmed through three additional interviews. Data were managed and coded using MAXQDA 2022. Directed qualitative content analysis was then performed, leading to the identification of three overarching themes and multiple subcategories. Three overarching themes emerged: (1) Knowledge and Practices of TFHR, encompassing types and methods used and sources of knowledge; (2) Attitudes toward TFHR, including perceived usefulness, consultation with healthcare professionals, advice and recommendations to others, and perception of safety; and (3) Use and Application of TFHR, covering determinants of use, prioritization and integration with modern medicine, and indications of use. The predominant pattern across all settings was the intergenerational transmission of TFHR knowledge through family networks, with grandmothers and mothers identified as primary knowledge holders. Herbal medicines (Za’atar, sage, black seed, olive oil), dietary therapies, and spiritual/religious practices were most commonly used. Attitudes ranged from strong belief in TFHR effectiveness to cautious acceptance, with safety concerns particularly heightened for pregnant women and children. Economic barriers, dissatisfaction with conventional care, limited healthcare access due to movement restrictions, and cultural identity emerged as key drivers of use. Regarding integration with conventional medicine, participants described three patterns: using TFHR as a first-line treatment before seeking biomedical care for mild symptoms, using TFHR alongside prescribed medications without informing providers, and, less commonly, discussing TFHR use with providers to obtain guidance on safe integration; most participants did not disclose their TFHR use to healthcare professionals. Healthcare providers should routinely inquire about TFHR use, recognize these culturally embedded practices, and engage patients in culturally sensitive discussions to minimize herb–drug interactions and other potential risks. Further research is needed to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and appropriate regulatory and educational strategies for integrating TFHR into Palestinian healthcare services.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67491-0.title: Hyperspectral handwriting analysis for writer verification and ink mismatch detection using a hybrid CNN–LSTM model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67491-0.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging captures detailed spectral reflectance information over a broad wavelength range, providing capabilities beyond those of conventional RGB imaging. This rich spectral information can be used in forensic document analysis to identify subtle variations in ink composition and handwriting characteristics that cannot be detected using conventional imaging methods. Nevertheless, current research tends to focus on writer analysis and ink discrimination as two distinct tasks, and in many cases, ignores the potential of their combination.This paper proposes a unified spectral–spatial metric-learning framework for hyperspectral handwriting analysis that jointly addresses writer verification and ink mismatch detection through a shared sentence-level embedding space. Each sample is modeled as a three-dimensional hyperspectral cube containing 149 spectral bands, with spatial dimensions standardized during preprocessing. To minimize variability introduced by image acquisition conditions, band-wise normalization is applied. The framework employs a hybrid CNN–LSTM architecture as the feature learning backbone, where convolutional neural networks extract discriminative spatial handwriting characteristics and the LSTM models spectral dependencies across hyperspectral bands. A contrastive learning strategy optimizes the shared embedding space, enabling similarity-based verification through Euclidean distance between learned representations. Comprehensive experiments conducted on a large-scale hyperspectral handwriting dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for both tasks. The results demonstrate that learning a unified spectral–spatial representation within a verification-oriented framework improves representation consistency, enhances generalization to previously unseen writers and ink samples, and highlights the practical applicability of hyperspectral imaging for forensic document analysis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69635-8.title: Sn-doped CuO nanostructures as a fast and sensitive miniaturized temperature sensor
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69635-8.abstract: This study reports the successful fabrication of a highly sensitive temperature sensor based on Sn-doped CuO nanostructures (NSs). Pure CuO NSs were synthesized via a solution-based process and Sn-doped CuO NSs were synthesized by a solution-based co-precipitation method by adding SnCl 4 .5H 2 O to the copper acetate solution with the aim of lattice incorporation of Sn 4+ ions into the CuO structure. Pure and Sn-doped CuO NSs were annealed at 400 °C for 2 h. Sensors were fabricated by coating of sensing materials on alumina substrate equipped with Pt electrodes. The sensor’s temperature was regulated with an integrated micro-heater. As temperature varied from 30 to 170 °C, the resistance changed accordingly, allowing the sensor to detect temperature shifts within this range. Sn-doped CuO NSs sensor demonstrated a temperature coefficient ratio (TCR) of -0.70%°C − 1 and a sensitivity of -41.93 MΩ/°C, indicating high sensitivity for practical applications. Additionally, the sensor exhibited fast response time and high stability. The obtained results suggest the high potential for developing a highly sensitive, stable, and portable temperature sensor based on Sn-doped CuO NSs. The enhanced performance is mainly attributed to the effects of Sn doping on the electronic structure and morphology of CuO

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68937-1.title: Bridging efficiency and heat-generation analysis in perovskite solar cells through integrated opto–electro–thermal modeling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68937-1.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive numerical opto-electro-thermal simulation framework for planar and half-tandem perovskite solar cells (PSCs), emphasizing the critical role of absorber-layer thickness in device optimization. Using CsPbI 3 and FASnI 3 as absorbers, we systematically analyze both planar and half-tandem configurations to simultaneously enhance light absorption, carrier generation, and electrical performance, and heat-generation characteristics. The simulation results show that for the planar PSC, increasing the CsPbI 3 thickness from 200 nm to 600 nm improves the J sc from 14.01 to 18.62 mA/cm 2 and raises the PCE to 21.76%. In contrast, a simulated half-tandem structure comprising a 200 nm CsPbI 3 layer and a 700 nm FASnI 3 layer achieves remarkable performance, with a J sc of 28.17 mA/cm 2 , a V oc of 1.32 V, and a PCE of 31.2%—demonstrating a substantial efficiency gain over single-junction devices. This study establishes a unified opto–electro–thermal simulation framework that correlates absorber-layer thickness with optical absorption, carrier transport, and dominant heat-generation mechanisms. The proposed framework systematically investigates the dominant heat-generation mechanisms, including carrier thermalization, Joule heating, and non-radiative recombination, as functions of absorber-layer thickness. The presented framework provides an effective numerical approach for simultaneously optimizing photovoltaic performance while evaluating internal heat-generation characteristics in perovskite solar cells.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67613-8.title: A metabolite-pair controlled quiescence switch via ATP-dependent phase separation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67613-8.abstract: Abstract Amino acid oxidation during carbon starvation inevitably generates NH₄⁺ and HCO₃⁻ as byproducts. Here we show that this metabolite pair acts synergistically to deplete cellular ATP, a task neither accomplishes alone. Rather than nutrient starvation itself, it is this specific energy crisis that triggers quiescence. ATP depletion relieves the nucleotide’s previously described function as a biological hydrotrope—independent of its hydrolysis—that normally maintains the solubility of a defined subset of proteins. The resulting selective phase separation assembles regrowth-delay (RD) bodies, which sequester key growth-related proteins and enforce a reversible dormant state. Crucially, restoration of ATP levels fully dissolves these condensates and permits resumption of growth, with initial ATP levels in dormant cells predicting awakening times. Strikingly, this NH₄⁺/HCO₃⁻-dependent pathway also induces a reversible quiescent state in yeast, suggesting a conserved metabolite-controlled dormancy switch across biological kingdoms.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69539-7.title: Dose-dependent cholinergic, inflammatory, and genotoxic effects of etoxazole in female Wistar rats
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69539-7.abstract: Etoxazole is a widely used oxazoline acaricide in agriculture; however, its toxicological profile in mammalian systems remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the dose-dependent effects of subchronic etoxazole exposure on serum biochemical, genotoxic, and haematological parameters in female Wistar rats administered 25, 100, 250, 500, or 750 mg/kg by oral gavage for 28 days. Body weight, feed and water consumption were monitored weekly, and acetylcholinesterase (AChE), butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), adenosine deaminase (ADA), myeloperoxidase (MPO), and oxidative DNA damage (8-OHdG) were evaluated as biochemical parameters in serum, liver, and kidney tissues, while haematological indices (WBC, RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, MCHC, PLT, and differential counts) were assessed from peripheral blood. AChE and BChE activities decreased in a dose-dependent manner, with significant inhibition observed at doses of 250 mg/kg and above across all three biological compartments ( p < 0.05); notably, serum AChE inhibition was detectable at the lowest dose tested. ADA and MPO activities were significantly elevated at 250 mg/kg and above ( p < 0.05), indicating enhanced inflammatory activity and oxidative stress. DNA damage increased progressively with dose and was particularly pronounced in the ETX500 and ETX750 groups, with renal tissue displaying significant genotoxic effects even at the lowest dose examined. High-dose exposure was further associated with leukocytosis, erythrocytic alterations, and reduced feed and water intake, while body weight gain was maintained across all groups without statistically significant intergroup differences. These findings collectively demonstrate dose-dependent inhibition of cholinesterase activity, consistent with altered cholinergic homeostasis, alongside oxidative-inflammatory and genotoxic effects in rats, identifying the liver and kidney as primary biochemical target compartments — as indicated by enzymatic and genotoxic markers — and highlighting the need for more comprehensive mammalian toxicological assessment of this compound.
