doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68343-7.title: Modelling resilient species for the restoration of the Green Dam in Algeria
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68343-7.abstract: Algeria has long suffered from ongoing desertification, resulting in the progressive loss of vegetation and soil erosion. This has had a severe impact on rural livelihoods in the north, making local communities more vulnerable and causing a decline in biodiversity. In an attempt to counter these trends, the Green Dam initiative was launched to establish a forest belt to mitigate desertification in the arid zone from east to west across Algeria. Unfortunately the project has faced failures as monocultures of P. halepensis Mill. experienced parasitic outbreaks and struggled to grow. Our study aimed to identify alternative tree species suitable for the climatic conditions in northern Algeria. We evaluated 20 woody species native to North Africa, projecting their potential distributions using MaxEnt 3.4 software under the current climate and two future climate scenarios (SSP 370, SSP 585). The environmental data was collected from the CHELSA database and the Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 3.70 and 5.85 were used. Based on these projections, we partitioned the Green Dam into three regions, Southern, Eastern and Northern. The regions were delineated by species predicted to perform well under both current and future conditions. We recommend two species for afforestation across the entire Green Dam: Juniperus oxycedrus L. and Pistacia lentiscus L. A risk assessment indicated that the Green Dam region is highly susceptible to wildfire due to elevated temperatures and low precipitation. Given these conditions, we also recommend planting Pistacia atlantica Desf. (Atlas pistachio), a species with reduced flammability. Incorporating the Atlas pistachio alongside region-specific species is expected to enhance habitat diversity and reduce overall wildfire risk.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68580-w.title: Recreational cannabis use and its association with arterial stiffness: the EVA-adic study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68580-w.abstract: The cardiovascular effects of recreational cannabis use on arterial stiffness in young adults remain poorly understood. This study aimed to examine the association between cannabis use and arterial stiffness parameters in a young adult population. A descriptive, cross-sectional observational study was conducted. Using non-probabilistic consecutive sampling, 501 participants (222 men and 279 women) aged 18 to 34 years were recruited from an urban setting. Cannabis use was assessed using the Alcohol, Smoking and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST V3.0). Arterial stiffness was evaluated via pulse pressure (PP), carotid–femoral pulse wave velocity (cf-PWV), brachial–ankle pulse wave velocity (ba-PWV), cardio–ankle vascular index (CAVI), and heart rate–corrected central augmentation index (CAIx75). Trial registration clinicalTrials.gov identifier: [NCT05866133], registered on July 29, 2023. The mean age of cannabis users was significantly lower than that of non-users (24.83 ± 4.84 vs. 26.74 ± 4.33 years; P = 0.008). No significant differences in arterial stiffness parameters were observed between non-users and cannabis users in the overall cohort or when stratified by sex. However, in the linear regression analysis adjusted for age and sex, we found a positive association between cannabis use and CAIx75 (β 13.682, 6.646–20.719, P < 0.05), which persisted after adjusting for the remaining lifestyle confounding factors (β 10.097, 2.697–17.497, P < 0.05). In the binary logistic regression models, no associations were observed between past or recent cannabis use and arterial stiffness parameters. No significant differences in arterial stiffness parameters were found based on cannabis use. In the linear regression analysis, after adjusting for age, sex, and lifestyle factors, a positive association between cannabis use and CAIx75 was observed. This isolated finding concerning CAIx75 may reflect a subtle functional or hemodynamic difference rather than established structural arterial stiffening. However, residual confounding and the possibility of a chance finding cannot be ruled out.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67756-8.title: Triple band Yagi antenna design and performance prediction for next generation (6G) wireless applications using supervised regression models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67756-8.abstract: This study presents a high-performance Yagi antenna designed for sub-terahertz (sub-THz) and terahertz (THz) wireless communication applications, addressing the growing demands of emerging technologies such as high-resolution imaging, short-range secure communication, sensing, spectroscopy, and next generation 6G systems. Developed on a polyimide substrate with compact dimensions of 53 μm × 47 μm, the proposed antenna achieves exceptional directional radiation characteristics across the targeted frequency bands. Simulation results reveal a maximum gain of 14.9 dB and an outstanding efficiency of 99.65%, highlighting its suitability for advanced high-frequency applications. To ensure reliable performance evaluation, the antenna is analyzed and validated using multiple approaches, including full-wave simulations through CST, HFSS, and Altair FEKO, as well as curve-fitting techniques and an RLC equivalent circuit model. In addition, machine learning techniques are employed to predict antenna efficiency based on extensive simulation datasets, incorporating both neural network models and supervised regression algorithms. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest Regression exhibits superior prediction accuracy compared to other neural network and regression methods. The integration of high gain, near-perfect efficiency, and robust predictive modelling establishes the proposed Yagi antenna as a promising candidate for future sub-THz and THz wireless systems, particularly for 6G communication infrastructure.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69480-9.title: Aberrant subcellular localization and aggregation of KIF1A in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis harboring a heterozygous p.I433V KIF1A variant of uncertain significance
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69480-9.abstract: KIF1A is the primary anterograde motor protein responsible for axonal transport of synaptic vesicle precursors and dense-core vesicles. Although heterozygous KIF1A variants have recently been proposed as candidate risk factors for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), their neuropathological correlates remain unknown. We conducted a comprehensive clinicopathological study of a Japanese patient with ALS carrying a heterozygous p.I433V KIF1A variant and analysed the subcellular localization of KIF1A in distinct neuronal populations, with quantitative comparison performed in lumbar anterior horn cells among the KIF1A variant case, sporadic ALS (SALS) cases, and control subjects. In addition, the motor activity of recombinant KIF1A harboring the p.I433V variant was assessed using biochemical assays. Neuropathological examination showed lower motor neuron loss with mild corticospinal tract degeneration, accompanied by pleomorphic neuronal cytoplasmic inclusions (NCIs) immunoreactive for transactive response DNA-binding protein of 43 kDa (TDP-43) and the presence of Bunina bodies. In contrast to control and SALS cases, which showed predominantly nuclear KIF1A immunoreactivity, the KIF1A variant case exhibited marked cytoplasmic redistribution of KIF1A in spinal motor neurons, occasionally forming KIF1A-positive NCIs. Similar inclusions were also observed in the substantia nigra and showed partial spatial overlap with phosphorylated TDP-43. Biochemical analyses demonstrated no apparent impairment of kinesin motor activity or overall microtubule binding caused by the p.I433V substitution. This study provides the first neuropathological characterization of an ALS patient harboring a heterozygous p.I433V KIF1A variant of uncertain significance. These findings suggest that aberrant subcellular localization of KIF1A, rather than primary impairment of kinesin motor activity, may contribute to ALS pathogenesis through mechanisms beyond conventional axonal transport dysfunction. This observation expands the clinicopathological spectrum of ALS cases harboring KIF1A variants and suggests a potential relevance of altered subcellular localization of KIF1A in ALS.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66771-z.title: Phillygenin protects against lipopolysaccharide-induced acute lung injury by acting as a PXR agonist via NF-κB inhibition
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66771-z.abstract: Abstract Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are life-threatening conditions with substantial mortality and limited targeted therapies. The pregnane X receptor (PXR) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for inflammatory diseases, though its role in ALI remains underexplored. This study characterizes phillygenin (PHI), a bioactive lignan isolated from Forsythia suspensa, as a PXR agonist, elucidating its protective mechanism in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI. PHI binding to PXR was characterized by ligand fishing using hollow fibers and luciferase reporter assays, revealing direct agonistic activity. In LPS-stimulated human bronchial epithelial cells, PHI-activated PXR competed with NF-κB p65 for RXRα, suppressing NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation and downstream inflammatory cascades. Concurrently, PHI upregulated antioxidant enzymes (GPX-2/GPX-7) and anti-apoptotic proteins (Bcl-2/Bcl-xL), while downregulating pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-6), in a PXR-dependent manner. PXR knockdown abolished these protective effects, confirming target specificity. In vivo, PHI dose-dependently attenuated lung histopathological injury, reduced inflammatory cytokine levels in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and mitigated alveolar epithelial apoptosis in LPS-challenged mice. These findings support PHI as a direct PXR agonist and the PHI-PXR-NF-κB axis as a mechanistic foundation for developing targeted interventions in acute inflammatory lung diseases.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68842-7.title: Cross-modal consistency gated fusion network for selfie-based body satisfaction prediction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68842-7.abstract: Accurately predicting users’ satisfaction with their body image in selfies is of significant importance for understanding body perception, preventing psychological issues, and developing personalized health services. To this end, this study proposes an innovative selfie-based body satisfaction prediction model that integrates Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers-Convolutional Neural Network (BERT-CNN). The model aims to achieve more precise inference of psychological states by deeply integrating multimodal information. It employs a dual-branch architecture: the text branch leverages a pre-trained BERT model to extract deep semantic features, capturing sentiment tendencies and self-evaluation in descriptions, while the image branch uses Residual Network-50 (ResNet-50) combined with a channel attention mechanism to focus on key visual cues such as facial expressions and body posture in selfies. A core innovation lies in the cross-modal attention fusion module, which enables fine-grained interaction between text and image features through a bidirectional attention mechanism. An adaptive gating unit dynamically integrates information from both modalities, producing a more discriminative joint representation. Experiments conducted on the Selfit dataset show that the model achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.310 and a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.211 on the test set. When converting predicted values into discrete satisfaction levels for classification tasks, the model attains an accuracy of 83.0% and a weighted F1 score of 0.828, significantly outperforming single-modality approaches and existing state-of-the-art multimodal fusion baselines. This study validates the effectiveness of deep text-image integration for predicting body satisfaction and also offers a methodological reference for multimodal psychological computing. The approach has potential applications in digital mental health assessment and intelligent content understanding.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-39077-3.title: Asbestos mineral fibre exposure significantly affects volatile organic compound profiles of mesothelial cell lines in vitro
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-39077-3.abstract: Abstract Malignant mesothelioma (MM) is a rare cancer caused by exposure to asbestos, this condition continues to represent a significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Due to the long disease latency, non-invasive diagnostic modalities such as breath analysis may enhance MM early detection by identifying the disease specific pattern of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath. In this study, solid phase microextraction (SPME) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used to extract VOCs from the headspace of two mesothelioma cell lines: MSTO-211 H (biphasic mesothelioma) and NCI-H28 (epithelioid mesothelioma) in addition to MET-5a (non-malignant mesothelial cell line), following exposure to asbestos mineral fibers (actinolite, amosite, crocidolite and chrysotile) and a non-asbestos fiber control (wollastonite). Multivariate statistical analysis was applied to identify VOC-based biomarkers associated with asbestos exposure within the cell lines. Data confirms that exposure to mineral fibers (including the non-asbestos fiber control) induces significant alterations in the levels of as many as 24 VOCs in each cell line. This is the first study to investigate the impact of asbestos mineral fiber exposure on the VOC profile of MM cell lines. This may be relevant to studies involving mesothelioma patients, as these VOCs could also serve as indicators of asbestos exposure in individuals who have been exposed to asbestos.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68994-6.title: Polarization selective nonlinear optical enhancement in hybrid silicon metamembrane based on bound states in the continuum via symmetry engineering
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68994-6.abstract: We present a hybrid silicon metamembrane incorporating two air and polymeric nanoholes for upconversion of near‑infrared (NIR) wavelength into the visible. By tuning the incidence angle, material composition and geometric parameters, the symmetry‑protected BIC (SP-BIC) is perturbed and converted into a high-quality-factor (Q-factor) quasi‑BIC (q‑BIC). The dominant multipolar contributions for all resonant modes are magnetic quadrupoles (MQ). Beyond characterizing each mode individually, we analyze their mutual interactions and select the optimal condition that maximizes stored electric energy and near‑field enhancement for nonlinear processes such as Third Harmonic Generation (THG) and Four-wave Mixing (FWM). Linear response comparisons, including near‑field distributions, transmission spectra, stored electric energy and Q-factors, together with nonlinear response, confirm a direct correlation between enhanced light–matter interaction, near‑field amplitude, and nonlinear conversion efficiency. Incorporation of a Poly methyl methacrylate (PMMA) material yields the largest improvements in both field enhancement and Q-factor, and using pure and anthracene chalcone derivatives (N-ANC) doped PMMA further enhances performance. The N-ANC-doped PMMA, owing to its higher third-order susceptibility, delivers larger frequency conversion efficiency (FCE). Through resonance and material engineering, we observe a significant enhancement in FCE arising from the combined effects of an increased Q-factor and the higher $${\upchi }^{\left(3\right)}$$ of the doped polymer. The proposed structure is shown to be a polarization‑selective, application‑versatile platform for both linear and nonlinear photonics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68468-9.title: Integrated experimental and computational exploration of 1,8-naphthyridine hydrazones as promising topoisomerase II-targeting anticancer agents
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68468-9.abstract: DNA topoisomerase II (Topo II) is essential for maintaining DNA topology during replication, transcription, and chromosome segregation. Its increased expression is associated with tumor progression, which makes it an appealing target for anticancer therapy. However, clinically used Topo II inhibitors such as etoposide and doxorubicin are limited by toxicity and resistance, illustrating the importance of safer, more effective chemotherapeutic scaffolds. This study reports the rational design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a novel series of hydrazone derivatives incorporating a 1,8-naphthyridine core as potential Topo II inhibitors. Hybrid molecules were generated by integrating hydrazone moieties with the naphthyridine scaffold and characterized using standard spectroscopic techniques. Their biological activities were assessed via in vitro cytotoxicity assays and Topo II inhibition tests. Complementary computational investigations, including density functional theory (DFT), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, MM/PBSA binding free-energy analysis, and per-residue MM/GBSA free-energy decomposition analysis, were performed to explore electronic properties, ligand–target interactions, and binding determinants. Among the synthesized series, compound 3b displayed notable antiproliferative activity, particularly against the HL-60 (TB) leukemia cell line (GI₅₀ = 1.99–3.02 μM), and exhibited potent Topo II inhibition (IC₅₀ = 1.79 ± 0.73 μM), outperforming doxorubicin (IC₅₀ = 3.08 ± 0.59 μM) under the same conditions. Computational modelling supported these findings by indicating stable binding conformations and suggesting a potential DNA-intercalative binding mode within the Topo II catalytic environment. However, this interaction remains a computational prediction that requires experimental validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67549-z.title: A non-open surgical rabbit model of ureteral stricture induced by transurethral endoscopic thermal injury
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67549-z.abstract: Iatrogenic thermal injury during endoscopic procedures is a predominant cause of benign ureteral strictures. Existing models rely either on costly large animals, unsuitable for large-scale screening, or on open surgery in small mammals, which causes substantial trauma and high complication rates. We established a rabbit model of ureteral stricture via transurethral endoluminal thermal injury, without open surgery. Under fluoroscopic guidance, endoluminal low-power bipolar electrocoagulation (10 W, 2 s; 20 J) was applied through a flexible ureteroscope. Stricture, defined as histological luminal narrowing with ipsilateral hydronephrosis, was induced in 10/10 rabbits versus 0/10 in both open-surgery models (P < 0.001). Histopathology confirmed collagen deposition, myofibroblast activation and renal tubular injury, while imaging demonstrated obstruction with hydronephrosis and delayed contrast excretion. The endoscopic approach shortened operative time (27.6 ± 6.7 versus 81.6 ± 12.6 and 111.4 ± 14.8 min, P < 0.001) and reduced urinary extravasation and hematuria versus transection–anastomosis (both P = 0.033); mortality (0% versus 30.0% and 40.0%; P = 0.211 and 0.087) and the overall complication rate (10.0% versus 60.0%; P = 0.057) were lower but not significantly so. This model provides a low-cost small-animal platform for large-scale preclinical studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63300-w.title: DeepPoseCare: a privacy-preserving pose-based temporal convolutional framework for real-time patient action recognition in healthcare environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63300-w.abstract: Continuous and automated surveillance of patient activities in clinical environments holds great promise for the early identification of falls and distress in patients. However, current vision-based systems face obstacles such as privacy issues, the need for real-time processing, and complex environments that hinder their performance. We present DeepPoseCare, a privacy-preserving pose-based deep learning framework that integrates 2D skeletal keypoint extraction from RGB video with temporal convolutional modeling for real-time patient action recognition in healthcare environments. Video streams were anonymized by blurring facial areas, keeping only the skeletal keypoints (25 joints) with corresponding confidence scores. A Savitzky–Golay filter was used to smooth the joint trajectories before sequences of length \(T=32\) were fed into a four-block residual TCN, which produced per-frame action probabilities using softmax across four categories: Walk, Sit, Fall, and Distress. We tested DeepPoseCare on two public fall detection benchmarks (UPFall and URFall) and conducted five-fold cross-validation on simulated ward recordings. For UPFall, our model achieved 94.0% accuracy and 93.5% F 1 for falls, outperforming the state-of-the-art baselines by more than four percentage points. On URFall, the model achieved an accuracy of 93.5% with an F 1 score of 93.0%. The measured processing latency was 22 ms/frame on the RTX 3090 workstation. Because the symmetric five-frame Savitzky–Golay smoother requires two future frames, the buffering-adjusted streaming latency is 88.7 ms at 30 fps, which remains below the 500 ms clinical alert threshold. An ablation study showed that four TCN blocks optimized the balance between the F 1 gain and latency overhead. By incorporating effective pose-based feature extraction, temporal modeling, and strict privacy measures, DeepPoseCare achieves state-of-the-art performance in detecting falls and distress while adhering to the constraints of clinical deployment. These results highlight the potential of the system to improve patient safety through timely alerts, reduce staff workload, and seamlessly integrate with existing nurse-call systems via HL7 FHIR messaging.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68144-y.title: Spatial flow of food supply services based on supply and demand relations in Chongqing main city
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68144-y.abstract: Ecosystem food supply services are the foundation of sustainable development of society and nature. Taking the Chongqing main city as an example, based on multi-source data such as land use, food production and population, the supply and demand of food supply services (FS) were quantified by food calorie method. Then, the supply and demand relationships were clarified based on the supply-demand ratio and bivariate local spatial autocorrelation. Finally, the spatial flow characteristics of FS were explored based on transportation accessibility. The results show that: (1) From 2000 to 2020, the FS supply decreased from 5.2 × 10 12 to 1.7 × 10 12 kcal, and the high-supply areas disappeared in the west and only remained in the northeast and southeast. The FS demand increased from 4.7 × 10 10 to 6.5 × 10 10 kcal, and the high-demand areas expanded from the middle to the east and west sides. (2) The average supply-demand ratio of FS decreased from 0.348 to 0.222, indicating an increase in supply pressure. The area of the surplus regions shrank while that of the deficit regions expanded. In particular, the areas with high demand and low supply were significantly increased. (3) The spatial flow of FS was mainly concentrated in two directions: from Banan to the central and southern demand areas and from Yubei to the northern demand areas. The research results can provide strong data support for optimizing regional food resource allocation and promoting regional sustainable development.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68586-4.title: HPV DNA negativity following AHCC or nonavalent vaccination or their combination in women with persistent HPV infection without HSIL
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68586-4.abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is a common clinical condition for which no validated systemic antiviral therapy is currently available, and in the absence of high-grade cervical lesions management is generally limited to surveillance. Active Hexose Correlated Compound (AHCC) is a standardized immunomodulatory extract that has shown potential to promote HPV clearance in controlled clinical studies. This multicenter retrospective cohort study evaluated outcomes observed in routine clinical practice among women with documented persistent HR-HPV infection lasting at least six months who had received AHCC supplementation alone, nonavalent HPV vaccination alone, or both. A total of 289 women were included: 114 had documented AHCC supplementation alone, 60 had documented nonavalent HPV vaccination alone, and 115 had documented concomitant AHCC supplementation and vaccination. In the AHCC-only group, HPV-DNA negativity increased from 51.8% (59/114) at the approximately 4-month assessment to 69.3% (79/114) at 6 months (exact McNemar test, p = 1.9 × 10^-6). At 6 months, HPV-DNA negativity was documented in 60.0% (36/60) of women in the vaccine-only group and in 94.8% (109/115) of women in the AHCC plus vaccine group. The overall comparison across the three exposure groups at 6 months was statistically significant (likelihood-ratio χ² test, p < 0.0001). Pairwise comparisons showed higher observed HPV-DNA negativity rates in the combination group than in either single-intervention group. Exploratory stratified analyses indicated that this overall pattern was maintained across cumulative age strata and in both smokers and non-smokers and was not readily explained, within the limits of the available retrospective covariates, by reproductive history, number of lifetime sexual partners, history of vaginosis/vaginitis, contraceptive use, or prior sexually transmitted diseases in the subgroups for which these data were available. Compliance was generally high, tolerability was acceptable, and adverse events were infrequent, mild, and self-limiting. Within the limitations inherent to a retrospective, non-randomized, center-dependent dataset, these findings identify a clinically relevant pattern of observed HPV-DNA negativity associated with AHCC use, particularly when combined with nonavalent HPV vaccination, and support prospective confirmation in adequately designed three-arm studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65426-3.title: Integrated central and autonomic signatures of concentrative and analytical meditation in expert practitioners
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65426-3.abstract: Meditation has long been associated with improvements in mental well-being, emotional regulation, and attentional control. However, the diversity of meditative techniques and variability in participant expertise across studies have hindered the systematic identification of their neurophysiological correlates. To address this challenge, we investigated the neurophysiological signatures of distinct meditation types in a relatively homogeneous cohort of 35 highly experienced Tibetan monk practitioners. We focused on concentrative meditation, characterized by sustained attention on a single object, and two analytical practices: Loving-Kindness, centered on cultivating prosocial affect, and Emptiness, involving reflective and deconstructive cognitive processes. EEG, ECG, EDA, and respiration were simultaneously recorded during these practices, which were performed in a fixed-order sequence (Concentrative → Loving-Kindness → Emptiness). Linear mixed-model analyses revealed significant modulations across conditions. Peripheral indices indicated enhanced parasympathetic activity (higher RMSSD and SDNN), reduced respiratory rate, and a progressive rise in tonic EDA across the entire three-phases meditation session. Cortically, EEG analyses showed changes in the gamma-band power during the meditation session. Overall, the pattern suggests that advanced meditative states involve coordinated autonomic–cortical integration, reflecting relaxed vigilance with improved emotional regulation and cognitive flexibility; nevertheless, given the fixed-order design, condition-related differences should be interpreted cautiously due to possible order or carryover effects.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68333-9.title: Explainable and imbalance-aware holistic swarm optimization for joint feature selection and random forest learning in educational analytics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68333-9.abstract: Accurately predicting students’ academic performance is a crucial component of educational analytics because it enables early detection and informed decision-making. However, existing machine learning methods are sensitive to class imbalance, have poor interpretability, and often rely on fixed feature representations. This paper proposes an imbalance-aware and explicable solution to these issues. An integrated framework of Holistic Swarm Optimization and Random Forest algorithms (HSORFC-FS) is presented to simultaneously optimize model hyperparameters and perform embedded feature selection inside a unified swarm-based search process. Unlike traditional optimization strategies that only focus on accuracy, the proposed framework includes a class-imbalance-aware fitness function that clearly promotes a balanced trade-off between minority-class recognition and overall classification performance. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is integrated to provide a global and class-wise understanding of the factors influencing academic performance. HSORFC-FS is evaluated using a real-world student academic performance dataset consisting of 1,194 records in four performance categories: poor, good, very good, and excellent. With a classification accuracy of 80.0% and a weighted F1-score of 0.80, experimental results show that HSORFC-FS performs better than standard Random Forest, bagging, artificial neural networks, k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, and Naïve Bayes models. The HSORFC-FS framework yields 0.62 for the minority (poor) class F1-score. The proposed framework achieves competitive performance in minority-class recognition while maintaining strong overall classification accuracy and balanced performance across all classes. SHAP analysis states that the most important factors are previous academic performance, attendance rate, and study habits. This explanation helps educational stakeholders to make suitable decisions based on data understanding. In summary, the proposed framework proved that the accuracy, equity, and transparency of academic performance prediction models are enhanced by combining explainable artificial intelligence, imbalance-aware learning, and holistic swarm intelligence.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68235-w.title: Exploring the influence of reverberation on the perceived quality of time-scale modified speech
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68235-w.abstract: One of the methods to enhance speech intelligibility is to use time-scale modification (TSM) algorithms. This approach is especially useful in challenging acoustic environments caused by noise or reverberation, for instance. Unfortunately, TSM algorithms tend to introduce distortions into speech, and these distortions become more audible as the slowdown ratio increases. The purpose of the experiment was to determine whether adding reverberation to slowed speech could improve perceived quality. To explore this, MUSHRA tests were conducted with two types of reverberation, three slowdown ratios, and sentences in both Polish and English. Under the experimental conditions investigated, the results indicated that at a slowdown ratio of 2.5, participants rated the speech with reverberation as higher in quality than the same speech without reverberation. No significant differences in quality perception were found between languages, although the characteristics of the reverberation itself were significant.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67471-4.title: Engineering proactive risk fields in mixed-autonomy traffic via anticipatory swarm intelligence: a digital twin perspective
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67471-4.abstract: Ensuring safety and resilience in mixed-autonomy traffic systems presents a critical engineering challenge due to the stochastic nature of human-driven vehicles (HDVs) and complex interactions with connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs). Traditional safety models predominantly rely on reactive post-conflict assessment, lacking the capability for proactive intervention. To address this gap, this study proposes an Anticipatory Risk Field Dynamics (ARFD) framework and develops an Anticipatory Swarm Intelligence (ASI) algorithm for proactive risk engineering. Methodologically, the ARFD framework establishes a novel closed-loop formulation of risk evolution governed by partial differential equations, distinguishing it from static potential models.The ASI algorithm integrates Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) for multi-step trajectory prediction and Distributed Particle Swarm Optimization (DPSO) for decentralized collaborative decision-making, enabling CAVs to actively reshape the spatiotemporal distribution of traffic risk fields. A high-fidelity digital twin platform, calibrated with empirical drone trajectory data and real-world road network topologies, was constructed to validate this methodology. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate that the ASI strategy reduces high-risk events by 42.8% and improves system resilience by 28% under extreme perturbations, with a marginal efficiency trade-off of only 3.5%. Furthermore, the algorithm exhibits robust performance under realistic communication imperfections. This research provides a robust, empirically validated technical toolkit that transitions traffic safety management from passive prediction to active field engineering, offering actionable insights for sustainable urban mobility infrastructure.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68057-w.title: Wideband mmWave antenna with integrated 1 × 8 feed-array configuration for high-gain 5G wireless applications using characteristic mode theory
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68057-w.abstract: Abstract This work presents a wideband millimeter-wave (mmWave) antenna designed and experimentally validated using the Characteristic Mode Theory (CMT). The proposed single-element is implemented on an ultra-thin 0.254 mm substrate and occupies a compact footprint of 8 × 6 mm 2 . The antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth from 22.5 to 39 GHz, corresponding to a fractional bandwidth of 53.66%, covering the major 28 GHz and 38 GHz 5G mmWave bands. CMT analysis is employed to investigate the dominant electric-dipole modes across various frequency bands. Further, by keeping the ground length constant at $$0.3{\lambda}_{0}$$ , the monople structure is varied to suppress the magnetic-dipole modes, thereby improving the linear polarization behavior with electric-dipole modes. The CMT for the proposed single-element structure illustrates that modes $${J}_{3}+{J}_{1}+{J}_{4}$$ , $${J}_{3}+{J}_{4}+{J}_{5}$$ , $${J}_{3}+{J}_{2}+{J}_{4}$$ , and $${J}_{2}+{J}_{3}+{J}_{5}$$ are contributing to resonance at 24, 28, 32, and 36 GHz, where the first modes in each band indicate the dominant mode with relatively higher magnitude. The summation of these multiple excited modes across multiple bands has led to a wideband resonance with a stable radiation pattern. To improve the radiation performance for high-gain mmWave applications, the optimized single element is extended into a 1 × 8 linear array configuration. The proposed array achieves a gain variation from 11 to 15.8 dBi across the operating band, with peak gains of 12.8 dBi at 28 GHz and 15.5 dBi at 38 GHz. The measured results obtained from the developed prototype show good agreement with the simulated responses, validating the proposed CMT-guided design approach. Due to its compact size, ultra-thin profile, wide bandwidth, high-gain array performance, and clear modal interpretation, the proposed antenna is a promising candidate for future 5G mmWave wireless communication systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68427-4.title: Temporal changes in age at diagnosis and the proportion of early-onset cases among diagnosed cases of 16 selected cancers in the United States, 2000–2023
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68427-4.abstract: Comprehensive evaluations of long-term changes in the age composition of diagnosed cancer cases, including the proportion of early-onset cases, remain limited. We conducted a descriptive registry-based analysis of diagnosed cancer cases aged ≥ 20 years across 16 selected cancer sites in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER)-21 database from 2000 to 2023. Mean and median age at diagnosis and age-group distributions were evaluated. Early-onset cases were defined as those diagnosed at ages 20–49 years, and the early-onset proportion was calculated by dividing the number of cases aged 20–49 years by the total number of diagnosed cancer cases aged ≥ 20 years. This within-case proportion did not represent an age-specific or age-standardized incidence rate in the underlying population. A total of 12,910,291 diagnosed cancer cases were included. The overall mean age at diagnosis decreased from 65.24 years in 2000 to 64.30 years in 2014 and subsequently increased to 65.40 years in 2023. The proportion of cases diagnosed at ages 20–49 years increased slightly from 13.17% in 2000 to a peak of 13.61% in 2005 and then declined to 11.55% in 2023. The absolute endpoint difference between 2014 and 2023 was − 0.77% points overall and + 3.75% points for colon and rectum cancer. Among diagnosed cases of the 16 selected cancers, the mean age at diagnosis was higher and the relative share of cases diagnosed at ages 20–49 years was lower in 2023 than in 2014 overall, although patterns varied by cancer site. Because the pooled overall estimates were composition-dependent, site-specific analyses provide a more informative basis for interpreting cancer-specific patterns. These findings describe changes in the age composition of diagnosed cancer cases and should not be interpreted as age-standardized incidence trends or population cancer burden.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68514-6.title: Comparative antimicrobial efficacy of chitosan and a high-potency papain gel (Brix 3000) as endodontic irrigants in deciduous teeth: an in vitro analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68514-6.abstract: In cases of irreversible pulpitis, root canal treatment is preferred over extraction. The success of endodontic therapy depends on chemical irrigation in addition to mechanical preparation. Sodium hypochlorite, although widely used, has disadvantages, including unpleasant taste and odor and potential toxic effects on periapical tissues and developing permanent tooth germs. Therefore, research on alternative irrigating solutions is ongoing. The aim of this study was to comparatively evaluate the antimicrobial efficacy of chitosan and a high-potency papain-based gel (Brix 3000) compared with sodium hypochlorite in deciduous teeth. In this study, thirty-two extracted anterior deciduous teeth were standardized to a root length of 12 mm, instrumented to size F3, and inoculated with E. faecalis to establish an early-stage colonization model. The specimens were randomly assigned to three experimental groups and positive/negative control subgroups. The experimental groups received 0.2 g/100 mL (0.2% w/v) chitosan solution (prepared in 0.5% v/v acetic acid), 1% (w/v) papain solution prepared from Brix 3000 in distilled water, and 2.5% sodium hypochlorite. The antimicrobial efficacy was assessed in terms of colony-forming units (CFU), and statistical analysis was performed. A p value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant for all tests. A statistically significant difference was observed among the groups regarding E. faecalis counts ( p < 0.001). The papain group showed significantly higher log₁₀(CFU/mL) values (3.10 ± 1.57) compared with the chitosan (0.11 ± 0.17; p = 0.010), sodium hypochlorite (0.0 ± 0.0; p = 0.008), and negative control (0.0 ± 0.0; p = 0.008) groups. No significant difference was found between the chitosan and sodium hypochlorite groups ( p > 0.05). Within the limitations of this in vitro study, chitosan showed a marked reduction in viable bacterial counts against early-stage E. faecalis colonization in deciduous teeth under the present experimental conditions, whereas the papain-based formulation showed reduced antibacterial performance. However, these findings should not be interpreted as clinical equivalence to sodium hypochlorite. Further studies using mature multispecies biofilm models, clinically relevant irrigation times, and biocompatibility assessments are required before clinical recommendations can be made.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68917-5.title: Quantum-inspired NSGA-III-BERT hybrid decision engine for high-frequency supply chain resilience configuration: design, simulation and engineering framework
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68917-5.abstract: High-frequency supply-chain disruptions require decision methods that combine many-objective search with policy-text constraints, yet hybrid systems are often described without sufficiently precise mathematical and evidentiary boundaries. This study presents a classical-computing Quantum-Inspired NSGA-III-BERT decision engine with three separable components: probabilistic population search, policy-aware dynamic reference-point adjustment, and an edge-cloud deployment layer. The robust formulation fixes binary route-activation decisions in the first stage and restricts affine recourse to continuous flow, inventory, and reserve-capacity variables. Across the reported 30-run summaries, the proposed method obtained HV = 0.947 with SD = 0.012 and IGD = 0.082 with SD = 0.007, together with cost and carbon reductions of 19.7% (SD = 0.7%) and 24.5% (SD = 0.9%), respectively. Because the archived package does not preserve paired run-level outputs, inferential comparisons are reported as summary-statistic Welch tests with Holm correction rather than as reconstructed paired tests. Pilot-enterprise observations are interpreted as descriptive deployment evidence rather than causal estimates. The study therefore contributes an explicit algorithm, a mathematically consistent recourse model, and an evidence-bounded interpretation of the empirical results.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68261-8.title: Robust unsupervised domain adaptation for medical image segmentation via frequency-conditioned graph diffusion
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68261-8.abstract: Abstract Cross-domain variability in medical imaging, arising from differences in scanners, acquisition protocols, and patient populations, remains a major challenge for reliable semantic segmentation. Existing unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) methods predominantly rely on image-level transformations or feature alignment, which often fail to preserve anatomical consistency under large domain shifts. In this work, we propose a novel structured latent UDA framework that performs domain alignment in a topology-aware representation space rather than directly modifying image appearance. Specifically, we introduce a Frequency-Conditioned Graph Diffusion paradigm, where convolutional features are transformed into anatomical graphs to explicitly capture structural relationships. A latent diffusion process then progressively refines these graph embeddings, guided by frequency-aware contextual cues, enabling robust cross-domain alignment. To further enhance generalization, we integrate structural consistency regularization with adversarial latent alignment, eliminating the need for labeled target data. A dedicated decoder reconstructs dense segmentation maps, while stochastic diffusion sampling provides uncertainty estimates for improved potential clinical reliability. Extensive experiments on multiple public medical imaging benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art UDA approaches, achieving superior segmentation accuracy and robustness under significant domain shifts. These results highlight the effectiveness of structured latent modeling and diffusion-based learning for robust domain-adaptive segmentation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55853-7.title: Soliton solutions and dynamical bifurcation analysis of the Yajima-Oikawa equations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55853-7.abstract: Abstract The Yajima–Oikawa equations describes the resonant interaction between ion sound waves and Langmuir waves in plasma. Despite its importance, the detailed dynamical behavior of this model has not been comprehensively explored. In this work, we present a unified analytical and dynamical framework that combines exact solution construction with qualitative and quantitative analysis. By employing traveling wave transformations together with the first integral method, a class of exact solutions in terms of Jacobi elliptic functions is derived. These solutions are systematically classified, according to bifurcation scenarios, into periodic, quasi-periodic, solitary, and kink-type wave structures. To investigate the global dynamics, an external periodic perturbation is introduced, transforming the system into a higher-dimensional dynamical model. This enables the study of transitions between regular and chaotic regimes. The presence of chaos is confirmed through phase portraits, Poincaré sections, time series analysis, and Lyapunov exponent calculations, while sensitivity to initial conditions is also examined. The results provide a deeper understanding of nonlinear wave interactions and reveal rich dynamical features of the classical Yajima–Oikawa equations. These findings are relevant for applications in plasma physics and related fields, where accurate prediction and control of wave dynamics are essential, including in plasma-based devices such as fusion systems and wave propagation technologies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68635-y.title: Digital transformation capabilities and innovation performance in skating manufacturing: a hybrid SEM–ANN analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68635-y.abstract: Digital upgrading in specialized manufacturing sectors is associated with firms’ development of flexible IT infrastructure, agile response capability, system integration, and strategic digital vision. However, limited empirical modelling has examined how these digital manufacturing capabilities are associated with innovation performance in niche equipment manufacturing contexts. This study developed a hybrid SEM-ANN model to examine configurations of digital transformation capabilities among skating equipment manufacturing firms in Guangdong and Zhejiang, China. Survey data from 383 senior and middle managers were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling and artificial neural network analysis. The SEM results showed that Digitalization Vision (β = 0.039, p = 0.026), IT Flexibility (β = 0.070, p = 0.003), and IT Agility (β = 0.187, p = 0.001) were positively and indirectly associated with perceived innovation performance through Business Model Innovation. IT Integration showed a statistically significant but negative indirect association (β = −0.030, p = 0.049), indicating that system integration did not support the predicted positive indirect pathway. The model explained 66.6% of the variance in Business Model Innovation and 19.0% of the variance in perceived innovation performance. The ANN analysis identified IT Flexibility as the strongest predictor of innovation performance, followed by Digitalization Vision and IT Agility, with normalized importance values of 100%, 73.7%, and 41.8%, respectively. These findings provide context-specific evidence on how digital transformation capabilities are associated with innovation performance among surveyed firms in the skating equipment manufacturing sector in Guangdong and Zhejiang.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67616-5.title: CT quantification of enlarged inguinal lymph nodes as a diagnostic approach for periprosthetic joint infection after hip arthroplasty
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67616-5.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA), posing significant diagnostic challenges. This study prospectively evaluated 114 patients from January 2021 to August 2023, including those with PJI and aseptic loosening, using computed tomography (CT) to count enlarged inguinal lymph nodes with a short-axis diameter greater than 5 mm as assessed by two blinded radiologists. Patients with PJI had significantly higher lymph node counts (median 4.5, range 1–13) compared with those with aseptic loosening (median 1, range 0–5). Using a threshold of more than 2.5 enlarged nodes, CT achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 85.5% specificity, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.91, which was superior to conventional markers such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). These findings suggest that CT-based enlarged inguinal lymph node counting is a simple, non-invasive, and accurate method for diagnosing PJI, and may enhance current diagnostic strategies. Trial registration number : No. ChiCTR2100050785.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65639-6.title: Terrestrial isopods shape carbon cycling through gut microbiota in variable environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65639-6.abstract: Soil invertebrates play an essential role in organic matter decomposition and nutrient cycling, yet the contribution of their gut microbiota to these processes remains underexplored. In this study, we investigated how the gut microbiota of the terrestrial isopod Armadillidium vulgare responds to variation in food source (maize vs. soybean), fertilization, and habitat type (tree-, shrub-, and herbaceous plant-dominated areas), and how these microbial communities contribute to carbon cycling. High-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing combined with enzymatic activity assays and functional predictions (PICRUSt2 and FAPROTAX) revealed that food source had the strongest influence on gut microbiota and predicted functional potential. Maize-fed individuals exhibited higher microbial diversity and enriched pathways for cellulose and xylan degradation, while soybean-fed isopods were dominated by symbiotic taxa such as norank_o_Rickettsiales , resulting in reduced carbon cycling activity. Fertilizer application suppressed microbial richness and promoted acidophilic or potentially pathogenic taxa. In contrast, unfertilized conditions supported beneficial bacteria involved in denitrification, hydrocarbon degradation, and sulfur metabolism. Habitat type further shaped community structure and function, with tree- and shrub-dominated areas favoring lignin- and chitin-degrading microbes and herbaceous areas enhancing cellulose decomposition. These findings highlight the ecological significance of A. vulgare as a vector of microbe-mediated carbon transformation and provide new insight into the functional links between soil fauna, microbial communities, and terrestrial biogeochemical cycles.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67659-8.title: Spatial correlation network structure and influencing factors of agricultural ecological efficiency under carbon constraints in China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67659-8.abstract: Agricultural ecological efficiency (AEE) is essential for coordinating agricultural development with carbon reduction and ecological sustainability. This study evaluates the spatiotemporal evolution of AEE in 31 provincial-level units in China from 2007 to 2024 under carbon constraints. A super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SBM) model incorporating undesirable outputs is used to measure AEE, while a modified gravity model and social network analysis (SNA) are employed to examine the interprovincial spatial correlation network. A spatial Durbin model (SDM) is further applied to identify the direct and spillover effects of key influencing factors.The results show that China’s overall AEE improved during the study period, although substantial regional heterogeneity persisted. The national mean increased from 0.738 in 2007 to 0.952 in 2024. The eastern region experienced the most pronounced improvement, whereas the northeastern region maintained the highest period average. The central and western regions also improved, particularly during the later years. Spatially, the provincial distribution of AEE evolved from a mixed pattern of low, medium, and high efficiency in 2007 to a predominantly high-efficiency pattern in 2024. The kernel density analysis further confirms an overall upward shift in AEE in recent years. However, the remaining low-efficiency tail and persistent regional differences indicate that improvements were uneven across provinces. From 2007 to 2024, the spatial correlation network of China’s provincial AEE remained fully connected. The interprovincial AEE network remained fully connected, with a slight increase in network ties and density and a substantial decline in network hierarchy. Henan consistently occupied a prominent position, while several provinces, including Shandong, Shaanxi, Hubei, Ningxia and Gansu, performed important connecting or bridging roles. Economic development, urbanization, education, informatization, rural residents’ income, and technological innovation all exerted significant positive direct effects on AEE. Informatization generated a positive spatial spillover effect, whereas economic development produced a negative spatial spillover effect; the other factors showed no significant spillover effects. These findings provide empirical evidence for designing spatially targeted and regionally coordinated policy frameworks to advance the sustainable enhancement of AEE, with broader implications for agricultural climate governance in developing economies undergoing rapid urbanization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67936-6.title: Non-linear associations of plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D with serum homocysteine and hyperhomocysteinemia in Chinese adults: a cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67936-6.abstract: Abstract Background Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] deficiency and elevated homocysteine (Hcy) levels are both well-established risk factors for cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, the relationship between 25(OH)D and Hcy remains unclear. To explore the association between plasma 25(OH)D and serum Hcy, along with the risk of hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy). Methods Based on baseline data from the Precision Nutrition and Health KAP Real-World Study (China), The associations of 25(OH)D with Hcy and HHcy were analyzed using multivariable linear regression and logistic regression models, respectively. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) served to investigate nonlinear patterns and threshold phenomena. Additionally, subgroup and sensitivity analyses were carried out to assess potential influencing factors and confirm the robustness of the findings. Results In the unadjusted analysis, 25(OH)D were positively associated with both Hcy and HHcy. After adjusting for age and sex, a non-linear U-shaped relationship emerged between 25(OH)D and both Hcy and HHcy, which remained significant after further multivariable adjustment. When plasma 25(OH)D levels were categorized into quintiles, individuals in quintiles Q1–Q3 (25(OH)D < 24.3 ng/mL) and Q5 (25(OH)D ≥ 28.2 ng/mL) had significantly elevated Hcy concentrations (by 0.16 µmol/L) and increased risks of HHcy (by 11% and 10%, respectively) compared with those in Q4 (24.3–28.2 ng/mL). In the overall population, the inflection point for 25(OH)D in relation to Hcy was 27.2 ng/mL. For HHcy, the inflection point was 26.1 ng/mL. Conclusions This study revealed a non-linear U-shaped association between plasma 25(OH)D and both Hcy and HHcy risk in Chinese adults, providing epidemiological evidence for understanding the relationship between 25(OH)D and homocysteine, with potential implications for cardiovascular risk assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67429-6.title: Sports tourism as a pathway to older adults’ psychological well-being: a dual-pathway model integrating broaden-and-build and social identity perspectives
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67429-6.abstract: This study explores how sports tourism is associated with older adults’ eudaimonic well-being through dual psychological mechanisms. Drawing on Broaden-and-Build Theory and Social Identity Theory, the research examines an emotion pathway in which positive emotions and sense of physical challenge achievement are linked to psychological resources, and an identity pathway in which sports group identification is linked to positive age identity. Survey data from 467 older Chinese sports tourism participants were analyzed using PLS-SEM and artificial neural network analysis. PLS-SEM results provide support for both pathways, while neural network sensitivity analysis further reveals that sense of physical challenge achievement is the most important predictor of psychological resource accumulation, and psychological resources showed greater importance in predicting well-being than positive age identity. Peer social support showed significant moderating effects on the achievement-to-resources and identification-to-age-identity relationships.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68224-z.title: Direct recording of electrically-evoked auditory brainstem responses (CI-eABR) using Advanced Bionics cochlear implants: a feasibility study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68224-z.abstract: Abstract Electrically-evoked auditory brainstem responses (eABRs) provide an objective measure of auditory pathway function, reflecting neural activity in the auditory nerve and brainstem. To date, eABRs have been predominantly acquired using conventional electrophysiological (EP) systems with far-field scalp electrodes, which require separate recording hardware and may limit clinical applicability. An integrated framework enabling direct recording through the cochlear implant (CI) system could overcome these limitations and support streamlined objective assessment. This study evaluates the clinical feasibility of direct cochlear implant–based eABR recording (CI-eABR) using the Advanced Bionics system. A prototype interface was developed to acquire eABRs via intracochlear electrodes using implant-based back telemetry, enabling synchronized bilateral recordings with stimulation from a single implant. Recordings were obtained from engineering test bench, and from CI users with a subset compared to conventional scalp recordings. Bench testing demonstrated stable acquisition, effective artifact rejection, and reliable waveform extraction. In human participants, measurable ipsilateral responses were observed at comfortable levels, with peak latencies within expected ranges. In subjects with scalp recordings, strong agreement in waveform morphology and latency was observed, with CI-eABR showing larger amplitudes consistent with near-field recording. These findings support the feasibility of direct implant-based eABR recording and represent a step toward rapid, clinically applicable objective auditory assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60917-9.title: Optimal integration of electric vehicle charging stations and distributed generator in microgrids using bio-inspired optimization techniques
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60917-9.abstract: The prompt adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) offers substantial challenges to modern power distribution systems, incorporating enlarged power demand, voltage variability, and elevated energy losses. To solve such problems, this paper proposes an integrated optimization scheme for the simultaneous allocation of EV Charging Stations (EVCSs) and Distributed Generators (DGs) within a microgrid. Using the IEEE 33-bus radial distribution network as a test case, an objective problem is expressed for reducing active power loss and voltage variation while increasing the Voltage Stability Index (VSI). The proposed framework is solved using three metaheuristic algorithms: the novel Walrus Optimization Algorithm (WaOA), alongside the well-established Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). Simulations across various scenarios reveal that uncoordinated EVCS integration severely degrades system performance, whereas the optimal co-placement of EVCSs and DGs dramatically enhances operational efficiency. The WaOA consistently demonstrated superior performance, notably in a scenario with three optimally placed DGs, achieving a 53.79% reduction in active power losses (from 202.53 kW to 93.59 kW) and a 50.44% reduction in reactive power losses. In addition, it significantly enhanced the voltage profile, boosted the minimum VSI from 0.6956 to 0.92721, and reduced the lowest voltage deviation to 0.000128 p.u. Comparative study confirms that WaOA outperforms PSO and WOA in both convergence speed and solution quality. This study underscores the critical importance of coordinated planning for EVCS and DG integration, providing a robust strategy to enhance grid reliability and support the sustainable transition to electric mobility.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67288-1.title: Early-age microstructural characteristics and improvement mechanisms of cement–fly ash stabilized dispersive soil
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67288-1.abstract: Dispersive soil is highly susceptible to erosion and seepage failure, posing significant risks to hydraulic and geotechnical structures. This study evaluates the effectiveness of a fly ash–dominated cementitious stabilization system for improving dispersive soil. A series of dispersibility, permeability, SEM, EDS, and XRD tests were conducted on soils treated with different cement and fly ash contents after 72 h of curing. C1F4 is the minimum dosage required to achieve a non-dispersive classification. The results show that the combined use of cement and fly ash effectively suppresses soil dispersivity. The permeability coefficient decreases by 20.4%–83.4% compared with untreated soil, indicating a substantial improvement in seepage resistance. Microstructural analysis reveals significant pore refinement, with the average pore diameter decreasing from 2.09 \(\mu\) m to 0.50 \(\mu\) m (approximately 76%). EDS and XRD results indicate that hydration reactions generated calcium-rich amorphous cementitious products, which filled pores and enhanced particle bonding. These findings demonstrate that the fly ash–dominated stabilization system provides an effective and sustainable approach for reducing dispersivity, improving impermeability, and enhancing the microstructural stability of dispersive soils.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67653-0.title: Self-efficacy and antenatal depression mediate the relationship between third-trimester maternal health literacy and adverse pregnancy outcomes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67653-0.abstract: Abstract This study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which maternal health literacy (MHL) influences adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), and to examine the mediating roles of self-efficacy (SE) and pre-pregnancy depression (AD) within this relationship for the first time. This cross-sectional survey recruited 322 pregnant women in the third trimester using a two-stage sampling method. Standardized instruments were used to collect data, including the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), the MHL questionnaire, the General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES), as well as self-reported information on demographic characteristics and indicators of APOs. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was applied to analyze the relationships and mediating pathways among the variables. Statistical significance was set at a P-value of 0.05. The incidence of APOs was 57.45%, while only 4.04% of the participants met the criteria for MHL. SEM revealed that MHL exerted a direct effect on APOs (β = -0.122, p < 0.01) and also indirectly influenced APOs through the mediating roles of SE and AD, with an indirect effect of -0.070, jointly explaining 36.46% of the association between MHL and APOs. Additionally, SE had a direct effect on APOs (β = -0.147, p < 0.01) and indirectly influenced APOs through AD, with an indirect effect of -0.046, accounting for 17.90% of the total effect. In contrast, AD had only a direct effect on APOs (β = 0.181, p < 0.01). MHL has the potential to mitigate the risk of APOs by enhancing SE and alleviating AD. These findings substantiate the theoretical pathway of “health literacy - psychological factors - pregnancy outcomes”. A multi-dimensional intervention system combining MHL promotion, SE training, and AD screening is recommended for more targeted and effective APO prevention and management.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68141-1.title: Microstructure-aware deep learning bridges atomistics to macroscale for shock-to-detonation prediction

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68187-1.title: SEQURNA enhances FLASH-seq gene detection while eliminating DTT dependence
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68187-1.abstract: Abstract Effective RNase inhibition is critical for single-cell RNA-sequencing, yet commercial recombinant RNase inhibitors (RRIs) require reducing agents for stability and impose substantial costs. Here, we systematically benchmark SEQURNA, a synthetic thermostable RNase inhibitor, against commercial alternatives using FLASH-seq in human retinal organoids and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). SEQURNA at 0.5–0.75 U/μl achieved 12–15% higher gene detection than Takara RRI in both cell types (p < 0.001) . Surprisingly, DTT supplementation at standard concentrations (5–10 mM) significantly impaired gene detection across all SEQURNA concentrations without improving RNA quality metrics, challenging established reverse transcription protocols. SEQURNA preserved biological heterogeneity, maintained sample stability during one-month storage at − 80 °C, and reduced reagent costs by over 75%. We recommend SEQURNA at 0.75 U/μl without DTT as an optimized formulation that simultaneously enhances data quality and cost-effectiveness for full-length single-cell RNAsequencing.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68325-9.title: sGC oxidation impairs NO-dependent ophthalmic artery vascular reactivity and alters long-term memory performance in mice
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68325-9.abstract: Nitric oxide (NO)-dependent activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC) is essential for maintaining cerebrovascular function and cognitive processes. However, sGC is susceptible to oxidative inactivation under vascular and neurodegenerative stress. This study investigated the impact of chronic sGC oxidation on ophthalmic artery (OphA) hemodynamics, brain cGMP signaling, and memory performance in vivo. Young adult C57BL/6 mice were treated for one month with the heme-oxidizing agent ODQ. Vascular responsiveness was assessed using Doppler flow velocity imaging. ODQ markedly blunted NO-dependent reductions in peak flow and end-diastolic velocity following sodium nitroprusside administration and altered pulsatility responses, demonstrating impaired NO-driven vascular reactivity. In contrast, the heme-independent sGC activator cinaciguat produced comparable hemodynamic responses in ODQ- and vehicle-treated mice, indicating preserved reactivity of oxidized or heme-deficient sGC. Biochemical assays of forebrain lysates revealed a significant reduction in NO-stimulated cGMP formation in forebrain tissue following ODQ treatment. Cinaciguat- and protoporphyrin IX–stimulated activities remained unchanged, consistent with a selective loss of NO sensitivity rather than reduced enzyme abundance; sGC protein levels remained stable across groups. Behaviorally, ODQ impaired long-term recognition memory, with significant post hoc deficits observed in male mice, whereas short-term spatial memory remained unaffected. These findings demonstrate that chronic sGC oxidation selectively disrupts NO-dependent vascular and sGC signaling while preserving responsiveness to heme-independent sGC activation. Because the efficacy of heme-independent sGC activators was maintained, these findings support their therapeutic potential for oxidative vascular and neurological disorders.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67017-8.title: Climate change based yield production using hybrid deep learning with optimal feature selection

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68829-4.title: Performance assessment of various polymer flocculant types in clay-dolomite flocculation of tincal ore using macroscopic metrics
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68829-4.abstract: Abstract Borax, an important, refined boron product, is obtained by processing tincal ore through dissolution, separation from clay, crystallization, dewatering, and drying processes in factories. Precipitation of suspended clays with flocculant is a crucial stage in the process. In this study, suitable flocculant properties and appropriate operating conditions were determined in a laboratory setting for the refined borax production process. The studies were conducted using samples taken directly from the process and under the process conditions (95 °C, pH = 9.5). Flocculants with different properties (anionic, cationic, nonionic), obtained from a commercial firm, were used. The effect of flocculant type, charge density, and molecular weight on supernatant turbidity and solid settling rate was investigated as a function of flocculant dose, mixing rate and duration. All flocculants showed a parabolic trend with minimum turbidity and maximum settling rate. Anionic flocculants provided significantly higher flocculation efficiency. The anionic flocculant (AH3), with high molecular weight and low charge, demonstrated the highest flocculation performance, resulting in a turbidity of 9 NTU and a settling rate of 67 mm/min. The optimum flocculant dosage, mixing rate, and time for all flocculants were determined to be 2 mg/L, 150 rpm, and 1 min, respectively.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68087-4.title: Hybrid model-based real-time simulation of switching devices: enhancing precision and resource efficiency
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68087-4.abstract: Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulation technology based on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) effectively addresses the need for high-power and circuit fault state simulation in the field of power electronics, owing to its high-speed parallel processing and precise real-time simulation capabilities. This approach optimizes resource utilization, reduces costs, and accelerates the research and development cycle. However, traditional FPGA simulation methods often exhibit inefficiencies in model conversion and parameter adjustment, thereby reducing model editability. Furthermore, code redundancy exacerbates resource consumption and increases the simulation step size, limiting the capacity for high-precision and flexible simulations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a real-time simulation method based on Mixed Logical Dynamical (MLD) theory, aiming to enhance simulation accuracy while optimizing FPGA resource utilization. First, the applicability of the MLD framework for simulating circuit dynamic behavior is verified through theoretical analysis. Second, an MLD model of the target circuit is constructed and deployed on an FPGA platform using a Speedgoat real-time simulator. Comparative simulation results indicate that the proposed method effectively achieves a smaller minimum step size and reduces FPGA resource consumption, offering a viable approach for future HIL-related research.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69180-4.title: AI competency, attitudes, and experience as predictors of overall learning interaction via AI integration and creative tasks in GenAI-supported EFL classrooms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69180-4.abstract: Abstract Although generative AI is increasingly integrated into higher education, its impact on student’s learning experience remains unclear. This study examined factors predicting learning interactions in EFL (English as a Foreign Language) contexts, focusing on student’s AI competency, attitudes, and experience. Grounded in constructivist theory and the WEST model (Will, Experience, Skill, and Tools), a questionnaire was administered to 884 students at a Chinese higher vocational college. Structural equation modeling shows that AI integration and involvement in creative tasks directly predict learning interaction, while competency, attitudes, and experience exert indirect effects via these variables. Theoretically, this study provides quantitative evidence that student’s AI-related characteristics may contribute to learning interaction through AI-supported learning practices and creative task involvement. In practice, students can be more active in classroom interactions by adopting AI tools and participating in appropriate creative tasks designed by their teachers. Consequently, teachers play an important role in determining how AI tools are integrated and what types of tasks are assigned to students in the English classroom to support a better interactive learning environment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64492-x.title: Biochemical aspects of aluminum tolerance in triticale (× Triticosecale Wittmack)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64492-x.abstract: Aluminum (Al) toxicity severely restricts root growth and crop productivity in acidic soils. Despite the agronomic relevance of triticale (× Triticosecale Wittmack) in Europe, the biochemical basis of Al tolerance remains incompletely understood. Here, we combined physiological screening with multi-platform metabolite profiling and multivariate modeling to characterize Al-stress responses in highly homozygous triticale lines contrasting in Al tolerance (tolerant, T; non-tolerant, NT) and seasonal type (spring, S; winter, W). Al exposure induced pronounced shifts in biochemical composition, particularly in cell wall-associated carbohydrates and phenolic metabolites. NT lines accumulated higher levels of monosaccharides, arabinoxylan-derived fractions (based on arabinose and xylose measurements), and non-starch polysaccharides, alongside altered phenolic acid profiles. FTIR-based analyses revealed treatment- and genotype-dependent variation in glutathione (GSH), S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM), fatty acids (FA), and spectral signals associated with esterified polygalacturonic acid (PGA), with stronger genotype × treatment interactions for GSH and pectic components. Elastic Net regression identified carbohydrate composition, particularly the arabinose-to-xylose ratio, as a correlative indicator of Al treatment, suggesting stress-associated remodeling of arabinoxylan structure rather than a causal mechanism. In contrast, FTIR-based models more effectively resolved seasonal differences than Al treatment or tolerance classes, underscoring the dominant influence of developmental background on spectral profiles. Mixed graphical models further indicated that Al treatment primarily structured metabolic associations, whereas seasonality shaped redox- and energy-related interaction networks. Overall, our results reveal coordinated, genotype-dependent biochemical reprogramming under Al stress, highlighting distinct contributions of cell wall carbohydrate remodeling and metabolic network reorganization in triticale responses.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68032-5.title: Associations between baby swimming and preschooler child intelligence quotient: a cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68032-5.abstract: Baby swimming is a widely practiced early childhood healthcare activity, but its long-term health outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether baby swimming participation during the first six months of life is associated with intellectual development at preschool age. Children from the Wuhan Healthy Baby Cohort who completed follow-up questionnaires at 1 and 6 months and intelligence quotient (IQ) assessments between March 2022 and November 2023 were recruited. Based on baby swimming data, children were classified by participation status (participation, non-participation) and period (none, birth to 1 month, 1 to 6 months, and birth to 6 months). IQ was assessed using the Chinese version of the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-Fourth Edition at 4 to 6 years old. Generalized linear and logistic regression models assessed the association between swimming and IQ, with stratified analyses for maternal and infant-related factors. We included 1935 mother–child pairs, with 1272 children (65.7%) participating in baby swimming. Participants had higher scores in full-scale IQ (FSIQ) [ β (95%CI): 2.46 (1.35, 3.57)], verbal comprehension index (VCI) [1.64 (0.35, 2.92)], visual-spatial index (VSI) [2.15 (0.76, 3.54)], fluid reasoning index (FRI) [2.48 (1.44, 3.51)], and working memory index (WMI) [1.75 (0.62, 2.87)]. Higher IQ scores were observed in the “1 to 6 months” and “birth to 6 months” groups. Point estimates were numerically higher among boys and children from higher socioeconomic status (SES) families. Participation in baby swimming during the first 6 months was associated with higher preschool intellectual development scores, especially among boys and children from higher SES families. These findings support further research on early-life aquatic activity and neurodevelopment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65996-2.title: Optimized Deep Boltzmann machine for intrusion detection in wireless body area networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65996-2.abstract: Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs), intended for active examining of vital health statistics, face significant security challenges due to their wireless nature and potential vulnerabilities. Intrusion detection in WBANs is essential for protecting sensitive health data generated by interconnected medical devices. Effective IDS employ advanced algorithms and Machine Learning (ML) techniques to identify anomalies and potential threats, affirming authenticity and privacy of health information. By proactively monitoring network traffic and detecting unauthorized access, these systems enhance patient safety, maintain compliance with regulatory standards, and foster trust in wireless healthcare technologies. Main intension of this research is to develop Intrusion Detection System (IDS) in WBAN. Here, WBANsimulation is done initially, followed by the data pre-processing that consider data cleaning and Normalization. Then, the significant features in the data are selected using Boruta so as to reduce the time complexity and storage space required. After the feature selection, intrusion detection is performed using Deep Boltzmann Machine (DBM), which is trained using a Hybrid optimization, named Trend factor Smoothing Running City Game Optimizer (TS-RCGO). Here, TS-RCGOis developed by fusingTrend factor smoothing and Running City Game Optimizer (RCGO). Thus, with optimized DBM, the intruders are detected effectively. Experimental evidence highlights TS-RCGO based DBM technique exhibited superior performance relative to standard methods with accuracy rate of 95.9%, a sensitivity of 94%, a recall of 96%, and an F measure of 94.9%.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68149-7.title: Estimating the sensitivity relationships between temperature, heat wave and electric load in a hot and humid region: a case study of the Iranian power system
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68149-7.abstract: Accurate peak load forecasting is a very important input for Integrated Resource Planning (IRP) processes involving utilities and regulators. Weather conditions are among the key parameters in determining the amount of energy consumed. Finding the sensitivity of the energy consumption pattern to each of the environmental factors is one of the important issues for independent system operators and distribution system operators in the electricity grid. Among them, temperature is one of the most important climatic elements in the formation of the load pattern. For this reason, several studies have been conducted on the role of temperature in increasing or decreasing the electrical load.
