In the present study, we used a previously established methodology to investigate the change in subjective appearance of transitions in healthy adults across a continuous age range between 18 and 64. Consistent with prior studies, we found that dominance durations increased with age without any change in transition durations. Importantly, we observed age-related changes in transition appearance, which depended on the exact stimulus content used to induce binocular rivalry and were affecting only certain transition types. These results extend previous work by demonstrating that the qualitative experience of binocular rivalry can reflect important age-related changes which are not evident by conventional quantitative parameters.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68864-1.title: Physics-informed inverse identification and dynamic reconstruction of high-speed gear systems with asymmetric mesh stiffness
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68864-1.abstract: Gear transmission systems are critical components in engineering applications, yet their dynamic modeling under high-speed conditions remains challenging. This study develops a physics-informed learning framework for inverse identification and model diagnosis in nonlinear gear dynamics. Rather than using PINNs only as a parameter-estimation tool, the proposed framework is employed to examine the structural validity of the classical symmetric mesh-stiffness assumption. Benchmark tests first confirm that the PINN can accurately recover effective stiffness and damping parameters. When applied to ADAMS-generated transmission-error data, the identified symmetric stiffness successfully reconstructs the low-speed heavy-load response but exhibits a clear mismatch under the high-speed light-load condition, showing that parameter adjustment within the classical symmetric formulation is insufficient. Additional contact-state information extracted from ADAMS reveals that the low-speed response remains predominantly on a single contact branch, whereas the high-speed light-load response repeatedly switches between the drive-side and coast-side contact branches. This independent contact-state evidence, together with the mechanical nonequivalence of the two tooth flanks, motivates the manual formulation of a bilaterally asymmetric mesh-stiffness model. The proposed model provides a more consistent reconstruction of the high-speed light-load response and demonstrates that direction-dependent stiffness switching can provide an independent source of non-smoothness, including grazing-type transitions in the zero-backlash limit.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67927-7.title: Multivariate predictive modeling of photothermal response of indocyanine green loaded graphene oxide under continuous and pulsed laser irradiation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67927-7.abstract: The integration of photothermal therapy (PTT) into a single nanoplatform is a promising approach for precise cancer treatment; however, achieving predictable and optimized thermal doses remains a key challenge. While previous studies have explored graphene oxide (GO) and indocyanine green (ICG) composites, this work introduces a data-driven strategy to model and predict the photothermal response. We developed an ICG-GO nanocomposite and systematically investigated its performance under 808 nm near-infrared pulsed and continuous-wave laser irradiation. ICG functionalization enhanced the photothermal response of GO by up to 2.5-fold, achieving a rapid temperature increase to 45 °C within 2 min compared to 5 min for GO alone at 0.3 mg/mL and 1.5 W. Pulsed irradiation (laser-on: 200–1000 ms; laser-off: 50–150 ms) was identified as a crucial parameter for optimizing thermal management, reducing unwanted heat diffusion while maintaining therapeutic efficacy. Biocompatibility assessments confirmed that the integration of ICG attenuated the inherent cytotoxicity of GO, and the ICG-GO platform enabled efficient cancer cell ablation (ICG-GO at a concentration of 0.3 mg/mL, when exposed to continuous-wave laser irradiation at 1.5 W for 5 min, resulted in 98% cell death (2% cell viability)). The core innovation of this study lies in the application of multivariate statistical analysis, including ANOVA and regression modeling, which generated a predictive equation for the temperature output based on key laser parameters. This model provides a quantitative framework for optimizing PTT protocols. Thus, this study establishes the ICG-GO nanocomposite as an experimentally characterized photothermal platform and presents a predictive statistical framework that may facilitate future optimization of photothermal treatment parameters in preclinical research.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68936-2.title: Multi-layered of IN625 cladding by DED on the AISI 304: metallurgical and mechanical approach
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68936-2.abstract: This study investigates the effect of cladding thickness, controlled by increasing the number of deposited layers, on the microstructural and mechanical behavior of IN625 cladding deposited on AISI304 stainless steel using the Directed Energy Deposition (DED) process. The observed microstructural evolution and localized refinement in the cladded region are believed to contribute to the improvement in mechanical behavior. The average microhardness of the cladded region increased from 234 HV in the thinnest specimen to 270 HV in the thickest specimen, while the overall hardness of the clad/substrate system decreased from 482 H.B. to 438 H.B. due to reduction in hardness gradient across the interface. Residual stress measurements revealed that thinner cladded specimens experienced higher internal stresses because of steep thermal gradients, whereas thicker multilayer deposits promoted stress relaxation and improved thermal distribution. The highest shear strength was obtained for the specimen with approximately 4100 μm cladding thickness, reaching 812.24 MPa at room temperature, accompanied by dominant ductile fracture behavior. In contrast, specimens with 2000 μm and 9711 μm thickness exhibited interfacial failure associated with void formation and delamination near the interface. Fractography confirmed strong metallurgical bonding in optimized conditions, with failure occurring predominantly in the substrate. These findings demonstrate the critical role of deposition thickness and process optimization in improving interfacial integrity and mechanical performance of DED-fabricated SS304-IN625 cladding systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68146-w.title: YOLO-SR and GeoTrack for distress target detection and tracking in UAV maritime search and rescue
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68146-w.abstract: Reliable detection and tracking of distress targets in maritime search and rescue (SAR) remain challenging because of the extreme scale variation associated with UAV operating altitudes, where swimmers and other small targets may occupy only a few pixels. This challenge is further compounded by sea-surface reflections, wave patterns, and dynamic ocean backgrounds. This paper presents an integrated detection–tracking framework tailored to small-object maritime SAR scenarios. The proposed YOLO-SR (Small Refinement) detector extends YOLOv8-L with a lightweight high-resolution refinement branch operating on P3 feature maps to enhance the representation of small and distant targets while maintaining computational efficiency. In addition, GeoTrack extends ByteTrack through geometric filtering and motion-consistency based confidence modulation to suppress false trajectories associated with wave patterns and sea-surface reflections. Experimental evaluation on the SeaDronesSee dataset shows that YOLO-SR achieves a mAP@50 of 0.8959, mAP@50–95 of 0.5506, precision of 0.9146, and recall of 0.8724, improving upon the baseline YOLOv8-L detector. For multi-object tracking, GeoTrack achieves a MOTA of 58.4%, HOTA of 64.2%, and IDF1 of 64.2%, with improvements over the baseline ByteTrack in MOTA and IDF1. GeoTrack also achieves a tracking precision of 90.0% and reduces the proportion of Mostly Lost (ML) trajectories to 18%. The proposed framework achieves real-time inference at approximately 38 FPS on a desktop GPU and 15 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano, indicating its potential for embedded UAV-based maritime SAR applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67997-7.title: Context-aware AI assistance reduces diagnostic error in chest X-ray interpretation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67997-7.abstract: Static AI assistance assumes uniform benefit, but evidence from AI-supported radiology indicates benefit varies by context. Using data from the public Collab-CXR release (104,800 pathology-level observations, or 20,960 reads, from 326 radiologists across 324 cases), we reframed AI display as a human-centered assistance problem, learning and evaluating offline a context-aware assistance policy. The confirmatory average treatment effect on absolute diagnostic error approached null (-0.0014; SE 0.0015; p = 0.329), indicating that average effects obscure heterogeneity. In held-out evaluation, the adaptive policy achieved MAE 0.1034, versus 0.1060 for always showing AI (reduction 0.0026, 2.48%; cluster-bootstrap p = 0.0067) and 0.1088 for never showing AI (reduction 0.0054). The policy was translated into a three-variable decision tree (algorithm prediction, case difficulty, case-level AI accuracy) achieving 93.97% test concordance and a comparable held-out MAE of 0.1033. Simulation-based sensitivity analysis showed the policy contrast remained positive under modest hidden confounding but grew sensitive at higher levels. We conclude that static assistance is suboptimal in radiology and prospective testing of adaptive, trust-aware AI support is merited. For radiologists, administrators, and AI developers, uniform AI deployment is not the best strategy; selective, context-aware use may offer modest benefit, pending prospective confirmation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67621-8.title: Reinforcement learning-guided archival question answering with adaptive curriculum learning
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67621-8.abstract: Abstract The digitization of archival resources has created unprecedented demands for intelligent retrieval systems capable of handling complex queries across heterogeneous documentary collections. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning-guided question answering model specifically designed for archival question answering scenarios, incorporating a hierarchical reward mechanism that evaluates answer quality across multiple dimensions including factual accuracy, semantic relevance, and provenance clarity. Additionally, an adaptive curriculum learning training strategy is developed to enhance learning efficiency by dynamically adjusting sample difficulty based on model competency progression. The curriculum framework introduces a multi-dimensional query difficulty assessment system encompassing reasoning depth, entity count, coverage scope, and semantic ambiguity. On a Chinese municipal-and-provincial archival corpus of 28,546 query-answer pairs, the proposed approach reaches 78.9% accuracy and an F1 score of 0.824, a margin of 5.7 percentage points over the strongest re-implemented baseline. Adaptive curriculum learning does not shorten per-epoch computation; rather, it accelerates convergence, so that the wall-clock time needed to reach the same validation plateau falls by roughly 28% relative to the ablated variant trained without a curriculum. The gap widens sharply on multi-hop reasoning queries, where the relative gain over the same re-implemented baseline exceeds 17% on this corpus. Because these results rest on a single monolingual archival corpus and on baselines re-implemented under a shared protocol, the evidence should be read as supportive of the proposed design in this setting rather than as an unqualified demonstration of broad applicability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65432-5.title: Socioeconomic, treatment, and sociodemographic predictors of health related quality of life among cancer patients in Bangladesh
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65432-5.abstract: Cancer patients in low- and middle-income countries face substantial physical, psychological, and financial challenges that compromise quality of life (QoL). This study assessed socioeconomic barriers, clinical treatment, and sociodemographic predictors of Health-related Quality of Life (HRQoL) among cancer patients in Bangladesh. It was a cross-sectional study that randomly enrolled 278 cancer inpatients from three tertiary hospitals in Dhaka and Chattogram (July–September 2025). Data on sociodemographic status, clinical profiles, and socioeconomic barriers were collected via interviews and medical records. HRQoL was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and analyzed with a median split of the Global health status score of QoL. Following Boruta feature selection, ten machine learning classifiers were developed using stratified 10-fold cross-validation, with model interpretability achieved via SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Mean QoL global health score was severely compromised (23.73 ± 13.59), with high symptom burden for fatigue (79.94 ± 26.01), pain (71.35 ± 27.86), and financial difficulties (89.41 ± 19.76). Bivariate analyses showed significant QoL associations with income, education, marital status, family type, mode of diagnosis, caregiver support, and treatment financing. In the primary median-split analysis, Boruta confirmed 27 predictors, and Gradient Boosting Machine and CatBoost performed best (accuracy 0.914, 95% CI 0.874–0.944; ROC-AUC 0.939; PR-AUC 0.954), well above the no-information rate of 0.622. SHAP analysis of CatBoost model identified mode of cancer diagnosis, family type, monthly family income, primary caregiver identity, and treatment-cost financing as the most influential predictors. Machine learning found key sociodemographic and socioeconomic determinants of HRQoL, highlighting the need for targeted financial protection, caregiver-centered interventions, patient education, and enhanced palliative care access to reduce inequities in inpatient oncology services.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67733-1.title: Adaptation to progressive addition lens-induced optical blur reduces peripheral blur sensitivity
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67733-1.abstract: Progressive addition lenses (PALs) introduce spatially varying blur, including blur associated with unwanted astigmatism, but the perceptual consequences of this blur remain poorly understood. We tested whether short-term PAL wear was associated with spatially localized changes in blur sensitivity corresponding to regions of unwanted optical blur or with changes that were more broadly distributed across the visual field. Seven myopic presbyopes with astigmatism and no prior PAL experience were tested before and after two weeks of PAL wear. Blur sensitivity was measured using a two-alternative forced-choice comparison task at randomized visual-field locations, including the fovea, and 7.5 \(^\circ\) and 25 \(^\circ\) eccentricities across eight meridians. Threshold-versus-reference functions measured across five reference blur levels were fitted to estimate intrinsic blur. Linear mixed-effects models showed that two weeks of PAL wear significantly increased blur thresholds and intrinsic blur, indicating reduced blur sensitivity. However, these adaptation-related changes depended on eccentricity, with significant increases observed at 25 \(^\circ\) eccentricity ( p < 0.001), and not at 7.5 \(^\circ\) eccentricity or the fovea. Among the seven participants who completed both assessments, short-term PAL wear was therefore associated with increased blur thresholds and intrinsic blur at 25 \(^\circ\) eccentricity. The absence of statistically detectable meridional dependence suggests that this peripheral change was broadly distributed across the tested locations rather than confined to a specific meridian.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69146-6.title: Condition-aware averaged ultra-local predictive control with switching-period input–output collaborative reconstruction for NPC three-level power conversion systems
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69146-6.abstract: Model-based predictive control for NPC three-level power conversion systems (PCSs) relies on accurate plant parameters and is sensitive to switching ripple, measurement noise, and digital-delay-induced prediction errors. To address these issues, this paper proposes a switching-period input–output collaborative-reconstruction-based averaged ultra-local model (SPIOCR-AULM). In the proposed framework, parameter uncertainties, coordinate-coupling effects, capacitor-voltage influences, and unmodeled dynamics are absorbed into a unified lumped-disturbance channel and reconstructed online through an extended-state-observer-based structure. On the output side, oversampling-assisted multi-point fusion constructs a switching-period averaged state representation to reduce local ripple peaks and noisy instantaneous samples. On the control-input side, subinterval integration reconstructs the fast variation of the equivalent control voltage, while adjacent-period input actions are coordinated to obtain an averaged equivalent input. The noise-suppression mechanism and observer–compensation error dynamics are analyzed to reveal disturbance attenuation and parameter robustness. To further balance steady-state noise rejection and transient response, a condition-aware adaptive-bandwidth configuration is incorporated as an extension of SPIOCR-AULM, forming CAAB-SPIOCR-AULM. Simulations and experiments on a 125 kW prototype verify improved current quality, effective switching-ripple and measurement-noise suppression, and stable control performance under inductance mismatch, noise disturbance, and bidirectional power-flow operation in practical PCS conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69080-7.title: A randomized trial comparing the safety and efficacy of straight and articulating instruments (ArtiSential) in laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer patients
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69080-7.abstract: Abstract In conventional multiport laparoscopic radical gastrectomy, there is a lack of evidence demonstrating that articulating instruments (ArtiSential) improve surgical quality, particularly for suprapancreatic lymph node dissection and pancreas-related complications. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of using an articulating instrument. In this single-center prospective study, 76 patients undergoing laparoscopic radical gastrectomy were randomized to a control or experimental (articulating) group. In the articulating group, an articulating instrument was used by the assistant for pancreatic traction during suprapancreatic lymph node dissection. The primary endpoint was suprapancreatic lymph node dissection time; secondary endpoints included operative outcomes, early postoperative complications, and the number of retrieved suprapancreatic lymph nodes. Between July and December 2023, 38 patients were allocated to each group. The suprapancreatic lymph node dissection time was comparable between the two groups (Control: 20.74 ± 8.2 min; Articulating: 20.42 ± 7.5 min; P = 0.861). Additionally, there were no significant differences in total operation time, pancreatic enzyme levels (in both the serum and peritoneal fluid), and the number of retrieved suprapancreatic lymph nodes (Control: 15.66 ± 4.7; Articulating: 15.79 ± 5.6; P = 0.912). Estimated blood loss was higher in the articulating group, whereas no significant differences were observed in the incidence of postoperative complications. Although articulating instrument did not demonstrate superiority over conventional instruments, it may be considered for use during suprapancreatic lymph node dissection depending on the patient’s anatomy. Further studies are needed to better define its role in laparoscopic gastrectomy and its impact on overall surgical outcome.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65414-7.title: Targeting individual pain catastrophizing to reduce migraine-related disability: a randomized controlled proof-of-concept trial using an online CBT intervention
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65414-7.abstract: Abstract This mechanistic randomized controlled proof-of-concept trial (RCT) investigated whether a brief online Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)-based avatar intervention can reduce individual pain catastrophizing in individuals with migraine and examined whether reductions in individual pain catastrophizing are associated with decreased migraine-related disability. Migraine is a highly disabling disorder, yet the mechanisms underlying migraine-related disability remain poorly understood. The Fear Avoidance Model (FAM) and recent research suggest that pain catastrophizing is a key mediator linking migraine experience with disability. A total of N = 55 individuals with migraine and ≥ 4 migraine days/month were randomized to either an intervention group (receiving cognitive restructuring targeting individual pain catastrophizing statements), or an active control group (contradicting false statements about migraine). Assessments at baseline, post-intervention, and six-week follow-up included individual Pain Catastrophizing (PCS-3), Headache Impact Test (HIT-6), as well as migraine-related and clinical characteristics. Intervention was evaluated using linear mixed-effects model. Hierarchical regression was used to determine the predictive effect of reductions in pain catastrophizing on reductions in disability. The intervention group demonstrated significantly greater reductions in pain catastrophizing at post-intervention ( p = 0.009), while group differences diminished by follow-up. Decreases in individual pain catastrophizing were associated with reductions in migraine-related disability in both groups, explaining 24% of the variance ( R 2 adj = 0.24; p = 0.004). These findings suggest pain catastrophizing as a relevant factor in cognitive-affective pain processing contributing to migraine-related disability, as proposed by the FAM. It represents a potential therapeutic target that can be addressed through CBT-based interventions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67504-y.title: Plastic pollution shapes ecosystem response to a storm event in intertidal sediments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67504-y.abstract: Plastic pollution is an emerging driver of ecological change in coastal sediments, yet real-world ecosystem responses remain poorly understood. During a two-month in situ experiment on an intertidal sandflat in Mahurangi Harbour, New Zealand, a storm event provided a unique opportunity to test whether plastics modulate ecosystem responses to short-term environmental change. We measured sediment oxygen consumption (SOC), nutrient and N₂ fluxes, pore-water nutrient pools, and sediment organic matter in control and plastic-polluted plots across six time points spanning pre- and post-storm conditions. Plastic pollution was realised through vertical insertion of polyester nettings (6 × 2 cm, 10 µm thick, microplastic) into the sediment. Multivariate analyses revealed an interaction effect between treatment and sampling time indicating that the plastic-polluted sediments reacted differently to the storm. In control plots, the storm reduced SOC (− 24%) and pore-water NH₄⁺ (− 53%), and increased NH₄⁺ efflux (+ 186%) and NOₓ − pools (+ 166%). Compared to the storm response in the controls, the storm impact on plastic plots caused a 43% increase in SOC and a 53% increase in NH₄⁺ efflux, and lower pore-water NOₓ − (− 63%). These results demonstrate that plastics can modulate benthic ecosystem responses to storms, potentially altering nitrogen source–sink dynamics. As both plastic pollution and storm frequency intensify, such interaction effects may have growing consequences for coastal ecosystem functioning.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64939-1.title: Effect of live yeasts and essential oils as functional feed additives on growth performance and stress response in juvenile cobia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64939-1.abstract: The intensification of aquaculture introduces significant challenges, including increased exposure to environmental stressors that promote disease outbreaks, historically managed through antimicrobial use. As sustainable alternatives, functional feed additives are being explored for their potential to enhance fish performance and resilience. This study screened six candidate functional feed additives, including two autochthonous probiotic yeasts ( Candida haemuloni C27 and Debaryomyces hansenii C28) and four essential oils (EOs): lemongrass, ginger, garlic, and oregano, to evaluate their potential benefits and adverse effects on growth performance, physiological status, stress response, and serum antipathogenic activity in juvenile cobia ( Rachycentron canadum ), a benthopelagic marine species with high aquaculture potential. Fish were fed functional diets for four weeks, maintained under controlled physicalchemical conditions. Overall, most additives had no significant positive effect ( p > 0.05) on productive parameters, except garlic EO, which reduced feed intake and was associated with lower growth performance and histological alterations (shorter intestinal folds and damaged enterocytes and hepatocytes). However, serum from juvenile cobia supplemented with C. haemuloni C27 and ginger EO exhibited inhibitory activity against three strains of Vibrio harveyi , pathogens of fish. Additionally, cobia supplemented with C. haemuloni C27, ginger EO, garlic EO, and oregano EO displayed reduced serum cortisol levels following hypoxia-induced stress. Overall, the response to functional additives was additive-specific. C. haemuloni C27 and ginger EO emerged as the most promising candidates, enhancing serum antipathogenic activity and stress resilience without adverse effects on growth or tissue integrity, whereas garlic EO negatively affected feed acceptance, growth performance, and tissue condition at the inclusion level tested. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating both efficacy and safety when selecting functional feed additives for juvenile cobia.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61343-7.title: Application of GNP and MWCNT-based Nano-MQL lubrication combined with vortex cooling when machining of bearing steel
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61343-7.abstract: This study investigates the performance of environmentally friendly hybrid cooling/lubrication strategies for the machining of 100Cr6 bearing steel, with a particular focus on integrating nanofluid-based minimum quantity lubrication and vortex tube cooling. Eight different cooling/lubrication methods were used: i.e., dry, MQL, Vortex, MQL+Vortex, MWCNT, MWCNT+Vortex, GNP, and GNP+Vortex. To characterize the tribological and thermophysical behavior of the nanofluids, viscosity, pH, and thermal conductivity measurements were conducted. Machining performance was assessed in terms of cutting temperature, surface roughness, power consumption, and flank wear under controlled turning experiments. The experimental results clearly demonstrate that hybrid systems outperform both conventional and single-mode cooling strategies. Among the tested conditions, the MWCNT + vortex configuration showed the greatest improvements across all performance indicators. Compared to dry machining, this hybrid approach reduced cutting temperature by 49.85%, surface roughness by 22.89%, power consumption by 20.97%, and flank wear by 87.94%. Similar, though slightly lower, improvements were observed in GNP-based hybrid conditions, confirming the effectiveness of nanoparticle-assisted lubrication in enhancing tribological performance. Overall, the combination of vortex tube cooling and nanofluid-assisted MQL creates a highly effective hybrid strategy for improving the machinability of 100Cr6 bearing steel. The results clearly indicate that MWCNT-based nanofluids combined with vortex cooling provide the most favorable balance between thermal management, energy efficiency, and tool protection.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68292-1.title: Population genetics of wild boars across South Korea shows broad-scale distance-driven structure and a region-specific riverine barrier
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68292-1.abstract: In South Korea, expanding wild boar populations have increased concerns regarding human-wildlife conflict and the spread of African swine fever (ASF). Yet their population genetic structure and connectivity remain poorly understood, limiting effective wildlife and disease management. We present the most comprehensive population-genetic analysis of wild boars ( Sus scrofa ) in South Korea, using 13 polymorphic microsatellite loci and1,813 individuals collected nationwide between 2019 and 2023. Overall, wild boars exhibited high genetic diversity across the peninsula with moderate regional variation. Gangwon region showed the highest diversity (N A = 7.3, H O = 0.70), whereas Jeolla region exhibited the lowest (N A = 6.6, H O = 0.61). Mild heterozygote deficits and non-random allelic associations suggested fine-scale population structuring, particularly in Chungcheong region. Pairwise F ST values indicated low but statistically significant genetic differentiation, with Gyeonggi and Gangwon forming a largely continuous genetic unit, while Jeolla was the most differentiated. The comparatively high differentiation between Chungcheong and Jeolla, despite their geographic proximity, suggests that the Geum River and associated landscape features reduce connectivity beyond that expected from geographic distance alone. Bayesian clustering analyses revealed two primary genetic clusters with additional hierarchical subdivision, while discriminant analysis of principal components indicated gradual geographic differentiation among predefined regional groups and extensive overlap among neighbouring populations. Significant isolation by distance and AMOVA further demonstrated that most genetic variation is maintained within individuals despite detectable regional genetic structure. These findings demonstrate that South Korean wild boars maintain high genetic diversity alongside stable regional genetic structure, shaped by habitat configuration, riverine barriers, and historical dispersal processes. This genetic framework provides a basis for regionally coordinated ASF surveillance and spatially informed wildlife management in South Korea.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61722-0.title: Research on trusted closed loop management of the whole process of service evaluation based on blockchain
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61722-0.abstract: Conventional service evaluation systems are increasingly plagued by data opacity, susceptibility to tampering, and delayed feedback loops, which erode stakeholder trust and hinder effective quality governance. To address these critical challenges, this study proposes and empirically validates a blockchain-enabled framework for trusted closed-loop management of the entire service evaluation process. The proposed architecture synergizes distributed ledger technology, autonomous smart contracts, and a dynamic Bayesian trust scoring model to achieve real-time data verification, automated corrective feedback, and adaptive trust computation. We analyzed a comprehensive dataset of 1,200 service interactions across the hospitality, healthcare, and e-commerce sectors, characterized by customer satisfaction scores ranging from 5.1 to 9.8, reliability indices between 0.72 and 0.96, and normalized positive interaction frequencies from 0.42 to 0.89. Empirical results demonstrate that the integration of the blockchain framework significantly elevated mean trust scores from 0.71 (± 0.12) to 0.88 (± 0.09), representing a statistically significant 23.7% improvement. Furthermore, the system reduced the variance in satisfaction ratings by 0.48 and lowered overall service discrepancy rates by up to 15.4%. Sector-specific dynamic weight adjustments yielded optimized outcomes, including a 7.4% increase in reliability for healthcare and a 6.3% improvement in consistency for hospitality. Comparative analysis reveals that while conventional digital evaluation systems typically achieve only 5–12% performance gains, our blockchain-based approach substantially enhances trust, accuracy, and process transparency. Crucially, the closed-loop mechanism facilitated timely interventions, reducing critical service deviations by 17.5% in healthcare and 15.4% in e-commerce. These findings offer robust theoretical validation and practical guidelines for deploying transparent, accountable, and adaptive service evaluation ecosystems in diverse industrial contexts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67387-z.title: Nippostrongylus brasiliensis and Heligmosomoides polygyrus exert anti-inflammatory effects through distinct immunomodulatory mechanisms in murine macrophages in vitro
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67387-z.abstract: Hookworm infections affect hundreds of millions of people worldwide and rank among the most significant neglected tropical diseases in terms of morbidity. Due to the inverse correlation between hookworm infection and the incidence of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, considerable research has focused on understanding how parasitic helminths modulate host inflammation. Heligmosomoides polygyrus and Nippostrongylus brasiliensis are two hookworm-like rodent models widely used to investigate fundamental aspects of immune regulation. However, no comparative study has yet analysed the distinct immunological pathways activated by these helminths in their hosts. In this study, we compared cytokine profiles and M1/M2 macrophage polarization markers induced by H. polygyrus and N. brasiliensis , alongside proteomic pathways involved in their activation, using the RAW 264.7 murine macrophage cell line. H. polygyrus downregulated proinflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and MCP-1, whereas N. brasiliensis did not affect TNF-α expression. Both parasites upregulated Th2 and regulatory cytokines, including IL-4 and TGF-β. Furthermore, H. polygyrus predominantly polarized macrophages toward an M2 phenotype, while N. brasiliensis maintained a balanced M1/M2 profile. Proteomic analysis revealed that N. brasiliensis and H. polygyrus exert their anti-inflammatory effects through distinct mechanisms, with N. brasiliensis acting via peripheral pathways and H. polygyrus via central regulatory mechanisms.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65752-6.title: Assessment of future meteorological droughts in Iran
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65752-6.abstract: Abstract Climate change amplifies the risk of hydroclimatic extremes, posing significant challenges for arid and semi-arid regions vulnerable to temperature and precipitation variability. This study projects future meteorological drought in Iran under different climate change scenarios, focusing on two key objectives: (1) evaluating the performance of the NASA Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP) from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6), and (2) quantifying future drought conditions using the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI). We employ a multi-model ensemble of 25 bias-corrected and downscaled General Circulation Models (GCMs) under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, SSP3–7.0, and SSP5–8.5) to project variations in temperature, precipitation, and meteorological drought occurrence in Iran for 2071–2100. The novelty of this study lies in integrating an Iran-specific evaluation of NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 with multi-timescale SPI–SPEI comparison and quantitative attribution of projected drought changes to precipitation and potential evapotranspiration (PET). Results reveal pronounced warming, especially under SSP5–8.5, exceeding 5 °C in many parts of the country by 2100. Although precipitation projections show slight increases overall, notably under SSP3–7.0, substantial regional variability persists. Projections indicate that meteorological droughts are expected to become more frequent and severe in the northwestern and southeastern parts of Iran, with SPEI indicating greater drought intensity and duration due to temperature-driven increases in PET. These findings highlight the need for climate-resilient water management and robust adaptation policies to reduce the impacts of future droughts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63883-4.title: Distributed event-triggered fault-tolerant secondary control for DC microgrids under mixed faults and communication impairments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63883-4.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a distributed event-triggered fault-tolerant secondary control framework for DC microgrids operating under actuator loss-of-effectiveness faults, current-sharing sensor anomalies, and communication impairments. The proposed approach integrates distributed secondary regulation, packetized event-triggered communication, residual-based fault detection and isolation, and health-aware supervisory reconfiguration within a unified control architecture. The secondary correction signals are injected into the primary layer through the exact outer-loop voltage reference update, while the supervisory mechanism modifies both the control path and the effective communication graph according to the diagnosed fault type and severity. Nominal quadratic stability is established around the healthy operating point, whereas the delayed fault-affected implementation is interpreted within a practical stability/uniform ultimate boundedness framework. Simulation results on a four-converter mesh DC microgrid demonstrate that the proposed method correctly isolates all injected fault cases and reduces the post-fault current-sharing spread by up to $$94.81\%$$ relative to the baseline event-triggered controller, while preserving DC-bus voltage regulation under single-fault, mixed-fault, and dual-actuator stress scenarios. These improvements are statistically validated through a Monte Carlo study over independent stochastic communication realizations, and a complementary robustness study shows that fault isolation remains fully reliable under FDD-model parameter mismatch of up to $$20\%$$ combined with realistic measurement noise.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68865-0.title: Biomimetic design and optimization of aero-engine blades inspired by humpback whale tubercles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68865-0.abstract: Aiming at the performance optimization of turbine power simulator fan blades, this study introduces the bionic structure of humpback whale pectoral fin tubercles to modify the original blade airfoil designed by Changchun University of Science and Technology, so as to improve aerodynamic performance while analyzing structural strength. Python is used to program the forming of bionic blades with quadratic curve controlled by three control points. The static aerodynamic elastic characteristics are solved by finite element method, and the unsteady compressible N-S equations are numerically calculated by node-based finite volume method with S-A turbulence model and LU-SGS time discretization. The partitioned fluid-structure coupling strategy is adopted for iterative computation. The results showed that the ratio of the maximum deformation of the bionic blade to the diameter of the blade disk decreased from 0.306% to 0.239%, indicating that the strength of the bionic blade was theoretically slightly enhanced. The flow field was effectively optimized, with a 4.09% increase in single-channel flow rate, a 4.85% increase in pressure ratio, and an improvement in blade efficiency from 67.014% to 89.861%(optimize fan seal). The bionic structure suppresses flow separation and vortex dissipation, homogenizes the pressure, temperature and Mach number distributions, and reduces flow loss. It is concluded that the humpback whale fin tubercle bionic design can greatly enhance the aerodynamic performance of fan blades, and subsequent structural optimization is needed to improve the stiffness and service reliability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67512-y.title: Urban green spaces as nature-based solutions for carbon storage and human thermal comfort: evidence from Jimma City, Ethiopia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67512-y.abstract: Urban green spaces provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon storage and thermal regulation, yet their condition remains poorly quantified in many rapidly urbanizing African cities. This study assessed the potential of urban green spaces as nature-based solutions for carbon sequestration and human thermal comfort in Jimma City, Ethiopia, using a locally calibrated Urban Green Space Condition Index (UGSCI) derived from Landsat 8 imagery and geospatial techniques. Key findings reveal that only 18% of the study area exhibits good green space conditions, with total aboveground carbon stock estimated at 2.18 million Mg C and a mean carbon density of 208.7 Mg C/ha. Dense vegetation stored substantially more carbon per unit area than built-up areas. A strong negative relationship between UGSCI and thermal discomfort (R 2 = 0.61) confirms that improving green space condition significantly enhances urban cooling. The UGSCI framework offers a replicable, low-cost methodology for monitoring urban environmental quality, readily transferable to other rapidly urbanizing cities in the Global South. By establishing a carbon stock baseline for Jimma City and identifying priority areas for green space investment and highlighting environmental justice implications, this study provides evidence-based guidance for sustainable urban planning and climate adaptation, directly supporting progress toward Sustainable Development Goals 11 (Sustainable Cities) and 13 (Climate Action).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67487-w.title: A multi-dimensional framework for quantifying dance movement complexity with hierarchical structure analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67487-w.abstract: Dance is a highly expressive form of human motion that involves coordinated changes in body posture, timing, rhythm, and spatial use. However, the analysis of dance movement complexity is still frequently based on subjective judgement, making it difficult to compare performances across dancers, styles, choreographic structures, and learning stages. This paper proposes a systematic framework for quantifying the complexity of dance movements from pose-based motion data and for analyzing the hierarchical organization of complexity within a performance. Raw video or motion-capture input is transformed into a standardized time series of human body keypoints. After interpolation, smoothing, alignment, and scale normalization, the motion sequence is represented through joint positions, velocities, accelerations, angular changes, and segment-level descriptors. Complexity is then decomposed into five interpretable dimensions: kinematic variation, temporal complexity, spatial complexity, structural diversity, and information-theoretic irregularity. These dimensions are computed locally over temporal windows and globally over complete performances, producing both a multi-dimensional complexity profile and an optional aggregate index. A hierarchical structure analysis is further introduced to connect joint-level behavior, short motion units, phrase-level segments, and complete choreographies. The framework supports standardized and reproducible comparison between dance styles, dancers, and choreographic sections while preserving interpretability. The proposed method provides a reproducible basis for dance analysis, intelligent feedback, digital performance evaluation, and broader computational studies of complex human movement.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63673-y.title: Predicting HbA1c levels using Bayesian long-short-term memory with attention mechanism for diabetes management
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63673-y.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is one of the most common and alarming long-term health conditions globally. The prevalence of diabetes is on the rise, with millions of adults reckoned to be living with the ailment due to sedentary lifestyles and traits. Ineffective glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) measurements and undiagnosed cases have resulted in a high rate of significant complications that characterize the diabetes crisis. HbA1c measurements are often used to assess the levels of blood glucose of patients with type 2 diabetes over a longer period. Thus, it is essential to design a robust model that can accurately predict the HbA1c levels of patients to augment early diagnosis and further treatment. In this study, a Bayesian self-attention bidirectional long short-term memory (Bayesian SA-BLSTM) model is proposed to leverage the time-series data from patients with type 2 diabetes, thereby accurately predicting their HbA1c levels. When compared with traditional LSTM, Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM), extreme gradient-boosting machine (XGBoost), BLSTM, and self-attention BLSTM models using the same dataset, our proposed Bayesian SA-BLSTM model exhibited superior prediction power with vigorous credible intervals to reflect the uncertainty in the predicted HbA1c levels. Our finding is a revelation that the Bayesian extension of SA-BLSTM models provides improved predictive performance for effective type 2 diabetes assessment to assist in early detection and subsequent management of the disease. This is an indication that employing Bayesian methods to extend SA-LSTM models can lead to improved predictive performance.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69087-0.title: Diet quality according to participation in a workplace nutrition assistance program
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69087-0.abstract: Abstract Public food policies reduce poverty and food insecurity; however, their impact on participants’ diet quality remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between participation in a workplace nutritional assistance policy and food quality. A combined stratified and two-stage cross-sectional survey compared random samples of workers from companies participating ( n = 480) and not participating ( n = 441) in the Brazilian Workers’ Food Program (WFP). Usual food consumption was assessed with 24-hour dietary recall and diet quality with the Diet Quality Index-International (DQI-I). Mixed-effects regression analyses examined the association between DQI-I scores, including its categories and components, and WFP participation according to workers’ sex, and their interaction. WFP participation was associated with greater DQI-I score but only among women ( p = 0.007, men p = 0.56, interaction p = 0.001). Among DQI-I categories, WFP participants scored higher in Variety, both for the food groups and protein sources components. Adequacy showed higher scores among WFP participants ( p = 0.025) only in women. No association was observed between WFP participation and Moderation or Overall Balance, although lower consumption of saturated fat and sodium was found among women participants (interaction p = 0.022 and p = 0.013, respectively). Participation in a WFP was positively associated with higher diet quality scores as assessed by the DQI-I, mainly among women.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68092-7.title: Genome-wide association study identifies candidate genes for agronomic traits under heat- and combined recurrent drought-and heat-stress in wheat
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68092-7.abstract: Combined heat and drought stress, mainly during sensitive growth stages, considerably limits wheat yields. Herein, we report on an experiment conducted to analyze and predict the phenology, architecture, and kernel yield component (PAKyC) traits of a diverse bread wheat population grown under heat stress and fully irrigated conditions (HSFIC), and combined recurrent drought and heat stress (CRDHS). 17,711 high-quality single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were used to perform a GWAS for 13 PAKyC traits on 187 genotypes, a subset of 234 genotypes, using the BLINK model. Nine constitutive SNPs, 24 marker-trait associations (MTAs), broad-effect pleiotropic SNPs, conditional pleiotropic SNPs, adaptive pleiotropic SNPs under CRDHS, and two robust SNPs were identified. Furthermore, 35 candidate genes were associated with cellular components, biological processes, and molecular functions under CRDHS and HSFIC. Among these genes, 12 were highly expressed (> 0.5 TPM) in response to drought, heat, and combined stresses. Nine genes were identified to be transcription factors regulating drought and heat responses, while the functions of the other three genes remain unclear. Overall, HSFIC and CRDHS environments enabled the dissection of heritable and strongly correlated traits, MTAs, and pleiotropy types: constitutive, adaptive, and conditional. They also helped identify robust SNPs and candidate genes that are important for bread wheat breeding.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66789-3.title: Rapid lignin degradation and reusability of a chitosan-immobilized fungal consortium: a comparative evaluation with the suspended system
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66789-3.abstract: Lignin-rich effluents generated from kraft pulp mills are difficult to treat because of the recalcitrant aromatic structure of lignin. Although fungal consortia can enhance lignin degradation through synergistic enzymatic activity, suspended systems often suffer from poor operational stability and limited reusability. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a novel fungal consortium comprising newly isolated Penicillium spp. and Leiotrametes flavida (MTCC 12927) for lignin degradation, investigate different immobilization matrices to identify a suitable support system, and evaluate the effect of immobilization on degradation efficiency, extracellular enzyme activity, operational stability, and reusability. The lignin degradation performance of the consortium was first evaluated using a model lignin-rich wastewater (lignin concentration of 1 g L − 1 ) under suspended conditions, followed by screening of different immobilization matrices and assessment of the effects of immobilization on degradation efficiency, enzyme activity, operational stability and reusability. Among the designed consortia, consortium C3, comprising Penicillium spp. AP1, Penicillium spp. AP2, and Leiotrametes flavida AP3 mixed in a volumetric ratio (v/v) of 3:1:2, exhibited the highest lignin degradation efficiency. Under optimized conditions, the suspended consortium degraded 86.27% lignin in 24 h, whereas the immobilized consortium achieved 97.5 ± 0.42% degradation in 24 h, with 97.1 ± 0.8% degradation attained within 6 h. The immobilized consortium retained > 80% degradation efficiency for 12 consecutive cycles, indicating excellent operational stability and reusability. Among the ligninolytic enzymes, manganese peroxidase (MnP) showed the highest activity, reaching 1925.1 ± 7.2 U mL⁻¹ in the suspended consortium and 592.7 ± 9.5 U mL⁻¹ in the immobilized consortium. Treatment also reduced COD (96.8%) and BOD (79.7%). Overall, chitosan immobilization enabled rapid, reusable, and highly efficient lignin degradation, demonstrating strong potential for treatment of lignin-rich industrial wastewater.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68450-5.title: Comparative experimental and quantum chemical investigation of para anisidine and para chloroaniline formaldehyde copolymers as corrosion inhibitors
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68450-5.abstract: This study investigates the application of para-anisidine formaldehyde (pAF) and para-chloroaniline formaldehyde (pCF) copolymers as effective corrosion inhibitors with potential environmental advantages for mild steel in 0.5 N HCl solution. These copolymers exhibited high inhibition performance at low concentrations and showed low volatility, indicating potential environmental compatibility. Gravimetric analysis revealed high inhibition efficiencies of 97.1% for pAF and 95.2% for pCF at an optimal concentration of 12 ppm. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results showed a significant increase in charge transfer resistance (R ct ) values from 54.3 Ω cm 2 for the blank solution to 173.8 Ω cm 2 for pAF and 149.5 Ω cm 2 for pCF, indicating effective surface protection. Potentiodynamic polarization studies confirmed that both inhibitors act as mixed-type, reducing both anodic and cathodic reactions, with corrosion current density (i corr ) values decreasing from 154 µA cm −2 for the blank to 4.5 µA cm −2 for pAF and 7.3 µA cm −2 for pCF. Adsorption behavior was consistent with the Langmuir adsorption isotherm, indicating the formation of a protective adsorbed layer on the mild steel surface. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were performed to investigate the electronic properties and adsorption mechanism of the copolymers. The results suggested that the higher electron density around the oxygen atoms in pAF and pCF facilitated stronger interactions with the mild steel surface. Surface characterization and DFT calculations supported the proposed corrosion inhibition mechanism. Overall, both copolymers demonstrated effective corrosion inhibition in acidic media, with pAF exhibiting a higher inhibition efficiency (97.1%) than pCF (95.2%) under the investigated conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68753-7.title: Associations of basic and decision-making health literacy skills with psychological factors related to breast cancer screening: a bayesian network analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68753-7.abstract: Breast cancer screening is vital for early detection, yet participation among rural women remains low. Basic and decision-making health literacy skills are associated with how individuals understand and act on screening information, and this study examined how these two skills relate to key psychological factors involved in breast cancer screening. A cross-sectional study was conducted between May and June 2024 among rural women aged 40 years and above in Minoodasht, northern Iran. Using a geographically stratified multi-stage sampling approach, 261 rural women were selected from Health Houses affiliated with four Comprehensive Health Service Centers. Standardized questionnaires were used to assess demographics, misbeliefs, attitudes, perceived barriers, and health literacy skills. A Bayesian Network model was used to assess probabilistic relationships; statistical analyses were conducted in SPSS (v21) and Netica. Women with lower education demonstrated poorer performance in both health literacy domains, married women reported higher levels of misbeliefs, and older women perceived more screening barriers. Barriers and misbeliefs were more sensitive to decision-making than basic health literacy, while attitudes showed minimal change. These findings indicate that basic health literacy alone is insufficient unless women can translate information into informed decisions, highlighting the need to prioritize decision-making health literacy in interventions targeting rural women.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68046-z.title: Linking phenotypic diversity to genomic hotspots using multi-environmental GWAS reveals genetic control of agronomic traits and drought resilience in wheat
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68046-z.abstract: Climate volatility demands wheat varieties with enhanced yield stability. Unraveling the genetic basis of stability, particularly genotype-by-environment (G × E) interactions, is critical in varirty development. We performed a high-resolution genetic analysis on 158 wheat recombinant inbred lines (RILs) for 19 traits across 12 contrasting environments. Using 14,676 SNP markers, we conducted a multi-environment genome-wide association study (GWAS) with Mixed Linear Model (MLM) and Fixed and Random Model Circulating Probability Unification (FarmCPU) models, followed by Linkage Disequilibrium (LD) block, haplotype, and pleiotropy analyses. Phenotypic data showed yield components were environmentally sensitive, while traits like plant height (PH) were strongly controlled by genetic components. Genomic analyses revealed distinct sub-genome architectures. Key results include the identification of 8,092 significant SNP-trait associations and the discovery of 57 environmentally stable, pleiotropic SNPs. Chromosome group 1 (1A, 1B, 1D) was a major hotspot, harboring 32 multi-trait loci. Multi-environment GWAS revealed that the extreme PH effects ( R 2 > 80%) were non-transferable across environments, with R 2 values falling to the 4–15% range in all other environments (E2–E12), indicating that such high values reflect single-environment bias rather than stable QTL effects. The megabase-scale LD blocks indicated extended haplotype conservation, a pattern that may arise from either directional breeding or the inherent recombination limitations of this biparental RIL population,, and haplotype analysis revealed diverse patterns from fixation to high diversity. Haplotype‑level analysis confirmed that many SNPs identified by MLM and FarmCPU are in high LD (e.g., on chromosome 5A for SPAD in E1, over a ~ 190 Mb region), indicating that they tag the same underlying quantitative trait loci (QTL). We prioritized 40 high-confidence candidate genes and confirmed stable QTLs, including a yield QTL on 1A (qGY-1A.1) and a multi-trait region on 2A. This study elucidates the complex genetic architecture of wheat productivity. Our integrated approach disentangled G × E interactions and identified genomic regions under selection. The pleiotropic hubs, stable QTLs, and candidate genes provide a robust framework for marker-assisted breeding, accelerating the development of climate-resilient wheat.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69014-3.title: ABDEG mutations in engineered IgG1 Fc fragments balance FcRn engagement and molecular stability to maximize IgG degradation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69014-3.abstract: Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies play a central role in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Therapeutic strategies targeting IgG recycling via the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) have shown promise. Here, we show how modulating FcRn engagement affects IgG clearance, through evaluation of five engineered Fc IgG1 fragments (YPY, ABDEG, YY, HN, HN/ABDEG). Fc IgG1 -ABDEG demonstrated superior pharmacological potential, exhibiting enhanced FcRn affinity at both physiological and endosomal pH while maintaining near-native stability, unlike YPY, which destabilized the Fc region despite maximal FcRn engagement. In vivo, ABDEG achieved favorable serum persistence and significant IgG reduction compared with YPY, confirming that increased FcRn binding improves outcomes only to a threshold. Subclass analyses identified IgG1 as the optimal backbone for ABDEG incorporation. Furthermore, the importance of FcRn:IgG binding stoichiometry was highlighted using an asymmetrically engineered Fc variant. These findings underscore Fc engineering as a viable approach for modulating IgG homeostasis and inform future optimization of FcRn-targeted therapies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65747-3.title: miRNA levels are associated with functional physical capacity and inflammation in patients with end-stage kidney disease
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65747-3.abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a global health problem, especially in the elderly, leading to renal failure through gradual progression and chronic inflammation, in addition to increasing cardiovascular risk. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression, act as chemical messengers and have been shown to be important for the diagnosis and prognosis of chronic diseases. This study investigates miRNAs such as miR-1, miR-16, miR-150 and miR-206, involved in inflammatory and cardiovascular processes in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). The objective was to evaluate the association of these miRNAs with cardiovascular risk factors, inflammatory status and physical-functional capacity. 23 individuals without CKD (control) and 25 with ESRD were selected. The results showed that the expressions of miRNAs and tumor necrosis factor alpha are higher in patients with ESRD, while fat-free mass, handgrip strength and functional capacity are reduced. All miRNAs analyzed showed a positive correlation with the inflammatory state and a negative correlation with physical-functional capacity. The miR-16 and miR-206 stood out in the study, supporting the potential role of these miRNAs, especially miR-16, as exploratory biomarkers associated with ESRD-related inflammatory and physical-functional impairment. Thus, the work contributes significantly to the development of more targeted and individualized therapeutic interventions, promoting significant advances in the care of ESRD and its complications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67545-3.title: Predicting next-generation farming succession intentions in northwestern Ethiopia using the theory of planned behavior and structural equation modeling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67545-3.abstract: Ensuring intergenerational farm succession is essential for sustaining smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia, where family farming remains the primary source of rural livelihoods. Although previous studies have mainly emphasized structural factors such as land access, farm size, and profitability, limited empirical evidence exists on the behavioral factors influencing rural youths’ intention to succeed family farms, particularly in Ethiopia. This study therefore examined the determinants of farm succession intention among rural youth in Sinan District, Amhara Region, northwestern Ethiopia, using the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). The study included rural youth aged 18–35 years, with the lower age limit of 18 years selected to avoid the ethical and procedural requirements for minors and to align with the African Union’s youth definition. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 370 potential farm successors selected through a multistage sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that the TPB explained 37.4% of the variance in farm succession intention (R² = 0.374). Perceived behavioral control was the strongest predictor of farm succession intention (β = 0.310, t = 6.687), followed by subjective norms (β = 0.268, t = 5.091) and attitude (β = 0.195, t = 3.955), with all relationships statistically significant ( p < 0.001). The findings demonstrate that rural youths are more likely to intend to continue family farming when they perceive themselves as capable of farming successfully, receive support from family and community members, and hold favorable attitudes toward agriculture. The study extends the application of the TPB to farm succession in the Ethiopian smallholder context and provides evidence to inform policies that strengthen youth access to land, agricultural finance, practical training, extension services, and family-based succession planning to improve generational renewal in agriculture.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67293-4.title: Wavefront improvement in Nd: YAG zigzag slab amplifier by optimizing pump beam configuration and mechanical stress
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67293-4.abstract: To optimize the wavefront quality in end-pumped Nd: YAG slab amplifier systems, the effects of three important parameters- pump beam configuration, torque-induced stress during slab chamber assembly, and increased convective heat-transfer coefficient- were optimized. As a result, the fluctuating optical path difference decreased from over 8.7 μm to 2 μm at pump power of 2.4 kW. Also, when the BQ parameter was calculated at a pump power of about 3 kW, it decreased from 12.22 to 4.35 in configurations 1 and 2. The optical path difference was evaluated using interferometric techniques, which provide high sensitivity for optimizing the parameters of the zigzag slab-pumping module. The optimized amplifier module results are in good agreement with the experimental observations, clearly validating the proposed approach.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66356-w.title: Pressure-dependent DFT study of A2LuCuH6 (A = Li, Na, K) hydrides for hydrogen storage and photo-catalytic water splitting applications
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66356-w.abstract: Abstract Next-generation clean-energy technologies seek efficient solid-state energy storage materials for hydrogen-based energy systems that exhibit thermodynamically stable properties and multifunctional optoelectronic performance. In the current article, the structural, hydrogen-storage, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermodynamic, and photocatalytic properties of the A 2 LuCuH 6 (A = Li, Na, K) cubic double perovskite hydrides are systematically investigated using first principles density functional theory calculations. The optimized lattice constant gradually rises from 7.78 Å in Li 2 LuCuH 6 to 7.94 Å in Na 2 LuCuH 6 and 8.18 Å in K 2 LuCuH 6 , and the bulk modulus gradually reduces from 43.48 to 39.29 GPa, showing gradually increasing lattice softening. Negative formation enthalpies of -43.08, -48.71, and − 54.99 kJ/mol verify their thermodynamic stability. The gravimetric hydrogen-storage capacities are recorded as 2.34, 2.08, and 1.87 wt%, while the volumetric capacities are 21.33, 20.06, and 18.35 gH 2 /L for Li, Na, and K-based compounds, respectively. The computed hydrogen desorption temperatures are 329.61, 372.54, and 420.73 K, which show tunable hydrogen-release behavior. The indirect semiconducting band gaps in the range of 1.46–2.01 eV at ambient pressure with strong optical absorption in the visible-UV range. In addition, the favorable band-edge alignment is indicative of photocatalytic suitability for overall water splitting, and the pressure-dependent thermodynamic parameters indicate lattice rigidity and a decrease in anharmonic effects under compression, which demonstrates the multi-functional energy potential of these hydride perovskites.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68312-0.title: Saussurea medusa Maxim extract suppresses triple‑negative breast cancer growth by disrupting mitochondrial lipid metabolism via the PPARα/CPT1A fatty acid oxidation axis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68312-0.abstract: Triple‑negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective targeted therapies and exhibits pronounced metabolic plasticity. Mitochondrial lipid metabolism and fatty acid oxidation (FAO) represent potential vulnerabilities. We investigated the antitumor activity and mechanism of Saussurea medusa Maxim extract (SMME) in TNBC models. SMME was profiled by HPLC–HRMS. Antitumor phenotypes, including viability, apoptosis, migration, and ultrastructural changes, were evaluated in TNBC cells. In vivo efficacy was assessed using an orthotopic 4T1 mouse model. Mechanism discovery relied on integrated proteomics and metabolomics. To validate target causality, we performed intracellular ATP quantification, representative active monomer evaluation, and pharmacological rescue assays. SMME and its representative active monomer inhibited cell viability across human and murine TNBC models. Furthermore, SMME impaired cell migration, induced apoptosis, and suppressed orthotopic tumor growth in vivo without obvious toxicity. Ultrastructural analysis revealed mitochondrial swelling and lipid droplet accumulation, which was accompanied by decreased intracellular ATP levels, suggesting impaired cellular bioenergetics. Integrated omics identified the PPARα/CPT1A-mediated fatty acid oxidation (FAO) axis as the primary metabolic target. Western blotting confirmed that SMME downregulated PPARα and CPT1A while activating intrinsic apoptosis. Subsequent pharmacological activation of PPARα successfully restored target protein expression and reversed SMME-induced cytotoxicity. SMME exerts significant antitumor effects against TNBC in vitro and in vivo. Multi-omics profiling and targeted validation suggest that the suppression of the PPARα/CPT1A-associated FAO program contributes to energy stress, lipid remodeling, and apoptosis, supporting mitochondrial lipid metabolism as a potential therapeutic target in TNBC.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68128-y.title: Effects of particle gradation and vibration intensity on the pore water pressure response of sandy mine waste*
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68128-y.abstract: Abstract Rainfall infiltration and heavy mine-truck traffic can promote pore-pressure build-up and reduce waste-dump stability. Shaking-table tests of four river-sand/quartz-sand mixtures examined the effects of gradation and vibration intensity on the pore water pressure response of sandy mine waste specimens prepared by underwater deposition. Coupled SEEP/W-QUAKE/W-SLOPE/W analyses evaluated engineering-scale response, and SLOPE/W calculated factors of safety using the Morgenstern-Price method. During the first vibration, pore pressure generally increased with acceleration. During the second and third vibrations, peak response varied non-monotonically as prior loading altered density and compressible pore space. Several high-acceleration cases reached or approached the common pore-pressure reference level used for cross-condition comparison. Relatively uniformly graded LS1 (100% quartz sand) was more sensitive to pore-pressure build-up, whereas LS3 (25% quartz sand and 75% river sand), with a relatively broader particle-size distribution than LS1, tended to stabilize during later stages. In the LS3-equivalent numerical case, traffic-induced loading concentrated excess pore pressure near the crest platform, slope shoulder, and shallow slope surface under the prescribed water-table and infiltration conditions. Increasing the peak load from 20 kPa to 100 kPa expanded the high-pore-pressure zone and reduced the minimum factor of safety from 1.30 to 1.25 (3.54%). These results indicate that rainy-season stability assessments should consider both sandy-waste gradation and traffic-load intensity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67523-9.title: Effects of esmolol on stress and inflammatory responses during endoscopic sinus surgery among patients with nasal polyps: a randomized controlled trial
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67523-9.abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to explore the effects of esmolol on stress and inflammatory responses during endoscopic sinus surgery among patients with nasal polyps. Eighty patients with nasal polyps who underwent endoscopic sinus surgery under general anesthesia were randomly divided into a control group (Group C, given normal saline during general anesthesia induction and maintenance) and an esmolol group (Group E, given esmolol during anesthesia induction and maintenance). Blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) were lower in Group E than in Group C at T1–T5 ( P < 0.01). The cortisol (CORT) and glucose (GLU) levels at T3 and T4 did not significantly differ between Group C and Group E ( P > 0.05). The levels of interleukins (IL-1β, IL-8, and IL-10) in Group E at T3 and T4 were lower than those in Group C ( P < 0.01). Blood loss and the dosages of propofol and remifentanil were lower in Group E than in Group C ( P < 0.01). The recovery time of patients in Group E was shorter than that in Group C ( P < 0.01). Esmolol was associated with lower cardiovascular parameters and inflammatory marker levels but had a relatively small effect on the endocrine stress response of patients with nasal polyps during nasal endoscopic surgery. Trial registration: This study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (registration number: ChiCTR2400095027; date of registration: December 31, 2024).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67925-9.title: Discovery of novel protein biomarkers for the detection of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome phenotype A
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67925-9.abstract: Abstract Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a prevalent endocrine condition affecting women of reproductive age. PMOS is underrecognized/underdiagnosed and associated with secondary comorbidities that may result from delayed diagnosis/management. Novel biomarkers are needed to improve timely diagnosis. This retrospective, case-control study used biobanked serum samples from women with PMOS phenotype A ( n = 51) and healthy controls ( n = 37). We performed protein biomarker discovery using Olink Proximity Extension Assay and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) analysis. We conducted an overrepresentation pathway analysis against Reactome. We investigated 1,196 protein biomarkers and conducted a pathway analysis using the 145 top-performing biomarkers (AUC > 0.750). Top 10 performing biomarkers (AUC ≥ 0.961) were linked to relevant biological pathways, including immune system regulation (serum amyloid A4 and leukotriene A4 hydrolase), lipid, carbohydrate, and protein metabolism (fibroblast growth factor binding protein 1, carboxylesterase 2, inositol polyphosphate-1-phosphatase, inositol polyphosphate-1-phosphatase like, pro-glucagon, and leptin), nervous system development (semaphorin 4C and plexin B1), and cellular response (peroxiredoxin 1). These pathways/sub-pathways may contribute to PMOS pathophysiology and related comorbidities (insulin resistance, obesity, and fatty liver disease). We discovered novel circulating protein biomarkers that distinguish women with PMOS phenotype A from healthy controls, supporting diagnosis and enabling timely intervention/appropriate management.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69147-5.title: The predictors of the triglyceride-glucose index in subjects with newly diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69147-5.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), metabolic syndrome, and insulin resistance (IR) have reciprocal relationships. Assessing IR is important but challenging in clinical practice. The triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) represents a simple marker of IR that can provide significant information on the metabolic status of patients with OSA. This study aimed to determine which parameters influence TyG in a population suspected of having OSA and to assess its association with endothelial function. We examined 131 consecutive individuals without a history of chronic diseases (except obesity) suspected of having OSA. Anthropometric parameters were measured, body mass index (BMI) was calculated, and fasting glucose and lipid profiles were assessed. Endothelial function was assessed using peripheral arterial tonometry and the reactive hyperemia index (RHI) was calculated. All participants underwent overnight polysomnography. Significant correlations were found between TyG and various anthropometric parameters (neck circumference, waist circumference, and BMI) and selected sleep parameters (arousal index, respiratory disturbance index, and oxygen desaturation index). No significant correlation with RHI was found. TyG was significantly higher in men than women (8.9 ± 0.6 vs. 8.6 ± 0.6, p = 0.010). In multivariate analysis, waist circumference (β = 0.417, p < 0.001) and male sex (β = 0.169, p = 0.034) were the only independent predictors of TyG. These findings suggest that TyG primarily reflects metabolic risk factors rather than OSA severity per se, and further studies are warranted to clarify its clinical utility in this population.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66274-x.title: Identification of reference genes for real-time quantitative PCR in different development stage in chili pepper fruits(Capsicum annuum and Capsicum chinense)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66274-x.abstract: Abstract The selection of appropriate reference genes is a fundamental prerequisite for reliable gene expression analysis using real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). To date, no systematic study has identified reference genes for normalizing RT-qPCR data in pepper fruits across different developmental stages. In this study, we evaluated the expression stability of seven commonly used internal control genes and nine additional candidates derived from available transcriptomic datasets in two widely cultivated chili pepper species (Capsicum annuum and Capsicum chinense) at various fruit developmental stages. The expression stability of the 16 candidate genes was assessed using four established algorithms: NormFinder, ΔCt, BestKeeper, and GeNorm. Our results demonstrated that CT8 and EIF were the most stably expressed genes during fruit development in Capsicum annuum ‘TJ’ and Capsicum chinense ‘7054’, respectively. This study provides a foundation for accurate normalization of RT-qPCR analyses in pepper fruits at different developmental stages and will help ensure the reliability of subsequent gene expression studies in these species.
