doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68673-6.title: A hybrid BiLSTM-MPC predictive control strategy for energy and thermal management of electric vehicles with real-time validation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68673-6.abstract: Energy management efficiency in battery electric vehicles (xEVs) is vital for enhancing their driving performance, battery safety, and energy management efficiency. Traditional controllers, such as PID, Fuzzy logic, ANN, and traditional Model Predictive Control (MPC), have provided an acceptable performance level. However, these methods do not provide enough capacity for tackling drive cycle dynamics, future uncertainty, and heat effects, resulting in higher tracking errors and lower SoC preservation. For solving this problem, a predictive intelligent control scheme combining BiLSTM-based future speed prediction along with constrained MPC optimization of control input was proposed for energy management in xEVs. Using the BiLSTM model, future speed trajectory over the prediction horizon is predicted, whereas the MPC method minimizes tracking error, energy expenditure, deviation of the battery temperature from its optimal level, and the control effort. The proposed method was evaluated under various drive cycles, such as UDDS, WLTP, HWFET, and MIDC, with simulations performed on MATLAB/Simulink, as well as on OPAL-RT OP4512 hardware-in-the-loop validation platform. As a result, the proposed controller provided the lowest RMSE value of 1.48 km/h, highest final SoC of 85.9%, regenerative energy recovery of 210 Wh, and maximum battery temperature of 42.1 °C.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68183-5.title: Risk factor analysis and predictive model construction and evaluation of fractional uric acid excretion in Chinese inpatients with type 2 diabetes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68183-5.abstract: Abstract Background and Aims: Fractional excretion of uric acid (FEUA) is currently acknowledged as a new risk factor of nephropathy. Precise measurement of FEUA requires withdraw medication during the washout time and 24h urine sample collecting, not always convenient, fostering construction of predictive models. No existing model could portrait FEUA. Our aim is to develop and evaluate a model which could predict FEUA based on several easily available factors. Methods : 2301 patients hospitalized in the Department of Endocrinology, Peking University People’s Hospital were chose. 1510 cases enrolled during 2018–2024 were used to construct predictive models using linear regression and to perform internal validation. 791 cases enrolled in 2017 and 2025 were used as an external validation. Results : Sex, SUA, SCr, and FPG closely related with FEUA in internal dataset. The predictive formula was: Ln (FEUA) = 1.9408 + 0.1462*gender (male=1female = 2) − 0.0031*SUA(µmol/L) + 0.0112*SCr(µmol/L) + 0.0068*FPG (mmol/L) Predicted FEUA = Exp(Ln(FEUA))*1.0265; 1.0265 was the Duan’s smearing factor. Root mean squared errors (RMSE) between the observed and predicted FEUA was 1.690%. Spearman correlation coefficient was 0.7870 ( P < 0.001). For predicting elevated FEUA (≥ 11%), the overall accuracy was 94.70%; ROC was 0.9552(95%CI: 0.9413 ~ 0.9691). Youden index (0.7814) at the cut-point (8.0257%) of FEUA was identified with a high sensitivity (0.9541) and specificity (0.8273). RMSE for 1-fold, 5-fold, 10-fold and leave-one-out cross-validation were 1.6898, 1.7087 ± 0.1716, 1.6964 ± 0.2761, and 1.7081, respectively. ROC values in subgroups of internal dataset were all higher than 0.949. In external dataset validation, Spearman correlation coefficient between observed and predicted FEUA was 0.7451( P < 0.001), ROC for elevated FEUA was 0.8946 (95% CI: 0.8545 ~ 0.9347). A stability of all indices was identified for subgroups of external dataset. Conclusion : Our study identified an effective and practical FEUA predictive model in T2DM inpatients using linear regression with four common indexes: sex, SUA, SCr, FPG.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68709-x.title: Bridge-RF-DETR: an edge-guided transformer framework for multi-type bridge surface damage detection
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68709-x.abstract: Abstract Bridge surface damage detection is essential for intelligent infrastructure monitoring, yet remains challenging due to large-scale variations, weak boundaries, complex backgrounds, and imbalanced damage categories. This study develops Bridge-RF-DETR, a task-oriented extension of RF-DETR for multi-type bridge surface damage detection. The framework introduces three targeted modifications. First, a progressive Asymptotic Feature Pyramid Network (AFPN) is integrated to improve multi-scale feature representation for damages of different sizes. Second, an Edge Branch (EB) and an Edge Guidance Module (EGM) are used to incorporate boundary cues for weak-texture and slender damage patterns such as cracks and leakage. Third, a class-balanced sampling strategy is adopted to reduce the effect of category imbalance. Experiments on a public bridge damage dataset show that Bridge-RF-DETR achieves an overall F 1 -score of 0.871 and mAP@0.5 of 0.862, providing moderate but consistent improvements over RF-DETR and other representative detectors. Alternative-component comparison, per-class analysis, three-seed variability analysis, and evaluation on DACL10K provide additional evidence for the observed performance trends. These results indicate that Bridge-RF-DETR provides a practical visual detection pipeline for bridge surface damage inspection, while broader validation under diverse field conditions remains necessary.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61605-4.title: Learning precise segmentation of neurofibrillary tangles from rapid manual point annotations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61605-4.abstract: Abstract Accumulation of abnormal tau protein into neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) is a pathologic hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD). Accurate detection of NFTs in tissue samples can reveal relationships with clinical, demographic, and genetic features through deep phenotyping. However, expert manual analysis is time-consuming, subject to observer variability, and cannot handle the data amounts generated by modern imaging. We present a scalable, open-source, deep-learning approach to quantify NFT burden in digital whole slide images (WSIs) of post-mortem human brain tissue. To achieve this, we developed a method to generate detailed NFT boundaries directly from single-point-per-NFT annotations. We then trained a semantic segmentation model on 45 annotated 2400 μm by 1200 μm regions of interest (ROIs) selected from 15 unique temporal cortex WSIs of AD cases from three institutions (University of California (UC)-Davis, UC-San Diego, and Columbia University). Segmenting NFTs at the single-pixel level, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic of 0.832 and an F1 of 0.527 (196-fold over random) on a held-out test set of 664 NFTs from 20 ROIs (7 WSIs). We compared this to deep object detection, which achieved comparable but coarser-grained performance that was 60% faster. The segmentation and object detection models correlated well with expert semi-quantitative scores at the whole-slide level (Spearman’s rho ρ = 0.654 ( p = 6.50e-5) and ρ = 0.513 ( p = 3.18e-3), respectively). We openly release this multi-institution deep-learning pipeline to provide detailed NFT spatial distribution and morphology analysis capability at a scale otherwise infeasible by manual assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68652-x.title: Exploring visual impairment as a risk factor for developing frailty in older adults: a cohort study from Thailand
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68652-x.abstract: Visual impairment (VI) and frailty often coexist in older adults, leading to an increased risk of adverse health outcomes. However, evidence based on objective measurements among adults living in the community remains limited. This study explored the association between VI and frailty progression among older adults. A retrospective cohort study was conducted among people 60 years and older who participated in health screenings at the Primary Care Unit (PCU) at Siriraj Hospital, Thailand between January 2020 and October 2023 and had their baseline assessment performed. VI was defined as having visual acuity worse than 6/12 in the better eye, while frailty status was assessed using the Thai version of the Frail scale. Follow-up data were collected in 2024 through structured telephone interviews. Multivariate ordinal logistic regression was used to examine the association between VI and frailty transition. Among 400 participants (median age 70 years; 76% female), those with VI had significantly higher odds of frailty progression compared with those without VI (adjusted OR 2.98, 95% confidence interval 1.97–4.52; p < 0.001). Participants with VI reported lower quality of life, with slightly higher rates of falls and hospitalizations. These findings indicate that VI independently predicts frailty progression. Early screening and timely ophthalmologic intervention may help delay frailty development and improve health outcomes in older adults.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69057-6.title: Experimental and theoretical study on the thermal conductivity of PA6/POE/AlN nanocomposites prepared by in-situ and melt polymerization methods
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69057-6.abstract: Polyamide 6/polyolefin elastomer (PA6/POE) nanocomposites containing \(\:5-20\:\text{wt}{\%}\) aluminium nitride (AlN) were prepared by two routes, in-situ anionic ring-opening polymerisation of ε-caprolactam and conventional melt compounding, in order to separate the effect of the processing route on filler dispersion, phase morphology and heat transport. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy showed that the in-situ route extends the POE phase into stable fibrils, whereas melt compounding leaves it as discrete droplets; image analysis of the filler-free references gives a median equivalent domain diameter of 2.8 μm for the in-situ blend against 3.5 μm for the melt-compounded blend. Oscillatory rheometry confirmed the difference: only the samples in which AlN is localised at the PA6/POE interface develop a low-frequency plateau in the storage modulus and a solid-like response. Thermal conductivity increased monotonically up to 15 \(\:\text{wt}{\%}\) AlN, reaching a maximum of 3.06 \(\:\text{W} \cdot {\text{m}}^{-1} \cdot {\text{K}}^{-1}\) for the in-situ material, seven times the value of the unfilled blend and 7% above the melt-compounded equivalent, and then fell to 1.36 W·m − 1 ·K − 1 at 20 \(\:\text{wt}{\%}\) as the thermal diffusivity collapsed. Model analysis was carried out over the complete composition range. Between 0 and 15 \(\:\text{wt}{\%}\) the Agari model describes the data well (R 2 = 0.95 in the logarithmic space in which it was fitted, 0.89 on a linear scale), whereas the Nielsen and Bruggeman models underestimate the measured conductivity roughly fivefold and return negative coefficients of determination. Across the full 0-20 \(\:\text{wt}{\%}\) range the Agari value falls to R 2 = 0.51, because every model considered increases monotonically with filler content and none can reproduce the reversal above 15 \(\:\text{wt}{\%}\) . That structural limitation, rather than scatter in the data, is what the full-range statistics record. Interfacial filler localisation and fibrillar networking are therefore confirmed as a workable route to thermally conductive polyamide compounds, with 15 \(\:\text{wt}{\%}\) AlN identified as the practical optimum rather than the highest loading examined.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68133-1.title: Workflow evaluation of a commercial deep learning-based image analysis tool for the quantification of angiogenesis in vivo
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68133-1.abstract: Abstract Angiogenesis plays a crucial role in tumor development as well as in wound healing and integration of biomaterials. However, quantification of complex vascular networks across different in vivo models is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to human error. Deep learning-based analysis (DLBA) appears to be a more efficient and reproducible method for vascular quantification . Yet, studies directly comparing its performance with human assessment remain limited. IKOSA CAM is a commercially available tool built for analysis of vascular networks. Here we evaluated IKOSA CAM against manual vessel tracing across three different angiogenesis models. Images obtained from three different in vivo angiogenesis models, the chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) assay, the rodent retina, and the dorsal skinfold chamber (DSC), were analyzed. The vascular network was analyzed using both manual tracing and the commercial deep learning-based image analysis tool IKOSA CAM. In addition, tracing results were reevaluated by human raters and the total workflow duration was assessed. Deep learning-based image analysis proved to be a time-efficient method for tracing and quantifying vascular networks. The level of agreement with manual human tracing varied among image types. The highest agreement between the two methods was observed for the CAM assay. The greatest differences occurred in the tracing of DSC branching points, as indicated by a downward trend in the Bland-Altman plots. Repeated analyses with the DLBA produced identical results for all tested angiogenesis models, confirming excellent reproducibility. Standardized vascular quantification remains a major challenge in experimental angiogenesis research. In this workflow validation study, the evaluated DLBA provided reproducible and time-efficient vessel quantification, particularly for the CAM assay, while showing limitations in the analysis of retinal and DSC images. Overall, DLBA represents a promising approach for standardized vascular analysis and may facilitate reproducible, high-throughput image quantification. Nevertheless, further validation using larger and more heterogeneous datasets is warranted.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67844-9.title: A human centered framework for translating machine learning diagnostic evidence into clinical practice guidelines
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67844-9.abstract: Abstract The continuous evolution of medicine necessitates the adoption of machine learning (ML) methods to strengthen global health systems. As an ethical, non-invasive, and cost-effective complement to randomized controlled trials (RCTs), ML holds great promise for generating clinical insights. However, its integration into practice remains severely limited, largely due to the absence of standardized frameworks that align ML research with clinical practice guidelines (CPGs). To address this gap, we developed the Human-Centered Medical Machine Learning (HCMML) protocol—a candidate framework for translating ML-derived diagnostic evidence into CPGs. The framework was built upon five systematic reviews encompassing more than 830 original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and CPGs, followed by a two-round Delphi consensus process and an expert-informed assessment. Across these reviews, no evidence was found that ML-based diagnostic models had been incorporated into the CPGs examined. The synthesis identified eight major adoption barriers and ten expert-endorsed complementary principles organized into three dimensions: Clinical Trust, Implementation Rigor, and Knowledge Evolution. These were subsequently mapped through a structured questionnaire, forming the basis of the proposed protocol. The questionnaire completed by 44 international domain experts provided preliminary support for the framework’s clarity, relevance, and perceived feasibility. The protocol also introduces three key methodological innovations: decoupling model design from clinical evaluation, promoting multidisciplinary collaboration throughout the translational pathway, and shifting the focus of systematic review from computational performance toward real-world clinical utility. Although developed using ML-based diagnostic studies, the framework is built on algorithm-independent design principles suggesting conceptual extensibility to broader intelligent methods—including deep learning and other AI paradigms—though this requires future investigation. By bridging the terminological and methodological gap between computational innovation and clinical practice, HCMML offers a systematic pathway for the responsible adoption of AI-based diagnostic systems in high-stakes medical settings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68680-7.title: Biopriming with liquid biofertilizers enhances productivity, seed quality, soil health, and resource use efficiency in soybean under semi-arid conditions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68680-7.abstract: Abstract Climate change and excessive dependence on the chemical fertilizers have threatened soil fertility, crop productivity and environmental sustainability through soil degradation and desertification. Use of liquid bio-fertilizers are one of the effective ways of improving the soil fertility and nutrient availability. Despite increasing use of liquid fertilizers, comparative information on effective microorganisms and other microbial inoculants with respect to nutrient use efficiency, energy balance and carbon budget in soybean is limited. To enumerate the role of biofertilizer on the soybean yield, seed quality, soil health, energy-carbon dynamics, a two-year field study was conducted during the kharif season of 2024 and 2025 using randomized block design comprising nine seed biopriming treatments with different liquid biofertilizers tested under three replications. The growth, yield and soil biological properties were recorded at different crop growth stages following standard procedures whereas, the carbon and energy inputs and output were calculated by multiplying the inputs and outputs with respective standard coefficients. The result revealed that, seed bio-priming with liquid effective micro-organisms (S 2 ) recorded significantly higher leaf area (2254.58 cm 2 plant −1 ), SPAD values (55.9) and dry matter accumulation (18.49 g plant −1 ) at 60 days after sowing (DAS). Similarly, S 2 recorded significantly higher number of pods plant −1 (28.08%), seed yield (8.3%) and haulm yield (14.6%) over 100% recommended nutrient rate (S 1 ). Seed biopriming with biofertilizers enhanced the soil biological activity with significantly higher microbial population and dehydrogenase activity at S 2 . The comparative climatic advantage of seed biopriming with liquid biofertilizers was observed in all treated plants, among which higher eco efficiency (57.74), carbon efficiency (14.58), net energy (71,213 MJ kg −1 ), energy profitability (0.17) and lower the GHG intensity (0.43) was observed at S 2 . Seed biopriming with liquid biofertilizers sustainably enhanced the soybean productivity with improved soil health while lowering the estimated GHG intensity. The present findings display the potential of liquid biofertilizer based seed priming as a sustainable strategy for enhancing soybean productivity while improving the resource use efficiency and support climate smart practices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69190-2.title: Performance evaluation of orange-fleshed sweet potato varieties at different intra-row spacing in North–West areas of Amhara regional state, Ethiopia
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69190-2.abstract: Orange fleshed sweet potato (OFSP) is one of the root crops that significantly contribute to ensuring food and nutrition security across most areas in Ethiopia. Its production remained very low (8 t ha − 1 ) as compared to the world average of about 14.8 t ha − 1 which is mainly attributed to the use of low-yielding variety including inappropriate intra-row spacing. Therefore, an experiment was conducted to determine the effect of varieties and intra-row spacing on the yield and yield-related traits of released OFSP varieties. It was conducted using four released OFSP varieties ( Alamura , Dilla , Kulfo and Birtukane ) and three levels of intra-row spacing (20, 30 and 40 cm) in factorial combinations. This field experiment was designed in randomized Complete Blocks with three replications in North–West areas of Amhara regional state, Ethiopia during the 2021 rainy season. The results obtained showed that the interaction effect of varieties and intra-row spacing had significant effect on days to physiological maturity, vine length, number of storage roots per plant, storage root length, storage root diameter, above-ground fresh weight, storage root weight, and storage root yield. However, vine survival rate was significantly affected by the main effects of varieties and intra-row spacing, but not by their interaction. Treatment combination of Birtukane variety with 30 cm intra row spacing gave the highest storage root yield of 22.8 t ha − 1 . Based on the cost-benefit analysis, this treatment also gave the highest net benefit of 397,855.3 ETB ha⁻¹ with an acceptable marginal rate of return (MRR) of 408.4%.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68676-3.title: Cerium-based organic framework with aliphatic ligand as an excellent catalyst in the green synthesis of polysubstituted 1,8-naphthyridines
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68676-3.abstract: A novel cerium-based aliphatic Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) was hydrothermally synthesized from ceric ammonium nitrate (CAN) and hexamethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (HDTA). This highly crystalline MOF, often forming hollow tubes, and exhibits thermal stability up to 300 °C along with exceptional structural integrity. This catalyst facilitated the efficient green synthesis of polysubstituted 1,8-naphthyridines from 2,6-diaminopyridine, active methylene sources (malononitrile or ethyl cyanoacetate), and aromatic aldehydes. This condensation, performed in ethanol under green conditions, yielded high product yields across a broad range of functional groups. Critically, the catalyst demonstrated outstanding recyclability, retaining its catalytic performance over five consecutive cycles with no significant activity loss. This positions it as a highly promising heterogeneous and sustainable catalyst for environmentally benign chemical transformations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69438-x.title: Comparative study of Ag-Au NPs and Ag-Au@SiO2 nanostructures synthesized by conventional chemical and plant-mediated chemical reduction routes: activity-stability relationships
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69438-x.abstract: Bimetallic Ag-Au nanostructures exhibit tunable surface and electronic properties, making them versatile platforms for functional nanomaterial design. In this study, Ag-Au nanoparticles synthesized by conventional chemical reduction and a plant-mediated chemical reduction route were systematically compared with their silica-coated counterparts (Ag-Au@SiO 2 ) to examine how synthesis strategy and surface modification influence electrochemical response, surface accessibility, and functional stability. Silica encapsulation was employed as a model surface modification approach to regulate interfacial properties while maintaining the overall nanostructure. Comprehensive characterization using UV-Vis spectroscopy, FT-IR, TEM, DLS, and zeta potential analysis was combined with electrochemical techniques (CV, DPV, and CA) to probe surface-mediated redox behavior and comparative electrochemical response. Catalytic reduction of 4-nitrophenol and methylene blue was applied as a well-established model reaction to assess surface accessibility and functional stability rather than application-specific catalytic performance. Uncoated Ag-Au nanoparticles showed faster apparent reaction kinetics, whereas silica-coated nanostructures exhibited a characteristic trade-off between apparent reaction kinetics and durability, which may be related to differences in surface accessibility and transport-related effects. Notably, chemically synthesized Ag-Au@SiO 2 nanostructures retained apparent catalytic performance after four weeks of ambient storage, despite a measurable decrease in apparent rate constants, while uncoated nanoparticles showed a more pronounced decline in apparent catalytic performance. Electrochemical analyses revealed synthesis-dependent differences in the comparative electrochemical response following silica encapsulation, particularly in systems obtained by plant-mediated chemical reduction. This work identifies qualitative relationships between synthesis route, surface modification, and electrochemical response under identical experimental conditions. By employing model reactions as probes of surface functionality, the study provides a reproducible framework for evaluating durability and performance in surface-engineered nanomaterials.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66465-6.title: Ecological associations of environmental and behavioral factors with provincial urinary system mortality trajectories in Türkiye
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66465-6.abstract: To characterize province-level mortality trajectories for bladder cancer, prostate cancer, and renal failure in Turkiye and to explore ecological associations between mortality-profile membership and environmental, meteorological, and behavioral markers. Annual crude province-level mortality rates for 81 provinces from 2010 through 2019 were modeled using group-based trajectory analysis in SAS PROC TRAJ. For each outcome, province-level profile membership was related to 33 markers using separate univariable proportional-odds models, with false-discovery-rate control across marker-specific tests. The analyses were ecological and exploratory. Three mortality profiles were identified for each outcome. For bladder cancer, higher-profile membership showed positive ecological associations with median air pressure, ever-alcohol-use prevalence, ever-smoking prevalence, and median humidity, whereas PM10 and multiple meteorological-variability measures showed inverse associations. Prostate-cancer profiles showed positive associations with ever-alcohol-use prevalence, ever-smoking prevalence, and median humidity; household second-hand smoke exposure, PM10, and several variability measures showed inverse associations. For renal failure, median air pressure, ever-alcohol-use prevalence, ever-smoking prevalence, and median humidity showed positive associations, whereas PM10 and several variability measures showed inverse associations. Estimates came from separate univariable models and should not be interpreted as independent or individual-level effects. The study identified heterogeneous ten-year provincial mortality profiles and several exploratory ecological associations. Because the rates were crude, exposures were summarized concurrently with the mortality period, and major demographic, socioeconomic, healthcare, and diagnostic factors were unavailable, the findings do not establish causality or biological protection. They are most appropriately used to generate hypotheses and to guide better-adjusted surveillance and longitudinal studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66596-w.title: Unveiling toxicological, microanatomical and in-silico assessment of beta-carboline alkaloids as potential acaricide against Haemaphysalis darjeeling ticks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66596-w.abstract: Beta-carboline alkaloids have been reported to show insecticidal and acaricidal activities. In the present study, Haemaphysalis darjeeling ticks were exposed to beta-carboline alkaloids, Harmaline, Harmalol, Harmine and Harmane, at concentrations of 10, 20, 30, and 40 mg/ml for 6, 12, 18, and 24 h to evaluate their potential acaricidal effect and mode of action. Although all four alkaloids induced substantial mortality in both larvae and adults, Harmaline followed by Harmalol showed a tendency to achieve higher toxicity compared to Harmine and Harmane with prolonged exposure times. Microanatomical study further revealed severe body surface damage in Harmaline and Harmalol-exposed adults. Although MM/GBSA analysis indicates slightly stronger binding for Harmalol with Chitin Synthase, binding energy alone does not fully explain inhibitory potential. Molecular Dynamics (MD) results show that Harmaline maintains more stable interactions, lower residue fluctuations, and better structural compactness within the binding pocket. Together with the experimental toxicity, microanatomical damages and MD results suggest that Harmaline is more effective in inhibiting chitin biosynthesis. This study suggests that all the beta-carboline compounds, especially Harmaline, showed potential acaricidal efficacy targeting Chitin Synthase, and thus can be used as potential alternatives and eco-friendly acaricides to eradicate tick infestation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66548-4.title: An ultra steep slope and low voltage split gate oxide dual gate vertical TFET based multi gas sensor
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66548-4.abstract: Abstract This work presents an ultra steep slope and low voltage split gate oxide dual gate vertical TFET (USS-LV-SGO-VTFET) based multi gas sensor for the detection of ammonia (NH 3 ), oxygen (O 2 ), and hydrogen (H 2 ) with different work-function variations of 0–200 meV at $$V_{DS}=1$$ V and $$V_{GS}=1.5$$ V. The vertical architecture employs a dual-gate configuration to achieve strong electrostatic control and effective modulation of band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) under gas-induced gate work-function variations. The sensing mechanism is governed by gas adsorption induced work function shifts in the range of 50–200 meV, which directly modulate the tunneling window at the source–channel(S-C) junction. The optimized device exhibits pronounced variations in transfer characteristics with increasing work function ( $$\Delta WF$$ ), confirming a significant improvement in sensitivity. Cobalt (Co), Silver (Ag), and Palladium (Pd), with work functions of 4.7 eV, 5.0 eV, and 5.1 eV, respectively, are employed as catalytic gate materials for selective NH 3 , O 2 , and H 2 detection. The USS-LV-SGO-VTFET gas sensor has an ultra-low OFF current around $$10^{-18}$$ A/ $$\mu$$ m and a sharp subthreshold swing of 17.5 mV/dec. It achieves ON current sensitivities of 0.594 for NH 3 , 0.933 for O 2 , and 0.987 for H 2 with a work-function variation of 200 meV. The dual-gate vertical structure greatly enhances tunneling barrier modulation during gas exposure, which increases BTBT probability and improves ON-state current and energy-band analysis. These findings indicate that the USS-LV-SGO-VTFET design offers a low-power, efficient platform for next-generation gas sensing applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66203-y.title: Personal values as antecedents of technostress and technology-related affective well-being during a simulated space mission
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66203-y.abstract: Abstract Space missions and analog space habitats are highly technology-dependent environments, where interactions with complex systems can elicit both stress and positive affective experiences. Despite increasing recognition of the role of psychological adaptation in isolated, confined, and extreme environments (ICE), little is known about how personal values shape astronauts’ and analog astronauts’ (i.e., participating in ground research on Earth) technology perception. Hence, in this study, we examined the associations between personal values, technostress, and technology-related affective well-being during two 14-day simulated space missions at the LunAres Research Station in Poland. Nine participants repeatedly completed the Technology-Related Affective Well-Being Scale and the Technostress Scale during the mission. They assessed their personal values before the mission through the Revised Portrait Values Questionnaire (PVQ-RR). Correlational and multilevel analyses revealed complex patterns of associations. Values such as Self-direction and Humility were negatively associated with technology-related affective well-being, while Conformity, Face, and Personal security predicted higher technostress. Conversely, Tradition was linked to lower technostress and higher affective well-being. Multilevel modeling provided preliminary evidence that Personal security and Universalism-societal concern significantly predicted elevated technostress across the mission. The findings suggest that personal values are significant to analog astronauts’ technology experience during a simulated space mission, as they may help or hinder human-technology interaction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68663-8.title: Larger females do not achieve higher lifetime fecundity in an extremely size-dimorphic spider
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68663-8.abstract: Female body size is often linked positively to clutch fecundity because size limits the number of eggs or offspring produced per clutch. Yet larger clutches may not increase lifetime reproductive success if offset by fewer reproductive events, shorter lifespan, reduced offspring survival, or mating-rate constraints. We tested this in the African hermit spider, Nephilingis cruentata , an extremely size-dimorphic species in which mating plugs restrict females to one or two lifetime copulations. Larger females produced heavier clutches, i.e., egg-sacs, indicating greater per-clutch fecundity, but produced fewer egg-sacs and had longer inter-egg-sac intervals. Consequently, total egg-sac mass, used as a lifetime fecundity proxy, did not increase with female size. In a standardised offspring sample, larger maternal size did not increase the probability that hatchlings reached sexual maturity. Females often produced several viable egg-sacs followed by a terminal phase of non-viable egg-sacs; viability declined with time since mating. This continued oviposition after viable reproduction shows that females retained the capacity to produce egg-sacs and is consistent with fertilisation limitation. However, the data do not distinguish fertilisation failure from sperm deterioration, oocyte or reproductive-tract ageing or embryo failure. Thus, in the African hermit spider with a strongly restricted mating system and reared under laboratory conditions, female body size predicts per-clutch but not lifetime fecundity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65813-w.title: Dynamic spectrum allocation in 6G MIMO systems using adaptive deep multiagent reinforcement learning with coordinate attention
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65813-w.abstract: Abstract The Millimeter-wave massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) is a core mechanism for the Sixth-Generation (6G) wireless communication networks. By including numerous antennas in the compact model of advanced smartphones, the MIMO enhances the network capacity and the Spectral Efficiency (SE). The growth of 6G technology is significant for the future and provided evolutionary and revolutionary solutions. The resource allocation in the MIMO-based wireless networks is selected for various users, aiming to optimize the network resource distribution. But the high increase in the antennas and users poses complexities for the resource allocation and interference suppression for the MIMO systems. In this research, an advanced Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based approach is proposed for efficient dynamic spectrum allocation in 6G MIMO systems. To perform spectrum allocation in 6G MIMO systems, an Adaptive Deep Multiagent Reinforcement Learning with Co-ordinate Attention (ADMRL-CA) model is developed. The DMRL mechanism is capable of handling varying traffic and channel conditions. The incorporation of the CA mechanism enhances the policy learning process for accurate spectrum allocation. The parameters of the ADMRL-CA are fine-tuned using the Flying workers phase Modified Termite Queen Algorithm (FMTQA). Finally, the model performance is analyzed with various existing models. The SE of the recommended FMTQA-ADMRL-CA is increased by 4.44% of DRL, 6.66% of SAC, 2.77% of DDPG and 10.88% of DMRL-CA when system uses as 32 nd batch size. Hence, it is guaranteed that the recommended FMTQA-ADMRL-CA can allocate the spectrum efficiently and robustly in 6G MIMO systems than the existing methods.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67918-8.title: Identification of equivalent GBM meso-parameters using GA-BP and crack fractal dimension
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67918-8.abstract: Aiming at the low efficiency of traditional trial-and-error parameter assignment in discrete element modeling and the lack of quantitative constraints on crack morphology, this paper proposes a GA-BP-based equivalent meso-parameter identification method that incorporates crack fractal dimension within a Grain-Based Model (GBM) framework. Within the GBM framework, the parallel bond (PB) and smooth joint (SJ) models were integrated to construct a particle system with intra- and inter-granular characteristics. Sensitivity analysis was employed to screen key mesoscopic parameters, and fractal dimension was introduced to quantitatively characterize crack morphology. Furthermore, a GA-BP neural network was developed to map selected macroscopic response indicators and crack fractal dimension to equivalent mesoscopic parameter sets within prescribed parameter ranges. Genetic algorithm was used to optimize initial weights, while ReLU activation function and dynamic strategies were adopted to enhance prediction performance. The results showed that, across five repeated randomized evaluations with 60 independent test records per run, the mean parameter-wise R² values ranged from 0.9563 to 0.9989 and the mean MAPE values ranged from 0.6809% to 9.1012%. Compared with conventional BP, GA-BP increased the aggregate mean R² from 0.9834 to 0.9899 and reduced RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by 35.07%, 41.02%, and 16.44%, respectively. Cross-lithology validation further showed good agreement between simulated and experimental mechanical responses and crack morphology. Equifinality analysis confirmed that similar response vectors may correspond to different mesoscopic parameter combinations; therefore, the identified parameters should be interpreted as model-dependent equivalent solutions within the adopted GBM framework rather than unique physical constants.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66870-x.title: Counting fluorescent emitters with a single photon avalanche diode array
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66870-x.abstract: For decades, the photon counting histogram (PCH) was used as the sole method to quantify fluorophore numbers in a diffraction-limited focal volume. This technique combines spatial excitation profiles, and the distribution of photon counts to register the photon emission statistics of individual fluorophores. However, this approach has not yet been transferred to widefield fluorescent imaging due to the lack of fast and single photon sensitive camera sensors which can capture the photon emission statistics of a single fluorophore. Here, we explore avenues towards quantitative analysis of the active fluorophore number by leveraging recent advancements in single photon avalanche diode (SPAD) array technology. Binary exposures of a SPAD array can be synchronized with picosecond laser pulses to measure the PCH in a widefield setting. Then, by modeling the statistical relationship between the active fluorophore number and the PCH in a region of interest following a laser pulse, we can perform Bayesian inference of this number. The model is demonstrated experimentally by counting quantum dots and various numbers of fluorescent dye molecules bound to DNA origamis. We find that this method has several important applications in widefield microscopy, including enhanced localization microscopy and constrained fitting of multiple unresolvable fluorescent emitters.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67475-0.title: A novel methodology for predictive modeling of patient outcomes using multi-modal transformer networks and SHAP models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67475-0.abstract: Abstract Precision medicine requires predictive models that can exploit genomic, clinical, imaging and continuously monitored physiological data at the same time, yet most existing models operate on a single modality and behave as black boxes. This paper proposes the Integrated Multi-Modal Contextual Network (IMCN), a predictive modelling framework that combines multi-modal transformer networks for cross-modal fusion, recurrent neural networks with attention for real-time sequential signals, pre-trained autoencoder networks for dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional genomic data, and a context-aware multi-task learning network for personalised risk and treatment predictions. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are integrated to provide global and local feature attributions, so that clinicians can see which genomic markers, clinical variables and contextual factors drive each prediction. Across breast, lung, colorectal, cardiovascular, diabetic and chronic kidney disease cohorts derived from The Cancer Genome Atlas, the framework reports higher AUC, precision, sensitivity, recall and F1-score than the literature-reported benchmarks used for comparison, together with a reduction in false positives. Limitations, including the use of simulated physiological monitoring signals and the absence of independently re-implemented baselines, are stated explicitly.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67222-5.title: Physics-guided residual learning for phase-aware UAV trajectory prediction in urban environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67222-5.abstract: Abstract Reliable and accurate trajectory prediction is critical for the safe and efficient operation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in complex urban environments, where flight dynamics are subject to wind disturbances, dense obstacle fields, and strongly phase-dependent behavior. Conventional physics-based approaches are limited by parameter uncertainty, simplifying assumptions, and unmodeled disturbances, while data-driven models may lack physical plausibility and robustness across different flight phases. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-guided hybrid residual-correction framework for UAV trajectory prediction. The approach combines a physics-based model with a data-driven sequence model and learns a residual correction that compensates for the deviation between analytical prediction and observed flight behavior. In addition, the model is trained with physics-guided feasibility regularization to promote realistic speed, acceleration, jerk, and landing descent behavior. Experimental evaluation on a real-world test set shows that the proposed method yields improved results relative to the stand-alone physics model, the LSTM model, and an MLP-based fusion model across all major metrics, including RMSE, MAE, ADE, and FDE. Phase-wise analysis further demonstrates strong improvements in cruise and landing, while highlighting takeoff as the most challenging phase. The results indicate that combining physical structure with learned residual correction provides a more accurate, physically consistent, and operationally interpretable approach for UAV trajectory forecasting.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67770-w.title: Effects of variable incubation temperature during embryonic days 10–13 on leg muscle transcriptomics in day-old broiler and layer chicks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67770-w.abstract: Abstract In chickens, secondary myogenesis occurs during embryonic days (ED) 10–13, which is a critical developmental window sensitive to incubation temperature as a key environmental factor. This study investigates transcriptional profiles in leg muscle of broiler (Ross 308; Ross) and layer chickens (Lohmann Brown; LB) at hatch following transient ± 1 °C deviations from standard incubation temperature during ED 10–13. Eggs were incubated at 37.8 °C (CON), 36.8 °C (Low), or 38.8 °C (High) for 72 h between ED 10–13 before being returned to standard conditions until hatch (ED 21). Leg muscle samples from both sexes were analysed using RNA sequencing ( n = 108). Hatch body weight and yolk-free body weight were higher in Ross compared to LB, but were unaffected by incubation temperature. Lowered incubation temperature in LB hatchlings was associated with altered mitochondrial and metabolic pathways, including the downregulation of genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation and reduced expression of myogenic regulators such as MYF5 and MYOG compared to CON birds. Increased incubation temperature involved enrichment of proteolytic processes and downregulation of genes associated with extracellular matrix organization ( COL1A1 , COL6A1 ) in LB hatchlings and myogenesis ( MYOG ) in Ross hatchlings compared to CON birds. Results suggest that deviations from standard incubation temperature during the critical window of secondary myogenesis modulate leg muscle development in a strain-specific manner.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68169-3.title: Structure–property correlation in Fe-substituted La0.7Sr1.3Co1−xFexO4 Ruddlesden–Popper oxides: insights into nonlinear optical behavior
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68169-3.abstract: This study reports the influence of Fe substitution at the Co site on the structural evolution, linear optical behavior, and nonlinear optical properties of La 0.7 Sr 1.3 Co 1−x Fe x O 4 via modified sol-gel method. XRD analysis indicated an increase in the lattice parameters, specifically ‘a’ and ‘c’, as the Fe content rose. According to FESEM images, when the Fe content increases, the average particle diameter grows from roughly 60 nm for the undoped sample (x = 0) to about 210 nm for x = 0.5. The influence of Fe substitution at the Co site on obtained band gap values are decreasing from 3.60, 3.50, 3.38, to 3.35 eV for x = 0.0, 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5, respectively. The nonlinear optical properties are measured using the Z-scan method, which is a common technique for studying optical nonlinearity. The highest nonlinearity responses belong to sample x = 0.5 at 55 mW incident power of laser that causes n 2 and β are 9.57 × 10 − 8 cm 2 /W and 5.44 × 10 − 3 cm/W, respectively. The results show that increasing the Fe content leads to higher values of the nonlinearity responses. This material is a promising candidate for optical devices and optoelectronic applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61626-z.title: GIS-based multi-criteria landslide susceptibility assessment in the Northwestern Himalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, India
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61626-z.abstract: This study presents a landslide susceptibility assessment using multiple parameters by integrating remote sensing, GIS, and field observations in the Jammu and Kashmir region. Eight contributing variables were selected for landslide susceptibility analysis: Land Use and Land Cover (LULC), proximity to roads, streams, slope gradient, slope orientation (aspect), geology, geomorphology, and elevation. In addition, an extensive landslide inventory consisting of 669 landslide events was developed using the Field Landslide Inventory Mapping (FLIM) application, LISS-IV satellite data, and field observations, covering an area of 42,950.43 km². Landslide susceptibility mapping (LSM) was carried out using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) approach and validated with MaxEnt software and field-generated landslide data. The resulting landslide susceptibility map was classified into five categories: very high, high, medium, low, and very low susceptibility zones. Based on the AHP approach, these zones cover 3.65% (1,569.0483 km²), 24.43% (10,492.8912 km²), 51.56% (22,147.2369 km²), 18.81% (8,079.2199 km²), and 1.54% (662.0301 km²) of the study area, respectively. The weighted overlay and MaxEnt models proved effective for landslide vulnerability mapping, with MaxEnt achieving AUC values of 0.82 for training data and 0.807 for testing data, indicating good predictive performance. Field validation further showed that 87% of landslides occurred within high and very high susceptibility zones. The Jackknife test identified road proximity, slope, and stream proximity as the most significant independent variables influencing landslide occurrence. The generated landslide susceptibility map provides important insights for reducing landslide risk and serves as a valuable tool for infrastructure planning, community development, and disaster management in the region.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66414-3.title: A low power dynamic latch comparator with grounded reset for gigahertz analog to digital conversion in 180 nm CMOS
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66414-3.abstract: Dynamic regenerative comparators are widely used in high-speed and low-power analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) due to their zero static power consumption, compact area, and fast decision capability. However, conventional dynamic comparator architectures often suffer from excessive power consumption, large delay, kickback noise, and complex clocking schemes, which limit their performance in GHz-range ADC applications. In this paper, a new low-power dynamic latch comparator is proposed, featuring a simplified current-mode regenerative structure combined with an efficient grounded reset technique. The proposed comparator is based on the StrongARM family and employs a minimal two-transistor cross-coupled latch along with a simple readout buffer, significantly reducing circuit complexity, parasitic capacitance, and power consumption. By resetting the output nodes directly to ground, the proposed architecture enables faster regeneration, lower offset, and improved robustness against process variations while eliminating the need for multiple clock phases. In addition, comprehensive analytical expressions for delay, power consumption, and kickback noise are derived to provide deeper insight into the circuit behavior. Post-layout simulations in a 0.18-µm CMOS technology demonstrate that the proposed comparator achieves reliable operation at a clock frequency of 1 GHz with a power consumption of 65.1 µW, a delay of 370.4 ps, a kickback noise of 17.9 mV, and an active core area of only 188.2 μm 2 at a 1.8 V supply voltage. Comparative results confirm that the proposed design offers a favorable trade-off between speed, power efficiency, and area when compared with conventional StrongARM, Lewis-Gray, and Elzakker dynamic comparators, making it a suitable candidate for high-speed and energy-efficient ADC applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66598-8.title: Minimal-preparation Raman platform for tracking small-molecule penetration in ex vivo skin
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66598-8.abstract: Monitoring molecular penetration in skin is important for evaluating topical administration and transdermal delivery systems, but conventional methods provide limited spatiotemporal resolution and often require additional specialized instrumentation or extensive sample preparation. In this study, we present a conventional Raman spectroscopy-based analytical platform for monitoring the penetration dynamics of a target substance in ex vivo skin with minimal sample preparation and without cryo-sectioning. Raman signals were acquired using 785 nm excitation, and skin-induced signal changes were characterized and corrected to improve detection reliability. Using methylene blue (MB) as a model substance, the Raman band at 1619 cm –1 was used as the primary spectral marker to identify MB-positive regions and determine penetration depth, while its fluorescence background was retained as additional supporting evidence of MB presence rather than being removed as an unwanted signal. Penetration-depth analysis was performed from an application time of 5 min to 60 min, revealing the time-dependent evolution of molecular penetration in ex vivo skin. This minimal-preparation approach may serve as a practical tool for evaluating penetration dynamics in skin tissue.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64741-z.title: Fuzzy RNN based IDS for secure routing using ACO meta heuristic algorithm in WSN
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64741-z.abstract: Abstract Provision of security against continuous threats through the effective detection and prevention of intrusions along with efficient and secure routing is essential for modern Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) applications. The traditional secure routing protocols and the intrusion detection systems developed with single-layer network data are not able to detect many attacks accurately leading to increased packet drops in routing. In order to address these security and routing challenges, this paper proposes a new Intrusion Detection System (IDS) which has been designed by combining spatial, temporal and fuzzy rules with Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and whale optimization to develop a cross layer IDS by considering the application layer and network layer data of WSN. Here, the nodes are clustered based on spectral clustering approach and the data are routed securely through the Cluster Head nodes using the proposed Cluster oriented Fuzzy Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and IDS based secure routing algorithm for effective route discovery and data delivery. Here, the data are routed securely by considering the IDS feedback to enhance the security of communication. The major advantages of the proposed cluster oriented fuzzy ACO based secure routing system with IDS are increase in security, packet delivery ratio and the overall network throughput with reduction in delay and energy consumption.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69252-5.title: Transverse carpal ligament thickness on wrist MRI in carpal tunnel syndrome: a retrospective case–control study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69252-5.abstract: Abstract Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is associated with structural alterations of the median nerve and surrounding components of the carpal tunnel; however, quantitative assessment of the transverse carpal ligament (TCL) remains limited. This exploratory retrospective case-control study evaluated transverse carpal ligament thickness (TCLT) on wrist magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in patients with CTS and controls. The analysis included 20 clinically classified CTS cases and 20 controls. TCLT was measured on axial T1-weighted images at the hook-of-hamate level, and measurement reproducibility and within-sample discrimination were assessed. Mean TCLT was greater in the CTS group than in the control group (1.24 ± 0.17 mm vs. 0.81 ± 0.16 mm), with a mean difference of 0.43 mm (95% CI, 0.32–0.54; p < 0.001) and a large standardized effect size (Hedges’ g = 2.55). Intra-observer and inter-observer intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86–0.96) and 0.88 (95% CI, 0.80–0.93), respectively. Receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.97 (95% CI, 0.94–1.00). An internally derived threshold of 1.01 mm yielded a sensitivity of 90.0% (95% CI, 68.3–98.8%) and a specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 68.3–98.8%) within the present sample. TCLT was greater in selected CTS cases than in controls and showed strong within-sample discrimination. However, given the small retrospective two-gate case-control design and absence of independent validation, these findings should be considered exploratory. The internally derived threshold should not be interpreted as a clinically validated diagnostic cut-off and requires evaluation in larger, independent cohorts using standardized imaging and reference-standard procedures.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68332-w.title: Detection of resonant knapped lithics using chirp sonar
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68332-w.abstract: Abstract Sub-bottom profiling (SBP) systems have been used to detect lithics on the seafloor, where their presence has been inferred from a convex pattern of reflections in the water-column portion of the profile, called haystacks. These signals have been attributed to the resonant properties of human-knapped lithics, but the physical mechanism responsible for their unexpected appearance has not been explained. We investigate the origin of these signals through controlled experiments and modeling. In experiments conducted over lithic assemblages in an anechoic pool, we demonstrate that flaked lithics on the seafloor generate water-column signals in chirp SBP data, with the strongest response coming from concentrations of smaller flakes, potentially due to their greater numbers of resonators with resonance frequencies within the chirp bandwidth. We developed an idealized model of a chirp SBP insonifying resonant objects on the seafloor which reveals that the haystack is a processing artifact. Together, experimental and modeling results confirm that narrowband lithic resonance, combined with standard chirp matched-filter processing, is responsible for the haystack signal. These findings suggest that SBP chirp parameters, particularly bandwidth and frequency range, could be optimized to target lithic resonance, and that alternative processing approaches operating on pre-matched-filter data may offer improved detection capability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66366-8.title: Stereotypes about tourette syndrome and associations with social media use: results from a large-scale german population survey
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66366-8.abstract: Abstract Misunderstandings about tic disorders are common in both the media and the genreal public. However, no large-scale population-based study has investigated public knowledge and stereotypes about tic disorders. We conducted such a survey about knowledge and stereotypes about Gilles de la Tourette syndrome (GTS) in Germany in 2024. Among respondents who had heard about GTS ( n = 1,175, 16–88 years, M = 47.9 ± 16.3), 50% of knowledge items were answered correctly. A score summarizing stereotyping statements revealed an average agreement of 39%. The vast majority associated GTS with coprolalia (87%), copropraxia (75%) and – less frequently – with other symptoms that are atypical but frequently portrayed in the media, such as contextualized commentaries (50%) and destroying objects (29%). Subjects who knew someone with GTS had better knowledge than those who did not know anyone with GTS. Regression analyses revealed a significant association between the estimation of own knowledge on GTS as good and stereotypical beliefs. Social media use to get informed about psychiatric diseases was linked to more knowledge and less stereotypes, however, having watched a video depicting individuals with presumed GTS was associated with more stereotypes. Our study demonstrated overall poor knowledge and widespread stereotypes about GTS in Germans. Studies evaluating options for stigma reduction are needed to foster equality and prevent disadvantages for affected persons.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68274-3.title: Standardized Sechium edule root extract attenuates LPS inflammation alongside transient STAT3 phosphorylation and an interleukin 10 biased macrophage response
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68274-3.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation is sustained by macrophage activation toward proinflammatory states and contributes to cardiometabolic and degenerative disorders. Given the growing interest in evidence-based medicinal plants, we investigated whether a hydroalcoholic root extract of Sechium edule (rSe-HA) attenuates LPS-induced macrophage inflammatory activation and modulates selected cytokine, surface-marker, functional, and signaling parameters under persistent in vitro inflammatory stimulation. Murine RAW 264.7 macrophages were activated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and treated with cinnamic acid-standardized rSe-HA. In culture supernatants, nitrite was quantified as an indirect index of nitric oxide production, and cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-10, TGF-β, and IL-4) were measured by immunoassays; the IL-10/TGF-β ratio was calculated as an exploratory indicator of cytokine balance. F4/80, CD86, and CD206 expressions and phagocytosis of latex beads were assessed by flow cytometry. STAT3 phosphorylation was assessed by immunoblotting, and NF-κB/AP-1-dependent reporter activity was examined in RAW-Blue reporter macrophages. rSe-HA reduced nitrite, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels; limited the increase in LPS-induced CD86, whereas it favored the increase of CD206 and partially restored phagocytic activity. Additionally, rSe-HA was associated with a transient increase in STAT3 phosphorylation and reduced NF-κB/AP-1-dependent reporter activity. These findings support an IL-10-biased immunomodulatory response rather than definitive assignment to a specific macrophage subtype. Further studies in primary macrophages and additional mechanistic models are needed to validate these in vitro findings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63863-8.title: Dipolar recoil force and torque are odd under time reversal and originate from retardation in mutual charge interaction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63863-8.abstract: Abstract The recoil optical force and torque acting on an electromagnetic dipole are typically derived by computing the imbalance in radiated linear and angular electromagnetic momentum coming from the source, using Maxwell stress tensor integration. This quantifies the recoil’s outcome without revealing its physical origin or the underlying mechanisms that produce it. The recoil force and torque exist even in the absence of external illumination, such that an isolated dipole emitter can experience them. In contrast to the other terms, the recoil terms are odd under time reversal. To clarify their nature and properties, we re-derive the recoil force from first principles using the total Lorentz force on a system of charges that form a simultaneous electric and magnetic dipole. The results agree with the standard momentum-based derivation and reveal their ultimate origin from retardation effects—arising from the finite speed of light—in the mutual interactions between charges. This result provides fundamental insight into the recoil mechanism, offering a clearer conceptual foundation for future theoretical and experimental studies of light-induced forces.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65971-x.title: Green electricity adoption as a catalyst for mitigating the ecological pressure of economic complexity in BRICS economies
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65971-x.abstract: Environmental sustainability has become an increasingly important policy challenge for emerging economies, where rapid industrialization and structural transformation are placing growing pressure on natural resources. This study examines the relationship between economic complexity and environmental sustainability in BRICS countries. Specifically, it analyzes the impact of the economic complexity index on the ecological footprint and investigates whether green electricity adoption moderates this relationship. The study uses annual data from 1995 to 2023 and applies the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) and Bootstrap Quantile Regression (BSQR) to capture heterogeneous effects across different levels of ecological pressure. The results indicate that higher economic complexity significantly increases the ecological footprint, suggesting that advanced production structures are associated with greater resource consumption and environmental pressure. In contrast, green electricity adoption consistently reduces ecological degradation across all quantiles. Furthermore, the interaction between economic complexity and green electricity adoption is negative and significant, confirming that green electricity adoption mitigates the environmental impact of complex economies. These findings suggest that BRICS countries should align industrial development with renewable energy expansion by promoting green technologies, supporting renewable electricity in advanced sectors, and gradually reallocating fossil fuel subsidies to achieve sustainable development.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67250-1.title: Characterization of multidrug-resistant Salmonella Typhimurium isolates from Korean swine farms and plasmids harboring fluoroquinolone and third-generation cephalosporin resistance genes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67250-1.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium is a major foodborne pathogen, and the overuse of antimicrobials has contributed to the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains. Resistance to third-generation cephalosporins and fluoroquinolones is of particular concern because of their critical importance in human medicine. In this study, we characterized the phenotypic and genotypic features of MDR S. Typhimurium isolates from pig farms using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Among 45 S. Typhimurium isolates recovered from 129 pig farms, 29 were identified as MDR based on phenotypic screening and subjected to WGS. Phenotypically, the MDR isolates exhibited high resistance to aminoglycosides (100%), penicillins (97%), and phenicols (90%). WGS identified five isolates coharboring the third-generation cephalosporin resistance gene bla CTX-M-65 and the fluoroquinolone resistance gene qnrS1 , whereas four additional isolates carried qnrS1 alone. The bla CTX-M-65 gene was detected exclusively on IncHI2-type plasmids, whereas qnrS1 was detected on IncHI2-, IncF-type, and unclassified plasmids. In the analyzed plasmids, bla CTX-M-65 was located between mobQ–fipA and IS 903 B , whereas qnrS1 was flanked by IS 15 DIV–transposase and hin–ISKpn 19. These findings improve our understanding of the phenotypic resistance profiles, resistance genes, and plasmids associated with MDR S. Typhimurium from pig farms and support continued genomic surveillance for monitoring the dissemination of clinically important resistance determinants.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68682-5.title: Combining RUSLE and vegetation health index model to unravel the relations between soil erosion and agricultural drought
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68682-5.abstract: Recurrent droughts, intensified by rising global temperatures, erratic rainfall patterns, and soil erosion, lead to crop failures, water scarcity, and food insecurity across most parts of Ethiopia. However, it has not yet been evaluated using appropriate data and methods. To address these research gaps for actionable policy development input on the integrating drought conditions and soil erosion problem, in Awash River Basin, Ethiopia, this study developed a Google Earth Engine (GEE) based Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) and Vegetation Health Index (VHI) modeling approach to assess soil erosion and drought event spatiotemporal occurrence and their relation for 23 years (2001–2023). To do this, the VHI was derived by integrating the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) and the Temperature Condition Index (TCI), both of which were computed using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from the MOD13A2 product and Land Surface Temperature (LST) from the MOD11A2 product, respectively. This integration was used to characterize the spatiotemporal dynamics of agricultural drought conditions. The GEE RUSLE approach was applied to estimate the qualitative and quantitative soil loss from the river basin. Pearson's correlation was used to examine the relationship between soil erosion and drought conditions. The results of these approaches revealed that the Awash River Basin experienced recurrent mild-to-extreme spatial and mild-to-severe temporal droughts during the study period. Spatially, the upper and middle parts of the river Basin experienced extreme drought (VHI ~ = 3%). Temporally, the months May (2002, 2009, and 2022), March (2008 and 20,216), and April (2015 and 2021) were characterized by severe drought in the area. The maximum, minimum, and mean soil erosion rates were determined to be 150, 5.0, and 25.67 $$t/ha/yr,$$ respectively. This amount of soil loss was intensified by rainfall, slope length, and steepness in the highland areas of the river basin and by soil texture, nature, and lower vegetation cover in the lowland area of the basin. Across the river basin, the interrelation between soil erosion and drought conditions showed spatial variation ranging from −0.2 to 0.4, with an overall mean weak positive correlation (r = 0.20). As a recommendation, policymakers and basin master plan developers should consider soil and water conservation and vegetation preservation as key activities in the upper and lower parts of the river basin, respectively.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66340-4.title: Multi-way analysis of the geographical impact on breastfeeding and nutritional indicators of Amazonian Kichwa infants from Ecuador
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66340-4.abstract: Kichwa communities of Ecuador are considered one of the most important native populations that are part of the country’s cultural wealth, however, studies on their nutritional status still need to be made available. This work examines the changes in the nutritional conditions (anthropometric, biochemical, breastfeeding and dietary indicators) of Kichwa babies from Tena, Ecuador, considering the domain of spatial location (three zones of residence). In order to understand how geographical location influence breastfeeding and nutritional indicators, we apply exploratory, inferential, multivariate analysis and the new three-way multivariate statistical method MixSTATICO, which allows mixed-type data (quantitative and qualitative) structured in two different groups ( \(K\) -matrices) to be related and measured on the spatial scale. The results showed a pattern of similar characteristics between the \(K\) -matrices of the breastfeeding and nutritional indicators of Kichwa babies from zones 2 (semi-rural) and 3 (rural), with very high proximities; while zone 1 (urban) had a different behavior. The analysis of the stable part of the \(K\) -matrices found that the average co-structures determined groups of variables highly associated in a positive way, including exclusive breastfeeding and infant feeding, ferritin and vitamin D, among others. This study has shown the associations between breastfeeding, anthropometric, biochemical, food consumption indicators from Kichwa babies and their zones of residence, the semi-rural and rural zones are similar, in contrast to the urban zone. The inferential , univariate and multivariate analysis of the information did not find significant differences between the study zones ( p -value > 0.05). However, the multi-way analysis , through the three-way multivariate method for mixed data MixSTATICO found different pattern structures according to the zones of residence.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68348-2.title: A hybrid adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm for two-echelon electric vehicle routing problem
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68348-2.abstract: The efficient management of urban logistics is important for smart production and service systems, requiring coordinated optimization and planning for sustainable and responsive operations. This study investigates a two-echelon electric vehicle routing problem with time windows (2E-EVRPTW), an important optimization problem in urban delivery networks. The problem involves using fuel-powered trucks for the first-echelon transport from a warehouse to satellites and electric vehicles (EVs) with limited range and charging needs for the second-echelon, time-sensitive last-mile delivery. To tackle this NP-hard problem, we first formulate it as a mixed-integer linear programming (MIP) model. We then propose a hybrid heuristic algorithm, CL-ALNS, which integrates clustering and adaptive metaheuristic search. Specifically, CL-ALNS combines K-means clustering for strategic facility allocation in the first echelon with an adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) to support routing and charging scheduling in the second echelon. This algorithm is designed to reduce total cost while obtaining efficient, high-quality solutions. Computational experiments and benchmarks against a commercial solver and heuristic baselines show that our CL-ALNS framework obtains competitive results under the tested settings. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis examines how key operational parameters influence the system, providing valuable insights for managers of smart logistics services.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69214-x.title: NR2F6 enhances glioma invasion and migration through upregulation of COL1A1 and activation of integrin signaling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69214-x.abstract: Glioma represents the most aggressive form of intracranial malignant tumor, characterized by a poor prognosis in affected patients. Nuclear receptor NR2F6 has been implicated as an oncogenic factor in various cancers; however, its specific role and underlying mechanisms in glioma invasion and migration remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate whether NR2F6 promotes glioma cell invasion and migration in IDH wild-type glioma cells through regulation of the COL1A1-integrin signaling pathway. Bioinformatics analyses were performed using data from The CPTAC databases to assess NR2F6 expression levels and identify associated functional pathways. Clinical glioma tissue samples were collected, and NR2F6 protein expression was validated via immunohistochemistry. In vitro experiments were conducted using human glioma cell lines (U251 and LN229), in which NR2F6 overexpression and knockdown models were established using lentiviral transfection. Western blotting was employed to detect the expression levels of NR2F6, COL1A1, and key components of the integrin pathway, including integrin, phosphorylated FAK (p-FAK) and phosphorylated Src (p-Src). Cell migration and invasion capacities were evaluated using scratch wound healing and Transwell invasion assays. NR2F6 was significantly upregulated in high-grade glioma tissues and cell lines. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that NR2F6 is functionally enriched in extracellular matrix organization and focal adhesion pathways and exhibits a positive correlation with COL1A1 expression. Functional assays demonstrated that NR2F6 overexpression markedly enhanced the migratory and invasive capabilities of IDH wild-type glioma cells, whereas NR2F6 knockdown suppressed these phenotypes. Mechanistically, NR2F6 positively regulates COL1A1 and integrin expression and activates downstream FAK and Src phosphorylation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68798-8.title: A large-scale integrated optical phased array with digital beamforming
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68798-8.abstract: Abstract Digital signal processing has driven much of the capacity growth in coherent fiber-optic communications, but its use in free-space coherent imagers and sensors has so far been limited. We report a 128-element optical phased array with a fully parallelized readout that performs beamforming in the digital domain at 1550 nm. The photonic integrated circuit consists of an array of waveguide grating antennas, each routed to its own balanced coherent receiver, with a common on-chip local oscillator delivered to all 128 receivers through a 1:128 binary splitter tree. Since every channel is digitized independently, we recover the per-channel amplitude and phase without on-chip phase shifters and perform image reconstruction by computing the array factor in software. Using 6 of the 128 elements, we obtain digitally reconstructed beams with an average half-power beamwidth of $$1.23^{\circ }$$ and a field-of-view of $$8.30^{\circ }$$ for illumination angles between $$-4^{\circ }$$ and $$+3^{\circ }$$ . Across the full array, the median common-mode rejection ratio is 57 dB and the median noise floor is $$-118.9$$ dBm in a 1 Hz bandwidth, corresponding to a per-channel sensitivity of $$-121$$ dBm/Hz. The phases extracted from the digitized channels show sub-degree noise, indicating that the coherent detection and digital processing chain is working as intended. The architecture removes the need for on-chip phase shifters and points toward a practical route to large-format, high-resolution coherent receiver arrays for free-space sensing, ranging, and optical communications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68883-y.title: Enhancing clinical reasoning and diagnostic precision through scaling laws and multi-stage supervised fine-tuning in open-weight medical large language models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68883-y.abstract: Abstract The emergence of large language models offers unprecedented opportunities to transform clinical workflows. However, reliance on proprietary closed-source models poses significant risks to data privacy, institutional autonomy, and reasoning transparency. This study investigates the optimization of open-weight architectures, specifically the Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct families, to function as specialized diagnostic tools rather than general-purpose conversational agents. Utilizing the MedQA USMLE-style benchmark, we evaluate the synergistic impact of context window scaling and multi-stage supervised fine-tuning within a localized Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework. Our findings identify a critical scaling threshold at 512 tokens, beyond which diagnostic accuracy stabilizes while preserving the computational efficiency required for on-site clinical deployment. Furthermore, we document a pronounced Brevity Shift, in which multi-stage supervised fine-tuning reduced model verbosity by over 99.7%. The models transitioned from long-form reasoning with an average of 465 tokens to single-token outputs for Qwen and near-single-token outputs for Llama. This shift effectively mitigated verbosity compensation, defined as the tendency of models to mask uncertainty through excessive text, while simultaneously improving diagnostic performance, which peaked at 70.0% accuracy for the Qwen architecture on the benchmark task. Additionally, our analysis reveals that systematic fine-tuning substantially reduces option-preference bias, as measured by Total Variation Distance, leading to more objective and consistent model outputs. Conducted under the INFOSTRATEG Strategic Program (PARROT AI) and funded by the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR), Poland, this work establishes a robust technical framework for developing trustworthy, high-efficiency medical AI systems capable of operating entirely within hospital-controlled infrastructure.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67020-z.title: Enhanced thermal stability and structural behavior of terbium-doped polyaniline-multiwalled carbon nanocomposite
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67020-z.abstract: Terbium chloride doped polyaniline/multiwalled carbon nanotube (Tb-PAniMW) nanocomposite was effectively prepared via an oxidative polymerization method to examine the effect of rare-earth metal doping on the structural and thermal characteristics of conductive polymer nanocomposite. The incorporation of Tb³⁺ ions within the PAni/MWCNT framework was established through FT-IR spectroscopy, which exhibited the major characteristic absorption bands at 1585 cm⁻¹ and 1485 cm⁻¹ related to the quinonoid (Q) and benzenoid (B) units of polyaniline. The Morphological studies of Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) revealed a compact nanostructured surface with homogeneous distribution of the dopant throughout the nanocomposite matrix. Thermogravimetric analysis confirmed a three-stage degradation process, with overall weight losses observed of 40.07% to 46.80% at heating rates between 10 and 50 °C min⁻¹. The maximum residue of 59.93% obtained at 30 °C min⁻¹ indicates enhanced resistance to thermal decomposition. The Kinetic estimation showed activation energy values in the range of 12.33–55.10 kJ mol⁻¹, which reflecting the variations in the decomposition mechanism across different degradation stages. The positive enthalpy values proposed an energy fascinating degradation process, whereas negative entropy values specified the formation of a more organized activated state during decomposition. The Gibbs free energy values observed between 81.26 and 213.08 kJ mol⁻¹ confirmed the thermodynamic stability of the polymer matrix. The improved thermal resistance achieved through terbium chloride incorporation of PAni/MWCNT nanocomposites for advanced functional and energy-related applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68723-z.title: Coupling of three combustion oscillators with large amplitudes
