doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68723-z.abstract: Abstract We investigate synchronization phenomena in systems of two and three coupled combustion oscillators. An alcohol lamp is employed as a combustion oscillator to realize stable limit-cycle oscillations with large amplitudes, i.e., far from a Hopf bifurcation point. The time evolution of the flame brightness is measured experimentally using a photodiode, and the phase of each oscillator is extracted from the recorded time series to identify synchronization modes. In the two-oscillator system, stable in-phase synchronization is observed at short flame-to-flame distances, whereas anti-phase synchronization becomes stable as the distance increases. In the three-oscillator system, in-phase, partial-in-phase, and tri-phase synchronization modes emerge with increasing flame-to-flame distances. Based on these experimental observations, we discuss the underlying interaction mechanisms between the oscillators within the framework of a phase model.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67579-7.title: Correction: Intravitreal injection of fibrillin 2 (Fbn2) recombinant protein for therapy of retinopathy in a retina-specific Fbn2 knock-down mouse model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67579-7.abstract: As a result of errors during figure assembly, several images in Figure 4 and 5 derived from the same source data. Specifically, the following images are overlapping: panels for fbn2-0.30 µg (2nd fbn2) and fbn2-3.0 µg (AAV-sh-fbn2) in Figure 4A, panels for fbn2-0.30 µg (3rd fbn2) and fbn2-1.50 µg (1st fbn2) in Figure 4A, panels for fbn2-0.75 µg (AAV-sh-fbn2) and fbn2-3.0 µg (2nd fbn2) in Figure 4A, panels for NC (AAV-sh-fbn2) and AAV-NC (AAV-sh-fbn2) in Figure 5, panels for AAV-NC (baseline) and AAV-NC (3rd fbn2) in Figure 5, and panels for fbn2-0.75 µg (baseline) and fbn2-0.75 µg (3rd fbn2) in Figure 5.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68373-1.title: An exploratory genomic landscape of unicuspid aortic valve
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68373-1.abstract: Abstract Unicuspid aortic valve (UAV) is a rare congenital malformation with severe clinical consequences, and its genetic background remains poorly defined. We present an exploratory genomic resource for UAV, generated from whole-exome sequencing (WES) of nine families (including probands and 19 unaffected relatives) and integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from human embryonic hearts. The scRNA-seq dataset enabled the identification of genes expressed in valve-forming cell populations during development, providing a biologically informed filter for candidate variant prioritisation. Further prioritisation identified 81 candidate variants across 68 genes with enrichment in extracellular matrix (ECM) organisation and developmental signalling pathways, particularly transforming growth factor-β-mediated signalling. Complementary exome-wide family segregation analysis further supported this pattern, again highlighting ECM organisation and developmental signalling as recurrently enriched biological themes. By establishing a preliminary genomic dataset, this study provides a resource for further validation, expansion to larger cohorts, and exploration of the molecular architecture underlying this rare disorder.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67752-y.title: Direct exposure of Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus extracts to engineered water nanostructures significantly prevent Der p-induced allergic airway inflammation in mice
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67752-y.abstract: Abstract House dust mite extract derived from Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus (Der p) is a major cause of allergic asthma; however, effective preventive approaches remain limited. This study examined whether direct treatment of Der p extract with engineered water nanostructures (EWNS) reduces the detectable allergen signal and biological responses associated with Der p 1. Der p extracts were exposed to EWNS for 1–24 h, and the ELISA-detectable Der p 1 signal was measured. Dendritic cell activation induced by EWNS-treated or untreated Der p extract normalized to Der p 1 content was evaluated in DC2.4 cells. A Der p-induced allergic airway inflammation model was generated by repeated intranasal administration of EWNS-treated or untreated Der p extract normalized to Der p 1 content. EWNS exposure reduced the ELISA-detectable Der p 1 signal. Ca 2+ influx, MHC class II expression, inflammatory cytokine production, and immune-related gene expression were attenuated by EWNS-treated Der p extract. In vivo, EWNS-treated Der p extract significantly reduced Der p-induced allergic airway inflammation, as indicated by improved percutaneous oxygen saturation and decreased pro-inflammatory responses. These findings suggest that EWNS treatment may reduce the allergenic activity of Der p extract.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64065-y.title: Sustainable mineral processing risk analysis based initial settling rates prediction using enhanced machine learning models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64065-y.abstract: Abstract The primary contamination concern of mineral processing tailings (MPT) is the leaching of hazardous substances into the environment. The literature indicates that MPT requires effective flocculation and polymer-assisted dewatering to ensure its disposal does not cause environmental damage. In this research, a theoretical modeling framework was adopted, based on the development of a hybrid machine learning (ML) model for predicting flocculation-dewatering efficiency, aiming to reduce the cost of laboratory tests. The proposed ML model is based on an efficient Gaussian process regression (GPR) model that uses a feature impact strategy (FIS) and a kernel matrix dynamically updated using error noise, named enhanced GPR (EGPR). Additionally, the kernel ridge model and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method are coupled for feature selection (FS), identifying the most important features among 17 input variables (features). The target variable in this research is the initial settling rate (ISR), which is predicted to utilize the EGPR model. The statistical analysis revealed that the EGPR model outperforms the Deep random vector functional link (DRVFL), least square support vector machine (LSSVM), cascade feedforward neural network (CFNN), and ridge regression with superior error metrics (R = 0.951, RMSE = 0.196, MAPE = 62.22). It also demonstrated the least uncertainty (UI = 17.65), which indicates its reliability and accuracy. Risk analysis (RA) indicates that the EGPR model yields the lowest total risk score (TRS) (5.6) and is classified as a “Very Low” risk method. Furthermore, SHAP analysis exhibits that the solids content (SC) and flocculant dose (FD) positively influenced the prediction of ISR. Consequently, this study presents a foundational methodology for predicting ISR, which could be introduced as an essential tool for flocculate-settling studies that contribute to optimal chemical dosage, real-time contamination monitoring, and the operation of water recovery storage capacity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68010-x.title: A large-language-model framework for automated humanitarian situation reporting
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68010-x.abstract: Timely and accurate situational reports are essential for humanitarian decision-making, yet current workflows remain largely manual, resource intensive, and inconsistent. We present a fully automated framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to transform heterogeneous humanitarian documents into structured and evidence-grounded reports. The system integrates semantic text clustering, automatic question generation, retrieval augmented answer extraction with citations, multi-level summarization, and executive summary generation, supported by internal evaluation metrics that emulate expert reasoning. We evaluated the framework across 13 humanitarian events, including natural disasters and conflicts, using more than 1100 documents from verified sources such as ReliefWeb. The generated questions achieved 84.7% relevance, 84.0% importance, and 76.4% urgency. The extracted answers reached 86.3% relevance, with citation precision and recall both exceeding 76%. Agreement between human and LLM based evaluations surpassed an F1 score of 0.80. Comparative analysis shows that the proposed framework produces reports that are more structured, interpretable, and actionable than existing baselines. By combining LLM reasoning with transparent citation linking and multi-level evaluation, this study shows that generative AI can substantially support the generation of humanitarian situation reports that domain experts judged more useful, better structured, and more transparently sourced than current approaches—marking a concrete step toward operational use, even as important challenges remain on the path to fully reliable autonomous deployment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67377-1.title: Optimizing tennis serve performance in university players through 2D kinematic motion analysis and biomechanical feedback
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67377-1.abstract: Tennis serve performance depends on the coordinated execution of multiple body segments and the timing of successive serve phases. Although biomechanical feedback has been used to support technical refinement, its immediate effects on university-level players remain insufficiently understood. This study examined whether two-dimensional (2D) kinematic analysis combined with structured visual and verbal feedback was associated with measurable immediate changes in selected serve mechanics and performance outcomes. Sixty male university tennis players aged 18–24 years were allocated to experimental and control groups ( n = 30 each) in a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design. The experimental group received one session of combined video-based and verbal biomechanical feedback, whereas the control group continued conventional training. Serves were recorded using calibrated 2D motion analysis software (Dartfish; RMS error < 1%) to assess temporal, ball-toss, kinematic, racket, and performance variables. Pre–post change scores were compared between groups using independent-samples t-tests or Mann–Whitney U tests, with within-group analyses conducted using paired-samples t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Effect sizes and percentage changes were also calculated. Compared with the control group, the experimental group showed greater immediate changes in total serve time ( p = 0.030, d = 0.56), forward swing time ( p = 0.012, d = 0.72), toss height ( p = 0.021, d = 0.60), horizontal toss deviation ( p = 0.003, r = 0.65), knee flexion ( p = 0.015, d = 0.61), hip extension ( p = 0.004, d = 0.86), trunk extension ( p = 0.006, d = 0.84), trunk forward flexion ( p = 0.011, d = 0.73), shoulder abduction ( p = 0.002, d = 1.02), wrist extension ( p = 0.003, d = 0.98), estimated planar racket velocity ( p = 0.001, d = 1.10), and ball impact height ( p = 0.015, d = 0.59). No statistically significant pre–post changes were found in the control group for the corresponding variables. Serve accuracy increased from 70% to 80% in the experimental group but was considered exploratory due to the limited number of trials and binary scoring method. A single session of combined 2D kinematic analysis and structured visual–verbal feedback was associated with immediate changes in selected planar serve mechanics and performance outcomes among university-level players. These findings should be interpreted as short-term performance adaptations rather than evidence of motor learning, long-term retention, or improvement in unmeasured biomechanical mechanisms.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67705-5.title: A critical analysis and proposed method for fermatean fuzzy sets
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67705-5.abstract: Since K. T. Atanassov introduced the intuitionistic fuzzy set (IFS), numerous extensions and and methodologies have been developed and applied in practical contexts. Among these, the Fermatean fuzzy set (FFS) has been recognized as particularly adaptable for handling the uncertainty inherent in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) problems due to its expanded domain space. Although various aggregation operators (AOs) have been proposed for FFSs, some of them yield unreasonable or counter-intuitive results in certain situations. In this paper, a detailed review and critical analysis are conducted to reveal the shortcomings of existing approaches. To address these issues, new operational rules (ORs) for FFSs are proposed, and their desirable mathematical properties are formally established. The advantages of the proposed method are demonstrated through several numerical examples that highlight its improved behavior compared with existing approaches. Furthermore, to validate the reliability and practical relevance of the proposed method, it is applied to selected MCDM and pattern recognition problems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68470-1.title: Dynamic interplay between cognitive load and teaching presence among university English teachers in generative AI-augmented instruction: a longitudinal mixed-methods study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68470-1.abstract: Abstract University teachers who bring generative AI into the classroom face a double demand: they must manage the mental cost of working with the tool while sustaining the pedagogical presence their students rely on. This study asks how the two are related. Survey data were collected from 186 English teachers at 24 Chinese universities across three waves of a single semester (Weeks 2, 8 and 15), and 28 of these teachers were interviewed once the final wave had closed. Structural equation modeling indicated that extraneous cognitive load was negatively associated with all three teaching presence dimensions, most strongly with facilitating discourse, whereas germane load was positively associated with presence, most clearly with direct instruction. AI proficiency moderated the extraneous-load pathway, flattening it for more proficient teachers, and AI attitude carried a small share of that association. Across the three waves extraneous load fell while germane load and teaching presence rose. The interviews corroborated these patterns for most participants and identified teachers for whom they did not hold, including some who experienced intrinsic demand as productive. Because the design is observational, spans one semester, and relies throughout on self-report, the results describe covariation rather than developmental or causal effect. The study nonetheless extends the Community of Inquiry framework by specifying cognitive antecedents of teaching presence, and offers situated guidance on tool procurement, tiered training and graduated support in Chinese higher education. Full instruments, the coding framework, the analysis code and the de-identified data set are provided at Related files.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66252-3.title: Purpose-built WAAM 316L benchmark walls for thermo-mechanical calibration and strain-based hardness prediction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66252-3.abstract: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) of 316L generates complex thermal cycles, distortion and work hardening that are difficult to validate in 3D. Hence, in this paper, we design, build and fully characterise two benchmark walls (two-layer and three-layer) expressly for calibrating and validating open-source thermo-mechanical simulations in MOOSE with emphasis on hardness prediction. The geometry combines unfinished passes, controlled overlap and steady-state regions so that a single build exercises transient and quasi-stationary behaviour. A multi-zone thermocouple layout (top and bottom) enables a robust thermal calibration that reproduces peak temperatures and cooling histories. Full-field 3D scanning yields distortion maps condensed into a normalised warping index; MOOSE reproduces longitudinal/transverse distortion with absolute errors ≤ 0.10 mm. Microhardness maps of two cross-sections are compared to hardness fields reconstructed from the simulated accumulated equivalent plastic strain using a single Tabor-type law. Across lines V1/V2/H1, the full J 2 -invariant surrogate achieves MAE ≈ 6–10 HV (comparable to test scatter), while a reduced “normal-only” strain measure shows MAE ≈ 25–35 HV and misses overlap-band peaks by ~ 20–40 HV, demonstrating the need for the full deviatoric invariant in WAAM 316L. Unlike prior WAAM validation studies that consider either single tracks or thermal/distortion only, this work delivers combined thermal, distortion and hardness datasets on multi-pass walls and an open, element-birth MOOSE workflow that enables full-field 3D hardness mapping from a calibrated strain surrogate. The benchmarks expose how layer count and pass pattern modulate hardness via reheating and constraint, and provide a reusable testbed for heat-source, boundary-condition and hardness-law comparisons.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66968-2.title: Leukocyte glycemic index associated with 30-day mortality in sepsis patients with new-onset atrial fibrillation: insights from the MIMIC-IV database
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66968-2.abstract: This study aimed to examine whether the leukocyte glycemic index (LGI), a compact marker linking inflammatory burden with stress-related glucose disturbance, is associated with 30-day mortality among patients with sepsis complicated by new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF). This retrospective cohort study used MIMIC-IV data. LGI was derived from the first available white blood cell count and glucose measurement within 24 hours after ICU admission; glucose was converted from mg/dL to mmol/L before multiplication, and LGI was then log-transformed using the natural logarithm. We evaluated LGI with tertile-based Cox models, restricted cubic splines, threshold-effect analyses, exploratory subgroup analyses, and prediction-performance analyses. The cohort included 691 patients, of whom 315 (45.59%) died within 30 days. The median age was 72.39 years, and 418 patients (60.49%) were male. The log(LGI) tertile cut points were 4.284 and 4.861. In the fully adjusted tertile analysis, T3 showed a borderline higher risk than T2 (HR 1.33, 95% CI 1.00-1.77, p=0.052), while T1 did not differ significantly from T2. A single linear log(LGI) term did not carry a clear adjusted association with mortality, whereas spline and threshold models supported a nonlinear association. The estimated inflection point was log(LGI) = 4.403. Below this value, each 1-unit increase in log(LGI) was associated with lower mortality risk (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.91), indicating that very low log(LGI) values identified a higher-risk subset. Above the inflection point, each 1-unit increase in log(LGI) was associated with higher mortality risk (HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.20-1.85). Adding spline-transformed log(LGI) to a clinical model modestly improved discrimination (AUC 0.715 to 0.732; DeLong p=0.023). In patients with sepsis and NOAF, LGI showed a nonlinear association with 30-day mortality, with increased risk at both lower and higher ranges, more pronounced at the high extreme. LGI may add a small but measurable layer of prognostic information to routinely available clinical variables, but it should be interpreted as an adjunctive, hypothesis-generating marker rather than a stand-alone risk tool.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66929-9.title: Genome-wide analysis of the Ehretia macrophylla AUX/IAA family under drought and SiO₂ nanoparticle treatment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66929-9.abstract: Abstract Auxin/indole-3-acetic acid (AUX/IAA) proteins are central transcriptional repressors in auxin signaling and are increasingly implicated in plant responses to water deficit. However, AUX/IAA family organization and drought-responsive expression remain poorly characterized in woody plants, and the transcriptional response to silicon dioxide nanoparticles (SiO₂ NPs) is still largely unexplored. In this study, we identified 42 EmAUX/IAA genes in Ehretia macrophylla Wall. and analyzed their chromosomal distribution, gene structures, conserved motifs, promoter cis-elements, phylogenetic relationships, and evolutionary constraints. RNA-seq analysis under control (CK), severe drought (SD), and SiO₂ NP-treated drought (NPs-SD) conditions showed treatment-associated changes in EmAUX/IAA expression. EmAUX/IAA13, EmAUX/IAA28, and EmAUX/IAA33 were induced under drought, and several drought-responsive patterns were attenuated or redirected after SiO₂ NP treatment. qRT-PCR analysis of eight selected genes, including these three candidates, supported the principal expression trends. GO and KEGG enrichment highlighted photosynthesis, ribosome biogenesis, carbon metabolism, secondary metabolism, and hormone-related stress responses. These results provide a genome-wide catalog of the EmAUX/IAA family and prioritize candidates for functional analysis. Because physiological, hormone, and genetic evidence was not obtained, the proposed links among SiO₂ NPs, auxin signaling, and drought responses should be regarded as preliminary associations requiring further validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64263-8.title: Identification of tissue-specific RBFOX1 alternative promoters in the developing brain, heart and muscle
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64263-8.abstract: The precise regulation of cell type- and time-specific gene expression is highly dependent on the use of alternative promoters, enhancers and silencers. The recent advancement of genomic technologies has driven the identification of potential promoter regions for a large number of genes. Nevertheless, comprehensive analyses of alternative promoter usage across diverse tissues and developmental stages remain limited for the majority of human genes. In this study, we identified putative promoter regions located upstream of the alternative first exons of RBFOX1 using publicly available databases and functionally validated them in vivo via reporter gene expression assays in transgenic zebrafish. We uncovered both tissue-restricted and ubiquitously active promoters that collectively shape the complex regulatory expression profile of this essential developmental gene. We also mapped the core promoter of RBFOX1 -E1B, defining its minimal functional unit and demonstrating that endogenous minimal promoters confer tissue-specific enhancer responsiveness that generic heterologous promoters lack. Together, these findings shed light on the complex cis -regulatory machinery driving the precise spatiotemporal expression of this key gene in neurodevelopment and muscle differentiation, and provide a foundation for the development of more specific reporter systems and gene therapy tools targeting neurological diseases.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67073-0.title: Drought and flood risk assessment under the IPCC risk framework in an agriculturally dominated tropical river basin, India
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67073-0.abstract: Climate change increases the severity and frequency of water-related hazards in tropical areas, posing significant risks to agriculture as well as the livelihoods of rural communities. The present work advocates an integrated approach to climate-induced risk assessment of agricultural systems in the tropical river basin, specifically the Shilabati River, India. In this work, risk maps were developed using the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) framework by integrating hazard, exposure, and vulnerability indices derived from 34 physiographic, climatic, hydrological, edaphic, and socio-economic indicators. The Random Forest (RF) model was employed to predict flood and drought risk across the study area, while RF-based Mean Decrease Gini analysis identified maximum temperature, relative humidity, drought intensity, soil moisture, elevation, population density, land use, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), proximity to rivers, and lithology as the most influential factors. The results indicate that 17.64% (407 km²) of the agricultural land is flood-prone, affecting approximately 3.63 lakh people, while 27.02% (623 km²) is drought-prone, impacting about 4.56 lakh people. Overall, 45% of the basin falls within the high agricultural risk category, highlighting the acute vulnerability of small and marginal farmers to climate-induced flood and drought hazards. By integrating multiple hazards (i.e., floods and drought) within a unified framework, this research advances beyond previous approaches on single-hazard studies and provides actionable insights for climate-resilient agricultural planning. The findings directly support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG1: No Poverty, SDG2: Zero Hunger, SDG13: Climate Action) by informing targeted adaptation strategies, strengthening food security, and promoting sustainable rural development in hazard-prone areas of the basin.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66954-8.title: A novel multi-layer security framework for medical image transmission in cloud-based wireless body area networks (BAN) using XAI-guided obfuscation and WDTW encryption
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66954-8.abstract: Abstract The existing frameworks for medical image encryption in the context of BANs have three major limitations: encrypting the whole image consumes enormous amount of processing time; failure to integrate explainable AI for identifying the importance of regions and prioritizing the same for permutation and XORing and inability of verifying the lossless integrity of the decryption process. To tackle these limitations, this paper introduces a novel scheme called weighted dynamic transform encryption (WDTW) for adaptive encryption of medical images. Firstly, a model based on convolutional neural network (CNN) is trained using the medical image data set and used for understanding image features. Once the image features are learned using the model, Grad-CAM heat maps are produced, which are used to generate region importance maps for selectively performing block-wise permutation and XOR operations. Further, to guarantee the lossless integrity of the process, a verification module is introduced based on weighted dynamic time warping. The experimental results indicate that our framework gives NPCR of 99.61%, Entropy of 7.99, and reduces processing latency by 35% when compared to the conventional full image AES encryption method. The encrypted outputs successfully passed all seven NIST SP 800-22 tests and also demonstrated excellent resistance to known plaintext attacks. The minimum entropy, maximum correlation, minimum NPCR and average UACI values were found to be 7.999956, 0.000997, 99.6036% and 33.4681% respectively.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68900-0.title: Nanorod formation, Hirshfeld surface analysis, and electrical properties of a Cu (II) coordination polymer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68900-0.abstract: A copper(II) coordination polymer, [Cu(μ-Cl)(μ-OCH3)(2-apy)]n·CH3OH, was reinvestigated to explore its nanostructural characteristics, intermolecular interactions, and electrical properties. Although the crystal structure has been reported previously, this study demonstrates the formation of well-defined anisotropic nanorods through a controlled solvothermal synthesis. Scanning electron microscopy revealed densely packed nanorods with diameters of approximately 30–50 nm and lengths of up to 2 μm. Powder X-ray diffraction confirmed phase purity and structural consistency between the bulk and nanocrystalline materials, with an estimated average crystallite size of approximately 23 nm. Hirshfeld surface analysis of the coordination polymer framework quantified the principal intermolecular contacts responsible for crystal packing, while electrical conductivity measurements revealed semiconducting behavior with conductivity values in the range of 10−8–10−6 S cm−1. The observed charge transport may be associated with π–π stacking interactions and metal–ligand charge-transfer pathways within the polymeric framework. These findings establish a relationship between crystal structure, nanoscale morphology, intermolecular interactions, and electrical properties, providing new insight into the functional characteristics of the Cu(II) coordination polymer.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67145-1.title: Analyzing the outcome of centripetal and coriolis acceleration on a nonlocal thermoelastic material using the modified Green-Lindsay hypothesis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67145-1.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the influence of rotation on a nonlocal thermoelastic material with temperature-dependent properties using the modified Green–Lindsay framework of generalized thermoelasticity. Exact analytical expressions for the displacement, stress, and temperature are obtained by employing the normal mode analysis without imposing simplifying assumptions on the field variables. Numerical computations are performed using MATLAB R2013a under appropriate boundary conditions. The results reveal that increasing the rotation parameter significantly alters the propagation and amplitude of thermoelastic waves, while the nonlocality parameter reduces the peak stress and temperature distributions by approximately 45% and 25%, respectively. Furthermore, variations in the empirical material coefficient produce noticeable changes in the displacement and stress responses, confirming its important role in the thermoelastic behavior of the medium. Compared with the corresponding reference model, the present temperature-dependent nonlocal formulation provides more realistic predictions of the coupled thermoelastic response, particularly in the presence of rotational effects. These findings are relevant to the design and analysis of advanced engineering materials used in aerospace structures, refractory components, and laser-assisted technologies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68441-6.title: Association between gestational diabetes mellitus and adverse pregnancy outcomes and effect modification by maternal age in a population based cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68441-6.abstract: Abstract Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a rising public health issue and comes with many negative pregnancy effects for both mothers and infants. Because there is an increasing pattern in advanced maternal age around the globe, it has become very important to know whether age changes the effect of GDM on pregnancy outcomes. This study aimed to look at the links between GDM and major maternal and neonatal complications in a large population-based cohort and see if maternal age modifies this relationship. This population-based cohort study was carried out using Sina electronic health records and what we found was after carefully applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria we had set, a total of 424,359 pregnant women made the cut. A diagnosis of GDM was made according to the strict criteria laid out by the International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (also known as the IADPSG ones) The study focused on various negative outcomes including Caesarean sections, premature births, low birth weights, babies being over-sized for their gestational age, admissions to the neonatal ICU and a range of hypertensive disorders. We plumped for logistic regression models to work out adjusted odds ratios (the fancy bit is that we tried to remove other possible factors that could have had an influence on the results) and 95% confidence intervals to see how reliable our findings were. To see whether the presence of GDM interacted with age of the mother we looked at two age groups < 35 years and ≥ 35 years. We did this by including a multiplicative interaction term in our analysis. Among the total cohort, 19,861 women (4.7%) had GDM.After full adjustment for sociodemographic, behavioral and clinical factors, GDM was associated with significantly higher odds of cesarean delivery (aOR 1.79, 95% CI 1.73−1.84; P < 0.001), preterm birth (aOR 1.76, 95% CI 1.66−1.86; P < 0.001), LBW (aOR 1.15, 95% CI 1.08−1.22; P < 0.001), macrosomia (aOR 1.75, 95% CI 1.66−1.85; P < 0.001), NICU admission (aOR 1.38, 95% CI 1.32−1.44; P < 0.001) and HDP (aOR 2.44, 95% CI 2.29−2.60; P < 0.001). In age stratified analyses, GDM remained associated with all adverse outcomes in both groups. A statistically significant interaction with maternal age was observed only for macrosomia (p-value for interaction term = 0.007), with a stronger association among women < 35 years (aOR 1.82, 95% CI 1.68−1.98) than among women ≥ 35 years (aOR 1.63, 95% CI 1.51–1.75). GDM was associated with higher risks of serious health problems for mothers and newborns in this large study. Younger mothers were more likely to have heavier babies as a result of GDM, but most associations were not modified by the mothers age. The study shows that GDM affects women of all ages. But it also indicates that fetal overgrowth has a tendency to occur in younger women with GDM.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63413-2.title: Clogging risk mapping of cemented paste pipeline transport using a knowledge guided transfer learning framework
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63413-2.abstract: Pipeline blockage is a critical reliability constraint in cemented paste backfill (CPB) transport. Existing machine learning studies mainly predict rheology, pressure drop, deposition velocity, or blockage diagnosis from relatively consistent input sets, but CPB clogging risk mapping often has to use sparse records, heterogeneous labels, and missing operating variables. This study proposes a knowledge guided transfer learning framework for screening transport failure related to clogging. The framework converts available slump and yield stress measurements into a unified flowability index (UFI), combines UFI with solids mass concentration to build an interpretable chart prior, and represents unreported inlet velocity and pipe diameter through latent process priors and Monte Carlo marginalization. Bootstrap samples with jitter provide a pseudo source dataset for pretraining, followed by fine tuning and evaluation on a compiled dataset of 52 records with six positives under the main label definition. The evidence is evaluated through repeated splits containing both classes, LOPO case level analysis, label sensitivity definitions, prior learning ablations, paired baseline comparisons, UFI uncertainty propagation, and process prior sensitivity tests. The resulting risk map integrates sparse field records with explicit prior information and shows plausible increases in screening score at higher solids concentration and poorer flowability, which provides a transparent tool for design screening, diagnostic scenario comparison, and selection of cases requiring closer hydraulic assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67309-z.title: Advanced hyperspectral snow and glacier classification using fully connected autoencoders
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67309-z.abstract: The accurate classification of snow and glacier surface features is essential for glacier monitoring, mass balance estimation, melt-runoff modeling, and climate impact assessment in high-mountain regions. Hyperspectral imagery provides rich spectral information that enables fine discrimination of materials with similar appearances, which multispectral data often cannot achieve due to broader bands. However, challenges such as high dimensionality, class imbalance, limited labeled data, and spectral similarity between transitional facies limit the effectiveness of traditional methods. This study applies a class-specific Fully Connected Deep Autoencoder (FCDAE) framework for pixel-wise classification of seven snow and glacier endmembers such as Clean Snow, Dirty Glacier Ice, Firn, Glacier Ice, Ice Mixed Debris, Waterbody, and Non-Snow using EO-1 Hyperion data from the North-Western Himalayas. The approach integrates field-collected spectral signatures with image-derived endmembers and trains independent Autoencoders per class based on reconstruction error. The proposed FCDAE achieved an overall accuracy of 97.47%, Kappa coefficient of 0.96, and F1-score of 0.97 on the held-out test set, outperforming traditional machine learning baselines (Random Forest (RF): 95.74%, Support Vector Machines (SVM): 88.79%). These results highlight the effectiveness of reconstruction-based deep learning for hyperspectral snow and glacier feature classification in data-scarce, spectrally complex Himalayan environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66042-x.title: Semi-automated object-based image analysis for peri-urban land use/cover classification using WorldView-3 imagery of Mankweng, South Africa
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66042-x.abstract: Abstract Peri-urban landscapes in semi-arid regions exhibit high spatial heterogeneity and fragmented land use/cover (LUC) patterns, challenging traditional classification methods. This study introduces a semi-automated, hybrid Object-Based Image Analysis (OBIA) framework for detailed LUC classification using WorldView-3 imagery of Mankweng, South Africa. The novelty of the approach lies in the sequential, order-dependent integration of statistical feature selection methods, specifically Coefficient of Variation (CV), Feature Space Optimization (FSO), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Otsu’s Multi-Thresholding, where each method resolves a limitation left by the previous step rather than being applied independently. These methods reduce the trial-and-error process in feature selection and rule-set development, enabling finer class separation. The Soil Adjusted Vegetation Index (SAVI) and New Built-up Extraction Index (NBEI), used as spectral indices, and Canny edge detection, used as an image derivative layer, were embedded as supplementary input layers to improve object segmentation across hierarchical levels. A four-level Hierarchical Classification Scheme (HCS) guided segmentation and classification, enabling the differentiation of 38 LUC subclasses, including roof types and diverse vegetation types. Applied to four peri-urban test sites within the study area, the method indirectly revealed settlement structures aligned with varying socio-economic and development stages. Compared to standard OBIA, the workflow improves classification efficiency while maintaining thematic detail without relying on extensive training data. The framework provides transferable rulesets adaptable to other fragmented, data-scarce peri-urban environments. It demonstrates that combining statistical measures with known OBIA-features, reduces user input, supporting a semi-automated approach that is helpful for spatial image analysis and ultimately policy-relevant urban planning.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69033-0.title: Mapping technological maturity and evolution in food innovation using patent analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69033-0.abstract: The advancement of food technology is driving transformative innovation across diverse areas, including biotechnology, smart packaging, and IoT-enabled food monitoring. This study presents a patent-based analysis of emerging trends, technological maturity, and industrial applications within the food sector. Drawing on a dataset of 86,888 patents, we applied K-Meansmeans clustering was applied to identify 15 distinct technological clusters, each representing a specialized domain. To assess development stages, we conducted S-curve lifecycle analysis, categorizing was then used to classify technologies into emergence, growth, maturity, or saturation phases. We also employed Porter’sPorter Value Chain frameworkanalysis was employed to map these technologies to various stages of food production, processing, and distribution. The analysis shows that clusters such as Mixing and Grinding Equipment and Food Packaging Coatings and Films are currently in their growth phase, offering strong potential for continued development. In contrast, IoT-Enabled Food Drying and Cooling Systems and Food Packaging Machinery have reached maturity, and eight clusters are identified as being in the saturation phase. The results emphasize how the convergence of digitalization, biotechnology, and sustainability imperatives is reshaping the technological landscape of food systems. These insights carry strategic relevance for industry leaders, policymakers, and researchers, informing decisions related to investment, regulation, and innovation management. The study contributes a structured, data-driven roadmap for understanding food technology evolution and guiding the alignment of commercialization strategies with sustainability goals.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66561-7.title: Single-step fabrication of a large-scale broadband sunlight absorber based on multiple directional grating structures
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66561-7.abstract: Broadband light absorbers have attracted great interest worldwide due to their high efficiency in converting light into heat. However, most absorbers show strong light absorption only in the visible spectrum, and their performance typically declines sharply in the near-infrared region. This work developed a large-scale broadband absorber by sputtering a gold (Au) layer onto a Morus alba L. leaf with submicron parallel grating structures. It was found that the grating structures in the Morus alba L. leaf consisted of many grating domains with different axes, making this grating structure distinct from those previously reported. The 10–20 nm thick Au-coated Morus alba L. leaf absorbed more than 88% of incident light in the wavelength range of 300–680 nm and maintained a high absorption efficiency (75%) in the wavelength range up to 2500 nm. Numerical simulations using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, including absorption spectra and electric-field calculations, suggest that Au-coated multidirectional grating structures, such as the naturally occurring anisotropic grating structures found on Morus alba L. leaves, can enhance light absorption compared with conventional uniaxial grating structures.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68619-y.title: Baseline-aware monthly PM10 prediction in Istanbul and Ankara: a city-level panel study comparing persistence, AR(1), and random forest models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68619-y.abstract: Monthly PM10 prediction was evaluated for Istanbul and Ankara with a 2020 − 2023 city-month panel combining air-quality, meteorological, and traffic-intensity variables. The calendar index comprised 96 city-months, of which 92 had observed PM10. Missing PM10 targets were excluded from scoring. The primary analysis required an observed one-month PM10 lag; a sensitivity analysis permitted linearly interpolated values only for lag construction. Persistence, city-specific AR(1), and Random Forest models were assessed in five expanding-window rolling-origin folds and a ten-month chronological holdout. Predictive R2 was calculated as 1 − SSE/SST. In pooled cross-validation, Random Forest achieved RMSE = 6.89 µg/m3, MAE = 5.53 µg/m3, and R2 = 0.50; corresponding values were 7.40, 5.68, and 0.43 for AR(1), and 8.65, 6.65, and 0.22 for persistence. In the final holdout, persistence achieved the lowest error (RMSE = 4.57 µg/m3; MAE = 3.71 µg/m3; R2 = 0.55), followed by Random Forest (5.87, 4.71, and 0.26) and AR(1) (6.20, 5.14, and 0.17). Block-bootstrap intervals supported an AR(1) RMSE reduction in pooled cross-validation; holdout differences from persistence included zero. Model ranking therefore varied between development and final holdout periods, with persistence providing the strongest holdout performance.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68781-3.title: First FISH-based physical mapping of Zea mays loci associated with haploid induction and anthocyanin biosynthesis reveals conserved chromosome loci and supports an integrated cytogenomics ideogram
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68781-3.abstract: Haploid induction is a key step to obtain Zea mays doubled-haploids, which are homozygous lines in breeding programs. Genes are related to haploid induction, as mtl and dmp, and to phenotypic screening based on anthocyanin biosynthesis, as r1-nj and b1. Despite their relevance, the cytogenetics mapping of these genes is unpublished. Using interphases and metaphases, we aimed to determine the number of detectable loci, map these genes and evaluate their potential as cytomarkers, providing a revised Z. mays ideogram. Locus-specific FISH signals were detected in interphase nuclei and metaphases from the haploid inducer ‘KHI’ and five distinct donor lines, indicating single loci under the resolution limits. mtl, b1 and dmp were, respectively, mapped on chromosome 1, 2 and 9 short arm, and r1-nj on chromosome 10 long arm. Conserved chromosome mapping was observed between ‘KHI’ and donor lines. An integrated ideogram was constructed by combining the physical positions of these loci with 18S rDNA and previously described chromosome-specific cytomarkers. For the first time, we mapped these genes using direct physical mapping in Z. mays. We integrate cytogenomics and other genomic data, contributing to a better understanding of the genome organization and supporting applications in Z. mays breeding programs.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69212-z.title: Frequency-dependent PI parameter optimization for enhanced terahertz near-field imaging quality
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69212-z.abstract: Abstract The trade-off between scanning speed and image quality constrains the application of terahertz near-field imaging in high-throughput scenarios. In this study, quantitative models were established to link the proportional (P) and integral (I) parameters to image quality—quantified by the Brisque score—at 0.4 Hz and 0.5 Hz using second-order polynomials (R 2 = 0.65 and 0.60). The optimal parameters were found to be frequency-dependent. At a scanning frequency of 0.4 Hz, the optimal proportional gain P and integral gain I were 560 and 575, respectively, yielding a minimum Brisque score of 35.70. At 0.5 Hz, the optimal values shifted to P = 100 and I = 225, with a corresponding minimum score of 41.11. With these optimized parameters at 0.5 Hz, the Brisque score decreased from 49.10 (obtained with conventional settings, P = 400, I = 300) to 41.11, representing a 16.3% relative improvement, while the scanning speed increased by 25%. This work offers a quantitative framework for PI parameter optimization in terahertz near-field imaging, enabling fast, high-quality imaging in biomedical and other applications. The frequency-dependent trends reported are based on experiments conducted at 0.4 Hz and 0.5 Hz, with supplementary validation at 0.3 Hz and 0.6 Hz.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67813-2.title: Trichoderma spp., Bacillus spp. and Pseudomonas spp. isolated from commercial products show biocontrol activity against soil-borne pathogens in soybean
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67813-2.abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the biocontrol potential of ten commercially available microbial soil additives and fungicides against major soil-borne pathogens ( Rhizoctonia solani , Fusarium oxysporum , Sclerotinia sclerotiorum and Diaporthe longicolla ) to identify immediate, market-ready solutions for farmers, in the case of soil additives without the delay of product registration. In vitro dual cultures demonstrated strain- and pathogen-dependent antagonistic activity, with Pseudomonas and Bacillus being less effective than the tested Trichoderma strains. Regarding bacterial antagonists, the production of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and lytic enzymes was confirmed in vitro, indicating potential mechanisms of antagonism. Compatibility tests on soybean plants demonstrated no negative effects on germination, overall growth, or nodule abundance in nearly all cases. In greenhouse bioassays, under high R. solani pressure (1.5%) microbial treatments did not significantly restore germination rate and seedling growth. However, T. harzianum T50 (Vitalin Trichoderma) and T. harzianum + P. fluorescens mixture (Trillus), significantly reduced hypocotyl lesion severity and increased the proportion of symptom-free seedlings. Overall, in planta efficacy was highly variable compared to the strong in vitro inhibition. Nevertheless, selected commercial strains show clear potential to mitigate severe disease symptoms under high R. solani pressure.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68700-6.title: Environmental DNA supports persistence of the mythical Japanese freshwater fish “Jindai Dojo” and its conspecificity with an Eastern Japanese relict species
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68700-6.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis provides a means of detecting cryptic and rare taxa and identifying their genetic lineages, even when they are no longer detected by conventional surveys. The freshwater dojo loach locally known as the “Jindai Dojo” was historically collected in Iga City, central Honshu, Japan, and morphological evidence has suggested that it is conspecific with Misgurnus sp. Type I, a cryptic relic species distributed in eastern Japan that is of high conservation concern. However, the “Jindai Dojo” has long been considered extinct, and neither its proposed taxonomic identity nor its persistence has been evaluated using genetic evidence. Therefore, we integrated a Misgurnus sp. Type I-specific eDNA assay with a phylogeographic framework and analyzed water samples collected from 33 sites in and around Iga City. Misgurnus sp. Type I eDNA was detected at six sites, including three sites within the historical range of the “Jindai Dojo” and three sites in nearby river basins with no previous collection records. Sequence analysis of the amplified mitochondrial DNA fragments showed that all detections belonged to subclade J of the Japan Sea-side clade of Misgurnus sp. Type I. These findings support the hypothesis that the “Jindai Dojo” is conspecific with Misgurnus sp. Type I and indicate that this lineage persists within its historical range and nearby river basins. Our study demonstrates the value of integrating species-specific eDNA assays with phylogeographic information to rediscover threatened lineages and clarify the taxonomic identities of organisms presumed to be extinct.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68899-4.title: Indirect comparison of prevalence, risk factors, and mortality in COVID 19 versus influenza associated pulmonary aspergillosis in critically ill adults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68899-4.abstract: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis is a severe complication of viral pneumonia in critically ill patients. COVID-19–associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA) and influenza-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (IAPA) are increasingly recognized as significant contributors to morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs). However, no study has systematically compared their prevalence, risk factor profiles, and attributable mortality within a single evidence synthesis. We therefore undertook an indirect comparative meta-analysis, in which CAPA and IAPA estimates were pooled separately and then contrasted indirectly, rather than compared head-to-head within the same patients. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to March 31, 2025. Eligible studies were observational cohort or case-control studies reporting on CAPA or IAPA in adult ICU patients. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using the Freeman–Tukey double arcsine transformation with DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models. Risk factors and attributable mortality were pooled as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). All-cause mortality was the only mortality outcome analysed and is referred to as such throughout. CAPA and IAPA were not compared at the individual-patient level; instead, separately pooled estimates were contrasted indirectly using tests for subgroup differences, and 95% prediction intervals, together with the between-study variance τ², were derived for all pooled estimates. The study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261365038) and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 and MOOSE guidelines. A total of 89 studies (68 CAPA, 21 IAPA) encompassing 19,482 critically ill patients were included. The pooled prevalence of CAPA in ICU patients was 10.2% (95% CI 8.1–12.6%; I² = 87%; τ² = 0.004; 95% prediction interval 3.7–19.6%), compared with 19.4% (95% CI 14.8–24.6%; I² = 83%; τ² = 0.004; 95% prediction interval 10.2–30.8%) for IAPA (p < 0.001). Pooled all-cause mortality was 51.2% (95% CI 44.8–57.5%; 95% prediction interval 31.3–70.9%) for CAPA and 51.8% (95% CI 43.1–60.4%; 95% prediction interval 36.6–66.9%) for IAPA (p = 0.92). Attributable mortality ORs were 2.65 (2.04–3.45) for CAPA and 2.44 (1.75–3.40) for IAPA (p = 0.68). The separately pooled prevalence of IAPA was nearly two-fold higher than that of CAPA in ICU patients, yet both conditions were associated with all-cause mortality exceeding 50%. These findings underscore the need for routine fungal surveillance protocols in patients with severe influenza and COVID-19. Because the comparison between CAPA and IAPA was indirect and based on observational studies, the reported associations should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66896-1.title: Non-intrusive identification and characterization of two-phase flow in horizontal pipes using broadband induced vibration
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66896-1.abstract: Gas–liquid two-phase flows in horizontal pipelines generate complex dynamic loads on the pipe wall due to the interaction between evolving flow structures and the pipe. These interactions often produce broadband vibration signatures whose physical origin remains poorly understood. This work proposes an experimental investigation on two-phase flow induced vibration in horizontal pipes. The relationship between characteristic flow structures and the resulting vibration response of the pipe is explored by the coupling between acoustic, elastic, and pressure waves. This is done using data from an experimental dataset using a test section equipped with accelerometers, piezoelectric pressure sensors, void fraction sensors and a high-speed camera with synchronized measurements under different air/water flow conditions. Signal processing techniques are used to investigate the main features of the induced vibration in the pipe in a broad frequency band. Subsequently, the pipe’s excitation mechanisms are investigated, including the effects from the flow structures and the bubble size distribution, and it is shown that they can be identified from vibration measurements external to the pipe. These findings provide new insight into the physical mechanisms governing broadband flow-induced vibration in multiphase pipelines. Their potential for vibration-based monitoring approaches is shown by the proposed identification and characterization method. It stands out for being non-intrusive/non-invasive, cost-effective, and with great potential for industrial applications, enabling more reliable monitoring and control of industrial two-phase flow systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68236-9.title: Vitamin D deficiency is associated with an increased risk of incident retinal vein occlusion in a propensity score-matched cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68236-9.abstract: Vitamin D deficiency (VDD) has been implicated in vascular dysfunction, but its relationship with incident retinal vein occlusion (RVO) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective propensity score–matched cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults aged ≥ 50 years with two serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D measurements recorded between 2010 and 2023 were classified as having VDD (< 20 ng/mL) or sufficient vitamin D status (≥ 30 ng/mL). The primary outcome was incident RVO over 12 years after a 2-year landmark period; secondary outcomes included central RVO, branch RVO, and all-cause blindness. After 1:1 matching, each cohort included 227,216 patients. VDD was associated with higher risks of incident RVO (hazard ratio [HR] 1.58, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.28–1.96; p < 0.001), central RVO (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.14–2.05), branch RVO (HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.24–2.21), and all-cause blindness (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.56–2.20). Estimates were comparable in the vitamin D insufficiency analysis and remained consistent across sensitivity and subgroup analyses. VDD was therefore associated with an elevated long-term risk of retinal vascular events, although causality cannot be inferred from this observational study.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68477-8.title: Deep generative models for enhanced vitreous OCT imaging
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68477-8.abstract: Abstract The aim of the work is to evaluate deep learning (DL) models for enhancing vitreous optical coherence tomography (OCT) image quality and potentially reducing acquisition time. Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (cDDPMs), Brownian Bridge Diffusion Models (BBDMs), U-Net, Pix2Pix, and Vector-Quantised Generative Adversarial Network (VQ-GAN) were used to generate high-quality spectral-domain (SD) vitreous OCT images. Inputs were SD ART10 images, and outputs were compared to pseudoART100 images obtained by averaging ten ART10 images per eye location. Model performance was assessed using image quality metrics and Visual Turing Tests, where ophthalmologists ranked generated images and evaluated anatomical fidelity. The best model’s performance was further tested within the manually segmented vitreous on newly acquired data. U-Net achieved the highest Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR: 30.230) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM: 0.820), followed by cDDPM. For Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), Pix2Pix (0.697) and cDDPM (0.753) performed best. In the first Visual Turing Test, cDDPM ranked highest (3.07); in the second (best-ranked model only), performed as exploratory analysis, cDDPM achieved a 32.9% fool rate and 85.7% anatomical preservation. On newly acquired data, cDDPM generated vitreous regions significantly more similar in SSIM to the ART100 reference than true ART1 or ART10 B-scans and achieved similar scores on whole images. Results reveal discrepancies between quantitative metrics and clinical evaluation, highlighting the need for combined assessment. Only SSIM was significantly positively correlated with clinical judgement. Overall, cDDPM showed potential for generating clinically meaningful vitreous OCT images. Dataset and code are made publicly available.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68654-9.title: Time-specific post-activation performance enhancement after drop jump and optimal-load jump squat in young elite rhythmic gymnasts
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68654-9.abstract: Abstract Background This study compared the acute effects of drop jump and jump squat with optimal power load on countermovement jump height at various rest intervals, and examined the relationships between strength level and the individual peak countermovement jump height. Eleven elite youth rhythmic gymnasts completed three randomized crossover sessions: one set of six drop jump repetitions, one set of six jump squat repetitions, and a control condition. Countermovement jump height was measured before, 30 s, 3 min, 6 min, and 9 min after each condition. Analyses included repeated-measures comparisons across time and baseline vs. each athlete’s individual peak; correlations tested relationships with relative back squat maximum strength. The two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance showed a condition × time interaction ( F (8, 80) = 3.685, p = 0.001, η 2 = 0.269) and a main effect of time ( F (4, 40) = 3.61, p = 0.013, η 2 = 0.265). Post hoc tests indicated that the jump squat condition significantly improved countermovement jump height at 3 min than at 6 min ( p = 0.015, d = 0.42). A greater improvement at 30 s was observed after drop jump than after jump squat ( p = 0.023, d = 0.49). No fixed post-conditioning time point showed a significant increase compared with baseline. However, individual peak analysis indicated higher CMJ height than baseline in both drop jump ( t = 4.068, p = 0.002, d = 0.42) and jump squat ( t = 2.844, p = 0.017, d = 0.35) conditions. No correlation ( r = – 0.404 to 0.05, p = 0.218 to 0.924) was found between maximum strength and post-intervention peak countermovement jump height. In early-adolescent rhythmic gymnasts, drop jump may offer an earlier, small enhancement of countermovement jump performance. Given the heterogeneity in time-to-peak, individualized timing rather than fixed windows is recommended for pre-performance routines.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66028-9.title: Single active antenna spatial modulation with transmit diversity of orders two and three
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66028-9.abstract: Conventional spatial modulation (SM) offers a low-complexity multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) transmission framework by activating a single transmit antenna per symbol interval, thereby eliminating inter-antenna synchronization requirement. However, SM is inherently unable to achieve transmit diversity. To address this limitation, this paper investigates the realization of higher order transmit diversity in SM systems where only one transmit antenna remains active at any given instance, while transmission is extended across two or three time slots. Specifically, we derive design criteria for second and third order transmit diversity in single active antenna SM systems when utilizing two or three time slots. Based on the obtained criteria, designs for more than one time slot are proposed that achieve higher diversity order for the maximum likelihood (ML) receiver. Unlike the conventional SM, the proposed schemes do not require the number of transmit antennas to be an integer power of two. Furthermore, we develop a low complexity coherent ML detector for the presented designs. The results show that the introduced schemes outperform previous approaches.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68122-4.title: Volatility-adaptive temporal learning framework using hybrid ARIMA-QuadGRU attention for multi-regime financial forecasting
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68122-4.abstract: Abstract Conventional financial market forecasting models are challenged by the non-stationarity, the existence of regime changes, the presence of structural breaks, and the phenomena of volatility clustering in financial markets. Linear approaches have only limited accuracy in terms of direction, as they do not capture the nonlinear behavior and long-term dependence. Given the above challenges, we introduce a multi-regime aware deep temporal forecasting framework, which combines the statistical modeling technique autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) with a novel quad-gated recurrent unit (QuadGRU) and multi-head attention (8 heads) in a hybrid way, depending on the volatility of the data. The framework is tested using 15 years of daily market price data from the NIFTY-50 index from Yahoo Finance API (2010–2025). Our pipeline systematically preprocesses the data by normalizing the data and masking filtering anomalies using the isolation forest (IsFo) algorithm with training-only fitting, and finally, we conduct regime-dependent feature engineering using technical indicators such as moving average, Relative Strength Index, and momentum oscillators. Gradient boosting machines (GBM) can be used for feature importance ranking and principal component analysis (PCA) for orthogonal representation of the features. The Granger causality test is used to define the temporal causality between predictors before sequence modeling. ARIMA is used for short-term linear component and QuadGRU is used for short-term nonlinear component of temporal dependency, the hybrid forecasting architecture is used. The novel QuadGRU gating mechanism offers adaptive memory regulation over the entire range of volatility, and multi-head attention delivers interpretable adaptive weighting of the historical information. The rolling window validation experiments with the baseline models ARIMA, LSTM and GRU improvements in MSE (0.012 ± 0.003 in normalized [0,1] scale, corresponding to 14,850 index-point MSE), RMSE (0.110 ± 0.014 normalized, corresponding to 121.8 index points), MAE (0.084 ± 0.011 normalized, corresponding to 93.1 index points), and directional accuracy (87.5 ± 2.1%), especially for time periods with high volatility. Error variance distribution analysis, bootstrap forecasting error distributions, volatility-conditioned error analysis, Granger causality validation, anomaly detection rate and false positive rate, as well as prediction stability metrics have been used for statistical validation of our performance improvements. The results justify the proposed regime switching hybrid approach as a scalable forecasting methodology for financial time-series accounting for the regime change in market conditions and provide investors, portfolio managers, and financial analysts with a practical tool to support their investment decisions in volatile markets.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68585-5.title: A cryptanalysis method for two classes of chaos-based image encryption algorithms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68585-5.abstract: Abstract Chaos-based image encryption has emerged as a compelling strategy for safeguarding highly correlated bulk data, particularly digital images. Most contemporary chaotic ciphers utilize chaotic systems for generating pseudo-random session keys within a conventional permutation–diffusion framework. To ensure high-speed performance, the diffusion layer frequently employs elementary operations such as bitwise XOR, modular arithmetic, and addition. Although various specific chaotic encryption schemes have been successfully compromised using standard cryptanalytic techniques-such as chosen-plaintext (CPA), chosen-ciphertext (CCA), and known-plaintext (KPA) attacks-there is a notable deficiency in generalized methods capable of analyzing entire classes of such algorithms. To address this gap, this paper proposes a generalized cryptanalysis framework for chaos-based image encryption. The encryption equations associated with the permutation-diffusion architecture are mathematically reduced to two generalized forms. A systematic and step-by-step cryptanalysis protocol is then established to evaluate these forms under the CPA, CCA, and KPA conditions. Experimental results confirm that the proposed methodology can fully reconstruct the encryption/decryption matrices and recover the equivalent diffusion/inverse diffusion keys. The success probability for these types of attacks is derived analytically. Moreover, the approach is highly feasible, exhibiting a modest computational complexity that is easily handled by modern hardware, thereby highlighting critical vulnerabilities in widespread chaotic encryption architectures.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68409-6.title: Multi-level inflammatory profiling reveals a cytokine signature associated with night-shift work exposure in female healthcare workers
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68409-6.abstract: Night-shift work is associated with circadian disruption and altered immune regulation, although the biological pathways underlying these interrelations remain incompletely characterized. A cross-sectional study of 243 female healthcare workers (147 night-shift workers, NSW; 96 day-shift workers, DSW) was conducted, to assess circulating cytokines (IL-6, IL-8, IL-18, TNF-α, IFN-γ), leukocyte-derived inflammatory indices (NLR, MLR, NMR, PLR, SII), and inflammatory network structure. NSW showed higher plasma cytokines, including TNF-α (7.76 vs. 6.51 pg/mL), IL-6 (1.72 vs. 1.40 pg/mL), IL-18 (204 vs. 172 pg/mL), IFN-γ (0.77 vs. 0.60 pg/mL), and IL-8 (3.88 vs. 3.55 pg/mL; all p < 0.05), with increased composite cytokine Z-score (0.95 vs. − 0.19, p < 0.0001). Leukocyte-derived inflammatory indices did not differ between groups. Multivariable analyses showed that the association between night-shift work and elevated cytokine levels remained directionally consistent after adjustment for age, BMI, menopausal status, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, and sleep quality, with IFN-γ showing a significant adjusted association. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering identified distinct cytokine patterns, including TNF-α–IL-8–IL-18 and IL-6–IFN-γ modules. Correlation analyses revealed differences in the coupling between cytokine and hematological inflammatory indices between NSW and DSW. Among long-term night-shift workers, higher IL-6, IL-18, and TNF-α levels suggested a duration-related association with inflammatory profiles. Overall, night-shift work was associated with a coordinated low-grade cytokine signature, supporting the potential role of circulating cytokine profiling as an exploratory indicator of biological perturbation related to circadian disruption. Future longitudinal studies are required to clarify temporal and causal relationships.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62549-5.title: Biomechanical exploration of cushioning and stability in auxetic lattice midsoles during jump landing
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62549-5.abstract: High-impact forces during jump landing pose a risk for lower limb injuries, highlighting the importance of shoe midsole cushioning, where the effectiveness of midsole hardness remains controversial. This study evaluated the biomechanical performance of three-dimensional auxetic lattice structure midsoles during jump landing, examining their cushioning mechanisms and stability. Four midsoles were tested: two auxetic lattices (A60 and A75), a non-auxetic structure (N90), and a traditional polyurethane (PU) midsole, using plantar pressure measurements (Pedar‑X system) and finite element simulations. Results showed that auxetic midsoles significantly improved overall performance, reducing peak plantar pressure and impact loading rate compared to non-auxetic designs. Specifically, A60 provided optimal forefoot pressure reduction, while A75 offered superior stability, with both enhancing pressure distribution uniformity through increased foot-shoe contact area. These findings demonstrate that auxetic lattice structures enhance jump landing cushioning in healthy young males. The angle-dependent performance trade-offs—forefoot pressure reduction for A60 and enhanced stability for A75—offer initial evidence for zoned midsole design concepts, warranting further sport-specific validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68091-8.title: Adaptive semantic structural fault localization at statement level using reinforcement learning
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68091-8.abstract: Software fault localization is critical for reducing debugging effort, still much of the current literature focuses on a single major source of evidence and limited to fine-grained localization scenarios. Spectrum-based techniques are very efficient in using test execution behavior, but they can often do poorly when failures propagate across structurally related statements or when lexical clues provided by bugs are present in both text and source-code artifacts related to a bug. To overcome this limitation, this research presents RLSFLoc, which is a reinforcement learning based semantic structural framework to fault localization at the statement level. The proposed framework is a combination of three evidence streams: execution-based suspiciousness through passing and failing tests, structural dependencies refinement based on program relations, and semantic relevance computed based on bug-related textual artifacts and program entities. Instead of using fixed weights to combine these signals, RLSFLoc uses a Proximal Policy Optimization-based adaptive fusion policy to learn context-sensitive weighting in various localization scenarios. The framework was evaluated on Defects4J v3.0.1 with 854 active bugs and statement-level localization setting. The experimental results indicated that RLSFLoc had a high performance compared to the compared methods with 48.7% Top-1 accuracy, an MRR of 0.612, a MAP of 0.587, and the lowest EXAM score of 0.184. Also, proposed approach minimized the inspection workload and ensured the performance (which was consistent across various projects) was not affected. Overall, the results indicate that a successful and practical approach to localizing software faults on a fine-grained level is to adaptively integrate the execution-based, structural and semantic evidence.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69053-w.title: Bidirectional association between MASLD and cardiovascular disease mediated by insulin resistance in middle-aged and older Chinese adults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69053-w.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) frequently coexist and share common pathophysiological mechanisms, but whether their association is bidirectional and whether insulin resistance mediates this link remain poorly defined. We conducted two complementary longitudinal analyses using data from five waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (2011–2020), a nationally representative cohort of Chinese adults aged 45 years and older. The analytic cohorts comprised 5,193 participants for the MASLD-to-CVD analysis and 3,342 participants for the CVD-to-MASLD analysis after exclusions. MASLD was defined using the lipid accumulation product index combined with cardiometabolic risk factors, and CVD was ascertained via self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models with three sequential adjustments were employed to evaluate the bidirectional associations. Mediation analyses were performed to quantify the mediating role of the triglyceride-glucose-waist circumference (TyG-WC) index and the triglyceride-glucose-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR) index, two composite surrogate markers of insulin resistance. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to test the robustness of the findings. Over a median follow-up of 9 years, baseline MASLD was associated with an increased risk of incident CVD after full adjustment (OR: 1.53, 95% CI: 1.32–1.78). Conversely, over a median follow-up of 4 years, baseline CVD was associated with an increased risk of incident MASLD (OR: 1.40, 95% CI: 1.09–1.79). TyG-WC and TyG-WHtR partially mediated the MASLD-to-CVD association, accounting for 46.15% and 42.16% of the total effect, respectively, whereas no significant mediation was observed in the reverse direction. Subgroup analyses revealed that marital status significantly modified the MASLD-to-CVD association (P for interaction = 0.040), while diabetes significantly modified the CVD-to-MASLD association (P for interaction = 0.025). Sensitivity analyses using alternative MASLD definitions and excluding events from different follow-up waves confirmed the robustness of the primary findings. MASLD and CVD exhibit a significant bidirectional association in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. TyG-WC and TyG-WHtR asymmetrically mediate only the MASLD-to-CVD direction, suggesting distinct pathophysiological mechanisms underlie each pathway. These findings highlight the importance of the cardiohepatic axis and support bidirectional screening and integrated management of both conditions, with particular attention to diabetic patients.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68827-6.title: Experimental and numerical investigation of frictional loss and empirical correlation in Taylor–Couette–Poiseuille flow for a high-speed PMSM with an H2O2-flooded gap
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68827-6.abstract: A high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) used in rocket propellant feed systems generates complex Taylor–Couette–Poiseuille (TCP) flow due to the H2O2-flooded gap and high rotational speeds, complicating the analysis of motor friction loss. To address this, a three-dimensional CFD model based on the RNG k–ε turbulence model with Enhanced Wall Treatment was established. The model was validated against drag method experiments on two prototypes (rotor diameters: 26.5 mm and 40 mm), achieving agreement within 7% across the full speed range. Systematic parametric simulations identified rotational speed as the dominant factor influencing friction loss, with a power-law relationship of Pf ∝ n2.85, and rotor-side surface roughness was found to be the most influential controllable design parameter (+ 26.6% over the studied Ra range). A dual-variable empirical correlation for the skin friction coefficient (Cf) was derived, incorporating both the rotational Reynolds number (Regap) and the axial Reynolds number (Reax). This correlation was validated to predict friction loss within 7% of experimental measurements across rotational speeds of 10,000–40,000 rpm and axial Reynolds numbers up to 5000. The sensitivity ranking and empirical correlation provide quantitative design guidance for reducing friction in high-speed liquid-filled PMSMs.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68672-7.title: Baseline premenstrual symptom severity is associated with pregnancy during Korean medicine infertility treatment: a cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68672-7.abstract: Infertility imposes a substantial burden, and simple, non-invasive baseline indicators may help characterize the probability of pregnancy during treatment. Premenstrual symptoms arise during the luteal phase and depend on ovulation, but their association with fertility has not been examined directly. This study examined whether baseline premenstrual symptom severity was associated with pregnancy during Korean medicine infertility treatment. This cohort analysis included 185 women undergoing a four-month Korean medicine infertility programme. Baseline premenstrual symptom severity was assessed across psychological, physical, and other MMP domains. Domain-specific logistic models reported both age-adjusted estimates and estimates adjusted for age, BMI, infertility duration, primary infertility, menstrual-cycle irregularity, PCOS, and prior IUI/IVF. Model performance was internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples and repeated 10-fold cross-validation. Higher baseline premenstrual symptom severity was associated with pregnancy. Pregnancy rates increased from 12.7% in the lowest psychological symptom quartile to 35.0% in the highest (unadjusted p for trend = 0.010). In fully adjusted models, the odds ratios per SD were 1.66 (95% CI 1.17–2.36, p = 0.005) for psychological symptoms, 1.51 (1.06–2.16, p = 0.023) for physical symptoms, and 1.43 (1.00–2.04, p = 0.049) for other symptoms. Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.66 (95% CI 0.59–0.74). These findings challenge the assumption that premenstrual symptoms impair fertility. We hypothesize that symptom severity may index ovulatory and luteal-phase activity, but ovulation, progesterone, and related hormones were not measured, so this interpretation remains unconfirmed. The results offer reassurance for symptomatic patients and point to the need for mechanistic studies that incorporate hormonal profiling.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66965-5.title: Exploring the anticancer potential of Albizia lebbeck: an integrated computational and in vitro study targeting oral cancer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66965-5.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) poses a significant global health issue, highlighting the need for new treatment options. This study assessed the anticancer effects of phytochemicals from Albizia lebbeck against oral cancer using a combination of in silico and in vitro methods. Network pharmacology revealed important targets related to oral cancer, and compounds such as alpha-gurjunene, β-sitosterol, indene, kaempferol, and quercetin-3-d-xyloside underwent evaluation through drug-likeness predictions, molecular docking, and 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations. The aqueous leaf extract of A. lebbeck was also tested for its antioxidant properties and cytotoxicity against KB cells using DPPH and MTT assays, using doxorubicin as the positive control.
