Speech recordings from 93 participants were collected under controlled conditions and evaluated using subject-independent validation. Supervised i-vector back ends achieved the strongest performance. The i-vector SVM system obtained the highest numerical accuracy of 96.3% and the strongest threshold-independent performance, with AUC-ROC of 0.987 and AUC-PR of 0.992, while the i-vector NN system showed closely comparable performance with a non-significant AUC-ROC difference from i-vector SVM. ECAPA-TDNN showed moderate class separability but did not outperform the i-vector systems. Demographic-only and speech-demographic fusion analyses indicated that sex, age, and body mass index carried predictive information but did not fully explain the best speech-based performance. These findings support speech-based OSA screening as a low-burden complementary approach, while emphasizing the need for larger, balanced, and externally validated cohorts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68454-1.title: Serum neutrophil elastase as a potential non-invasive biomarker for assessing hepatic fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B patients
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68454-1.abstract: The role of neutrophil elastase (NE) in liver fibrosis caused by chronic hepatitis B (CHB) has not been fully clarified. This study sought to measure serum NE concentrations in individuals with CHB and to determine whether NE could serve as a noninvasive indicator for assessing CHB-related hepatic fibrotic changes. The study enrolled 134 individuals with chronic hepatitis B and 50 healthy participants as controls. According to liver stiffness measurement (LSM) results, the CHB cohort was classified into groups with absent or mild fibrosis, significant fibrosis, and cirrhosis. Serum neutrophil elastase concentrations were determined using an ELISA assay. Correlation analyses were applied to examine variables related to serum NE in patients with CHB. In addition, binary logistic regression was used to assess determinants of significant liver fibrosis, while receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to determine the diagnostic performance of serum NE in predicting significant hepatic fibrosis. Serum NE was significantly higher in CHB patients than controls (P < 0.0001) and increased with fibrosis severity (P < 0.05). NE was positively correlated with LSM, liver enzymes, HBV DNA levels, APRI, and FIB-4 (all P < 0.05), and was an independent risk factor for significant hepatic fibrosis (P < 0.01). ROC analysis showed NE had moderate diagnostic value, outperforming APRI and FIB-4 in patients aged ≤ 50 years; combining NE with APRI/FIB-4 improved accuracy. Serum NE is elevated in CHB patients, correlates positively with the severity of hepatic fibrosis, and may serve as a promising non-invasive biomarker for CHB-related hepatic fibrosis, especially in younger patients.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67320-4.title: Lie symmetry analysis, soliton solutions, and bifurcation dynamics of ionic current model in intracellular environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67320-4.abstract: This study presents a unified analytical framework for investigating ionic currents along microtubules by integrating Lie symmetry analysis, exact soliton solutions, bifurcation dynamics, chaotic behavior, and conservation laws into a comprehensive mathematical model. The ionic current equation, which governs ion movement within intracellular environments, is systematically analyzed through Lie point symmetries, yielding an optimal system of generators that reduce the governing nonlinear partial differential equation to solvable ordinary differential equations via similarity transformations. A new extended direct algebraic method is employed to construct 37 distinct families of traveling wave solutions, encompassing dark, bright-dark, dark-bright, and combo-type solitons, each with specific biological relevance to microtubule electrophysiology. The qualitative dynamics of the system are rigorously examined through bifurcation analysis, revealing the dependence of equilibrium stability on the damping parameter $$\lambda $$, while the introduction of an external periodic perturbation uncovers quasi-periodic and chaotic regimes, quantitatively confirmed by the positive largest Lyapunov exponent ($$\lambda _{\max }=0.097$$). Sensitivity analysis demonstrates the system’s strong dependence on initial conditions, with numerical experiments clearly specifying the perturbation amplitudes used. Additionally, conservation laws are derived via the multiplier method, providing invariant quantities that govern the system’s dynamics. This integrated approach not only advances theoretical understanding of ionic transport mechanisms but also offers potential insights for investigating neurological disorders associated with abnormal ion flows and for designing bio-inspired nanodevices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63861-w.title: Monte Carlo simulations and characterization of hazardous substances detection using the SABAT neutron-based sensor integrated with an underwater drone
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63861-w.abstract: The aquatic environment contains numerous hazards, particularly those resulting from human activities, such as chemical and explosive remnants deposited on the seafloor. Detection and identification of these hazardous substances remains a major challenge due to limited accessibility and the risks associated with safe sampling and analysis. A promising alternative to commonly used methods is the use of neutrons, which enable non-invasive identification of substances using the neutron activation analysis technique. Additional separation based on the type of process by which the neutron interacts with matter through time measurement can increase the efficiency of material identification. Monte Carlo simulations in the Geant4 environment were performed by generating $$10^9$$ events for the SABAT detector mounted on a remotely operated vehicle, for five hazardous materials that may be found in the sea, such as: TNT, Mustard Gas, Clark1, Clark2, and Adamsite. The analysis of the generated energy spectra was performed by estimating the quality of a given characteristic line based on the Line Classifier parameter for identification using a dedicated spectral analysis program. Four characteristic lines with the highest intensity were selected as candidates for signal normalization: the annihilation line (0.511 MeV), the hydrogen line (2.223 MeV), the oxygen line (6.110 MeV), and the chlorine line (1.950 MeV). Water and hydrogen lines (2.223 MeV) were used as references for the material and the characteristic line, respectively. The annihilation line (0.511 MeV) proved to be at least twice as good (according to the line classifier) at identifying hazardous materials as the next-best lines, chlorine (0.79 and 1.17 MeV) and carbon (4.44 MeV). Additionally, time separation significantly improved only the quality of the oxygen (6.11 MeV) and chlorine (7.79 MeV) lines.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68130-4.title: Research on cutting parameter optimization for plunge-cutting of cyclo-palloid spiral bevel gears
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68130-4.abstract: Cyclo-Palloid spiral bevel gears hold significant application value in high-end equipment manufacturing due to their superior transmission smoothness and high load-bearing characteristics. However, traditional machining processes face technical bottlenecks such as pronounced cutting force fluctuations and low processing efficiency. This research systematically investigates kinematic modeling, cutting force formation mechanisms, finite element numerical simulation, and process parameter optimization for the plunge-cutting process, utilizing the YKV2250 fully CNC spiral bevel gear milling machine platform. By establishing a precise machining kinematic model, a cutting force prediction model was developed based on the instantaneous cutting area theory. The cutting force coefficients required by the theoretical model were calibrated through physical specimen-cutting tests. The ABAQUS finite element analysis platform was employed to reveal the mapping relationships between key cutting parameters (particularly feed rate) and cutting forces. Building upon this, a process parameter optimization method based on the constant cutting-area principle was proposed. Under the investigated finite element conditions, the proposed method reduced the cutting force fluctuation range by approximately 79.4%. Meanwhile, the required number of feed cycles was reduced from 272 to 185, corresponding to a reduction of 31.99%. These results indicate the potential of the proposed method to improve cutting force stability and machining efficiency.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67558-y.title: Effect of intermediate heat treatment on the properties of profiles used in the manufacture of slotted screens
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67558-y.abstract: Slotted screens are a group of products with demanding service requirements, in which durability, geometric accuracy, and the stability of performance characteristics depend largely on the quality of the working and support profiles. During manufacturing, profile rolling leads to strain hardening and microstructural changes that may impede further forming and affect the final properties of the product. This study investigates the effect of intermediate heat treatment carried out in a plasma furnace on the mechanical properties, microhardness, and microstructure of the 42Sbb working profile made of 1.4482 duplex steel and the Q55 support profile made of 1.4016 ferritic steel, both intended for the manufacture of slotted screens. The investigations were performed for three heat treatment temperature variants applied between profile rolling and sizing rolling. The process was evaluated using static tensile testing, microhardness measurements, optical and scanning electron microscopy, and X-ray diffraction residual-stress measurements. The results enabled the most favorable heat-treatment conditions within the investigated parameter range to be identified with respect to the material condition prior to sizing rolling and resistance welding.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61039-y.title: Influence factor of nasal airflow laterality in patients with obstructive sleep apnoea: an exploratory study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61039-y.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) and nasal ventilation laterality (NVL) may exhibit a bidirectional pathophysiological relationship. This study quantified the influence of OSA severity on NVL dynamics through synchronized split-channel airflow measurements and polysomnographic recordings in 65 patients. Analysis across three dimensions—NVL instability, skewness, and nasal cycle duration—revealed distinct pathological patterns: compared to primary snore and mild OSA patients, moderate-to-severe OSA patients demonstrated significantly reduced skewness, increased instability during sleep, and shortened nasal cycle duration. Sleep architecture, particularly the N3 stage, exerted a stabilizing effect on NVL patterns. Notably, the lateral position enhanced both skewness and stability, regardless of left and right nasal cycle dominance. These findings may indicate that autonomic dysfunction associated with OSA preferentially affects NVL regulation, whereas neuroregulatory capacity appears to remain intact during the consolidated deep sleep stage. Clinical trial registration: Clinical trial registered with www.chictr.org.cn. The distribution characteristics and influencing factors of left and right nasal and oral airflow in OSA patients (CTR2400088754).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67481-2.title: A drainage and gas recovery optimization method for maximizing natural energy utilization efficiency in shale gas wells
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67481-2.abstract: During the natural-energy production stage of shale gas wells without external energy supply, the utilization efficiency of formation energy directly determines a single well’s cumulative gas production and free-flowing life. Using the maximization of natural-energy utilization efficiency as the criterion, this paper establishes an integrated reservoir–wellbore–process energy model to determine the intervention timing and production allocation of the velocity string and foam drainage processes, and to predict the cumulative gas production and free-flowing life after optimization. The model couples three parts: on the reservoir side, based on Tan fractal theory, it accounts for matrix stress sensitivity, Knudsen diffusion, Klinkenberg slippage, and Langmuir adsorption–desorption; on the fracture side, it defines a non-uniform conductivity distribution function along the horizontal section, which agrees with field PLT measurements; on the wellbore side, it establishes a variable-mass-flow pressure-drop equation accounting for density variation. Application to Well W1 in the Sichuan Basin shows that the optimized scheme improves natural-energy utilization efficiency by reducing wellbore energy loss, thereby prolonging the effective production period and increasing cumulative gas production during the natural-energy production stage.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67954-4.title: A probabilistic long-term health risk assessment framework for wildfires: the case of California
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67954-4.abstract: The increased wildfire activity across the Western United States in recent decades has amplified the health risk from wildfire smoke. Existing risk assessment frameworks, however, remain at the conceptual level or target immediate and direct economic and health consequences. Here, we develop a probabilistic risk assessment (PRA) framework to estimate the health impacts of wildfires in California, integrating (1) wildfire probability, (2) fire spread, (3) emissions, (4) PM2.5 transport, and (5) long-term mortality from degraded air quality. The findings reveal that the frequency-mortality curve due to PM2.5 exposure from wildfires follows a power law distribution with exponent $$\beta =1.44$$, emphasizing the dominant influence of extreme wildfire events. Wildfires originating in the northwestern parts of California are found to be the most significant contributor to mortality from PM2.5 exposure, due to the high vegetation density as well as the dominant winds directing the emissions towards densely populated regions. Additionally, our results show that wildfire fatality risk is comparable to that of California earthquakes and significantly higher than the risk associated with nuclear energy generation in the state.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68557-9.title: Physicochemical design and in vitro biocompatibility of thermoresponsive PNIPAM nanogels as biomedical nanoplatforms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68557-9.abstract: Smart drug delivery systems have attracted considerable interest in nanomedicine because they enable controlled release of therapeutic agents. Among them, poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) nanogels are promising candidates owing to their thermoresponsive behavior. However, their biological safety must be thoroughly established before biomedical application. In this study, thermoresponsive PNIPAM nanogels were synthesized by precipitation polymerization and comprehensively characterized in terms of their physicochemical properties and in vitro biocompatibility. The nanogels exhibited a spherical and monodisperse morphology, a hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 138 nm, a lower critical solution temperature close to physiological temperature (32 °C), and a near-neutral surface charge (− 2.195 ± 0.285 mV). Biological evaluation demonstrated high hemocompatibility, with hemolysis remaining below 5% at all tested concentrations. Cell viability exceeded 90% in Caco-2, PK-15, and MRC-5 cells after 24 and 48 h of exposure, without significant alterations in metabolic activity, DNA content, or cell cycle distribution. No genotoxic effects were detected in the Allium cepa assay, while confocal microscopy suggests cellular internalization of the nanogels and their possible localization in lysosomes. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the synthesized PNIPAM nanogels combine suitable physicochemical characteristics with a favorable in vitro safety profile, supporting their potential as biocompatible platforms for controlled drug delivery and other nanomedicine applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68940-6.title: A hybrid framework of rock typing mechanism and data driven modeling for permeability prediction in heterogeneous carbonate rocks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68940-6.abstract: Accurate permeability prediction is essential for characterizing and efficiently developing heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs. Conventional core analysis is not only costly but also inherently limited in spatial representativeness. Purely data driven models, while capable of capturing complex nonlinear relationships between pore-structure descriptors and permeability, often suffer from limited generalizability and poor physical interpretability. To address these limitations, we proposed a hybrid permeability prediction framework that integrated the rock-typing guided physical constraints with data-driven learning. Based on the hydraulic rock-typing theory, we first developed a binary permeability–porosity model specifically adapted to carbonate lithologies. Four microstructural parameters extracted from cast thin sections, namely porosity, dominant pore size, perimeter-to-area ratio, and pore roundness, were then used as inputs to train different machine learning models under a nested cross-validation scheme comprising 10 outer folds and 5 inner folds for estimating the flow zone index (FZI) and discrete rock type (DRT). The predicted FZI/DRT was subsequently coupled with the rock-typing constrained permeability–porosity model to enable indirect, thin-section-scale permeability inference. Compared with the purely data driven models and DRT-based coupled models, the FZI-based coupled model achieves substantially improved performance, yielding the R2 values of 0.689 on the testing dataset. Particularly in the medium-permeability interval, it achieves the highest R2 (0.63) alongside the lowest RMSE (0.51), MAE (0.34), and mean residual (− 0.05) on the log-scale. These results demonstrate that mechanism-informed data fusion improves both the predictive accuracy and the model interpretability for heterogeneous carbonate samples, offering an alternative and cost-effective pathway for rapid reservoir evaluation using routine thin-section analysis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68941-5.title: Constructing and optimizing the ecological security pattern in the Sanjiang Plain based on ecosystem services and ecosystem health
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68941-5.abstract: In response to accelerating ecological degradation and land-use conflicts in Northeast China, this study constructs a comprehensive Ecological Security Pattern (ESP) for the Sanjiang Plain by integrating ecosystem services (ES) and ecosystem health (EH) indicators. We quantified six critical ES—including food production, carbon storage, soil retention, water yield, water purification, and habitat quality—using remote sensing and ecological models. Simultaneously, we assessed EH through indicators of ecosystem vigor (net primary productivity), organization (landscape metrics), and resilience (land-use-based recovery coefficients), combining them into an integrated ecological security index. Ecological sources were identified using natural breaks and minimum patch size thresholds, while resistance surfaces were derived from land use, topography, NDVI, and human disturbance factors. Circuit theory was employed to model ecological corridors, current density, pinch points, and barriers, delineating zones for prioritized restoration. Results show a spatial structure dominated by north-south corridors with cross-cutting east-west linkages. High-value ecological sources are concentrated in the eastern and southern margins, while central regions face severe connectivity fragmentation due to agricultural and urban expansion. Based on spatial overlap among corridors and ecological bottlenecks, we propose a four-tier zoning framework: ecological conservation priority zones, ecological restoration priority zones, ecological security control zones, and ecological function enhancement zones. This study offers a systematic, multi-scalar paradigm for regional ecological planning and provides actionable strategies for landscape sustainability in agro-wetland mosaics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68497-4.title: Research on the pose reconstruction method of soft mechanical arm based on fiber optic sensing
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68497-4.abstract: Soft robotic arms, due to their high flexibility and environmental adaptability, have shown broad application prospects in minimally invasive surgeries, precise operations, and special tasks. However, their continuous deformation characteristics pose challenges to pose perception and precise modeling. This paper proposes a pose reconstruction method for soft robotic arms based on fiber Bragg grating sensing and variable curvature modeling. A fiber sensing network capable of sensing combined stretching and bending deformations was constructed, and the distribution positions of the sensing network were optimized using the particle swarm optimization algorithm. Through numerical simulations and experiments, the results show that the proposed method has high reconstruction accuracy and significantly reduces the end position error. The research results provide effective technical support for the high-precision perception and closed-loop control of soft robotic arms.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68935-3.title: Resting state network energy abnormalities in Alzheimer’s disease mouse model and the reversal through central thalamic deep brain stimulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68935-3.abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) disrupts intrinsic brain activity, particularly within the Papez and cortico-thalamo-hippocampal circuits, contributing to cognitive decline. Despite extensive research, AD remains incurable, and effective therapies are limited. This study investigates how AD alters brain-state organization and whether central thalamic deep brain stimulation (CT-DBS) modulates these alterations. Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 26 wild-type mice (WT group), 26 AD mice without treatment (AD without CT-DBS group), and 26 AD mice receiving CT-DBS (AD with CT-DBS group). A maximum entropy model (MEM) was used to estimate energy values for each group across the 64 possible brain states defined by six brain regions: prefrontal cortex (PFC), caudate putamen (CPu), thalamus (THA), hypothalamus (HT), entorhinal cortex (EC), and hippocampus (Hipp). To characterize group-associated differences in brain-state organization, MEM-derived energy values were compared across corresponding brain-state configurations among the WT, AD without CT-DBS, and AD with CT-DBS groups. The AD without CT-DBS group showed differences in MEM-derived energy values across multiple single- and multi-regional state configurations, including the CPu, Hipp, THA, EC-Hipp, THA-HT, and HT-Hipp. These findings indicate altered organization of network configurations in AD. The AD with CT-DBS group showed energy values shifting toward WT-like patterns, suggesting a partial shift toward WT-like network organization following stimulation. CT-DBS was associated with a partial shift of AD-associated network configurations toward WT-like patterns within Papez and cortico-thalamo-hippocampal circuits, and energy-state analysis provides a quantitative framework for assessing circuit-level effects of neuromodulation in AD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69076-3.title: Interaction of water and supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO2) with rock and joints
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69076-3.abstract: Reservoir stimulation by hydraulic fracturing has become a superior technique by injecting high-pressure fluid into deep rock to initiate fractures, creating new fluid paths to improve oil and gas extraction. Water is the primary fluid used in hydraulic fracturing and has demonstrated advantages over the decades in enhancing reservoir permeability. While water is the most common fluid used in hydraulic fracturing, its use presents several significant limitations. Chief among them is the intense demand on local freshwater supplies, which can exacerbate water scarcity and compete with agricultural and municipal needs in arid regions. Furthermore, the flowback of contaminated water -containing dissolved salts, heavy metals, and naturally occurring radioactive materials -poses serious risks of soil and groundwater pollution if not properly managed. Finally, the disposal of this produced water through deep-well injection has been conclusively linked to induced seismicity, or human-caused earthquakes, creating geological instability. These limitations encourage the search for alternative fluids, such as supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO2). This paper employed a 2D fully coupled hydromechanical finite-discrete element method (FDEM) to study the performance of water and ScCO2 in intact and jointed rocks. Important factors, including flow rate, in-situ stress magnitude, and fluid viscosity, are assessed for both the fluid and the results, and the results are compared with respect to the fluid-driven fracture pattern and breakdown pressure. The results confirm the extraordinary performance of ScCO2 compared to water. ScCO2 penetrates easily into rock grains and joints, easily dilates them, and generates fracture branching and long fractures. Moreover, breakdown pressures are lower than those of water, making it a preferred alternative to enhance permeability with less fluid energy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67724-2.title: CAP-UNet: frequency-decoupled and geometry-aware attention for medical image segmentation across multiple imaging modalities
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67724-2.abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is frequently hampered by pervasive challenges such as severe visual camouflage, extreme scale variations, and highly irregular anatomical boundaries across diverse imaging modalities. To address these challenges, we propose CAP-UNet, a geometry-aware encoder-decoder framework evaluated across four independent single-modality medical image segmentation benchmarks. Specifically, we introduce a decoupled skip-connection pathway featuring a Camouflage-Decoupled Frequency Attention (CDFA) module, which leverages parallel spatial and frequency-domain transformations to explicitly enhance target structures while suppressing low-contrast background interference. This pathway is further refined by a Boundary-Aligned Multi-scale Masking (BAMM) module that dynamically aggregates hierarchical contextual features and improves boundary consistency. Furthermore, we design a Curvature & Recalibration Attention (CRA) module to replace conventional decoder convolutions. By jointly modeling local geometric deformation and channel-wise feature recalibration, the CRA module effectively adapts to irregular anatomical structures while reducing modality-specific imaging interference. Extensive experiments on four representative public datasets, including colonoscopy, dermoscopy, ultrasound, and panoramic X-ray images, demonstrate that CAP-UNet consistently achieves superior segmentation performance compared with recent CNN-based, Transformer-based, and hybrid methods. These results indicate that CAP-UNet provides a robust and effective segmentation framework across diverse single-modality clinical scenarios.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68248-5.title: Integrative transcriptomic profiling reveals convergent coding and non-coding signatures in pediatric bone marrow failure syndromes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68248-5.abstract: Pediatric bone marrow failure (BMF) comprises heterogeneous inherited and immune-mediated disorders, yet many cases remain genetically unclassified despite comprehensive genomic evaluation. To identify shared transcriptional features beyond protein-coding variants, we performed total RNA sequencing on bone marrow samples from pediatric patients with BMF (n=12) and controls (n=2). Based on whole-genome sequencing, patients were stratified into genetically defined BMF (g-BMF, n=4) and genetically undefined BMF (u-BMF, n=8). Comparative transcriptomic analyses revealed minimal differences in protein-coding genes and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) between g-BMF and u-BMF, indicating strong transcriptional concordance. Compared with controls, 55.2% of differentially expressed protein-coding genes were shared between g-BMF and u-BMF and were predominantly upregulated. Pathway enrichment analyses consistently identified immune activation and cellular stress-response pathways, suggesting a shared inflammatory transcriptional state across pediatric BMF irrespective of genetic classification. lncRNA profiling showed that 69.6% of differentially expressed lncRNAs were common to both BMF groups. ATP1A1-AS1, USP3-AS1, and SNHG32 were reproducibly overexpressed and validated by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Correlation-based pathway analyses associated ATP1A1-AS1 and USP3-AS1 with immune-related and biosynthetic programs, whereas SNHG32 showed a distinct co-expression pattern. Collectively, these findings suggest shared coding and non-coding transcriptomic patterns in pediatric BMF that appear largely independent of genetic classification within this cohort.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67854-7.title: Dynamic teaching quality assessment relying on real-time student posture recognition with YOLOv11_BWC
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67854-7.abstract: Traditional classroom teaching evaluations often rely on subjective feedback and post hoc academic metrics, which limits their objectivity and timeliness. To address these limitations, this study proposes YOLOv11_BWC, a real-time object detection framework for student behavior detection, classroom attention assessment, and teaching quality evaluation in intelligent education. YOLOv11_BWC integrates a BiFormer module to improve occlusion robustness in complex classroom scenes, a Wise-IoU v3 loss to enhance multi-scale localization, and a lightweight Shuffle Attention mechanism to improve computational efficiency. Using real classroom videos from 257 students, three posture-related behaviors, namely head-up, head-down, and sprawled posture, were annotated, augmented from 840 to 1,326 images, and used for model training and evaluation. On the classroom behavior dataset, YOLOv11_BWC achieved 0.9672 mAP@0.5, 0.7594 mAP@0.5:0.95, 0.931 recall, and 136 FPS, outperforming YOLO26, YOLOv8, YOLO11, RT-DETR, and YOLOv12 in the overall balance between detection accuracy and real-time performance. Additional Jetson Orin Nano testing and POCO/SCB-Dataset3 validation further supported its embedded deployment efficiency and cross-domain robustness. Heatmap visualizations verified more focused feature responses, and temporal analysis revealed an exploratory classroom attention pattern of high initial attention, mid-class decline, and final resurgence. The framework provides objective, non-invasive, and fine-grained behavioral evidence for instructional feedback and dynamic classroom quality assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65878-7.title: Diffusion tensor tractography of the corpus callosum in major depressive disorder: a case-control study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65878-7.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a common and disabling psychiatric disorder that has been associated with alterations in white-matter microstructure, including abnormalities of the corpus callosum. This study aimed to compare the brain tracts of the corpus callosum using diffusion tensor tractography in MDD patients and healthy individuals. This case-control study included 30 patients with MDD referred to the 5 Azar Hospital Psychiatric Center in Gorgan, Golestan, Iran, and 30 healthy controls with normal MRI findings and no history of psychiatric medication use. Fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) were assessed for the whole corpus callosum and its five anatomical subregions: the rostrum, genu, body, isthmus, and splenium. Group differences in corpus callosum diffusion measures were assessed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), with diagnostic group and sex entered as fixed factors and age and education included as covariates. After adjustment for age, sex, and education, whole corpus callosum fractional anisotropy (FA) was significantly lower in the MDD group than in controls (F(1, 55) = 13.15, p < 0.001, η² = 0.178). Regional analyses showed lower FA in the rostrum, genu, body, isthmus, and splenium, and these effects remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In contrast, no significant group differences were observed for whole or regional mean diffusivity MD (all p > 0.05). These findings support altered interhemispheric white matter integrity in MDD and suggest that FA may be more sensitive than mean diffusivity for detecting group-related microstructural differences in this sample.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67520-y.title: Curvature-controlled instability coupling in hypersonic three-dimensional boundary-layer transition
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67520-y.abstract: Abstract Boundary-layer transition on hypersonic lifting bodies is strongly affected by three-dimensional effects and surface curvature, which influence instability development and aerodynamic heating. However, the specific role of curvature in modulating transition behavior remains not fully characterized. This study investigates the effect of geometric curvature on transition mechanisms using a parameterized lifting-body configuration. Variations in concave and convex curvature are introduced to examine their influence on pressure distribution, boundary-layer structure, and instability interaction. Simulations are performed using an improved k–ω–γ transition model. Results show that curvature modifies the circumferential pressure gradient and boundary-layer thickness, leading to significant changes in dominant instability modes and transition patterns. Increasing concave curvature promotes the interaction between crossflow and streamwise instabilities, resulting in a shift from single- to double-cone transition structures. Changes in convex curvature produce non-monotonic variations in transition behavior, including switching between different dominant mechanisms and corresponding transition-front shapes. These results demonstrate that geometric curvature provides an effective means of controlling transition behavior and offers practical guidance for the aerodynamic design of hypersonic vehicles.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66836-z.title: Associations between early maladaptive schemas and other-directed interpersonal emotion regulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66836-z.abstract: Abstract Although early maladaptive schemas (EMSs) are known to affect self-focused emotion regulation and psychological symptoms, little is known about how they are associated with individuals’ emotional behaviors toward others. This study examined the associations between EMSs and other-directed interpersonal emotion regulation (IER). Four hundred Japanese adults (mean age = 40.1 years; 50% female) completed the Young Schema Questionnaire–Short Form and Interpersonal Emotion Regulation Scale. Structural equation modeling was used to examine pathways linking five higher-order EMS domains (i.e., Disconnection and Rejection, Impaired Autonomy and Performance, Other-Directedness, Overvigilance and Inhibition, and Impaired Limits) to three IER strategies (i.e., Positive Reappraisal Support, Emotional Expression Support, and Distraction Support). In the constrained model, Other-Directedness was positively associated with Positive Reappraisal Support and Distraction Support, whereas Overvigilance and Inhibition showed a marginal positive association with Emotional Expression Support. No statistically significant associations were observed for the other EMS domains in this model. However, the full hypothesized model showed a broader pattern of associations across EMS domains, indicating that conclusions regarding domain-specific associations depended in part on model specification. The findings provide evidence linking EMSs to other-directed IER. Interpersonal regulation tendencies appeared to be associated with relational dependency and overcontrol schemas in the constrained model; however, supplementary analyses suggested that the precise pattern of associations depended in part on model specification. These results suggest that EMSs may be relevant beyond self-focused emotion regulation in interpersonal contexts, with potential implications for interventions targeting relational emotion-regulation difficulties.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63410-5.title: Protective effects of cirsimaritin in mice model of alcohol-induced liver disease
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63410-5.abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is the result of excessive alcohol intake that manifests in the initial stage as fatty liver, resulting in alcoholic hepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. This study investigates the role of cirsimaritin on hepatic regeneration, protection, and fibrosis in in vivo and in vitro model of ALD. In vivo model of ALD was developed with chronic-plus-binge ethanol feeding in C57B6 mice. Cirsimaritin was administered intraperitoneally at a dose of 1 µg/g body weight. An in vitro model was established by treating HepG2 cells with 0.1% ethanol to mimic alcoholic liver injury and treated with different cirsimaritin concentrations (500 ng and 1000 ng/mL). mRNA and protein expression levels of fibrotic, regenerative, hepatoprotective, and inflammatory genes were analysed. The molecular docking of cirsimaritin was performed against important signalling molecules using AutoDock 4.2.2. Our results suggested that there is an increase in the ratio of AST/ALT levels predictive of ethanol induced liver damage in the ethanol-fed group, which was abrogated with cirsimaritin administration. Cirsimaritin treatment also reduced the severity of liver injury in the ALD in-vivo model by inhibiting hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and liver fibrosis. We observed liver regeneration in the ethanol-treated mice treated with cirsimaritin. Cirsimaritin showed significant binding affinities ranging from − 4.46 to − 8.46 kcal/mol, with the strongest interaction observed for ERK1 (− 8.46 kcal/mol) followed closely by p38 MAPK (− 8.39 kcal/mol). These results demonstrated that cirsimaritin showed preventive action by modulating the fibrotic, inflammatory, hepatoprotective and regenerative cascades.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68201-6.title: Regime shift in high arctic fjord signals the vulnerability of the Arctic’s Last Ice Area
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68201-6.abstract: A consequence of the collapse of Arctic ice shelves is the draining and loss of epishelf lakes and their unique ice-dependent ecosystems. Epishelf lakes are formed by meltwater runoff that is dammed behind an ice shelf resulting in a perennial layer of freshwater (or lake), floating directly on seawater. They were once widespread in the Arctic and have been present for thousands of years. After several drainage events across the region, the last epishelf lake in the Canadian Arctic was lost during the collapse of the Milne Ice Shelf in 2020. We assess the range of oceanographic, atmospheric, and cryospheric factors that likely contributed to this major calving event, and analyze an unprecedented record of epishelf lake drainage from an ice-tethered mooring. A decadal time series of water column profiles collected pre- and post-calving shows the abrupt one-way transition from a relatively stable freshwater ecosystem to a marine system. The loss of the Milne Fiord epishelf lake marks the extinction of a rare feature of a colder world and highlights the vulnerability of even the ‘Last Ice Area’ of Arctic sea ice to climate warming.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65661-8.title: Nutritional, immunomodulatory, and metabolic benefits of whey incorporated black wheat instant idli mix: in vivo rat model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65661-8.abstract: Abstract The valorization of dairy by-products and pigmented cereals offers a promising strategy for developing functional foods that address protein-energy malnutrition and metabolic disorders. The present study was conducted to assess the efficacy of black wheat idli along with different whey formulations (paneer whey and whey protein concentrate) on growth, nutrient utilisation, clinical chemistry, and viscera yield in rat models. Twenty-five, three-week-old Charles Foster rats were randomly assigned to five groups ( n = 5 each) and either on standard basal diet incorporated (@25%) with conventional idli , black wheat idli , and/or different whey formulations instant mix as follows: standard basal diet (G1), conventional control idli (G2), black wheat idli (G3), black wheat idli incorporated with paneer whey (G4), or black wheat idli incorporated with whey protein concentrate (G5). G5 demonstrated higher body weight gain and feed efficiency than G1, indicating improved nutrient utilisation. In contrast, the whey-incorporated groups (G4 and G5) exhibited enhanced organ health by reducing liver enzyme levels and blood urea levels, suggesting enhanced detoxification and renal function. Haematologically, the whey-incorporated groups exhibited significant increases in haemoglobin, erythrocyte count, and immune cell activity, and reduced platelet counts. Black wheat idli (G3) demonstrated notable metabolic benefits, particularly through the reduction in blood glucose levels. In addition, the G3 group may have contributed to maintaining stable creatinine levels, indicating potential protective effects on renal function. The metabolic parameter, particularly serum albumin and globulin levels, improved in the whey-incorporated groups, indicating enhanced protein utilisation and reduced anti-nutritional effects, which collectively contributed to improved digestibility and nutrient absorption. The combination of black wheat and bioactive whey peptides creates a sustainable functional food that supports the circular bioeconomy and strengthens public health food security systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67457-2.title: Low-loss dielectric radome with RFID for intelligent scanning in sub-THz, future autonomous defense systems
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67457-2.abstract: The proposed antenna design incorporates a 0.3 mm thick Roger substrate, a 0.00125 mm thick patch, and a cylindrical hollow radome made of Preperm HF H1500 material. The radome encloses a 1 × 11 linear array with a radius of 5.40 mm without affecting its radiation characteristics. The antenna operates at two distinct resonance frequencies: 129.5 GHz and 238.9 GHz. At 129.5 GHz, the antenna shows a minimum 3 dB beamwidth of 50°, indicating a broader directional focus. In comparison, at 238.9 GHz, the performance significantly improves, with a peak gain of 7.8 dBi, a wider minimum 3 dB beamwidth of 130°, and a sensitivity of -2 dB. The front-to-back ratio improves to 12 dB, demonstrating enhanced directional capability. Return loss characteristics for both resonances show excellent impedance matching, with values of 20.7 dB at 129.5 GHz and 18.43 dB at 238.9 GHz. The bandwidth percentages at both frequencies (0.93% at 129.5 GHz and 6.35% at 238.9 GHz) are within acceptable limits. The design effectively addresses critical challenges in sub-THz scanning, such as environmental interference and limited range, making it a versatile solution for logistics, healthcare, IoT, and industrial automation applications. Furthermore, the design supports automated beam steering and integration with AI-enhanced radar logic, making it a viable candidate for future autonomous defense systems and cyber-physical infrastructure with sub-THz communication and scanning.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69016-1.title: Exploring barriers to professional ethics in intrapartum care: a qualitative study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69016-1.abstract: Abstract Professional ethics is a cornerstone of quality midwifery care and is essential for safeguarding women’s rights, dignity, and well-being during childbirth. Intrapartum care settings are among the most ethically complex clinical environments, where midwifery students and practicing midwives frequently encounter challenges that may hinder ethical practice. Understanding these barriers is crucial for promoting ethical care and improving maternal health services. This study aimed to explore barriers to professional ethics in intrapartum care from the perspectives of midwifery students and midwives. This qualitative study was conducted using a conventional content analysis approach. Participants were selected through purposive sampling with maximum variation from hospitals affiliated with Isfahan University of Medical Sciences, Iran. Twenty-one participants, including 13 undergraduate midwifery students, 6 midwives, and two faculty members in midwifery and reproductive health, were recruited. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and analyzed according to the approach proposed by Graneheim and Lundman. Trustworthiness was established through credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability. Analysis of the interview data identified three overarching categories of barriers to professional ethics in intrapartum care: organizational, behavioral, and individual–psychological barriers. Organizational barriers included physician-centered dominance, hierarchical power relationships, limited educational opportunities, and resource shortages, which constrained professional autonomy and ethical decision-making. Behavioral barriers encompassed inappropriate interpersonal interactions, excessive workload, and overcrowded clinical environments that undermined motivation and hindered ethical practice. Individual–psychological barriers involved moral conflict, ethical uncertainty, occupational stress, and fear of challenging unethical practices, often leading to moral distress and feelings of guilt. These barriers interacted dynamically, shaping participants’ experiences of ethical practice within intrapartum care settings. Professional ethics in intrapartum care is influenced by a complex interplay of organizational, behavioral, and individual–psychological factors. Addressing these barriers requires supportive organizational policies, equitable interprofessional relationships, strengthened ethics education, and the creation of clinical learning environments that foster ethical competence and professional autonomy among midwifery students and midwives.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68484-9.title: Long-memory functional time series modeling for electricity spot price forecasting using fractionally integrated functional autoregression
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68484-9.abstract: Electricity spot prices are found to be highly long-range dependent, with hyperbolically decaying instead of geometrically decaying autocorrelation functions that challenge traditional functional time series models of forecasting. In existing hybrid forecasting frameworks, the stochastic intraday part is usually modeled by first-order Functional Autoregressive (FAR(1)) models, which have a short memory structure which fails to capture the temporal dependence adequately. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a new forecasting model, the Fractionally Integrated Functional Autoregressive model, FFAR(d), which introduces a long-memory dynamics into the functional autoregression. The proposed methodology is to estimate the fractional differencing parameter for the functional principal component scores retained after the reduction, to model the fractional differenced series by short memory autoregression and to obtain forecasts of the original series using fractional integration. The framework is easily incorporated into a generalized additive model (GAM)-based deseasonalization pipeline for exogenous variables, creating the extended FFARX(d) model. In order to make better-informed estimates more reliable, we detect and correct for the small-sample bias of the Geweke–Porter–Hudak estimator, develop asymptotic inference for memory parameters and use residual whiteness tests to evaluate model appropriateness. In extensive simulation studies using synthesized functional electricity prices with known long-memory properties, the local Whittle estimator proves to have a good ability to recover the fractional memory parameters, and FFAR(d), FFARX(d), consistently outperforms the conventional FAR(1), FARX(1), seasonal benchmark models as well as the functional neural-network approach over various forecasting horizons. Improvements are substantiated by evaluations based on the rolling-origin and the corresponding RMSE, MAE, MASE, sMAPE, prediction interval coverage and CRPS; statistically significant gains are corroborated by paired hypothesis tests. Robustness and efficiency of the proposed framework is further validated by additional sensitivity analyses, ablation experiments and computational complexity assessments. While the empirical validation is still hampered by the lack of a public long-term hourly electricity price database, the proposed FFAR(d) methodology gives a rigorous and practically feasible approach for modelling persistent dependence in functional time series and is a promising starting point for long-memory forecasting applications in the energy markets and other complex functional data environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68579-3.title: Triticale straw fiber reinforced concrete effect of fiber length on mechanical and thermal properties and microstructure
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68579-3.abstract: The incorporation of agricultural waste into cementitious composites represents a promising strategy for improving sustainability while enhancing selected engineering properties. This study investigates the influence of triticale straw fiber length (2.5, 5.0, and 7.5 cm) on the fresh, mechanical, durability, microstructural, and thermal properties of cement-based composites. Fresh concrete properties, flexural and compressive strength, water absorption, freeze–thaw resistance, microstructure, and thermal conductivity were evaluated after different curing periods. The results showed that increasing fiber length reduced workability but had no significant effect on fresh density. The highest flexural strength was achieved for composites reinforced with 7.5 cm fibers, reaching approximately 8.5 MPa after 21 days, representing an increase of about 18% compared with the reference mixture. Although compressive strength was reduced at early curing ages, prolonged curing improved the mechanical performance of all fiber-reinforced composites. Straw incorporation increased water absorption, with the greatest effect observed for mixtures containing 5.0 cm fibers, whereas specimens reinforced with 7.5 cm fibers exhibited comparatively better freeze–thaw stability. Microstructural observations confirmed that fiber geometry and fiber–matrix interaction governed pore development and crack-bridging mechanisms. Sensitivity-based thermal analysis indicated that straw fibers reduced the normalized thermal conductivity by approximately 5–7% for mixtures containing 2.5 and 5.0 cm fibers, while the reduction for 7.5 cm fibers was limited to approximately 1–2%. The results demonstrate that fiber length is a key parameter controlling the balance between mechanical performance, durability, and thermal efficiency of straw-modified cementitious composites.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67980-2.title: Correlation aware hierarchical split CIF architecture for multiple antenna GNSS and INS vehicle attitude determination
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67980-2.abstract: Vehicle attitude determination is essential for autonomous driving and intelligent transportation. Gyroscopes provide continuity, accelerometers constrain pitch and roll to gravity, and multi-antenna Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements provide an absolute reference. Because the processing branches share platform dynamics, state propagation and cross-sensor aiding information, the errors in their attitude estimates are not independent. Treating them as independent can double-count shared information and produce overconfident covariance estimates. We present a correlation-aware hierarchical architecture for multi-antenna GNSS/inertial navigation system (INS) attitude determination. Two local filters and a master filter integrate gyroscope-, accelerometer- and GNSS-derived attitudes using Split Covariance Intersection Filter (Split CIF), which bounds correlated information while preserving independent measurement information. Analysis showed weak raw inter-source correlations in pitch and roll (|r|≤ 0.19) but strong correlation between gyroscope- and antenna-derived heading errors (r = 0.975). Correlations between the local-filter outputs reached 0.805, 0.361 and 0.989 for pitch, roll and heading, respectively. On a suburban–urban route, with all methods evaluated on identical inputs against the post-processed SPAN-FSAS reference, the proposed architecture achieved pitch, roll and heading root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 0.192°, 0.447° and 0.105°, reducing the mean attitude RMSE by 60.9% relative to a centralized extended Kalman filter.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68595-3.title: A pan-matrix meta-analysis of microRNAs signature in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68595-3.abstract: Effective treatments for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are still lacking and early and precise diagnosis is crucial for the development of successful therapies. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for AD. This meta-analysis is the first to combine altered miRNA expression in AD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) across a wide range of biological matrices. A comprehensive search of PubMed and Embase was conducted to identify relevant studies investigating miRNA expression in AD or MCI patients compared to healthy controls (AD/HC and MCI/HC) in brain tissue, plasma, cerebrospinal fluid, blood, serum, and extracellular vesicles. Data on miRNA expression levels were extracted, and a meta-analysis was performed using P-value meta-analysis. Results obtained from 224 data sets across 151 independent studies were quantitatively assessed in 655 meta-analyses. In the AD/HC comparison, 356 miRNAs showed differential expression across these matrices. The MCI/HC comparison revealed 16 differentially expressed miRNAs. The most reproducible miRNA alterations converged on biological processes relevant to AD pathophysiology, including β-amyloid protein (Aβ) metabolism, tau pathology, neuroinflammation, apoptosis/cell death, immune response, lipid metabolism, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and adipogenesis. By preserving brain tissue, CSF, plasma, serum, whole blood, and extracellular vesicles as distinct matrices, this pan-matrix approach highlights both concordant and matrix-specific miRNA signatures that may inform future biomarker discovery and disease-stage characterization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68802-1.title: Procedural accuracy and efficiency of 3D versus conventional dental microscopes in novice users
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68802-1.abstract: Abstract This study compared procedural performance and user experience under three visualization conditions: unaided vision, dental operating microscope (DOM), and three-dimensional dental operating microscope (3D-DOM). In this experimental repeated-measures study, thirty dental students performed a targeting task in randomized order using a DOM (Flexion Advanced, CJ-Optik, Germany) and a 3D-DOM (Promise Vision 3D™, Seiler, USA) at 8× magnification, with a two-week washout period. Accuracy (0–4 scale), task time, and participant-reported outcomes (CVI-S = 0.90) were assessed. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA, Friedman test, Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons, and Spearman correlation ( p < 0.05). Magnification significantly improved procedural accuracy compared to unaided vision ( p < 0.001). The DOM achieved the highest accuracy (3.40 ± 0.30), required the longest task time (5.14 ± 1.70 min) and provided the greatest visual clarity, although 13.3% of participants reported image splitting with greater difficulty in spatial orientation. In contrast, the 3D-DOM demonstrated a more balanced performance between accuracy and efficiency (3.36 ± 0.20; 3.20 ± 0.81 min), with improved spatial orientation, reduced visual discomfort, and the most favorable ergonomic outcomes ( p < 0.05). These findings indicate that while DOM optimizes visual precision, 3D-DOM achieves a more favorable balance between efficiency, usability, and operator ergonomics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66144-6.title: Isolation, in vitro cytotoxicity and in silico analysis of methoxylated flavone derivatives from Kaempferia parviflora on breast cancer cell lines
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66144-6.abstract: Abstract Kaempferia parviflora ( K. parviflora ) is a plant native to Southeast Asia known to contain bioactive methoxylated flavone derivatives, including polymethoxyflavones (PMFs) and hydroxy-substituted methoxyflavones. This study aims to isolate and characterize methoxylated flavone derivatives from K. parviflora , evaluate their cytotoxic activity against breast cancer cell lines, and perform in silico analyses to predict their possible molecular interactions with selected cancer-related targets. PMFs were isolated from the optimized ethanolic extract of K. parviflora using gravitational column chromatography, followed by structural characterization via 1 H-NMR and 13 C-NMR spectroscopy. The cytotoxic activity of the isolated compounds was evaluated in vitro against hormone-dependent MCF-7 and hormone-independent MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines, as well as NIH/3T3 mouse fibroblast cells using an MTT cytotoxicity assay . In silico analyses included molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, drug-likeness evaluation, ADMET screening, and Pearson correlation analysis. Four PMFs and five hydroxy substituted methoxyflavones were successfully isolated and identified: 5-hydroxy-3,7-dimethoxyflavone (1), 5-hydroxy-7-methoxyflavone (2), 5-hydroxy-3,7,4′-trimethoxyflavone (3), 5-hydroxy-7,4′-dimethoxyflavone (4), 5-hydroxy-3,7,3′,4′-tetramethoxyflavone (5), 3,5,7-trimethoxyflavone (6), 5,7-dimethoxyflavone (7), 3,5,7,3′,4′-pentamethoxyflavone (8), and 5,7,4′-trimethoxyflavone (9). The isolated compounds exhibited selective cytotoxicity, with stronger IC₅₀ effects on MCF-7 cells than MDA-MB-231 cells after 72-h treatment. PMF 4 showed the strongest cytotoxic effect against MCF-7 cells, with an IC₅₀ value of 24.12 ± 0.45 µM. Toxicity screening of selected compounds on NIH-3T3 mouse fibroblast cells at their respective MCF-7 IC 50 concentrations showed 77.86–88.41% cell viability, suggesting comparatively lower toxicity under the tested in vitro conditions. PMF 4, 7, and 9 showed predicted binding interactions with selected protein targets, particularly Bcl-xL, Bcl-2, and mTOR. DFT analysis revealed stabilized PMFs and hydroxy-substituted methoxyflavones with favorable frontier molecular orbitals, indicating strong electron-accepting capabilities. Drug-likeness and ADMET screening provided preliminary predictions of pharmacokinetic and toxicity-related properties of both PMFs and its hydroxy-substituted derivatives. Pearson correlation analysis showed exploratory associations between cytotoxic activity (IC₅₀) and predicted binding scores for selected targets, including Bcl-xL (r = 0.831) and mTOR (r = 0.860). However, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary because metabolism, achievable systemic concentrations, tissue distribution, and protein-level target validation were not investigated.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68084-7.title: Integrating early-life gut microbiota with maternal–infant clinical data to classify mild head-circumference restriction at one month
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68084-7.abstract: Early head circumference is a vital proxy for neurodevelopment. We investigated whether the one-month gut microbiome adds predictive value to clinical factors for mild growth restriction. We analyzed anthropometry and stool 16S rRNA gene sequencing from 161 mother–infant dyads in a prospective cohort. Four machine-learning models classified mild restriction (Z-score < −1) using clinical and genus-level microbiome features, evaluated via repeated stratified cross-validation to assess incremental predictive value. Restricted infants (n = 14) exhibited lower microbial richness, reduced Bifidobacterium, and taxonomic shifts. Clinical-only LightGBM achieved the highest AUC overall (0.808), whereas microbiome-only models showed weaker discrimination (AUC 0.432–0.636). A small, non-significant AUC increase was observed for elastic-net logistic regression after microbiome features were added (0.761 → 0.802, 95% CI including zero). The other three learners showed lower combined-model AUCs, including a significant decrease for LightGBM; none of the four paired comparisons showed a statistically significant improvement. Mild head-circumference restriction at one month was associated with lower microbial richness and altered gut ecology. Although clinical anthropometry provided the strongest classification signal in this cohort, the concurrent richness association is biologically plausible and supports continued investigation of the early-life microbiome as a candidate contributor to growth restriction in larger, prospectively sampled cohorts.

doi:10.1175/bams-d-25-0009.1.title: Decision Calendars for Cold Regions Hydrological Forecasting: Collaboration in the Transboundary Yukon River Basin
doi:10.1175/bams-d-25-0009.1.abstract: Abstract Supporting decision making in hydrological forecasting depends on aligning scientific outputs with the practical needs and timelines of operational centers. This study documents the collaborative development of decision calendars with forecasters from the Alaska-Pacific River Forecast Center and the Yukon Government River Forecast Center in the transboundary, high-latitude Yukon River Basin, where hydrology is dominated by cold region processes. Decision calendars were used as a tool to synthesize shared operational knowledge, map recurring forecasting modes to an annual cycle, and identify critical timing for monitoring, forecasting and communication. The process highlighted challenges in transitioning research advances into operational practice, including reconciling data sources, communication needs, and the integration of new models and methods. Decision calendars inform the development of open-source forecasting workflows using the existing operational software framework. They also provide a basis for developing user-informed evaluation that assesses forecast performance based on operational needs. Findings emphasize the importance of knowledge sharing and structured methods to exchange information in developing actionable hydrological science. Lessons learned from the Yukon River Basin may be transferable to other regions seeking to improve forecast usability and uptake through structured collaboration between researchers and operational forecasters.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77349-8.title: Microenvironment-aware transcriptome reconstruction in spatial transcriptomics
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77349-8.abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics provides single-cell resolution, but remains limited to targeted gene panels, leaving much of the transcriptome and cellular-state variation unobserved. Existing approaches infer unmeasured genes primarily through transcriptional alignment between spatial and reference datasets, which effectively recover broad cell identities, but may not fully capture context-dependent variation within cell types. Here we show that local microenvironmental organization is associated with transcriptional variation beyond cell identity and provides complementary constraints for transcriptome reconstruction. Based on this observation, we present Emerge, a microenvironment-aware framework that integrates transcriptional identity with the local microenvironment to reconstruct transcriptome-scale expression. Across MERFISH and Xenium datasets spanning neural and tumor ecosystems, we show that Emerge improves recovery of structured transcriptional variation and reveals coordinated relationships among cellular states, ecological niches and intercellular communication programs that are only partially captured by targeted gene panels. Together, we demonstrate that Emerge extends transcriptome reconstruction from gene completion to context-aware recovery of cellular states. Current methods for spatial transcriptomics data analysis do not fully capture context-dependent variation within cell types. Here the authors present Emerge, which integrates cellular identity with tissue environments to reveal hidden cellular states and microenvironment-associated transcriptional programs.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69070-9.title: Quantification of intervertebral disc degeneration using dual-energy computed tomography collagen maps: a comparative study with MRI Pfirrmann grading
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69070-9.abstract: Abstract To determine the correlation between quantitative HU values derived from DECT collagen maps and the MRI-based Pfirrmann grade. We retrospectively reviewed IVDs in patients who underwent both spinal DECT and MRI within one year. CT scans were acquired using single-source DECT at 80 and 135-kVp with automatic exposure control. Three readers scored IVDs according to Pfirrmann et al. on T2-weighted MRI images. Quantitative evaluation involved placing three standardized regions of interest in each IVD in DECT-based cMaps; in corresponding 135-kVp DECT scans and MRI images. Mean density measurements of AF and NP were compared with PF-grades using linear mixed model analysis. We included 339 IVDs of 97 patients [mean age 59.1 years]; (53 women [mean age 63.5 years] and 44 men [mean age 53.8 years]). cMap analysis revealed a significant difference of AF and NP collagen and chondroitin density between PF-grade I and V(AF: MD = − 31.1HU (95% CI − 59.5 to − 2.7), p = 0.032;NP:MD = − 37.8HU (95% CI − 73.6 to − 2.0), p = 0.038). 135-kVp DECT showed no IVD density reduction corresponding to PF-grades. MRI showed significant reduction of signal intensities in AF and NP with increasing PF-grades. IVD collagen and chondroitin density declined with increasing PF-grade in DECT-based cMaps, suggesting DECT-based cMaps as an additional tool for IVD classification.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69230-x.title: Effect of gradient phase-change temperatures on the thermal performance of floor heating systems with encased phase-change materials
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69230-x.abstract: As phase-change materials (PCMs) are increasingly used in radiant floor heating systems (RFHS), their ability to reduce temperature fluctuations and improve energy efficiency has been widely demonstrated. However, existing studies have primarily focused on PCMs with a single phase-change temperature, whereas gradient PCMs in encased floor systems remain insufficiently investigated. This study proposes an optimized design that integrates gradient PCMs into a single–layer encased RFHS. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was used to systematically investigate the effects of the phase-change temperature ranges of the inner and outer PCM layers on the thermal behavior of the RFHS. The results reveal a distinct optimization mechanism between the two PCM layers: the outer PCM layer dominates the floor surface response speed and temperature uniformity by regulating heat transfer near the floor surface, whereas the inner PCM layer governs the heat release rate and high-temperature duration by controlling latent heat storage near the hot water pipe. By optimizing the phase-change temperature gradients of the inner and outer PCM layers, the optimal configuration was identified (outer layer: 32–37 ℃; inner layer: 38–43 ℃). Compared with the conventional singletemperature PCM design, the optimized system achieved a 9.89% increase in phase-change rate, a 24.32% extension in high-temperature duration, a 1.8% rise in average temperature, and a 5.41% reduction in temperature fluctuation. This study provides theoretical guidance and technical support for improving the thermal efficiency of encased RFHS and promoting their application in green buildings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69926-0.title: Oral midazolam combined with brief inhaled sevoflurane provides effective sedation for paediatric magnetic resonance imaging
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69926-0.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a non-invasive sedation protocol combining oral midazolam solution with a brief inhaled sevoflurane for outpatient pediatric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) examinations. Prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment. Outpatient pediatric MRI unit at Xi’an International Medical Center Hospital, China. 104 children aged 1–6 years, ASA physical status I-II, scheduled for single-site MRI under sedation. Patients were randomized to: (1) oral midazolam (0.82 mg/kg) plus inhaled sevoflurane (MS group, n = 35); (2) intranasal dexmedetomidine (3 µg/kg) plus inhaled sevoflurane (DS group, n = 34); (3) intranasal dexmedetomidine monotherapy with sham inhalation (DA group, n = 35). Sedation success rate (proportion achieving MRI scan without rescue sedation). Sedation success was 91.4% (32/35) in MS, 47.1% (16/34) in DS, and 25.7% (9/35) in DA groups. Rescue sedation was required in 8.6%, 52.9%, and 74.3% of cases, respectively. Patient behavior scores during premedication were significantly better in MS vs. DS or DA. Mask acceptance was higher in MS and DA vs. DS. Median time from premedication to scan start was 32, 27, and 30 min, respectively. Recovery time was comparable across groups. Adverse events were mild and infrequent, with hypoxemia (SpO₂ <95%) occurring in 8.6% (MS) and 5.9% (DS). No serious adverse events occurred. Oral midazolam combined with brief inhaled sevoflurane demonstrated higher sedation success rates compared with the intranasal dexmedetomidine-based regimens tested in this study for pediatric MRI.
