doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69143-9.title: Hypoadiponectinemia does not enhance anxiety-like behaviour in a lean PCOS-like mouse model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69143-9.abstract: Abstract Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by reproductive and metabolic disturbances and associated with higher prevalence of anxiety and depression. Circulating adiponectin, an insulin-sensitizing adipokine, is reduced in women with PCOS, and low adiponectin has been linked to impaired mental health, particularly in females. We investigated whether low serum adiponectin is associated with impaired mental health in women with PCOS and whether adiponectin deficiency exacerbates anxiety-like behaviour in a PCOS-like mouse model. Serum adiponectin was measured in women with (n = 179) and without PCOS (n = 228), stratified by body mass index (BMI). Health-related quality of life was assessed using the short form 36 (SF-36), generating physical and mental component scores. In parallel, the prenatal androgenization (PNA) PCOS-like mouse model was combined with adiponectin-deficient mice (APNhet) to assess the impact of reduced adiponectin on anxiety-like behaviour with and without prenatal androgen exposure. Women with PCOS had lower total and high molecular weight adiponectin levels compared with controls. Adiponectin positively correlated with mental component scores in women with BMI < 30, but not in those with obesity. Free testosterone was inversely correlated with adiponectin. In mice, PNA induced anxiety-like behaviour. However, despite a 65% reduction in serum adiponectin levels in APNhet PNA mice, adiponectin deficiency did not exacerbate the anxiety-like phenotype. Unlike women with PCOS, adult PNA mice were not hyperandrogenic. These findings suggest that adiponectin is associated with mental health in non-obese women, but reduced adiponectin alone does not induce anxiety-like behaviour in the absence of hyperandrogenism. Further studies in hyperandrogenic models are needed to clarify how adiponectin and hyperandrogenism interact across developmental stages and in different BMI groups to influence vulnerability to anxiety and depression in PCOS. Trial registration Clinical trial.gov: NCT01319162, NCT00484705, NCT01457209, and NCT00921492.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67839-6.title: Breast cancer diagnosis using a new evolutionary forest approach
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67839-6.abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and early, accurate diagnosis is crucial for improving patient outcomes. Traditional diagnostic methods often rely on manual feature selection, which can be biased and suboptimal, especially in high-dimensional medical datasets. To address this, we propose an automated feature selection framework based on an evolutionary algorithm integrated with a Random Forest classifier. Our method iteratively evolves compact, high-performing subsets of features by maximizing classification performance during cross-validation. This approach eliminates reliance on domain-specific heuristics and improves model generalization. Experimental results on the Wisconsin diagnostic breast cancer dataset demonstrate that the proposed evolutionary random forest model achieves high diagnostic performance, with an accuracy of 98.59%, balanced accuracy of 98.21%, precision of 98.07%, recall of 99.72%, F1-score of 98.89%, and AUC of 99.68% using 5-fold cross-validation. These findings confirm the effectiveness and practicality of the ERF method for breast cancer diagnosis. The approach is fully automated and adaptable to other structured medical classification tasks.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68413-w.title: Progressive coronary atherosclerosis in a porcine model of diabetes: a pilot study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68413-w.abstract: This pilot study characterizes the spectrum of atherosclerotic coronary artery pathologies in a porcine model of streptozotocin-induced diabetes, with a particular focus on the spontaneous progression of atherosclerotic plaques. Four pigs (designated P01 - P04) were subjected to an identical streptozotocin regimen to induce diabetes and studied using blood biochemistry, lipid profiling, coronary angiography, optical coherence tomography, and histological analysis of the coronary arteries to assess for the development of coronary atherosclerosis. All animals developed sustained hyperglycemia and dyslipidemia, with total cholesterol levels ranging from 14.9 to 36.7 mmol/L and low-density lipoprotein concentrations reaching up to 32 mmol/L. Notably, the study captured the full pathological continuum: from nearly no coronary abnormality in P01 and early atheromatous plaque formation in P02, to advanced atherosclerosis in P03, and finally, in P04, severe fibrofatty atheroma, and myocardial infarction. Unlike conventional animal myocardial infarction models that rely on interventional triggers, the infarction in P04 occurred spontaneously, demonstrating the spontaneous cascade of plaque development and acute plaque rupture with thrombosis. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using streptozotocin-treated pigs to model key stages of diabetic coronary artery disease.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67865-4.title: Polyphasic taxonomic characterization of two novel species from agricultural water, Chitinimonas fontana sp. nov., and Roseateles fontanus sp. nov.
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67865-4.abstract: Two Gram-stain-negative, rod-shaped, non-motile bacterial strains, designated BJYL2T and BJYL3T, were isolated from an agricultural pond and characterized using a polyphasic taxonomic approach. Phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences revealed that strain BJYL2T was affiliated with the genus Chitinimonas, whereas strain BJYL3T belonged to the genus Roseateles. Strain BJYL2T showed the highest 16 S rRNA gene sequence similarity to Chitinimonas prasina LY03T (97.73%), and strain BJYL3T showed the highest similarity to Roseateles saccharophilus DSM 654T (97.72%). Whole-genome comparisons based on average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) showed values below the accepted species delineation thresholds, supporting the proposal that the two strains represent novel species within their respective genera. Both strains grew optimally at 30 °C and were oxidase-positive and catalase-negative. The predominant respiratory quinone was Q-8, and the major polar lipids were phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylglycerol, and diphosphatidylglycerol. The genomic DNA G + C contents were 61.29 mol% for BJYL2T and 69.11 mol% for BJYL3T. Genome analysis revealed multiple carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) families potentially involved in chitin utilization. These genomic features suggest that both strains have substantial genetic potential to utilize chitin-derived substrates. This trait may be ecologically relevant given the abundance of chitin sources in agricultural freshwater environments. Strain BJYL2T contained three GH18 genes and one GH3 gene, whereas strain BJYL3T possessed four GH18 genes, one GH19 gene, and two GH3 genes. Both genomes also contained several CE4 and GH23 family genes, although the specific roles of these genes in chitin utilization require further functional validation. Domain architecture analysis further indicated that several chitinase-related proteins contain carbohydrate-binding modules and secretion-associated signal sequences, suggesting the potential for extracellular chitin degradation. Quantitative assays further confirmed detectable chitinase activity in both strains, with BJYL2T yielding 661.3 ± 44.2 and 561.1 ± 13.6 µg mL−1 GlcNAc after 3 and 5 days, respectively, and BJYL3T yielding 506.3 ± 45.7 and 66.3 ± 2.1 µg mL−1 at the corresponding time points, compared with 39.2 ± 0.4 and 41.4 ± 0.8 µg mL−1 for the negative control. Based on the phenotypic, chemotaxonomic, phylogenetic, and genomic evidence, strains BJYL2T and BJYL3T represent novel species within the genera Chitinimonas and Roseateles, respectively.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69925-1.title: MDP-YOLO: underwater object detection based on enhanced feature extraction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69925-1.abstract: Underwater object detection is crucial for ocean exploration and conservation but remains challenging because of poor illumination, a high proportion of small objects, weak textures, and large-scale variations in underwater images. To address these issues, we propose MDP-YOLO, an underwater detector built on the YOLO11 baseline. The method focuses on feature-extraction enhancement and detail-preserving upsampling. In the backbone, we design an MDRFF module to jointly aggregate directional spatial statistics, frequency cues, and global context. In the neck, we replace fixed interpolation with DySample, which predicts content-adaptive sampling offsets and uses bilinear grid sampling to preserve high-resolution details. In the detection head, we add a P2 branch and prune P5 to better match the small-object scale distribution. For box regression, MPDIoU replaces CIoU to strengthen corner-level geometric alignment and reduce boundary jitter. Experiments show that MDP-YOLO achieves mAP0.5 values of 85.3%, 84.9%, and 86.7% on URPC2020, URPC2021, and RUOD, outperforming YOLO11n by 2.9, 2.2, and 2.5% points, respectively. Overall, MDP-YOLO consistently improves detection accuracy while retaining a compact parameter count across different underwater datasets.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65274-1.title: Integrative transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis reveals variety-specific metabolic divergence and regulatory networks in fresh leaves of flue-cured tobacco
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65274-1.abstract: The metabolite composition of fresh tobacco leaves determines cured tobacco quality, yet the metabolic diversity among flue-cured tobacco varieties and its underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed integrated widely targeted metabolomics (UPLC-MS/MS) and transcriptomics (RNA-seq) on fresh leaves of five major flue-cured tobacco cultivars (YY87, ZC208, KRK26, NC55, and YY301) grown in Shandong, China, to decipher the molecular basis of inter-varietal metabolic variation. We identified 2,522 metabolites, revealing significant metabolic divergence among varieties, with the most pronounced differences between NC55 and YY87 (748 differentially accumulated metabolites). Multi-omics integration highlighted phenylpropanoid and flavonoid biosynthesis as the core pathways driving this differentiation. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and K-means clustering identified gene modules strongly associated with specific metabolic phenotypes. Gene–metabolite association analysis identified key associations: the peroxidase 43-like gene LOC107786050 showed a strong positive correlation with the aroma precursor sinapaldehyde, whereas the cytochrome P450 98A2-like gene LOC107797681 was primarily associated with the accumulation of the antioxidant taxifolin. This study reveals distinct metabolic and transcriptional patterns among representative flue-cured tobacco cultivars and identifies candidate gene–metabolite associations related to aroma-precursor and flavonoid antioxidant metabolism. These findings provide potential targets for future validation and may support quality-oriented improvement of flue-cured tobacco cultivars.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64786-0.title: The cultural adaptation and psychometric properties of the Employment Barrier Questionnaire (EBQ) for Arabic-speaking workers
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64786-0.abstract: Abstract This study aimed to assess the psychometric properties of the newly translated Arabic Employment Barrier Questionnaire (A-EBQ), designed to identify obstacles faced by People with Disabilities (PWDs) in securing and maintaining employment. A total of 90 participants aged 18–64 years (Med = 31.70, IQR = 16) were recruited, comprising 60 participants without hand injuries (HI) and 30 participants with HI. The EBQ was translated into Arabic utilizing a forward-backward translation method. Reliability was assessed through Cronbach’s alpha and the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC). Construct validity was evaluated by comparing responses between participants with and without HI, while concurrent validity was examined by correlating the A-EBQ with the Work Rehabilitation Questionnaire-A (WORQ-A). The A-EBQ demonstrated excellent reliability (Cronbach’s α = 0.847–0.950; ICC = 0.795–0.950). Construct validity was supported by significant group differences: participants with HI reported higher physical barriers and restrictions ( p < 0.001), while those without HI reported higher environmental, communication, and cognitive barriers ( p ≤ 0.05). The findings confirm that the A-EBQ is a reliable and valid instrument for assessing employment barriers within Arabic-speaking populations. It demonstrates strong ecological validity, capturing real-life challenges faced by individuals with HI. Physical barriers and restrictions emerged as the most prominent challenges for this group, often overshadowing other potential barriers.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67933-9.title: Essential oil nanoemulsions as a sustainable postharvest treatment to control anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum spp. in papaya and banana
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67933-9.abstract: Brazilian fruit production faces substantial postharvest losses due to anthracnose, creating demand for control strategies less dependent on synthetic fungicides. This study developed, characterized, and evaluated essential oil nanoemulsions of Cymbopogon flexuosus, Cymbopogon winterianus, and Zingiber officinale against Colletotrichum plurivorum and C. musae in papaya and banana. Formulations were prepared by low-energy emulsification and showed nanometric droplet sizes (95.9 to 171.3 nm) and low polydispersity indices (< 0.28); zeta potentials ranged from − 4.3 to -24.5 mV, consistent with steric stabilization typical of nonionic (polysorbate) systems. GC/MS identified geranial and neral in C. flexuosus, citronellal, geraniol and citronellol in C. winterianus, and ar-curcumene and α-zingiberene in Z. officinale as main constituents. In vitro, the C. winterianus and C. flexuosus nanoemulsions inhibited mycelial growth of both pathogens at low concentrations (0.03–0.07% essential oil). In fruit assays, the C. winterianus nanoemulsion reduced anthracnose severity in papaya in a concentration-dependent manner, with no visible lesion at 0.16% and no deterioration of the physicochemical parameters measured. Under the same conditions, the formulations did not reduce disease severity in banana, and the Z. officinale nanoemulsion showed low activity throughout. The C. winterianus nanoemulsion is therefore a potential candidate for postharvest control of papaya rather than a confirmed alternative to conventional fungicides, warranting further evaluation before broader application.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69248-1.title: Cerebral dopamine neurotrophic factor (CDNF) affects hippocampal neuroplasticity and fear memory in rats
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69248-1.abstract: The role of CDNF in modulating learning and memory remains largely unexplored. Here, hippocampal CDNF overexpression significantly accelerated extinction of contextual and cued fear memory in rats. Molecularly, overexpressed CDNF was retained in the ER and upregulated mRNA levels of Perk, Atf6, and spliced Xbp1, indicating activation of UPR-related signaling. Furthermore, CDNF overexpression increased CREB transcription and phosphorylation. Additionally, Cdnf mRNA levels correlated positively with transcript levels of Bdnf exons I, II, and IV. In primary hippocampal neurons, CDNF enhanced spontaneous bioelectrical activity, network burst complexity, and functional connectivity, as evidenced by multielectrode array and calcium imaging. These findings suggest that CDNF facilitates fear memory extinction, potentially through UPR-related signaling and enhanced neuronal excitability and network synchronization, positioning it as a potential regulator of hippocampal-dependent plasticity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68658-5.title: Optimizing solar panel placement using fuzzy OWA–BWM approach
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68658-5.abstract: Abstract Selecting reliable sites for solar-panel installation remains challenging because most GIS-based multi-criteria decision-making approaches produce a single deterministic suitability map and therefore do not reveal how site priorities change under different levels of risk acceptance. This study proposes a risk-sensitive GIS framework that integrates fuzzy spatial standardization, the Best–Worst Method (BWM), and Fuzzy Ordered Weighted Averaging (Fuzzy OWA) for solar-panel site selection across six climatically distinct regions. The methodological innovation lies in combining the relatively consistent and comparison-efficient criterion weighting of BWM with OWA aggregation applied to ordered BWM-weighted fuzzy values under multiple α-based decision scenarios. This integration generates conservative, intermediate, and risk-tolerant suitability maps and distinguishes spatially stable priority zones from locations that become suitable only when greater compensation among criteria is permitted. Nine climatic, topographic, geological, and accessibility criteria were evaluated. Solar radiation received the highest importance, but the final suitability patterns were also strongly influenced by road accessibility, slope aspect, distances to rivers and faults, and regional climatic conditions. Estimated annual electricity generation ranged from 5544.99 to 17,663.66 kWh/year under the BWM scenario and from 3377.24 to 17,704.66 kWh/year under the OWA–BWM scenarios for the assumed effective panel areas. These differences demonstrate that risk attitude can materially alter both the extent of suitable land and the associated energy-production potential. ROC validation produced AUC values of 0.721–0.971, indicating moderate to excellent discrimination among suitable and unsuitable locations, while also showing that model reliability varies among climatic regions. The framework therefore improves preliminary decision quality by supporting the identification of robust low-risk sites, prioritization of field verification, and comparison of alternative development scenarios. Potential environmental benefits, including reduced soil-surface exposure and improved soil-moisture retention, are interpreted as post-selection co-benefits.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69119-9.title: Real-time ambient neutron dosimetry based on TOF-derived response and G(E) convolution
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69119-9.abstract: Abstract Accurate assessment of the ambient dose equivalent, $$H^*(10)$$ , for both neutrons and gamma rays is essential for radiation protection in complex mixed-radiation fields within nuclear facilities and medical environments. Because neutrons exhibit high biological effectiveness and strong energy dependence, precise spectral characterization is crucial for reliable dosimetry. Conventional dosimetry approaches face limitations arising from trade-offs between real-time monitoring capability, spectral sensitivity, and practical deployability. We propose a spectrum-based dosimetry framework for the real-time, simultaneous estimation of $$H^*(10)$$ using an organic scintillation detector. A neutron-response matrix was obtained experimentally through time-of-flight measurements using a $$^{252}$$ Cf source and validated by a reference fission Watt spectrum. Based on the experimentally derived response, a spectrum-weighted function G(E) was obtained to directly convert the pulse-height spectra to $$H^*(10)$$ without a conventional unfolding procedure. G(E) was optimized using least-squares minimization and adaptive moment estimation optimization, achieving minimum mean absolute percentage errors at optimized orders of $$k_{\max }$$ =6 and $$k_{\max }$$ =22, respectively. The proposed framework demonstrated strong linearity over a dose-rate range of 3–150 $$ \upmu \mathrm{Sv/h}$$ , with relative errors within approximately 5 $$\%$$ and a minimum mean absolute percentage error of 2.36 $$\%$$ . These experimentally derived response functions enable stable real-time neutron-dose estimation, providing a practical alternative to simulation-dependent methods for radiation protection.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69762-2.title: Development and comparative analysis of predictive length of stay models using machine learning in Malaysian tertiary hospitals
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69762-2.abstract: Abstract Hospital length of stay (LOS) is a critical indicator of healthcare efficiency and resource allocation. While predictive modelling has escalated globally, there is a notable sparsity of literature utilising large-scale, real-world data from the Malaysian public health framework. This study developed and evaluated localised machine learning models to predict LOS in tertiary public hospitals in Kelantan, Malaysia, calibrated to regional operational dynamics. A retrospective cohort study was conducted utilising eight years of inpatient records (2017–2024). From an initial cohort of 849,593 admissions, a final analytic sample of 251,321 was retained after systematic exclusion and stratified sampling to handle heterogeneous records and to optimise the models against an extremely skewed LOS distribution. Predictive performance was compared across four supervised regression models: Decision Tree, Elastic Net, Random Forest, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBR). The XGBR model emerged as the superior architecture ( R 2 = 0.305, MAE = 5.075). SHAP analysis identified clinical discipline as the primary determinant, while systemic factors such as public holidays and night-shift admissions significantly influenced stay durations. This research establishes an empirical foundation for the digital transformation of hospital resource management in Malaysia, providing a pathway to optimise bed management and ensure healthcare sustainability.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60850-x.title: Green fabrication and biological evaluation of glucose-conjugated silver nanoparticles derived from Bixa orellana seeds
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60850-x.abstract: This study reports a novel bioencapsulation approach for the synthesis of glucose-stabilized silver nanoparticles (BOAg NPs) using Bixa orellana seed extract. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized using UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, FESEM, TEM, EDX, XRD, and DLS/zeta potential analysis. A characteristic surface plasmon resonance peak was observed at 432 nm, while microscopic analysis revealed predominantly spherical nanoparticles with an average size of 15–21 nm and good colloidal stability (− 14 mV). GC–MS analysis confirmed the presence of phytochemicals, including fatty acid derivatives, phenolic compounds, and terpenoid-related constituents, supporting their role as reducing and capping agents. Biological evaluation demonstrated strong antioxidant activity, significant dose-dependent α-amylase inhibition exceeding that of metformin, and notable antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus (MIC: 75–100 µg/mL). Molecular docking studies showed a favorable binding affinity (− 7.33 kcal/mol) with key catalytic residues (ASP197 and ASP300) of α-amylase, supporting the observed inhibitory activity. The study highlights the synergistic role of glucose and phytoconstituents in nanoparticle formation and stabilization. Overall, these findings provide mechanistic insight into nanoparticle-enzyme interactions and suggest the potential of BOAg NPs as multifunctional agents for therapeutic applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69679-w.title: Micro solid phase extraction of Pb (II) and Cu (II) from water and food samples with MWCNTs@Nb₂O₅@ NiMn2O4 nanocomposite
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69679-w.abstract: Exposure to heavy metals through activity and food consumption is a common cause of concern, and metals such as Pb (II) and Cu (II) have been shown to exhibit toxic effects even at low concentrations. In order to enhance the sensitivity and selectivity of heavy metal analyses, a novel MWCNTs@Nb2O5@NiMn2O4 nanocomposites was synthesized and utilised in micro solid-phase extraction (µ-SPE) technique. The robust, morphological, crystalline and surface properties of the synthesized adsorbent were obtained by a range of analytical techniques, including FT-IR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy), FE-SEM (Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy), XRD (X-ray Diffraction), and BET (Brunauer-Emmett-Teller) analyses. Optimization of analytical conditions was conducted at a pH of 8.0, and the proposed method was successfully applied for a various samples including, coffee, tobacco, corn kernels, wheat chickpeas, semolina, roasted chickpeas, and tap water and river water. The determination of metal ions was performed by flame atomic absorption spectroscopy (FAAS); the enrichment factor was set at 20. A preconcentration factor of 20 was achieved under the optimized experimental conditions. The LOQ values for Pb (II) and Cu (II) were determined to be 18.5 µg/kg and 17.4 µg/kg, respectively. The suggested method’s intra-day and inter-day precision, measured as RSD%, were 3.1% and 4.2%, respectively, indicating acceptable repeatability and intermediate accuracy. In the process of modifying the method, the incorporation of 8433 Corn Bran and TMDA 64.3 sections as reference materials was undertaken. The resulting alternatives demonstrate that the proposed µ-SPE method offers a sensitive, selective, and applicable analytical solution for the determination of Pb (II) and Cu (II) in food and water matrices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68380-2.title: Breathing-driven autonomic modulation preserves working memory performance under emotional distraction
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68380-2.abstract: Breathing-based interventions are widely used to regulate emotional distress, yet the biobehavioral nature of this effect has not been fully clarified. Here, we conceptualized breathing not as a therapeutic practice but as an adaptive behavioral response to acute mental stress and examined the immediate effects of different breathing strategies on psychological and physiological functioning. Healthy female participants (n = 54) performed working memory tasks in the presence of emotional distractors with three breathing strategies: involuntary breathing, volitional slow–deep breathing, and volitional fast–shallow breathing. Working memory performance was subsequently decomposed into latent decision processes by fitting a diffusion decision model. During volitional slow–deep breathing, improvements in working memory under emotional distraction temporally followed autonomic changes, suggesting an association between breathing-evoked parasympathetic dominance and emotional regulation. Within the involuntary breathing condition, participants who spontaneously slowed their breathing under emotional distraction exhibited comparable cardiovagal enhancement and preserved working memory performance, consistent with an endogenous regulatory response. Volitional slow–deep breathing supported both decision and non-decision processes, whereas volitional fast–shallow breathing disrupted decision processes while accelerating non-decision speed. This pattern reflected a speed-prioritized trade-off, alongside elevated sympathetic arousal during volitional fast-shallow breathing.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70161-w.title: Anti-leishmanial and immunomodulatory effects of harmaline against Leishmania tropica through molecular docking, gene expression profiling and oxidative stress modulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70161-w.abstract: Cutaneous leishmaniasis continues to represent a significant health concern in many endemic areas, largely due to the limitations of currently available therapies, including adverse effects, reduced responsiveness, and the growing emergence of drug-resistant parasites. The present investigation explored the antileishmanial potential of harmaline (HAR) against Leishmania tropica through a combination of experimental and computational approaches. Parasite susceptibility was examined in both promastigote and intracellular amastigote stages using MTT-based viability assessment and microscopic enumeration of Giemsa-stained infected macrophages, respectively. The safety profile of HAR was evaluated in THP-1-derived macrophages to calculate IC50, CC50, and selectivity index values. In addition, transcriptional changes in apoptosis-associated markers (Bax and Bcl-2), cytokines related to Th1/Th2 immune responses (IFN-γ, IL-12, TNF-α, IL-10, and TGF-β), and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) were quantified by real-time PCR. Reactive oxygen species generation, nitric oxide release, and antioxidant enzyme activities were also determined, while apoptotic alterations were confirmed using Annexin V/PI staining and flow cytometric analysis. Computational docking studies were conducted to evaluate the binding behavior of HAR toward iNOS and selected apoptosis-regulating proteins. Harmaline reduced parasite viability in both developmental stages in a concentration-dependent manner and promoted apoptotic responses, as reflected by an elevated Bax/Bcl-2 ratio and increased Annexin V-positive populations. Exposure to HAR further enhanced ROS and NO production while diminishing SOD and CAT activities, suggesting a shift toward a pro-oxidative cellular environment. Moreover, treatment favored a protective immune profile characterized by increased expression of IFN-γ, IL-12, and TNF-α together with suppression of IL-10 and TGF-β. Docking results supported the possibility of biologically relevant interactions between harmaline and proteins involved in nitric oxide synthesis and apoptosis regulation. Collectively, these findings indicate that harmaline exerts both antiparasitic and immunoregulatory effects and may serve as a promising candidate for further in vivo evaluation as an adjunctive approach for cutaneous leishmaniasis management.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68995-5.title: Evaluating walkability and vitality in cold-region historic districts of China via street view semantics and SHAP
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68995-5.abstract: As historic districts undergo sustainable urban regeneration, enhancing walkability is important for supporting local vitality. However, conventional walkability evaluation frameworks often emphasize openness and may not fully account for the climate-adaptive characteristics of compact spatial configurations in severe cold regions. Moreover, traditional linear models may overlook nonlinear and threshold-like relationships between micro-scale built environments and population vitality. To address these gaps, this study developed an integrated framework combining Street View Imagery, points of interest (POIs), and Location-Based Services (LBS) thermal data to evaluate two typical historic districts, Buzili and Dajingmen, in Zhangjiakou, China. DeepLabV3 + semantic segmentation and K-Means clustering were used to characterize street-view environments and identify spatial patterns, while Random Forest regression coupled with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was employed to examine nonlinear associations between built-environment characteristics and population vitality. The prediction model achieved an $$\:{R}^{2}$$ of 0.736, with an RMSE of 4.22 and an MAE of 2.94. Global SHAP analysis identified POI Density (mean absolute SHAP = 3.0496) and Functional Mix (2.1150) as the dominant predictors, followed by Walkable Space Ratio (0.9645) and Green View Index (0.6504). The POI-density relationship exhibited a reproducible nonlinear transition around the standardized range of approximately 0.067–0.083, whereas GVI showed a robust J-shaped response pattern across bootstrap models, but with substantial uncertainty in the exact turning-point location. Walkable Space Ratio showed a predominantly negative nonlinear association with population vitality within the observed study area. These findings suggest that openness-oriented walkability criteria may require climate- and context-specific reconsideration in cold-region historic districts, where compact spatial configurations may be compatible with pedestrian vitality. However, because the LBS observations were collected during the National Day period and no direct winter microclimatic measurements were conducted, the proposed mechanisms should be interpreted as associations rather than direct evidence of thermal adaptation. The findings provide context-specific empirical evidence for differentiated historic-district renewal and highlight the need for multi-season and multi-site validation before these transition ranges can be generalized as planning standards.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68555-x.title: Comparative analysis of proton collision effects in silicon on insulator MOSFETs using steady-state and transient responses
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68555-x.abstract: Proton irradiation degrades MOSFETs through multiple, spatially distinct mechanisms, yet separating the dominant damage sites remains challenging. This work presents a region-resolved electrical study of proton-irradiated partially depleted silicon-on-insulator (PDSOI) nMOSFETs, focusing on degradation at the Si/SiO2 interface states, body- source/drain junctions, and the gate insulator (GI). Devices were irradiated with 15 and 100 MeV protons at fluences of 1012 and 1013 p/cm², corresponding to estimated total ionizing doses of approximately 0.43 and 4.3 Mrad at 15 MeV and 0.10 and 1.0 Mrad at 100 MeV, respectively, and were characterized using electrical measurements. In the transfer characteristics, increased subthreshold swing and mobility degradation, together with a positive threshold-voltage shift and enhanced hysteresis, indicate substantial trap generation. Interface trap density extracted from the subthreshold region increases systematically across the tested combinations of proton energy and fluence, enabling quantitative tracking of interface damage. Importantly, the kink behavior in output characteristics is strongly suppressed after irradiation, consistent with reduced floating-body dynamics. Junction analysis–via parasitic diode I-V and laser-assisted body-current transients–reveals increased SRH recombination, reduced carrier lifetime, and elevated defect density in the depletion region. GI degradation is further supported by prolonged current transients under on-state bias, indicative of slow oxide-trap filling. Across the tested conditions, 15 MeV protons induce stronger electrical degradation than 100 MeV, consistent with their higher linear energy transfer (LET) and more effective energy deposition within the active device regions. These findings provide a measurement-based comparative picture of proton-induced degradation in PDSOI MOSFETs under representative proton energy conditions (15 and 100 MeV), offering qualitative physical insights into radiation-induced degradation pathways in SOI devices.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67051-6.title: Hybrid intensity normalization and translation network for structure-preserving intensity normalization in medical imaging
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67051-6.abstract: Intensity generalization among the training and test images of one modality from different vendors is the key for better performance of deep learning models. During inference, deep learning classifiers trained on chest X-rays from one scanner often fail when applied to images from a different scanner due to contrast variations. With Shenzhen–Montgomery tuberculosis benchmark, the drop can be as large as 0.95 to 0.73 in AUC. We present HINT-Net, a single-generator framework for unpaired, multi-domain intensity normalization of medical images. The architecture builds on a U-Net backbone and introduces two mechanisms: (i) Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) layers that conditions every encoder and decoder stage on a target-domain vector so that one model can serve any number of domains without retraining and (ii) an Additive Spatial Gate (ASG) at the bottleneck that learns a pixel-level intensity correction map to suppress scanner-specific artifacts while leaving anatomy intact. Training combines a hybrid loss of adversarial, Patch-based Noise Contrastive Estimation (PatchNCE), Structural similarity Index (SSIM), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and gradient terms. On paired synthetic intensity domains from NIH ChestX-ray14, HINT-Net reaches SSIM above 0.98, LPIPS below 0.008, and Peak Signal-to-noise Ratio (PSNR) above 34 dB-outperforming CycleGAN by 3.3% in SSIM with 86% lower LPIPS. On the unpaired Shenzhen–Montgomery benchmark it achieves SSIM of 0.78 (versus 0.74 for CycleGAN) and raises area under the curve of tuberculosis detection from 0.64 to 0.91 with AlexNet and from 0.78 to 0.97 with ResNet-18.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69719-5.title: Integrated transcriptomic and network-based analysis identifies miR-3187-3p–SGK2 as a candidate co-dysregulated molecular pair in breast cancer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69719-5.abstract: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy underpinned by complex genomic and transcriptomic alterations. Integrative analysis of large-scale transcriptomic data offers a powerful strategy for identifying robust molecular signatures associated with disease development and progression. This study aimed to identify and validate candidate molecular biomarkers in breast cancer through integrated transcriptomic and network-based approaches. Four breast cancer microarray datasets comprising 321 tissue samples (271 tumours and 50 normal breast tissues) were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database and subjected to integrative analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed using the limma package, followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), protein–protein interaction (PPI) network construction, functional enrichment analysis, and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network modeling. Candidate biomarkers were subsequently evaluated in independent public datasets and experimentally validated by RT-qPCR in 23 breast cancer and 14 normal breast tissue specimens. A total of 7,547 genes were analyzed across the integrated dataset. Applying predefined significance thresholds (|log2FC|>1.5; adjusted p < 0.05), 218 differentially expressed genes were identified, comprising 63 upregulated and 155 downregulated genes. Convergence analysis of WGCNA and differential expression results yielded 150 candidate genes for downstream investigation. PPI network topology analysis identified IGF1, IGFBP6, and CAV1 as hub genes, while pathway enrichment analysis further implicated AKT2, FOXO1, and PDK1, in the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. ceRNA network analysis identified miR-3187-3p as a candidate microRNA potentially associated with SGK2. Validation in independent datasets confirmed significant dysregulation of SGK2 expression, while RT-qPCR demonstrated significant downregulation of both SGK2 and miR-3187-3p in breast cancer tissues compared with normal controls. Receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated promising diagnostic performance for miR-3187-3p, whereas SGK2 did not demonstrate statistically significant performance in the validation cohort. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger, independent cohorts. Through multi-layered transcriptomic integration, network-based modeling, independent cohort validation, and experimental confirmation, this study identified the miR-3187-3p/SGK2 pair as a candidate co-dysregulated molecular signature associated with breast cancer. These findings provide additional insight into the molecular network underlying breast cancer and identify candidate biomarkers for further mechanistic investigation and validation in larger, clinically well-characterized cohorts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68473-y.title: Use of a dynamic systems framework to quantify the insulin transition gap to reduce treatment complications in diabetic ketoacidosis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68473-y.abstract: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) affects over 200,000 adult hospitalizations annually in the United States. Despite established treatment protocols, iatrogenic complications remain common, with hypoglycemia occurring in 5–25% of cases. The transition from intravenous to subcutaneous insulin is particularly vulnerable to rebound ketoacidosis due to the pharmacokinetic mismatch between rapid intravenous (IV) insulin clearance and delayed subcutaneous (SC) absorption. We developed a three-compartment ordinary differential equation model incorporating plasma glucose, intravenous insulin, and subcutaneous insulin depot dynamics. Through dynamical system and dimensional analysis, we derived timescales governing DKA treatment to allow better prediction of effect when transitioning from IV to SC insulin. Mathematical analysis identified three distinct timescales governing DKA treatment: rapid insulin clearance (τI ≈ 5–10 min), intermediate glucose decline (τG ≈ 60 min), and slow subcutaneous absorption (τS = 2–24 hr). A disparity between these timescales quantifies the ‘insulin gap’ phenomenon. Sensitivity analysis of the composite dimensionless parameter s (renamed here ‘glucose disposal efficiency per unit insulin’) revealed the largest influence on time to glucose target, explaining inter-patient variability in insulin requirements during acute illness. A supplementary analysis directly varying the physiological insulin sensitivity SI (0.5×–2× baseline) confirmed this heterogeneity, producing a 3.5-fold range in time to target (2.85–9.93 h). This dynamical systems framework reconfirms the current recommendations about the need for an overlap between IV insulin and the SC insulin and furthermore provides quantitative recommendation for the IV-SC insulin overlap timing and dextrose initiation thresholds. The model-derived dimensionless parameters offer trajectory-aware metrics for protocol optimization and could guide personalized insulin titration in patients with altered insulin sensitivity. Future applications include integration with continuous glucose and ketone monitoring for real-time risk stratification.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66764-y.title: Global population genomics reveals the lineage-dependent distribution of the YeaWX trimethylamine-associated module in Escherichia coli
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66764-y.abstract: Trimethylamine (TMA) and trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) have attracted increasing attention due to their potential involvement in host–microbiome interactions and cardiometabolic processes. In Escherichia coli, the YeaWX system has been proposed to participate in trimethylamine-associated metabolic pathways; however, its population-level distribution and population genomic organization remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed a large-scale population genomics analysis of the YeaWX module across 9700 quality-filtered E. coli genomes. Genome-wide detection of yeaX and yeaW was conducted using TBLASTN-based comparative genomics approaches, followed by integrated analyses of phylogroup distribution, sequence type (ST) composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles, multidrug resistance (MDR) prevalence, plasmidome structure, and resistance gene localization patterns. The YeaWX module displayed near-complete co-occurrence across the global E. coli population, with 3798 genomes (39.2%) carrying both genes simultaneously, whereas only nine genomes exhibited dissociation between yeaX and yeaW. The module displayed a strongly lineage-dependent distribution across phylogroups and sequence types. YeaWX carriage was almost completely absent from phylogroup B2 and major extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli (ExPEC)-associated lineages including ST131, ST95, ST73, ST127, and ST12, while significant enrichment was observed in phylogroups B1, D, A, F, and G as well as in ST69, ST101, ST10, and ST393. YeaWX-positive genomes displayed modest differences in AMR profiles and plasmid-associated characteristics compared with YeaWX-negative populations. However, adjusted multivariable analyses demonstrated that these apparent enrichments were largely explained by underlying lineage-associated population structure. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the YeaWX trimethylamine-associated module exhibits a strongly lineage-dependent population structure within global E. coli populations and provide new insight into the population genomic organization of bacterial trimethylamine-associated metabolic pathways.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55154-z.title: Expression and role of miR-126-3p and RAAS biomarkers in primary hypertension
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55154-z.abstract: To compare plasma levels of miR-126-3p between patients with essential hypertension (EH) and healthy individuals, and to investigate its correlation with renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) biomarkers. 29 healthy controls and 71 EH patients were enrolled. Total RNA, including miRNA, was extracted from plasma. Relative expression of miR-126-3p was determined by qRT-PCR. The discriminative ability of miR-126-3p and a combined panel was evaluated using ROC curves. The relative expression of miR-126-3p was significantly higher in the EH group (3.20 ± 2.15) than in the healthy group (1.54 ± 1.27, P < 0.001). Spearman correlation showed a significant negative correlation between miR-126-3p and serum ACE2 activity (r = − 0.205, p = 0.041). The AUC of a combined indicator (miR-126-3p, AngII, LDL-C, TC) was 0.859 (95% CI: 0.769–0.950, P < 0.001). Stepwise regression identified AngII, TC, LDL-C, and miR-126-3p as significant (P < 0.05), although collinearity was within an acceptable range (VIF < 5). miR-126-3p is significantly upregulated in the peripheral blood of EH patients and correlates negatively with ACE2. The combined panel shows moderate exploratory discriminative ability. However, due to the absence of continuous blood pressure data, no claim of added value over blood pressure measurement can be made. The potential role of miR-126-3p in modulating the RAAS counter‑regulatory axis requires further validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69335-3.title: Fully model predictive control-based solar water pumping system with sensorless induction motor drive
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69335-3.abstract: Solar water pumping systems offer a practical and sustainable solution for irrigation and water supply in remote areas without access to the electrical grid. This article proposes a standalone photovoltaic (PV) water pumping system based on an induction motor (IM) drive operating under a fully model predictive control (MPC) framework. The system consists of a DC–DC boost converter for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and a three-level neutral-point-clamped (3L-NPC) inverter supplying an IM-driven centrifugal pump. Both the DC–DC and DC–AC converters are controlled using dedicated MPC schemes to maximize energy extraction from the PV system under varying environmental conditions while ensuring high-performance motor control. In addition, a weighting-factor-free control strategy based on a normalized multi-objective decision mechanism is developed for the 3L-NPC inverter to improve control performance under varying operating conditions while reducing design complexity. A model reference adaptive system (MRAS) estimator is also employed for rotor speed and flux estimation, thereby enabling sensorless operation. Simulation results demonstrate a reduction of up to 70% in PV power settling time, a decrease in total harmonic distortion from 5.26% to 2.63%, and robust control performance under changing operating conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69612-1.title: Longitudinal associations with cognitive impairment differ between AWGS 2019 and 2025 sarcopenia criteria
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69612-1.abstract: This study compared the impact of the updated 2025 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) criteria, which prioritizes muscle strength, versus the multidimensional 2019 criteria on identifying individuals at risk for cognitive impairment, and examined how muscle components jointly influence cognitive outcomes. In this longitudinal study of 6,040 participants (aged ≥ 50) from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), sarcopenia was defined at baseline (2011) using both AWGS 2019 and 2025 criteria. Cognitive impairment was assessed in 2020. Multivariable logistic/linear regression, response-surface, and spline analyses were used. Possible sarcopenia prevalence was higher under AWGS 2019 (25.05%) than AWGS 2025 (11.16%). Both criteria identified sarcopenia associated with significant cognitive impairment (AWGS 2019 OR = 1.42, P = 0.003; AWGS 2025 OR = 1.41, P = 0.004). However, only AWGS 2019-defined possible sarcopenia was significantly linked to cognitive impairment (OR = 1.16, P = 0.04). Analysis revealed a significant non-linear protective effect of skeletal muscle mass against cognitive impairment, while grip strength showed no independent or synergistic association. Both criteria identify sarcopenia as a cognitive risk marker. The key difference lies in classifying possible sarcopenia: AWGS 2019 identifies a broader population with early functional impairment linked to cognitive risk, while AWGS 2025 defines a more narrowly defined group with stronger links to core muscular pathology. The choice should align with goals of early risk detection (AWGS 2019) versus etiological specificity (AWGS 2025).

doi:10.1016/j.atmosres.2026.109309.title: Spring and summer sea ice anomalies synergetically enhance summer precipitation over the Indochina Peninsula

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77470-8.title: Interfacial hydride transfer for dehalogenation with water
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77470-8.abstract: Reductive dehalogenation of organohalides through hydrodehalogenation with water is critical for environmental and chemical industries. Conventional hydrodehalogenation proceeds via electron transfer pathways (e.g., stepwise electron/hydrogen radical transfer, or two-electron transfer followed by protonation), which are often hampered by limited dehalogenation kinetics and selectivity. While the interfacial transfer of reductive hydride (Hδ−) species presents a compelling concerted two-electron pathway, its application has been constrained by the difficult surface hydride formation under mild conditions. Here, we overcome this challenge by developing mechanochemically activated zero-valent iron (ZVI) that generates reactive silicon-hydride (Si–Hδ⁻) species in the presence of trace water. Trace water induces ZVI corrosion to produce H2, which is heterolytically cleaved by in situ formed surface Siδ+–Oδ⁻ Lewis pairs, yielding nucleophilic Si–Hδ⁻ motifs. These motifs drive direct interfacial hydride transfer for highly efficient hydrodehalogenation and regioselective deuteration with rate constants 2-50 times greater than conventional radical-based hydrogen transfer on ZVI. The water-mediated regeneration of the hydride donor enables continuous-flow decontamination of actual halogenated groundwater and valorization of organohalides into high-purity deuterated products with selectivity of 93.4%. This work presents a promising mechanochemical platform that suggests a more sustainable approach for selective hydrodehalogenation of organohalides. The authors report mechanochemically activated zero-valent iron converts water-generated H2 into surface Si–Hδ⁻ via heterolytic cleavage under mild conditions, enabling efficient hydrodehalogenation reactions.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77479-z.title: Multiple overlapping SNARE complexes drive endosome maturation in Drosophila nephrocytes
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77479-z.abstract: Endosomal maturation determines whether internalized cargo is recycled or degraded, yet the logic governing early endosomal fusion remains incompletely defined. Although commonly depicted as a linear Rab5-to-Rab7 transition mediated by a single SNARE pathway, we show that early endosome maturation is driven by multiple parallel, non-interchangeable SNARE complexes. Using Drosophila nephrocytes as a tractable in vivo model, we define a Syx12L–Snap29–Ykt6 complex that mediates homotypic early endosomal fusion and identify two related assemblies–Syx7L–Snap29–Ykt6 and Syx7L–Snap29–Vamp7–that promote later endosomal and lysosomal fusion with distinct Rab requirements. When the canonical Syx12L pathway is disrupted, alternative complexes remain active and generate aberrant endolysosomal swirls which also form in the absence of Rab5 or early endosomal tethers. Thus, Rab5-independent membrane progression toward lysosomes persists but is insufficient to produce fully functional degradative organelles. Together, our findings reveal a network of parallel fusion pathways underlying endosome maturation. Hargitai, Molnar et al. show that parallel, non-interchangeable SNARE complexes drive endosome maturation in Drosophila nephrocytes, revealing alternative routes that allow membrane progression toward lysosomes.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77280-y.title: Functional annotation of insulin-responsive genes in human adipocytes reveals PLCXD1 as a lipid storage regulator
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77280-y.abstract: Abstract Insulin-driven gene regulation is central to adipocyte function, but the roles of many of these genes in lipid metabolism remain unclear. Here, we integrate three transcriptomic datasets to identify insulin-responsive genes and define their functions in human adipocytes using a multiparametric lipid turnover screen. Our results reveal four major clusters involved in metabolic regulation, transcription, stress responses, and lipid metabolism. Among lipid-related hits, phospholipase C X domain-containing protein-1 (PLCXD1) emerges as a regulator of insulin-stimulated lipogenesis, without affecting lipolysis or adipogenesis. PLCXD1 is induced by insulin via sterol regulatory element-binding proteins, a response attenuated in insulin-resistant states. This atypical phospholipase is genetically associated with fat mass-related traits, localizes to early endosomes and catalyzes phosphatidylinositol conversion into diacylglycerol. Through structure-function analyses, we show that PLCXD1 catalytic activity is required for insulin-stimulated lipogenesis. Altogether, our results uncover PLCXD1 as an insulin-regulated enzyme linking endosomal phosphoinositide metabolism to lipid storage in adipocytes.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77438-8.title: K-MARVEL: K-Mer-based antimicrobial resistance virtual exploration lab
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77438-8.abstract: Abstract The rapid spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates new computational surveillance tools. Current methods for analysis of next-generation sequencing data have trade-offs: assembly-based approaches are computationally intensive, and direct long-read mapping is hampered by high error rates that obscure resistance-conferring mutations. Here, we present K-MARVEL, an open-source method that captures antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and resistance-conferring mutations from both short- and long-read datasets. Operating in protein k-mer space, K-MARVEL tolerates nucleotide-level sequencing errors. We benchmarked K-MARVEL on 209 long-read and 205 short-read datasets across 22 bacterial species and achieved F1-scores of 0.976 (short-read) and 0.958 (long-read), outperforming assembly-based methods in speed and memory usage. K-MARVEL had higher F1-scores than seven widely used short-read-based ARG classifiers (0.979) and two widely used long-read-based classifiers (0.961) for homology-model-based ARGs. K-MARVEL can accurately identify both homologous ARGs and structural genes containing resistance-conferring mutations, including multiple variants, directly from raw sequencing data.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69314-8.title: Clinically approved ALDH inhibitor combined with a chemotherapeutic agent sensitizes triple-negative breast cancer stem cells to PD-L1 blockade
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69314-8.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is among the most aggressive cancers due to the lack of specific therapeutic targets. Conventional chemotherapy often enriches cancer stem cells, driving therapeutic resistance and tumor relapse. In TNBC, epithelial-like ALDHhi and mesenchymal-like CD44hiCD24lo cancer stem cells are associated with cell hyperproliferation, tumor initiation, and metastatic potential. Additionally, PD-L1 expression enhances cancer stem cell survival, further promoting tumor progression and positioning it as a promising immunotherapeutic target. Both the ALDH inhibitor disulfiram and the anti-PD-L1 atezolizumab are FDA-approved drugs investigated in preclinical and clinical studies for metastatic breast cancer. This study explored the therapeutic potential of combining these drugs to target TNBC cancer stem cells enriched by the chemotherapeutic agent doxorubicin. Using human TNBC cell lines and clinically relevant patient-derived xenograft tumor fragments, we assessed post-treatment cell viability, cancer stem cell survival, and the expression of associated genes and proteins. Results suggested that doxorubicin and disulfiram increased PD-L1 expression on both epithelial- and mesenchymal-like cancer stem cells irrespective of baseline PD-L1 expression, and the subsequent addition of the PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab effectively reduced cancer stem cell frequency, expression levels of stemness-associated markers, and bulk TNBC cell viability in an immune-independent context. These results support a clinically translatable therapeutic strategy for targeting chemotherapy-enriched cancer stem cells with varying PD-L1 expression levels, and identify immune-competent in vivo validation as a necessary future direction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69810-x.title: School climate does not buffer the association between aggression beliefs and bullying perpetration
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69810-x.abstract: Bullying is a pervasive issue in schools, influenced by individual cognitive factors such as normative beliefs about aggression and contextual factors such as perceived school climate. Positive school climate dimensions—including connectedness, value of learning, and quality of relationships—are generally associated with reduced bullying perpetration. Here, we analyzed data from 4919 adolescents using ordinal logistic regression to assess whether student-perceived school climate moderates the relationship between endorsement of normative beliefs about aggression and bullying perpetration frequency. Stronger endorsement of aggression-related beliefs was associated with higher perpetration frequency, whereas several relational school climate dimensions were associated with lower perpetration frequency. However, we found no evidence that perceived school climate weakened the association between aggression-related beliefs and bullying perpetration frequency. These findings are more consistent with direct associations between perceived school climate and bullying perpetration than with a buffering effect on the belief–perpetration association. Bullying prevention efforts may therefore benefit from integrating climate-building actions with targeted interventions addressing aggression-related norms and beliefs.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70402-y.title: Prediction of dielectric behaviour of FDM printed-acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) reinforced with 10% carbon fiber: a machine learning approach

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66184-y.title: A servo network architecture for deterministic real-time synchronization in wheeled mobile platforms: hardware design and communication-layer validation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66184-y.abstract: In wheeled mobile (WM) platforms, coordinated multi-wheel motion requires that motion commands be dispatched to, and feedback collected from, several independently driven servo actuators with tightly bounded timing. Standard serial communication introduces non-deterministic delays, while commercial fieldbus systems that guarantee deterministic timing impose high cost and licensing complexity. To address this gap, our work proposes a servo-based real-time synchronization architecture for omnidirectional wheeled platforms, implemented directly at the hardware communication layer. The method supports all-wheel-drive (AWD) and four-wheel differential-drive (FWDD) configurations through a network of distributed servo motors operating under a real-time protocol over standard 100 Mbps Ethernet. A dedicated motion controller—integrating a microcontroller unit, a real-time protocol module, a physical-layer transceiver, and a pulse-transformation module—ensures deterministic command dispatch and synchronized feedback. A physical mobile platform and a custom control board are constructed, and the three-synchronization metrics (command dispatch, feedback alignment, and inter-servo timing) are measured experimentally. The results demonstrate sub-microsecond synchronization with low latency at the servo-network level. We emphasise that this timing synchronization is a necessary but not sufficient condition for physical trajectory accuracy: it removes command-dispatch skew as a source of coordination error, but end-to-end trajectory tracking additionally depends on mechanical factors (wheel–ground contact, gearbox compliance, load) and the motion-control law. Validation of trajectory accuracy under dynamic motion and manipulation load is accordingly identified as the subject of future work. The presented architecture provides an effective, low-cost, and accessible foundation for coordinated motion in advanced mobile platforms.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66854-x.title: Bridging yield gaps to enhance greengram (Vigna radiata L.) productivity in India: insights from crop simulation and water productivity analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66854-x.abstract: Greengram (Vigna radiata L.) plays a crucial role in India’s nutritional security and agroecosystem sustainability, though constrained by climatic variability, moisture stress, and suboptimal crop management. To identify pathways for sustainable intensification, the APSIM model was employed to simulate potential yield (Yp), quantify yield gaps, and assess water productivity across twenty major greengram growing districts of India during 2003–2023. Simulations integrated weather, soil profiles, region-specific management practices, and cultivar-specific genetic coefficients, while physical (PWP), irrigation (IWP), and economic (EWP) water productivity indices were evaluated. Observed yields (162–611 kg ha−1) remained lower than simulated potential yields (386–1220 kg ha−1), resulting in yield gaps of 27–66% (average ~ 389 kg ha−1). Central Zone districts exhibited relatively higher EWP. Model performance was robust during calibration and validation (R2 and NSE ≈ 0.97–0.99; RMSE ≤ 20%; NMSE < 0.05). Carbon budgeting revealed carbon efficiency ranged from 0.65 to 1.98 and a mean Carbon Sustainability Index (CSI) of 0.32. Principal Component Analysis identified irrigation, soil fertility, and crop geometry as dominant yield drivers, while correlation-density matrix highlighted the dependence of grain yield on irrigation. The results demonstrate that improving irrigation management, optimizing nutrient use, and adopting region-specific agronomic practices can substantially reduce yield gaps and enhance water productivity in greengram.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70092-6.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis identifies MMP11-positive cancer-associated fibroblasts associated with bladder cancer progression and extracellular matrix remodeling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70092-6.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) play critical roles in bladder cancer progression, yet their heterogeneity and functional contributions during the transition from non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) to muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated multiple single-cell RNA sequencing datasets comprising 21 bladder tumors and 4 adjacent normal tissues to characterize CAF heterogeneity and identify progression-associated subpopulations. A high-risk (HR) gene signature associated with invasive progression was first established using the Lund bladder cancer cohort. HR gene expression was predominantly enriched in CAFs, and reclustering analysis identified an MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic CAF (myCAF) subtype with the highest HR signature activity. Functional analyses revealed that MMP11⁺ myCAFs were strongly associated with extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, collagen metabolism, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, and angiogenesis. Multi-cohort deconvolution analyses demonstrated that MMP11⁺ myCAFs increased with tumor stage and were associated with significantly worse survival outcomes. Cell–cell communication analysis suggested that these CAFs interact with tumor epithelial cells through FN1- and collagen-related signaling pathways. Based on the expression levels of MMP11, FN1, COL1A1, and COL1A2, we developed an MMP11⁺ myCAF signature score, which was associated with advanced tumor stage and shorter overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) in univariate analyses. However, the association between the signature score and survival was not significant after adjustment for tumor stage and invasiveness, indicating that its prognostic information was largely captured by established clinical variables. Immunohistochemistry further confirmed elevated expression of these markers in MIBC tissues. These findings identify MMP11⁺ myCAFs as a progression-associated CAF subpopulation in bladder cancer and suggest that their ECM remodeling programs and inferred epithelial communication pathways may contribute to tumor progression.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69184-0.title: Grid-based optimization for DBSCAN clustering with periodic boundary conditions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69184-0.abstract: Periodic boundary conditions (PBC) occur in scientific and geospatial data, where conventional density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) can fragment clusters at the domain seam. This study proposes GPDBSCAN, a replica-free grid-indexed DBSCAN algorithm for rectangular domains with periodic dimensions. GPDBSCAN canonicalizes periodic coordinates, indexes the original samples in $$\varepsilon $$-governed cells, wraps adjacent-cell coordinates across periodic faces, and verifies candidates with the minimum-image Euclidean distance. A cell-width construction with $$h\ge \varepsilon $$ guarantees candidate completeness, and an adaptive strategy selects between offset enumeration and occupied-cell comparison. Formal analysis shows that the resulting neighborhoods and density-connected core components are equivalent to exact periodic DBSCAN. Experiments on representative and controlled synthetic datasets show identical PBC-DBSCAN and GPDBSCAN clusterings while GPDBSCAN consistently reduces peak Python-managed memory. Runtime is data-dependent: GPDBSCAN is faster when PBC replica overhead is large, but slower when grid-candidate costs dominate. On 17 IBTrACS dateline-crossing storm tracks, both periodic methods achieve ARI, NMI, and FMI of 1.000; GPDBSCAN reduces peak memory by 26.4% on the full subset but requires more runtime. GPDBSCAN is therefore most useful when exact periodic clustering and reduced memory overhead are priorities.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69374-w.title: Association of digital pulse diagnostic indices with survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer receiving immunotherapy
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69374-w.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is associated with poor survival, and evaluating quality of life (QoL) and clinical outcomes has become increasingly important in assessing the treatment efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Given the limited predictive value of existing biomarkers in NSCLC immunotherapy, this study aimed to assess the association between digital pulse diagnostic indices and survival and QoL in patients with advanced NSCLC receiving immunotherapy. This study enrolled patients with stage IIIB–IV NSCLC who had failed first-line platinum chemotherapy and were scheduled to receive ICI monotherapy (pembrolizumab or atezolizumab) across 10 university hospitals in Korea. Pulse diagnostic indices collected every 9 weeks over a 45-week follow-up were analyzed for their association with overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), treatment response, and QoL using regression analyses with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate adjustment for multiple comparisons. Of the 170 patients enrolled, 91 were included in the analysis. The median PFS and OS periods were 107 and 406 days, respectively. In unadjusted analyses, higher body mass index (BMI) and estimated cardiac output (ECO) and lower heart rate (HR) were nominally associated with longer OS. HR showed the most consistent association with OS; each 10-beat/min increase was associated with higher mortality after clinical adjustment (hazard ratio 1.487; 95% CI 1.192–1.854; p = 0.0004). No robust associations were observed between baseline pulse indices and PFS, durable clinical benefit, or QoL changes after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Among patients with NSCLC receiving ICIs, several pulse indicators showed nominal associations with OS and QoL changes. Notably, baseline HR showed the most consistent association with OS after clinical adjustment and FDR correction. These findings are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68647-8.title: Regional skin temperature responses to exhaustive cycling under normoxia and normobaric hypoxia in trained and non-trained men
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68647-8.abstract: The combined effects of exercise bout, body region and hypoxic severity on post-exercise skin temperature (Tₛₖ), measured by infrared thermography (IRT), remain unclear. Twenty-four healthy men (12 trained cyclists, 12 non-trained controls) completed three sessions under normoxia (FiO₂ 0.209) and normobaric hypoxia simulating ≈ 2000 m (0.16) and ≈ 3000 m (0.14), each comprising graded and constant-load cycling bouts to exhaustion. Anterior trunk and thigh Tₛₖ were imaged at rest and immediately after each bout and analysed by mixed-design ANOVA (Time, Region, FiO₂ within-subject; Group between-subject). Tₛₖ fell over time, more and earlier at the trunk than at the thigh (− 4.4 vs. − 0.9 °C), reversing the pre-exercise trunk–thigh gradient. Mean Tₛₖ did not differ between oxygen conditions, but lower FiO₂ amplified and advanced the decrease at both regions (Time × FiO₂); the Time × Region × FiO₂ interaction was not significant. Trained men were warmer at rest at both regions; exercise abolished this difference at the trunk but widened it at the thigh. Exploratory correlations linked Tₛₖ inversely to body fat and positively to VO₂max. Post-exercise Tₛₖ therefore tracks region- and time-specific thermoeffector activity, not whole-body heat content; because skin blood flow and core temperature were not measured, this interpretation remains inferential.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69532-0.title: Emission spectra and diagnosis of C4F7N/CO2 discharge faults
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69532-0.abstract: The C4F7N/CO2 mixed gas is regarded as one of the most promising environmental-friendly alternatives to SF6. Studying its discharge spectral characteristics under different voltages and fault types is of great significance for insulation condition monitoring and fault diagnosis. Based on a 126 kV real-scale GIL experimental platform, this paper conducted DC breakdown, DC surface flashover, and AC surface flashover experiments for 10% C4F7N/90% CO2 mixed gas at 0.1 MPa. By constructing a spectral data preprocessing method to eliminate the shot-to-shot variations in discharge emission intensity, the emission spectral differences between C4F7N/CO2 and SF6, as well as pure CO2 gases, were systematically compared, and the spectral evolution laws under different conditions were analyzed. The experimental results show that, compared with SF6, the C4F7N/CO2 mixed gas exhibits more pronounced characteristic emission peaks, with the main emission features concentrated in the ultraviolet–visible and near-infrared regions. In the DC breakdown condition, the spectrum is mainly dominated by electrode evaporation (Al resonance line) and gas decomposition (CN, C, O spectral lines); in the DC surface flashover condition, due to the participation of insulator solid materials in discharge decomposition, the CN radical spectral band (385.0–387.6 nm) and CII ion spectral lines are significantly enhanced, while the Al and O spectral lines are relatively weakened; in the AC surface flashover condition, the time-integrated spectrum shows a stronger near-infrared contribution, with the O atomic characteristic peak at 777.3 nm becoming dominant, while the CN characteristic band is weakened. The study reveals the microscopic luminescence mechanism of the C4F7N/CO2 mixed gas under the combined action of electrode evaporation, gas ionization, and material decomposition, confirming that changes in specific spectral line intensities can be used as criteria for distinguishing fault types and voltage levels, providing theoretical support for the optical diagnostic technology of environmentally friendly gas-insulated equipment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70070-y.title: Modeling the effects of horizontal and vertical road geometries on traffic crashes in rural roads
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70070-y.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between road geometry and traffic crashes on rural state roads in Zonguldak, Turkey, between 2016 and 2022. The objective is to quantify how specific combinations of geometric elements influence average crash frequency per kilometer. A total of 941 crashes were analyzed across approximately 156 km of roadway, using officially authorized crash reports and project-based geometric data. Crash locations were spatially matched with corresponding alignment segments. Four geometric combinations were evaluated: horizontal curve–vertical curve, horizontal curve–longitudinal grade, horizontal tangent–vertical curve, and horizontal tangent–longitudinal grade. Multiple linear regression models were developed to assess their joint effects. The results indicate that horizontal curves result in higher crash frequencies than horizontal tangents, while vertical curves exhibit greater risk than longitudinal grades. The highest crash rates were observed where horizontal and vertical curves coincided, suggesting a potential interaction effect between geometric elements. The final models demonstrated statistically significant relationships ( p < 0.05) and satisfactory explanatory power, identifying critical geometric configurations associated with increased crash occurrence. These findings provide quantitative evidence for prioritizing safety improvements on existing rural roads and offer guidance for safer geometric design in new roadway projects.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70192-3.title: Ultraslow entorhinal oscillations induce persistent reorganization of internal spatial representations through grid cell drift
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70192-3.abstract: Grid cells in the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) of head-fixed mice exhibit ultraslow (< 0.01 Hz) oscillations (USO) during walking in a 1D running wheel in darkness. Unfortunately, there is no clear link between the functional role of these oscillations and the navigation strategy used by animals to calculate their current position by continuously summing self-motion cues (path integration). Given the synaptic projections from MEC to the hippocampus, we hypothesized that ultraslow oscillations have a role in shaping the internal spatial representation modulating path integration. A realistic computational model of the entorhinal-grid cells and hippocampal-place cells is proposed. The model exhibits ultraslow oscillations and is capable of sustaining path integration of a rodent-like simulated animal. Results indicate that ultraslow oscillations induced persistent changes in the grid cell dynamics, represented as a positional drift of grid fields. Such drift resulted in position estimation errors but generated new grid-place cell associations when combined with synaptic plasticity. We discuss that, ultraslow entorhinal oscillations produced long-lasting and structured reorganization of the internal spatial representation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69733-7.title: A graph-based cyber threat modeling and risk assessment framework for smart microgrid systems
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69733-7.abstract: Abstract The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in smart microgrids (SMGs) improves monitoring and control capabilities but also increases exposure to cyber–physical threats. This paper proposes a graph-based cyber–physical threat modelling and quantitative risk assessment framework for smart microgrids that evaluates device criticality, attack propagation, and overall system risk. The microgrid is modelled as a heterogeneous directed graph in which devices and communication links are associated with vulnerability, dependency, and communication exposure attributes derived from CVE/CVSS information. Mathematical formulations are developed to define attack risk indicators, determine success rate of attacks, and its impact. The framework is evaluated using a 24-hour smart microgrid simulation, case study of cyber-attack scenarios including False Data Injection (FDI), and Denial-of-Service (DoS), followed by IEEE 33-bus distribution system validation. The proposed framework facilitates simulation of attacks on smart microgrid system and allows user to automatically visualize, attack outcomes such as attack success rate, associated cost, and its impact. It generates a risk profile along with propagation path for security-oriented planning of future microgrids and testing of new techniques even before they get implemented. The experimental analysis is conducted to show high-risk attack paths within the communication infrastructure, economic impact, resilience, and mitigation analyses. The proposed framework provides an effective decision-support tool for vulnerability assessment, risk prioritization, and cybersecurity planning in smart microgrid environments.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69955-9.title: A context-aware dynamic model selection framework based on proximal policy optimization for day-ahead PV power forecasting
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69955-9.abstract: To enhance the accuracy of day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting and overcome the limited adaptability of individual models under varying weather conditions, this paper proposes a scenario-aware dynamic model selection method based on an actor-critic contextual policy learning approach. The approach first performs cluster analysis on temporal features extracted from meteorological variables that influence PV output, classifying historical weather patterns into four typical scenarios: clear, partly cloudy, overcast, and rainy. A forecasting model library comprising multiple deep learning architectures is then constructed. A reinforcement learning agent based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is trained to learn an optimal policy that dynamically selects the most suitable model from the library according to the day-ahead meteorological features of the target day. By adaptively matching the optimal model to the specific characteristics of each target day, the proposed method substantially improves prediction accuracy.
