Experimental results on real-world PV data show that the proposed method effectively leverages the complementary strengths of multiple models. Compared with the static optimal strategy, it reduces RMSE by 13.97% overall. These results demonstrate its strong effectiveness and adaptability to complex and variable weather scenarios.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70080-w.title: Stage-dependent activation of the circulating AIM2–caspase-1–GSDMD axis in silicosis: a cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70080-w.abstract: Silicosis is a progressive occupational lung disease caused by long-term inhalation of crystalline silica, in which persistent inflammation contributes to lung injury and fibrotic remodeling. Experimental studies suggest that DNA-sensing pathways involving AIM2 may be engaged after silica exposure. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 187 male workers, including unexposed administrative controls (n = 57), dust-exposed workers without silicosis (n = 57), and patients with radiographically confirmed silicosis stage I (n = 37), stage II (n = 20), or stage III (n = 16). Serum cell-free double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) was quantified by fluorometry. AIM2, ASC, caspase-1, and gasdermin D (GSDMD; full-length and cleaved fragment) were assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by Western blotting in a small subset of participants. Serum IL-1β and IL-18 were measured by ELISA. Nonparametric tests were used for group comparisons, and multivariable regression models were used to evaluate associations with IL-1β. Serum dsDNA increased with silicosis severity and was highest in stage III (median 54.76 ng/mL; P for trend < 0.001). PBMC AIM2 and caspase-1 expression showed a similar stage-related pattern, whereas cleaved GSDMD (GSDMD-N) was mainly elevated in advanced disease. After adjustment for age, smoking status, shift work, educational level, physical exercise, and midday napping, IL-1β remained associated with exposure and disease status. Compared with controls, dust-exposed workers without silicosis had higher IL-1β levels (adjusted GMR = 3.02, 95% CI 1.78–5.12; P < 0.001). IL-1β was markedly elevated in silicosis across stages (adjusted GMR range 11.21–15.93). Circulating markers along the AIM2–caspase-1–GSDMD axis display stage-dependent changes in silicosis, supporting systemic involvement of inflammasome-related inflammatory signaling. These blood-based markers may help capture inflammatory activity across the exposure–disease continuum, although prospective studies are needed to determine their predictive value. Because our measurements were restricted to peripheral blood, confirmation of tissue-level cellular events and mechanisms will require dedicated morphological and functional investigations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66430-3.title: Explainable image aesthetic assessment via semantic segmentation-guided cross-attention fusion
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66430-3.abstract: Most existing image aesthetic assessment methods rely on global representations or simple aggregation of local features. This makes it difficult to model semantic region information and provide region-level explanations. To address this issue, we propose a Semantic Segmentation-Guided Cross-Attention Fusion (SSG-CAF) method for explainable image aesthetic assessment. The method first uses SegFormer-B0 to generate semantic masks for eight semantic categories, thereby introducing explicit semantic and spatial priors. It then combines region-level features with global visual context. A cross-attention mechanism is used to model dependencies between semantic regions and the global representation. This design supports the representation of high-level aesthetic cues, including compositional balance, subject prominence and regional harmony. SHAP is further used for region-level attribution analysis. Experiments on the cleaned AVA test set showed that SSG-CAF achieved an MSE of 0.3412 ± 0.0150, an MAE of 0.4565 ± 0.0103, a PLCC of 0.6517 ± 0.0029 and an SRCC of 0.6370 ± 0.0034. Compared with the selected baselines, SSG-CAF showed stronger correlations with human aesthetic ratings under the cleaned AVA protocol. It also produced post-hoc, quantitative region-level attribution evidence that describes model behaviour.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69054-9.title: Physiological adaptation of the jugular venous pulse during long-duration spaceflight
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69054-9.abstract: The jugular venous pulse (JVP) offers a non-invasive window into right atrial pressure. In microgravity, the serial JVP waveform during long-duration spaceflight had never been characterised. Using ECG-synchronised high-resolution ultrasound and a validated AI model, we quantified internal jugular vein cross-sectional area (IJV-CSA) throughout the cardiac cycle in four astronauts before and after flight, with in-flight measurements in one astronaut. Mean IJV-CSA fell significantly post-flight in three astronauts (ASTRO 0: from 0.723 ± 0.076 to 0.453 ± 0.061 cm2, ASTRO 2: − 46.0%, ASTRO 3: − 48.4%; p < 0.001). The reduction in ASTRO 0 developed between the first and fifth month in orbit. Maximum CSA declined consistently with reduced central venous pressure. Pulsatile excursion, an index never previously reported in spaceflight, increased markedly (ASTRO 0: + 105.0%, p < 0.001; ASTRO 2: + 337.1%, p < 0.001), suggesting enhanced transmission of cardiac pressure waves towards the cerebral venous compartment in the absence of hydrostatic gradients. ASTRO 1 showed the opposite pattern (minimum CSA + 42.5%, pulsatile excursion − 60.3%, p < 0.001), probably due to IJV thrombosis, representing the third documented case in space medicine. The JVP waveform retains terrestrial morphology and ECG timing in microgravity. Whether JVP parameters predict venous thrombosis or relate to glymphatic function in long-term spaceflight warrants further studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68980-y.title: Comparative effectiveness of three treatment strategies for submacular hemorrhage secondary to age-related macular degeneration
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68980-y.abstract: We aimed to compare the three treatment strategies for extensive submacular hemorrhage (SMH) secondary to age-related macular degeneration (AMD): intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) monotherapy, anti-VEGF combined with sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas tamponade, and triple therapy consisting of anti-VEGF, SF6 gas, and intravitreal tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). This multicenter retrospective study included 61 eyes of 61 patients treated at three institutions. Patients received anti-VEGF monotherapy (n = 19), anti-VEGF plus SF6 gas tamponade (n = 20), or triple therapy (n = 22). Inclusion criteria were logMAR best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) ≥ 0.40, SMH ≥ 2 disc diameters, and treatment within 14 days of onset; time from hemorrhage onset to treatment differed significantly among groups. The primary outcome was longitudinal BCVA change over 12 months, analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline BCVA. Triple therapy was associated with better BCVA than the other strategies. Treatment modality and baseline ellipsoid zone disruption were independent predictors of 12-month BCVA. Hematoma displacement rates were 100%, 35.0%, and 5.3%, and re-hemorrhage rates were 18.2%, 55.0%, and 42.1% in the triple, combination, and monotherapy groups, respectively. These findings suggest that triple therapy may be a useful treatment option; however, interpretation is limited by the retrospective, non-randomized design, and prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69415-4.title: Evaluating the readability and quality of ai-generated stress urinary incontinence education materials: a comparative analysis of five large language models
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69415-4.abstract: Abstract Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) substantially impairs quality of life, yet accessible and comprehensible patient education remains limited. Large language models (LLMs) may support health-information delivery, but their outputs require systematic evaluation. To compare the readability, reliability, and patient-oriented usability of SUI education materials generated by five LLMs. ChatGPT Free, Claude Free, Microsoft Copilot Free, DeepSeek Free, and Gemini Free were tested through their official web interfaces on March 15, 2026. Each model answered 12 core SUI questions, yielding 60 responses. Six readability indices were assessed: Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease (FKRE), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Gunning Fog Score (GFS), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), Coleman-Liau Index (CLI), and Automated Readability Index (ARI). Information quality and patient usability were evaluated using the Global Quality Scale (GQS), DISCERN, Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP), and Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT). Overall differences were examined using Friedman tests with Kendall’s W, followed by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction. Significant inter-model differences were found for FKRE ( P = 0.005), FKGL ( P = 0.016), GFS ( P = 0.002), SMOG ( P = 0.007), and CLI ( P < 0.001), but not ARI ( P = 0.107). Gemini had higher FKRE than ChatGPT (30.06 ± 12.63 vs. 23.60 ± 11.72; adjusted P = 0.036), Claude had higher GFS than Copilot (18.41 ± 4.56 vs. 15.43 ± 1.59; adjusted P = 0.018), and DeepSeek had higher SMOG than ChatGPT and Copilot (adjusted P = 0.013 and 0.049). GQS, DISCERN, EQIP, and PEMAT all differed significantly among models (all P < 0.001; Kendall’s W = 0.212–0.373). Gemini scored higher than Copilot on GQS; Claude scored higher than all other models on DISCERN; Gemini scored lower than all other models on EQIP; and ChatGPT scored lower than all other models on PEMAT (all adjusted P < 0.05). Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC [2, 1] = 0.954). EQIP correlated positively with PEMAT ( r = 0.69), whereas DISCERN showed limited associations with all readability measures. The five LLMs differed significantly on all quality instruments, but no model performed best on every dimension. AI-generated SUI education materials therefore require independent factual verification, targeted simplification and final review by qualified healthcare professionals before any patient-facing use.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69393-7.title: An end-to-end multi-modal pipeline for person search in unconstrained CCTV environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69393-7.abstract: Abstract In real-world surveillance, situations arise in which two people wear nearly identical clothing or in which identifying features are obscured by heavy occlusions and shifting poses. In these environments, traditional uni-modal systems that rely on static appearance do not perform well and often produce false matches. This paper presents a multi-modal Re-ID framework that combines appearance, facial features, and gait to accurately perform this task. In the first stage, robust person tracklets are extracted from video using a YOLOv8 detector and a DeepSORT tracker. A multi-modal feature extractor is then applied to each person crop through three parallel streams. A custom GaitSet-inspired network produces a 256-dimensional gait embedding from RGB tracklet frames. An OSNet backbone is used to get a 1024-dimensional omni-scale appearance embedding. For facial biometrics, a Multi-Task Cascaded Convolutional Network (MTCNN) is used to explicitly detect the face and five-point landmarks followed by a facial landmark regression model. Each crop is aligned to a landmark and the aligned face is sent to FaceNet for computing the 128 dimensional facial embedding. In the last step, an Ensemble Concatenation module merges these three normalised embeddings into a single $$\mathbb {R}^{1408}$$ identity descriptor ( $$1024 + 256 + 128$$ ). The discriminability is significantly improved through the combination of facial features and temporal motion cues. Furthermore, the fusion strategy prevents any single modality from causing identity leakage, thereby providing a strong defense against appearance-based identity errors.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69576-2.title: Mitigating repetition and loops via implicit signal self-tuning for self-correcting inference
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69576-2.abstract: Large language models often suffer from logical hallucinations, repetitive generation loops, and imbalanced reasoning efficiency during complex mathematical reasoning. Existing static prompting and explicit intervention methods cannot dynamically regulate the decoding process based on the model’s real-time reasoning state. This paper proposes the Implicit Signal Self-Tuning (ISST) framework. It synchronously computes two internal uncertainty metrics during decoding: attention distribution entropy and token confidence entropy. These are fused via Sigmoid multiplication to obtain a unified entropy value. This value quantifies the risk level at each reasoning step. When the unified entropy exceeds a threshold, the framework activates an exploration mode. It increases the sampling temperature and narrows the top-p sampling interval to break reasoning loops. When the entropy falls below the threshold, it switches to an exploitation mode. Parameters are gradually restored to baseline values. This balances reasoning accuracy with token consumption. Validation is conducted on multiple mathematical datasets including AIME24, AMC23, and MATH500. Models ranging from 1.5B to 7B parameters are tested. The framework achieves an average 50% reduction in repetitive generation rate. It reduces token consumption while maintaining reasoning accuracy. No modification to the model backbone is required. This provides a lightweight new approach for adaptive reasoning optimization in large models.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69605-0.title: Diversity and pathogenicity of emerging and novel Paramicrosphaeropsis species associated with olive canker and dieback
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69605-0.abstract: Olive (Olea europaea L.) is an economically and ecologically important crop that is increasingly threatened by trunk diseases such as canker and dieback. This study investigated the occurrence, taxonomy, and pathogenicity of Paramicrosphaeropsis species associated with these diseases in Fars Province, Iran. A total of 73 fungal isolates were recovered from symptomatic olive trees across five regions and six cultivars. Morphological characterization and RNA polymerase II second largest subunit (rpb2) sequence analysis of representative isolates identified Paramicrosphaeropsis eriobotryae as the dominant species, whereas multilocus phylogenetic analyses of representative isolates based on the internal transcribed spacer (ITS), rpb2, and β-tubulin (tub2) loci supported the recognition of two novel species, P. oleae sp. nov. and P. sarvestanensis sp. nov. This study provides the first evidence linking P. eriobotryae to olive canker and dieback. Pathogenicity assays on detached shoots showed that 95% of isolates caused necrotic lesions, and principal component analysis (PCA) of six traits clustered isolates along a continuum from highly aggressive to non-aggressive. The tested aggressive isolate of P. eriobotryae fulfilled Koch’s postulates on olive saplings and exhibited the greatest aggressiveness and the shortest incubation period among the three tested representative isolates. Pathogenicity assays on wounded detached shoots showed that the tested aggressive isolates of the three Paramicrosphaeropsis species were capable of causing necrotic lesions on all evaluated fruit tree hosts under controlled experimental conditions. The representative isolate of P. eriobotryae was the most aggressive, particularly on walnut, while olive inoculated with P. oleae sp. nov. showed the least susceptibility. Susceptibility of six international and Iranian olive cultivars to P. eriobotryae, identified ‘Conservalia’, ‘Koroneiki’, and ‘Tokhm-Kabki’ as highly susceptible cultivars, whereas the dominant native cultivar ‘Zard’ showed moderate susceptibility. Notably, ‘Abou-Satl’ was the least susceptible cultivar under the present inoculation conditions and showed no measurable internal lesion depth following inoculation with the tested aggressive isolate. This study provides the first comprehensive evidence of Paramicrosphaeropsis species associated with olive canker and dieback and introduces two novel species, contributing to the understanding of their taxonomy, aggressiveness, and potential impact on important fruit trees.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69116-y.title: Mask-guided region-aware underwater image enhancement Mamba network
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69116-y.abstract: Underwater images are often affected by region-aware inconsistent degradation. Specifically, foreground objects, background regions, and boundaries of the image exhibit inconsistent and conflicting degradation states, which affects the processing performance of underwater image enhancement (UIE) networks. Existing UIE networks enhance the underwater image as a whole, ignoring the degradation differences between regions. This can lead to the destruction of foreground details, insufficient background enhancement, and the introduction of artifacts or distortions at boundaries. To address this issue, we proposed MRU-Mamba, a mask-guided region-aware underwater image enhancement network based on Mamba. The MRU-Mamba network uses a semantic mask to segment the foreground, background, and boundary regions of an image, and applies Region-Oriented Selective Scan (ROSS) strategies to different regions. ROSS utilizes Region-aware Spatial Selective Scanning (RSSS) and Region-aware Channel-oriented Selective Scanning (RCSS) to integrate long-range dependencies in spatial and channel dimensions, respectively, to achieve accurate texture restoration and color modeling. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that MRU-Mamba outperforms recent UIE methods in both qualitative and quantitative experimental results.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70280-4.title: A population-based analysis evaluating risk of second primary upper abdominal cancers following radiotherapy for resectable gastric cancer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70280-4.abstract: Abstract Radiotherapy is widely used in the perioperative treatment of gastric cancer. But the risk of second primary upper abdominal cancers in gastric cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy is still unclear. From the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, 6666 patients with gastric cancer between January 1975 and December 2010 from 8 registries were included in the analysis. Fine-Gray competing risk regression was used to analyze the cumulative incidence of second primary upper abdominal cancers. The radiotherapy-associated risk for gastric cancer patients was estimated by Poisson regression. The long-term survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier method. Among 6666 patients, 1138 (17.1%) patients received radiotherapy and surgery, 5528 (82.9%) patients only received surgery. The cumulative incidence of second primary upper abdominal cancers was 6.38% in patients received radiotherapy and 2.56% in patients received surgery only ( P < 0.001). In multivariable competing risk regression, radiotherapy was a risk factor of occurring second primary upper abdominal cancers ( P = 0.032; HR 1.656). In multivariable Poisson regression, radiotherapy for gastric cancer was associated with second primary upper abdominal cancers ( P = 0.002; RR 1.754). There was no significant difference in five-year survival among second primary upper abdominal cancer patients received radiotherapy or not received radiotherapy ( P = 0.167; HR 1.367). However, the 5-year survival among second primary upper abdominal cancer patients received radiotherapy was significantly lower than matched only primary upper abdominal cancer patients ( P = 0.034; HR 1.399). Radiotherapy for gastric cancer was associated with the risk of second primary upper abdominal cancers. Further research for the prevention and treatment of second primary upper abdominal cancers is necessary.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69596-y.title: Melatonin enhances drought tolerance in Myrtus communis via antioxidant defense and osmotic regulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69596-y.abstract: Drought stress is a major constraint on plant growth and metabolic stability, particularly in medicinal species. This study investigated the effects of foliar-applied melatonin (0, 50, 100, and 200 μM) on drought tolerance in Myrtus communis at three field-capacity levels (100%, 70%, and 40%). Drought significantly reduced growth, relative water content, and photosynthetic pigments, while increasing oxidative damage, as indicated by elevated H₂O₂, malondialdehyde, and ion leakage. Melatonin application, particularly at 200 µM, mitigated these effects by enhancing antioxidant defense and osmotic regulation. Increased activities of superoxide dismutase and catalase were associated with reduced oxidative stress, while higher accumulation of soluble carbohydrates, proline, and glycine betaine improved cellular water balance. In addition, melatonin stimulated the synthesis of phenolic and flavonoid compounds, thereby enhancing antioxidative capacity. Correlation analysis revealed strong associations among physiological and biochemical traits, indicating coordinated regulation of drought responses. Overall, melatonin acts as an effective modulator of drought tolerance in M. communis by integrating antioxidant and osmotic mechanisms. These findings highlight its potential for improving plant performance under water-limited conditions. Further studies are required to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and gene regulatory networks underlying melatonin-mediated drought tolerance.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69326-4.title: Coupling effects of nano-silica and steel fibers on concrete performance and microstructural characterization
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69326-4.abstract: Abstract The present investigation examines the coupled effects of steel fibre reinforcement and nano-silica (NS) addition on the permeability and mechanical properties of concrete. End-hooked steel fibres (designated as D) and sheared crimped steel fibres (designated as B) of varying lengths were first incorporated into concrete mixtures to evaluate their influence on water permeability, with the objective of identifying the fibre geometry and size that yield optimal impermeability. Experimental results demonstrated that the inclusion of either fibre type effectively enhanced the resistance to water penetration; among all tested variants, D50 (end-hooked steel fibres of 50 mm length) and B40 (sheared crimped steel fibres of 40 mm length) exhibited the most pronounced improvements, corresponding to a 33.33% and 25% reduction in permeability, respectively, relative to the plain concrete(PC) without fibres. Subsequently, D50 and B40 fibres were combined with NS at various dosages to investigate the coupling effect of fibre and NS addition on the mechanical behaviour of concrete. An orthogonal experimental design was adopted, with fibre contents of 1%, 1.5% and 2% by volume, and NS contents of 0.5%, 1% and 1.5% by mass of cementitious materials. The results indicated that the most significant enhancement in mechanical performance was achieved at 2% fibre content and 1% NS content. Under these optimal proportions, end-hooked steel fibre-reinforced concrete (E-S) exhibited a compressive strength improvement comparable to that of sheared crimped steel fibre-reinforced concrete (S-W); however, the splitting tensile strength and bending strength of E-S were considerably superior to those of S-W. The underlying mechanism governing the coupled effect of steel fibres and NS on concrete performance was further elucidated through scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analyses from a microstructural perspective. The findings provide a solid theoretical basis for understanding the combined influence of fibre reinforcement and nanoparticle incorporation on both the impermeability and mechanical response of concrete.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69397-3.title: A wearable-based pathway for characterizing COMISA, Insomnia, and OSA: a feasibility study in a community hospital
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69397-3.abstract: Abstract Comorbid insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea (COMISA) – the co-occurrence of both disorders – is associated with greater morbidity and is underdiagnosed in fragmented care outside sleep centers. This study examined the feasibility of using an AI-powered wearable device, the Belun Ring (BR), to characterize COMISA, insomnia, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in a community hospital setting. Consecutive new patients undergoing baseline diagnostic evaluation were classified as having OSA if AHI ≥ 15, as insomnia when met ICSD-3 clinical criteria or ISI ≥ 15 pragmatically when interview data were inconclusive. Diagnosed COMISA if both conditions were present. Participants completed at least 3 nights of BR assessment with sleep architecture, respiratory metrics, and pulse rate variability compared using nonparametric tests, regression analyses, and principal component analysis. Among 96 participants (13 COMISA, 47 insomnia, 36 OSA), COMISA and insomnia showed longer sleep onset latency, greater wake after sleep onset (WASO), and more awakenings than OSA, while AHI was higher in OSA and COMISA. In the prespecified primary non-AHI multinomial model, sleep efficiency, REM, total sleep time, and WASO retained discriminatory information. A supportive robustness model replacing AHI metrics with BR-derived hypoxic burden improved model fit. Multi-night wearable monitoring may complement group-level phenotype characterization and early triage in real-world sleep services.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69513-3.title: Duty cycle shapes multi-mode transient responses in intermittent rotor–stator rub with no evidence of Sommerfeld capture
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69513-3.abstract: A multi-mode model is presented for the transient passage of a flexible rotor through its first critical speed with unilateral rotor–stator contact. The shaft is discretised with Euler–Bernoulli finite elements, with disks and elastic supports included before modal extraction and mass normalisation. Penetration is calculated from the physical displacement at the rub plane, and the contact forces are projected onto all retained modes. A torque-limited drive law is coupled to the lateral equations through the unbalance acceleration and friction torque. Contact near the first critical speed increases the displacement peak from 38.04 to 46.70 $$\mu$$m over 0.110 s, with a maximum normal force of 4.67 N. No Sommerfeld capture is observed over the parameter ranges examined. The instantaneous friction torque reaches $$68\%$$ of the drive torque, but the revolution-averaged value that the drive must overcome stays below $$5\%$$ because contact occupies about one tenth of a revolution. A nonlinear induction-motor law of matched torque near resonance changes the peak by $$0.08\%$$. Non-synchronous amplitudes remain below $$0.5\%$$ of the synchronous component, and a constant-speed scan over 51 operating points remains period one. Four published datasets are used only for contextual comparison, because their rigs and contact parameters differ from the model.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69844-1.title: LDA-YOLO11: a lightweight detail-attention detector for edge-deployable road surface defect detection
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69844-1.abstract: Road surface defects, such as cracks, pavement damage and potholes, shorten road service life and affect driving safety and preventive maintenance. Existing lightweight object detectors are computationally efficient but still suffer from missed detections and unstable localization when dealing with elongated cracks, weak-texture damage and complex pavement backgrounds. To address these issues, this study proposes LDA-YOLO11, a lightweight detail-attention road defect detector based on YOLO11n. The model improves the neck feature fusion stage while keeping the original YOLO11n backbone and $$P_3^{\prime }$$, $$P_4$$ and $$P_5$$ detection heads unchanged. A $$P_2$$-guided Detail-Neck is designed to inject shallow high-resolution detail information into the $$P_3^{\prime }$$ feature without adding an independent $$P_2$$ detection head. Efficient Channel Attention modules are further introduced after the final $$P_3^{\prime }$$ and $$P_4$$ fusion features to recalibrate defect-related channel responses and suppress background interference. Experimental results show that LDA-YOLO11 achieves mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 values of 0.951 and 0.791, improving YOLO11n by 2.3 and 1.7% points, respectively. On the Jetson Orin NX platform, TensorRT FP16 acceleration reduces the inference latency to 27 ms/image, corresponding to 37.03 FPS, while causing only a 0.2%-point decrease in mAP@0.5. These results indicate that LDA-YOLO11 demonstrates promising edge deployment feasibility and real-time inference capability for road surface defect detection.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69430-5.title: MAFT: a multimodal attention fusion transformer framework with frozen pretrained encoders for conversational emotion recognition
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69430-5.abstract: This paper addresses multimodal emotion recognition in multi-party dialogue, combining transcripts, speech waveforms, and video of speakers’ faces. This article presents Multimodal Attention Fusion Transformer (MAFT), a framework built around various persistent difficulties such as: neutral utterances account for close to half of all labels, the transcript channel outperforms audio and video by a wide margin, and the non-text signals on this particular dataset suffer from laugh-track contamination, frequent camera switches, and occluded faces. MAFT presents an attention-based multimodal fusion framework evaluated on the MELD benchmark using frozen pretrained encoders. The current fusion mechanism pairs every combination of two modalities through cross-attention, then applies a per-pair sigmoid gate an explicit kill switch that lets the network zero out a channel when it degrades the prediction for a given input. Modality importance starts at a hand-picked ratio of 0.5/0.3/0.2 (text/audio/video); a lightweight MLP conditioned on conversational context adjusts these on every sample. Training uses cosine-annealed class-level curriculum scheduling that rotates emphasis from high-frequency emotions toward rare ones over 50 epochs, alongside a combined focal and supervised contrastive objective. All feature encoders are frozen: RoBERTa-large (1024-d), HuBERT-large (1024-d), MARLIN (768-d). The system reaches 69.2% weighted F1 on MELD’s test partition on this earliest prototype, which relied on base-scale encoders without any of these mechanisms, managed 57.3%.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69966-6.title: Relationships between temperature-humidity index and the cheese-making potential of dairy milk in temperate environments
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69966-6.abstract: Abstract In response to climate change, indoor stalling challenges, and the sensitivity of dairy cows to elevated temperatures (often initiated at THI > 68), previous research has primarily targeted the effects of elevated THI, creating a gap in knowledge regarding low THI. Yet, freezing winters still reduce milk quality and productivity of high-yielding cows. This study investigates the association between different THI classes (< 40, 40–70, and > 80) on the yield, composition, and technological properties of milk from temperate-climate dairy cattle by analyzing 867 records across two years from 338 healthy cows in three herds. THI classes were associated with milk yield and its adjusted yields ( p < 0.01, p < 0.05). Milk production was highest within THI 40–70. Fat-corrected milk (FCM) yield peaked under high thermal conditions (THI > 80, p < 0.01), whereas value-corrected milk (VCM) and laboratory curd yield significantly decreased as THI rose ( p < 0.01). THI did not affect coagulation time or visual quality scores. Somatic cell count (lnSCC) and free fatty acids remained stable across all groups. Therefore, temperate-climate breeding programs and immediate herd management strategies must mitigate these challenges. This should enhance cow resilience to THI extremes, which is crucial for high-yielding breeds like Holstein-Friesian.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70400-0.title: Characterization of Escherichia coli isolated from wildlife in Iran: a comparative study with human isolates
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70400-0.abstract: Information on wildlife-derived bacteria, particularly in Iran, remains limited. This study determined the phenotypic and genotypic features of 103 fecal Escherichia coli (E. coli) isolates from wildlife in Bamou National Park, southern Iran, and compared them with 30 human fecal isolates (20 park rangers and 10 controls without wildlife contact). Wildlife isolates exhibited low resistance (< 15%) to only three of nine tested antibiotics (gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, and doxycycline), whereas resistance was more common in human isolates. Multidrug resistance occurred in < 2% of wildlife isolates but reached 20% in rangers. No wildlife isolate produced extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs), compared with 25% of ranger isolates and 10% of controls. Class I integrons were detected in 12.6% of wildlife isolates, 35% of ranger isolates, and 30% of controls, while Class II integrons were identified only in 2.9% of wildlife isolates. Biofilm formation occurred in 13.6% of wildlife isolates, 5% of ranger isolates, and 40% of controls, predominantly as weak biofilms. Adhesion-related virulence genes were widely distributed with no significant differences among groups. The findings suggest the infiltration of antimicrobial resistance determinants into the wildlife microbiota. Also, biofilm-forming isolates and the high prevalence of adhesion-related virulence genes highlight their potential survival and transmissibility in natural ecosystems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69942-0.title: Production of 3D-printed functional milk chocolate with postbiotics of Bifidobacterium animalis ssp. lactis BB-12
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69942-0.abstract: The present study was conducted to evaluate the impact of three different concentrations of Bifidobacterium animalis ssp. lactis BB-12 postbiotics (0.5, 0.75 and 1%) on the functional and physicochemical properties of 3D-printed milk chocolate. Supplementation of postbiotics resulted in significant changes in chocolate attributes in a concentration-dependent manner. The antioxidant capacity was enhanced at all concentrations, with the highest activity observed at 1%, despite minimal changes in total phenolic content. This suggests that the improved antioxidant capacity was largely due to non-phenolic compounds. Rheological and textural properties were significantly influenced; 0.5–0.75% of postbiotics reduced chocolate hardness (1377–1488 g) and enhanced its flowability, whereas 1% postbiotics increased chocolate hardness by up to 2558 g and viscosity, which may be associated with changes in the physical organization of the chocolate matrix. The thermal stability remained largely unchanged (Tp ≈ 34.4–35.7 °C; To ≈ 28–31 °C), indicating that postbiotics incorporation did not affect the cocoa butter crystallizing behavior. Significant differences in color (L* reduced, a* increased) occurred at 0.5–0.75% concentrations. In general, 3D-printed functional milk chocolate enriched with B. lactis BB-12 postbiotics can be considered a promising approach for incorporating bioactive ingredients into confectionery products.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70076-6.title: Rotenone targeting the oxidative phosphorylation pathway improves invasive lesions in ovarian endometriosis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70076-6.abstract: Abstract Endometriosis (EM) is a prevalent gynecological disorder characterized by diagnostic difficulty and high recurrence rates. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to characterize endometrial stromal cell (ESC) subpopulations in EM, investigate the involvement of the oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathway in EM pathogenesis and fibrosis, and assess the therapeutic effects of Rotenone, a mitochondrial electron transport chain complex I inhibitor. Twelve endometrial single-cell samples from the GSE179640 dataset were analyzed to compare cellular composition between EM and control groups, and to identify EM-associated pathways using Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis. The role of OXPHOS was further validated using clinical samples, in vitro assays, and in vivo animal models, with evaluation of histopathology, fibrosis, and mitochondrial function. scRNA-seq analysis demonstrated increased proportions of stromal, lymphoid, and myeloid cells in EM. Subcluster analysis of ESC subclusters revealed enrichment of the eStromal_cycling population, with differentially expressed genes significantly associated with the OXPHOS pathway. Ectopic EM lesions exhibited disrupted tissue architecture, increased collagen deposition, elevated mitochondrial complex I activity and adenosinetriphosphate (ATP) levels. OXPHOS-related proteins were co-localized with Vimentin in ectopic tissues. In vitro, Rotenone suppressed proliferation, migration, and invasion of ectopic endometrial stromal cells (ecESCs), and reduced complex I activity, ATP production, and OXPHOS protein expression. In vivo, Rotenone treatment reduced ovarian cystic lesions and adhesions, decreased fibrosis area, restored estradiol and progesterone levels, and reduced the co-localization of OXPHOS and stromal markers. These findings indicate that activation of the OXPHOS pathway in stromal cells is associated with disease progression and fibrosis. Inhibition of mitochondrial complex I attenuated lesion development and fibrosis in experimental models, suggesting that metabolic modulation may represent a potential therapeutic approach for EM.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-57766-x.title: Effect of dietary Solanum nigrum on growth, immunity, and disease resistance against Aeromonas hydrophila infection in Labeo rohita (Hamilton, 1822) fingerlings
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-57766-x.abstract: Abstract Solanum nigrum leaf meal (SNLM) could be a promising phytobiotic with growth and immunomodulatory effects in aquaculture species. Phytochemical profiling revealed a diverse composition of bioactive constituents, which includes flavonoids, phenolic acids, terpenoids, amino acids, minerals, and vitamins. Further, a sixty-day feeding experiment was undertaken to study the influence of SNLM-incorporated diets on growth promotion, haematobiochemical indices, and immunological responses in rohu infected with Aeromonas hydrophila . Control and SLNM incorporated diets containing graded concentrations of SNLM, viz., 0%, 0.25%, 0.5%, 1.0%, and 2.0% were fed to fish. The results revealed a pronounced elevation in growth parameters in the 2.0% SNLM-fed group. The haematological and immunological parameters, including RBC, PCV, haemoglobin, lysozyme, respiratory burst, and myeloperoxidase activity were highest in rohu fed with 2.0% SNLM diet. Furthermore, dietary SNLM notably enhanced serum protein, albumin, and globulin levels, while curbing triglycerides, glucose, cholesterol, ALT, and AST after pathogen challenge. The SNLM groups demonstrated substantially higher cumulative survival compared to the post-challenge control group against A. hydrophila . Hence, this study established that supplementation with SNLM at 2.0% level significantly improved growth, haematological, and immunological responses, and lowered mortality of L. rohita against A. hydrophila infection, indicating its potential as a phytobiotic aquafeed additive.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69304-w.title: Few-shot learning with enhanced calibration for language- and harm-aware multilingual hate speech detection (FLEC-HS)
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69304-w.abstract: Multilingual hate speech detection remains challenging in low-resource settings, where labelled data are limited, particularly for identity-targeted and context-dependent content. We present Few-Shot Learning with Enhanced Calibration for Language- and Harm-Aware Multilingual Hate Speech Detection (FLEC-HS). This modular framework combines few-shot prompting with a frozen GPT-4o model and a lightweight Feature-Conditioned Calibration Layer (FCL) for post-hoc probability calibration. The primary evaluation uses HateDay (approximately 160,000 posts across eight languages), while HateCheck and HateXplain provide complementary functional and cross-dataset diagnostics. The term few-shot refers specifically to the prompting stage, which uses up to K = 16 demonstrations per language. The complete system additionally uses approximately 400 labelled development instances per language to train the FCL and select operating thresholds. Thresholds are selected by five-fold cross-validation on development data and frozen before test evaluation. On HateDay, FLEC-HS achieves a macro-F1 of 0.64, compared with 0.56 for the fully fine-tuned XLM-R-large. At the development-selected operating point requiring hate-class precision of at least 95%, hate recall increases from 0.48 to 0.61. Relative to the fully fine-tuned XLM-R-large baseline (48% review share), FLEC-HS reduces the share of posts sent to human review to 28% under the evaluated entropy-routing policy. Removing the FCL reduces macro-F1 to 0.59 and increases the protected-group false-negative rate from 5.1 to 10.4%. Protected-group fairness is operationalised narrowly through false-negative rates derived from dataset metadata; no broader fairness guarantee is claimed. The findings are limited to the evaluated benchmarks and configuration and remain subject to domain shift, commercial API dependencies, and incomplete coverage of dialects and protected groups.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69386-6.title: A randomized field experiment comparing nudges and boosts for household electricity conservation in student housing
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69386-6.abstract: Abstract Behavioral interventions can promote household energy conservation, yet evidence on the mediators and moderators driving their effects remains limited. In a 24-week randomized field experiment with 140 student households, we contrasted two behavioral interventions: a social comparison “nudge” with a competence-enhancing “boost”. Specifically, the nudged group received weekly normative feedback on their electricity use relative to their peers, while the boosted participants accessed device-specific energy-saving tips. Both treatments significantly reduced electricity consumption relative to control by attenuating the seasonal increase observed among untreated households, corresponding to avoided consumption of ~7 MWh. Exploratory analyses indicated that the effects were concentrated among participants with higher baseline consumption. Within this group, the Boost intervention was associated with a statistically significant reduction of 3.97 kWh per week relative to control. The nudged participants reduced their weekly consumption by 3.12 kWh. While both interventions performed similarly over time, evidence for competence enhancement was limited: competence scores increased modestly in the boost group relative to control, but this effect became marginal after correcting for multiple testing. Further evidence indicates that intervention effects were strongest among participants with higher pre-treatment competence and environmental motivation, suggesting a moderating role of these variables.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61498-3.title: A framework for spatial modelling of potentials for vegetation development and associated land use in heterogeneous landscapes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-61498-3.abstract: Understanding spatial variation in ecological opportunity is fundamental to predicting vegetation development and informing land-use planning, yet existing geoecological models are often constrained by categorical inputs, genesis-based classifications and dependence on current land use and vegetation patterns. Here we present a holistic, unsupervised framework for delineating geoecological land units and gradients using continuous environmental variables selected for high temporal permanence. The method integrates topographic, pedological, and hydrological factors through a grouped principal component analysis followed by multivariate clustering, enabling balanced representation of interacting ecological factors without predefined hierarchies. Applied at 10 m resolution in Eastern Denmark, the model identifies 16 geotope categories representing discrete, functional land unit types for vegetation development. Statistical validation shows that multivariate heterogeneity is concentrated at geotope boundaries, while interiors are internally more homogeneous. This indicates a robust delineation of patch–gradient landscape structure and validates the model design. The framework provides a scalable approach for mapping geoecological potentials relevant to conservation planning, vegetation modelling, land suitability assessment, opportunity mapping and land system analysis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68447-0.title: Analysis of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases medications and diagnostic equipment in primary healthcare institutions in Henan Province, China
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68447-0.abstract: To evaluate medication and diagnostic equipment availability for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases (CCVDs) in primary healthcare institutions and identify gaps between urban and rural settings. A mixed-methods study was conducted in Henan Province from July 1 to October 30, 2024. For the quantitative component, a stratified random sample of 2,000 primary healthcare institutions was selected; 1,895 valid electronic questionnaires were analyzed. For the qualitative component, 24 staff from 8 purposively selected institutions participated in online semi-structured interviews. Categorical variables were compared using chi-square tests, while continuous variables with non-normal distribution were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Among 1,895 institutions (461 urban, 1,434 rural), the mean number of available CCVD drug categories was significantly lower in rural than in urban settings across most therapeutic classes (P < 0.05). Only six medications (valsartan, amlodipine, epinephrine, atorvastatin, Compound Danshen Dripping Pills, and Suxiao Jiuxin Pills) reached an availability rate exceeding 80%. More than 30% of institutions reported unmet demand for nitroglycerin, amiodarone, digoxin, intravenous antihypertensives, and norepinephrine. Although over 80% of institutions could perform basic diagnostics (ECG, complete blood count, fasting glucose, lipid profile, serum creatinine, and urinalysis), qualitative interviews revealed substantial shortages of up-to-date equipment. Pronounced urban–rural disparities in medication availability persist. Despite basic testing capacity, diagnostic equipment is often obsolete and insufficient. Policy measures—including supply chain improvements, prescribing regulation reforms, and collaborative hospital networks—are urgently needed to strengthen CCVD care in primary settings.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70392-x.title: Cervical cancer prevention and control strategy in Ethiopia: key informant clinicians’ perspective
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70392-x.abstract: Cervical cancer is a major public health burden in Ethiopia, ranking second among women and disproportionately affecting HIV-positive individuals. In 2023, an estimated 7445 new cases and 5338 deaths occurred. Such encumbrance escalated as compared with earlier reports, necessitating exploration of challenges and gaps in prevention and control strategies from frontline expert clinicians’ perspectives. A qualitative study design using a descriptive phenomenology strategy was employed to collect data from eight experienced clinicians selected purposively. The study conducted from eight governmental hospitals with a large client flow of HIV patients rendering cervical cancer screening services between September and October 2021 in Ethiopia. Semi-structured interviews were conducted using pre-tested guides, with detailed notes taken and later expanded. The data were translated, coded in Open Code, and analyzed using an inductive thematic analysis approach. Key findings highlighted the implementation of health education and provider training as primary prevention and screening using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) and cryotherapy as secondary prevention strategies. Challenges included lack of awareness among women (both HIV-positive and HIV-negative), staff burnout, inconsistent screening algorithms, socio-cultural barriers, and difficulties in follow-up of positive cases, with high loss to follow-up attributed to the asymptomatic nature of cervical cancer and lack of awareness about its severity. Facilitators and recommendations emphasized strengthening awareness through multi-modal approaches, assigning dedicated and trained screening staff, expanding access to screening services, improving follow-up systems, and addressing socio-cultural concerns. Self-sampling was viewed positively as a means to increase screening uptake by reducing fear and privacy-related discomfort, although ensuring specimen quality was considered essential. Evidence from this study identifies a critical need for targeted interventions among women with HIV to overcome current gaps in cervical cancer control. We urge policymakers to leverage these insights to strengthen screening programs and advance the public health goal of eliminating cervical malignancy.

doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02739-3.title: Body parts used for ancient Egyptian artworks traced to surprising source
doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02739-3.abstract: Nature - Coffin decorations and wall paintings were made with tissue from a broad range of organisms.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77564-3.title: Overcoming polarization-breakdown trade-off via hydrogen bonding-modulated molecular stacking in high-temperature high-energy-density flexible dielectric
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77564-3.abstract: Flexible dielectrics suffer from an inherent polarization-breakdown trade-off. Herein, we propose a hydrogen bonding-modulated molecular stacking strategy to improve high-temperature capacitive energy storage performance. A series of polyetherimide copolymers with tunable hydrogen bond donors and acceptors was synthesized. Highly polarizable hydroxyl groups boost dielectric constant and increase hydrogen bond donor density. The constructed hydrogen bonding network strengthens intermolecular interactions, thermal stability, and breakdown strength. Bulky trifluoromethyl substituents enlarge interchain spacing and suppress interchain charge transport. Ultimately, the copolymer with optimal molecular stacking delivers a maximum discharged energy density of 7.34 J/cm3 with efficiency exceeding 90% at 680 MV/m and 200 °C, representing a 395.95% improvement over the pristine film and outperforming most reported flexible dielectrics. This intrinsic molecular modulation route offers a facile design strategy for designing high-temperature high-energy-density flexible dielectrics. The authors propose a molecular stacking strategy regulated by hydrogen bonding to enhance the high-temperature capacitive energy storage performance of polymer dielectrics. This special structural design achieves an energy density of 7.34 J/cm3 and an efficiency of 90% at 200 °C.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77523-y.title: Ultrahigh-sensitivity adaptive solar-blind organic neuromorphic sensors for robust corona discharge monitoring
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77523-y.abstract: Abstract Low‑cost and high‑efficiency corona-discharge detection is essential for safe high‑voltage transmission operation, yet state‑of‑the‑art solar‑blind ultraviolet (SBUV) photodetectors for corona monitoring suffer from insufficient sensitivity, poor stability and weak anti‑interference capability. Herein, we demonstrate a high-sensitivity adaptive organic neuromorphic SBUV sensor via low‑cost solution‑shearing. The device achieves ultraweak detection down to 60 nW cm −2 , with key figures‑of‑merit (photosensitivity: 1.1×10 7 , photoresponsivity: 4.6×10 7 A W⁻ 1 , specific detectivity: 2.9×10 18 Jones and external quantum efficiency: 2.2×10 8 %), all outperforming state-of-the-art SBUV detectors. The sensor exhibits strong SBUV spectral selectivity, featuring a 25 ms photoresponse and favorable stability after one‑year storage. Enabled by integrated sensing‑storage‑calculation neuromorphic mechanism, it enables reliable scotopic/photopic adaptive detection and rapid patterning within 2 s at 100% analog recognition accuracy. Practical corona‑discharge simulations confirm its high anti‑interference performance, precise classification and reliable early‑warning capability. This work provides a feasible proof‑of‑concept for adaptive organic neuromorphic SBUV sensors toward intelligent corona‑discharge monitoring in smart power systems.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77407-1.title: Unified down-stream analysis of crosslinking mass spectrometry results with pyXLMS
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77407-1.abstract: Abstract Crosslinking mass spectrometry has become the method of choice for the identification of protein-protein interactions and for gaining insight into the structures of proteins in vivo. However, connecting crosslink search engine results with down-stream analysis tools, and therefore gaining biological insight from crosslink identifications, has remained a manual and cumbersome step in the analysis that often requires expert bioinformatics knowledge. Here we introduce pyXLMS, a python package and public web application which aims to simplify and streamline this intermediate step, enabling researchers even without bioinformatics knowledge to conduct in-depth crosslink analyses. In its current state pyXLMS supports input from more than seven different crosslink search engines, as well as the mzIdentML format of the HUPO Proteomics Standards Initiative. Data processing and quality control is facilitated by functionality that is directly available within pyXLMS such as aggregation, validation, annotation, filtering, and visualization. In addition, the data can easily be exported to more than ten supported down-stream analysis tools and formats. We demonstrate the applicability and benefits of pyXLMS by re-analyzing a publicly available crosslink dataset with a variety of different search engines and show how the same data analysis workflow can be applied using pyXLMS.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69047-8.title: Mixed T-cell chimerism at 3 months predicts late relapse in acute myeloid leukemia after allogeneic stem cell transplantation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69047-8.abstract: Abstract Relapse remains the leading cause of treatment failure after allogeneic stem cell transplantation (HCT) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), yet predictors of late relapse remain poorly defined. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study including 388 patients with AML, representing a disease-specific cohort undergoing first HCT across six Scandinavian centers to evaluate the prognostic role of early T-cell chimerism assessed at three months post-HCT. Mixed T-cell chimerism (MTC) was defined as < 95% donor-derived CD3 + T cells. Among patients alive and relapse-free at 12 months, three-month MTC was associated with a significantly higher 5-year cumulative incidence of relapse compared with complete T-cell chimerism (29% vs 17%, p = 0.024) and inferior 5-year RFS (62% vs 74%, p = 0.017). In contrast, pre-HCT measurable residual disease (MRD) was primarily associated with early relapse and showed a weaker association with relapse beyond 12 months. Exploratory analyses suggested that the adverse impact of pre-HCT MRD-positivity was most pronounced among patients with MTC. These findings indicate a temporal distinction in relapse dynamics, in which residual disease burden drives early relapse, whereas impaired immune reconstitution is associated with late relapse. Early T-cell chimerism may therefore identify patients at increased risk of late relapse and could contribute to improved post-HCT risk stratification.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70061-z.title: Kinematic relationship between solar extreme ultraviolet waves and type II metric radio bursts
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70061-z.abstract: Solar extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) waves are large-scale disturbances that manifest as bright wavefronts, often during coronal mass ejections (CMEs). According to the magnetic field line stretching model, this phenomenon comprises two components: a fast-mode CME piston-driven shock wave and a slower, nonwave component. They are often associated with solar type II radio bursts. It is expected the radio source and the fast-mode EUV wave should come from different parts of the same shock, i.e., the CME piston-driven shock, and their speeds should be strongly correlated. To investigate this relationship, we utilized high spatiotemporal resolution observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory in conjunction with radio data from the Radio Solar Telescope Network. Our analysis reveals that there exists a linear correlation between the EUV fast-mode speeds ($$v_{euv}$$) and the shock speeds derived from metric (m) type II radio bursts ($$v_{radio}$$), which is $$v_{radio}=0.89v_{euv}+51$$ km s$$^{-1}$$, with a correlation coefficient of 0.77. This strong correlation suggests that original coronal EIT waves, which are about three times slower than type II radio bursts, are not fast-mode waves, and it is misleading to map type II radio bursts to EIT waves in the literature.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69763-1.title: Mechanistic investigation of electrokinetically-controlled enhanced oil recovery in sandstone and carbonate reservoirs using a tailored cationic gemini surfactant
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69763-1.abstract: Although cationic Gemini surfactants show promise for chemical enhanced oil recovery (cEOR), the coupled influences of brine salinity and reservoir lithology on their performance remain poorly understood. This study addresses this gap by synthesizing and systematically evaluating a hexadecyl-based cationic Gemini surfactant (GEM16-2) in sandstone and carbonate systems under varying salinity and temperature conditions. Successful synthesis was verified via FTIR and NMR, while TGA/DTG indicated thermal stability up to 220 °C. GEM16-2 formed nanoscale aggregates (≈ 9.31 nm hydrodynamic diameter) and exhibited excellent halotolerance, remaining phase-stable in NaCl brines up to 22.5 wt% at 45 °C. At a concentration of 25 PPM (near its critical micelle concentration), GEM16-2 reduced oil–water interfacial tension (IFT)to 0.85 mN/m. The IFT-salinity relationship followed a U-shaped trend with a minimum at ⁓4500 ppm Na2SO4, whereas rising temperature monotonically decreased IFT up to 70 °C. Thermodynamic profiling confirmed spontaneous micellization and adsorption, the latter being energetically favored. Zeta potential, adsorption isotherms, and contact angle dynamics revealed that lithology-dependent performance is driven by electrostatic interactions. Specifically, adding 2000 ppm Na2SO4 screened electrostatic attraction in sandstone, reducing surfactant adsorption from 0.75 to 0.64 mg/g. Conversely, in carbonate, sulfate ions shifted the surface charge negatively, promoting surfactant uptake from 0.11 to 0.53 mg/g. Consequently, water contact angles decreased to 43o (sandstone) and 65o (carbonate), altering wettability. Surfactant performance in porous media was found to be lithology-dependent; specifically, ultimate spontaneous imbibition recoveries reached 24.74% and 20.85% OOIP at ≈ 2000 ppm Na₂SO₄ for sandstone and ≈ 4000 ppm Na₂SO₄ for carbonate, respectively, corresponding to improvements of 9.44 and 9.05% points over seawater. These findings demonstrate that optimal salinity for cationic Gemini-mediated cEOR is governed by lithology-specific surface-charge modulation rather than IFT minimization alone.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70105-4.title: Droplet digital PCR reveals that transgene copy number determines lifespan in SOD1G93A ALS mice
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70105-4.abstract: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a devastating neurodegenerative disease resulting in muscle weakness and eventually paralysis. Pre-clinical ALS models are a useful tool to understand mechanisms of disease development and to test therapeutic candidates. Approximately 20% of ALS cases have a genetic component, and of those, approximately 20% are attributed to mutations in the superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) gene. Multiple mouse models have been generated to study the different mutations in ALS, however, the most popular and well-characterized is the transgenic SOD1G93A mouse model. In this model, copies of the mutated human SOD1 (hSOD1) gene are inserted into the mouse genome and the number of copies correlates with severity of disease. To obtain accurate and reproducible data, it is recommended that animals are screened for their copy number prior to enrollment in a study. However, there is no widely-accepted standardized protocol for testing SOD1G93A copy number and the absolute copy number of hSOD1 insertion in mice has never been quantified. Here, we isolated DNA from a cohort of SOD1G93A animals (JAX Strain: 004435) and validated a method for absolute quantification of transgene copy number via droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). We found that both ddPCR and the current standard, qPCR, reliably determined genotype, however, ddPCR copy numbers ranged from 51.68 to 119.5 whereas qPCR reported 23 to 44.65 copies. We demonstrate that ddPCR copy number correlated significantly with disease phenotype and progression and in comparing ddPCR to real-time PCR, we determined ddPCR to be a more accurate and reliable way to measure SOD1G93A copy number.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70443-3.title: The effect of liberal and restrictive transfusion practices on survival in oncology patients with sepsis in the intensive care unit
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70443-3.abstract: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion is a commonly utilized supportive therapy in intensive care units (ICUs). However, the optimal transfusion practice in oncologic patients with sepsis remains controversial. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of liberal versus restrictive transfusion practices in oncologic patients with sepsis admitted to the ICU. This retrospective, non-randomized study included oncologic patients with sepsis admitted to the ICU between 2014 and 2023. Patients were classified as having restrictive or liberal transfusion practice based on serial hemoglobin (Hb) measurements and corresponding decisions to administer or withhold RBC transfusion, reflecting lower (< 7–8 g/dL) or higher (≤ 9–10 g/dL) Hb thresholds, respectively. Among patients who did not receive RBC transfusion, withholding transfusion at Hb levels of 7.1–8.9 g/dL and 9.1–10.0 g/dL was classified as restrictive and liberal transfusion practice, respectively; thus, actual receipt of RBC transfusion was not required for group assignment. Patients with mixed or otherwise unclassifiable transfusion practices were excluded. As treatment decisions were determined by treating physicians, the approach may introduce selection bias. Demographic characteristics, clinical scores, primary tumor type, laboratory parameters, organ dysfunction, infection characteristics, and mortality outcomes were compared. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Propensity score analysis with stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to minimize confounding and selection bias. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between transfusion practice and binary outcomes, and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess survival. A total of 658 patients were included. Baseline severity scores were higher in the restrictive transfusion group, as reflected by significantly greater Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores. There was a marked imbalance in primary tumor type’s distribution between groups, with lung cancer more frequent in the liberal group and gastrointestinal malignancies predominating in the restrictive group. Overall organ dysfunction rates were similar between groups; however, acute kidney injury occurred more frequently in the restrictive group. No differences were observed in duration of mechanical ventilation, use of vasopressors, or requirement for renal replacement therapy. Unadjusted analysis suggested higher 90-day mortality in the restrictive group, but this association was not significant after IPTW adjustment. No difference in 28-day mortality was observed. The restrictive transfusion group was associated with an increased risk of renal injury compared to the liberal transfusion group, and this association remained significant after clinical adjustment. In critically ill patients with sepsis and malignancy, restrictive and liberal transfusion practices were not associated with significant differences in mortality after IPTW adjustment. The observed association between restrictive transfusion practice and renal injury should be interpreted cautiously, as it does not establish a causal relationship. Prospective studies evaluating individualized transfusion practices are warranted.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70009-3.title: Evaluation of clinical prognostic factors for radium-223 therapy in castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone metastases: the KYUCOG-1901 study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70009-3.abstract: We evaluated clinical factors associated with symptomatic skeletal events (SSEs), radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS), and overall survival (OS) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and bone metastases treated with radium-223 (Ra-223). Of 101 enrolled patients, 93 were included in the final analysis (median follow-up, 25.2 months; interquartile range, 12.4–31.8). SSEs occurred in 26 patients (28.0%). Median rPFS and OS were 8.8 months (95% CI, 6.1–12.2) and 23.0 months (95% CI, 17.9–27.9), respectively. In multivariable analyses, prostate-specific antigen doubling time (PSADT) ≥ 3 months, estimated glomerular filtration rate ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m², and treatment completion (5–6 cycles) were independently associated with a lower risk of SSEs. Treatment completion, PSADT ≥ 3 months, and no prior androgen receptor signaling inhibitor use were independently associated with longer rPFS, whereas treatment completion was independently associated with improved OS. Treatment completion and favorable baseline tumor kinetics, particularly longer PSADT, were associated with better outcomes. Given the potential for selection bias and the exploratory nature of these observational findings, prospective studies are warranted to determine whether initiating Ra-223 during periods of lower disease activity improves outcomes and to clarify the optimal timing of treatment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69895-4.title: SPH-based numerical simulation of uniaxial compression of concrete with random polygonal aggregates
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69895-4.abstract: Random polygonal aggregates represent the most realistic morphology of aggregates in the mesostructure of concrete. Their angular characteristics and spatial distribution play a decisive role in the stress concentration, crack initiation, and planar structural response of concrete under uniaxial compression. Consequently, in-depth investigation into this subject is essential for revealing the fundamental mechanisms underlying the macroscopic mechanical behavior of concrete. To this end, this paper proposes a simulation method for uniaxial compressive failure of concrete based on smoothed particle hydrodynamics and develops a proprietary particle generation program for random polygonal aggregates. The proposed method adopts a Mohr–Coulomb criterion with tensile cutoff as the failure criterion and introduces a modified smoothing kernel function to accurately simulate spontaneous crack initiation and propagation. In terms of aggregate modeling, the separation axis theorem and ray casting method are employed to achieve automatic generation of random polygonal aggregates satisfying geometric constraints and precise classification of particle properties. Through three sets of comparative numerical examples, the effects of aggregate quantity (30, 40, 50), particle size range (4–8 mm, 4–10 mm, 4–12 mm), and effective weak interfacial zone (EWIZ) width (0.5 mm, 1.0 mm, 1.5 mm) on the two-dimensional plane-strain failure patterns of concrete are systematically investigated. The results indicate that an increase in aggregate density or a widening of the particle size range enhances the material’s brittleness within this 2D simulation framework, promoting a transition in the 2D-simulated planar failure pattern from “localized shear” to “diffuse cracking”. In contrast, an increase in the thickness of the interfacial transition zone induces a similar transition in 2D-simulated plane-strain planar failure patterns from “localized shear” to “diffuse cracking”, and reduces peak stress while increasing peak strain, which substantially enhances the material’s ductility in the 2D numerical system. Comparative verification with existing results demonstrates good agreement in terms of 2D-simulated failure morphology and crack evolution. It is worth noting that the simulated 2D failure patterns cannot be directly equated to the real 3D failure morphology of concrete, but this classification effectively reflects the meso-damage concentration and dispersion law under unified numerical conditions, supporting comparative parametric analysis. This study provides an efficient modeling approach and theoretical support for two-dimensional mesomechanical qualitative analysis of concrete with irregular aggregates, and its quantitative conclusions cannot be directly extrapolated to three-dimensional structural members without further correction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69801-y.title: Co-occurring bronchoalveolar lavage fluid microbiota and inflammatory features across BSI-defined disease severity groups during acute exacerbations of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69801-y.abstract: Airway dysbiosis and inflammation characterize bronchiectasis, but their relationship with underlying disease severity during acute exacerbations remains unclear. We analyzed 135 adults hospitalized with acute exacerbations of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis from a prospective single-center cohort. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing and inflammatory profiling. Participants were stratified by the Bronchiectasis Severity Index (BSI) as mild (n = 27), moderate (n = 37), or severe (n = 71). Covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses showed higher genus-level Pseudomonas and species-level Pseudomonas aeruginosa abundances in the severe group than in the mild and moderate groups (pairwise Padjusted ≤ 0.029) and lower Shannon diversity and Pielou evenness in the moderate and severe groups than in the mild group at both taxonomic levels (pairwise Padjusted ≤ 0.002), without moderate–severe differences in diversity. Community-level differences were modest (adjusted PERMANOVA marginal R² = 0.021–0.024, P ≤ 0.020), and PERMDISP detected no significant dispersion differences. BALF inflammatory measures also varied across groups: IL-6 and IL-8 were higher in the moderate and severe groups than in the mild group (Padjusted ≤ 0.020), and the neutrophil proportion was higher in the severe group than in the mild group (Padjusted = 0.038). An exploratory inverse association was observed between species-level Pielou evenness and reported disease duration after multiplicity correction (ρ = −0.320, Padjusted = 0.036). During acute exacerbations, BSI-defined bronchiectasis severity was associated with greater representation of Pseudomonas, particularly P. aeruginosa, within the BALF microbiota, reduced diversity and evenness, and differences in measured BALF cytokine concentrations and cellular composition. These co-occurring microbial and inflammatory features in BALF warrant longitudinal evaluation across clinical states to define their temporal dynamics and clinical relevance.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68465-y.title: Sensitivity analysis of flood frequency to the length of the data recording period
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68465-y.abstract: Abstract Floods are the significant natural events that can have profound impacts. This study examines how the length of data records affects the sensitivity of continuous probabilistic models applied in the flood frequency analysis and record periods were analyzed. The FREQ software was utilized to conduct the flood frequency analysis for the Karkheh watershed, Iran. The results revealed that the stations were categorized into two regions. In the first region, as the length of the record period increased, the coefficient of variation, skewness, and kurtosis decreased. In contrast, in the second region, these parameters increased with the extension of the record period. In terms of geomorphology, it was found that the average catchment area in the regions with decreasing parameters is larger, while the elevation in these areas is lower. This suggests that the decreasing areas are situated at the lower latitudes, lower-elevation and downstream portions of the basin, with the influence of dams also playing a significant role. In this part of the study, the 2-parameter and 3-parameter log-normal distributions exhibited a better fit compared to the other distributions. It was concluded that 46.7% of the stations showed the uncertain or unstable trends for the extreme return periods, 40% of the stations displayed a consistent trend across all of the return periods, while 13.3% of them showed an uncertain trend for the return periods greater than 50 years.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70043-1.title: A comparative study of path planning algorithms for low-altitude emergency medical UAVs considering task priorities
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70043-1.abstract: In urban emergency medical scenarios, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) path planning faces severe challenges from superimposed uncertain factors: dynamic emergency task insertions, sudden no-fly zones (NFZs), and day-to-night environmental transitions. While existing studies frequently address these issues in isolation, there remains a critical lack of systematic benchmarking frameworks that incorporate these stress factors simultaneously. Based on Guangzhou geographic data, this study constructs a medical network with 6 blood centers and 12 hospitals, designing six composite stress-testing scenarios. Seven algorithms spanning a three-tier capability gradient (exact MILP, metaheuristics MSHOA/ACO/GA/PSO, and learning-driven QALNS/PPO) are systematically evaluated across six performance dimensions. Results show MILP establishes the theoretical optimality bound (1 582 CNY) in baseline scenarios but fails to solve within 1 200 s under sudden NFZ constraints. MSHOA yields the best solution quality (1 648 CNY) in conventional settings, though performance deteriorates under high-frequency emergency insertions. Notably, PPO demonstrates exceptional robustness across all dynamic scenarios, achieving a 0.4 s replanning time and > 95% task satisfaction after 10 consecutive emergency insertions, exhibiting the strongest robustness under tested conditions. Conversely, ACO and GA path feasibility plummets (23.8% and 44.9%) upon NFZ activation, exposing limitations in knowledge transfer under coupled constraints. This study pioneers a comprehensive benchmarking framework, providing a quantitative decision-making basis for robust low-altitude medical network scheduling.
