doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68777-z.title: Dynamical and structural properties of deep eutectic solvents based on hexadecan-1-ol(cetyl alcohol) and choline chloride : influence of water on intermolecular interactions
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68777-z.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as a promising, eco-friendly, and economically viable class of solvents with broad applicability across various scientific and industrial fields. In this work, the structural and dynamic properties of a deep eutectic solvent composed of hexadecan-1-ol (cetyl alcohol) and choline chloride were systematically investigated using computational approaches, with particular attention to the effect of water content at 298 K. The intermolecular interactions governing the formation and stability of the DES were explored using COSMO-RS calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The results show that hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions play a fundamental role in determining the structural organization of the DES, as well as its molecular mobility and overall interaction network. These findings provide valuable insight into how the properties of DESs can be tuned through water content, offering guidance for improving their performance in practical applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70342-7.title: Age associations, sex differences, and interrelationships of five skeletal maturity indicators: a cross-sectional study in a Korean clinical sample
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70342-7.abstract: Abstract Skeletal maturity indicators are widely used to time orthopedic intervention, but the extent to which they convey overlapping information is unclear. In an age-balanced sample of 203 Korean subjects (100 males, 103 females) aged 6.0–20.8 years, five indicators—cervical vertebral maturation (CVM), spheno-occipital synchondrosis (SOS) fusion, and midpalatal (MPS), zygomaticotemporal (ZTS), and zygomaticomaxillary (ZMS) suture maturation—were evaluated concurrently. Age–maturation associations were assessed with Spearman correlations and Somers’ D yx , age-adjusted sex differences with the van Elteren test, and between-sex differences in these associations with age × sex interaction tests; inter-indicator relationships were examined using bootstrapped age-adjusted partial Spearman correlations. All indicators were associated with age ( P < 0.001), most strongly CVM (r s = 0.90) and SOS (r s = 0.87), whereas the intermediate stages of MPS, ZTS, and ZMS spanned broad age ranges. After age adjustment, females showed more advanced SOS and CVM stages, whereas ZTS and ZMS showed significant age × sex interactions, with stronger age–maturation associations in males. Age-adjusted inter-indicator associations were generally weak to moderate (partial r s = 0.31–0.49), except between ZTS and ZMS (partial r s = 0.76). These represent residual associations conditional on age; correlation analyses alone cannot establish interchangeability or clinical complementarity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69838-z.title: Functional resonance analysis method and monte carlo simulation: evaluating performance variability in a socio-technical direct reduction iron plant
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69838-z.abstract: Direct Reduction Iron (DRI) units are complex socio-technical systems where traditional failure-centric risk models often fail to capture emergent behaviors. This study aims to develop an integrated resilience-based framework to quantify performance variability and identify critical systemic vulnerabilities in DRI operations by combining the Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM), the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP), and Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS). The proposed framework integrates FRAM-based functional modeling with FAHP-based expert judgment weighting and MCS-based uncertainty analysis. The simulation was implemented in R, with 10,000 iterations, to quantify the propagation of variability across critical functional interactions under different operational scenarios. The results identified increased workload conditions, production shutdown and system restart, and operational delay or coordination failure as major contributors to systemic instability. Among the identified interactions, human resource evaluation and the influence of training on inspection processes were found to be critical pathways affecting system performance variability. The findings demonstrate that improving safety in DRI units requires proactive management of functional variability rather than focusing solely on preventing isolated component failures. This framework provides decision-makers with a quantitative approach to enhance operational resilience and support safety management in complex industrial systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69629-6.title: Limited structural reliability in public educational prediction benchmarks: a four-dimension audit of seven datasets
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69629-6.abstract: Abstract Across seven public educational prediction datasets, three passed all four pre-modeling reliability checks; the remaining four either failed group-aware generalization tests or lacked the provenance metadata needed to run them. One dataset was initially classified as failing but corrected after excluding group-identifier features from the holdout matrix, demonstrating that the audit can distinguish genuine cross-group confounding from feature-encoding artifacts. Each dataset was audited before model optimization using four checks: baseline gap, split instability, null separation, and metadata adequacy under group-aware holdout. The dominant failure mode was not weak iid performance alone but cross-group fragility: in the clearest case, UCI Student declined from iid $$R^2 = 0.242$$ to group-holdout $$R^2 = -0.097$$ , while Higher Ed collapsed from 0.041 to $$-8.79$$ . Increasing model complexity did not remove this pattern: ensemble models improved structurally sound datasets but amplified instability or failed under group holdout on fragile ones. An exploratory cross-dataset comparison further showed that stronger profiles clustered in larger, richer-grouped, performance-proximal datasets, while random-split performance severely overstated deployable signal in fragile datasets. Classification-metric sensitivity analyses reached the same substantive conclusions. The results show that benchmark reliability in educational AI is constrained less by algorithm choice than by data structure, group heterogeneity, and evaluation design. A reusable pre-modeling audit offers a minimum quality gate before public educational datasets support strong benchmark or deployment claims.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69586-0.title: Utilization of mobility assistive devices and associated factors among stroke survivors in Ethiopia: a multicentre cross-sectional study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69586-0.abstract: stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, associated with impaired activities of daily living, reduced independence living, poor functional outcomes, and lower quality of life. Although the use of assistive devices (ADs) for post-stroke mobility is essential, evidence from the Ethiopian context is limited. Therefore, this study aims to assess the utilization of ADs for mobility and associated factors among stroke survivors in public hospitals of the Amhara regional state, Ethiopia. An institutional-based cross-sectional study was conducted in tertiary hospitals in the Amhara region from July 01 to August 31 2024. Study participants were selected using a systematic random sampling techniques. Data were collected through a structured interview-administered questionnaire and chart review. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis were employed to identify factors significantly associated with the utilization of ADs. Variables with a p-value less than 0.05 in the multivariable analysis were considered statistically significant. Out of the total participants, 53.4% utilized ADs for mobility. Factors significantly associated with assistive device (AD) utilization included being male (AOR = 2.13, 95% CI: 1.22, 3.73), being unmarried (AOR = 2.54, 95% CI:1.39, 4.63), higher educational attainment (primary education: AOR = 2.66, 95% CI:1.29, 5.45); secondary education: AOR = 3.02, 95% CI:1.34, 6.78; diploma and above: AOR = 4.29,95% CI:2.01, 9.15), prolonged hospitalization (AOR = 2.97, 95% CI:1.34, 6.70), participation restriction (AOR = 2.58, 95% CI:1.24, 5.32), and anxiety symptoms (AOR = 2.41, 95% CI:1.29, 4.48). More than half of stroke survivors utilized ADs for mobility. Being male, being unmarried, higher educational attainment, prolonged hospitalization, participation restriction, and anxiety symptoms were positively associated with AD utilization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70526-1.title: Diagnostic performance of strain ratio combined with conventional ultrasound for cervical lymph node metastasis in head and neck neoplasms
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70526-1.abstract: Cervical lymph node metastasis is a key prognostic factor in head and neck neoplasms, yet conventional ultrasound alone is limited by morphological overlap between metastatic and benign nodes. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a combined model integrating the ultrasound strain elastography (USE)-derived strain ratio (SR) with conventional ultrasound parameters and to assess its superiority over individual parameters alone. This prospective diagnostic-accuracy study with blinded index-test consecutively enrolled patients diagnosed with head and neck neoplasms who had cervical lymph node biopsies at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University between January and December 2025. They were categorized into a metastatic group (N₁) and a non-metastatic group (N₀) based on pathological results. The study compared conventional ultrasound parameters, long-to-short axis ratio (L/S), lymph node hilar architecture, and color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI) classification and SR between the two groups. A binary logistic regression model was developed to incorporate all four variables, and a nomogram was constructed for individualized prediction. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) was used to assess the correlation of SR and cervical lymph node metastasis. Diagnostic performance was assessed and compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and DeLong’s test for area under the curve (AUC) comparisons. Model calibration and clinical utility were further assessed using a calibration curve and decision curve analysis (DCA). Subgroup analyses stratified by sex, age, and education level were also performed. 90 patients with head and neck neoplasms were analyzed. Four parameters (age, sex, marital status, and smoking) differed significantly between the N1 and N0 groups (all P < 0.05). RCS analysis result revealed that SR had a significant association with cervical lymph node metastasis (P-overall = 0.005). Among individual parameters, CDFI classification achieved the highest AUC of 0.809. The combined model demonstrated superior diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.910 (95% CI: 0.831–0.960), sensitivity of 89.5%, specificity of 78.8%, and accuracy of 83.3%, significantly outperforming each individual parameter by DeLong’s test (all P < 0.05). The calibration curve indicated acceptable model fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.549), and decision curve analysis confirmed positive net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities (0-0.90). Subgroup analyses revealed that combined model had favorable clinical utility and wide generalizability (all AUC > 0.870). The combined model integrating SR with conventional ultrasound parameters achieved an AUC of 0.910, significantly outperforming each individual parameter, and demonstrated favorable calibration and clinical utility. These findings support its potential as a practical and radiation-free tool for preoperative cervical lymph node evaluation in patients with head and neck neoplasms, warranting further validation in multicenter studies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67886-z.title: Iron(III) complex impacts Toxoplasma gondii growth by inducing parasite membrane alterations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67886-z.abstract: Therapies for toxoplasmosis are limited, emphasizing the need for treatment options. The in vitro effect of the mononuclear iron(III) complex [Fe(HL1)Cl₃](HL1 = N-2[(pyridine-2-ylmethyl)amino]ethanol) on LLC-MK2 host cells infected with Toxoplasma gondii was investigated. Complex showed low cytotoxicity to host cells up to 500 µM but inhibited parasite growth with IC50 values of 12.4 nM and 56.0 nM after 24 h and 48 h, respectively demonstrating selective cytotoxicity toward the parasite. These values indicate that the complex is more potent than sulfadiazine and pyrimethamine, two clinically used anti-Toxoplasma agents. The effect of the complex was irreversible after 48 h of treatment and compound withdrawal. Treated infected cells displayed fewer parasites with a rounded morphology. Ultrastructural analysis revealed severe damage of the parasite, including membrane blebbing, cytoplasmic clefts, and rupture of membranes. Biophysical studies demonstrated that the complex caused membrane disruption in parasite-mimicking membranes while increasing order in mammalian-like membranes. These findings suggest that the complex induces membrane alterations in the parasite and displays potent antiparasitic activity at nanomolar concentrations.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67905-z.title: Kinetics and adsorption isotherm of cadmium and lead on waste- agricultural derived biochar and their stabilization in two different polluted soils
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67905-z.abstract: Abstract The current study evaluated sugarcane bagasse biochar (SCBB) as an adsorbent for cadmium (Cd²⁺ ) and lead ( Pb²⁺). By using the stirred-batch technique, a kinetic experiment was conducted at two concentrations, while an adsorption isotherm experiment was performed at five concentrations. Furthermore, the role of SCBB at doses (0%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%) for stabilization of Cd 2+ and Pb 2+ in two polluted soils (S(I), S(II)) and decreasing their bioavailability was assessed through pot experiment. Results showed that equilibrium was achieved after 2 h for Cd 2+ and after 1 h for Pb 2+ . Pseudo second-order model was more fitted for kinetic data (R²= 0.99) for Cd²⁺ and Pb²⁺ at two concentrations; thus, chemisorption may controladsorption process. Adsorption isotherm results were better represented by the Langmuir model (R²= 0.99). Consequently, monolayer adsorption may be the main mechanism in Cd²⁺ and Pb²⁺ adsorption. The efficiency of Pb²⁺ removal by SCBB was higher than that of Cd²⁺, where it was 60%, while for Cd²⁺ it was 50% at the same initial concentration. Cultivation experiment demonstrated that SCBB could significantly decrease Cd²⁺ and Pb²⁺ uptake by radish plants. The percentage of decrease in Cd²⁺ content in shoot was 49% and 54%, while it was 57% and 45% for Pb 2+ at SCBB 2% in S(I) and S(II), respectively. A positive correlation between DTPA- extracted Cd 2+ and Pb 2+ in soil and their content in plant was obtained. An increase in CEC, OM of the agricultural environment, and dry biomass of shoot and root was observed. Therefore, resourceful utilization of SCBB is a beneficial method for removing lead and cadmium from aqueous solutions and stabilizing them in polluted soil.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63236-1.title: Gamma irradiation effects on optical, luminescent, and electrical properties of CeO2, Ho2O3, and Sm2O3 doped borophosphate glasses
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-63236-1.abstract: Abstract A series of undoped and rare-earth oxide-doped borophosphate glasses (CeO 2 , Ho 2 O 3 , Sm 2 O 3 ) was successfully synthesized via melt-quenching and annealing techniques, with x-ray diffraction confirming their amorphous nature through characteristic broad halos devoid of sharp crystalline peaks. Ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) absorption spectra of the undoped base glass revealed prominent UV bands at 265 nm and 330 nm before gamma irradiation, which persisted post-75 kGy exposure with only modest intensity reductions, indicating subtle radiation-induced modifications in defect states without profile disruption. CeO 2 —doped glasses exhibited three strong UV peaks at 220, 260, and 327 nm. At the same time, Ho 3+ -doped variants displayed a UV band at 295 nm alongside visible-NIR transitions at 418, 451, 482, 539, 644, 894, 1146, and 1944 nm from 5 I 8 ground state excitations; Sm 2 O 3 -doped glasses showed distinct f-f transitions at 354, 403, 470, 920, 1064, 1221, 1365, 1474, and 1520 nm. Photoluminescence analysis highlighted intrinsic features such as a 330 nm excitation and 408 nm emission in CeO 2 —doped glasses, three excitation peaks (350, 364, 387 nm) and emissions at 487 and 573 nm in Ho 2 O 3 -doped glasses, and seven excitation peaks (345–475 nm at λ ex = 598 nm) in Sm 2 O 3 -doped glasses, all exhibiting characteristic intensity decreases post-irradiation. CIE 1931 chromaticity coordinates positioned CeO 2 —doped emissions in bluish-purple, Ho 2 O 3 -doped in green (0.275, 0.405 pre-irradiation), and Sm 2 O 3 -doped in reddish-orange regions. Electrically, AC conductivity showed a slight decrease followed by an increase with rising temperature across compositions, DC conductivity displayed non-monotonic behavior with a minimum at 384 K, and real dielectric permittivity (ε′) was elevated at low frequencies due to space charge polarization. Overall, gamma irradiation induced only minor effects on optical and electrical properties, attributable to dopant-driven structural modifications like non-bridging oxygen formation and enhanced charge carrier pathways via modifier ions, underscoring the radiation resilience and potential of these glasses for luminescent, photonic, and radiation-resistant applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69669-y.title: CE-RS-SBCIT: A novel channel-enhanced hybrid CNN–transformer with residual, spatial, and boundary-aware learning for brain tumor MRI analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69669-y.abstract: Brain tumors are among the most life-threatening diseases, where early detection and accurate classification are critical for effective diagnosis and treatment planning. Although deep learning-based computer-aided diagnosis systems have shown remarkable progress, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) still face challenges such as limited global-local feature integration, sensitivity to structural heterogeneity, and high computational cost. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid framework, termed CE-RS-SBCIT, which integrates residual and spatial learning with transformer-driven contextual modeling. The proposed framework architecture combines five core components: (i) a smoothing and boundary-based CNN-integrated Transformer (SBCIT) for enhanced local-global representation learning, (ii) residual and spatial CNNs modules for capturing fine-grained textures and structural variations, (iii) a multi-scale channel attention and squeezing (MSCAS) mechanism for adaptive feature weighting, (iv) a channel enhancement (CE) strategy for enriched feature fusion, and (v) a pixel-level spatial attention module for improved inter-class discrimination. Extensive experiments on publicly available magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance, with 98.30% accuracy, 98.08% sensitivity, 98.43% precision, and an F1 Score of 98.25%. Comparative and ablation analyses further confirm the effectiveness of the proposed architecture in capturing both heterogeneous and homogeneous tumor characteristics while maintaining computational efficiency. These results indicate that CE-RS-SBCIT provides a robust and generalizable solution for brain tumor classification and has strong potential for deployment in clinical decision support systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70148-7.title: Ecological momentary insights into cannabis use and its contexts: a pre-post legalization study in Germany
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70148-7.abstract: Abstract Globally, cannabis ranks third in psychoactive substance prevalence after nicotine and alcohol, with heavy use linked to psychosis, anxiety, and depression. However, real-time data on how legal reforms influence consumption remain scarce. This Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) study analyzed daily cannabis use patterns before and after Germany’s recreational cannabis decriminalization in April 2024 in 49 individuals (34.7% women, age 33.8 ± 11 years). Following the legal reform, a selective increase in consumed amounts among younger individuals (β = 0.01, 95%CI = 0.00–0.02, z = 3.05) was observed. Further, consumed amounts increased in outdoor (β = 0.19, 95%CI = 0.04–0.34, z = 2.51) but decreased in public settings (β = -0.46, 95%CI = -0.66 - -0.25, z = -4.36), and consumption was more likely to occur on holidays (β = 3.91, 95%CI = 1.68–9.08, z = 3.17). All ps < 0.05. By capturing the immediate post-legalization period, this study contributes to important early insights to inform prevention, treatment, and regulation.
