doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67870-7.title: Genetic fate of the endangered Scarce fritillary Euphydryas maturna with a focus on East Central Europe
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67870-7.abstract: Abstract DNA in museum collections harbours rich information on the past population genetics of endangered species, including butterflies. The remnant (meta)populations of Euphydryas maturna (Nymphalidae), a specialist of open-canopy woodlands, are imperilled by habitat loss and fluctuations in abundance; earlier allozyme studies documented low effective population sizes. Triggered by the fate of the last Czech population (extinct in the wild, highly inbred ex situ), we analysed 24 past, 17 recent, and 3 captive-reared population samples from Central Europe spanning over a century (past amplification rate: 72%). We also analysed 92 individuals for the mitochondrial COI barcode. The populations displayed higher expected (mean H e : 0.60) than observed ( H o : 0.36) heterozygosity, extreme inbreeding ( F IS : 0.39), and high differentiation ( F ST : 0.19). Time-defined samples from identical locations revealed cases of genetic deteriorations, but also extinctions not preceded by genetic declines, and genetic augmentation, possibly by unreported past transfers. The COI barcodes revealed 12 haplotypes, several of which were widespread across Europe and adjacent regions, with local derivatives in particular areas. The species was once persisting via metapopulation dynamics over contiguous open-canopy woodlands. Traditional forest uses contributed to its survival in progressively fragmented landscapes. We recommend crossing the inbred ex-situ individuals with butterflies from several extant populations for reintroductions. Restoring open-canopy woodlands is imperative for long-term survival of the species.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67251-0.title: Chemometric insights into Lactiplantibacillus plantarum effects on onion (Allium cepa L.) metabolism and antidiabetic activity under cadmium stress
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67251-0.abstract: Abstract Cadmium (Cd) is a toxic heavy metal that causes severe physiological damage in plants, inhibiting growth and ultimately reducing crop yield. Lactic acid bacteria regulate Cd availability through bioaccumulation and biosorption. This study evaluated the Cd tolerance of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum 10CH by determining its survival capacity under Cd stress and its potential to mitigate Cd-induced stress in onion ( Allium cepa L.). The bacterial strain tolerated Cd concentrations up to 100 µM, and whole-genome sequencing identified genes involved in Cd biosorption, accumulation, and efflux. Exposure of onion to increasing CdCl 2 concentrations significantly reduced root and shoot biomass. Inoculation with Lb. plantarum 10CH alleviated Cd stress at 100 µM, enhancing root and shoot biomass, reducing Cd accumulation, lowering oxidative damage markers, and stimulating antioxidant enzyme activities. Metabolic profiling revealed that Cd stress significantly reduced primary metabolites and amino acids, particularly at 100 µM, while bacterial inoculation restored key amino acids and peptides, including arginine, tyrosine, and glutamic acid. Chemometric analysis using unsupervised (PCA) and supervised (OPLS-DA) models revealed clear metabolite variation among untreated, Cd-stressed, and bacterial inoculated Cd-stressed onion leaves. Furthermore, leaf extracts exhibited α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, with the highest activity in control plants (IC 50 = 425.2 ± 0.5 µg/mL). Cd-stressed plants showed moderate antidiabetic activity, which was significantly reduced by bacterial inoculation. Overall, these findings demonstrate that Lb. plantarum 10CH can survive under Cd stress and alleviates Cd-induced stress in onion, highlighting its potential as a bioinoculant to mitigate heavy metal stress.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67910-2.title: Complex LED light regimens differentially regulate tomato growth, yield formation and fruit quality
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67910-2.abstract: Abstract Tomato is a very important horticultural crop worldwide, valued for its economic significance and nutritional benefits. Tomato fruits are rich in essential nutrients and bioactive compounds, including vitamins, carotenoids, and polyphenols. In this study, we investigated how light quality and intensity influence plant growth, yield, and fruit quality parameters in tomato. Plants were grown under six different light regimens, including varying red-to-blue ratios, wide spectral white light with or without far-red application at two light intensities (300 μmol m −2 s −1 and 500 μmol m −2 s −1 ). Our results demonstrated that blue light promoted flowering and fruit set, leading to a higher number of fruits; however, under lower light intensity, this resulted in smaller fruits. In contrast, red-dominant or broad-spectrum light conditions produced less but larger and sweeter fruits, even at low light intensity. Higher light intensity overall increased total yield and sugar accumulation, also indicating enhanced photosynthetic activity and preferential allocation of assimilates to fruit biomass. Interestingly, lycopene content was not affected by any light treatment at all. Our findings showed that a careful consideration is required when selecting the intensity and spectral composition of an artificial lighting in indoor cultivation systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70229-7.title: An intelligent model for surface and subsurface water simulation considering the effect of pipeline siltation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70229-7.abstract: Siltation in stormwater pipes is an important contributor to urban flooding, yet its effects on pipe-scale hydraulic resistance and surface–subsurface flow exchange are not adequately represented in existing models. This study integrates the multi-factor coupling probability sedimentation function, Chaos adaptive genetic algorithm for optimization of probabilistic deposition, and attention bidirectional long short-term memory neural network, and proposes an intelligent prediction model for the sedimentation of pipeline siltation particles. On this basis, the instantaneous continuity control equation of fluid dynamic evolution process, instantaneous momentum conservation control equation, sedimentation pipeline flow control equation, and translation control equation are introduced to establish a high‑resolution model of overflow characteristics in sediment‑clogged pipes. Finally, by integrating the water flow exchange control equations of clogged pipes in different scenarios, a flood evolution simulation model considering the influence of pipe clogging is proposed. The comparative analysis results show that when the clogging degree increases from 0 to 0.3, the average accuracy and correlation coefficient evolution intervals of high‑resolution model of overflow characteristics in sediment‑clogged pipes are [0.934, 0.951] and [0.975, 0.986], respectively. Hydraulic analysis further showed that pipe siltation reduced conveyance capacity through the combined effects of effective-flow-area reduction and additional sediment-bed resistance, while the blocked flow increased nonlinearly with siltation degree and became more sensitive as the pipe approached the half-full condition. Compared with traditional flood simulation models, the flood evolution simulation model considering the influence of pipe siltation has high accuracy.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67055-2.title: An efficient photo-Favorskii rearrangement of α-chloroketones for the synthesis of 2-arylpropionic acids
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67055-2.abstract: 2-Arylpropionic acids, exemplified by ibuprofen, are important structural motifs widely found in bioactive molecules and pharmaceutical agents, and their industrial synthesis is therefore of considerable significance. Herein, we report a systematic study of the photo-Favorskii rearrangement synthesis of 2-arylpropionic acids using zinc acetate as a cost-effective, readily available, and environmentally benign acid scavenger. Under mild visible-light irradiation conditions, this protocol enables efficient conversion of α-chloroketones into the corresponding 2-arylpropionic acids, delivering moderate to good yields across a broad range of more than 11 substrates. This work demonstrates the potential of zinc acetate for sustainable organic synthesis and provides an environmentally benign, efficient strategy for the preparation of valuable carboxylic acid derivatives.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69590-4.title: Nonlinear hydrological responses to intermediate development pathways in semi-arid watersheds
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69590-4.abstract: Hydrological vulnerability in semi-arid watersheds is increasingly shaped by coupled climate and land-use change, yet the relative importance of runoff and sediment dynamics remains unclear. Here, we develop an integrated socio-hydrological framework that combines SWAT modeling, CA–Markov land-use projections, and CMIP6-based Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) to quantify runoff, sediment yield, and vulnerability at the sub-watershed scale. Across 16 sub-watersheds and two future periods (2021–2040; 2041–2052), simulations reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity in runoff responses, whereas Sediment yield increased by approximately 15–30% relative to the baseline period under all evaluated scenarios. This divergence indicates a systematic decoupling of runoff and sediment dynamics, with sediment emerging as a more sensitive indicator of watershed degradation. Notably, the intermediate SSP2-4.5 pathway produces more consistent hydrological responses across sub-watersheds than SSP5-8.5, highlighting nonlinear relationships between development trajectories and hydrological risk. A spatially explicit Integrated Vulnerability Index incorporating dynamic adaptive capacity identifies persistent vulnerability hotspots in central and downstream sub-watersheds. These findings demonstrate that moderate development pathways can induce disproportionate hydrological stress and underscore the importance of sediment-focused, transferable frameworks for climate adaptation in semi-arid regions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68631-2.title: Diversified pomegranate-based intercropping systems to enhance productivity, profitability, and soil fertility in semi-arid ecosystems
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68631-2.abstract: Diversified intercropping is increasingly recognized as a strategy to enhance the productivity and the sustainability in orchard-based agroecosystems, particularly in water-limited environments. A five-year field experiment (2016–2020) was conducted under semi-arid conditions of Rajasthan, India, to evaluate the agronomic performance, system productivity, economic viability, and soil physicochemical properties under pomegranate-based intercropping systems involving legumes, non-legumes, and vegetables. The experiment was established in a randomized block design with three replications, integrating legumes (green gram and cluster bean), non-legumes (mustard and fenugreek) and vegetables (okra and cabbage) within pomegranate orchards during the kharif and rabi seasons. Intercropping significantly enhanced fruit yield and mustard equivalent yield (MEY) compared with sole pomegranate cultivation. Among the evaluated systems, the pomegranate + green gram–mustard combination recorded the highest MEY (3,738.9 kg ha⁻¹) and land equivalent ratio (2.76), indicating superior land-use efficiency and complementary resource utilization. During the kharif season, pomegranate + okra produced the highest intercrop yield (2,758.6 kg ha⁻¹), whereas in the rabi season, pomegranate + cabbage achieved the maximum yield (18,515.4 kg ha⁻¹) and MEY (3,174.0 kg ha⁻¹). Overall system productivity was greatest in the vegetable-based intercropping system, particularly pomegranate + okra–cabbage system (23,099.2 kg ha⁻¹), followed by pomegranate + cluster bean-fenugreek system (9,921.6 kg ha⁻¹). Economic analysis identified the pomegranate + okra–cabbage system as the most profitable (benefit–cost ratio 1.16), while legume-based systems showed progressive profitability over time. Soil fertility improved notably in legume-based systems, with available nitrogen increasing up to 277 kg ha⁻¹ and soil organic carbon reaching 7.74 Mg ha⁻¹ after five years. Overall, the results demonstrate that diversified intercropping in pomegranate orchards enhances productivity, profitability, and soil fertility while maintaining comparable fruit yield across most intercropping systems. Intercropping should be preferred over sole pomegranate cultivation in semi-arid regions to enhance system productivity and resource use efficiency.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68613-4.title: Anti-LL-37 antibodies in synovial fluid reflect disease-specific immunopathogenic mechanisms in psoriatic arthritis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68613-4.abstract: The antimicrobial peptide LL-37 has emerged as a key mediator linking innate and adaptive immunity and has been implicated in the pathogenesis of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. While circulating levels of LL-37 and anti-LL-37 antibodies have been investigated in several conditions, their presence and relevance within the local joint microenvironment remain insufficiently explored. This study aimed to evaluate anti-LL-37 antibodies in synovial fluid from patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and knee osteoarthritis (KoA), and to analyze their associations with pro-inflammatory cytokines. Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by dysregulated innate and adaptive immune responses. Autoantibodies against the antimicrobial peptide LL-37 have recently emerged as potential contributors to PsA pathogenesis, although their relationship with synovial cytokine profiles and disease activity remains insufficiently characterized. To investigate synovial anti-LL-37 autoantibody levels in patients with PsA and evaluate their association with inflammatory cytokines, clinical disease activity, and laboratory markers of inflammation. A total of 120 participants were enrolled, including 30 patients with PsA, 30 with RA, 30 with KoA, and 30 non-inflammatory orthopedic controls. Synovial fluid concentrations of anti-LL-37 antibodies, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-23 were measured. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including CRP, ESR, BMI, and disease activity scores (DAPSA for PsA and DAS28 for RA), were recorded. Group differences were analyzed using appropriate comparative statistics, followed by post hoc testing. Spearman correlation and multiple linear regression analyses were performed to identify associations and independent predictors of anti-LL-37 levels. Patients with PsA demonstrated significantly higher synovial anti-LL-37 antibody concentrations than patients with RA, KoA, and controls (all p = 0.001). IL-23 levels were also significantly elevated in PsA, whereas IL-1β and IL-6 were highest in RA. In PsA, anti-LL-37 levels showed strong positive correlations with IL-23 (ρ = 0.962, p < 0.001), IL-1β (ρ = 0.855, p < 0.001), IL-6 (ρ = 0.627, p < 0.001), DAPSA score (ρ = 0.874, p < 0.001), and CRP (ρ = 0.618, p = 0.001). Similar but weaker correlations were observed in RA, while no significant associations were identified in KoA or controls. Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated that DAPSA score was the only independent predictor of synovial anti-LL-37 antibody levels (β = 0.384, p = 0.026). The regression model explained 89.1% of the variance in anti-LL-37 concentrations (adjusted R2 = 0.891). Synovial anti-LL-37 autoantibodies are markedly increased in PsA and are closely associated with IL-23-driven inflammation and clinical disease activity. These findings support the involvement of LL-37-directed autoimmunity in PsA pathogenesis and suggest that synovial anti-LL-37 antibodies may represent a promising synovial biomarker for disease activity and a potential therapeutic target in psoriatic arthritis.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67556-0.title: Associations of major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and aggression with subclinical variations in kidney function biomarkers among young adults: A cross-sectional study from the rafsanjan youth cohort study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67556-0.abstract: Psychiatric disorders emerging during adolescence and young adulthood may be associated with variations in physiological systems beyond the brain, including kidney function biomarkers. However, most previous research examining psychiatric disorders and kidney-related outcomes has focused on patients with established chronic kidney disease (CKD), while evidence from generally healthy young populations remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the associations of major depressive disorder (MDD), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and aggression (AGG) with kidney function biomarkers, including serum creatinine (Cr), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), among young participants of the Rafsanjan Youth Cohort Study (RYCS), Iran. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study utilizing data from the RYCS, which comprised 3006 participants aged 15–34 years. After applying predefined exclusion criteria, 2940 participants were included in the final analysis. Psychiatric disorders were assessed using the Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI), and kidney function biomarkers were evaluated using serum Cr, BUN, and eGFR measurements. Logistic regression models were used to examine associations between psychiatric disorders, GAD, and kidney function biomarkers after adjustment for potential confounding variables. Among 2940 participants with a mean age of 25.78 ± 6.04, the prevalence of MDD, OCD, GAD, and AGG was found to be 14.9%, 9.9%, 7.7%, and 39.54%, respectively. In fully adjusted analyses, GAD was associated with higher odds of above-median serum Cr level (OR: 1.74, 95% CI: 1.16–2.61). No significant associations were observed between MDD, OCD, or AGG and Cr, BUN, or eGFR. In this population-based study of generally healthy young individuals, GAD was associated with higher odds of above-median serum Cr level; however, the clinical significance of this finding remains uncertain. The absence of consistent associations across other psychiatric disorders and kidney biomarkers suggests that these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Longitudinal studies incorporating repeated renal measurements and mechanistic assessments are required to clarify whether psychiatric disorders are associated with future changes in kidney health.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68135-z.title: Maternal dimethoxyethyl phthalate exposure enhances nicotine challenge-induced locomotor sensitization in adult male offspring rats: role of striatal dopamine D1 receptor
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68135-z.abstract: Early-life exposure to environmental endocrine disruptors, such as phthalates and bisphenol A, has been linked to neurobehavioral disorders, including autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Recent studies have also reported that individuals with ADHD exhibit higher rates of nicotine dependence than controls do. Moreover, bisphenol A has been reported to potentiate morphine- and methamphetamine-induced addictive behaviors in rodents. Based on these findings, the present study investigated whether maternal dimethoxyethyl phthalate (DMEP) exposure influences susceptibility to locomotor sensitization induced by nicotine challenge in young adult male offpring rats. Compared with the saline control treatment, maternal exposure to DMEP did not induce locomotor hyperactivity in adult male offspring rats. However, repeated nicotine treatment induced greater development and expression of locomotor sensitization in adult male offspring rats that were maternally exposed to DMEP than in those maternally exposed to saline. Moreover, maternal exposure to DMEP resulted in elevated dopamine (DA) levels and elevated mRNA expression of the DA D1 receptor, but not the DA D2 receptor, and c-Fos in the dorsal striatum of adult male offspring rats. Furthermore, the administration of the D1 receptor antagonist SCH23390 attenuated the enhanced locomotor hyperactivity induced by nicotine challenge following a 3-day abstinence period in adult male offspring rats maternally exposed to saline or DMEP. Interestingly, a low dose of SCH23390 significantly suppressed nicotine challenge-induced locomotor sensitization in the offspring that were maternally exposed to DMEP, but not in the offspring maternally exposed to saline. Collectively, these findings provide novel evidence that maternal DMEP exposure increases vulnerability in adult male offspring rats to at least nicotine-induced behavioral sensitization, potentially through the upregulation of the D1 receptor in the dorsal striatum.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67368-2.title: Late Miocene capybara in the Atacama Desert reveals a wetter climate and a transcontinental dispersal pathway
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67368-2.abstract: Abstract We report the oldest record of a capybara (Caviidae: Hydrochoerinae) in Chile, dated at ca. 8.8 Ma, which along with paleobotanical proxy records, indicates a markedly wetter late Miocene Atacama Desert. Today hyperarid, the Atacama contrasts sharply with the semiaquatic ecology of capybaras, which are restricted to perennial wetlands east of the Andes. A partial left M3 (MPC 3000), assigned to Cardiatherium , along with stable isotope data from pedogenic carbonates indicating C 3 -dominated vegetation and phytoliths documenting palms and dicots, provides evidence for persistent freshwater and riparian ecosystems in the southern Atacama during the late Miocene. This occurrence requires ecological connectivity between foreland wetlands and the Pacific margin, implying a transcontinental dispersal pathway. Such connectivity may have been achieved either through a trans-Andean corridor or via a northern route linking the Amazon basin to the Pacific through westward-draining systems. Both scenarios indicate continent-scale hydrologic integration and challenge the long-term persistence of hyperaridity in the region. Instead, they support a substantially wetter late Miocene Atacama, characterized by expanded riparian networks and vegetation capable of sustaining large semiaquatic herbivores.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65626-x.title: Hypothalamic c-Fos expression changes during late chicken embryonic development and increases following experimental stimulation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65626-x.abstract: Abstract The timing of functional hypothalamic responsiveness during embryogenesis remains incompletely defined. We examined hypothalamic activation in chicken embryos from embryonic day (ED) 12–17 following experimental stimulation consisting of a localized foot injection of paraformaldehyde (PFA) together with the associated handling procedures required for its administration. Hypothalamic activation was quantified as the proportion of c-Fos-positive cells within the paraventricular nucleus (PVN). Generalized linear modelling revealed significant effects of both embryonic age and stimulation condition on c-Fos expression, with no evidence of an Age × Stimulation interaction. Across development, stimulated embryos exhibited higher proportions of c-Fos-positive cells than age-matched controls. Independent of stimulation, the only significant difference between adjacent developmental stages occurred between ED14 and ED15, suggesting a candidate transition in hypothalamic maturation. Exploratory analysis indicated that these findings are consistent with an early (ED12–ED14) and a late (ED15–ED17) developmental phase and suggest that ED14–ED15 may represent a candidate phase boundary in hypothalamic maturation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67951-7.title: Exploration of novel anti-TB agents targeting the serine/threonine kinase enzyme (PknE) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis: an in silico study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67951-7.abstract: Abstract Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) remains a deadly infectious agent and a global health challenge, particularly due to the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains. Mycobacterial serine/threonine protein kinase E (PknE) is vital for mycobacterial survival under nitric oxide stress by altering Toll-like receptor expression, suppressing apoptosis, increasing inflammation, and modulating costimulatory molecules. This study employed a structure-based in silico workflow comprising virtual screening of 2,202 FDA-approved compounds, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulation molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) binding free energy calculations, principal component analysis (PCA), free energy landscape (FEL) analysis, and in silico toxicity profiling, to identify candidate PknE inhibitors. Molecular docking identified netilmicin, dirithromycin, acarbose, and ertapenem as top candidates, with docking scores of − 13.13 to − 15.86 kcal/mol. MD simulations confirmed complex stability with RMSD values near 1 nm, while MM/PBSA analysis revealed favourable binding free energies: netilmicin (− 1.47 ± 0.18), ertapenem (− 11.70 ± 1.22), dirithromycin (− 17.80 ± 0.13), and acarbose (− 18.90 ± 0.06 kcal/mol). PCA-based FEL analysis confirmed thermodynamic stability across all complexes, with DTM–PknE exhibiting the lowest minimum Gibbs free energy (15.7 kJ/mol). In silico toxicity profiling demonstrated acceptable safety profiles for all leads. These findings provide a strong computational basis for repurposing these agents as adjunct anti-TB therapies, pending experimental validation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69606-z.title: Structural characterization and in vitro anticancer activity of biogenic NiFe₂O₄ nanoparticles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69606-z.abstract: Nickel ferrite (NiFe₂O₄) Nanoparticles were prepared using a green co-precipitation method with a natural reducing and stabilizing agent of Crocus sativus flower petal extract. The synthesis was performed by the controlled co-precipitation of nickel and iron precursors with the plant extract, followed by drying and calcination to obtain NiFe₂O₄ nanoparticles. The green synthesis method minimizes the use of toxic chemicals and offers an environmentally friendly method to synthesize nanoparticles. The synthesized nanoparticles were highly crystalline with an average crystallite size of about 29.8 nm and predominantly cubic spinel NiFe₂O₄ structure. The morphological analysis showed that the nanoparticles were almost spherical and moderately aggregated. The synthesized nanoparticles exhibited concentration-dependent in-vitro anticancer activity against human lung carcinoma (A549) cells with an IC₅₀ value of 51.23 µg/mL as determined using the MTT assay. In comparison, relatively high viability (> 85%) was maintained in normal HEK293 cells at 100 µg/mL, which is evidence of good cytocompatibility and selective biological response. The exact mechanism of anticancer activity was not directly studied in the present study, and further mechanistic studies are needed. Overall, the study demonstrates the successful green preparation of nanocrystalline NiFe₂O₄ nanoparticles with potential anti-cancer activity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70083-7.title: A rocket debris impact threat assessment method incorporating value distribution of ground avoidance zones
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70083-7.abstract: With increasing launch frequency in China, rocket debris impact threats have become significant.Traditional trajectory methods often neglect nonlinear stochastic factors and spatial heterogeneity of population activities, leading to risk assessment deviations.This study aims to develop a comprehensive threat assessment framework to enhance statistical confidence in impact prediction.Employing Monte Carlo simulations incorporating mass deviations, engine parameters, and stochastic wind fields, we modeled first-stage debris impact points.A bivariate normal distribution characterization constrained by a 99%confidence ellipse is established to describe impact point dispersion.The proposed data-driven framework integrates stochastic trajectory simulation and fine-grained population data, providing a quantitative approach for ground risk evaluation.Utilizing high-resolution WorldPop data in China and a"severity"index, we optimized ground avoidance zone polygons via boundary merging algorithms.Results demonstrate that impact points exhibit a distinct two-dimensional normal distribution under random couplings.Risk assessment reveals that cumulative risk values increase significantly when intersecting high-density areas.The proposed data-driven framework effectively integrates Monte Carlo simulation with multi-source stochastic disturbances and population data, providing a quantitative method for risk evaluation.The comprehensive risk value(R)offers a single, actionable metric to optimize launch operations and mitigate casualties.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68776-0.title: Adaptive multi-scale attention-enhanced V-NET for accurate and efficient multi-shell diffusion MRI estimation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68776-0.abstract: Multi-shell acquisition protocols sample diffusion signals at different b-values. While higher b-values (e.g., $$b = 2000\, \mathrm {s/mm^2}$$) offer increased sensitivity to microstructural features, their acquisition is time-intensive and suffers from reduced signal-to-noise ratio and motion sensitivity, which limits their routine clinical applicability. To address this challenge, we propose a deep learning framework for predicting high b-value ($$b = 2000\, \mathrm {s/mm^2}$$) spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients directly from low b-value ($$b = 1000\, \mathrm {s/mm^2}$$) SH coefficients. Our method is based on a simplified V-NET architecture augmented with adaptive multi-scale attention. This attention mechanism dynamically learns optimal receptive field combinations through scale-weighting networks. Unlike conventional fixed-scale approaches, our model incorporates three dilated convolutional branches with adaptive weighting, cross-scale feature fusion, and integrated spatial–channel attention. These components enable context-aware feature extraction that emphasizes the most relevant scales for diffusion pattern recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate reconstruction with significantly reduced computational cost compared to modern state-of-the-art approaches.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69583-3.title: ATAD2 is a novel regulator of myogenesis and autophagy in skeletal muscles
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69583-3.abstract: Abstract The nuclear protein ATAD2 (ATPase family AAA domain containing 2) is a known positive regulator of cell proliferation in various cancer types. The expression and functional roles of ATAD2 in skeletal muscle cells are unknown. In this study, we used transient and stable knockdown approaches using siRNA and shRNA oligos to evaluate how ATAD2 regulates proliferation, migration, differentiation, and autophagy in C2C12 myoblasts. Atad2 knockdown (KD) significantly increased myoblast proliferation rate, S-phase entry, overall cell viability, and early differentiation into myotubes. However, Atad2 KD also elicited myotube atrophy and upregulation of ubiquitin E3 ligases Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. Basal autophagy was inhibited in Atad2 KD cells as a result of downregulation of autophagy-related genes ( Lc3b , Gabarapl1 , Atg5 , and Atg7 ). Immunoblotting and immunostaining revealed significant decrease in LC3B protein levels and the number of LC3B punctae per cell with Atad2 KD, respectively. LAMP1 staining confirmed the presence of enlarged lysosomes in Atad2 KD cells. Additionally, genes involved in lysosome function and integrity including Rab7 , Rab29 , Rab32 , Nrbf2 , and Cathepsin L were downregulated in Atad2 KD cells. Collectively, these results indicate that ATAD2 is a critical regulator of muscle cell proliferation, differentiation, autophagy and lysosomal integrity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66018-x.title: Efficient hardware realization of 2D-chaotic Baker map using FPGA for secure image encryption
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66018-x.abstract: As the digital ecosystem evolves, the widespread generation, transmission, and storage of medical images expose sensitive healthcare data to significant security threats, necessitating robust and efficient encryption techniques. While several chaos-based encryption methods have been proposed, many suffer from limited key spaces and high computational complexity, making them unsuitable for real-time and resource-constrained environments. This paper presents a hybrid image encryption framework that integrates a two-dimensional Chaotic Baker Map (2D-CBM) with XOR-based diffusion to achieve both high security and computational efficiency. The proposed method performs chaotic permutation using a pseudo-random sequence derived from the Baker map, followed by an XOR-based diffusion process to enhance pixel randomness and resistance to attacks. Extensive experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed method achieves high entropy H = 7.9897, indicating near-ideal randomness, along with NPCR = 99.6521% and UACI = 31.306%, confirming strong resistance against differential and statistical attacks. In addition, the proposed framework ensures low correlation among adjacent pixels and maintains high reconstruction quality after decryption. Furthermore, the algorithm is efficiently implemented on a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), demonstrating low resource utilization and suitability for real-time secure medical image processing. The proposed system is well-suited for deployment in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) and Healthcare 4.0 environments, where both security and efficiency are critical.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68161-x.title: Highly efficient pyrazine-based organo-lanthanide luminescent ionogels for white light emission through energy transfer
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68161-x.abstract: A novel pyrazine based bichromophoric system was designed to achieve the efficient white light emission through partial resonance energy transfer in ionic liquid based gel medium i.e., ionogel. The partial resonance energy transfer was taken place between the pyrazine based bichromophoric unit and lanthanide ion {Eu3+}. Herein, pyrazine based bichromophoric unit acts as a donor while lanthanide ion as an acceptor. The ionogel was self-assembled from pyrazine based bichromophoric units in a carboxylic acid functionalized imidazole based ionic liquid. The corresponding absolute quantum yield values for pyrazine-phenanthrene-Eu3+ (PPE), pyrazine-naphthol-Eu3+ (PNE), and pyrazine-pyrene-Eu3+ (PPyE) were 10.4%, 8.6%, and 5.3%, respectively in ionogel. The CIE (Commission International d’Eclairage) coordinates values for PPyE, PNE, and PPE are {0.32, 0.36}, {0.37, 0.30}, and {0.28, 0.34}, respectively in ionogel. In solution phase, the CIE coordinates are significantly away from the white light region owing to the inefficient energy transfer between bichromophoric unit and lanthanide ion. Moreover, the electrical conductivity was measured for pyrazine based bichromophoric systems in the presence and absence of lanthanide ion in ionogel. The electrical conductivity was increased up to 2–3 times in the presence of the lanthanide ion for the pyrazine based bichromophoric systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64685-4.title: Land-use and land-cover change and response of ecosystem service value: a case study from Guizhou Province
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64685-4.abstract: Monitoring land use and land cover changes (LUCC), combined with their impact on ecosystem service value (ESV), is the most direct and effective method for evaluating the benefits of ecological engineering. Focusing on Guizhou Province in China, this study examined the 40-year process of LUCC through two lenses: type conversion and dynamic degree. Using LUCC area indicators, the study employed an improved equivalent factor method to assess changes in ESV. The findings indicate that from 1985 to 2024, the region was predominantly forest. Post-2000, the primary conversion involved cultivated land reverting to forest. The most intense dynamic changes occurred between 2010 and 2024. Over the study period, the regional ecosystem service value initially decreased and then increased significantly after the implementation of ecological engineering in 2000. Overall, total ESV increased by 3,855 million yuan, mainly because of the restoration of cultivated lands and grasslands to forests. The impact of these changes on ESV was substantial. Thus, ecological construction efforts should focus not only on methods such as converting cultivated land to forests but also on the restoration and recovery of grasslands and forests. Moreover, maintaining and adding quality improvements of ecological engineering achievements remain crucial.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69637-6.title: Predictive normative modeling of neurocognitive performance in Irish jockeys using regression and neural quantile methods
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69637-6.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of regression-based methods for generating normative data for neuropsychological test scores, using retrospective cross-sectional data from Irish jockeys between 2010 and 2024. The analysis focuses on four key cognitive assessments used in concussion protocols: Digit Span Forward and Digit Span Backward (assessing working memory), Speed of Comprehension from the Speed and Language Processing battery (assessing language processing speed), and the Symbol Digit Modalities Test (assessing attention and processing speed). In addition to the widely used linear regression (LR) approach, we evaluate conditional percentile estimation using both linear quantile regression (LQR) and a neural network-based quantile regression (NNQR) framework with monotonicity constraints across quantile levels which has not been previously applied in the context of normative modeling to the best of our knowledge. Results highlight that percentile thresholds vary substantially depending on the chosen method and the covariates for corresponding test score under consideration. This variation underscores the importance of selecting an appropriate modeling approach based on the clinical scenario and the specific percentile range of interest. To make this work more viable in a practical sense, we provide an interactive dashboard that estimates normative percentiles using pre-trained LR, LQR, and NNQR models based on age, education, and sex. It automatically highlights the best-performing method based on coverage offset analysis and supports detailed report generation. While the dashboard operates on pre-trained models for ease of use, the underlying code is open-source and available via GitHub, allowing researchers and clinicians to customize it with their own datasets and model configurations for more tailored normative estimation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70269-z.title: Response surface optimization of nitrogen fertilization and grain density for sustainable wheat yield
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70269-z.abstract: Given the escalating demand for wheat and the imperative to mitigate the environmental consequences stemming from excessive chemical fertilizer use, this study investigated the combined effects of grain density and nitrogen fertilizer levels on wheat grain yield and its components under sustainable agricultural conditions. Utilizing the response surface methodology (RSM) and a central composite design (CCD), the impact of three grain density levels (100, 160, and 220 kg ha− 1) and three nitrogen fertilizer levels (0, 110, and 220 kg ha− 1) was evaluated on parameters such as grain yield, plant height, number of spikes per unit area, number of grains per spike, and grain weight per spike. The results indicated that both factors significantly affected the studied variables, with nitrogen fertilizer identified as the primary factor. A reduction in grain density considerably improved grain yield and augmented the positive effects of nitrogen. The regression models, exhibiting a high coefficient of determination (R2 > 0.97), provided accurate predictions of the responses (P < 0.05). Findings suggest that increasing nitrogen application enhances yield and yield components, while decreasing grain density can amplify this trend for grain yield, number of grains per spike, and grain weight per spike. A grain density of 100 kg ha− 1 is proposed as the optimal treatment for enhancing yield while minimizing chemical fertilizer consumption. This represents an effective and sustainable approach to improving wheat production efficiency, offering an environmentally and economically viable solution for sustainable agriculture.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70439-z.title: Serum C4/C3 ratio at disease onset predicts end-stage renal disease in microscopic polyangiitis: the multicentre REVEAL cohort
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70439-z.abstract: We investigated whether serum complement C3 and C4 levels and the C4/C3 ratio at disease onset were associated with clinical features, renal involvement, and prognosis in microscopic polyangiitis (MPA). Patients were stratified into tertiles according to baseline C3 and C4 levels. Associations with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) were assessed using multivariable Cox regression and sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment-related factors, missing data, and competing risk. Five-year time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated discrimination for ESRD. Among 308 patients included in the C3 analysis and 264 in the C4 analysis, the low C3 tertile had higher serum creatinine levels, more frequent rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, a higher incidence of ESRD, and poorer overall survival. C4 tertiles were not associated with renal outcomes or survival. A higher C4/C3 ratio was associated with an increased risk of ESRD in multivariable analysis, with generally consistent effect directions across sensitivity analyses. Its 5-year discriminatory performance was comparable to that of C3 alone (area under the curve, 0.718 vs. 0.739), with higher specificity (0.775 vs. 0.662). The C4/C3 ratio may serve as a complementary marker for renal risk stratification in MPA.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70216-y.title: Carbon fibers as active substrates for engineering Ni/Au interfaces toward enhanced hydrogen evolution in ammonia-containing alkaline electrolytes
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70216-y.abstract: Abstract The development of material-efficient electrode platforms for controlling metal dispersion and interfacial charge transfer is central to advanced electrochemical technologies. Here, carbon fibers are used as active substrates for engineering metal–carbon interfaces via thermal activation and sequential electrodeposition. Surface modification exposes graphitic domains and increases roughness, enabling uniform metal nucleation and strong interfacial bonding of the deposited nickel–gold layers, resulting in a hierarchical and highly accessible surface architecture. Electrochemical analysis reveals enhanced charge-transfer behavior and increased electrochemical accessibility, highlighting the role of the carbon scaffold in facilitating electron transport and interfacial charge transfer. The modified fibers exhibit reduced overpotential (168.2 mV at − 10 mA cm⁻²), a Tafel slope of 57 mV dec⁻¹, and decreased charge-transfer resistance (~ 651 Ω), indicating improved interfacial kinetics and more efficient utilization of deposited metals. In an ammonia-containing alkaline electrolyte, a further increase in current response (~ 14–15%) is observed, consistent with a modification of the interfacial reaction environment. The findings demonstrate that carbon fibers function beyond passive supports, acting as conductive and structurally adaptive frameworks that govern metal dispersion, interfacial bonding, and charge-transfer behavior. This work highlights carbon fibers as scalable, material-efficient substrates for designing high-performance metal–carbon hybrid systems for ammonia-containing alkaline electrochemical systems and future alkaline wastewater technologies.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69588-y.title: Unsteady reactive hybrid nanofluid flow between coaxial cylinders with variable transport properties and Einstein–Hamilton crosser model
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69588-y.abstract: This study investigates unsteady hybrid nanofluid flow between concentric stretched cylinders, incorporating homogeneous-heterogeneous (h–h) reactions. The SWCNTs/MWCNTs are selected as hybrid nanoparticles in a base fluid engine oil, with Newtonian heating at the inner wall. The shape factors of the nanoparticles were also considered, as they are important in the heat transfer rate of the system. Uniquely, in order to better explain the heat transfer phenomenon, the Hamilton-Crosser model and the Einstein model are used, which explain the variable temperature-dependent viscosity and variable temperature-dependent thermal conductivity in the present study. The presumed model is represented by Partial differential equations. The governing equations are transformed into nonlinear ODEs by similarity transformation and then solved numerically using the bvp4c method. Key findings reveal that radial velocity increases with the unsteadiness parameter, whereas axial velocity near the outer cylinder decreases. Rising variable viscosity reduces radial velocity, while variable thermal conductivity enhances temperature profiles. Wall friction at the outer cylinder increases with unsteadiness, but decreases at the inner cylinder, and the Nusselt number drops on both walls, signifying reduced heat transfer. Model validation is also included, endorsing the proposed framework. This analysis with an annular geometries model provides critical insights for optimizing thermal systems in many engineering applications where precise flow control is essential.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69959-5.title: LLM-assisted value assessment and strategy design for virtual power plant participation in coupled electricity–carbon markets
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69959-5.abstract: As power systems transition toward low-carbon operation, virtual power plants (VPPs) increasingly aggregate distributed renewable generation, energy storage, electric vehicles, and flexible loads to participate in coupled day-ahead energy, ancillary-service, and carbon markets. However, existing carbon-accounting methods may double count low-carbon electricity because they overlook the distinct emission-reduction mechanisms of heterogeneous resources. Conventional optimization models also cannot readily incorporate natural-language user preferences or other unstructured information. This paper proposes a large language model (LLM)-assisted electricity–carbon co-optimization method for a source–load–storage–vehicle VPP. The method introduces a carbon-credit mechanism that traces renewable-energy utilization and explicitly prevents double counting. This mechanism quantifies emission reductions associated with directly accommodated renewable electricity, renewable-origin energy shifted through storage, rescheduled electric-vehicle charging, and controllable-load curtailment or shifting. The LLM converts users’ natural-language preferences into hard constraints, soft constraints, prohibited time windows, and penalty parameters. These elements are then embedded in a deterministic day-ahead co-optimization model. The resulting mixed-integer linear programming model maximizes net revenue subject to operational, user-preference, carbon-credit, and market-performance constraints. Case-study results show that the proposed method improves economic returns, carbon-market revenue, emission reductions, renewable-energy accommodation, and the quality of demand-side response.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70233-x.title: ConvLSTMNet-EMD: leveraging 1D-convolutional encoder-decoder model with self-attention mechanism for improved energy consumption forecasting
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70233-x.abstract: Providing a constant, economic, and dependable energy source to end users is a difficult and complex task. To overcome these challenges, energy providers rely on precise load forecasting, especially during periods of peak demand. Although existing deep learning models show potential results, they often struggle to predict peak demand values accurately. To improve energy consumption forecasting, this paper presents ConvLSTMNet-EMD, an overall framework designed to enhance the precision of peak demand values in short-term load forecasting. The introduced framework integrates a 1D-Convolutional encoder-decoder architecture with a long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) to learn local features and global temporal dependencies. Next, the input time series data is decomposed using Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) into multiple components by isolating peak-related patterns, so that the sudden demand variations can be effectively captured. Further, a self-attention mechanism (SAM) is used in a 1D encoder-decoder model to emphasize the informative time steps dynamically by minimizing information loss from the relevant decomposed components. As a result, it enhances the peak demand behavior and overall forecasting performance. The experimental results reveal that the ConvLSTMNet-EMD surpasses the current models with the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.069, which is considerably less than the 0.120 of the existing approach.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69896-3.title: Dengue virus serotype classification from complete genomes using a Transformer with chunk-based sequence modeling and explainability analysis
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69896-3.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used for genomic surveillance of infectious diseases, but predictive models must be evaluated under realistic generalization settings and interpreted cautiously. We present XAI-DENFormer, an explainability-oriented framework for dengue virus (DENV) serotype classification from complete viral genomes. A curated dataset of 29,091 publicly available DENV genomes was encoded as nucleotide-level one-hot sequences and processed with a chunk-based Transformer encoder designed for memory-efficient whole-genome analysis. Generalization was assessed using three complementary validation protocols: CD-HIT cluster-aware, geographical, and temporal validation. DENFormer variants were benchmarked against Logistic Regression, a feed-forward neural network, Longformer, and Performer under identical conditions. The mean-pooling DENFormer configuration maintained high performance across all three validation protocols, with accuracies of 98.68–99.91% across CD-HIT folds, 97.18–100.00% across geographical holdouts, and 96.35–99.86% across temporal holdouts. To inspect model behavior, we combined attention maps, Gradient × Input attributions, embedding visualizations, and regional statistical analyses. The resulting profiles supported distributed serotype-associated signals across structural, non-structural, and untranslated regions rather than reliance on a single genomic locus. XAI-DENFormer provides a robust and interpretable framework for large-scale DENV genome classification and model-guided genomic inspection.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68081-w.title: Secure and scalable client pre-filtering and authentication framework for federated learning systems
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68081-w.abstract: Abstract A federated learning system, which emphasises decentralisation, allows cooperative model training to ensure the privacy and security of the data. Client authentication is an important factor in a decentralised system to prevent unauthorised access and unauthorised users from adding exceptions or irrelevant facts during model preparation. Due to which model becomes weak, poisoned, and inconsistent. The proposed framework adopts a two-stage client verification pipeline. In the first stage, probabilistic data structures serve as a lightweight admission pre-filter that screens candidate clients before any cryptographic operation is performed: a Bloom Filter (BF) is used for static client populations, and an Adaptive Quotient Filter (AQF) is used for dynamic client populations, enabling fast membership screening both before base-model distribution and during collection of gradient updates. In the second stage, clients admitted by the pre-filter undergo ECDSA-based signature verification, which constitutes the actual authentication step and compensates for the residual false positives inherent to probabilistic filtering. This design allows the server to reject the majority of unauthorized requests cheaply via BF/AQF while reserving expensive cryptographic verification for genuine candidates. The dataset used in this study is the IP Address Geographic Profiles dataset, comprising 129,857 entries. Evaluation covered memory utilisation, lookup time, and false-positive behaviour of BF and AQF against six alternative data structures. BF and AQF reduced server-side memory usage by up to 90% relative to a Trie (e.g., 1.9 MB and 3 MB versus 23.2 MB for 100,000 password-derived credentials), at the cost of a modest lookup-time overhead relative to hash-based structures (0.054–0.064 s versus 0.003–0.006 s for a HashSet on 100,000 records). At the protocol level, combining BF/AQF pre-filtering with ECDSA verification reduced authentication messages and communication cost by roughly 30% relative to ECDSA-only authentication under a simulated environment with 30% Byzantine clients, with the gain compounding over rounds (communication cost falling from 125,000 KB to 87,537.5 KB over 50 rounds). The study concluded that the proposed model provides a secure and scalable client screening and authentication framework by combining BF/AQF with ECDSA-based signature verification in a decentralised environment where multiple clients participate from different regions. Experimental results present significant changes in memory usage, performance analysis, and resistance to unauthorised clients.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69090-5.title: Awareness and management of post-bariatric hypoglycemia: an international survey of healthcare professionals
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69090-5.abstract: Abstract Postprandial hypoglycemia (PBH) is a recognized complication following bariatric surgery, but real-world data on its management by healthcare professionals (HCPs) is lacking. To address this, a 25-item multilingual questionnaire was developed and distributed online to HCPs treating patients after bariatric surgery. The survey assessed awareness, diagnostic criteria, and treatment strategies related to PBH, with 312 responses analyzed from 32 countries. Respondents had a mean age of 48.8 years; 54.5% were male, 46% worked in bariatric surgery, and 59% had over 10 years of experience. While awareness of PBH was high (> 73%), estimates of PBH prevalence varied considerably. The largest proportion of respondents estimated that 1–5% of their bariatric patients were affected (38.2%), followed by 6–10% (25.9%), with progressively fewer respondents selecting higher prevalence categories. There was no clear consensus on diagnostic thresholds, and management strategies differed significantly. Nutritional therapy was the most common first-line approach, and acarbose was the most frequently used medication (59%). However, preferences for second-line treatments varied. Notably, over half of the HCPs cited lack of reimbursement as a barrier to optimal care. Despite strong awareness, the management of PBH remains inconsistent, underlining the need for clearer guidelines and further research to standardize diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68670-9.title: Utilising urban energy structure as a carbon management strategy for carbon emissions mitigation and climate neutrality
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68670-9.abstract: Abstract Achieving urban carbon neutrality is critical to mitigating global warming and demands transformative regulation of carbon flows within urban energy systems. This study constructs an energy structure influencing factors (ESIF) evaluation system for urban energy structure, using improved principal component analysis (IPCA), to explore the factors influencing energy structure and carbon emissions within urban carbon cycles. Based on historical data spanning 2003 to 2023, this paper selects Suzhou, Wuxi and Nanjing, three homogeneous energy-reliant riverine cities in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD), to develop an ESIF-linked carbon emissions prediction model for the carbon trajectories from 2024 to 2060. The results reveal that dependence on non-renewable energy sources and certain socioeconomic factors, such as the urbanisation rate, hinder the development of the energy structure. Multi-scenario forecasts show that accelerated growth in energy, social, and economic indicators delays the carbon peak and raises peak emissions. All three cities will reach carbon peaks no later than 2030 under Scenarios 1–3, with peak emissions ranging from 195.20 to 255.90 megatonnes. While Scenarios 1–4 enable carbon neutrality by 2060, the high-growth Scenario 5 precludes this target. This research offers targeted low-carbon policy recommendations for homogeneous riverine cities, such as those in the YRD.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70329-4.title: Cold priming reshapes DNA methylation and transcriptional memory in Arabidopsis thaliana
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70329-4.abstract: Abstract Stress priming is a critical adaptive mechanism that enables plants to enhance responses to recurring environmental stresses. Although transcriptomic changes associated with cold stress priming have been reported, the underlying epigenetic mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here, we investigated transcriptomic and DNA methylation dynamics in cold priming in Arabidopsis thaliana . Cold stress induced distinct transcriptional responses in primed and non-primed plants and was accompanied by widespread DNA methylation changes, particularly in non-CG contexts, across both protein-coding genes and transposable elements (TEs). Genes exhibiting transcriptional memory were associated with lower gene-body DNA methylation than non-primed genes. Furthermore, DNA methylation mutants exhibited altered cold stress memory, supporting a role for DNA methylation in preventing inappropriate gene activation and maintaining the specificity of priming responses. Notably, the CG methylation-deficient mutant met1 exhibited enhanced activation of cold-responsive genes, including genes in the CBF pathway. Together, our findings suggest that DNA methylation contributes to cold stress memory by maintaining transcriptional precision in Arabidopsis .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68942-4.title: Recycled aggregate concrete based on an improved SVM method a study on the prediction of compressive strength
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68942-4.abstract: The mix design of recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) has long relied on extensive trial-and-error testing, which is costly and time-consuming; moreover, existing empirical models struggle to accurately capture the complex nonlinear relationship between material components and compressive strength. To address these challenges, this study aims to develop a method for predicting RAC compressive strength that combines high accuracy with interpretability, thereby providing data-driven support for the engineering application of recycled materials. To this end, this study proposes a hybrid kernel support vector regression (SVR) model, whose core innovation lies in the weighted combination of linear and radial basis function (RBF) kernels. This enables the model to simultaneously capture both the global linear trends (dominated by the linear kernel) and the local nonlinear fluctuations (dominated by the RBF kernel) between RAC mix design parameters and compressive strength, thereby overcoming the limitations of a single kernel function in characterizing complex material systems. Based on 178 sets of experimental data, the study constructed a comprehensive database. Nine input variables were systematically selected across three levels—cementitious system, aggregate content, and aggregate characteristics—and the model hyperparameters (C, σ, λ) were systematically optimized using grid search combined with five-fold cross-validation. The results show that the optimal hybrid kernel SVR model achieved a coefficient of determination (R2p) of 0.99506 and a root mean square error (RMSEP) of 0.52589 MPa on the test set, with prediction accuracy significantly superior to that of the linear kernel SVR model (R2p = 0.88116, RMSEP = 2.9519 MPa). Ten rounds of five-fold cross-validation showed that the mean R2 of the hybrid kernel SVR was 0.993, and its 95% confidence interval [0.989, 0.997] did not overlap with that of the linear kernel model [0.786, 0.852] (p < 0.01), confirming the statistical significance and robustness of the model’s accuracy. This study marks the first systematic introduction of the hybrid kernel strategy into the field of RAC strength prediction, filling a research gap regarding this method in highly variable recycled concrete material systems; through a permutation importance analysis, cement content, water content, and recycled coarse aggregate content were identified as the dominant factors influencing strength, thereby enhancing the model’s physical interpretability; The established model achieves high-accuracy predictions under limited sample conditions, providing a viable tool for reducing the number of mix design trials and lowering material R&D costs. This method can be further extended to the prediction of properties in other construction solid waste materials, holding positive significance for promoting the resource utilization of solid waste and low-carbon construction.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69806-7.title: Anti-methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Anti-MRSA) flavonoids from Iraqi Citrus sinensis (L.) Osbeck
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69806-7.abstract: Citrus sinensis (L.) Osbeck (Rutaceae) was investigated as a potential source of anti-MRSA compounds. A bioassay-guided isolation approach afforded fourteen compounds from the peel and leaf extracts of C. sinensis, including a new flavanone glycoside, sinensidin (10). Structural elucidation was based on spectroscopic analyses, including 1D and 2D NMR and HRMS data. Among the isolated compounds, 3-methoxynobiletin (4), sinensetin (7), and rutin 3′-methyl ether (12) exhibited moderate anti-MRSA activity (MIC = 128–256 µg/mL). The crude extract showed higher apparent activity than the individual compounds, suggesting possible contributions from additional constituents and/or synergistic interactions. This study expands the phytochemical profile of C. sinensis and suggests that its polymethoxylated flavonoids and flavonoid glycosides may contribute to anti-MRSA activity.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70001-x.title: Mechanical properties and damage evolution mechanism of rubber-gangue cemented backfill under different loading rates
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70001-x.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the rate-dependent mechanical behavior and damage evolution of rubber-modified cemented gangue backfill through multi-scale macroscopic and microscopic tests. A piecewise statistical damage constitutive model based on the Weibull distribution is established to quantitatively characterize the dynamic failure process of modified backfill. The results reveal that rubber particle incorporation eliminates the critical loading rate effect observed in conventional backfill materials and remarkably improves the ductility of backfill specimens. The compressive strength and elastic modulus exhibit clear loading-rate sensitivity and decrease gradually with increasing rubber content. Both higher loading rate and larger rubber dosage effectively restrain the growth of internal damage variables, allowing the backfill to sustain greater deformation before final failure. Microscopic analysis further indicates that rubber particles expand internal pore distribution and promote progressive crack propagation, which dominates the transition of failure mode from brittle microcracking to ductile macroscopic fracture. The proposed constitutive model accurately reproduces the rate-dependent damage behavior of rubber-modified backfill, providing a reliable theoretical reference for the safety evaluation and engineering application of modified filling materials.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70006-6.title: Adults have rather stable, yet domain-specific tendencies in social and temporal comparisons
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70006-6.abstract: Abstract Past research on how people evaluate and compare themselves in central characteristics focuses strongly on preconditions, processes, and consequences of such comparisons while neglecting individual differences. The current study bridges social and personality research by examining domain specificity, temporal stability, and age differences of social and past-temporal comparisons. Using lifespan samples from Germany ( N = 313, 18–84 years, 49.8% female) and the USA ( N = 302, 18–72 years, 52.0% female), participants reported the frequency and perceived usefulness of social and past-temporal comparisons concerning five domains: emotional stability, extraversion, physical appearance, professional success, and personal life. The results show that individual differences in comparison tendencies were rather domain-specific. Within a specific life domain, the usage of social and past-temporal comparisons was strongly correlated. Individual differences in comparison tendencies were moderately stable over four weeks (~ 0.60). With older age, participants indicated using comparisons less frequently and seeing them as less useful than young adults. We discuss that future research on social and temporal comparisons would benefit from a trait-state approach taking individual differences in domain-specific comparisons and the co-occurrence of social and temporal comparisons into account.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69819-2.title: Wind shear severity regimes and multi-step forecasting at Hong Kong International Airport: evidence from the central runway 07C/25C
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69819-2.abstract: Wind shear is a critical meteorological hazard in aviation, especially during takeoff and landing, where rapid changes in wind speed and direction can affect lift and airspeed, compromise aircraft performance, and threaten safety. Existing studies predominantly focus on single-horizon wind shear prediction, which limits the characterization of wind shear evolution across multiple future horizons. This limitation restricts early assessment and timely intervention; thus, multi-step forecast frameworks are necessary. This study presents a comprehensive framework for wind shear severity regime analysis and short-term multi-step time series forecasts at Hong Kong International Airport, with a focus on the central runway (RWY 07C/25C). The approach employs unsupervised methods, K-Means and Gaussian mixture models (GMM), for data-driven classification of wind shear severity, alongside a hybrid forecast framework that combines Salp Swarm Algorithm-optimized variational mode decomposition (SSA-VMD) with deep learning models, which include GRU, LSTM, and their bidirectional (BiGRU, BiLSTM) and residual (ResGRU, ResLSTM) variants. Doppler LiDAR data from July 2023 to August 2025 provide the basis for model development and evaluation. The severity classification identifies four distinct levels, with K-Means providing clearer cluster separation than GMM, with silhouette scores of 0.322 for 07C and 0.329 for 25C and reveals clear differences in event frequency and duration between the two RWY directions. The forecast results show high accuracy at short horizons, followed by a gradual decline as the forecast horizon extends. For 07C, the VMD-based models achieve R2 values of 0.995–0.997 at 1 step and 0.728–0.868 at 9 steps, while for 25C, R2 ranges from 0.995 to 0.998 at 1 step to 0.735–0.819 at 9 steps. Model performance varies across forecast horizons and RWY directions, with no single architecture providing the best performance across all cases. The ablation study confirms the contribution of VMD, with RMSE reductions of 57.88–94.03% for 07C and 61.25–96.15% for 25C across the evaluated forecast horizons. The results highlight the value of multi-scale wind shear decomposition combined with optimized deep learning models and severity-based classification for reliable short-term wind shear forecasts and proactive operational decisions in aviation.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70074-8.title: Feasibility study of a single-device Phoswich detector for mixed-radiation monitoring: simulation-based evaluation of α/β/γ spectroscopy and practical applicability
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70074-8.abstract: Abstract Conventional surface contamination monitoring at radiation facilities and nuclear-medicine settings requires separate detectors for α-, β-, and γ-rays, complicating simultaneous measurement. A three-layer Phoswich scintillation detector (ZnS(Ag)/plastic/GSO(Ce)) enables single-device discrimination via pulse shape discrimination (PSD), but predicting its response is challenging due to complex optical transport and nonlinear energy loss in dead layers. We developed a Geant4 simulation model validated against SRIM (Stopping and Range of Ions in Matter) and ESTAR (Electron STopping powers And Ranges) stopping-power codes to evaluate radiation-type discrimination and nuclide identification feasibility. The simulated photomultiplier tube (PMT) photon-count distributions revealed substantial overlap between β-particles and γ-rays, demonstrating that PSD is essential. Provided that PSD-based classification is achieved (experimentally established for the present configuration), energy resolutions of 3.92–5.24% (α, 3.5–8.0 MeV) and 12.77–17.83% (β, 1.0–3.0 MeV) were obtained, sufficient for identifying α-emitter ( 211 At) and β-emitters ( 90 Sr– 90 Y, 137m Ba). γ-emitters ( 99m Tc, 111 In, 201 Tl, 18 F, 137 Cs) were identified via photopeaks, while higher-energy γ-rays produced Compton continua. L’Hoir asymmetric fitting extracted α and β peak centroids under area-source conditions. This study provides a quantitative foundation for single-device Phoswich detectors in mixed-radiation monitoring across radiation-facility and nuclear-medicine environments.
